# Tacet shared-core consolidation — decisions record, v4.309

**2026-07-31 · A living record of what has been decided so far for the Tacet shared-core consolidation, so the decisions stop living in chat. Supersedes v0.1. The questions in §23 Open questions are NOT decided and must not be treated as settled.**

## HOW THIS FILE IS NUMBERED — one rule, read it before adding a section

> **Section numbers are permanent. New sections append to the end and take the next number, wherever Related documents happens to sit. No section is ever renumbered, for any reason. A number in this file is a citation target and must stay valid.**

**That is the whole rule.** Related documents is §38 and stays §38 even though sections now follow it. If that offends the eye, leave it offended — a tidy appendix is worth less than a citation that still resolves.

**The previous convention — "the reference appendix stays last", which required renumbering the appendix on every addition — is RETIRED as of 2026-09-03 (v4.125).** It existed only as narration inside three changelog entries (v4.97-era, v4.101, v4.124), was invisible to anyone who had not read them, was broken twice by sessions that could not see it, and on the second occasion produced a real collision: two unmerged branches each defining a §39, one of them having renumbered a live section to get there. **Those three entries are historical and are not edited; this block overrides them.** If you are reading one of them and about to renumber the appendix — don't.

## HOW CITATIONS IN THIS FILE ARE READ — one rule, and it governs every dated entry

> **A `file:line` citation anywhere in this file is a HISTORICAL COORDINATE: true on the day it was written, never re-checked since, and almost certainly stale now. Re-verify it before acting on it, and never quote one as a current position.**

Section numbers are permanent by the rule above and always resolve. **Line numbers are the opposite and always rot**, and the difference is worth stating once rather than being learned per reader.

**This is measured, not assumed.** The Step 3 location commerce survey (2026-09-05) re-read every position it needed across the survey and design documents in `docs/` and found drift of up to several thousand lines — `retail_stores` cited at `database.js:2565` now sits at `:3383`, and cited positions in `routes/retail-purchasing.js` and `routes/retail-waste.js` were out by roughly a hundred each. **In every case the prose at the old address held up and only the coordinate had moved.** That is the failure mode to expect: a file grows, a citation is never revisited, and a later reader either follows it into unrelated code or discards a sound finding because its address is wrong. The second is the worse outcome and the harder one to notice.

**So: read the claim, then find the code by NAME** — a function, a column, a table, a constant — **and cite the position you actually found if you are writing a new entry.** This applies to every document this file points at as evidence, not only to this one.

2026-09-18 · v4.308 — **§172 · WHAT THE SHOP KNOWS ABOUT A PERSON IS READ ON EVERY ORDER, AND IS EDITED IN ONE PLACE — DECIDED BY ASH.** Ash, on TC000750's drawer: *“an order note will appear only for that order. however we need a note that will appear for this customer order everytime he place an order”*. **NO STORAGE IS ADDED — A READ IS.** `retail_customers.note` and `.tags` have existed since the customer drawer's Know block and no order ever looked at them, so the knowledge sat in the right place and reached nobody at the moment it was needed. **THREE NOTES, NOT ONE**: `customer_note` is the BUYER's, for that order; `staff_note` is the SHOP's, for that order; `customer_standing_note` (aliased from `retail_customers.note` on the order read) is the shop's, about the PERSON, on every order they place. **THE COPY RULE IS THE ARCHITECTURE**: the note is READ through the `LEFT JOIN retail_customers` that `GET /api/retail-admin/orders/:id` already made for the nickname and phone, and never stamped onto an order — correct it once and every order past, open and future reads the correction, because one copy exists. **READ-ONLY IN THE DRAWER**, Edit navigates to the customer: an editable box there sits pixels from the per-order Shop note under a near-identical label, which is how “no ice THIS time” gets typed into a note that follows a person for a year. **IT NEVER REACHES THE CUSTOMER** — `loadOrderForCustomer` names its columns by hand and does not select it, deliberately and load-bearingly. **NOTHING RENDERS WITHOUT A PERSON**: walk-ins and most channel orders carry no `customer_id`, so it is null and absent, with no empty state. **THREE SURFACES, ONE ENDPOINT**: the desktop drawer, the mirrored channel drawer and the phone's order detail; the Orders LIST and the kitchen print were considered and left to their own change under one-PR-per-change. **NO CHINESE IS MINTED** — `About this customer · 关于该顾客的备注` lifts its Chinese half whole from the live aria-label on the textarea the text is typed into, recorded as `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.124.

2026-09-18 · v4.306 — **§170 · THE WAIT GETS A DATE ON THE CARD, AND §108's “a pill cannot” IS OVERTURNED — DECIDED BY ASH**, reading Shop from a Shenzhen address at 10:04 on a batch morning: *“our real issue isn't the tag — it's that a Shenzhen shopper sees NEXT BATCH with no date attached until they're deep in checkout. The word alone sounds like an indefinite wait.”* **THE REPORTED ROW WAS NOT A BUG** — shelf at zero, today genuinely on the cadence (anchor 2026-06-16, interval 2, verified through `lib/batch-cadence.js`), before the 11:00 ready hour, and a Shenzhen address so §108's local-run silence correctly did not fire. Honest, and still the wrong thing to show. **§108's ruling that the word describes the ITEM stands untouched**; what is overturned is its second half, that a date *“belongs in the checkout notice ... not in a pill, which cannot”*. It can: `local_fresh_date` has ridden every browse row since §80 and only the one transit day was missing. **A customer decides whether to tap on the CARD**, so answering three screens later was the defect. **THE CARD NAMES THE ARRIVAL, WHICH DIFFERS BY SHOPPER** — the local run is served the make day, a couriered order the day after — and both are stamped SERVER-SIDE (`fresh_ship_date`, `local_fresh_in_days`) for §82's reason: no handset clock decides whether a date is tomorrow. The client adds one to an integer and formats a string it was handed. **BOUNDED AT TWO DAYS**: `TODAY · 今天` and `TOMORROW · 明天` need no reading, past that the date itself (`SEP 20 · 9月20日`) rather than a count the shopper must do arithmetic on. **NO CHINESE IS COMPOSED** — both forms are lifted whole from live pairs (`checkout.wxml:400`, `checkout.js:1911`) — so Rule 4 is not amended; the lift is recorded as `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.123. **ALL SEVEN BROWSE SURFACES MOVE TOGETHER**, which is §108's own lesson and not an enlarged brief: dating the grid alone would rebuild the exact screenshot-pair bug §108 was written for. One derivation (`miniapp/utils/fresh-eta.js`); `public/shop.html` holds the only second copy because it is a standalone storefront that requires nothing, and its copy names the original. **The add toasts, `add-to-order` and the checkout notice are untouched** — the last answers a harder question (cart, store, zero-stock roll-forward) and stays binding where the two differ, which is the safe direction. Covered by `scripts/test_fresh_batch_eta.js`.
2026-09-18 · v4.307 — **§171 · A PRINTER IS A BRAND, NOT A CONSTANT — ASKED BY ASH.** Ash, with a 商鹏 SP-T6-H for the new Yuexiu shop: *"we need to add this printer as well to our system"*, then, against a recommendation to return it for a Feie unit: *"think about different tenant, not all of them will use the same printer brand, so adding more printer options its better"*. **The second message overrides the first recommendation, which was argued on Roots' costs alone and was wrong on the product** — a tenant arrives with the printer already screwed to the counter. **The objection that survived is that slip templates must not exist twice**, and the shape answers it: `lib/feie.js` is 1210 lines of which ~120 are transport and ~1090 are 58mm layout, so there is **one renderer emitting house markup and a translation table at the wire**, per vendor, forever. **The house markup is Feie's tag set deliberately** — `<CB> <B> <L> <BOLD> <C>` — so the Feie adapter is a pass-through and no renderer moved. **The vendor is a per-store field** (`printer.by_store[].vendor`, `printer.kitchen_vendor`) because a four-shop tenant buys printers one shop at a time; **absent means `feie`**, which every saved row already is, so there is no migration. `integrations.spyun = { appid, appsecret }` rides the existing secret-box, and the global gate stops being `feieEnabled()` and becomes "is ANY vendor configured?" or a Shangpeng-only tenant is told printing is off while their printer works. **A chat-time claim that Shangpeng authenticates per-device off the label is CORRECTED here before it becomes folklore**: it is account-level like Feie, and the label's KEY binds the device once in the console — the same warning the Feie panel has carried since it was written, one vendor over. Endpoints and both signature shapes (`sha1(user+ukey+stime)` / sorted-params `MD5(…&appsecret=…)`) were **read off the published `@xesam/cloud-vendor-spyun` client and cross-checked against the base URL compiled into Shangpeng's own console bundle, not recalled**. **One thing is explicitly unverified**: Shangpeng's tag NAMES, because both vendor doc sites are client-rendered and would not open through this session's proxy — so the map ships as a commented one-screen table defaulting to pass-through, a one-line fix if a test print returns literal `<CB>`, and `BIG_WIDTH` moves into the adapter for the same reason. The SP-T6-H has **no auto-cutter** where the FP-V58-D does; nothing depends on it, recorded so the first "the printer is broken" finds the answer. **No Chinese composed** — the picker shows the vendors' own names 飞鹅 and 商鹏 — so Rule 4 is not engaged. Label printing and status polling are deliberately NOT in the contract.

2026-09-17 · v4.305 — **§169 · BUYERS ARE A BREAKDOWN, NOT A NUMBER — ASKED BY ASH.** Ash, reading the phone's Trend screen: *"people bought I see low number it can't be all channels"*. It could not, and the reason is that every customer figure on both halves of the product is keyed on `retail_orders.customer_id`, which `routes/meituan-internal.js` and `routes/eleme-internal.js` have never written — so `COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)` silently skips every marketplace order while the revenue four tiles above counts them. 79 buyers under ¥149,344. **THE DECISION IS THAT THEY STAY SEPARATE.** Summing the channels into one "people bought" would count the same human twice the moment they order in the mini app and on Meituan, and no join exists that could ever detect it — the identity spaces do not reconcile and never will. A breakdown is the closest to real that is also true. **THREE CHANNELS CAN BE COUNTED AND ONE CANNOT.** Storefront is exact on `customer_id`; Meituan is exact on `channel_customer_id` (wmUserId, "the only stable customer identity Meituan gives a merchant", stored since 2026-09-15); wholesale is countable on the real unmasked `recipient_phone` the gzgrocery daemon writes. **Eleme cannot, and that is now evidenced rather than assumed**: the shape digest was read back on 2026-09-17 and its `userInfo` object — the only person-shaped container in 189 field names — holds 33 keys that are consignee name, phones, address, distance and IM state, and no id of any kind. It identifies a DELIVERY, not a customer. **NEW-VS-RETURNING IS NOT ONE DEFINITION ACROSS THE THREE, and the doc says so rather than the screen implying otherwise**: storefront's *new* means first-ever paid order falling inside the window, which we compute; Meituan's means `channel_customer_orders = 1`, which is MEITUAN'S OWN lifetime count at the moment the order arrived and covers business done before this daemon existed. They are both honest and they are not the same question, so they are labelled by channel and never added together. **THE MEITUAN COUNT UNDER-REPORTS UNTIL MID-SEPTEMBER AND IS SHOWN ANYWAY, WITH ITS DATE.** `channel_customer_id` has only been stored since 2026-09-15, so a 30- or 90-day window reads low and will climb as history accrues; backfilling means re-reading every historical order from Meituan and is not done. A figure carrying *from 15 Sep* is honest; one silently reading 3 is not. **NOTHING ELSE MOVES.** Revenue, orders, products, stores, payments and visits are untouched — this section decides the customer figures and only those. Covered on the phone by `scripts/test_mobile_trend.js` and asserted against the payload's real key names so a server-side rename breaks a test rather than a card.

2026-09-17 · v4.304 — **§168 · THE FACILITY NAMES COME INTO ENGLISH, AND §30's "KEEP IT CHINESE" NARROWS TO ONE CASE — ASKED BY ASH.** Looking at TC000761 on the English side: *"can we do city and provinces also in English?"* **This REVERSES a decision taken the same day, six hours earlier, by the session that shipped the carrier-event translator (PR #676).** That decision kept FACILITY names Chinese inside a translated sentence on two arguments — they are proper nouns, and a customer ringing the carrier needs the Chinese. **Both fail on a real timeline.** A customer quotes a WAYBILL, never a sorting centre; and `Left 深圳航空分拣中心 — heading to 北京大兴航空分拣中心` withholds the single most useful fact on the screen — the parcel flew Shenzhen to Beijing — from precisely the reader the translation exists for. Half the sentence was English and the half carrying the geography was not. **PARSED, NOT TRANSLITERATED.** These names are structured `[city][district][type]`, so three tables reassemble them: `广州黄埔集货分拣中心` → Guangzhou Huangpu Consolidation Sorting Centre, `广州黄村站` → Guangzhou Huangcun Station. **ALL OR NOTHING** — one unknown part and the WHOLE name stays Chinese, so `广州市-保利天汇项目接驳点` renders unchanged rather than as a half-English `Guangzhou 保利天汇项目 Transfer Point`; the same rule the location field already follows, and what stops a growing table producing mixed lines while it grows. **PICKUP POINTS STAY CHINESE, and are now the whole of that rule rather than a blanket**: the customer physically walks to a `菜鸟驿站` and matches the name against a shopfront sign, which is the one case the original reasoning was right about. **Also here: air legs.** TC000761's newest event — the top line of the screen, the first thing a customer reads — was `您的快件在【深圳市飞往北京】的航班上,已起飞` and had no rule at all; it now reads `In flight — Shenzhen to Beijing, departed`, the two names taken as cities because that is what they are. **No Chinese is composed** — every string added is English read out of Chinese the carrier wrote — so `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` Rule 4 is not engaged and this is not an amendment to it. `scripts/test_tracking_translation.js` grows to 94 checks; its section 6 previously asserted the opposite and now carries the reversal in its own comment, so the change is readable rather than merely absent.

2026-09-17 · v4.303 — **§98 ADDENDUM 7 · THE FOUR STEPS ARE NUMBERED, AND THE THREE THAT ARE NOT NEXT STOP SHOUTING — REPORTED BY ASH** from the phone, against TC000716 with the case open on screen: *"not clear, maybe step by step better?"*. **THE PANEL WAS ASKED FOR A WIZARD AND DID NOT GET ONE, AND THAT REFUSAL IS THE DECISION HERE.** One step at a time was put up and rejected on three grounds, recorded because it is the intuitive answer: the steps are **not strictly ordered** — the carrier rings while the remedy is still open, which is ordinary, and the renderers have carried controls for an out-of-turn step since §98 precisely so it is reachable; a wizard **costs the glance**, and seeing where a case stands without tapping is the whole reason the panel exists rather than a page; and it would **undo the weight pass** §98 addendum 6 shipped off Ash's own *"can make a better design?"*. Ash chose the alternative. **WHAT WAS ACTUALLY UNCLEAR, MEASURED OFF THE PHOTOGRAPH, WAS THREE THINGS.** The header counted `✓ 1/4` and **no row on screen carried a 1, a 2, a 3 or a 4** for it to be counting. **Six controls were visible at once** — `Claim filed`, `Not claiming`, `Add photo`, `Send replacement`, `Refunded`, `Nothing needed` — and three of them belonged to a step that was not next, sitting directly under the one that was; the one-primary rule held and was never the problem, the greys were. And the footer printed *"to do: Replacement or refund · Carrier settled"*, **naming two rows two and three lines above it** — the same words twice, in a block whose complaint was that there was too much to read. **THE FIX IS THREE CHANGES AND NO NEW BEHAVIOUR.** A later step's marker is its NUMBER, the NEXT pane's eyebrow carries `n/total`, and the blocker codes are worded as NUMERALS so the footer points at the rows instead of repeating them — `to do: 3 · 4`. A later step's controls FOLD, behind a chevron, one open at a time; an out-of-turn step stays reachable and costs a tap. **NOT A WORD WAS MINTED IN EITHER LANGUAGE** — numerals, a chevron and a dash, with `下一步` and `待办` already live — so `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched and deliberately so; this is the *"a numeral or a name often needs no label at all"* preference taken rather than a composition declared. **THE n/a ROW STOPPED LOOKING FINISHED**: a case that will not claim drew its carrier step with a green tick and a `–` in the STAMP slot, which reads as a step somebody did; the dash is now the marker and the tick is gone, matching the count that has never counted it. **THE TWO SURFACES FOLD BY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, ON PURPOSE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING TO READ BEFORE TOUCHING EITHER.** The phone repaints on the 60-second live backstop, so its fold is `state.dcMore` or the row would close under the thumb of whoever opened it. The drawer does NOT repaint on a fold, and must not: its claim number and amounts are **inline inputs**, so calling `renderOpenOrder` to open a row would have thrown away a claim number half-typed two rows above — it flips two attributes and touches nothing else. Same panel, same picture, two correct answers. **Tests:** `scripts/test_mobile_delay_panel.js` 47 → **55 assertions across 11 cases**, gaining the fold, the numerals, the footer and a geometry measurement of the FRESH state — every measured case in that file until now drew a panel whose steps were all finished, so the numbered row and the chevron had never been measured at all. **Three breaks were confirmed red**: the fold removed, the numerals put back to circles, and the footer returned to labels. `scripts/test_delay_panel_rows.js` had **pinned `delayDone`'s ARITY** through a regex matching to the closing bracket, so a fourth argument read as the stamp-and-sentence fault that file exists to catch; it now matches up to `note`, which is what its own comment says it guards. 274 fast suites pass, 0 fail. A build under §98 and §125 with no rule reversed, hence a patch.

2026-09-17 · v4.302 — **§167 · MAKING ONE: SCALE IT, GATHER IT, WORK THE STEPS — AND WRITE NOTHING — ASKED BY ASH.** Stage two of §164's phone screen, option C of the mockups. A recipe gains *Make it*: a batch multiplier in halves (clamped 0.5–20), the ingredient list scaled live and tickable as it is gathered, and a full-height step sheet that covers the tab bar because nothing else on the phone is wanted while somebody is working a step. **NOTHING IS WRITTEN, and that is the design rather than a limitation.** The scale and the ticks are facts about this afternoon, not about the recipe; the row on the server is untouched by doubling it, so the screen needs no write capability and carries no save. One week after §164's addendum found that hiding a tab whose inputs a save still read had armed a silent data loss, a new phone screen that writes to recipes is not what this needs. **THE FINISH HANDS OFF INSTEAD OF LOGGING A BATCH OF ITS OWN.** What a recipe PRODUCES is not a settled question — it may back a material, feed several products at different pack sizes, or neither — and `logbatch` already answers that in product units and is tested doing it. So the foot of the screen OPENS that screen, gated on `canRoute('logbatch')` because `production:log` is a different key from `recipes:view` and the button would otherwise open onto a refusal. Inventing a second, recipe-shaped write beside a tested one would have been answering the material-versus-product question in passing. **TWO THINGS THE MOCKUP DREW WERE NOT BUILT, because the data cannot back them:** `recipe_steps` holds id, recipe_id, step_number, name and instructions — there is no step→ingredient link and no timer, so the per-step *This step uses* block and the rest-timer note are both absent, and the test asserts their absence rather than leaving it to memory. Vocabulary: `Step N of M · 第 N 步,共 M 步` is LIFTED from the broadcast composer, and Back, Next and Done are the app's own live pairs; only `Make it · 开始制作` and `Start the steps · 开始步骤` are composed, each two live words joined. Coverage: `scripts/test_mobile_recipes.js` grows to cover it, including that the screen contains no write verb at all.

2026-09-17 · v4.301 — **§166 · A CHOICE THE CUSTOMER MAKES IS PART OF WHAT THE PRODUCT COSTS — AND A FEATURE THAT WAS ALREADY DESIGNED IS WITHDRAWN.** Ash reported a waste problem (*"fresh meals sometimes are waste without the dressing, we keep dressing many time in the freezer"*) and then, two turns later, the thing underneath it: *"beet salad is an example of a salad that we offer to choose 2 types of dressing. the staff made a mistake and put both of them inside the recipe."* **The second report killed the first fix.** A tick on the material and a *was the dressing kept?* question on the waste sheet was designed, measured against the live ledger (¥27.65 of ¥121.93 in thirteen days, `scripts/diagnose_dressing_waste.js`) and is now **withdrawn, not deferred**: it was a workaround for the dressing being buried in a recipe, and once the dressing is its own stocked product a binned salad is a binned salad. **Waste is the one reader this section does not change.** The real fault is not waste at all — Beet Salad carries ¥11.43 where the truth is ¥8.31 or ¥9.33, **20–27% too high on every sale at a ¥48 price**, and the live sweep found it is the ONLY genuine instance among five candidate recipes. The hole it opens is far wider than dressings: 54 option choices draw down a real shelf today and 15 can be priced, on 8.5% of all order lines, and `routes/finance-summary.js` had already written the gap down in its own words — *"OPTIONS carry a price delta with no cost counterpart"*. So `lib/option-cost.js` answers the two questions separately: a SALE takes the chosen choice's cost into the new `retail_order_items.options_cost_at_sale`, and the CATALOGUE takes the **dearest REQUIRED** choice, because nobody has chosen yet and a mean reads plausible while flattering. **A second column rather than a wider `unit_cost_at_sale`, and that is provable rather than tidy**: that column is multiplied by `pack_units` downstream while a linked choice is added once per unit bought, so one column would have charged a six-pack for six oat milks. **The direction of the error is the whole point** — taking the dressing out of the recipe replaces a cost that was too high with one that is too low, and too low is what gets a price cut, so the editor's margin ships in the same commit and a required choice nobody priced **blocks it outright** rather than falling back to the typed figure. Two pairs COMPOSED and declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.117. `cost_coverage`, the channel ingest paths and `is_default` are all deliberately untouched, each for a stated reason. Covered by `scripts/test_option_cost.js` (23 checks).

2026-09-17 · v4.300 — **§164 ADDENDUM · THE WIRE IS CLOSED, AND CLOSING IT FOUND A LIVE DATA LOSS THE SCREEN GATE HAD CREATED — ASKED BY ASH**, who was told the figures were still one devtools tab away and said to close it. `routes/retail-recipes.js` now strips money from all four reads and 403s the one write, through `lib/recipe-cost-visibility.js` — EXTRACTED like `lib/product-cost-visibility.js` beside it, so the rules can be held to a contract without standing up a database. Same three rules as waste and materials, deliberately: **fails closed** (a null cap set is not a grant), **keys DELETED not zeroed** (a 0 reads as free), **a FIELD refused, never a request** — with `costs_hidden: true` on the envelope so a client can tell *withheld* from *there was none*. The computed cost object is **ALLOW-LISTED, not deny-listed**, and that is the one shape here that differs in kind: `computeRecipeCost()` returns thirty-odd keys, fifteen of them money, and it GROWS (`materialCostPerGram` and `embeddedOverhead` both arrived after the first of them), so a deny-list is a list of the money keys that existed the day it was written. Percentages go with the amounts — `foodCostPct`, `overheadPct` and `targetFoodCost` print no currency sign and are still cost — and the three COUNTS stay, because a count and a cause are what make a fault fixable. **AND THE REAL FINDING: §164's screen gate had quietly armed a data loss.** `draftCostData()` reads the Cost & Pricing inputs out of the DOM; §164 stopped rendering that tab; `v()` returns null for an element that is not there and `parseFloat(null) || 0` is **0** — so an operator holding `recipes:edit` without `recipes:costs` who corrected a recipe's NAME would have PUT `{labour: 0, overhead_pct: 0, sell_price: 0, target_food_cost: 30}` and wiped the labour, the overhead and the sell price, taking every margin built on that recipe with them. Live from the moment #669 deployed; no preset holds edit-without-costs, so the exposure was the by-name grants alone. **OMITTING THE KEYS WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT**, which is the trap worth naming: `lib/recipe-cost-data-write.js` grants preserve-on-absent to `packaging_type_id` ALONE and says in terms that "an absent `labour` still writes 0, an absent `target_food_cost` still writes 30" — the packaging comment in `draftCostData()` is about that one column and does not generalise. Not sending the REQUEST is the only shape that preserves what is stored, and the route refuses it anyway for a tab left open across the deploy, a retry, or a hand-rolled request. Coverage: `scripts/test_recipe_cost_visibility.js` grows to 106 assertions, including that a money key invented tomorrow does not leak, that the sell price survives, and that no GET 403s.

2026-09-17 · v4.299 — **§164 · A RECIPE IS NOT ONLY A COST, AND THE KITCHEN NEEDS THE HALF THAT ISN'T — ASKED BY ASH**, choosing how the desktop Recipes screen should reach the phone: *"the only thing is that cost section should be only accessable per role permission . kitchen staff for example can't reach there"*. **THERE IS ONE KEY WHERE THERE SHOULD BE TWO.** `lib/capabilities.js` gives materials, products and waste each a PAIR — a view key that opens the screen and a costs key that reveals the money on it, with `waste:costs` deliberately off in both floor presets — and gives Recipes only `recipes:view`, which **alone among the view keys carries `money: 'shows'`**, justified by MONEY_NOTES' `A recipe is a cost. · 食谱本身就是成本。`. A button offering to refresh some words must not change what the shop shows; `keepFlag` now carries the live value, and the two callers that genuinely mean *turn it on* — the Design switch and the wizard's option — are unchanged. **COVERAGE:** `test_product_duplicate_fields.js` section 5 runs the SHIPPED duplicate handler against a real in-memory database (sections kept, source recorded, source itself unmarked, mark in the reply, and **not** marked when there was nothing to copy — `NULL` and `'[]'` both); the new `test_product_editor_open_freshness.js` asserts the flush, the iframe handover, the gate, `keepFlag` and that the clear rides on the `description_blocks` write itself. **Every case red-proofed against the tree before the fix.** **ONE PAIR COMPOSED** — `Designed page came from X · 设计页来自 X`, both halves lifted (`设计页` from the bar's own existing line, `来自` from the locked `来自仓库`), declared with its rejected live candidates in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.112; the compact summary row keeps the existing locked pair. `test:fast` **274 suites, 0 failed** — the suite COUNT is unchanged because this adds cases to two existing files rather than a third: 6 to `test_product_duplicate_fields.js` and 10 to `test_product_editor_open_freshness.js`, which was itself added earlier in the same branch and is already in the 274. eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS; swallowed-errors PASS at budget. **Schema: one idempotent `addColumn`, no rebuild, no backfill.** No change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-16 · v4.289 — **§153 · A PICK-ANY QUESTION CAN NOW SAY HOW MANY — DECIDED BY ASH**, from a screenshot of the product editor showing a three-choice group headed *Choose 2 crunchy sides · 爽脆配菜（选2款）*: *“need to limit how many can choose. in this example can choose only 2 from the 3 option.”* **THE SENTENCE LIVED IN THE LABEL AND NOWHERE ELSE.** `type='multi'` took ANY number of answers, including none: a customer ticked one side or all three and checked out either way, and `is_required` — a yes/no — can say *at least one* but never *exactly two*. **TWO COLUMNS, NOT ONE, AND THE SECOND ONE WAS ARGUED FOR RATHER THAN ASSUMED:** a maximum alone is what was asked for and is NOT what shipped, because with `max 2` and no floor a customer ticks one cracker and checks out under a label promising two — the same complaint, one control later. `min_choices` + `max_choices` on `retail_product_options`, **0 on both = no limit**, which is what every row written before today carries, so nothing already authored changes shape. `is_required` and the floor are two faces of one rule and are kept in step on save. **THE FLOOR IS NOT ABSOLUTE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE TRAP.** *Choose 2* whose stock-backed sides have sold down to one cannot be answered; an unanswerable required question does not make a product unbuyable here, it stops being a floor — the same principle §120 states for a question whose answers were all deleted. Both storefronts and the counter menu are served a floor **already clamped to the choices still pickable**, and every checkout measures pickability the same way. **Clamp one side and not the other and the endpoint refuses the very order the page told the customer to place**, with nothing on screen able to explain it; that is the assertion the new suite exists for. **ENFORCED ON BOTH CHECKOUT PATHS, not one** — the QR menu basket (`routes/shop-menu.js`) and customer order-create plus add-to-a-live-order (`routes/retail.js`) — because a limit enforced on one of two checkouts is not a limit. **A REPEATED CHOICE ID COUNTS ONCE**: a tick-box is on or off, so counting the repeat would refuse a correct line and counting it toward a floor would let one side satisfy a request for two. **ONE MODULE FOR THE RULE**, `lib/option-limits.js` — the save path normalises, the menu and both checkouts clamp, and **the browser clients get no copy of the arithmetic**, only the already-clamped numbers: a limit the client computes is a limit the client can compute differently. `addonAvailabilityById()` was extracted from the product response in `routes/retail.js` for the same reason — the floor needed to ask *is this extra still on the shelf* and a second copy would have been a second answer. **WHAT THE OPERATOR SETS:** two number boxes on a Pick-any row, hidden on Pick-one. **WHAT THE CUSTOMER READS:** *Choose 2* / 选 2 项 under the question, the tick-box that would break the ceiling greyed out (a ticked one stays live — untick is how you change your mind), and the Add button blocked under the floor naming the number. **FIVE COMPOSED CN STRINGS, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.99**, every one a live shape with a numeral swapped in; 不限 is a verbatim lift from four live admin strings, and **款 — Ash’s own word in the label that prompted this — was weighed and recorded as rejected** in favour of 项, which is what `至少选一项` already establishes as the counter for an option answer. **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, named so nobody reads silence as coverage:** the wizard offers no limit control; `routes/retail.js` order-create still does not enforce the older `is_required` flag (a pre-existing gap that a floor of 1+ now closes for pick-any groups, and a separate change otherwise); `public/shop.html` still does not grey out a sold-out paid extra although the server has answered `addon_available` since §120 — the mini app does; and there is no per-choice quantity, so two sides cannot both be corn chips. New suite `scripts/test_option_limits.js` **19/19**, nine of them pure rule tests and the rest driving the REAL router over HTTP. `test:fast` 265 → **266**; lint 0 errors. **REBASED THREE TIMES MID-BUILD, onto db7de6f, 9ef2400 and then 1480456** — three other sessions merged into this tree while it was being written, which is what the enumerate-first rule in `CLAUDE.md` exists to make visible. PR #640 landed first and took §151 and v1.97; PR #643 landed last and took v1.98 AND §152. This renumbered each time rather than renumbering theirs — section numbers are permanent. **§152 IS DELIBERATELY LEFT EMPTY IN THIS FILE**, not skipped by accident: PR #643's vocabulary entry cites §152 for the sign-out work but never wrote that section here, so the number is held for it rather than taken. A reader following v1.98's citation today lands on nothing, and that is a gap in #643 to close, not one to paper over by filling §152 with something else. PR #641 landed second, in the same admin file: it makes the WIZARD's Required tick visible on a pick-any question, which this reinforces rather than contradicts — a wizard-set required multi now normalises to `min_choices 1`, and a floor of 1 IS required. **One assertion of that PR's suite had to be updated**, and it is named here rather than quietly edited: `test_wizard_required_pick.js` pinned the web storefront's block to the literal `o.is_required && !selIds(o).length`, which the floor rewrote. 2026-09-16 · v4.288 — **§151 · A LOCKED DATABASE IS NOT A SIGNED-OUT OPERATOR — DECIDED BY ASH**, shown the finding and asked whether to fix it: *“fix it”*. **FOUND BY A TEST THAT FAILED ONCE.** During the §150 build, one parallel run of `npm run test:fast` came back with `scripts/test_manual_restock_park.js` failing `401 !== 200`; it passed alone and passed on three later full runs. **A flake is not a root cause**, so it was read rather than re-run: `requireRetailAdmin` wraps its two control-plane queries in a try/catch written for a FIRST BOOT — *tables not ready* — and that catch swallowed every error, `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked` included, then fell through to `401 Not authenticated`. **`public/retail-admin/01-core.js` sends a 401 to `/backend/login` with no prompt**, so a moment of write contention signed an operator out mid-task and said nothing about the database. The suites share one sqlite file, which is why a test met it first; production has one file and several writers too. **WHAT SHIPS:** `lib/sqlite-errors.js` tells the two cases apart, and the gate answers each honestly — schema not ready falls through to the same 401 as before (there is nobody to sign in as yet), anything else is **503 `service_busy`, logged**. **MATCHED ON THE MESSAGE, NOT THE CODE, and that is forced rather than chosen:** better-sqlite3 gives `no such table` and `no such column` the generic `SQLITE_ERROR`, which a constraint violation and a syntax error also carry. The match is narrow on purpose — an unrecognised error is treated as a real failure, so a miss costs a first boot one wrong status and the opposite default would restore the bug. **THE SAME SWALLOW, ONE FLOOR DOWN**, found by grepping for the pattern rather than closing on the one `file:line`: `lib/require-cap.js`'s `loadCaller` catches everything around its tenant read, and a swallowed error there leaves `tenant` null, which sends `resolveOperator` to the SHIPPED PRESET instead of the tenant's own edited role — **a permission decision made on capabilities nobody granted**, which is worse than a failed request. Both catches are narrowed to the schema gap they were written for. **A CLAIM MADE AND WITHDRAWN IN THE SAME BUILD, recorded because the mutation is what caught it:** the first draft also moved `next()` out of the try and said this fixed a second bug — a handler throwing synchronously after its write had landed, reported as a login problem. **A mutation putting `next()` back inside the try changed no status the suite could see**, because express catches a handler's throw at the layer boundary and turns it into `next(err)`; it never reached this gate. The code stays (this catch should be about this gate's two queries and nothing downstream) and **the comment now says it fixes nothing observable**, because a comment claiming a bug that does not exist is how the next reader is sent hunting. **WHAT THE OPERATOR READS:** `service_busy` → *The system is busy right now — try again in a moment.* / 系统繁忙,请稍后重试。 **ONE COMPOSED STRING, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.97** with its rejected candidates: the three live alternatives all blame the operator (操作过于频繁, 尝试次数过多) or describe a read only (加载失败), and the person clicking did nothing wrong. 请稍后重试 is live in five pairs in that same error table; 系统繁忙 is WeChat's own word for this state and is already in the tree. **401 REMAINS THE ONLY STATUS THAT SENDS ANYBODY TO THE LOGIN PAGE**, and every ordinary refusal — no such operator, an inactive one, a suspended tenant — is still exactly 401: the fix must not widen a gate, and a test holds each one. New suite `scripts/test_retail_admin_gate.js` **14/14**, driving the REAL router over HTTP with the failure injected onto the shared database module so the error arrives from where a real one would; proven non-vacuous by four mutations, **one of which walked past the check meant for it** and is the withdrawal above. **Its own runner had to be fixed first**: the checks are async and a synchronous runner would have let every assertion escape as an unhandled rejection and printed a tick — a suite that cannot fail is worse than none. `test:fast` 262 → **263**; lint 0 errors. No schema, no migration, no change to the mini app, the QR menu, the web storefront, `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-16 · v4.287 — **§150 · THE COUNTER SELLS WHAT THE SHOP HAS AND WHAT THE SHOP MAKES — DECIDED BY ASH from a Tianhe till**, on a screenshot of the counter search: *“i cant see the products made in the location in the counter till”*, and then, shown the two shapes the fix could take, the argument that settled it: *“people might order from the mini app products that offered in the warehouse of that location, the till will not show them because they are not on the menu list”*. **THE TILL WAS ASKING THE WEBSITE WHAT THE COUNTER MAY SELL.** `public/till.html` built its product list from `/api/retail-admin/products?published=1` and its quantities from `/stores/:id/stock?published=1` — `is_published`, the ONLINE STORE's flag. **§42 draws the line the other way round and the public QR menu has honoured it since §47**: *is_published governs the online store; a shop listing governs the shop*. Nothing built at a counter is ever sold on a website, so nothing built at a counter was ever published, so nothing built at a counter reached a till. **A latte was invisible to the cashier standing next to the machine that makes it**, and publishing it to get it on screen would have put it on the website AND drawn it greyed out, because a made-here row has no shelf record by design (§47) and the till reads 0 as sold out. **THE SHAPE ASH REJECTED IS THE TIDY ONE.** Menu-only was put to him and argued against here before he answered; his own reason for refusing it is better than the one offered, and it is recorded in his words above: **the mini app already sells that location's warehouse stock**, so a till narrowed to the menu would take a walk-in customer's sale off a shelf the app is selling from. **THREE SOURCES, ONE LIST**, and the change is ADDITIVE — no tile a cashier can see today disappears: this location's menu at ITS price (§42 puts the price on the listing, so the counter and the QR code can no longer quote two figures for one drink); anything counted on this location's shelf, published or not, because **publishing is a decision about a website and has nothing to do with whether a cashier may sell a box somebody put on the shelf in front of them**; and everything the till already showed. **A LISTING GOVERNS ITS PRODUCT ABSOLUTELY** — where one exists it decides the price, the mode and whether the row appears at all, so a product switched off for the day is ABSENT rather than reappearing two rows down at the catalogue price, which is exactly what concatenating the two halves would have done. **MADE HERE IS NEVER STOCK-GATED**: its stock comes back `null` rather than 0 and §42's manual switch is the whole of its availability, per §47's closing line. **ONE NEW ROUTE, NO NEW TABLE, NO SCHEMA, NO MIGRATION**, and **the containment around `shop_listings` was NOT widened**: the route lives in `routes/retail-shops.js` for the reason `/products/:id/shops` already gives in that file — a reader in `public/till.html` would have forced the allowlist in `scripts/test_shop_listings.js` open, and a reader there widens nothing. The till FETCHES it and never names the table; a check in the new suite holds that. **THE ORDER PATH IS UNCHANGED AND WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM** — `resolveManualOrderLines` resolves on `is_active` alone, with no published gate, and has always accepted a per-line `unit_price`. **The till posts one on menu lines and only on menu lines**: a listing's price is the single figure that endpoint cannot resolve for itself, and a till that posted its own number for everything would charge a stale one every time the office corrected a catalogue price between two reloads of the tablet. **`shops.is_active` IS DELIBERATELY NOT CONSULTED** — it governs the `/s/:shopCode` page, and switching a QR menu off is a statement about a public URL, not about whether the counter may ring up a coffee; the till's own closed-store gate (`posClosedForStore`) is untouched. New suite `scripts/test_counter_catalogue.js` **21/21**, proven non-vacuous by four mutations (made-here gated on the shelf, a switched-off listing falling through to the catalogue half, listed rows priced from the product, the published/counted narrowing removed) each caught by the check meant for it; `test:fast` 261 → **262**; lint 0 errors. **One correction to an older document made in the same pass**: `scripts/test_shop_listings.js` printed *“Nothing else reads these tables yet — the till is unchanged”*, which this makes false, so the heading and the allowlist's note now say what is actually true. No new UI string in either language, so nothing to declare in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`. No change to the mini app, the QR menu, the web storefront, `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-16 · v4.286 — **§149 · PEANUTS AND TREE NUTS ARE NOT THE SAME ALLERGEN, AND “NONE DECLARED” WAS ALREADY BUILT IN — DECIDED BY ASH, asked about the nuts specifically rather than shown a usage count:** *“Peanuts and Tree nuts separate”*. **THE ONE BLOCK WHERE A WRONG WORD HAS A CONSEQUENCE.** The catalogue had **five words for nuts** — `Nuts` 55, `Tree nuts` 36, `Other tree nuts` 15, `Other nuts` 14, `Peanuts` 7 — and these are not spelling variants: somebody allergic to peanuts is often fine with almonds and the reverse. **A customer reading `Nuts` cannot tell which they are being warned about.** So most-used-wins, the rule that decided every other list in §145 to §148, was deliberately NOT applied: the most-used word is the one being dropped. **The 55 cards saying `Nuts` are not rewritten** — they keep their wording, the editor shows it as typed, and they become a visible worklist rather than a silent inconsistency. **A FINDING THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER ASH HAD ALREADY GIVEN, and it was mine to have found earlier.** Asked which of three hand-typed sentences should be the single form for *nothing to declare*, he chose `None declared` / 未声明常见致敏原. Reading the renderers afterwards shows **all three surfaces already print `None declared` / 未声明 when the contains row is blank** — `lib/product-blocks-read.js`, `public/shop/product-blocks.js` and the mini app's product-blocks component each carry their own copy. So the 66 cards that type it by hand (43 `None declared`, 15 `None`, 8 `No known allergens`) produce a CHIP saying what the empty state says quietly, and the built-in Chinese is **未声明**, not the 未声明常见致敏原 he was shown. **His choice is implemented through the mechanism that already exists rather than by adding a fourth variant:** the form now says, in both languages, that leaving both boxes empty prints it. The three surfaces are held in agreement by a test, because a product that reads one way on the counter menu and another in the app is exactly the difference a customer with an allergy would notice. **QUICK-ADD CHIPS, NOT CHECKBOXES, and the departure is deliberate.** Both rows are ONE comma-separated string and the catalogue is more specific than any checkbox — `Tree nuts (hazelnuts)`, `Sesame (tahini), Legumes (chickpeas)`. A checkbox would have to decide whether `Tree nuts (hazelnuts)` counts as ticked, and un-ticking would have to decide what to delete, **which is how an allergen line gets silently truncated**. A chip APPENDS, never removes, fills both languages with each one's own separator (`, ` and `、`, both already read by `_paSplitChips`), and is a no-op when the term is already there. **NO CHINESE COMPOSED** — all eight terms lifted, each half verified live in the committed tree. New suite `scripts/test_allergen_options.js` **12/12**, proven non-vacuous by four mutations; **one walked past the check meant for it a second time** — a removal written as `split(term).join('')` used none of the forbidden method names — so the check stopped naming methods and pins the invariant instead: the field is assigned exactly once, inside the only function that can grow it. `test:fast` 260 → **261**; lint 0 errors. 2026-09-16 · v4.283 — **§146 · A COST FILED UNDER NOTHING IS FIXED WHERE IT WAS DECIDED, NOT BY UNDOING IT — REPORTED BY ASH off a live Transactions row:** a ¥299 staff claim, *“bai · take taxi to the office and Ramada”*, approved and in the books with no category and no control anywhere in the product that could give it one. **THE GAP WAS INVISIBLE BEFORE IT WAS UNFIXABLE.** The approval row printed the category only when there was one, so a claim filed under nothing and one filed under Transport drew the same meta line; `/decide` read a `note` from its body and nothing else; and `routes/finance-transactions.js` refuses to edit a claim-posted ledger row — **correctly, and that refusal is untouched here**, since the row is a projection and any value typed onto it is lost the next time the claim re-posts. But nothing could edit the CLAIM either, so the only way to file that ¥299 was to VOID it and ask the employee to send it again — destroying an approval record to correct a classification. **WHAT SHIPS:** one category control on the claim row, in both queues, carrying the claim's current value and editable before the decision and after it; `/decide` takes an optional category and applies it in the same write that posts the row; and a new `POST /staff-expenses/:id/category` re-files an approved claim, re-posting its ledger row under the new heading. **THE PROMPT-ON-APPROVE SHAPE WAS REJECTED**, and it is the obvious one: asking only when the category is blank catches the empty case and waves the WRONG case straight through, and a category picked by a submitter who does not know the chart of accounts is wrong at least as often as it is missing — wrong data reads as good data in a report, blank data announces itself. **COMPULSION WAS REJECTED TOO** — forced, the approver clears the queue with whatever is at the top of the list, trading a visible problem for an invisible one. The claim form is unchanged. **WHY A BLANK IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY:** `finance-summary.js` gives it its own “Not recorded” line and counts it as OPERATING, so a private cost with no category silently inflates the operating total. **NO MONEY MOVES IN A RE-FILING** — same claim, same sum, same date, same person, same approval record; `postClaim`'s DELETE-then-INSERT does the work, so the ledger says what the claim says. **A SETTLED CLAIM IS STILL RE-FILEABLE**, the one place this parts company with `/decide` and `/void`: those refuse a settled claim because they would take an expense out of the books while leaving the repayment made, and nothing leaves the books here — refusing would mean a category could only be corrected before payday. **A CLAIM THAT RAISED AN ORDER IS REFUSED**, on `awaiting_delivery` as well as `po_id`, and the refusal names the way out: the order owns that cost, under the line's category. **THREE THINGS A LATER EDIT COULD QUIETLY UNDO, named:** `category = COALESCE(?, category)` in `/decide` (a bare assignment blanks the category on every claim decided by an older client); `expense_id` cleared in the same UPDATE before `postClaim` runs (§90's FK trap, third occurrence); and the submitter's name resolved BEFORE the transaction, or a re-post rewrites the ledger line stripped of whose taxi it was. **THE PICK IS HELD IN STATE, NOT THE DOM** — both queues re-render when a receipt is opened, so a category chosen and then checked against the photo would have been thrown away at the exact moment the approver was being careful. **WHO MAY RE-FILE — EITHER `expenses:approve` OR `expenses:cancel`, DECIDED BY ASH** on being shown the route as first built: the `bookkeeper` preset holds `cancel` and not `approve`, so the accountant could remove a claim from the books entirely and could not rename the heading it sat under — the bigger hammer and not the small screwdriver, for the one role whose job this is. Re-filing moves no money and is strictly less power than the void they already hold; it is not a third key, for the reason `/settle` gives about sharing one. **AND A PERMISSION WITH NO SCREEN IS NOT A PERMISSION** — `/pending` is approver-gated, so the claim row on TRANSACTIONS gains the same control, beside the Void link that is there for the same reason (§90) and where the ¥299 was noticed in the first place. Void stays hidden once a claim is settled and re-filing does not, which is the whole asymmetry in one row. **NEARLY WRONG, RECORDED:** `finTxCatOptions()` branches on the FORM's kind, so a claim row would have been offered INCOME categories whenever the income form had last been opened; the expense half is now its own function. **TESTS:** thirty-three new checks in `scripts/test_staff_expenses.js` (82 → 115), fast shard, covering the re-post behaviour against a fixture ledger, both pickers and the ledger row's actions EXECUTED in a VM rather than grepped, and every invariant above. No schema, no migration, no change to what a claim means, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-16 · v4.282 — **§145 · A LABEL TYPED 724 TIMES IS A LABEL TYPED SEVERAL WAYS — DECIDED BY ASH, shown the measurements and asked which to build:** *“do all as you recommend”*. **WHAT THE CATALOGUE SAID.** `scripts/diagnose_spec_strip_labels.js`, read-only against production, over the **724 spec-strip cells on 242 products**: the same label has been typed several ways — `Net Wt` **163** beside `Net Weight` **29**, `Certification` / `Certified` / `Certifications` across **13** cells, and **four Chinese words for “category”** (类别 14, 品类 6, 分类 5, …). Nobody was careless; that is what happens when a label is retyped 724 times on different days. **THE VALUES WERE THE BIGGER FIND, and were not what anybody guessed:** under Origin, **“Guangzhou, China” is 109 of 156 cells (70%)**; under Shelf Life, **“See packaging” is 46 of 57 (81%)** — and its Chinese came out three ways (见包装标示 38, 见包装 8, 请见包装标注 2); under Diet, **“100% plant” is 28 of 29**. **242 cells whose answer was typed out by hand, in two languages, every time.** **WHAT IS DECIDED:** two dropdowns per cell — one for the label, one for the value, the second depending on the first, because “Guangzhou, China” is an answer to Origin and nonsense under Net Wt. **A PICK FILLS BOTH LANGUAGES**, which is the half that matters more than the typing saved: a typed label is one somebody can finish in English and forget in 中文, and nothing on the English view shows the gap. **`Type` IS DELIBERATELY NOT OFFERED beside `Product Type`** — they are not spellings of each other but two labels for one idea (66 and 64 cells, holding the same answers); only one can be offered or the split continues, and `Product Type` wins on the Chinese where 产品类型 (83) already beats 类型 (40). **NET WT GETS NO VALUE LIST ON PURPOSE** — 67 distinct weights across 163 cells is exactly what a weight field should look like; so do Certification and Storage, too thin to draw a list from. **NOTHING REWRITES A LIVE PAGE.** The 66 cells that say `Type` keep saying it; the list is an offer, and `peMount` and `paBlocksCollect` never consult it. The match is on the ENGLISH only and case-insensitive, so a cell reading `Net wt` is not shown as unusual and a cell carrying a good 中文 the list spells differently is never demoted to “Something else”, which would invite somebody to overwrite it. **THE PICK IS A CONVENIENCE LAYER, NEVER A SECOND WRITER** — the `k_en`/`k_cn`/`v_en`/`v_cn` inputs never leave the DOM and still ride `paBlocksSyncFromDOM` unchanged; the selects write into those inputs and never into the block, so free text is not a special case but what the control already was. **ONE ORDERING BUG, CAUGHT IN A BROWSER RATHER THAN IN REVIEW, and now held by a test:** the handler must write the inputs BEFORE it syncs, because syncing first reads the OLD values into the model and `paRenderDoc` paints them back over the pick — choosing `Product Type` left the cell saying `Net Wt`. **NO CHINESE COMPOSED — every pair in both lists is LIFTED from production with its count**, recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.92. New suite `scripts/test_spec_strip_picklists.js` **15/15**, proven non-vacuous by four mutations (sync-before-write, an unscoped cell query, `Type` re-offered, a label with no Chinese) each caught by the check meant for it; `test:fast` 257 → **258**; lint 0 errors. No schema, no migration, no change to the mini app, the QR menu, the web storefront, `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-15 · v4.281 — **§144 · THE PRODUCT EDITOR IS A FORM, NOT A BUILDER — AND THE READING ORDER IS OFFERED, NEVER IMPOSED — DECIDED BY ASH from three working prototypes:** *“option a”*. **WHY A BUILDER WAS THE WRONG SHAPE, measured rather than felt.** A read-only production run of `scripts/diagnose_block_spine_order.js` over the 260 live products that carry any blocks finds nine types on 73–99% of them — `hero_intro` 99%, `spec_strip` 93%, `how_to_use` 90%, `notes_callout` 89%, `ingredients_chips` 87%, `why` 86%, `storage_box` 84%, `big_stat` 83%, `allergen_card` 73% — then a cliff to `nutrition_facts` 8%, `pull_quote` 5%, `recipe_steps` 3%, `ingredients_line` 0%. Four offered types (`image_band`, `pairings`, `faq`, `stat_callout`) are on no product at all. **Nobody is composing a page; everybody is filling in the same one.** So the editor stops asking the office to assemble what it already knows, and the nine become a spine that is always present — written sections inline, unwritten ones as a named line carrying how many products do say it, so a gap reads as unusual or ordinary without opening anything. **WHAT IS DECIDED, and the second half is the one that matters:** the spine is rendered, and **the stored order is preserved**. The same run found **71 distinct block orders in use**, with only 145 of 260 products (56%) sitting inside the commonest — so an editor that rendered a canonical order and saved it would have silently reordered **115 live customer pages on first save, with no edit made**. That is rejected outright. Placeholders for missing sections are inserted at their canonical position *relative to the blocks the product already has*; **no stored block is ever moved by rendering, by typing, or by saving.** Reordering stays a thing the operator does, now also available as one deliberate action that says what would move before it moves it. **THE CANONICAL ORDER IS THE HOUSE'S, NOT AN INVENTION** — `spec_strip > hero_intro > big_stat > why > ingredients_chips > allergen_card > storage_box > notes_callout > how_to_use`, which is what 74 products already carry and which puts the spec strip above the opening paragraph, where no whiteboard would have put it. **THE FREQUENCY IS READ LIVE, NEVER FROZEN INTO A CONSTANT** — a percentage baked into the source is a percentage that is wrong by next quarter and that nobody re-measures; a new endpoint counts the tenant's own products. **THE RISK THIS CHANGE CARRIES, NAMED:** `paBlocksSyncFromDOM` read one form at a time and wrote every `[data-bkey]` in the mount onto one block; with nine forms on screen it must scope per section, and a scoping bug writes one section's words into another's. §142 is the same family of mistake eleven days younger, so the invariant is held by a test rather than by care. **OPTIONS B AND C ARE RECORDED, not discarded:** B kept the block list and moved the settings beside it — fixes the distance, leaves the assembly work; C made the customer's page itself the editor — defeated by the bilingual pair, since only one language is ever on the page and chips, allergens and tables have nowhere to sit. Both were built as working prototypes before the choice was made. **NOT DONE, so it is not assumed:** no field deleted (the 30 never-filled colour fields stay, per v4.280); no schema, no migration; no change to the mini app, the QR menu or the web storefront; no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-15 · v4.280 — **§143 · THE FILE NAME IS THE WHOLE OF THE PERMISSION, SO A TEST HOLDS IT — found while running the block-field usage report against production.** `.github/workflows/ro-query.yml` will run ANY `scripts/diagnose_*.js` against the LIVE database and its only gate is that file-name shape; the workflow's header promises such a file opens SQLite `readonly: true` and PROVES it by attempting a write. **That promise lived in a comment and in each author's care, which is not a mechanism — and it had been broken twice.** `diagnose_hide_qr_flags.js` (written by this session earlier the same day) opened the database through `require('../database.js')`, the APPLICATION'S READ-WRITE handle; it failed on the box as MODULE_NOT_FOUND because the workflow stubs `database.js`, **so the mistake surfaced as a path error rather than as what it was.** `diagnose_variant_descriptions.js` opened `data/roots.db` with no options at all. Both fixed. **ENFORCED:** `readonly: true` on every open of the LIVE database. **COUNTED, NOT ENFORCED:** the run-time probe, which 13 of 58 live-opening scripts predate — failing those would make the gate red on a main that is not unsafe, and a suite red for a reason nobody intends to fix is one people learn to ignore. **THE CHECKER CRIED WOLF TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, and all three ways are recorded:** it failed seven file/HTTP diagnostics that open no database; it failed three seam audits that open a writable SCRATCH database on purpose (so the question is not “is it readonly” but “is this the LIVE database”); and then it failed five CORRECT scripts because `/new Database\([^)]*\)/` cannot see past the `)` closing `path.join(...)` and never saw the options object. The scan now balances parentheses — **a checker that cries wolf is one whose next real finding gets waved through.** **THE USAGE REPORT THAT STARTED IT**, `diagnose_block_field_usage.js`, also lands: its first production run found **30 of 78 fields in the product page editor never filled in by anybody across 260 products** (`accent_color`/`bg_color`/`fg_color` on all ten types offering them). Deleting them was proposed and **Ash declined**, on the reading that nobody using a control buried in a closed fold is not the same as nobody wanting it — recorded so it is not re-derived or re-opened. **TESTS:** `test_diagnostics_are_read_only.js`, four checks in the fast shard, reading the workflow itself so it fails loudly if the gate is renamed. Proved by mutation. No change to `ro-query.yml` or `oneoff.yml`, no probe added to the 13, no field deleted, no schema, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.
2026-09-15 · v4.279 — **§142 · AN INVERTED CONTROL CANNOT RIDE A SYNC THAT MEANS “THE FIELD EQUALS THE INPUT” — REPORTED BY ASH against §135, shipped the same day:** *“i cant really click hide/unhide the same block, i have to click on one block to hide and another block to unhide.”* **IT WAS WORSE THAN THE SYMPTOM AND IT REACHED THE DATABASE.** No click was needed: `paBlocksSyncFromDOM()` copies `b[dataset.bkey] = el.checked` verbatim, and the QR switch is INVERTED — ticked means SHOWN — so wiring it in with `data-bkey` wrote `hide_qr = true` for a VISIBLE block. 2026-09-15 · v4.277 — **§140 · A PACK CAN HOLD A COUNT, NOT ONLY A WEIGHT — DECIDED BY ASH,** shown why J-57 Label Paper costs ¥9.27 a sticker and what the three ways out were: *“ok fix it properly”* — the third, the one that changes the model rather than working around it. **THE SHAPE THAT COULD NOT BE SAID.** `lib/ingredient-cost.js` keys on the RECIPE unit: g/ml divides, pcs/bag/bottle/box does not, because a recipe calling for one bag consumes one bag whatever is inside it (2026-08-17, 29 live rows). A count of zero, or contents in grams, behaves exactly as before. **A ZERO PACK SIZE IS REFUSED, not waved through on a divisor of 1** — the same requirement the weight path makes, because a divisor of 1 invented here would store the roll price, which is the bug. **THE EDITOR NOW PRINTS THE DIVISION** (`¥9.27 ÷ 1000`), numerals only and no label, because `buy_pack_size` carried a different meaning before the `pack_size_semantics_v2` migration and that migration could only normalise rows whose buy unit was a MEASURE — a pcs-bought row can still sit on a stale 1000 nobody has been asked about, and printed it reads as an absurd divisor instead of a quietly wrong cost. **AND THE FIGURE IS SHOWN TO THE PLACES IT NEEDS:** `acMoney()` renders two, so ¥0.00927 read as ¥0.01 — eight percent out — and ¥0.0316 a gram read as ¥0.03. `unitMoney()` in `18-materials.js` gives four places below a jiao and five below a fen, on the record line and the list column; nothing at or above ¥0.10 changes shape, and it is local to this screen rather than a change to `acMoney()`. **NO MIGRATION AND NONE WANTED** — an affected row is fixed by filling in its contents, and the save re-derives and fires the recipe recompute. **THE PO WRITE-BACK NEEDED NO CHANGE AND IS WHERE THE LOOP WAS:** it already runs the one derivation, so the ¥9.27-per-label rows it wrote on every order (two of them in J-57's live cost history) stop; `buy_price` stays the ROLL price, because it is what the supplier charges and what the ±5% alert compares against. **NO CHINESE COMPOSED** — `pcs` is a unit token beside `g` and `kg`, the arithmetic line is numerals, and `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched. **TESTS:** new `scripts/test_material_piece_pack.js`, 18 cases in three parts — the rule, the editor wiring, and a guard band over the four shapes §140 promised not to touch — proven non-vacuous (six fail when the divisor is removed); `scripts/test_price_writeback.js` gains case 10, the same material through a real PO against a real database, 9 → 10 cases. `test:fast` 251 → **252/252**; lint 0 errors; the bilingual-banner gate passes. No schema, no migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

Three wraps are made for nobody and go in the bin. **A NEGATIVE HAS TWO CAUSES WITH OPPOSITE REMEDIES:** a DEBT (three sold that were never held → make or re-order them) and a MISCOUNT (three were on the shelf and the record was short → count the shelf). §84 established the first and is untouched; the owed block cannot tell them apart because it reads the balance and never asks how it got there. **WHAT IS DECIDED:** a counter sale that lands the shelf below zero corrects itself to zero, in the same transaction, with a second ledger row (`counter_miscount`) recording the lift — two rows, not one netted figure, because the sale really happened and the correction really happened. The reasoning is arithmetic rather than policy: if three wraps physically left in a customer's hand, the shelf held three, so §84's “sold and never held” is disproved by the sale having happened. The negative was the error; the correction is the truth. **THE CONFLICT WITH §39 RULINGS 1 AND 7 IS STATED, NOT GLOSSED:** those removed floors for the CHANNEL INGESTS, where a negative is the only record that Meituan or Eleme sold what we did not have — real units owed to a waiting customer. The ingests, the delta path and every non-counter commit still write the honest negative, and the tests hold it; the claim here is about this one door only. **AND THE MISCOUNT IS NOT SILENCED,** which is the other half: correcting the shelf removes the kitchen's signal, and the kitchen's signal was the wrong one. The merchant alert already says `可能是数错了` / *so it was likely counted wrong* on this path, naming the product and how far the record was short; it previously skipped batch-made products because the owed block carried them, and on the counter path it no longer does, so the exclusion is lifted THERE and only there. Supplier-direct stays excluded on both paths — no inventory of ours, so no count to be wrong. **NOT DONE, so it is not assumed:** no gate on the till (a walk-in holding the item is still never refused, which is what makes this necessary rather than avoidable); no change to the delivery path (a web or mini-app order that outruns the shelf still leaves the negative and still reports `有客户订单等待`, because those units genuinely are owed); no retrospective repair of negatives already on the shelf; no schema change and no migration (`counter_miscount` is a value in the existing `reason` column); no change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds work. **NO CHINESE COMPOSED** — no new string; `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` untouched.



2026-09-15 · v4.273 — **§136 · A SHORTAGE FOUND AFTER THE MONEY LANDED HAS SOMEWHERE TO GO — DECIDED BY ASH, having been told §134 could not rescue the orders it had already happened to:** *"build all and automatically deploy to live."* **'awaiting_restock' COULD ONLY EVER BE REACHED BY THE CHECKOUT** — the customer answered the shortage modal, or §80/§128/§134's park caught a short pre-order line. `STATUS_TRANSITIONS` offered no step from 'paid', so a picker who reached the shelf and found nothing could only prepare an order that cannot be picked, or cancel and refund a customer who would rather wait. TC000735 is the live case: §134 stops it recurring and could do nothing for the order itself. **WHAT IS DECIDED:** `paid → awaiting_restock`, the only backwards step in that table, driven by a **Hold for restock · 等待补货** button in the order drawer. Safe backwards because the two states differ in what the OFFICE is told, not in what the customer paid or what the shelf holds: no money moves, no stock moves, and 'awaiting_restock' already steps forward to exactly what 'paid' does ('preparing', 'cancelled'), so nothing downstream gains a path it lacked. `col` is null — no `awaiting_restock_at` column, no schema, no migration; the activity log records who moved it. **THE PIDS ARE COMPUTED, NEVER TAKEN FROM THE OPERATOR.** They are reporting a shelf; which SKUs that means is a fact about the shelf. Asking would invite a park on a product that is not short (never released) or one the order does not need (released by an irrelevant restock). **AND THE GUARD IS THE POINT, because a careless park is STRICTLY WORSE than the bug it fixes** — an order stranded in a queue whose whole promise is that orders leave it by themselves. A checkout RESERVATION is deliberately not enough to count as taken — a courier order reserves its 'strict' lines and parks anyway, holding stock it has not taken, and those must still be deducted on release. For every checkout-parked order that set is empty and nothing changes. **`orderStockNeed` AND `orderCommittedPids` ARE EXPORTED SO THE PARK AND THE RELEASE READ ONE VIEW** — a precondition that disagreed with the release is exactly how an order gets stranded. **NOT IN THE BULK BAR, deliberately:** that bar is forward steps on the fulfilment track, and each park needs its own shortage check and can be refused for its own reason. **NO CHINESE COMPOSED** — 等待补货 is lifted verbatim from this same file's awaiting-restock card (`cuT('Waiting on stock', '等待补货')`), so the button and the card it produces say the same word; `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.89 records the lift and the three rejected candidates. **THE DELIVERY WINDOW IS NOT TOUCHED** — §128's park clears it because there is no date behind a pre-order, but an operator parking a settled order may be parking it for an afternoon, and silently rewriting a date the customer was promised is a different decision. New suite `scripts/test_manual_restock_park.js` **14/14**, the double-deduct case proven non-vacuous by disabling the skip; `test:fast` 245 → **246**; lint 0 errors. No schema, no migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI. **Numbered §136 rather than §135: a parallel branch claimed §135 and v4.272 while this one was in flight, and section numbers are permanent — this appends rather than renumbering theirs.**

2026-09-15 · v4.271 — **§134 · A PAID EXTRA IS STOCK, NOT A REASON TO STOP COUNTING — DECIDED BY ASH on being shown why order TC000735 sat in Paid with a sold-out pre-order line on it:** *"fix it."* **THE PARK HAD AN ARM NOBODY WOULD HAVE CHOSEN.** §80/§128's pre-order park ran inside a guard that included `!hasStockedAddon` — a cart holding a paid extra with its own inventory refused to park AT ALL. A short add-on that is pre-orderable parks the order; a short add-on that is 'strict' refuses it, exactly as a strict LINE does. **AND THE OTHER END MOVED WITH IT, or the fix would have been half of one:** `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` in `lib/inventory.js` decided release from `retail_order_items` alone, so an order parked ON an add-on would have cleared while the very item it waited for was still missing, and handed back stock it never deducted. 2026-09-15 · v4.266 — **§131 · A FEEDBACK THREAD CAN BE FINISHED WITHOUT ANSWERING IT — DECIDED BY ASH from the front door**, on a "Feedback to answer · 1 · oldest 17h" row that had been up most of a day about a thread that needed no answer: *"need to have the option to not answering a feedback and this message should be gone."* **THE ROW WAS NOT WRONG, IT WAS UNREACHABLE.** Nothing in the existing design ever demanded a reply — opening a thread stamps `admin_read_at` and the clause drops it. **The gap was WHERE that clause could be reached from: the Inbox list prints the customer's message inline, photos and all, so the reading that settles the question happens in the LIST and the stamp only fires in the DRAWER.** An operator who reads a row, decides it needs nothing and moves on has done the work and left no trace of it, and the front door goes on naming the job. 2026-09-14 · v4.262 — **§56 AMENDED AND BUILT: THE TWO COST ROWS CARRY A FIGURE, ON THE CONDITION THAT THE FIGURE NEVER APPEARS WITHOUT THE SHARE OF THE PERIOD IT RESTS ON — DECIDED by Ash.** §56 (2026-09-07) held `cost_of_goods` and `gross_profit` null and gated them on §31: *"when §31 lands, these two rows fill from it and nothing else."* **§31's storage HAS since landed** — `product_build_lines` exists, `computeProductBuildCost()` reads it and `applyProductBuildCosts()` feeds `store_products.unit_cost` from it — so whether the gate was open became a question about the DATA, and nobody had looked. **IT WAS MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS DECIDED, which is the part worth copying.** `scripts/diagnose_cost_coverage.js` (new, read-only, run through `ro-query.yml` on 2026-09-14 against the live database) answered three questions: **29.1% of the last thirty days' line revenue carried a cost, 56.7% of September's, 2.7% of August's and 0% of July's**; 97 of 251 active products carry a `unit_cost` and 43 a §31 build list; and of the costed lines, 13.5% sit on a product flagged `cost_incomplete`. **The margin the screen WOULD have printed unqualified was 91.6% on a food business**, and the month-on-month shape was worse than the level: 97.9% in August against 86.4% in September, an 11-point "decline" that is nothing but coverage arriving. **TWO DESIGNS WERE PUT UP AND ASH CHOSE THE FIRST:** (A) whole revenue minus partial cost, with the shortfall stated beside the figure; (B) cost and margin on the costed SUBSET only, as a separate card. **Ash: *"version a"*.** B was the truer ratio and is recorded as rejected on a structural ground rather than a numerical one — **operating expenses are the whole business's, so a subset gross profit cannot be continued into Net**, and the card stops being five steps that follow from one another; §36's *Finance Summary ships without a location filter* refuses a store filter on exactly that shape, the top line scoped and the bottom line not. **THE CONDITION IS THE AMENDMENT.** `cost_coverage` is not a statistic beside the figure — the rows were blank precisely because a partial cost printed alone reads as a whole one, so a payload or a screen that drops it has undone the decision rather than tidied a response. **THREE STATES, AND THE FIRST IS §56 UNCHANGED.** No costed line at all → both rows keep the §1.12 seventh state they have had since §56, because **a `¥0.00` there would publish a 100% margin for July's ¥56,792 of real sales**; some coverage → the figures with the shortfall beneath them; full coverage → the figures and nothing beneath them. **The third state is Ash's own *"once we fix manually everything you will remove that note"*, built as a consequence of the data rather than a task anybody has to remember** — the note cannot outlive the shortfall it describes, which is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` opens by warning about. **TWO OF §36's SIX TRAPS ARE CARRIED IN THE LINE FORMULA AND THREE CANNOT BE.** Pack units (`unit_cost_at_sale` is per unit, `line_total` per line — the cost half takes the multiplier and the revenue half must not) and itemised partial refunds (`qty − refunded_qty`; §36 records that nothing else in the codebase subtracts it, and this is the first reader that does). **Not closed, and recorded rather than glossed:** an amount-only refund writes nothing to the line at all (7 orders, ¥328, in the measured window), options carry a price delta with no cost counterpart, and a bundle line goes null when ONE component is unpriced — so `cost_coverage` counts what carries a cost, never what carries a RIGHT one, and §36's two accuracy findings are untouched. **A THIRD REVENUE FINDING ARRIVED WITH THE MEASUREMENT AND IS RECORDED AS A KNOWN MISMATCH:** the Summary's revenue is `SUM(retail_orders.total)` while cost can only be summed from order LINES, and shipping, order-level discounts and tax sit on the header and never reach a line — **the gap runs from +¥18,033 (July) to −¥3,944 (September) and CHANGES SIGN**, so it is not an adjustment anyone can net out later. Gross profit is header revenue minus line cost, deliberately, for the same staircase reason B was rejected. **NET IS UNCHANGED and cost is still NOT subtracted from it** — a partial cost taken off net would put a known-incomplete number into the one figure on the card that nothing else qualifies. **The predicates are the shared ones**: `PAID_O` and `odateFor()` from `lib/finance-window.js`, never spelled out here, because revenue and cost must agree about which orders exist or the margin is a ratio of two different populations — §36's finding that the allow-list was re-declared inline four times is the reason, and a test asserts no fifth. **Tests:** `scripts/test_finance_summary.js` 85 → **97**, gaining a new section `2b` that **SLICES THE COST SQL OUT OF THE LIVE ROUTE AND RUNS IT** rather than transcribing it, against rows that spring each trap — a `pack_units` 6 line, an itemised partial refund, an uncosted line, a cancelled order and a §98 replacement. **Four breaks were confirmed red**: the coverage note removed, `floor` changed to `round`, the zero-coverage guard dropped, and the revenue half given the pack multiplier. **One of those four — the zero-coverage guard — passed green on the first attempt and exposed a real hole**, which is why section `2b` exists at all; the screen-level test had been handed a null rather than deriving it. **Chinese:** ONE composed pair, `此期间 {n}% 的营收已记录成本 —— 实际毛利更低。`, assembled wholly from live pieces — `此期间` and `已记录成本` from this card's own `noCostRecorded`, `营收` from its own revenue label, and `—— 实际毛利更低。` verbatim from `09-products.js:1647`, which says the same thing about a single product's margin drawn from an incomplete cost. Declared with three rejections in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.81. **NOT DONE, and named so it is not assumed:** no backfill (§36 refuses it and the reason stands), no cost derived from ingredient purchases in the window (§56 rejected it and that rejection is untouched), nothing for `sales_entries` market and till sales, and **product 3's ¥990 `unit_cost` is NOT repaired here** — Ash reports the material at ¥54.85/kg, so the stored figure is roughly 18kg of material in a per-unit field, which is §36's own no-conversion-step finding with a source price against it; it is a manual correction in the product editor and it distorts 17% of the measured cost of goods until it is made.
