It parks as `awaiting_restock` holding nothing, window cleared, same-day surcharge refunded, promoted by `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock()` when the count covers every line: **the column, the promotion and the Awaiting restock chip the customer's own `wait_for_restock` choice already uses**, so no new fulfilment concept and no new operator screen. **THE ASK ASH ANSWERED, because it changes the build and not just the copy:** in a mixed basket the whole order waits, in-stock items included, and a grocery restock has no date the way a batch does — Ash chose *whole order waits* over an all-pre-order-only rule and over a split shipment. The help text and the product-page note both say so; an operator who sets this is told what it costs before a customer tells them. **ROUTING HAD TO BE TOLD FIRST, and this is the half that would have shipped broken:** `routeOrder` under the stock gate hunts for a store holding the stock, finds none and returns `needs_fallback_confirmation` — the 5-option shortage modal — **before the park ever runs**, so widening the park alone would have offered a pre-order and then demanded a substitute. `preorderAllShort` is computed once, before routing, and relaxes it; pickup is deliberately never relaxed. **THE EXEMPTION IS OPT-IN (`preorderParkOk`), for exactly the reason `freshPreorderOk` is:** only a caller that can carry the consequence may claim it. The push is idempotent (a pending row is refreshed, never duplicated) and the person who sees a wrong number is at the shelf holding a phone; turning sync OFF is a lasting change afterwards visible only as a grey chip somebody goes looking for, which is the wrong shape for one hand on a small screen. **THE VERB IS OFFERED ON THE SAME ROWS AS THE DESKTOP'S** — neither `none` nor `off` — and the suite proves it by SLICING BOTH CONDITIONS OUT OF THE TWO LIVE FILES and running them against one table of eight states, so neither can be edited alone. **THE REFERRAL TO THE DESKTOP IS NARROWER ON THE PHONE, ON PURPOSE**: the desktop's *Open Meituan* costs one click on the machine already in front of you, while the phone's version is a sentence asking somebody to go and find a computer. It now appears only for `no_name` / `name_not_found` / `no_option` — the three that need the channel's own catalogue picker and the three part two deliberately did not build. **The read-only note is DELETED rather than reworded**: the card that needs a desktop already says so on the item it is about (§122's rule applied to an instruction), and a standing line at the foot telling every operator to go to a computer is the §1.7 shape. **THE BUTTON CARRIES A CLIENT-SIDE CAPABILITY GATE WHERE THE DESKTOP NEEDS NONE, AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC**: this file's `apiWrite` sends a **403 to `/backend/login` exactly as it sends a 401**, so an ungated Sync now answers a missing permission by throwing the operator out of the app. It is drawn through `mCan('{channel}:sync')`, whose null-caps case means allowed — the server is still the gate. The screen's own row gate is unchanged and stays any-of the three `:view` keys: somebody who may look but not push gets the whole alarm with no button on it. **Chinese: nothing composed.** Four pairs, all lifted — `Sync now · 立即同步` is the desktop button's (which took it from `11-meituan.js`), `Sending… · 发送中…` is this screen's own `csCellWord`, the `not_mapped` / `not_syncing` refusal is `01-core.js`'s pair character for character because it is the same fact, and the fallback is `orderErrorText`'s own default on this file. `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is not touched, and a test asserts that §124 wrote nothing into it. **THREE STALE COMMENTS CORRECTED**: `29-channel-sync.js`, `retail-admin.html`'s `#tab-channel-sync` block and the phone's `SUBS.channelsync` all still called the page read-only after part two gave it two verbs. The product editor's Channels card (§103 step 4) is **still** read-only and was left alone. **Tests:** new `scripts/test_mobile_channel_sync_repair.js` — **36 cases**, auto-discovered into the fast shard, five load-bearing rules confirmed red against deliberate breaks (the `off` state re-admitted to the push, the sentence widened back to every amber channel, the `mCan` gate dropped, the path's `/channel-sync` prefix removed, the footer note restored). `npm run test:fast` 233 passed, 0 failed; `npm run lint` 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. No route, no schema, no migration, no new capability, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.**

2026-09-13 · v4.257 — **§123 · §117 PART THREE BUILT: GZ GROCERY WEARS THE CHANNEL FRAME, AND THE FRAME IS ONE SET OF RULES RATHER THAN A THIRD COPY OF IT.** §117 left this page named as *"the odd one out"*: its own heading shape, two purpose paragraphs, a bespoke health strip, its own sub-nav, and ~30 lines of inline `<style>`. **THE SURVEY FOUND MORE THAN A STYLE MISMATCH.** `#tab-meituan` and `#tab-eleme` each remap the admin's BASE token family (`--line`, `--text-1`, `--bg-pane` — warm-grey, pre-Tacet) onto the Tacet palette at the top of their blocks; **`#tab-guanyi` never did**, and its inline rules were written against that base family, so this page has been painting its cards, borders and text off-palette next to two pages that were not. The remap is now here, the same list they carry. **THE FRAME IS SHARED BY SELECTOR, NOT COPIED.** 33 rules (pagehead, status, tiles, store lines, tab strip) now name `.gy-` alongside `.mt-`, so a change to one is a change to all — the same additive move §117 part two used on the switch, and for the same reason. Consolidating them is the real end of this drift, and it is a mechanical move of ~112 rules through a 15k-line stylesheet across two live pages **that cannot be visually verified here**: the browser suite lives in the slow shard, which is off by Ash's standing instruction. The session's own @media-nesting scanner got that file's structure wrong on its first pass, which is the evidence for not attempting it blind. **Additive joining carries none of that risk and delivers the same thing for GZ Grocery.** **THE NAME IS THE SHARED TABLE'S NAME**: the heading read *"gzgrocery 同步 · Guanyi Sync"* while the Channel sync page, the dashboard row and the phone all say **GZ Grocery** — three names for one channel, which is what §103 step 5 exists to prevent. `CH_NAME` is the one table and it says GZ Grocery on both sides, so the h2 does too and carries no language pair to drift. **THE TWO PURPOSE PARAGRAPHS ARE GONE** (§1.7 bans them); the one fact in them a reader could not get from the screen — that products match on the SKU inside the Guanyi name — moved verbatim onto the **Mapping** panel, where somebody is actually doing that. **Billing and Mapping stayed on this page**, per Ash: *"it's got nothing to do with syncing products"*. **THE MAPPED TILE IS NOT CALLED SYNCED**, and the test says so: `mappedCount` counts mappings with the switch on, while the Channel sync page's `ok` counts items the channel holds the right number for — one word over two different numbers on two screens is the §103 step 5 defect exactly. **Chinese: nothing composed.** `Mapped · 已映射` and the three freshness phrases are this page's own from the strip that stood here; `Needs attention · 待处理` is `chStateWord('att')`, the one table; `Stock updates waiting · 待推送库存` is the Meituan and Eleme tile whose number means the same thing; `nothing needs you · 无需处理` and the `N 个待处理` / `N 发送中…` shapes are the Channel sync strip's, number in the same slot. A wrong fallback wording (`Need attention`, missing the s that `CH_STATE_WORD` carries) was caught by the suite before it shipped. **Tests:** new `scripts/test_channel_frame.js` — **13 cases**, auto-discovered into the fast shard, all five load-bearing rules confirmed red against a deliberate break; three of its own cases were wrong on first run (a slicer that swept in a neighbouring global `<style>`, two checks matching the explanatory comment rather than the markup) and were fixed rather than loosened. `npm run test:fast` 230 passed, 0 failed; eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. No route, no schema, no migration, no new capability, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.**

2026-09-13 · v4.256 — **A SWITCH BELONGS ON THE ROW WHOSE VALUE IT CHANGES — §122, REPORTED BY ASH against §116's own record, with the block circled: *"this part need to redesign. not clear."*** Five centred sentences at the foot of the customer record, with no container, no icons, nothing saying they could be pressed, labels that were clauses rather than verbs, and Brick TEXT where §5 gives destructive a Brick OUTLINE — so Block, which locks a person out, read at the same weight as Reissue, which is undone in one tap. **The fault that was not styling:** the block was the desktop's More menu lifted whole, and four of its five controls act on facts already on screen a few rows up. **Three mockups were put up and Ash chose Option B** (`design-handoff/customer-actions/`): each control now sits on the row whose value it changes — Their code · Reissue, Referring · Stop, Ongoing share · Allow, Signed in on 2 devices · Sign out — through `custRowAct`, which renders `custRow`'s exact shape when no control is passed, and **that null is where the capability gate lands**: an operator who may not write is passed no control and the row goes on stating its fact. **Block keeps the foot alone**, as a Brick outline: it is the only thing there that takes something away from a person, and it has no fact-row to sit on. Unblock is NOT dressed as destructive — it gives something back. **The open question is settled by the choice:** §116 drew the Referring row only once referring had been STOPPED; a switch that materialises the first time you use it is worse than the drawer it replaced, so the row is always drawn now (Active / Stopped), gated on the affiliate FEATURE rather than the flag. The ongoing share keeps its narrower 'selected'-mode condition, which is about meaning rather than about carrying a control. **Tests:** 84 → **103 assertions across 37 cases**, asserting WHERE a control is — each switch resolves to the list carrying its own fact, labels are at most two words, the foot holds exactly one button, and every `.rowact` measures 44px or more. **Chinese:** one composed pair (`有效`), four trims and one lift, v1.75; every long label survives on the confirm its verb opens. No route, no schema, no migration, no capability change, no CI or .gitignore change.**

2026-09-13 · v4.255 — **§121 DECIDED AND BUILT: OPERATIONS IS EIGHT GROUPS, AND THREE PILLS SAY WHAT A LABEL CANNOT — DECIDED BY ASH in two words, *"do option a"*, completing the set.** `docs/tacet-operations-clarity-options.md` now has no open options: **B** shipped as §118, **two of A's four renames** as §119, and **A's grouping and pills** here; only the `Invoices` rename stays declined, for §119's reason. **THE GROUPING IS THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS WHY NO ROW GAINED A SUBTITLE**: every pair that read as one row now sits in a different group from its twin — Purchasing under *Stock coming in* and Ask to buy under *Ask someone else*, Add stock and Ask for stock likewise, Kitchen queue and Ask the kitchen likewise — so position says it and a sentence under all twenty-two would say it twice at four times the strings. **Row order inside a group is the order of the job**, not the old flat order. **TWO GROUPINGS THAT LOOK WRONG AND ARE NOT**: the two receiving rows are TOGETHER, because §119 gave them names that differ and side by side those names are the whole difference; and Expense and Approvals are together with the **PILL as their only separator**, because they are two ends of one feature and under a shared heading Approvals would otherwise read as a second Expense — the suite asserts both halves. **ONE ROW MOVED ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE**: *Ready from the kitchen* sat in *Making things* in the first draft, which reads naturally since all three sound like production, and was wrong — `ROUTE_CAP` gates it on `['restock:request','restock:pick']`, *"the people who RAISE these requests"*, so it is the requester's side and sits with the asks, **wearing no pill**: the three rows above it ask, and this one is the answer coming back. **THREE PILLS, AND NO PILL IS THE DEFAULT** — Ask · 申请 on the three request screens, Approve · 审批 on Approvals, Settings · 设置 on Delivery settings. A row you simply do wears nothing, which is the only thing keeping a pill scarce enough to read, and all three are NEUTRAL: a direction is a fact about the row, not a state needing attention (the tier-pill rule), so Sage, Amber, Brick and Dusk are unspent. Keyed in `ROW_PILL` rather than as a seventh positional element, the shape `QUICK_VERB` already uses. **A GROUP WITH ONE ROW IS ACCEPTED**: a picker sees *Send it out* over a single row and the heading still says what it is for; collapsing back below some row count would change the shape of the screen as permissions change. **RECORDED: AN OR-SHAPED GUARD THAT DID NOT GUARD.** The confusable-pair case first asserted separation *by the grouping OR by the pill* — and since every one of those pairs has a pill on one side, the OR was satisfied by the pill every time and the grouping half never bit: **moving Ask to buy back beside Purchasing passed.** Red-proofing found it; each pair is now named with the mechanism that actually carries it. §119 recorded a label-shaped guard that had stopped guarding, and **this is the same failure wearing an `||`.** **Tests:** new `scripts/test_mobile_ops_groups.js` — **12 checks, reads only, FAST shard and part of the gate**, four of them red-proofed (a pair regrouped, the receiving pair split, Approvals' pill dropped, the pill painted Sage); `test_mobile_ask_strip.js` re-pointed at the eight groups by the FIRST HEADING rather than a group count, so a ninth cannot silently narrow what it counts; `test_mobile_home.js` updated where it asserted the retired `Operations` heading. `npm run test:fast` **231 passed, 0 failed**; nav 100/38, home 153/46 green; eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. **Eleven strings, every one a LIFT and not one composed** — four headings are two live row labels joined by `与`, and the three pills are each a row label or its stem — declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.77 with the rejections, including `出货`, which is live in no UI pair and has a test case guarding that claim. No route, no schema, no migration, no new capability, no CSS file, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.**

2026-09-13 · v4.254 — **§120 DECIDED: THE QR MENU ASKS THE QUESTIONS THE COUNTER WOULD HAVE ASKED — DECIDED BY ASH, who answered both open questions and then said *"do all as you see fit"*.** Asked whether the QR menu has variant options, the answer was flatly no: it sells a flat row, tap Add and get one unit, and it reads NEITHER of the two choice mechanisms this system already has. **THE SURVEY IS THE VALUABLE HALF and it shrank the job from days to about one:** `options_json` on `retail_order_items` already exists and the web/mini-app checkout already fills it; `lib/feie.js` already prints every chosen option with its question in both languages on both templates; and the till NEVER re-prices a QR order — `recall()` loads it read-only and the settle path only marks it paid — so base-plus-extras needs nothing from the till but a line that shows what was chosen. **TWO RULES DECIDED BY ASH: a sold-out paid extra greys out and the drink still sells (1A), and a required question BLOCKS and names itself (2B).** **NO CHINESE COMPOSED** — `请选择 ` + the question is the storefront's own required-option toast and the mini app's, character for character, and the vocabulary document is not touched. **AND THE PRECEDENT THIS WAS ABOUT TO COPY TURNED OUT TO BE DEAD CODE:** `addon_available` was read by both mini-app surfaces and written nowhere in the repository, so the sold-out-extra guard had never once fired and a shopper could be billed for an extra the counter had run out of. Fixed separately, one PR per change, before this build starts. **NUMBERED §120, NOT §117.** This was drafted and its PR opened as §117 while that number was free; three sections (§117, §118, §119) landed on main from other sessions in the hours it sat open. **its grouping and its three pills remain undecided**, and `Invoices` is deliberately left alone because batch three already folds that row into Orders. **THE DEFECT WAS GREPPED BEFORE IT WAS CALLED CLOSED, and it went four levels deeper than the row it was reported on**: `Receiving` and `Receive delivery` shared `收货` in both row labels, in **both screen titles**, in **three buttons inside the transfer screen** (two back rows and one step-back control, all rendering `T('Receiving','收货')` — the screen calling itself by the other row's name), and in `SUBS.receive`'s `backLabel`. **Eleven sites, one change.** `收货` STAYS WITH THE SUPPLIER FLOW — it is correct there and 48 other uses put it there, so the supplier row changes **in English alone** (`Receive from a supplier`) and only the transfer flow takes a new Chinese label, `调拨收货`, **copied from that screen's own error copy** rather than composed. `Delivery` → `Delivery settings · 配送设置` closes the second, unrelated defect in the same list: zones, holiday mode and a printer, the only configuration screen among twenty-one tasks, which the design canvas had already drawn as an A4 Console. **THE TWO BACK CONTROLS ARE NOT THE SAME CONTROL**: the two back ROWS go to the screen's own list and take its name, while the third goes back one STEP, so it says `Back to the count · 返回清点` — the one composed string, and composed precisely because the screen's name on it would have put one label on two destinations. **§118 NEEDED NO EDIT**: its rule 1 (a question reads its destination's label off the More row) meant the strip picked both new names up for free — and the Chinese render of that strip showing `收货` twice is what turned this rename from an argument into an observation. **A GUARD THAT HAD STOPPED GUARDING**: `test_mobile_nav.js` proved a view-only buyer is not offered the receiving row by asserting the word `Receiving` was absent — which a renamed row satisfies whether or not the row is shown. 2026-09-13 · v4.251 — **§117 PART TWO BUILT: THE CHANNEL SYNC PAGE REPAIRS AS WELL AS REPORTS — AND IT IS NARROWER THAN PART ONE PROMISED, ON PURPOSE.** Part one recorded part two as *"fold the Meituan and Eleme sync views into the one frame, and carry the repair panel into depth 3"*. **THE FOLD WAS NOT BUILT AND THE SURVEY SAID WHY.** The channel views are a one-line-per-product list plus a side panel; this page ALREADY has a one-line list — its table — and the channel picker already narrows it, so folding `mt-list`/`el-list` in would add a second list to the page that replaced them. And the panel could not be shared: all three channels write through `/products/:id/map` and **the three payloads agree on exactly one field, `sync_enabled`** — Meituan sends `meituanName` through `lib/meituan-map-write`, Eleme `elemeName` plus a spec pair, an `extendCode` and a `remove` flag, GZ Grocery a `skuId` and no store field at all. A panel driving all three would carry that difference on the one page §117 exists to take it off. **SO THE LINE WAS DRAWN AT THE TWO VERBS THE CHANNELS ALREADY SHARE UNDERNEATH**: every map table has `sync_enabled`, every queue table takes the same five columns. New `lib/channel-sync-write.js` is those two verbs for all three channels; `routes/channel-sync.js`, until now a read, carries them. **Between them they clear four of the seven reasons an item can need attention** — `sync_off` by the switch, `push_failed`/`wrong_number`/`never_synced` by the push — and every amber row keeps its button to the channel's own tab for the three that need that channel's catalogue picker (`no_name`, `name_not_found`, `no_option`). **THE PUSH IS ALSO THE RETRY FOR A DEFECT ALREADY ON FILE**: the daemon picks up only `pending`, so an item whose last push errored sits there forever (`docs/meituan-findings.md` #6; a session on 2026-09-12 found Black Beans stuck amber for exactly this), and a fresh pending row is both the retry and the fix because the verdict reads the latest queue row. **A PENDING ROW IS REFRESHED, NEVER DUPLICATED** — push-all's own comment carries the scar, *"877 pending for 208 products"*, and this button is worse placed for it. **THE TRAP THE SURVEY CAUGHT: GZ Grocery's pre-order key is `gzgrocery`, not `guanyi`** — every other surface calls it `guanyi`, `lib/channel-publish` knows it only as `gzgrocery`, and getting it wrong drops §85's allowance from every GZ Grocery push invisibly until a pre-order window closes itself; the test pins the key to the string `routes/guanyi-admin.js` itself passes, so the two cannot drift. **THE SWITCH IS THE CHANNEL PANELS' SWITCH**, joined to the `.mt-panel`/`.el-panel` `toggle-label` selector group rather than given matching values of its own — and a careless first attempt at that widening dropped ` input` from the Eleme half, which the suite now asserts per suffix. **Both writes are gated** (`push` → `{channel}:sync`, the switch → `{channel}:map`); `lib/cap-routes.js` **fails open for a mutation it does not know**, so all six paths are asserted. **Chinese: nothing composed** — `Sync now · 立即同步` and `Sync on / off · 同步开关` are the Meituan and Eleme panels' own, and the two refusals carry `row_moved`'s pair verbatim because they are the same fact. **Tests:** new `scripts/test_channel_sync_write.js` — **26 cases**, auto-discovered into the fast shard, every key rule confirmed red against a deliberate break (and one case rewritten when the break showed it was not exercising the 套餐 guard it claimed to). `npm run test:fast` 225 passed, 0 failed; eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. Two new routes, no schema, no migration, no new capability, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.**

2026-09-13 · v4.248 — **§114 DECIDED AND BUILT: A PURCHASE THAT HAS NOT ARRIVED IS TRACKED AS AN ORDER, WHOEVER PAID FOR IT — DECIDED BY ASH, AND IT REVERSES §111 PART THREE.** The case that broke it, in his words: *"an employee use the company money to buy a food processor. it wasn't the person that do purchasing... the item didn't arrive and it need tracking"*. §111 part three had left claims alone because *a claim is money already out of a pocket — there is nothing to order and nothing to receive*; **true of a cook buying ginger, false of an appliance still in transit**, where the money is gone AND the goods are owed. Neither door held it: the claim path has no delivery to track, and the order path sits behind `purchasing:edit`, which the floor presets withhold on purpose. **Ash ruled twice**: the APPROVER raises the order from the claim (so nobody gains a capability), and it applies to the employee's OWN money too (the order tracks the delivery and owns the cost; the debt stays on the claim). **THREE FINDINGS MADE IT CHEAP**: `store_manager` already holds `purchasing:receive`, so the missing half was never the tracking but the CREATION; *paid, not yet arrived* is a state the record already has (`postRetailPOExpenses` posts on Ordered, `Delivered` seeds `qty_received`), so the order is raised at Ordered and never as a draft — a draft posts nothing and the money has already gone; and §111 part one's TYPED LINE is what carries a food processor, which is in no catalogue, so this could not have been built a day earlier. **THE MONEY IS POSTED ONCE**: `postClaim` writes nothing for a claim awaiting its delivery — keyed on `awaiting_delivery` and NOT on `po_id`, because on a first approval the order does not exist yet when it runs, and a `po_id` test would leave the same purchase in the books twice. **REJECT AND VOID ARE REFUSED while an order stands** (§114 part four): the claim has no ledger row of its own to take back, and cancelling the order behind the scenes would reach into a document that may already have been received — the refusal names Cancel order instead. **THE OWED FIGURE COSTS NOTHING**, verified rather than assumed: it reads status + paid_by + settled and never `expense_id`, so an employee who laid out their own money is still owed it and **Mark paid** still settles it. A claim marked *not arrived* must name a shop and a description — goods turn up at a door, and §111 part one refuses a line with no name. **Tests:** new `scripts/test_claim_purchase_order.js` (**47 cases**, both routers real, inventory stubbed but RECORDING), and `test_staff_expenses.js` 75 → **82 cases**, whose file-wide *one table, and it is the claim table* guard is NARROWED rather than dropped — the allowed set is named, the two new tables are pinned to `raiseOrderForClaim`, and a new case proves the SUBMIT path still writes the claim and nothing else, which is the assertion that actually carries §87 part one and which the old regex only implied. `npm run test:fast` 223 passed, 0 failed; eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. **Three composed strings and one taken whole**, all declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.72 with a test case that re-reads each source and fails if a term stops being live. Two migrations (`staff_expenses.awaiting_delivery`, `po_id`), no new route, no new capability, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.**

2026-09-13 · v4.245 — **§111 PART TWO BUILT: THE EXPENSE FORM ASKS ONCE PER CATEGORY, AND WHAT WAS ORDERED GOES TO PURCHASING INSTEAD OF THE LEDGER — DECIDED BY ASH (v4.244), built on request the same day.** On money out the Transactions form now asks *was this ordered from a supplier?* and writes the answer onto the CATEGORY, so rent is asked about once, ever, and ingredients once, ever. **THE COLUMN CARRIES NO DEFAULT AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM**: `categories.needs_po` is nullable — NULL is *nobody has been asked*, 1 *ordered*, 0 *not ordered* — and the ledger payload sends `category_needs_po` as a map of the ANSWERED ones only, because absence is the third state and a 0 for the unasked would be the same wrong default wearing a different hat. §36's "an empty list cannot offer a wrong option", one field further in. **DISMISSING THE QUESTION DOES NOTHING AT ALL** — no row, no wizard, nothing remembered, the form still open with every value in it — which is why it is `askChoice` and not a two-button confirm: on a confirm, Escape lands on whichever answer sits in the cancel slot, so pressing it would either write a row nobody committed to or throw the operator into another tab. **NOTHING IS WRITTEN ON THE WAY TO PURCHASING, NOT EVEN A DRAFT**: Finance's form has no supplier or store field (§36 — the ledger has no location column) and the create route requires a store, so the wizard opens on STEP ONE with the part Finance already knew filled in, as part one's typed line. Settings gains the way back — a second checkbox beside *Operating expense*, INDETERMINATE where nobody has been asked, because a plain unticked box would say "not ordered" about every category that has simply never come up. Not asked on an edit, and not on money in. **Tests:** two new suites, `test_finance_po_question.js` (**31 cases**, both finance routers real against a fixture) and `test_finance_po_question_client.js` (**41 cases**, the VM sandbox over `22-finance.js`, dismissal given its own case). 2026-09-12 · v4.235 — **§107: THE STALL CARD NAMES BOTH ITS COUNTS, SO THE ONE SCREEN THAT SHOWS THEM TOGETHER STOPS LOOKING WRONG.** Asked by Ash, reading the phone's Channel sync screen: *"why it say 3 stock update when can see only 2"* — the Meituan card said *3 stock updates waiting since Sep 7* directly above a Needs attention list holding 2 items. **THIS IS §104'S OWN DIVERGENCE, NOT A NEW ONE.** §104 already ruled the two figures must never be summed: `channelSyncStale().waiting_count` counts (store, product) push TARGETS still pending or errored; `channel_items_attention.count` (`ch.counts.att` here) counts PRODUCTS, worst-store-wins, so one product wrong at two stores is two targets and one card. §104 settled where each number lives; it did not say the stall line naming only the target count would read as a bug on the one page — the Channel sync page's own strip — that also shows the item count a breath away. **THE FIX NAMES BOTH, IT DOES NOT RECONCILE THEM.** Desktop's `29-channel-sync.js` `strip()` and the phone's `m.html` (new `csStaleLine`, mirroring `csBlockLine`'s shape) append the channel's own `counts.att` to the stall sentence they already had, only when it is nonzero — a channel stalled on pushes still in flight, with nothing yet provably wrong, says only the original sentence, per §104's own "no single item is yet provably wrong" case. **THE SERVER IS UNCHANGED**, same as §104: `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` and `lib/channel-sync-items.js` are untouched, both counts already travelled to both surfaces, and this is display only. **Chinese: one pair lifted whole, one arrangement composed.** Desktop's `N 个待处理` is its own live fragment three lines below in the same file, reused verbatim. 2026-09-12 · v4.234 — **§106: THE CHANNEL SAYS WHAT IS STOPPING IT, AND THE ITEMS STOP GUESSING.** Asked by Ash, reading §105's own output: **"meituan refused it and couldn't reach it — can't the system also provide the reason?"** Three things proposed, all three approved with **"ok do they"**. **THE REASON WAS ONE FUNCTION AWAY AND NOBODY HAD ASKED.** §105 gave every item its own failure sentence and then shipped *"Cannot reach the sync service"* onto forty rows at once, while `meituanStoreHealth` in `routes/meituan-admin.js` — next door, driving the Meituan tab's store lines for months — already knew it was a **captcha on 天河 since 09:14**. Same shape as §105 itself and as §103 step 5: one rule, two copies, two screens drifting. **THE RULE MOVES TO `lib/channel-block.js` AND BOTH CALLERS ASK IT.** A store is blocked when its most recent blocking event with `status='error'` has not been overtaken by a successful `stock_push` or an explicit clearing event — two ways to recover because the daemons use both. **`status='error'` is the whole test**: `poll_paused` is logged `ok` and means "outside opening hours", and reading the event type alone turned 天河 amber the moment it shut for the night; that warning is carried over verbatim. Copying the algorithm into `lib/channel-sync-items.js` was rejected for §103 step 5's reason; the route now delegates and keeps its exact fields, and the suite runs **the tab's ORIGINAL algorithm beside the shared one over nine fixtures** and demands they agree. **ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, AND IT CHANGES WHAT AN EXISTING SCREEN SAYS: the shared list also blocks on `proxy_down`**, which the tab's private list omitted even though the daemon logs it as an error reading *proxy cannot reach Meituan — sync paused*. A store in that state pushes nothing and the tab called it fine. **EACH DAEMON HAS ITS OWN NAMES, AND THE FIRST DRAFT GOT THAT WRONG.** The descriptor was first written by giving Eleme and GZ Grocery Meituan's event names — it would have reported nothing at all for Eleme, for ever, in silence, because **Eleme calls a lost session `auth_required`**. The names are now read out of each daemon's own `logSync` calls, and **a test reads the daemons' source and fails if a name in the table is one nothing writes**, because a wrong string in a descriptor produces silence rather than an error. GZ Grocery announces recovery with the fault's OWN event type at status `ok`, so `needs_login` sits in both its lists; that is safe because clearing must be strictly later than the fault, and all three directions are pinned. **Only faults that stop the STOCK PUSH are listed** — Meituan's `sync_stalled` is about order reads and `browser_down` about a process that restarts itself. **WORST = EARLIEST**, not most recent: the fault that has been stopping pushes longest is the one nobody has looked at. It rides on the channel entry and is said **once on the channel's card**, never down forty item rows (§103's founding rule). **AN ITEM DEFERS TO IT IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY**: `chCauseFor` (desktop) and `csCauseFor` (phone) swap an item's cause for the channel's only where the item's own code is generic — `unreachable`, `http`, `signed_out`, `gave_up`, or none. **A stated refusal always keeps its own words**: *美团返回：商品已下架 (code 8003)* is a fact about that item no channel fault explains, and deferring would lose the only actionable sentence on the row. **THE MEITUAN CODES: THE EVIDENCE SAID THERE WAS NOTHING TO MAP.** All three codes the tree has met are handled BEFORE an operator can reach them — 10002 and 30000 are a lost store binding (`_isBindingError` → transient, flushes after re-login), 10048 is a 套餐 combo whose component is out of stock (`_apiSetSku` treats Meituan's refusal as the correct end state). **A what-to-do line for any of them would be a sentence no operator can reach — dead code that reads like coverage.** What ships is the evidence path: `MEITUAN_CODES` records what is known AND where it is handled, `meituanCodeOf` pulls the code back out of a rejection sentence, and **`scripts/report_reject_codes.js` counts every code the logs actually carry and names the ones missing from the table**. It writes nothing and needs no schema — the codes are already in `meituan_sync_log.error_msg` and the queue row — reads every tenant database on the box retroactively, and **refuses (exit 2) when nothing could be read** rather than printing "no unknown codes", per §30 rule 4. **Chinese: nothing new is minted.** `验证中心风控，同步已暂停，需要人工验证` is the Meituan daemon's own merchant alert verbatim; `同步已停` is the Eleme tab's own fallback; the sign-in and cannot-connect sentences come from §105's declared set; `自` is the Orders page's own "since". **One arrangement is composed** — `无法连接同步服务。同步已暂停。` — declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` with the candidates rejected. **Tests:** `scripts/test_channel_block.js`, new, fast shard, **40 cases**, plus four in `test_channel_sync_items.js` (**61 total**). No schema, no migration, no new capability, no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-12 · v4.233 — **§105: A FAILED PUSH SAYS WHY, BECAUSE IT ALWAYS KNEW — THE REASON WAS BEING DISCARDED ON THE WAY OUT.** Asked by Ash from a live phone screenshot showing *Push failed: transient push failure — retries exhausted*: **"the system can tell the exact reason it won't sync so the tenant can fix it faster?"** The answer was yes, and worse than yes. **THE CAUSE WAS COMPUTED AT EVERY FAILURE AND THROWN AWAY BY THE WRAPPERS ABOVE IT.** `lib/eleme-browser.js`'s `_rpc` resolves an HTTP status, a fetch error or Eleme's own error object; `_apiUpdateFoodStock` **logged it and dropped it one statement later**. `lib/meituan-browser.js`'s `_apiSetSku` captures Meituan's own `{status, code, msg}`, **logged `res` in full to a daemon log nobody reads**, and returned `{ ok, apiRejected }`. Seven Eleme exits and six Meituan ones returned `{ ok, transient }` while holding the reason in scope. So `last_error` — the one field an operator reads — said *retries exhausted*, **which is not a reason but a count of how many times we gave up**, and `docs/channel-mapping-findings.md` F4 had measured exactly that string appearing **17–35 times a day, every day, for two weeks**. It was the dominant error, and it said nothing. **THE FIX IS RETURN VALUES, NOT BEHAVIOUR.** Every check, every order of checks and every `transient` flag in both browser modules is unchanged; thirteen returns gained a field. **The Eleme daemon's preference is corrected to match Meituan's**, which already read `reason || (transient ? …)` and only ever lacked a reason to use — Eleme's read `transient ? <generic> : (reason || …)`, so three failed attempts discarded whatever had been learned. A row still retrying now says why too. **`lib/channel-push-reason.js` CLASSIFIES, IT DOES NOT TRANSLATE**, and that split is the point: the raw text is English from the browser layer and some of it is the PLATFORM's own Chinese, so wording it server-side would mean shipping English to a Chinese operator or inventing Chinese for Meituan's own words. It returns a stable code plus the detail worth keeping; `01-core.js` holds the bilingual sentence beside the rest of the channel vocabulary (§103 step 5). **An uncategorised failure comes back `code: null` with the raw text intact** — the failure nobody has seen is the one most worth reading, and a confident wrong category is worse than none (§30 rule 4's own rule for a check that cannot run). **Rule order is load-bearing and tested**: `cannot reach Meituan (HTTP 502)` matches both `http` and `unreachable`, and a status an operator can act on must not be swallowed by the general case. **MEITUAN'S OWN CHINESE IS KEPT VERBATIM.** A tenant now reads `美团返回：商品已下架 (code 10032)` rather than *retries exhausted* — the platform's sentence about the platform's own refusal, which nothing we could write in its place would improve on. **NOTHING IS COMPOSED IN CHINESE.** `无法连接同步服务` is live whole on the Meituan tab, `已退出登录` and `重新登录` on both channel tabs, `找不到该商品` on Eleme's, `尚未读取商品` on its store line, `多次重试仍失败` in both daemons' own logs, and **`{平台}返回：` is the shape WeChat's own error already uses** (`微信支付未通过校验。微信返回：`) for precisely this job. Two arrangements of those fragments, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`. **Surfaces:** the Channel sync page, the product editor's Channels card and the phone's Channel sync screen all render the worded cause, falling back to the channel's raw sentence. **Tests:** eight added (57 total) — the platform's refusal kept verbatim, every cause the browser layer can write categorised, `http` winning over `unreachable` on a string both match, an uncategorised failure keeping its raw text, a retrying row classified on the cause beneath its suffix, the verdict carrying code + detail + raw together, **and two source-level guards: that neither browser module still has a bare `return { ok: false, transient: … }` and that both daemons prefer the reason over the wrapper**. `test:fast` green at 213. No schema, no migration, no new capability, no CI change. **The risk, named: this edits the browser-automation layer**, which drives live risk-controlled sessions. The diff is return values and comments only — nothing changes about what either module DOES, only about what it says when it fails.

2026-09-12 · v4.232 — **§103 ADDENDUM: THE THREE CHANNEL TABS LEARN WHETHER THE PUSH LANDED, AND THE LAST SCREEN THAT COULD LIE STOPS.** Asked by Ash, who read step 5's own "what this deliberately does not do" and said **"do it"**. §103 built a page, a dashboard row, a phone screen, dots and an editor card that all read the push result; the three TABS still classified locally, so the Meituan tab could show a green dot and the word *Synced* for Harissa Chilli Paste — the product the whole section exists because of — while every push had failed for 75 days. **THE GAP IS EXACTLY ONE STATE WIDE, AND THAT IS WHY THE FIX IS SMALL.** The server runs every check a tab runs AND the push result, and it tests the mapping's SHAPE FIRST: no map, sync off, catalogue unread, bad name and unclaimed option all return before it looks at the queue. So the two can only ever disagree in one place — **the tab says `ok`, the server says `att`** — and `chApplyVerdict` (01-core.js) applies only there. It can turn a green dot amber and can do nothing else: **it never rewrites a state the tab already named** (the operator is on that screen fixing the cause the tab gave them, and swapping it for another cause is a worse screen), never downgrades, and a failed or unread fetch leaves every tab exactly as it was. **PER STORE, NOT PER PRODUCT.** Meituan has two and a folded verdict would light the wrong one's dot, so the tabs ask the new `?channel=KEY` projection — one channel with its per-store detail, a third of the work and a third of the payload of the full read — rather than the compact one the Products dots use. **`compact` now also carries `reason`**, because a surface with a bare `k` falls back to *Needs attention* where the page names a cause. **THE READ NEVER BLOCKS A TAB**: fired after the list is painted, repainted when it lands, 60-second cache, one in-flight request shared by every caller, and dropped after a Push all (which changes every verdict at once). **A server-contributed state brings the page's own sentence with it** — *the last push to Meituan failed, so Meituan still shows the previous number* — because unlike every other state on those screens it has nothing on the page to point at. **WHAT THIS MOVES, SAID PLAINLY: the tabs' own "Needs attention" chips will count MORE.** That is the point and it is the correct number — those products were always wrong, the tab just could not see it. §103's earlier note declined to bundle this into a wording change; asked for on its own, it ships on its own. **AND THE SWALLOWED-ERROR BUDGET GOES DOWN, NOT UP.** The first cut added three `.catch(function () {})` and `scripts/check-swallowed-errors.js` correctly failed at 459 against a ceiling of 457. They were **removed rather than documented**: `chLoadVerdicts` cannot reject — it try/catches its own fetch and resolves either way — so each was dead, and a swallow there could only ever have hidden a bug in the repaint beneath it. Count 457 → **456**, and **the gate's ceiling is ratcheted to 456 in the same commit** so the one freed cannot be silently re-spent. That is a change to a build gate and is called out here and in the PR body per `CLAUDE.md`. **Tests:** five added (49 total) that **lift `chApplyVerdict` out of the shipped `01-core.js` and run it** — Harissa's exact shape turning amber with the server's reason, the sibling store untouched, every non-`ok` state refused, no downgrade, an unread channel and an unknown product both changing nothing, and all three tabs calling both halves. **Checked to fail** with the one-direction rule removed. `test:fast` green at 212. No schema, no migration, no new capability.

2026-09-12 · v4.231 — **§104 DECIDED AND BUILT: ONE CHANNEL ROW ON HOME, AND THE STALL KEEPS ITS VOICE INSIDE IT.** Decided by Ash from a live phone screenshot of Home showing both rows stacked — *"we don't need anymore the individual channel sync notification like meituan. we have the new one that all channels combined"*. **THE SCREENSHOT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT**: *Meituan not syncing · stock updates waiting since Sep 7, 5:56 PM · 3* sitting directly above *Channel sync · Meituan 2, wrong since Sep 7, 5:56 PM · 2* — same channel, same minute, two amber plugs, two chips going to two different places, in a list whose heading is *Needs you*. §103 built the second row and deliberately left the first alone (*"the stall is the CHANNEL's fact, said once on its own card"*), which was right about WHERE the fact belongs and wrong about how Home would read with both. **THE HALF THAT WOULD HAVE GONE SILENT, AND IT IS THE WHOLE SUBSTANCE OF THE RULING.** Deleting the per-channel row outright was rejected after checking what would still fire: **a channel that has stopped taking pushes shows GREEN on every one of its items**, by §103's own rule — a push in flight is green whatever its age, and a queue that never sends leaves each item's `last_pushed_qty` matching what the platform still displays — so `channel_items_attention` is **0** for a dead channel. The naive removal would have made 越秀's 1,683 pending Meituan pushes (§102's addendum: no successful push since 2026-08-22) say **nothing at all** on Home, which is the opposite of what was asked for: Ash's reading is that the combined row already covers all channels, so the build makes that true rather than assuming it. **THE RULING: the stall is not a row, it is a NAMED CHANNEL inside the one row's state line** — *Meituan not syncing, Eleme 4, wrong since Sep 7, 5:56 PM* — and it is still spelt out in full, with its waiting count and its own sentence, on the Channel sync page's channel strip, which is where the chip lands. **A channel says ONE thing about itself, worst first**: a channel that is not syncing at all is not also described by how many of its items have been caught out, because the stall contains them and *"Meituan not syncing, Meituan 2"* says one channel twice in seven words. **THE TWO COUNTS ARE NEVER SUMMED.** They have different denominators — `channel_items_attention.count` counts PRODUCTS wrong, `channelSyncStale().waiting_count` counts (store, product) push TARGETS waiting — and 2 + 3 = 5 would mean neither, the same trap the Restock pill three rows up carries its own comment about. **The pill shows the items count, or the waiting count when a channel is down and no single item is yet provably wrong** — the same either-or as Restock's `oosc || lowc`, with the state line naming which is on screen. **The clock is the OLDER of the two facts**, which is also the age the row sorts on: the earliest moment a customer could have started reading a wrong number, whichever way it went wrong. **THE SERVER IS UNCHANGED.** `/dashboard/ops` still sends both `channel_sync_stale` and `channel_items_attention`, and `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` is untouched: the merge is on the screen, and dropping the key would have taken the stall away from the Channel sync page too — the one place it is said in full. **THE CHANNEL'S NAME IS NOT ANSWERED HERE.** v4.229 landed mid-build and took the Products page off its own copy of the channel names, for the reason that applies to this row exactly: two copies are how two screens drift. The desktop row resolves through `csChannelName`, guarded by `typeof` the same way `09-products.js` guards its own call, and keeps a pair map only as the page-without-that-module fallback. The phone cannot reach that export at all and keeps its own, as §103's phone row already did. **TWO SURFACES, ONE CASE TABLE.** Desktop (`03-dashboard.js`) and phone (`m.html`) carry separate copies of the row builder, so the suite runs both through the identical cases and asserts the rows are equal; that check immediately found a pre-existing §103 mismatch — the desktop joined its Chinese line with an ASCII `, ` where the phone used `，` — now corrected to the phone's. **The stall-only chip lands on All items, not Needs attention**, which is empty in exactly that case: a chip that answers the row with a blank table is worse than no chip. **Chinese: nothing composed and nothing to declare.** `未同步` came off the row being removed and off `29-channel-sync.js`; `渠道同步`, `查看商品` and the `自 … 起不符` pair off §103's own row; the channel names off its `CH` map. The suite pins the exact set of Chinese fragments in both blocks, so an ADDED string goes red rather than shipping undeclared. **Tests:** `scripts/test_channel_sync_home_row.js`, new, fast shard, 31 cases — and it does not grep for phrases: it SLICES the §104 block out of both files and RUNS it against stubbed helpers and a payload per case, asserting the fire object. The screenshot's own payload collapsing to one row; the stalled channel not also counted as items; the pill not summing; **stall alone still lighting Home, with the waiting count and the stall's own age**; nothing wrong raising nothing; an absent payload answering rather than throwing; one channel down while another drifts; the older-of-two clock in both directions; all three channels each with its own worst fact; a fourth channel the name map has never heard of still named, drifting or down; two channels down at once; today's fact as a bare time and another day's carrying its date; an unreadable stamp still lighting the row; the duration suffix suppressed; the whole line in Chinese with no English leaking; both chips; a role that cannot open the screen still SEEING the row; the desktop asking `csChannelName` and falling back to its own pair when that module has not loaded; and the two surfaces asserted equal across every case in both languages. **13 of the 31 checked to fail against the naive removal** (the stall dropped, §103's row left alone). `test:fast` green at 213, plus `test_channel_sync_items`, `test_channel_sync_stale`, `test_mobile_home`, `test_phone_dashboard`, `test_app_home` and `test_confined_role_home` run alone. No schema, no migration, no new capability, no new string, no change to `.gitignore` or CI. A build under a new decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.224 — **§101 DECIDED AND BUILT: THE NIGHT'S ORDERS RAISE THEIR OWN KITCHEN REQUEST IN THE MORNING, BECAUSE THE PUSH AND THE PRINTER ALREADY KNOW HOW TO CARRY ONE.** Asked by Ash from the §84 walkthrough — the screen block answers *how many to prepare* and answers it only to somebody who opens the screen — and the ask was three words: **"we need it to be push, print"**. **§84 BUILT A NUMBER; §51 AND §71 BUILT A DELIVERY MECHANISM; NOTHING CONNECTED THEM.** Push (`_fireRestockPush`), the kitchen slip (`lib/kitchen-print`), the deep link onto `kitchenqueue`, the tickable card, §61's per-line close and §61's handover to *What you made* that actually moves the shelf — **every one of those keys on a `restock_orders` row**, and a night of `awaiting_restock` pre-orders creates no such row. So eighteen owed wraps pushed nothing, printed nothing, and waited for somebody to walk in and tap the right tab. **THE RULING: ONE REQUEST, RAISED BY THE SERVER, AT A PER-TENANT HOUR, DEFAULT 06:00** (`fresh.morningRequestHour`, blank turns it off) — chosen over a digest push/slip carrying the same numbers because a digest is a SECOND thing to build and a second place the kitchen reads, and it still leaves them nothing to close; and over per-order push/print, which on a thirty-order night is thirty slips at 2am and still never states the total. **THE SHAPE IS A REQUEST NOBODY TYPED, AND THAT CROSSES §84'S OWN LINE ON PURPOSE.** §84 refused to write orders into the request table and that refusal stands **in the direction it was made**: `lib/batch-owed.js` is unchanged, learns nothing, and is still the one definition of owed — the request is DERIVED from it once a day and never feeds back, so the number on the screen and the number on the paper cannot disagree. **The row is an ordinary kitchen request in every respect a reader can see**: `from_role` warehouse, `to_role` kitchen, `purpose` `'order'` — which already prints *For an order · 用于发货* (`lib/feie.js`) and already sorts below §65's urgent — `status` `'sent'`, a `PR-` number from `genRsNumber` (**injected, not copied** — §80's copy rule), no locations at all per §51, `created_by` NULL. **ONE NEW COLUMN, `restock_orders.auto_source`, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THE ONCE-A-DAY GUARD EXACT** rather than inferred: `created_by IS NULL` is also true of rows predating `drop_created_by_user_fk_v1`, and a guard that is usually right raises a second request on the morning it is wrong. NULL means a person raised it, which is true of every row already written, so **no backfill and no migration beyond one `addColumn`**. **THE GUARD IS THE DATABASE, NOT A FILE LATCH.** `lib/alert-latch`'s `claimWindow` was the obvious reach and is deliberately NOT used: it is per-box file state, so a rebuilt container forgets and sends twice, and the thing being guarded here is not an advisory but a row the kitchen will cook from. The query asks whether today already has an `auto_source` request — which is also the answer after a restart, a redeploy and a second app server. **IT CATCHES UP AND THEN STOPS**: it fires at the configured hour or up to three hours after, so a box that was down at 06:00 still prints at 07:10, while an order landing at 15:00 does not raise a surprise request for food wanted tomorrow. **QUANTITIES SUM PER PRODUCT ACROSS SHOPS** because a kitchen request carries no locations to split them into (§51) — which shop gets the wraps is a transfer's question, asked after they exist. **LINES CARRY SKU AND NAMES AND NO `product_id`**, matching every live kitchen request, because §61's recorded-derivation matches SKU-then-name and a line shaped differently would not tick off. **NOT SOLVED, AND THE DIRECTION IS CHOSEN RATHER THAN MISSED: a human request for the same food is not subtracted.** Subtracting would mean matching lines across open requests by SKU-then-name and trusting the result to REDUCE what gets cooked; wrong, the kitchen under-makes and a customer who paid gets nothing, where the opposite error is a visible over-make on a card somebody can read. Named here so the next reader knows it was weighed. **NO new push channel, NO second printer, NO new capability, NO change to `batch-owed`, and the kitchen's on-screen block is untouched** — it now agrees with a slip instead of being the only place the fact lived. **Chinese: nothing minted for the request, the slip or the push** — `purpose='order'`, `厨房新请求` and `用于发货` are all live and all reached unchanged; the note reuses `有客户订单等待` verbatim from §84's own block. **Two settings strings are ARRANGEMENTS of live fragments** (`厨房制作请求` whole from `routes/restock.js`, `留空则…` from the low-stock and campaign hints, `每天` from the low-stock digest), declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.60 under Rule 4's standing delegation with the candidates rejected. **Tests:** `scripts/test_kitchen_morning_request.js`, new, in the fast shard — the owed night end to end (parked order in, request out, push and print fired exactly once), the once-a-day guard across a simulated restart, the catch-up window's both edges, nothing-owed raising nothing, the hour switched off, the per-product sum across two shops, lines carrying SKU and no `product_id`, and `batch-owed` asserted unchanged by source. Checked to fail with the change reverted. `test:fast` green at 210, plus `test_batch_owed`, `test_kitchen_queue_item_split` and `test_restock_tenant2_split` run individually per CLAUDE.md. **One `addColumn` — called out here and in the PR body, not slipped in.** A build under a new decision, hence a patch.
2026-09-12 · v4.230 — **§103 STEP 5 BUILT: THE THREE CHANNEL TABS STOP SPEAKING DIFFERENT LANGUAGES, AND A WRONG CHARACTER THAT SHIPPED TO PRODUCTION DIES WITH THE STRING THAT CARRIED IT.** Asked by Ash (*"start step 5"*), the last of the five steps §103 recorded and the only one that edits the channel tabs themselves. **EIGHTEEN PHRASES BECOME ELEVEN, AND NO STATE HAS TWO NAMES.** The Meituan tab had seven state phrases, Eleme eight, GZ Grocery none at all — and two of them worded the SAME state differently: a stored name matching no listing was *Name not in catalogue* on Meituan and *Listing not found · 找不到该商品* on Eleme. **THE TABLE LIVES IN `01-core.js`, NOT IN ANY TAB**, because six files ask it (three tabs, the Channel sync page, the Products list's dots, the product editor's card) and a table in any one of them would have made that file the odd one out — which is exactly how the divergence arose. Four state words, five named causes, and `chWord(channel, k, reason)`: **the cause wins over the state where there is one**, because *Listing not found* tells an operator what to do and *Needs attention* only tells them to look; the dot's colour carries the state either way. **`no_name` IS THE ONE CAUSE ASKED OF THE CHANNEL RATHER THAN FLATTENED**, and that is a judgement rather than an exception: on Meituan 外卖 a missing name is WORK the operator does on that screen and stock stays frozen until they do it (*Add name · 待填名称*); on Eleme the mapping exists and pushes anyway, against the product's own name, which is a live wrong-target risk rather than an unfinished form (*No listing name · 缺商品名*). One state, two jobs. **FIVE PHRASES RETIRED**: Meituan's `Not linked · 未关联` → `Not listed · 未上架`, its `Name not in catalogue` → `Listing not found · 找不到该商品` (Eleme's, and the page's), its `Pick an option · 待选规格` → `No option picked · 未选规格`; Eleme's `Ready, sync off · 已就绪 · 同步关闭` → `Sync off · 已关闭` (Meituan's), and its `Not on Eleme · 未上架饶了么` → `Not listed · 未上架`. **THAT LAST ONE CARRIED 饶 (ráo) WHERE THE PLATFORM IS 饿 (è)** — a wrong character live in the admin for as long as that screen has existed, while the correct `饿了么` sat in three other files. It is RETIRED rather than corrected, because the shared word does not name the channel at all; **the same 饶 in that tab's no-listing-name sentence IS corrected in place**, since that sentence survives. This is the failure mode `CLAUDE.md`'s Chinese rule names outright — *an undeclared string is indistinguishable from a locked one to everyone who comes after, which is how a wrong character survives*. **MEITUAN'S "CATALOGUE NOT READ" BECOMES `unk`, THE KIND ELEME ALREADY USED** for that identical state; it still draws neutral (`.mt-dot.unk` is the twin `retail-admin.css`'s own header rule asks for) and **no chip reads `k`, so nothing counted moves**. **GZ GROCERY GAINS THE VOCABULARY IT NEVER HAD**: a State column with the same four words and the same dot, comparing our shelf against `last_pushed_qty` — which for this ERP is *the target we last reconciled to* and is exactly what `lib/channel-sync-items` compares server-side. The Δ column keeps showing the ERP's own number, a different and also useful fact. **WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO, AND IT IS THE REMAINING GAP**: the three tabs still classify LOCALLY, so none of them yet reads whether the last push landed — a tab can still say *Synced* for a product the Channel sync page correctly calls *Needs attention · push failed* (Harissa, §103's own worked example). Step 5 as recorded was the WORDS; overlaying the server verdict onto the tabs would change what their *Needs attention* chips count, which is a number Ash reads daily, and is **not bundled into a words change**. Recorded as the open item and offered. **Verification.** Words are display-only: every chip and count on all three tabs filters on the state KIND, never on the phrase — checked before writing a line, and it is what makes this safe. Five new checks in `scripts/test_channel_sync_items.js` (44 total) **lift the real table out of `01-core.js` and run it** rather than re-declaring it: the four words in both languages, cause-beats-state with `no_name` split by channel, all four surfaces calling `chWord`, every retired phrase gone from every live string, and no live string carrying 饶. `test:fast` green at 212. No schema, no migration, no new capability, no CI change.

2026-09-12 · v4.229 — **§103: THE CHANNEL'S MARK AND NAME ARE BILINGUAL, AND THEY WERE LEAKING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Reported by Ash in four words — *"Chinese in English version"*. **THE GLYPH WAS ONE CHARACTER FOR BOTH LANGUAGES**: `GLYPH = { meituan: '美', eleme: '饿', guanyi: 'GZ' }`, drawn on the channel cards and, after steps 3–4, on every row of the Products list — so an operator reading the app in English got two Chinese characters in a column headed *Channels*. **AND THE OTHER DIRECTION WAS LIVE TOO, UNREPORTED**: the Products dots' tooltip and the product editor's Channels card took the channel's name from the server's `label`, which is English-only, so the CHINESE app said *Meituan* and offered *前往Meituan*. GZ Grocery is already Latin and takes the same string twice. **A SOURCE-LEVEL GUARD, BECAUSE NO DATA TEST CAN SEE THIS.** Three checks read the shipped client files: the glyph table is a pair per channel with no Chinese on the English side, the Products page resolves names and glyphs through the shared exports rather than `ch.label`, and those exports exist. Checked to FAIL with the original one-character table pasted back. `scripts/test_channel_sync_items.js` now 39. `test:fast` green at 212. Both languages rendered and read before pushing. **Step 5 stays parked** at Ash's word (*"later"*). No schema, no migration, no new capability, no CI change. A fix under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-12 · v4.228 — **§103 STEPS 3 AND 4 BUILT, AND THE PHONE'S CHIP ROW CORRECTED.** Asked by Ash from a live screenshot of the shipped phone screen — *"fix the scrolling left right it's tight there with the text"* — then *"keep going with step 3 and 4, build them"*. **THE CHIP ROW WAS A HOUSE HELPER NOT USED.** `m.html` has carried `chipRow()` and the `.hscroll` class (which hides the scrollbar) for as long as the phone has had chips; §103's own row hand-rolled `overflow-x:auto` inside the screen's 16px-padded wrapper instead, so the bar showed and the last chip was shaved by the screen edge with no gutter. Fixed by using `chipRow()` and by moving the screen to the house layout it assumes — **wrapper carries no side padding, every block carries its own, the scroller runs full bleed** — which is how every other phone chip row on this app is already built. **No new markup and no new CSS**: the fix is the deletion of a local copy. **STEP 3 — THREE DOTS ON THE PRODUCTS LIST**, table column and card, drawn from `?compact=1` (verdict only). **PA_CH_ON is the whole gate and it asks the MAPPINGS, not the config**: a tenant with no product mapped to any channel gets no column and no card, because a column of grey dots on every row is precisely the noise §103 exists to avoid; a channel switched on with nothing mapped has nothing to say about any product on this page. **A variant family's dot is the worst of its members**, the same precedence the server folds stores with — a family row is one line and may stand for three products, and calling it green while one size is wrong is the failure this whole section is about. Clicking the dots opens Channel sync **on that product** (`csOpenProduct`), not on the catalogue. **The load never blocks the grid and never shouts**: it lands after the list is painted, and a failure leaves the rows exactly as they were. **STEP 4 — A CHANNELS CARD IN THE PRODUCT EDITOR**, one row per channel: state, what the platform last took, and — only when something is wrong — the sentence and a button onto that channel's tab. Hidden for an unsaved product and for a tenant with nothing mapped. **The button sits UNDER the sentence, not beside it**: beside it, in a pane that narrow, it took a third of the row and wrapped the explanation into three-word lines (caught on the render, before the push). **TWO PROJECTIONS, ONE COMPUTATION.** `channelSyncItems` gains `compact` (verdict only) and `productIds` (that product alone, and **not filtered on `is_active`** — the editor can be open on a paused product whose mappings are still pushing). Both are projections of the SAME read, deliberately: a second, lighter query written for the dots is how a dot and the page it links to start disagreeing about one item. 2026-09-11 · v4.226 — **§102 ADDENDUM: THE STALE CARD LEARNS BOTH WINDOWS, AND ONE OF THEM WAS §102'S OWN FAULT.** Asked for by Ash (*"do both"*) after §102 shipped. **ELEME WAS NEVER HOURS-GATED AND THE CARD THOUGHT IT WAS**: the channel table declared `hoursAware: true` because eleme-daemon looks like meituan-daemon, but its `processStockQueue` filters on `channelClosedStores('eleme')` alone — only the ORDER POLL reads hours — so an Eleme push could always go at 03:00 and **the card was quietest exactly when Eleme was most likely to be stuck**. **AND §102 BLINDED IT ON THE MEITUAN SIDE**: a Meituan jam at 00:30 on a batch morning scored zero elapsed until 08:00, so the card would have stayed silent through the very window §102 exists to keep syncing. `pushableElapsedMs` now walks the union of both intervals, merged; `preorderSpans()` ASKS lib/batch-cadence rather than mirroring it, cutoff-beats-lock ruling included (§80's copy rule). Every off switch returns null before a day is walked. **PRODUCTION CORRECTED THIS SESSION TWICE.** `diagnose_meituan_sync_window.js` at 01:51 on 2026-09-12: **neither store has opening hours set**. Meituan falls back to LEGACY_STORE_HOURS so §102 does the work claimed for it — but **Eleme has no fallback, reads always-open, and was already polling round the clock, so the overnight Eleme oversell §102 describes could not have occurred on this tenant's data**. 2026-09-11 · v4.225 — **§102 DECIDED AND BUILT: THE PRE-ORDER WINDOW OPENS THE SYNC GATE, AND THE TENANT SAYS WHEN IT OPENS — DECIDED by Ash** from the phone, off Home's *"Meituan not syncing · stock updates waiting since Sep 7, 5:56 PM · 19"* card: *"meituan syncing only on the morning it's a problem for pre order"*. **TWO CLOCKS WERE SET INDEPENDENTLY AND NOTHING CHECKED THEY AGREED**: §85's pre-order window opens at 00:00 — not a choice anyone made, just the absence of a lower bound — while the daemons' sync gate opens at the store's "Channel sync starts" time or two hours before opening, which is 08:00 for a shop opening at 10:00. **The hours between are dead, and they are the hours §85 exists to sell in.** **THE TWO CHANNELS FAIL DIFFERENTLY AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS VISIBLE**: on Meituan `flipTick` enqueues the allowance at midnight and `pushableStores()` holds every row until 08:00, so the listing shows yesterday's bare shelf all night — that queue IS the card. On Eleme the push was never hours-gated so the allowance publishes at 00:00, but the ORDER POLL is, and **§85 is self-capping only because each pre-order drives the shelf down**: an order nobody reads moves no shelf, so a twenty-unit allowance can take sixty orders before breakfast. **The oversell §85 was built to be incapable of, arriving through the one edge §85 did not look at.** **ASH DECIDED BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS**: *"tenent can choose when start , defult can be midnight"* → `preorder_open_hour`, defaulting to 0 so an untouched tenant is unchanged; and *"ok do it"* on the overnight order read, which is the half that matters — widening only the push would publish an allowance nothing could decrement. **THE WIDENING IS ONE FUNCTION, `batchCadence.preorderSyncOpen()`, called by both daemons** — §80's rule about a fourth copy of the cadence is the same rule here. Every one of §85's five off switches still holds, so a tenant with the schedule off has an unchanged daemon. **SETTING "Sync starts" TO 00:00 WAS REJECTED** though it needs no code: it widens every day batch or not, and runs a five-minute order poll at 04:00 on a Sunday the kitchen is not cooking — a fingerprint, not a preference. **TWO THINGS ARE NAMED AS NOT DONE**: `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` still marks Eleme `hoursAware: true` when its pushes never were, so the card under-reports Eleme — a real defect, a different one, not this section's; and **the 19 rows are NOT explained by §101** (17:56 is inside the window), the likely shape being the stale `error` row that file's own line 105 documents from production. Unconfirmed without a production read. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, one composed CN pair declared in the vocabulary, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-11 · v4.223 — **§58 ADDENDUM: A PARCEL GOING OUT IS NOT THE ORDER GOING OUT. THE THREE ROUTES THAT SHIP ONE BOX NOW SAY WHICH BOX.** Reported by Ash from the stock ledger — *"明天发快递的订单，鲜食自动扣了库存。原因，订单的陆运部分，点击发货，触发了扣除库存"* — TC000656 (Pesto 'Chicken' Wrap, Beet Salad, Quinoa Salad) and TC000647 (Tofu Banh Mi Wrap), 小程序 / Tianhe, four units off the count at 18:19 and 18:22 on food going out the next day, one of them to **-1**. **THIS IS §58's OWN COMPLAINT ARRIVING THROUGH A DOOR §58 DID NOT LOOK AT** — the ruling said the fresh line decrements at "the first forward transition into fulfilment … a parcel dispatched", which is exactly right for an order with one parcel and exactly wrong for an order with two. **A SPLIT ORDER'S BOXES DO NOT LEAVE TOGETHER, AND THAT IS THE FEATURE, NOT THE FAULT**: `planShipments` fans an out-of-Guangdong mixed basket into 空运 + 陆运, and the land box is sent days ahead **so that it arrives with** the air box carrying the food. So the first parcel out is, by design, the one with no kitchen line in it. **THE BUG WAS NEVER IN THE RULE, IT WAS IN THREE CALL SITES PASSING THE ORDER WHERE A PARCEL HAD LEFT**: `shipments/:sid/dispatch`, `shipments/:sid/deliver` and `orders/:id/jd-waybill` each stamp ONE shipment's `dispatched_at` and then handed `prepareCommitUnreservedOrder` the whole order id, whose per-product guard (`lib/inventory.js`) correctly found the held-back fresh products uncommitted and correctly took them. **Every guard behaved as written; none of them was ever told what had actually shipped.** **THE RULE, STATED SO IT SURVIVES THE NEXT SHAPE: a batch-made line decrements when the parcel CARRYING IT goes out.** A parcel-level caller passes `shipmentId`; `parcelsStillInTheBuilding` names the order's other parcels with no `dispatched_at`, and kitchen lines riding those are held exactly as payment holds them. **Whole-order callers pass nothing and take everything, unchanged** — PATCH /status, both auto-deliver sweeps, Start preparing — which is the backstop that makes the hold-back safe, and it is asserted rather than assumed. **HELD BACK WHOLE-PRODUCT, AND THE DIRECTION IS DELIBERATE**: the commit guard is per product and cannot hold part of one, so a fresh product split across both boxes waits for the later of them — §58's error to avoid is taking food off EARLY, and the last parcel always sweeps up. **EXPANDED, not order-level**, so a bundle on the waiting parcel is held by the components that carry the flag and not by its wrapper. **A line with `shipment_id` NULL is claimed by no parcel and is therefore NOT held** — this rule only ever defers a line demonstrably somewhere else. **Supplier parcels are not special-cased** because they carry nothing the kitchen makes. **NO SCHEMA CHANGE**: `retail_order_items.shipment_id` has recorded which box a line is in since the split-shipment table was added. **No new ledger reason, no new decrement site, no new strings, vocabulary untouched.** **Tests:** `scripts/test_fresh_stock_deferral.js` 45 assertions (was 24), the new ones reproducing TC000656 end to end — land box out, fresh untouched and a sold-out shelf still at 0 rather than -1; batch made; air box out; fresh off exactly once — plus the fresh line riding the parcel that IS leaving, the single-parcel and last-parcel sweep-ups, the bundle, the unassigned line, and the whole-order backstop. **13 of them checked to fail with the change reverted, in both directions** (behaviour and wiring separately), and the call-site check is by LABEL so a fourth parcel route wired the old way fails here rather than on a shelf. `test:fast` green at 209. **RECORDED AND NOT DONE: the four units already taken are left alone** — the per-product guard means tomorrow's dispatch will skip them, so the count is one day early and not double-counted, and a manual add-back today would leave it over by four from tomorrow; Ash was given the choice and the fix shipped without the adjustment. A fix under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.222 — **§100 DECIDED AND BUILT: CONVERSION DIVIDES ONE CHANNEL BY ITSELF, AND THE CARD SAYS WHICH ONE.** Reported from the phone with Home's second card circled — *"this part should only reflect the mini app channel, nothing else. title should say that as well … it's the only private sale channel platform that can count conver[sion]. others are meituan, eleme, gzgrocery."* **THE SCREENSHOT IS THE PROOF**: *Sessions 25 · Conversion 68.0% · 17 orders ÷ 25 sessions*, where the 25 were mini-app opens and the 17 were the day's paid orders across the mini app, Meituan AND the counter till. **IT COULD ONLY EVER BE WRONG, NOT SOMETIMES WRONG.** `retail_visits` has exactly one writer in the tree — `miniapp/utils/track.js` posting to `/api/retail/track`; not `shop.html`, not any daemon — so a session is a mini-app session by construction, while a marketplace hands over finished orders and will never report a browse. **The error therefore runs one way only: every Meituan order the shop wins inflates a number meant to describe browsing we can watch**, so the better the marketplace day, the healthier the mini app looked. **THIS IS §36's FINANCE FINDING FROM THE OTHER SIDE** — that one had a blended NUMERATOR over a storefront denominator; this is the denominator's half of the same rule, and m.html's own AOV note already states it ("revenue and its denominator must stand on the same population") two cards from where it was being broken. **FIXED AT SOURCE, NOT ON THE CARD THAT REPORTED IT**: there is no all-channel conversion to lose — only an arithmetic mistake to stop repeating — so `kpis.conversion_rate` is now mini-app orders ÷ mini-app sessions for every caller, with `kpis.mini_app_orders` riding alongside so any screen quoting "N orders ÷ M sessions" names the numerator it actually divided by. **§100 says so rather than leaving it to be discovered.** Chinese: `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.59, **one pair lifted whole from the Orders screen's own channel chip** and two arrangements of live strings; nothing minted. **Tests:** `scripts/test_mini_app_conversion.js`, 20 assertions in the fast shard, which **lifts the predicate out of `routes/retail.js` by regex** and runs it against an in-memory database seeded one order per channel, so a later widening fails here instead of shipping; checked to fail in both directions. Two rendered cases added to `test_mobile_home.js`, two to `test_backend_nav_parity` §4, and the fake server's fixture made deliberately SMALLER on every mini-app figure than its all-channel neighbour — a fixture where the two agreed would pass whether or not Home read the right one. `test:fast` green. A build under a new decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.221 — **THE CUTOVER: NO CASE IS RAISED FOR A PARCEL DELIVERED BEFORE TODAY, AND THREE THINGS v4.220 BROKE ARE FIXED.** Reported by Ash off the live phone within the hour — "Delivery needs a call · 7, oldest 79d", and tapping it opened unrelated orders from today and yesterday. **WIDENING A LIVE ALERT IS RETROACTIVE UNLESS YOU STOP IT**: the rule changed from `mode='air'` to every mode and the query does not care when the rule changed — it asked the same question of every parcel ever shipped and correctly answered that a pile were late, the oldest seventy-nine days, which is work nobody will ever do on the one card whose job is to list work that will be. 2026-09-11 · v4.220 — **§98'S LAST TWO OPEN ITEMS ARE BUILT AND THE SECTION CLOSES: EVERY MODE RAISES A CASE, AND THE EVIDENCE IS ATTACHED.** **AIR-ONLY WAS A HOLE, NOT A CONSERVATIVE DEFAULT** — `planShipments` sends every Guangdong order by land "regardless of any item's air flag", so the destination closest to the kitchen, ice packs included, was the one whose late parcels raised nothing at all. Thresholds are now per mode in `LATE_AFTER_DAYS` (`lib/delay-case.js`): air stays **1** because widening must not restate an existing case, local **1** against a same-day promise, land **3** because at 1 it would fire on ordinary two-day freight until the badge became noise. A mode absent from the map never raises one, so supplier-direct is excluded without being named. **Fixed in this phase and not tenant-editable, exactly as §32 fixed the waste reason codes.** The rule had been written out four times in `routes/retail.js` and twice more on the clients — same drift as the paid predicate, consolidated the same way; **the clients no longer do date arithmetic at all**, the server computes `late_days` and both screens render it. The `air_` names on the wire and in the database are historical and STAY (two client releases and a migration for nothing an operator can see); the function was renamed to `orderHasDelayedParcel` because that is free. **EVIDENCE IS A CHILD TABLE** — a claim is several photographs where a staff receipt is one — and **the bytes never travel with a list**, per `staff_expenses`'s own rule; only a `data:image/…;base64,` URI is accepted, since both screens render it into an `<img src>`; a file is reachable only through its own case; the phone downscales to 1280px/JPEG 0.7 as the claim photo already does. **Evidence does not gate closing**, deliberately: plenty of claims settle on a call, and a checklist that demands a photograph teaches people to attach a blank one. One replacement per case is enforced — a double-tap would send real stock twice. **THREE EXISTING GUARDS CAUGHT THIS AND ALL THREE WERE RIGHT**: `test_customer_currency` rejected "a ¥0 order" in a multi-currency product and **also caught two ¥ literals from stages one and two, live since this evening**, which had evaded it only because `'¥' + Number(x)` puts a quote between symbol and digit; `test_finance_summary`'s fixture lacked the new column and now names its columns explicitly; `test_handle_threading_batch2`'s call-site pin moved from eleven to twelve while the rule it guards still runs over every site.
