A build under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.217 — **§99 ADDENDUM 1: THE SNOOZE IS BUILT, AND IT IS NOT A DISMISSAL.** Asked for by Ash after §99 shipped; that section had recorded it as not built and named the four things it needed, all settled here. **THE JUSTIFICATION IS `lib/push-events.js`'s OWN SENTENCE** — *"The switch that gets used is the one that turns the whole thing off, and then the pick that mattered arrives nowhere"* — because §99 correctly gave a dismissed banner no effect at all, which leaves an operator who cannot act today with exactly one working control: killing every push. **A SWIPE STILL WRITES NOTHING AND STILL MUST**; the deferral is a press on a screen, by somebody holding `invoices:manage`. **THREE PROPERTIES STOP IT BECOMING A WAY TO NEVER DO THE WORK**: it reaches tomorrow's reminder hour and no further, so one press hides at most ONE ask; **IT QUIETS THE PUSH ONLY** — the row still matches `pendingSql`, so Home keeps counting it and still goes brick at month-end, which is the safeguard and is asserted directly; and the row is SKIPPED, never claimed, so a deferral moves the cadence rather than restarting it. **MONTH-END HONOURS IT, RECORDED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS**: the control means *do not ask me again before tomorrow's hour*, so inside month-end's daily cadence a press before the day's ask defers it and a press after it changes nothing — **and that second case must NOT be "fixed" by lengthening the snooze at month-end**, which would invert the rule §99 turns on; both cases are pinned. Disabling the control for three days a month was rejected: a button that reads as set and buzzes anyway is a lying control. **THE GATE ALREADY EXISTED** (`cap-routes` maps every write under the invoices prefix to `invoices:manage`) and the suite proves it through the REAL middleware — `invoices:view` gets 403 and writes nothing while still reading the list. Only a WAITING row may be deferred; issued, cancelled, unpaid, never-requested and non-existent all answer `not_pending`, and `isSnoozed` treats a lapsed, blank or unreadable stamp as not snoozed so nothing ever has to clear the column and an unparseable value fails towards ASKING. **ONE STRING FOR BOTH STATES** — the app's own `.chip` fill says "set", and no date is printed because the button and the server already agree on tomorrow. Chinese: `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.57, one composed pair and one lifted, **`忽略` and `跳过` rejected because both describe a dismissal**. 27 new assertions across two suites, load-bearing ones checked to fail reverted; `test:fast` green at 206. **A §99 claim is corrected**: it framed month-end survival as survive-or-not, and the real answer is a third option. **Auto-issue remains open**, asked twice and unanswered. A build under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.216 — **§99 BUILT: THE FAPIAO CHASE, AND THE COUNT THAT DISAGREED WITH HOME.** Asked from the phone with a screenshot reading *Pending 2* — *"why we have 2 open invoices and the system doesn't alert me … if customer close the notification and invoice still open, system should recognize it and pop up again."* **TWO DEFECTS WEARING ONE COAT, AND ASH FOUND THE SECOND**: told that *"those invoice that not settled came from canceled order"*, the survey found why there was nothing to alert about — **five call sites asked which fapiao were pending and `GET /api/retail-admin/invoices` was the only one not requiring the order to be alive**, filtering on `needs_invoice = 1` alone while Home, the unseen dot, the Orders pseudo-status and its badge all excluded `cancelled` and `pending_payment`. So the list counted the dead, Home did not, and the operator drew the more damaging of the two available conclusions — that the ALERTING was broken — which is the reasonable one to draw from two sincere numbers that disagree. `lib/fapiao-queue.js` is the predicate now and the regression guard is in the suite, not in review: the test fails if `routes/retail.js` states the exclusion anywhere itself, because **the defect was never a wrong clause but five copies of one**. Dead requests are excluded from the count and NOT hidden — they wear the order's own live `已取消` / `待付款` in the muted pill, so no new string and no row vanishes; `counts.blocked` is new so All still sums its rows; an issued fapiao keeps reading issued whatever became of its order, being a 红冲 waiting to happen. **THE REMINDER IS A WINDOW, NOT A LATCH, AND `lib/alert-latch.js` HAD ALREADY DRAWN THE DISTINCTION** — which is why `lib/delivery-reminders.js` could not take a fifth case: its claim is `WHERE … IS NULL`, once ever. **DISMISSING WRITES NOTHING, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION**: there is no dismissed column because there must not be one, the row still matches `pendingSql` next sweep, and only ISSUING stops it — by dropping out of the queue, so no state is ever cleared. Tagged per order, so `sw.js`'s existing `renotify` replaces the tray entry rather than stacking. **THE CADENCE KEYS OFF MONTH-END, NOT ELAPSED DAYS** — silent 24h, then 48h, then DAILY in the last three days with Home's row going brick, because what makes a late fapiao expensive is the tax period closing and not its age; the window is computed from the month's own length so February is not exempt, and the phone reads the SHOP's date. At 10:00, **which is NOT the quiet hours `push-events.js` refuses** — that file drops an alert by a clock, this one schedules its own send, the same `DAYOF_HOUR = 10` the delivery sweeper uses. One digest above three; a digest claims every row it covered. Audience `invoices:manage` ("issuing a 发票 is a fiscal act"), switch `invoice_pending`, ON by default. **NOT BUILT AND NOT DECIDED: the snooze** (its own column, endpoint and month-end question — held back rather than folded in) and **why auto-issue is off**, raised in session and unanswered. Chinese: `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.56, two composed pairs and one lifted, **`逾期` rejected and the reason recorded** — a 发票 unissued on the 29th has broken no promise to the customer. 52 new assertions across two fast suites, the load-bearing ones on each side checked to fail with the change reverted; `test:fast` green. Two commits, one PR — the session was pinned to one branch; recorded in the section. A build under a new decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.215 — **THE PAID PREDICATE IS CONSOLIDATED: ELEVEN HAND-WRITTEN COPIES IN `routes/retail.js` NOW ASK `lib/finance-window.js`, WHICH HAD ALWAYS CLAIMED TO BE THE ONE PLACE.** Decided by Ash after addendum 2 measured it. **IT WAS NOT NEW ARCHITECTURE, IT WAS AN EXISTING DECISION BEING HONOURED** — that module's header has always said "editing a constant here is the only way to change what Finance counts", which was true of the two Finance routes that import it and quietly false of `routes/retail.js`, which had never imported it at all; the claim was a description of two files sold as a property of the system. **THE LIST IS NOW THE SOURCE AND THE SQL IS RENDERED FROM IT**: `PAID_STATUSES` holds the five statuses, `paidWhere(alias)` renders them, and `PAID` / `PAID_O` are its two callers — six of the eleven copies were alias-qualified and five bare, which is why one constant could not have replaced them and why the drift was easy to miss. **NOTHING ABOUT WHAT IS COUNTED CHANGED, AND IT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN PROMISED**: `scripts/test_paid_predicate.js` pins the generated string byte-for-byte against a frozen copy of the pre-consolidation literal, so reordering the list fails a test instead of quietly restating every money figure in the product, and the same suite fails if any file under `routes/` or `lib/` hand-writes the list again. **FIVE NEIGHBOURING PREDICATES WERE LEFT ALONE** — `('paid','awaiting_restock')`, `('paid','preparing')`, `('paid','preparing','rider_pickup')` and the two channel-internal ones answer different questions, folding them in would have been a behaviour change wearing a refactor's clothes, and a test asserts they are still present. **ONE EXISTING SUITE ARGUED FOR ITS OWN AMENDMENT**: `test_finance_summary.js` scraped `PAID` with a regex and counted the literal, and both were fixed the way that file had already fixed the same problem for `ODATE` in a comment it wrote itself — require the module, because that tests the value that ships rather than a copy of its spelling. **Stage three is now one line away and is still not built**: the exclusion is a single clause in `paidWhere`, but what a ¥0 replacement order IS remains open, and the per-customer counts are not gated on payment at all. 203 fast suites pass, 0 fail. A refactor with no behaviour change, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.214 — **§98 STAGE FOUR IS BUILT: A CARRIER'S PAYMENT POSTS ONE LEDGER ROW WHEN IT LANDS. STAGE THREE IS NOT, AND THE REASON IS A NUMBER.** `lib/delay-case-posting.js` writes exactly one `income_entries` row keyed on a new `delay_case_id`, by the same delete-then-reinsert shape `postClaim` uses; **only `paid` posts**, and a rejection, a withdrawal or a re-filing after a payment takes the row back OUT rather than offsetting it with a negative one — §87's rule for money out, restated for money in. It is **the first projection this ledger has ever had on the money-IN side**; every `income_entries` row before it was hand-typed, which is why `loadTyped` needed a third refusal and the Transactions screen a third mark. The row carries **no category**, deliberately: §36 records that the income category list ships empty so the form cannot offer a wrong option, and seeding one to label carrier compensation would be a library deciding a question that document says is the tenant's. **STAGE THREE STOPPED ON A MEASUREMENT.** A ¥0 replacement order adds ¥0 to every revenue sum, so revenue was never the problem — COUNT and AVG are. The gate those surfaces share, `status IN ('paid','preparing','dispatched','delivered','awaiting_restock')`, is **written out verbatim twelve times** (eleven in `routes/retail.js`, one in `lib/finance-window.js`) with no single definition to amend, and a replacement parcel must pass through `preparing`, `dispatched` and `delivered` to be picked, shipped and tracked — so it sits inside that predicate by construction at all twelve, with the ungated per-customer counts beyond them. Twelve hand-copied predicates and missing one is a silently wrong report, which no test in the tree would catch. **Recorded, not decided:** consolidating that predicate to one exported definition first, as its own change with no behaviour attached, would make excluding a replacement one line — but it edits how every money figure in the product is computed and is **not a decision a session may take**. Until then step three of the case stays what stages one and two shipped: an operator's tick over a replacement raised by hand. Chinese: `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.55, two composed pairs, each the live claim refusal with one noun phrase swapped. 202 fast suites pass, 0 fail; all six finance suites green. A build under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.213 — **§98 STAGES ONE AND TWO ARE BUILT: THE LATE-PARCEL CASE, AND THE CHECKLIST THAT WILL NOT CLOSE WHILE THE CARRIER STILL OWES AN ANSWER.** Two tables, `lib/delay-case.js` holding the rule, one step endpoint, and the checklist on BOTH surfaces. **THE THREE READ SITES DID NOT SWAP AND v4.212 SAYS THEY WOULD** — that entry was written before the code and is wrong; it is left standing and corrected in a §98 addendum rather than edited, per this file's own rule about dated claims. `air_delay_cleared_at` REMAINS the single flag meaning "still on the worklist" and the case row gates who may set it: `/dashboard/ops`'s `delivery_alerts` already counts these orders, ages them from `dispatched_at` and refreshes every sixty seconds, so the weeks-long chase surface needed no change at all — and swapping would have required backfilling a closed case for every parcel already cleared in production, or every handled order from the last year lights up on deploy morning. **THE PHONE ALREADY HAD THE BANNER AND THE SURVEY MISSED IT**, having grepped the column name where `public/m.html` keys off `o.airDelayed`; once the server refuses the close, a phone still offering a one-tap dismiss is §97's own "the same button with the safety removed", so both surfaces ship or neither does. **`none` HAD TO HOLD THE CASE OPEN** — an operator who never touched the dispute track has not decided not to claim, and choosing not to claim is its own state needing a typed reason, which is what makes "the dispute, if any" expressible; `scripts/test_delay_case.js` guards that second only to the refusal itself. Chinese: `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.54, seventeen composed pairs and fifteen lifted, **none introducing a word the repository did not already ship**; the one thing that could not be carried forward is 京东, hard-coded into both surfaces' live instruction, since the claim is against whichever carrier carried the parcel. Stages three (the ¥0 replacement order) and four (the ledger row) are NOT built and nothing here decides them further. 199 fast suites pass, 0 fail; `test_mobile_screens` renders 142 screens clean. A build under an existing decision, hence a patch.

2026-09-11 · v4.212 — **§98 DECIDED BY ASH: A LATE PARCEL THAT SPOILED THE FOOD IS A CASE WITH STEPS, AND THE CARRIER'S MONEY IS NOT INCOME UNTIL IT LANDS.** Asked from the phone, in Ash's own scenario: the package arrived complete but late, the fresh items were spoiled, the carrier is given evidence and pays for the spoiled goods, and replacement goods go back to the customer — *"where would you suggest to record it?"* **THE STEPS ALREADY EXIST ON SCREEN AS PROSE WITH ONE CHECKBOX UNDER THEM.** Measured against `5ab75c8`: `orderHasDelayedAirShipment` already raises the `AIR DELAYED · contact customer` badge, a dashboard card and an `order_air_delayed` customer warning not to eat the perishables, and the order drawer already prints TWO numbered instructions — contact the customer, contact the carrier for compensation — above a single button that writes `retail_shipments.air_delay_cleared_at` and nothing else. **Four facts behind one checkbox cannot answer whether the carrier was ever chased**, and no money or stock is recorded at all. So the instructions become the steps IN PLACE: not a new screen, not a new module, and the detector is untouched. **THE SHAPE IS `retail_refund_events`, DELIBERATELY** — one row per step with an amount, a note and who did it, because refunds already read as a timeline and a second shape would have to agree with the first forever; **there is no task or checklist table anywhere in this repo** (grepped) and a general one must not be built here, which is §32's "a reason, not a feature" arriving from the other side. **THE CASE LIVES ON THE SHIPMENT, NOT THE ORDER**, because an order fans out into air and land parcels and both the detector and the ack route are already scoped per parcel. **THE SESSION'S FIRST READING OF THE MONEY WAS WRONG AND ASH CORRECTED IT**: *"jingdong will pay a certain amount for the spoiled products so it doesn't really cost roots … but we do have the cost for the new food that been shipped out."* **Measured, and it makes the accounting SMALLER than it looked**: `routes/finance-summary.js` returns `cost_of_goods: null` / `gross_profit: null` and no route in `routes/retail.js` writes an `expense_entries` row for a sale, so food is an expense the day it is BOUGHT — the spoiled goods book nothing, the replacement books nothing and merely moves stock, and **the carrier's payment is the ONE row this whole case puts in the books**. **NOT INCOME UNTIL IT LANDS** — §87's rule for money out restated for money in, because a claim the carrier rejects or part-pays would otherwise leave money in the books nobody received; posting takes `postClaim`'s delete-then-reinsert shape, and **`income_entries` has no `claim_id`-shaped column where `expense_entries` has one.** **THE REPLACEMENT'S COST IS RECORDED ON THE CASE, NOT IN THE LEDGER**, because the only question worth asking is whether the payment covered what it cost to put right, and a flat-rate carrier against a larger replacement leaves a gap no ledger row in this model would show. **TWO RULINGS TAKEN IN SESSION**: the replacement leaves as a **¥0 order linked to the first** (a stock adjustment is rejected — the customer needs a waybill to follow and only an order carries a parcel), and step three **branches to a refund** where the customer would rather have their money. **AMOUNTS ARE TYPED, NOT CALCULATED** — flat sums, percentages and assessed values all differ per carrier, so a typed "claimed" and "received" serves every tenant with no configuration, which is what *"other tenants have different configuration"* asks for; a compensation-rules engine is rejected. **NOTHING MAY NAME JD** — `lib/tracking.js` already holds the general carrier list, and the text being replaced is the one place that hard-codes it. **RECORDED AS OPEN, NOT DECIDED**: which parcels raise a case (today air-only, delivered-only, >1 day — a late land parcel and a late rider raise nothing, and widening needs a lateness number per mode because a day late is ordinary for land), whether evidence is held in Tacet, which readers must exclude a ¥0 order from counts and averages, and whether a case can ever be both a replacement and a refund (offered, not taken). **Rejected: recording the spoiled goods as waste** — `waste_records` demands a `location_id` and a subject at that location while the food is at the customer's house, and the carrier pays for it so it is not the tenant's loss; recorded because it is the intuitive wrong answer. The Chinese is deliberately not composed here: the live pair `空运延误 · 联系客户` exists and the labels should restructure around it per `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` Rule 4. A new decision reversing no earlier rule, hence a patch. **Docs only; no code changed.**

2026-09-10 · v4.211 — **"ALSO TODAY" IS GONE: THE TWO TODAY CARDS ON THE PHONE'S HOME SHARE ONE HEADING — DECIDED by Ash.** No new section: this is v4.159's own screen being worded, and it decides nothing about what either card contains. Asked from the phone with a screenshot of Home — *Today* over Revenue / Orders / Avg. order / New customers, *Also today* over Sessions / Conversion / Returning / Refunded — and one question: *"today and also today? maybe better wording?"* **THE SECOND HEADING NAMED ITS POSITION, NOT ITS CONTENTS.** *Also today · 今日其他* meant "the card after the other one". Sessions, Conversion, Returning and Refunded are not *other today*; they are the SAME day the card above counts, read a different way. It was the only heading on Home that did not say what it sat over — *Needs you*, *While you were away* and *Quick actions* all do. **AND IT COULD CONTRADICT THE SCREEN.** The two cards are gated INDEPENDENTLY, on the `orders` and `customers` keys v4.159 wired, so a role with the money card hidden and this one shown read *"Also today"* with no *Today* above it for it to be ALSO to. That is not hypothetical — it is the money gate doing its job on a stock or delivery board, which is the case v4.159 existed to fix. **FOUR NAMINGS WERE PUT UP AND THE HEADING WAS DELETED RATHER THAN RENAMED**: *Today / Traffic · 流量* (a live pair, but honest only if Refunded moves up beside the revenue it bites); *Today / Customers · 客户* (the desktop twin's own name, free, but that word is already a nav tab); a rewrite in Home's voice (the only option needing composed Chinese); and the deletion, which Ash took. **THE HEADING NOW BELONGS TO THE SECTION, NOT TO EITHER CARD.** `todaySection()` draws one *Today · 今日* over whichever cards survive their gates and none at all when both are hidden — a bare *Today* over an empty column is precisely what the money gate exists to prevent. Nothing needs to name the day twice: `pageHead` already carries the date line under the greeting, and says in its own comment that it "names the day every other number on the screen is counted over". **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED — a string was REMOVED, not added**, so `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched. The two cards' staggered entrance (.12s, .15s) collapses to one, which is the only visible change beyond the words. `scripts/test_backend_nav_parity.js` §4 gains four static assertions (fast shard, 59 total) and `scripts/test_mobile_home.js` gains the gate CROSS-PRODUCT in Chromium — all four combinations, the empty one included (115 assertions across 34 cases); the load-bearing ones on each side were checked to fail with the change reverted, and `npm run test:fast` is green at 198. **Serialised against three live sessions**, one of them editing `public/m.html`: held until `claude/settings-ui-redesign-bztm8h` was pushed, then confirmed its hunks (559, 1187, 7855, 11186, 13221+, 14287) do not touch Home's blocks. Wording and tests; no schema, no migration, no capability grant, no endpoint touched.

2026-09-10 · v4.210 — **§97 DECIDED BY ASH: THE PHONE MATCHES THE PC, PAGE BY PAGE, STARTING WITH ORDERS.** *"mobile version functionality should be the same as PC."* **THIS OVERRIDES A WRITTEN RULE THAT WAS CORRECT UNTIL TODAY**: `docs/tacet-mobile-parity.md` §"How the two surfaces differ by design" — *"a missing capability is only a defect when it is part of that loop"* — which is why roughly thirty rows in that document are `➖` rather than bugs and why its 2026-08-22 audit could close with Orders marked done. **RETIRED, NOT DELETED**: the old document is not rewritten, every `➖` stays with its reason, and what changes is how they are READ — an open gap with an argument attached, the argument now Ash's to overrule rather than a session's to inherit. **WHY IT IS WORTH RETIRING RATHER THAN DEFENDING**: two of its own reasons had already expired before anyone re-read them — the staff note was blocked on an endpoint that now exists (`PATCH /orders/:id/note`) — and **a rule whose exceptions rot has to be re-checked to be used, which nobody was doing.** **THE SAME CAPABILITIES, NOT THE SAME LAYOUT**: a sheet where the desktop has a drawer is not a gap; *"can an operator do this at all from a phone"* is the only question. **Authoring stops being an automatic exemption** and travels with the rule that produced it. **THREE EXCEPTIONS, RECORDED AS OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSED**: the courier map, the Qingyun point picker and the JD label printer each need a phone DESIGN before any code, which is a different question from parity. **TWO STANDING RULES FOR EVERY STEP**: every added write is asserted on the REQUEST, not the toast (this app has twice shipped a write that reported success and sent nothing); and every guard the desktop puts in front of a write comes WITH the write — a confirm the PC asks and the phone does not is the same button with the safety removed. **REJECTED: one change for the whole page** (twenty-odd endpoints and eight list-level features; unreviewable, unrevertable in pieces). **REJECTED: editing the closed audit** to match a later decision — it destroys the record of what was believed when; the pointer is one-way and forward. **REJECTED: deciding the three exceptions permanently either way**, with no phone design to look at. Survey and staging: `docs/tacet-mobile-orders-parity-survey.md`. No code in this commit.

2026-09-10 · v4.209 — **§96: THE SWEEP §95 LEFT OPEN IS DONE, AND IT FOUND NOTHING ELSE BROKEN.** Asked for by Ash after §95: other clients of `/api/retail-admin/customers` might spell its columns the same wrong way the till did. **THEY DO NOT.** Every caller of that route was read: the desktop roster (`08-customers.js`), the global search (`02-settings-ops.js`), the New order picker (`04-orders.js`), the importer (`24-import.js`) and marketing's grant search (`05-marketing.js`) all read the **raw column names** — `points_balance`, `lifetime_spend`, `tier_key`, `orders_count`, `is_blocked` — correctly. The other two customer routes are clean for their own reasons: `by-phone` returns `is_blocked`/`nickname` and its reader uses exactly those, and **`store-admin`'s lookup camel-cases on the SERVER**, so its client never guesses. **EXACTLY TWO CLIENTS RENAME THIS ENDPOINT'S COLUMNS**: the till's `custRow` (added by §95) and the phone back office's own customer mapper — and the phone's has been right all along. **A NEGATIVE RESULT IS THE FINDING, and it is recorded rather than left as a silence**, because "nobody swept" and "somebody swept and it was clean" are different states and only one of them is worth anything to the next person. **ONE GUARD IS ADDED, and it is the whole of the code change.** The phone's mapper was correct and had **nothing holding it there** — which is precisely the standing §95's own subject had on the morning it shipped broken. Two clients renaming one endpoint's field is two chances to drift, and the endpoint is the thing both must follow, so both are now pinned to it in one place beside the assertion §95 added. **PROVEN RED by breaking the phone mapper and re-running**, not assumed. **REJECTED: aliasing the column to `points` in the endpoint.** It would have removed the need for either normaliser and changed the shape under all five readers that are correct today — fixing nothing and putting five working screens at risk. **REJECTED: a general lint that no client may read a field the server does not send.** The rule is right and the mechanism is not available: the routes return `SELECT`s built from interpolated fragments, so the returned shape is not statically knowable, and a check that guessed it would fail on the endpoints it could not parse. Two named pins that are exact beat one general rule that is approximate. `npm run test:fast` 198/198 green on `df0d2a9`; `test_till_credit.js` 43 → 44. No schema, no migration, no server change, no Chinese, no `.gitignore` or CI change.

2026-09-10 · v4.208 — **§95 FIXED: PAY WITH POINTS WAS DEAD ON ARRIVAL, BECAUSE THE TILL READ A FIELD NO CUSTOMER ROW HAS EVER CARRIED.** Reported by Ash off the live till within the hour, from the customer picker: *"it doesnt show points, everyone at 0, only wallet amount work."* **THE SCREENSHOT WAS THE WHOLE DIAGNOSIS.** `/api/retail-admin/customers` returns its `SELECT` verbatim, so a row carries `points_balance` — the column's name — while the wallet's column is simply `balance`. `public/till.html` read `c.points`. One of the two happened to be spelled the way the file guessed, which is exactly why it looked like a points problem rather than a naming one. **THE DISPLAY HAD BEEN WRONG SINCE THE ROW WAS WRITTEN and it was cosmetic until §93**, which gave the till something to SPEND: `creditOffer` reads the same field, so `pMax` was zero for every customer, the points control never drew, and **the headline half of what shipped an hour earlier could not be reached at all**. The wallet worked throughout, which is what made the report so precise. **NORMALISED AT THE BOUNDARY, NOT AT THE READERS.** `custRow()` maps a row once, where rows come in, and the four readers are untouched. Patching each reader was the obvious smaller diff and is the reason the bug existed: knowing the trick was the requirement, so the next reader added would have had to know it too. Both spellings are accepted and both coerced to numbers, so the shape does not depend on which endpoint a later caller uses. **WHY THE SUITE THAT SHIPPED WITH §93 DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth keeping.** `test_till_credit.js` had forty assertions over the arithmetic, the route, the transaction, the ledger rows and the till's wiring, and every one of them passed against a feature that could not be used. **Each built its own customer object**, and every one of them spelled the field the way the code being tested spelled it. A test that invents its input cannot catch an input invented wrongly. The three new assertions do not invent one: the endpoint's own `SELECT` is **read** for the field name (so a later rename fails here rather than in front of a cashier), `custRow` is **run** against a row shaped like the endpoint's, and `creditOffer` is **run** against the result — with a companion row deliberately left un-normalised, so the fixture stops proving anything the moment the boundary stops mattering. All three were **proven red against the shipped file**, by checking it out and re-running, not by assuming. **NO CHINESE, no schema, no migration, no server change** — the endpoint is correct and is not touched; this is one normaliser on the client that reads it. `npm run test:fast` 198/198 green on `d68efff`; `test_till_credit.js` 40 → 43, still red under `TC_MUTANT=1`. No change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-10 · v4.207 — **§94 DECIDED: THE NEW ORDER FORM STOPS OFFERING A COUNTER SALE — the second half of §93's decision, carried out.** Ash's original question was whether the New order button could go away entirely in favour of the till; §93 answered no and recorded that the two surfaces overlap in exactly one row. This removes that row. **THE OPTION COULD NOT PRODUCE A CORRECT ROW AND HAD NOT SINCE §44 WAS AMENDED.** A shop sale is `channel: 'shop'` with a `shop_entry_method` naming the door it came through, and the server enforces both halves symmetrically. **This form sends neither** — it offers no 'shop' origin, deliberately, because a shop sale is not an answer to "how did the customer reach us?", and it has no door to name. So a walk-in keyed here filed as `pickup` or `other` and **fell out of the shop's revenue line**, which is the one thing §44's amendment exists to keep whole. The defect was silent: the order was created, the stock moved, the money was recorded, and only the attribution was wrong. **THE PHONE'S COPY OF THIS FORM HAS ONLY EVER OFFERED TWO** (`ONW_FULS`, `public/m.html`) — so this is the desktop catching up with a choice already made, not a new rule, and the two surfaces now agree. **WHAT IS NOT CHANGED, and the distinction is the whole of the risk here**: `counter` remains a server fulfilment type, the till goes on writing it, `lib/fulfilment` goes on branching on it, and every counter error code keeps its slot and its sentence in both forms' catalogues — the endpoint can still answer with them, to the till. This is a change to one picker, not to what a counter sale is. **TWO BRANCHES ARE DELETED RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING.** `ordNewFulChange` opened a counter sale on Paid · Cash and put the pending defaults back on the way out; `ordNewPaintFeeNote` had a counter sentence. Neither had a way of being reached once the option and the draft path were closed, and **an unreachable branch reads as a rule the form still has**. **AN OLD DRAFT SAVED AS A COUNTER SALE COMES BACK AS A PICKUP, and that is the one behaviour an operator can walk into.** Setting a `<select>` to a value it has no option for leaves it on whatever was already selected — so without a map the draft would have restored as a **DELIVERY**, silently acquiring an address requirement it was never written with. Pickup is the honest neighbour: nothing ships, the customer collects at a store, and the address block stays absent exactly as it was when the draft was saved. The status and pay method the operator had chosen are restored on top, untouched. **The draft's stored payload is NOT rewritten** — this is a reading of an old draft, not an edit to it. **NO CHINESE IS MINTED OR TOUCHED.** The option's own pair leaves with it; every counter sentence in both catalogues stays exactly as it is, because the till can still cause every one of them. **No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. NO SIGNPOST WAS ADDED and that is a decision rather than an omission**: a caption pointing at the till would have had to carry two bilingual pairs inside one element, which is precisely the shape `check-i18n-banners.js` exists to refuse, and the till is already a rail row on this screen. **FOUR ASSERTIONS WERE RE-SCOPED, NOT RELAXED, and the replacements were PROVEN RED against the pre-change source** — checked by reverting both files and re-running, not assumed. The counter-defaults assertion is replaced by three that hold more: the picker offers exactly delivery and pickup; neither remaining fulfilment writes the status or the pay method; and `counter` is still a server type, asserted through `lib/fulfilment` itself. The address-block and hand-picked-fulfilment rows drop their counter case, the latter keeping the case that still exists. **The draft map is EVALUATED, not described** — the mapping expression is lifted out and run over all three inputs — while the wiring around it is read, because `ordNewRestore` drives a dozen DOM nodes and two async pickers and a harness for it would test the stubs. What the source is held to is that **no read of the raw stored fulfilment survives outside that one expression**, which is exactly how the bug would come back; counted with the mapping line removed rather than as a total, so a harmless rewrite of the expression does not go red. `npm run test:fast` 198/198 green on `120f278`; `verify-fulfilment-types.js` 321 → 329. No schema, no migration, no server change at all — this is one `<option>`, two dead branches and a draft map. No change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-10 · v4.206 — **§93 DECIDED: THE COUNTER TAKES POINTS AND WALLET BALANCE, AND THE NEW ORDER BUTTON STAYS — asked for by Ash**: *"maybe better remove the new order button and just use the till with some extra improvment that we need already anyway, like pay with points, banace etc..."* **THE DELETION HALF WAS SURVEYED AND ANSWERED NO, WITH THE OVERLAP NARROWED INSTEAD.** The till is a cashier screen — one store, tap-to-add, always paid, always `channel: 'shop'` — and the New order page is an order-authoring page: delivery addresses with zone-driven fees, unpaid orders with a pay link, wholesale, drafts, notes, a grand-total override. **Removing it would have removed the ability to take a phone order.** The two surfaces overlap in exactly one row, New order's Fulfilment = "Counter sale", and that row leaves in its own PR. **THE FEATURE HALF TURNED OUT TO BE A HOLE.** `POST /api/retail-admin/orders` has listed `'points'` and `'balance'` in `ALLOWED_PAY` since the off-app tenders landed **and touched neither ledger** — so an order could be filed as paid in points with the balance untouched, and `markOrderPaid` would then award earn-points on top. **It had never happened only because no screen offered the values**, which is why this is a feature and not an incident; the fix also makes the word have to be earned, refusing a credit tender on a bill credit did not settle. **THE RULE IS THE CHECKOUT'S, LIFTED**: `manualOrderCredit` calls the same `pointsRedeemableBase` / `pointsRequiredFor` / `pointsCashValue` / `walletSpendForOrder` / `sweepExpiredPoints` the customer path redeems through, in the same order — points first, because they expire and a wallet does not. **`points_to_use` IS A REQUEST**: the till sends the whole balance and the server clamps it to what the order can absorb, so the till never re-implements `points.redeemRate`; asking for more than the customer HAS is refused instead, because that means a stale screen and charging the difference silently is the failure `insufficient_points` exists to prevent. **A SECOND CEILING IS NEW AND THE CHECKOUT HAS NO NEED OF IT** — the bill actually due, because this route has a grand-total override, and without it an order overridden to ¥5 would redeem against the ¥50 of goods behind it. Balance is capped again at the bill less shipping, with no switch: store credit never pays carriage. **DECIDED BEFORE THE TRANSACTION, SPENT INSIDE IT**, on the same conditional UPDATEs, so two tills cannot both spend one balance; a lost floor check throws, rolls the order back and answers 409 rather than clamping. **THE TENDERS ARE STORED BESIDE THE CASH** (`points_used`, `points_amount`, `balance_used`) so `splitRefundAcrossTenders` returns each refunded ¥ where it came from — folding them into `total` would have made every refund all-cash. **AT THE TILL: two checkboxes, both off on every sale** (defaulting to "spend everything" burns a balance somebody was saving, one tap from done), square indicators because they are independent where the wallets are a radio group, each row carrying its own figure. **THE WALLET PICKER DISAPPEARS WHEN NOTHING IS LEFT TO TAKE, narrowing the counter-sale wallet rule rather than breaking it**: no terminal was touched, so the order names `'points'` or `'balance'` — every ¥ of CASH still names the wallet that took it. **The done screen prints the SALE, not the residual**, since a bill settled entirely in points shows ¥0.00 and reads as a giveaway. **NOT OFFERED ON A RECALLED QR ORDER**, because a recall PATCHes status only and credit chosen there would be charged and never deducted — a control that silently does nothing is worse than none. **THE TILL MINTS NOTHING — the rows reuse its own locked `points` / `wallet` / `total` pairs and every other value is a numeral — BUT THE SERVER'S FOUR NEW REFUSALS DO**, and that was not foreseen: both order forms are gated by suites requiring every code the endpoint can answer with to have a slot and a sentence, and neither form can even cause these. Two are quoted (`insufficient_points` from the admin's shared catalogue, `insufficient_balance` from the pair the storefront and mini app already ship); **two are composed under Rule 4's standing delegation and declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`** with rejected candidates, every content word checked live in the tree — `未付清` was the natural phrase and appears in zero files. Separately, two comments in `till.html` quoted Chinese to illustrate a rendered row, which that file's house rule forbids in comments too; both were rewritten. **HELD BY A SUITE PROVEN RED IN BOTH HALVES**: `scripts/test_till_credit.js` exercises the helper and then **lifts the real handler and drives it**, asserting the balances actually move, both ledger rows are written, the residual is charged and a refusal writes nothing. The mutation is a function because the file lifts the helper twice — mutating one lift left eleven end-to-end assertions green against a helper returning nothing — and its first anchor fired on `sweepExpiredPoints`, reporting a mutation that had taken as failed. **ONE ASSERTION RE-SCOPED, NOT RELAXED**: `verify-fulfilment-types.js` pinned the literal text of the till's settle gate and went red for a change that made it more careful; it now LIFTS AND RUNS the gate over four rows, and a `ready` returning true satisfies none of them. **THREE SECTION NUMBERS WERE BURNED GETTING HERE and it is worth recording why**: §90, §91 and §92 were each taken by concurrent sessions between this work starting and its commit — two of them discovered only because their strings or their entries had already reached `main` while their sections had not. Checking the section heading list alone is not enough; grep the whole of both documents. `npm run test:fast` 198/198 green on `546fc48` (`test_till_credit.js` new at 40, `verify-fulfilment-types.js` 317 → 321, `test_phone_order.js` 124, `test_tax.js` 145 and `test_tx_conversion_manual_order.js` 14 unchanged once both lift the real helper rather than a stub); `test_till_back.js` run individually, green. 2026-09-10 · v4.205 — **§92 DECIDED: THE LEDGER ROW SAYS WHO PUT IT IN THE BOOKS — asked for by Ash** off the live Transactions screen, one line: *"why it doesn't show the user name that post this?"*, against the ¥200 `Asher · personal` claim row. **THE NAME HE WAS LOOKING AT WAS THE SPENDER'S, NOT THE POSTER'S, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CONFUSION.** §87 (v4.196, merged that morning) put the spender in the DESCRIPTION — `Asher · personal` is who spent ¥200 and the note they typed — while `expense_entries.created_by` has meant *who put this row in the books* since the table existed, and on a claim row `postClaim` writes `decided_by` into it deliberately. **BOTH FACTS WERE ALREADY IN THE DATABASE ON EVERY ROW; ONE OF THEM HAD NEVER BEEN READ BY ANYTHING.** `routes/finance-transactions.js` selected `description` and not `created_by`, the row payload carried no such field, the screen had nowhere to draw it, and even the CSV's `Entered by` column named a MECHANISM (`Purchasing` / `Staff claim` / `Entered by hand`) rather than a person. **SO THIS IS NOT A NEW FACT BEING RECORDED — IT IS A RECORDED FACT REACHING A READER**, which is why there is no migration and no new column and why it is true of every row already in the books. **RESOLVED AT READ TIME, AND v4.196 REJECTED EXACTLY THAT FOR THE OTHER NAME** — recorded there as "the more robust mechanism… it reaches every existing row and follows a later rename", rejected only because v4.190 had placed the SPENDER in the description where the poster snapshots it, so resolving it again at read would print it twice. **NEITHER OBJECTION REACHES THIS NAME**: nothing snapshots the approver, so there is nothing to print twice; and read-time is what makes the answer true of the rows Ash was actually looking at rather than only of rows written from now on. Approving somebody else's spending and typing a row are two different acts by two different people — one of them an exercise of authority §87 built a whole capability around — and a single label over both would flatten an approval into a piece of typing. **A PO ROW IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNNAMED**: one PO row on this screen is a COLLAPSE of several `expense_entries` rows whose posters can differ, so naming it means picking one arbitrarily; it keeps `Posted by Purchasing`, which is the true answer for a row nobody typed, and the CSV cell is empty for the same reason. **A NAME THAT DOES NOT RESOLVE RENDERS NOTHING** — §1.12 prefers an empty cell to an invented one, and the live `Someone · 未知` belongs to the approvals queue where the name is the column's whole purpose. **THE LOOKUP BECAME A FILE, `lib/user-names.js`, AND THAT IS v4.196's OWN ARGUMENT APPLIED TWICE**: it held that ONE lookup is what stops the name on the approver's screen and the name in the books from drifting, "a second lookup shaped slightly differently is the whole mechanism by which they would". Relaxing the assertion to let the route reach the global handle would have been the same edit that makes the next real instance invisible. **ONE READ FOR THE WHOLE PAGE**, ids collected across all three lists before the list is built — a per-row lookup over a 2,000-row window is 2,000 cross-handle queries to print a handful of distinct names. Two composed pairs, declared under Rule 4 in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.52; both are built from words already live on this feature (`审批` from `待审批`/`审批通过`, `录入` from `可录入交易`, the `人` suffix from the queue's own `申请人`). `npm run test:fast` green, `test_finance_transactions.js` 50 → 61 assertions, plus `test_staff_expenses.js` and `test_finance_approvals.js` green on the shared lookup. **No schema, no migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.** The breakdown's third-level rows (`finCatRow`) are deliberately NOT given the name — that surface is a dense figure inside an opened category, not the ledger an operator works — and this is recorded so a later reader finds a decision rather than an omission. **WRITTEN AS §91 AND v4.204, RENUMBERED TO §92 AND v4.205 ON REBASE** — both numbers were taken on main while this branch sat open, by PR #477's *the approval queue is brought into line with the rulebook*. Per this file's numbering rule nothing was renumbered to make room: main's §91 is live and keeps its number, and this section took the next free one. 2026-09-10 · v4.197 — **§88 DECIDED: A LINE OF THE EXPENSE BREAKDOWN OPENS ONTO THE ROWS BEHIND IT — asked for by Ash** off the live Summary card: *"there should be an option to click on each category and see details payment break down."* **THE CHEAP BUILD WAS REJECTED BEFORE IT WAS STARTED, and the reason is the whole of this decision.** Sending the operator to the Transactions tab filtered to that category would have shown a SMALLER NUMBER than the line they tapped: `readTransactions` collapses PO-derived rows to one per purchase order — a purchase order buys several categories at once, so the collapsed row carries `category: null` and no category filter can match it — and it windows those rows on the PO's own date rather than the expense row's. PO rows are listed individually; PO-0050 twice in one category is one purchase that bought it on two lines. **THE MATCH IS ON RAW TEXT AND DELIBERATELY NOT ON `spacingKey`**: the breakdown groups by the column as stored, so the two live spellings of the ingredients category are TWO lines on the card, and a detail read keyed on `spacingKey` would gather both under either line and overshoot. §87's flag resolution matches on `spacingKey` and this does not — the rule is *match what the `GROUP BY` grouped*, and the two are different questions. **ONE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FIXED IN PASSING AND CALLED OUT**: SQLite groups `''` and `NULL` apart while the payload maps both to `null`, so a tenant holding one of each rendered TWO identical "Not recorded" lines with different figures. `NULLIF(category, '')` folds them; `TRIM` was rejected because it would merge ` Ingredients` onto `Ingredients` and decide a question about typography that `lib/category-text.js` refuses to. **NO ROW CEILING, and that is a decision**: a capped list is a list that does not add up, which is the one guarantee this endpoint makes. The category is read off the ROW, never accepted from the request. **BILLABLE QUANTITY, NEVER `qty`** — `billableQtySql` from `lib/po-returns.js`, referenced not restated, because a reader using `qty` prices a returned item at what it cost before it went back: the fixture bills 8 of 10 gift boxes at ¥80 and drops a fully returned line out of the list entirely, both of which is what the figure above already did. **THE BLANK-CATEGORY FALLBACK DIFFERS BY REALM AND IS RESOLVED PER ROW IN SQL** from `purchase_orders.scope`: a line with no category posts as `门店进货 Retail stock` from `postRetailPOExpenses` and `未分类 Uncategorized` from `postPOExpenses`, both realms write into this one ledger, and binding either label across a mixed read files the other's lines under a name they were never posted with. **THE TWO LITERALS ARE COPIED INTO THE READER, WHICH THIS FILE NORMALLY FORBIDS, AND THE TRADE IS STATED**: lifting them into a shared module means editing two posters that WRITE MONEY inside a change that only reads, so they are copied and pinned by a test that reads both shipped posters and fails if either string moves. If a third poster appears, lift them properly. **THE LANDED-COST ROW GETS NO CHEVRON.** Freight, tax and handling post as their own expense row against the order with no `po_line_items` behind them, so the server counts the lines and the client draws a control only where there is one — this screen's existing rule, that a chevron opening onto nothing is a control that lies, applied rather than restated. **ONE BUG CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE**: the first draft rendered the unit cost with `finMoney`, which renders whole units — correct for a period total and A LIE ABOUT A PRICE. A ¥3.50 jar drew as **¥4**. `01-core.js` already states the rule — *"anywhere an operator might reconcile the number against something… uses acMoney and shows the real amount"* — so the inline arithmetic is `acMoney` while the ALIGNED COLUMN stays `finMoney` at all three levels, that column being the staircase's own and its magnitude §36's decision. For the same reason the payload no longer passes a unit cost through `fen()`: a price can be sub-cent, and rounding it server-side would destroy the value to save nothing. **ROUNDING IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED**: the poster rounds once over the group (audit I-02), `lines_total` is computed the same way and equals the posted figure exactly — asserted — while per-line display rounding can differ by a cent on a three-decimal price; allocating the total across the lines with `splitMinor` was REJECTED because it would print a price the supplier never charged, and a line's truth is quantity times unit cost. **NO NEW CHINESE for the third time** — the three state sentences are the pairs already live on the two levels above, and the item name is two columns picked by language with a fallback across, the house pattern for bilingual DATA (`tmStoreLabel`) and NOT `finCatLabel`, which splits one glued free-text value. **ONE TEST RE-BOUNDED**: v4.197's own one-read assertion sliced to the end of the route file, which a third route breaks; each handler is now held to one read of `expense_entries` separately, and the new one is held to deciding no split at all. `npm run test:fast` 197/197 green; `test_finance_summary.js` 51 → 63, `test_finance_categories.js` 28 → 29. Verified end to end over HTTP: all three levels reconcile, the fees row draws no control, a non-PO id 404s and a missing id 400s. No schema, no migration, no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-10 · v4.198 — **§89 ADDED: MONEY IN IS LISTED FROM THE BEGINNING AND SUMMED FROM 1 AUGUST 2026 — DECIDED by Ash under an explicit in-session delegation, on measurements taken read-only against production.** **§55's open collision is closed, and the figure it names is corrected first**: it says ¥151,895.69 and two Mini App rows; the live ledger holds ELEVEN month-end per-channel rows totalling **¥224,591.68**, across Mini App, Meituan (Yuexiu and Tianhe), Eleme (Yuexiu and Tianhe), Gzgrocery and Manual Order — CLAUDE.md's finding-is-not-the-extent rule landing on a money figure. **BOTH SIMPLE ANSWERS WERE PROPOSED BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT AND BOTH WERE WRONG.** June: 169 orders / ¥38,767.35 against ¥118,140.07 of ledger (3.05×). July: 445 orders / ¥74,825.44 against ¥106,451.61 (1.42×), and for Meituan and Gzgrocery the ORDER RECORD NOW EXCEEDS THE LEDGER — correctly, an order total being gross where a payout is net. So excluding the rows discards ~¥79,000 of real June trading the order record never captured, and summing them double-counts most of July. **June and July are a migration in progress, overlapping by an amount no arithmetic recovers.** **THE RULING IS A FLOOR ON SUMMING AND ONLY ON SUMMING**: rows before 2026-08-01 contribute zero to any total, Net or AI figure; **the LIST stays unfloored and §36's *Finance is not floored at the cutover date* is untouched** — a floor on a summand and a floor on a list are different things, and §36's own reason argues for displaying these rows, not for adding them. The date is read off the data, not chosen: the ledger's last row is 31 July and the order record runs complete from 1 August. A floored total must SAY SO on screen; a silently reduced total is the failure the ruling exists to prevent. **REJECTED: backfilling `income_entries.channel`** (all 26 live rows are NULL) — a flag would encode a per-row judgement that June does not support at any granularity, making an unmeasurable thing look measured. **REJECTED: matching ledger rows to orders** — one month-end net figure against hundreds of gross rows, mostly absent in June, is a matcher inventing its answer. **§55's Eleme survey question is CLOSED and revenue is NOT short today**: Eleme is live in `retail_orders` from 2026-08-31, 12 orders, ¥1,520.38. **TWO NEW OPEN ITEMS ARE RECORDED WHERE THEY WERE FOUND**: the `shop` channel has produced 38 orders and ZERO revenue (6–8 September, all cancelled, ¥2,065.00) while every other channel converts; and Meituan fell 97% across the cutover (158 → 38 → 5 paid orders) while wechat and gzgrocery grew. Neither is ruled on. **No figure on any screen moves**: `routes/finance-summary.js` has never read `income_entries`. Docs only — no code, no schema, no routes. Two read-only diagnostics back it, `diagnose_income_ledger_overlap.js` and `diagnose_channel_order_presence.js`. Appended as §89 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays §38. **WRITTEN AS §88 AND RENUMBERED TO §89 ON MERGE, 2026-09-10 — the FIFTH collision of this kind recorded in this file**, after the two branches that each defined a §39, after §46/§47, and after the §52-54 → §55-57 move. It arose the way every one of them did: two branches open at once, each taking what was the next free number when it was written. PR #459's *a line of the breakdown opens onto the rows behind it* reached main first and keeps §88; nothing was renumbered to make room and no live section moved. The version moved with it, v4.197 having been taken by that same PR. **AND THE HEADER LINE MERGED WITHOUT A CONFLICT, which is exactly the failure `doc-numbering.yml` was written to catch**: both branches changed it to the same bytes — `v4.197` — and a three-way merge reads identical text as agreement. The section bodies conflicted and the version silently did not; only a check against the MERGE ref sees that, which is why that workflow runs on `pull_request` rather than against a branch head. The ruling is untouched in substance. 2026-09-10 · v4.195 — **§87 FIXED: ONE LANGUAGE ON SCREEN, AND A RECEIPT THAT ALREADY EXISTS.** Two reports from Ash off the live screen. **THE ENGLISH SURFACE WAS RENDERING BOTH LANGUAGES** — `Logistics&Delivery 物流与配送费用` — because a category is DATA and not a locked pair: `T()` reaches every other string on that screen, while the category is a value the tenant typed, held as ONE free-text column with both halves glued in (§36). **The desktop solved this on 2026-09-02 and the phone never got it**, the claim screen having been written months later and reaching for the value directly. `finCatSplit`/`finCatLabel`/`finCatLabels` are PORTED, not re-derived, and the suite now **runs the phone's copy and the desktop's over the same values and asserts they agree**, so the two cannot drift. **FIVE RENDER SITES, NOT ONE** — CLAUDE.md's rule that a finding is where it was found rather than the extent of the problem, applied literally: the collapsed row, the picker, the receipt, the submitter's list and the approver's queue all drew the raw value. **THE SEARCH STILL READS THE STORED VALUE**, so `物流` and `logistics` both find the row; searching the rendered half would make half the vocabulary unreachable in each language, a worse bug than the one being fixed. **THE COLLISION RULE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL HERE**: the live list holds `Marketing&Promotion 市场推广费用` beside `营销 Marketing`, and both render whole rather than as two rows nobody can tell apart. **A STORE NAME FOLLOWS THE LANGUAGE TOO** — the Shop chips shipped as `name_cn || name_en`, Chinese on an English screen for any store named in both, with the fallback ACROSS kept so a store named once shows its name rather than a number. **AND THE PHOTO CAN COME FROM THE GALLERY**: the file input carried `capture="environment"`, which makes Android open the camera and offer nothing else — so a receipt already photographed, screenshotted or sent by a supplier could not be attached at all, which is most of them. `accept="image/*"` is what keeps the chooser to pictures. `npm run test:fast` 195/195; the suite reaches 64 assertions. No new Chinese: every string here is a value the tenant already owns. No change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-10 · v4.194 — **§87 AMENDED: THE CATEGORY CONTROL IS A SEARCHABLE PICKER, NOT A WALL OF CHIPS — DECIDED by Ash** from the live screen: thirty-one categories as chips, alphabetical, the amount field pushed off the top. Given three options in `reference/expense-category-picker-mockup.html`, he chose **B**, a collapsed field opening a picker with **this person's own recent categories on top**. **THE LAYOUT WAS THE SYMPTOM; THE CAUSE IS THAT THE PHONE WAS HANDED THE BOOKKEEPER'S LIST** — step two offered every active `kind='accounting'` category on the reasoning that the tenant's own list is the right list, which is true of Finance and false of a phone: rent, wages, social insurance, electricity and ingredients are real costs that **nobody raises out of their own pocket**. **WHY B RATHER THAN THIS SESSION'S OWN RECOMMENDATION (A, a per-category *offer on the phone* tick)**: A needs the shop to curate a second list and keep curating it, and a category added later is invisible on the phone until somebody remembers to tick it — a silent failure on the screen where silence means an expense filed under the wrong name or not at all. B maintains nothing and is correct at thirty-one categories or three hundred. **A is NOT withdrawn**: it narrows what the picker offers and can land later without undoing this. **WHAT B DOES NOT FIX, recorded so it is not read as fixed**: every category stays reachable, so a driver can still file a taxi under Salaries if they set out to — that is a curation problem and A is its answer. **RECENTS ARE THE PERSON'S OWN AND NEVER THE SHOP'S**: a driver and an office manager do not want the same six, and a shop-wide most-used would hand the driver whatever the office manager files most. **THE SEARCH BOX FOLLOWS THE RULE #437 AND ITS FOLLOW-UP ESTABLISHED** — `oninput` stores the query and repaints ONLY the results box, never the app, because `render()` rebuilds the `<input>` and a rebuilt field reopens the soft keyboard on its letter page; a new box calling `render()` would be the fifth instance of a defect four screens were just repaired for. **TWO DUPLICATE PAIRS RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON**: the live list holds `Marketing&Promotion 市场推广费用` beside `营销 Marketing`, and the two spellings of `低值易耗品`. Each splits the monthly breakdown into two lines that read alike — §36's three-rent-payments defect arriving through the vocabulary rather than a typo — and hiding one of each is fifteen seconds on the Categories screen, but WHICH spelling survives is a decision about the shop's books and is the tenant's.

2026-09-10 · v4.193 — **FOUR MORE PLACES PUBLISHED THE BARE SHELF, AND ONE OF THEM CLOSED THE WINDOW ON A LIVE MORNING. No new section: §85 enforced against the enqueues it missed.** Found by reading production during the first batch morning, not by a test: gzgrocery was carrying shelf + allowance at 07:05 and was back to the bare shelf by 07:23. **The cause was `enqueueCurrentStock` in `scripts/guanyi-daemon.js`** — the healer that re-asserts our numbers after a session recovery or a drift — which read `COALESCE(physical_qty, 0)` straight out of the table and queued it. Every heal and every resync therefore re-published the shelf and quietly withdrew the morning's pre-orders, on a timer, from the component whose job is keeping the channel honest. **§85 TAUGHT THE SWEEPS AND MISSED THE ENQUEUES THAT LIVE OUTSIDE `lib/*-sync.js`.** Three more had the same shape and are fixed with it: `routes/guanyi-admin.js` and `routes/meituan-admin.js`'s "push all" buttons, where an operator's click would have closed an open window by hand, and `lib/store-close.js`'s sweep, where a close and reopen would have done the same. All four now go through `channel-publish.publishableAt`, which is the whole point of that module existing. **WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE ORIGINAL CHANGE**: §85 found the enqueues by following `bundleStock.sellableAt`, and the one that mattered most did not call it — it read the column. A grep for the FUNCTION found three call sites; a grep for the TABLE would have found four more. **PROVED**: `scripts/test_preorder_window.js` grows two cases that walk all four files by name and assert both halves — that each publishes through `channel-publish` for its own channel, and that the healer no longer mentions `physical_qty` at all. `npm run test:fast` 194 passed, 0 failed. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no new strings, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.


2026-09-09 · v4.191 — **§87 STEP FOUR BUILT: SETTLEMENT, AND THE SECTION IS COMPLETE END TO END.** `POST /staff-expenses/:id/settle` writes ONE column and **posts nothing** — the ¥38 was recorded once, at approval, and a second row for the repayment would report ¥76 of taxis; the suite asserts the handler touches `expense_entries` in no way at all. **WHAT IT IS FOR is a question the ledger cannot answer**: the books know the shop spent ¥38 on transport, not that the ¥38 is still in a driver's pocket. **THE ROW IS A PERSON, NOT A CLAIM**, because that is how it is paid — one transfer, not four taps — so the owed total carries the claim ids behind it and the phone settles them SEQUENTIALLY, four writes racing on a shop's wifi being how two of them land. **THE OWED FIGURE IS COUNTED OVER EVERY CLAIM AND NOT THE QUEUE'S 200-ROW PAGE**: a debt does not stop existing because it fell off the end of a list, so it has its own uncapped query, and the name lookup covers everybody either half of the payload mentions — otherwise an owed person outside the queue shows a total with no name against it. **GATED ON `expenses:approve` RATHER THAN A KEY OF ITS OWN**: a third capability would gate a single toggle, be granted to the same people, and add a row to a matrix somebody has to understand — and saying "we have paid Wei back" is an assertion about money by the person who already decides money on this screen. If it ever belongs to a bookkeeper who is not an approver, that is when the key earns its place. **ONLY A DEBT CAN BE SETTLED, WITH TWO SEPARATE REFUSALS**: an unapproved claim might still be rejected, and a company-account one owes nobody; a shared message would send an operator hunting a permission problem that is not there. **UN-SETTLING EXISTS BECAUSE THE UN-APPROVE REFUSAL DEPENDS ON IT** — step three refuses to un-approve a settled claim, so one marked paid by mistake would be stuck for good otherwise. Both directions are logged. Nine composed pairs in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.48, completing a SET OF THREE lines meant to be read together — not in the accounts yet / approving records it / paying it back changes nothing — the third being the least obvious and therefore the one that had to exist. **`报销` REJECTED A SECOND TIME**, on the very button v1.46 reserved it for: `标记已付` says what the control does, while `报销` would suggest this app pays the money out. `npm run test:fast` 193/193; the suite reaches 47 assertions. **§87 is now built end to end — a category list, a claim, an approval that posts, and a debt that clears** — with OCR prefill, recurring expenses, per-role limits and multi-step approval deliberately unbuilt and named as such. No change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-09 · v4.190 — **§87 STEP THREE BUILT: THE APPROVAL LIST, THE POSTING STEP, AND THE MONEY REACHES THE BOOKS.** `lib/expense-posting.js` posts; the queue and the decide route are in `routes/staff-expenses.js`; the screen is **Approvals** on `/m`. **IT IS ON THE PHONE RATHER THAN IN THE BACK OFFICE, and that is a choice**: the person approving a ¥38 taxi is a manager standing in a shop, and §81 is the long record of what happens when the people who do a job have no login for the screen that does it — the back office still reads the money, because the posted rows appear on Transactions the moment they are approved. **POSTING IS `postRetailPOExpenses`'s SHAPE**: delete every `expense_entries` row carrying the claim's id, insert from the document as it now stands. So approving twice RE-POSTS rather than double-posting, and rejecting after approving REMOVES the row — §36 decided a hand-typed row is freely deletable because mistakes here are typos, and an accidental approval is that kind of mistake; an offsetting entry turns a two-row ledger into four nobody can read. **THE STATUS AND THE ROW MOVE IN ONE TRANSACTION**, and the post reads the claim AFTER the update rather than the copy loaded before it: a claim that says approved with nothing behind it is a discrepancy nobody finds until the month does not add up. **`created_by` ON THE POSTED ROW IS THE APPROVER, NOT THE SPENDER** — that column has always meant who put this in the books — and WHO SPENT IT IS IN THE DESCRIPTION, because a ¥38 line with no supplier, no invoice and no purchase order behind it is answerable months later only if it says whose taxi it was. **THE TRAP §87 NAMED IN ADVANCE IS CLOSED**: `readTransactions` selected hand-typed money out with `po_id IS NULL`, which a claim-posted row satisfies — it would have rendered as freely editable and the edit would have been undone by the next decision. The predicate is now `po_id IS NULL AND claim_id IS NULL`; `loadTyped` refuses a claim row with its own wording (the PO pair with one noun swapped, because it is the same refusal for the same reason); the screen tints it, marks it **Staff claim** with `· own money` where that is what it was, and drops the Edit link. The client's `row.source !== 'po'` became `=== 'manual'`: with one projection those read alike, with two the negation is the bug. **`store_id` LANDS ON `expense_entries`, NOTHING IS BACKFILLED, and §36's open column is closed** — every existing row is NULL, which is what those rows always meant. **The Summary's store filter is NOT built here**; it stays §36's, Contribution rule included. What this step owed it was the column. **ONE EXCEPTION TO THE FAIL-OPEN CONTRACT, and it is the only one in the feature**: cap-routes gates mutations only where `rbac_enforce` is on, which is off by default, so on this route falling open would mean anybody who can raise a claim may approve their own on every tenant. `requireApprover` refuses in the route as well — including when the capability set cannot be resolved, because a money route does not fall open on an unanswered question — and the `/decide` rule sits ABOVE the general one, since below it every submitter would be an approver. **`expenses:approve` IS REGISTERED NOW THAT IT GATES SOMETHING**, carries `money: 'moves'` where its submitting sibling carries no marker, and is in NO floor preset: owner, admin and manager hold it because those presets are the whole registry, and every other role is ticked on by an owner who has decided that this manager approves spending. **SELF-APPROVAL IS ALLOWED AND MARKED** — the row says `本人提交` rather than the button refusing, and the activity log records whether a decision was on the approver's own claim. **A SETTLED CLAIM CAN NO LONGER BE UN-APPROVED** (409): money has changed hands outside this system, and reversing the expense would leave the payment made and the cost unrecorded. 2026-09-09 · v4.187 — **§87 ADDED: WHAT AN EMPLOYEE SPENDS IS A CLAIM UNTIL SOMEONE APPROVES IT; ONLY THEN IS IT AN EXPENSE — DECIDED by Ash**, who was given two readings of where a submitted expense lives and chose **B**: a claim table of its own, with **nothing in the books until approval**, rather than a status column on `expense_entries`. Three further answers settle the rest: **a shop column on the expense**, **an operating / non-operating flag on the tenant's expense categories**, and **an approver may approve their own claim**. The cases that opened it are his: an owner taking a private transfer, a driver paying a taxi on a work run, and small irregular staff spending that today reaches the month only if somebody remembers to type it. **MOST OF THIS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NOT BUILT HERE**: the ledger (`expense_entries`, `schema.sql:272` on this date, `payment_method` and `updated_at` added by migration at `database.js:1152`/`:1160`), the window sum and category breakdown (`routes/finance-summary.js`), the typed write surface and bookkeeper's CSV (`routes/finance-transactions.js`), the category normaliser (`storeCategory`, `lib/category-text.js:153`), the staff phone app whose `screenWaste()` is the precedent for recording something small and attributable in seconds, and receipt reading (`lib/alipay-ocr.js`). **WHAT WAS MISSING IS FOUR THINGS**: no door (every finance write is `requireRetailAdmin` and there is no finance screen on `/m` at all); **no tenant-managed category list, the thing asked for by name** — the admin category CRUD in `routes/retail.js` serves `kind='product'` only, nothing seeds or writes `kind='accounting'`, and the expense form derives its suggestions from the categories already on rows on screen, **so the list is the accumulated history of what people typed and the first typo is a permanent option**; no way to say the business OWES an employee (`created_by` is who typed the row, not who was out of pocket); and no location. **WHY B**: under a status column the ¥38 taxi submitted on Monday sits in the ledger while unapproved, and the Summary's operating sum, its breakdown, the Transactions list and the CSV must each remember to exclude it — **miss one and unapproved money is in the accounts, silently** — while rejected claims stay as rows every future query steps around. Under B it is not in the ledger and cannot appear; on approval ONE row posts carrying `claim_id`, **on the `po_id` projection pattern the purchase orders already use**, and the posted row refuses edit in the ledger for the reason a PO row does. **ONE INTEGRATION TRAP IS NAMED NOW**: `readTransactions` selects hand-typed money out with `WHERE po_id IS NULL`, which a claim-posted row satisfies — it would render as freely editable and the edit would be undone by the next re-post, so the predicate becomes "no `po_id` AND no `claim_id`", an edit to a shipped file. **THE CATEGORY LIST STILL SHIPS EMPTY** — §36's no-defaults rule is unchanged, an empty list cannot offer a wrong option — but each category now carries ONE FLAG, does this count as an operating expense: the owner's ¥5,000 private transfer is real money that belongs in the record and is not a cost of running the shop, and summed with rent it takes ¥5,000 off Net **with nothing on the screen looking wrong**. **A REFERENCED CATEGORY IS DEACTIVATED, NEVER DELETED** — rows store the category as TEXT and the flag lives on the record, so deleting it turns every row that named it back into an operating expense with no event to see. **The Summary must therefore SPLIT**, showing the excluded amount on its own line rather than dropping it. **§36'S OPEN COLUMN IS CLOSED**: its *An expense may carry a location* (2026-09-01) left placement and shape undecided; it is `store_id INTEGER`, nullable, on `expense_entries` and on the claim, referencing `retail_stores(id)`, defaulted from the submitter's `scopeStores`. **NULL keeps §36's meaning and nothing is backfilled** — every existing row is business-wide, which is what it always meant. **This unblocks the Summary's store filter and its CONTRIBUTION row, which stays §36's to build.** **WHO PAID reuses `payment_method`**, already a column and already a tenant-editable list (`categories` `kind='payment_method'`, seeded `database.js:898`), plus one entry it lacks: the employee's own money. **WHAT IS OWED is a settlement state on the CLAIM, not the ledger row, and paying it back POSTS NOTHING** — the ¥38 is one cost recorded once, and a system writing a row for the repayment would report ¥76 of taxis. **TWO NEW CAPABILITIES, submit and approve, and NOT `finance:record`** — that grant is money-marked and opens the whole ledger, and the staff floor presets carry no finance capability at all and withhold even `waste:costs` from the people who record waste. **SELF-APPROVAL IS ALLOWED**: in a one-manager shop the spender and the approver are the same person, and forbidding it produces an unusable screen and spending recorded outside the system rather than a second approver — **the guard is the record, not the refusal**, the approver being stored, shown, and already logged. **NOT DECIDED HERE**: where the receipt bytes live (`supplier_documents.data`'s base64-in-the-database is the precedent and receipts arrive at a different volume), OCR prefill (later, fail-soft, and a human confirms every figure), recurring expenses, per-role spending limits, and multi-step approval. **BUILD ORDER, one PR per step**: categories in Settings with the flag and the Summary split → the claim table and the phone submit screen → the approval list, the posting step, the `claim_id` predicate fix and the `store_id` column → settlement → OCR. **No Chinese is minted here**;
