2026-09-10 · v4.192 — **TODAY'S BATCH IS NOT A PRE-ORDER, AND EVERY CUSTOMER SURFACE WAS SAYING IT WAS. No new section: this is §80 being enforced against its own labels, not a new ruling.** Reported by Ash from the live mini app at 07:00 on a cooking morning — a Guangzhou address, a sold-out Quinoa Salad, and both the hero badge and the buy button reading **PRE-ORDER**: *"I can order, which is correct but why it show pre order? it shouldn't show any message like this."* **HE WAS RIGHT AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY AGREED WITH HIM IN PROSE**: `miniapp/utils/delivery.js` opens with *"PRE-ORDER is for orders we SHIP"*, and the list-row comment in `routes/retail.js` says the Guangzhou case is what lets a shopper *"see NEXT BATCH"*. **THE DEFECT IS ONE MISSING QUESTION.** When §74/§80 opened the local run to a dated fresh meal, four surfaces were taught to ask *"is there a batch date?"* and none was taught to ask *"is that date TODAY?"* — so a meal the kitchen puts on the shelf at 11:00, inside the lunch window the customer was about to pick, was labelled with the word reserved for a parcel that leaves after the next batch. **§80's ruling is that nothing is short from the customer's side while the batch is on its way; a badge saying otherwise is the same claim in a smaller font.** **THREE STATES REPLACE TWO, and only the middle one is new**: made TODAY → orderable and SILENT, no badge and an ordinary ADD TO BASKET; made LATER → orderable, `NEXT BATCH · 下批现做`, which is what the shop grid has always called that row, so the list and the page stop disagreeing; SHIPPED → `PRE-ORDER · 可预订`, untouched, because it is the right word there. **NO NEW CHINESE**: every string is already live, and the change is which of them applies. **THE TRAP THIS FIX HAD TO AVOID, and it has its own cases**: on two of the four surfaces the flag carrying the WORD is the same flag that keeps the row out of SOLD OUT (`soldOut: out && !preorder`), so the tempting one-line fix — turn the flag off to silence the badge — marks the meal sold out on the one morning it is most available. The word and the orderability are now separate values everywhere, and the suite red-proofs exactly that inversion. **THE SHOP'S CLOCK DECIDES, NEVER THE HANDSET'S (§82)**: the server ships `local_fresh_today` beside `local_fresh_date`, resolved through `toYmdLocal`, and a case asserts no client compares the date itself — a phone in another zone, or with a wrong clock, must not be what decides whether a customer is told to pre-order. **A SESSION-LEVEL INSTANCE OF THE SAME §82 MISTAKE IS RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT SHAPED THE DIAGNOSIS**: this session first told Ash the report could not be a batch morning, having read the container's UTC date (2026-09-09T23:02Z) instead of the shop's (2026-09-10 07:02 Asia/Shanghai). §82 forbids that in code; it is worth saying that prose gets it wrong the same way. **PROVED**: `scripts/test_fresh_today_label.js` is new — 16 cases running the SHIPPED `slStock` and `stockState` in a vm rather than a copy, covering all three states in both languages, the out-of-city shopper being untouched, the grocery row still plainly sold out, and the keep-it-alive inversion. `npm run test:fast` 192 passed, 0 failed. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no new strings, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-09 · v4.185 — **§85 ADDED AND BUILT: THE PRE-ORDER WINDOW REACHES THE PLATFORMS — DECIDED by Ash**, and it is the half §84 deliberately did not build. §74/§80 made a sold-out fresh meal orderable in the mini app while today's batch is still coming, §84 made what is owed visible to the kitchen, and this carries the same morning to Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery. **TWO PARAMETERS WERE ASH'S AND ARE NOT THIS SECTION'S TO CHOOSE**: a lock hour defaulting to **11:00 and adjustable** (*"let's say lock time is 11 am but it's need to be able to adjust"*), and **all three channels in scope**, gzgrocery included over this session's caution about its silent month of failed pushes (*"I have no problem with gzgrocery sync it works great"*). **THE MINI APP'S MECHANISM CANNOT BE COPIED**: there the rule works by DECLINING TO REFUSE and parking an order that holds no stock, because we own that checkout; on the platforms we own nothing but a number we push, and all three push the same one (`bundleStock.sellableAt`), so a shelf at zero is pushed as zero and the listing reads 售罄. There is no parking on a platform — an order it accepts is live, and one we cannot fill is a cancellation with a penalty. **THE RULE, IN ONE LINE: while the window is open `published = max(0, shelf + preorder_qty)`, otherwise `max(0, shelf)`, which is exactly today's behaviour.** Open means the schedule is enabled, today is a batch day, the hour is before `lock_hour`, `preorder_qty` is set and this channel is named — **any one of them missing is the off switch**, the same shape §74 chose for `ready_hour` and for the same reason: no migration, no backfill, nothing to undo. **IT CAPS ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY IT IS ONE TERM AND NOT A QUOTA MECHANISM**: each pre-order drives the shelf down by one (§84 having stopped the ingests clamping) so the published figure falls with it — 20, then 19, then 18, and at −20 it publishes 0 and the platform shows sold out. **The morning cannot sell more than the allowance and nothing has to remember how many it sold**, because the shelf already knows. **ONE NUMBER FOR EVERY PRODUCT, DELIBERATELY FOR NOW**: a per-product allowance is the better answer and is NOT built here, because the stock-layer fields it would join (`safety_buffer`, `wechat_quota`, `meituan_quota`, `restock_target`) are ALL API-only with no control anywhere in the back office, and shipping a per-product number nobody can set is worse than a blunt one they can — **recorded as the first thing to revisit**. §74's caution is restated with more force: **set `preorder_qty` only where the batch reliably covers it**, a surplus parking harmlessly in the mini app and being a cancellation on a platform. **WHERE THE CADENCE LIVES, WHICH §84 LEFT OPEN**: `nextBatchShipDate` MOVES to `lib/batch-cadence.js` and `routes/retail.js` calls it there — a move, not a copy, because §80 collapsed three copies of this rule into one so that the pill, the checkout and the order agree, and a fourth in a daemon would undo that; a daemon cannot require a 36,000-line express router to answer a date question. `lib/inventory.js` still learns nothing and §80's pinning suite is unchanged. **THE CLOSE IS EXACT, NOT SWEPT**: at `lock_hour` the figure must fall back to the shelf whether or not the batch was recorded, or a kitchen running forty minutes late leaves a platform selling food that does not exist — and the queue is edge-triggered with nothing happening at 11:00 to trigger it. The drift sweep is the backstop but runs every 30 minutes, and half an hour past a lock the operator set makes the setting a lie; **the daemons' own loops run every ten seconds**, so the flip is detected there on a config read and a comparison, with no browser, no network and no query when nothing changed. **THE OVERSELL ALARM LEARNS THE DIFFERENCE**: a pre-order against an empty shelf trips `order_oversold`, correct everywhere else and noise here, and an alert firing on every pre-order buries the one that matters — that alarm exists because 54 undeducted lines accumulated unseen from June to September. It is suppressed exactly where the window explains it (channel in the window, shortfall inside the allowance) and fires unchanged otherwise, INCLUDING for a shortfall exceeding the allowance, which is a real oversell in a pre-order's clothes. **The sync-log row is written in both cases** — suppressing the page is not forgetting, and the log is where the count is reconciled. **WHAT IS STILL NOT SOLVED, named so it is not read as done: the order that arrives one minute after the lock.** The batch is closed, the platform order is live, and it must be filled or cancelled; narrowing the window shrinks that gap and never closes it. That is the difference between a surface we own and one we do not, and the cost of being sellable there at all.

2026-09-09 · v4.184 — **§84 ADDED: THE SHELF TELLS THE TRUTH, AND WHAT IT OWES IS WHAT THE KITCHEN MAKES — DECIDED by Ash**, on the question of how §74/§80's pre-order rule reaches Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery. **IT CANNOT, AND THE REASON IS NOT THE PUSH.** Ash described the routine the rule depends on — *"in the morning when kitchen come to work they already see how many fresh meals and wraps need to be prepared and they will add those extra to the batch they are about to do"* — and the path back from the platform to the kitchen found the system does not do it. **THREE FINDINGS, ONE CAUSE**: the kitchen's morning list never reads customer orders at all (`retail_order_items` appears in none of `routes/restock.js`, `routes/retail-production.js`, `lib/kitchen-ready.js` — 厨房制作队列 renders REQUESTS somebody typed, so a night of orders with no request raised opens an EMPTY queue); the waiting-orders card counts orders rather than units and excludes all three platforms by SQL as "read-only channel mirrors"; and a platform order on an empty shelf leaves no trace of what it owes, the ingest clamping at zero and writing the shortfall to a JSON log column in a table the same file calls having "no index, no screen and nothing watching it". **So the number the kitchen would add to its batch exists NOWHERE — not as a total, not per product, not for any channel, the mini app included.** **THE RULING: the morning number is DERIVED, never typed** — Ash chose automatic when the fork was put to him, with the manual request path kept for what the orders do not cover. **AND THE NUMBER IS NOT A NEW CONCEPT: §39 ALREADY DEFINED IT.** `adjustStock` stopped flooring at zero in words this section only points at — *"Negative one is ugly but true: it says stock was sold that was never held, which really happened"* — and a platform order taken at 08:00 against an empty shelf IS that. **owed = how far the shelf has fallen below zero, plus the units on `awaiting_restock` orders**, which hold no stock by design and never dent the shelf. No new table, no forecast, no batch declared in advance, nothing parsed from a log. **THIS PAYS OFF DEBT `adjustStock` RECORDED BY NAME** — the four channel-ingest paths still computing their own `Math.max(0, …)`, called "recorded debt, per-channel work". **The Meituan and Eleme half is paid off here, at FOUR call sites rather than two** — each channel clamps once on arrival and again when a cancelled order comes back to life and is re-deducted, and a debt lost on the second path is lost as completely as one lost on the first. **GZGROCERY IS LEFT CLAMPED DELIBERATELY AND IT IS NOT AN OMISSION**: it has no order-ingest path at all, selling through the Guanyi ERP so that a sale reaches us as an OBSERVED DROP reconciled by an operator through `/guanyi/pickups/:id/apply`, on a row already flagged `capped`. A debt from a real order line is a fact; a debt from an inference that overshot is a phantom the kitchen would cook for, and gzgrocery's owed units do not arise in the first place — an ERP drop is a sale that already happened, not a promise waiting on a batch. **THE TRUTH GOES NEGATIVE; THE NUMBER WE PUBLISH DOES NOT** — `rawStockAt` returns the raw column and `sellableAt` passes it through, so the floor moves to the PUBLISH boundary, a platform being told 0 because a platform cannot hold a debt, and clamping at the ingest putting the floor on the wrong side of the fact. **HOW IT RETURNS TO A TRUE NUMBER, asked by Ash directly** (*"after it's minus eighteen, how it will go back to the right stock?"*): it corrects itself through the door the kitchen already uses — 加库存 and Log a batch both pass `deltaQty`, so −18 plus a batch of 40 is 22, no reset and nothing to clean up, and *做好一批,马上加库存* is already that door. **THE RECOUNT DOOR IS THE ONE THAT WOULD ERASE IT**: "set the new total" writes an absolute, and §46 deliberately asks nothing of an upward correction, so somebody typing 0 at a shelf of −18 wipes eighteen owed units in silence — a recount RAISING a count across zero must now acknowledge what it clears, §46's asymmetry not holding once a negative can mean a debt. **WHERE IT IS SHOWN**: above the request list in 厨房制作队列 and rendering on an EMPTY queue, which is the case it exists for; plus one row on the phone Home beside 厨房已完成. Not on 加库存 (the batch is already cooked), not on 登记批次 (that records what was made), not in the desktop back office (§81 is the long record of the kitchen having no login for it). **WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE, named so it is not read as done: the pre-order window on the three channels is the NEXT section's.** Ash has settled two of its parameters — a lock hour defaulting to 11:00 **and adjustable**, and all three channels in scope, gzgrocery included over this session's caution (*"I have no problem with gzgrocery sync it works great"*) — but publishing a forward quantity is a separate change with its own guard rails and is unsafe until the number above is visible to the kitchen. **This section makes the demand legible; it does not yet make it sellable.**

2026-09-09 · v4.182 — **§82 AND §83 ADDED: TIME IS A TENANT PROPERTY, NEVER A HOST PROPERTY; AND EVERY DISTRICT MUST BE COVERED, AN UNMATCHED ADDRESS IS REFUSED — BOTH DECIDED by Ash**, on the delivery-logic survey (`docs/surveys/delivery-logic-survey.md`). **§82 SETTLES THE QUESTION THE SURVEY COULD NOT (its Q1)**: every date and time decision — cutoffs, batch dates, slot generation, business-date rollover, "today", "tomorrow", pre-order gates — resolves in the **tenant's** timezone, read from a tenant setting, and **no business decision may read the host clock's local time** (`new Date().getHours()`, `.getFullYear()`, `.getDate()`, `.toDateString()` are forbidden wherever a cutoff, date or slot is computed). **THE HOST IS PINNED TO UTC ON PURPOSE, AND THE DEPLOY CONFIG MUST SET IT EXPLICITLY** — not for neutrality but so that un-migrated code is **visibly wrong rather than silently correct for one tenant**; a tenant offset matching the host is a coincidence, never a fallback. **A TENANT WITH NO TIMEZONE FAILS LOUDLY AT STARTUP and does not default**, a default being the host fallback in different clothes. **CI RUNS IN UTC**, so the logic cannot pass by inheriting a convenient offset — `.github/workflows/tests.yml` currently pins `TZ: Asia/Shanghai` on the belief that production runs UTC+8, and that pin is precisely what kept survey finding F2 invisible to the suite. Roots is `Asia/Shanghai`; other tenants will be elsewhere. **§83 SETTLES F1/F23**: a tenant's zone table must cover every district it serves — **coverage is a data obligation on the tenant, enforced by the platform** — and **an address matching no zone is a configuration error, not a delivery option**, refused by every order-creation path with an explicit error, identically. **NO LEGACY FEE FALLBACK, NO DEFAULT FEE, NO DEFAULT SLOT SET**, because **a guessed fee is worse than a refusal: a refusal is visible and a wrong fee is not.** The rule `/checkout/quote` already applies is the correct one and **the other paths conform to it rather than it being relaxed to match them** — which is the direction the code had drifted. **NEITHER RULING IS BUILT HERE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** §82's call sites (`routes/retail.js` — `parseYmdLocal`/`toYmdLocal`, `earliestBatchMakeDate`, `nextFreshBatchDate`, `computeDeliverySlots`, `expressEarliestIso`, `rescheduleEligibility`) are unmigrated, with `lib/business-date.js` already the shape to copy; §83's refusal is **gated on a zone-coverage report first**, since a district that has taken real orders and is missing from `retail_delivery_zones` would begin rejecting them the day the refusal ships. **The survey is amended, not rewritten** — its dated findings stand as written and gain cross-references to §82/§83, and its Q1 is marked answered. Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration, no test change, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-09 · v4.180 — **§80 ADDED AND BUILT: NOTHING IS SHORT FROM THE CUSTOMER'S SIDE WHILE THE BATCH IS ON ITS WAY — DECIDED by Ash, against §74 as shipped.** Walked through §74's own Guangzhou scenario, Ash stopped at the checkout step: *"why tell him its short? he doesnt need to wait. there is a new batch made and ready at 11, we deliver on time according to his request. am i wrong?"* **He was not, and the shipped behaviour was WORSE than the walkthrough that prompted the question.** §74 made the meal orderable and stopped there: `requiresStockGate` still read Guangzhou + same-day + an empty shelf, `analyzeShortage` still returned `options_5`, the customer still met a five-option out-of-stock modal — and the only way through it, `wait_for_restock`, **CLEARS `scheduled_for`, refunds the same-day surcharge and relabels the order *Ships when restocked*.** He asked for 12:00–14:00 and got an order with no delivery time at all. **THE RULING: while today's batch is still coming and it lands before the customer's own window CLOSES, that line is not short — no modal, and the window he picked survives.** **THE END OF THE WINDOW, NEVER ITS START, and Ash said so in one line when the design was put back to him: *"it can also be 10-12."* A batch landing at 11:00 serves a 10:00–12:00 delivery, so keying on the start hour would have refused exactly the slot he named; keying on the end also keeps the rule honest for a late ready hour, where a window CLOSING before the batch lands is correctly not covered. `'right_away'` is never covered — it names no window to close by. **WHERE THE RULE LIVES IS ITSELF A DECISION**: `lib/inventory.js` knows shelves and is NOT taught a production cadence; `routes/retail.js` resolves the covered ids beside the schedule that defines them and hands them down as `coveredProductIds`, and a suite asserts `inventory.js` never learns the words. **THE ORDER PARKS WITHOUT RESERVING, AND KEEPS ITS WINDOW.** The automatic parking path that already existed for stock-gate-OFF orders gains one arm rather than a twin — every other guard (no bundle, no stock-backed add-on, backorder lines only) applies unchanged, and with the gate ON *every* short line must be covered or the order does not park silently. The new `isBatchPark` shares `isWaitFlow`'s reservation skip (there is nothing on the shelf to hold) and deliberately does NOT share its slot-clearing: that clearing is right when nobody knows when stock lands and wrong when the schedule names the hour. `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` promotes the order the moment a cook records the batch, as before. **THREE COPIES BECAME ONE**: `todaysBatchStillComing()` now holds the four conditions that were written out in `earliestBatchMakeDate`, `nextFreshBatchDate` and the new gate — for a rule whose whole job is that the pill, the checkout and the order agree, three copies was two too many. **A DEFECT CAUGHT IN BUILD THAT LINT CANNOT SEE**: the first wiring read `quoteNow` above its own `const`, a temporal-dead-zone `ReferenceError` on **every customer's checkout quote**, with eslint reporting 0 errors. The clock is now declared once at the top of the handler and a case asserts the declaration precedes its first read. **WHAT IS STILL NOT DONE, and it is now the only thing left**: nothing caps the sell against the batch size, so a busy morning can promise more windows than the batch covers — the surplus parks rather than overselling silently, but a customer can be told a time and get the next batch. Ash chose this shape knowing that (*"i choose option a"*); the cap needs the forward production plan and is its own section. **PROVED**: `scripts/test_fresh_today_batch.js` grows to 46 cases — the 10:00–12:00 window covered, a window closing before the batch not covered, `right_away` never, the day chip yes, non-cooking day no, after the hour no, no ready hour no, a grocery line no, `slotWindowEnd` reading the zone's own duration rather than assuming two hours, and source assertions that the gate closes, that `inventory.js` stays a stock question, that the reservation is skipped, and that a batch park never reaches the slot-clearing branch. Red-proofed both ways: keying on the window's start turns the 10–12 case red, and removing the reservation skip turns its case red. `npm run test:fast` 181 passed, 0 failed; eslint 0 errors; doc-numbering PASS. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no new route, no new strings, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

2026-09-08 · v4.174 — **§74 ADDED AND BUILT: A SOLD-OUT FRESH MEAL IS ORDERABLE FOR TODAY WHILE TODAY'S BATCH IS STILL COMING.** Reported by Ash as the shape of the loss rather than a bug in a screen: the shelf empties at 17:00, a customer opens the app at 08:00 the next morning wanting lunch, the kitchen puts the batch out at 11:00, and *"he has no way to order it at 8am… the customer already ordered from a different place."* **EVERY AVAILABILITY DECISION RESOLVES TO `inventory.getAvailable`, WHICH IS A STATEMENT ABOUT NOW** — true and useless on a batch morning: it knows the shelf is empty and cannot know the kitchen is three hours from filling it, so the app said sold out and named the NEXT cooking day. **THE RULING: on a day the kitchen is scheduled to cook, before the hour the batch reaches the shelf, zero stock stops being proof that today is unreachable.** `batch.schedule` gains `ready_hour` (0–23, optional) and **its absence is the off switch** — unset, every function behaves exactly as before, for every tenant, no migration and no backfill. **ONLY THE STOCK STRAND IS UNPICKED.** `earliestBatchMakeDate` folds stock, an unresolvable store and the day's cutoff into ONE roll-forward; an unresolvable store still rolls (we cannot promise a shelf we cannot name) and the cutoff still rolls, which is also what makes a `ready_hour` set later than `cutoff_hour` harmless. New reason `today_batch_pending` — the one reason meaning *today, and not yet*. **THE PILL AND THE CHECKOUT STILL NAME ONE DAY**: `nextFreshBatchDate` takes the same exemption, its header having always committed it to the same arithmetic on the same config, or the grid would offer a meal the calendar refuses — the contradiction PR #400 had just removed from the web PDP. **THE CALENDAR IS NOT TOUCHED — RULED BY ASH** against the first build, which withdrew today's windows starting before the ready hour and withdrew "right away" with them: *"I don't think that necessary. people can pre order fresh meals and request 10-12 slot as it is now."* Redundant twice over — a window is a WINDOW, so 10:00–12:00 is honoured by a batch landing at 11:00 and withdrawing it refused an order the kitchen could serve; and the honesty it reached for is enforced a layer down and enforced better, `analyzeShortage`'s `wait_for_restock` branch CLEARING `scheduled_for`, refunding the same-day surcharge and relabelling the order *Ships when restocked*, so a parked order carries no time promise whatever window was picked, `right_away` included. The floor stays a plain date and a floor of TODAY reads as no constraint everywhere downstream. Both the quote and the order path now read ONE `localFreshFloorFor` answer instead of deriving it twice. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED (§30)**: no live pair says *made this morning, ready from 11*, so the control ships without the sentence — `computeLocalFreshNotice` still fires on `rolled_stock` ALONE and stays silent here, and the two admin labels are lifts (*Order-by hour · 当日截单* from this card's own live refusal toast, *Ready from the kitchen · 厨房已完成* verbatim from `public/m.html`). **THE BACK HALF WAS ALREADY LIVE AND IS REUSED WHOLE**: a Guangzhou same-day order that is short reaches `analyzeShortage`'s five-option modal, whose `wait_for_restock` branch parks it as `awaiting_restock` holding no stock, takes payment, and is promoted to `paid` by `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` the moment a cook records the batch — reserving only when the FULL quantity is there. **A LIVE DEFECT FOUND WHILE WIRING THE FIELD AND FIXED HERE**: `#batch-cutoff` was read by `saveBatchSchedule` and **had never existed in `public/retail-admin.html`**, and since the save REFUSES a non-numeric cutoff, the entire Fresh batches card could not be saved while the switch was on. Restored as the input rather than by relaxing the validation, which was the half that worked. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, named so it is not read as done: it does not cap the sell against the batch size.** Nothing knows forty wraps are coming — `production_batches` records what WAS made, `kitchen_orders` is an ingredient requisition — so a morning can take more orders than the batch covers. It does not oversell *silently* (the surplus parks and waits for a quantity that covers it) but a customer can be told today and get tomorrow; **until a forward production plan exists, `ready_hour` should be set only where the batch reliably covers a morning.** **PROVED**: `scripts/test_fresh_today_batch.js` is new — 31 cases, and what it protects is the NARROWNESS (the off switch, the non-cooking day, the skipped holiday, after the ready hour, the unknown store, the cutoff, the unfloored control proving the withdrawn morning is §74 talking and not the hour of day). **It caught a real defect in the first version**: without `!pastCutoff` in the condition, the date rolled to tomorrow while the reason still said `today_batch_pending`, and the floor would then have carried a morning-withdrawing hour on a future date; red-proofed by removing the term and watching the case fail; and its own source assertion for the wait branch first

2026-09-08 · v4.166 — **THE UNDO ON THE RECEIVE LINE WAS DEAD FOR AN HOUR. §70 addendum records it; the ruling it corrects is v4.164's, shipped the same hour.** Reported from the floor with a screenshot of RPO-0030, Goji Berries open on its counter, *"cant click now , not checked yet"* — the button circled in red. **§70 ruled that pressing the answer a RECORDED line already holds should open it to be corrected rather than un-answer it, and the ruling is sound; the wiring was not.** The guard went into `recvArrived`, and the only control that ever reaches `recvArrived` on an answered line is the "Not checked yet" undo — the arrived chip renders only on an UNanswered line. So the guard set `recvOpenLine` to the id it already held, the render changed nothing, and the row had no other way to close: **a dead button on the one control that row offered.** The correction path §70 named — tapping the folded row — already went straight to `recvOpenLine` and was never the thing the guard affected. **THE CHECK THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT is the one I did not make: I verified the RULE was sound and never asked which control reaches it.** The case added here presses the button through the DOM and asserts the screen MOVED, because the whole failure was a handler that ran and painted nothing. **Now: on a line not yet recorded, "Not checked yet" un-answers exactly as before. On a recorded one that sentence is no longer available to say — the receipt is written and the stock is booked — so the control becomes `Done` and folds the correction away, and the way back to nothing is the counter beside it, where a zero IS a correction and a zero does reverse the stock. It is drawn ONLY where pressing it would fold the row**; on a recorded line mid-correction there is no button rather than an inert one, which is the rule the bug earned. **A SECOND DEFECT, OLDER THAN AUTO-SAVE, FELL OUT OF THE SAME READING.** "Not checked yet" borrowed `recvArrived`'s toggle, whose first test is `on && recv > 0`; on a line answered *nothing arrived* that is false, so the press fell through to the else branch and marked the line **fully arrived** — the one control for "I have not checked this" asserting the whole order had turned up. It has its own command now, `recvUnanswer`, which says only what it does. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED**: `Done · 完成` is live six times in this file, including on this same screen (the damage panel's own Done), and is taken verbatim. **Both defects were proven to fail with the fix reverted**, each through the button rather than the command — `test_mobile_receiving.js` 163 → 171 assertions, 43 cases. `npm run test:fast` green at 176. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no server change.

2026-09-08 · v4.164 — **THE RECEIVE SCREEN SAVES ITSELF, AND ONE VISIT IS ONE DELIVERY. §70 records it.** Asked from a phone with a screenshot of a nineteen-product order: *"no need the button 'record delivery' should be auto saving"*. **The button was the last thing between a delivery somebody had counted and a delivery the system knew about**, and it sat at the foot of the list — a scroll away from the work, disabled until something was marked, on a screen where sixteen products were still unanswered. It earned nothing by being there: every per-product answer above it was already a complete statement about one product. **Every answer now schedules the write and the pause sends it (1200 ms, last tap wins), and leaving the screen — Back, or the phone going to the lock screen — spends whatever the timer was still holding.** Rejected: a write per tap (a dozen stock-and-finance passes where one belongs); rejected: writing only on the way out, which loses the delivery if the app is killed mid-count, the one failure `scripts/test_mobile_receiving.js` names at its head as unforgivable. **THE COLLISION THIS TURNED ON IS THAT A DELIVERY IS NOT A SAVE.** The Received list shows one row per receipt that brought a line for the FIRST time (`DELIVERY_SQL`), so that a person reads van-loads rather than button presses — and a screen writing on every pause would have put one van in that list as many times as the counting paused, destroying the derivation the list is built on. **So a save may now name the receipt to add its lines to**: the first write of a visit opens the delivery and answers with its id, every later write in that visit amends it, `received_at` is not touched, and a line answered twice in one visit is REPLACED on the receipt rather than listed twice — the delivery brought four, not "five, then four". Corrections ACROSS visits are still their own receipt, which is what the journal reads as a revision, and that is unchanged. **The desktop passes nothing and is untouched** — one press of Save there is one delivery, as it always was. **A named receipt that no longer qualifies opens a new one rather than refusing**, because the desk can undo a receive while the door is still counting and an extra row in the journal is a blemish where a refusal at the door is the failure above. **TWO COSTS, BOTH RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** An answer that has been recorded can no longer be un-answered by pressing its control again — clearing `qty_received` back to null would leave the booked units on the shelf, since `applyReceivedToStock` skips a null line and reverses nothing — so that press now opens the line to be CORRECTED, and `Not 40` books the zero that does reverse the stock; undo is untouched for the second or so before the pause is spent, which is where a mis-tap is caught. And a confirmed short line with no reason yet is HELD BACK rather than blocking: the server refuses the whole payload over one such line, and with no button to grey out that refusal would have stranded the twelve lines that ARE answerable behind the one that is not. **The confirmation screen is gone with the button that reached it** — it was the receipt for one deliberate save, and there is no such moment now; the summary card's eyebrow changes tense instead. **ONE CHINESE PAIR WAS COMPOSED and adds no new word** — the amber line now says the held lines are not recorded, from this screen's own existing warning plus the 「X的不会Y」 shape of Add stock's live `已登记的不会重复计入`; declared with six verbatim lifts and four deletions in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.35. **Proved by a new `scripts/test_receive_amend.js`** (26 assertions, fast shard: the amend, the replace, the desktop's unchanged behaviour, and both ways a named receipt is refused — each counted through the real deliveries endpoint rather than a `COUNT(*)` that would agree with a broken derivation) **and by four new cases in `scripts/test_mobile_receiving.js`** (163 assertions, green). `npm run test:fast` green at 176. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no new route.

2026-09-08 · v4.162 — **THE ORDER PAGE IS REGROUPED, AND LIME NOW MEANS ONE THING.
