One row now: name flexing, quantity and price travelling together at the right edge, where a receipt puts them. The basket's own `.ln` is untouched and still stacks. **THE TOTAL GAINS EDGES AND A LABEL AND KEEPS ITS SIZE.** It was a centred inline box aligned to nothing, unlabelled — so a one-line order showed the customer the same figure twice with nothing saying which was the line and which was the total. It now spans the column it totals and carries `Total · 合计`, **which is this same file's basket footer**, so the figure quoted before submitting and the figure found on return are visibly the same row. **AND THE ACCENT IS GIVEN A SINGLE MEANING, which is the one change here a customer could be misled by rather than merely annoyed at.** Lime is what must still be acted on, and it was painted on the total in every state alike — **a cancelled order showed the same bright ¥89.00 as one still waiting to be paid**, which is the page telling somebody who owes nothing to walk to a till. The status chip and the total now take their tone from one class on the wrapper, and **the tone is read off `order.status` inside `payScreen` rather than passed in beside the screen**, so a caller cannot hand the paid face the colour that means money is owed: lime for owed, ink for settled (the chip the order list already wears), olive outline for cancelled. **THE PAGE GETS A FLOOR.** The last 40% of the phone was bare oat with Back adrift in the middle of it; Back moves into a bottom rail — `flex:none`, a 2px top rule, safe-area padding — **which is the rail the product sheet already ends with**. **The cancel deliberately does NOT come with it**: it stays under the total, behind its own disclosure, and the band between them is what keeps the destructive control out of reach of the thumb resting on the safe one. **This INVERTS v4.157's reading order and the inversion is the point.** There, Back came first and the cancel last; with Back pinned to the foot of the screen the cancel now reads first and Back last. What v4.157 was actually protecting was the visual register — a bordered box against an underlined olive link, so a thumb cannot confuse them — and that is untouched. The distance between them is larger, not smaller: the destructive control used to sit immediately under a centred Back and now has most of the screen between it and the one the thumb rests on. **SCOPED TO `payScreen` ONLY, AND THAT IS A NARROWING WORTH NAMING.** Everything is an override under a new `.ordp` wrapper, never an edit to the `.done` rules. **The done sheet the customer sees the instant they submit, and §50's in-page WeChat screen, draw the same classes and are LEFT AS THEY WERE** — neither was reported and neither was in the approved mockup, so they still stack their rows and still centre. That is a real divergence between two views of one order, of exactly the kind v4.160 argued against, and it is recorded here rather than left to be discovered: **bringing them across is a separate change and should be made.** **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED AND NONE WAS NEEDED.** Every pair this layout draws is already live on this same page: `Total · 合计` and `Order · 订单号` from the basket and the order block, `Back · 返回`, `已取消`, `下单成功！`, `支付成功！`, `请到收银台付款。`. The shop's name in the bar is `shopName()`, the menu's own, so no name is written into the file. No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. **Held by the checks v4.160 and v4.157 left behind**, which is why the class names were kept rather than renamed: `test_shop_menu.js` still holds that all three faces name every line in both languages with quantity and line total, that the lines precede the amount, and that every face has a way back to this shop's menu. Code and docs; no schema, no migration, no new route, no new string and no behaviour change — a cancelled order is still cancelled and a paid one still paid.

2026-09-08 · v4.161 — **§69 ADDED: "READY FROM THE KITCHEN" COUNTS PRODUCTS, NOT REQUESTS, AND NAMES THEM ON THE ROW.** Reported by Ash from the phone, with a screenshot of the Kitchen queue on `PR-260908-005` — three lines, one of them made — and the Needs-you strip above it showing nothing: *"if only 1 product marked as made , it wont show it on dashbaord ,thats a problem , why not to mention the speicifc product kitchen made directly on the dashbaord this way the user wont need to open the order and check inside ,too many clicks"*. **ONE DEFECT AND ONE ASK, AND THEY HAVE THE SAME FIX.** §61 split the kitchen's WORK to the line and left `restock_orders.status` a ROLLUP that catches up only when every line is done — deliberately, because dispatch, the push fan-out and the slip print are all keyed on it. §66's fire, the phone's dot and the Ready list were all written against that rollup, so a request with one of three products made sat at `sent` and **every surface stayed silent about a jar already on the shelf**. Moving the grain to the line fixes that and, in the same move, gives the row something worth printing: the NAME. **A request number is the one fact about a finished jar the warehouse cannot act on**, and it was two taps down behind a row whose whole job is to save the trip. **THE STAMP HAD TO COME DOWN WITH THE COUNT** — with one `seen_at` per request, reading the news about the first product would have silenced the second — so `restock_items.seen_at` is added and **not backfilled**: `lib/kitchen-ready.js` reads `restock_orders.seen_at` ALONGSIDE it, because under the old clause an order could only be stamped once every line was done, so an acknowledged order means acknowledged lines. **NOTHING RE-LIGHTS ON THE DEPLOY**, which a swap would have done to months of read history. **THE SAME ARM SHAPE COVERS THE OTHER LEGACY GAP**: the clause reads the line's status OR the request's, because §61's backfill was main-database only and a tenant file got the columns with their plain `'sent'` default — so the new clause is a strict SUPERSET of the one it replaces rather than a different set. **THE OLD `{ids:[…]}` REQUEST SHAPE IS STILL HONOURED** on the seen endpoint and resolved to that request's own unseen lines, because a page cached on a phone before this deploy goes on sending it and the sentence it makes is as true per line as it was per request. **TWO NAMES AND AN HONEST TAIL**, on both dashboards: `.td-nmeta` truncates at a narrow width by design (a row that wraps makes the card jump every time an age ticks over), so a third name would ellipsize mid-word rather than read, and the tail counts off the COUNT rather than the 8-line preview. **The two screens the fire opens now list PRODUCTS too** — a fire that disagrees with the queue it opens means one of the two is lying, which is the rule `lib/kitchen-ready.js` exists to keep — and both detail screens stop saying *"the kitchen has put this on the shelf"* over a request that is only partly made, a state they could never be in before. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** `more · 更多` is live in `public/retail-admin/16-purchasing.js` in this exact `+N more` construction; `, · ，` is `public/m.html`'s own meta-fragment join; `made · 完成` and `To make · 待制作` are both live on the screens being edited; partial progress is stated as the numeral `1/3` rather than a clause minted for it. No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. **`scripts/test_kitchen_ready_dashboard.js` gains §2b and the naming section (51 assertions), `scripts/test_kitchen_ready_signal.js` gains the one-of-three section (42)**; the fixture now builds `restock_items` as well, because a suite holding only `restock_orders` proved nothing about a signal counted per line. Code, tests and docs; **one schema change and one migration — `restock_items.seen_at`, added and deliberately not backfilled.**

2026-09-08 · v4.160 — **THE CUSTOMER CAN SEE WHAT THEY ORDERED. No new section: this is §44 and §50 carrying out what they already say, and it decides nothing.** Reported from a phone, hours after v4.157 went live: *"qr code menu order - after order was made cusotmer cant see the order details at all, nowhere."* **AND THERE WAS NOWHERE, ON ANY SURFACE.** The lines are written to `retail_order_items` the moment a QR order is created — bilingual name, quantity, unit price and line total per row — and **no customer-facing reader ever read them back**. The order page selected the header columns only, so it could show the number, the name, the status and the amount and nothing those figures were FOR; the done sheet was handed the items in the create response and dropped them on the floor. **The customer's own basket is the third copy and it is memory only (§44), cleared on submit** — so between the three, the shop kept every line of every order and showed the customer none of them. The screen in the report is correct in every particular and answers a question nobody asked: a number, a name, an amount, an order number. **THE FIX IS A READ, NOT A FEATURE.** `orderLines()` reads the rows by `order_id` and renders them on `/s/:shopCode/pay/:token` — which reaches all three of its faces at once, because placed, paid and cancelled all render through `payScreen`, and §50's in-page WeChat screen on both of ITS faces, since a customer who dismisses WeChat's own sheet is standing on a counter screen like any other. The done sheet draws the same rows from the `items` the create response has always returned. **WHY BOTH AND NOT ONLY THE PAGE**: they are two views of one order, and a confirm screen richer or poorer than the page its bar links to is how a customer learns not to trust either. **THE ROWS ARE THE BASKET'S OWN ROW WITH THE STEPPER TAKEN OUT** — `.ln`, `.ln-t`, `.ln-r` and `.ln-p` reused rather than restyled, plus one quiet olive `.ln-q` where the stepper was, because on a placed order the quantity states a fact rather than offering a control. A placed line and a line still in the basket are the same line and must not have two layouts. **THE LINES LEAD INTO THE AMOUNT on both surfaces**, and that is the one ordering rule held by a test: a total printed above the things it totals asks the customer to read the screen backwards. (The status sub-line sits below the amount on the done sheet and above it on the order page. That predates this and is left alone — what had to agree between the two is the lines-then-figure reading, and it does.) **A FAILED ITEMS READ RENDERS NO LINES AND NOTHING ELSE CHANGES.** An order page that would not draw because the items table would not answer would cost the customer the number they are about to be called by, which is the one thing that screen exists to carry. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED, AND NONE WAS NEEDED.** `name_en` and `name_cn` are on every row, written from the menu the customer ordered from, so `bi()` has both halves of every string it draws; the quantity is a numeral and the price is a figure, and neither takes a label. **No heading over the list either** — `YOUR BASKET · 购物车` is false on a placed order and anything else would have had to be minted, so the rows sit under the customer's name and read as a receipt without one. **No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed.** **Both halves are held by checks that were proven to fail with their fix reverted**: `test_shop_menu.js` (fast shard) holds that all three faces of the order page name every line in both languages with its quantity and its line total, and that the lines precede the amount; `test_shop_menu_render.js` places a real order in Chromium and compares what the done sheet drew against `retail_order_items` row by row — that file is in the browser shard, which is not run (CLAUDE.md), so it was run individually and green. Code and tests; no schema, no migration, no new route and no new string.
2026-09-08 · v4.159 — **THE ROLE'S DASHBOARD CARDS REACH THE PHONE, AND THE ONE CARD THAT NEVER HAD A MONEY GATE GETS ONE. §67 addendum records it.** Reported with a screenshot of each side: the Roles editor for Stockroom — *"Has a dashboard"* ticked, layout **The full view**, and **Today, Customers and Unhandled orders UNTICKED** — and the phone's Home underneath it showing **Today: Revenue ¥732, Avg. order ¥222.45, New customers 10**, with *Also today* beneath it. **THE DATA WAS ON THE WIRE THE WHOLE TIME AND THE PHONE THREW IT AWAY.** `/api/backend/me` has shipped `dashboardCards` since the field existed (`routes/backend-auth.js`), and the DESKTOP has honoured it since then (`dashCardGate`, 03-dashboard.js); `public/m.html` read the same endpoint, ignored the key, and drew every card regardless. **The screen was contradicting its own control**: the Roles editor says, in its own words, that the dashboard is *"this role's first screen on desktop and the Home tab on the phone"* and that *"the layout and cards below decide what is on it"* — on the phone they decided nothing. **FOUR OF THE TEN CATALOGUE KEYS HAVE A SECTION OF THEIR OWN ON HOME and are now gated on exactly the key their desktop twin carries**: `recap` → *While you were away*, `needs` → *Needs you*, `orders` → *Today* (the desktop block headed *Today · 今日*), `customers` → *Also today* (the desktop *Customers* card, whose contents are Sessions / Conversion / Returning). **The other six — `unhandled`, `inventory`, `incoming`, `onroad`, `ready`, `delivery` — are desktop cards with NO phone twin**, because the phone surfaces those states as Needs-you fires and Quick actions; **the divergence is named rather than papered over**, and inventing a section on Home to hold a tick would be worse than the gap. **null STAYS "no override" on both surfaces** — a role whose owner never opened that field must not lose every card on the phone. **THE MONEY HALF IS WORSE THAN THE CARD HALF AND WAS FOUND WITH IT.** *Today*'s twin is hidden for the `warehouse`, `dispatch` and `customer-service` boards by `retail-admin.css`; on the phone that card carried **no money gate at all** — not even the `recapNoMoney()` one its own immediate neighbour `vitalsBlock()` already had — so a stock or delivery role read the shop's takings off the FIRST SCREEN THE APP OPENS. It now carries both gates, **in the desktop's order of precedence**: an owner's card override cannot switch the money back ON for a board that hides it (over there the override CLEARS an inline style and the board's CSS rule still wins), so either gate hiding is enough. **THE REPORTING ACCOUNT'S LAYOUT IS `default` ("The full view"), NOT the warehouse board** — which is why neither `recapNoMoney()` nor the `body.pos-warehouse` rules were ever going to save it, and why the card override was the only thing that could. **Verified in Chromium** through the shared `m-probe` harness, four cases: no override leaves Home exactly as it was; the reporting role's own array takes *Today* and *Also today* away with no revenue left on the screen and Quick actions still in place; an unticked `needs` takes the fires with it; and the warehouse board with no override at all now hides the money too. `scripts/test_backend_nav_parity.js` gains §4 (fast shard, 56 assertions total), and the two load-bearing ones were checked to fail with their fix reverted. No Chinese was composed — no string was added. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no capability grant changed.

2026-09-08 · v4.158 — **§68 ADDED: A VARIANT FAMILY IS EDITED FROM THE SHEET ITS CARD OPENS, AND SAVE WRITES THE FAMILY.** Reported by Ash from the phone with the sheet open on `Raspberry Mango Sorbet · SKU (3-210) X5`: *"on mobile, if product have variants - cant change"*. **The catalogue collapses a family into one card — correctly — and then opened only its representative**, `members.find(m => m._id === p.gid) || members[0]`, whichever size happens to own the group. The other sizes were printed along the card's second line as TEXT, and were reachable from nowhere on the phone: not the card, not the sheet, not search, which matches the same collapsed units. A price or a count on any size but one could only be changed from a desktop. **The sheet carries the family now** — a chip row under the quick-edit note, one chip per size, the marked one being the size on screen. **Switching writes nothing, and THEREFORE Save writes the family**: once the sheet moves between sizes freely, a Save that took only what was in front of the operator would drop the rest silently, so pending edits are held per product id and Save walks every size and writes the ones that changed. Save-on-switch and warn-on-switch are both recorded as rejected, as is turning the card's size line into three ~40px targets. **A failure part-way through a family no longer claims nothing changed** — the count of writes that landed picks the message, and the partial one says the rest can be pressed again; one composed pair, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.34. **And one bug it uncovered, fixed in the same pass because it is the same box:** `render()` rebuilds the price `<input>` on every paint, so a price typed and then followed by a tap on a stock stepper was painted back to the stored figure — no variants required, and shipping for as long as the sheet has had both controls.

2026-09-08 · v4.157 — **THE ORDER PAGE HAS A WAY BACK, THE PHONE REMEMBERS MORE THAN ONE ORDER, AND v4.154's RE-SCAN CASE HAD NEVER ACTUALLY WORKED — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08**, from a phone, hours after v4.154 went live: *"qr code menu order, custoner cant go back from this page. dead end. customer should always be able to see his order even if he goes out fromt he screen completly, scan the qr code again, should have his order there."* **This does not narrow §44 any further and decides nothing new about identity**: v4.154's receipt is the same receipt, doing the job it was written for. Three faults, and the middle one is the serious one. **ONE: THE ORDER PAGE WAS A DEAD END.** Every face of `/s/:shopCode/pay/:token` — order placed, payment received, cancelled — ended at the order and offered nothing but the browser chrome, which inside a WeChat web view is a single X that closes the whole thing. It is worst on the face that says CANCELLED, which reads *"You can place a new one anytime."* and, until now, gave no way to. All three carry a plain link back to the menu, as does §50's in-page payment screen, on both of its faces. **A BOX, NOT A SECOND UNDERLINED LINE**: the cancel beside it is an underlined olive link, and a Back that looked the same would put "leave this page" and "destroy this order" in one visual register a thumb cannot tell apart — so the safe way out is bordered and comes FIRST, and the destructive one stays last and behind its own disclosure. **The language is carried only where the customer's own address carried one**, and that is not tidiness: the pre-paint script takes an explicit `?lang=` over the phone's own language, so appending a lang to every link would force English on a Chinese phone that had simply never touched the toggle — the page would be right and the menu it sent them to would not. **TWO: THE BAR WAS NEVER PAINTED ON LOAD, SO A SECOND SCAN SHOWED NOTHING.** v4.154 read the receipt at startup and then repainted the bar only from `add()`, from the steppers and from the done screen — so closing the sheet worked, because the done screen had just painted it, and RELOADING THE PAGE showed an ordinary empty menu. **A second scan of the QR code is a fresh load**, which is the case the report names and the one v4.154 claimed to have answered. One call at the end of the script fixes it; nothing else changes for a phone with no order, where that call hides a bar that was already hidden. **It is recorded rather than quietly fixed because of HOW it survived**: this behaviour is drawn entirely by script from `localStorage`, so the only suite that can prove it is a browser suite — and the browser shard is not run (CLAUDE.md, Ash's standing instruction). A served-bytes assertion can prove the script was SENT and nothing more. The new checks were run individually, as one file, not as the shard. **THREE: THE RECEIPT IS A LIST, NEWEST FIRST, FIVE DEEP.** It held one order, so a customer who came back for a cake could no longer reach the coffee — or cancel it, the cancel living on the page that address opens. Each entry is judged on its own twelve-hour stamp, so a morning order drops off while one placed ten minutes ago stays. **The cap is a cap on what the PHONE remembers, not on what exists**: a sixth order is placed, printed and paid for exactly as before, and the counter still has it. The bar names the NEWEST — it is the number about to be called, and a bar naming the oldest would name the one already collected. **One order goes straight to its page; several open the sheet's fourth face**, a list of rows, because putting a list in front of the single-order case would charge every customer a tap to be shown one row they then have to tap again. **And the list is repeated at the FOOT of the basket**, since with something in the basket the bar IS the basket — that was the state where the earlier orders used to disappear. **Below every stepper, deliberately**: the basket is memory only (§44) and a tap that leaves the page loses it, so nothing that navigates may sit where a thumb reaching for a + or a − can find it. **A receipt written before the shape changed is read as a list of one**, since a customer holding the old shape mid-trading-day must not be handed an empty bar; and the stored address is checked for SHAPE, not merely presence, because it is read out of storage and put straight into an `href`. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** `Back · 返回` is live in six places including `public/till.html`, `public/m.html` and `public/retail-admin/28-shops.js`; `My orders · 我的订单` is the web storefront's own heading for this exact list (`public/shop.html`) and the mini app's (`miniapp/pages/orders/`). No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. **ONE STALE ASSERTION IS CORRECTED, AND IT IS THE SAME CLASS OF THING v4.154 CORRECTED.** `test_shop_menu_render.js` held that the cart bar is HIDDEN once an order is placed — which was how it proved the basket had been emptied. v4.154 inverted that meaning (an empty basket is exactly when the bar is shown, carrying the order) and the check went red the day it shipped, seen by nobody because that file is in the browser shard. It is corrected rather than relaxed, and the replacement proves more than the original: a bar still saying YOUR BASKET would mean the basket survived, and a bar naming the order means it was emptied AND the order took its place. Code and tests; no schema, no migration.

2026-09-08 · v4.156 — **THE RAIL OBEYS THE SAME CAPABILITY RULES AS THE PHONE — §67 records it.** Reported from the Stockroom account: *"it has the dashboard but the moment i click anything on the left menu i cant go back to dashboard"*, then, of the same account, *"there is no syncing between what the warehouse account sees on mobile compared to what it sees on pc with the same permission. one thing obvious is the dashbaord differences."* **BOTH SENTENCES ARE ONE DEFECT WITH THREE HALVES, and the phone had already answered all three when its tab bar was capability-filtered; the desktop, built first, had answered none.** (1) **A ROLE WAS LANDED WHERE IT COULD NOT COME BACK TO.** `#tab-dashboard` is `class="active"` in the shell — it is what the backend boots showing — and `applyCapGates` takes its rail row away for a role without `dashboard:view` **without moving the operator off the section**. One click on any other row and the dashboard was reachable only by reloading the page. `landOnSomethingReachable()` is the phone's rule, under the phone's name, for the rail: it runs ONCE, on the first gate after the caps arrive, and only moves an operator whose current section has no row leading back to it. (2) **HIDING A ROW IS NOT REFUSING IT.** A hidden rail button is still in the DOM and still answers `.click()`, which is exactly what `goTab()` does — so the dashboard's own *"The full numbers live in Reports"* foot link opened Reports for a role holding neither key. `canTab()` now refuses, before the lookup, and the foot link and the command palette read the same table. (3) **TWO ROWS CARRIED NO GATE AT ALL.** *Manage team* — the roster, every teammate's role and permissions — has been open to every operator on every tenant since it moved out of the avatar menu in 2026-07; it is `team:view`, the key `ROUTE_CAP.team` has always named. *Sales* — today's takings, per channel — is any-of, and **deliberately wider than the phone's `dashboard:view` alone**, because on the desktop that page is the ONLY door to the Meituan / Eleme / Guanyi admins (they lost their own rail rows in the Sales redesign). Gated on `dashboard:view` it would shut the channel screens away from the very role that holds `meituan:sync` — the role whose own dashboard tells it to go and restart a stalled channel. **So the door opens for anyone with a reason to walk through it and the money on the far side carries its own gate**: `#sales-summary` and all seven `.sales-ch-metrics` are `data-cap="dashboard:view"`, so a stock role gets the channel cards and their Configure buttons with the revenue, orders and AOV gone. **`setup` is the one deliberate divergence** and its reason is written where the table is: `#setup-nav`'s display is OWNED by `suRefreshChrome`, and a second writer would put *"Open your store"* back in the rail every time a screen painted a `[data-cap]` button. **WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, and is Ash's:** whether the Stockroom role should HOLD `dashboard:view`. It does not today on the reporting tenant — which is why that account has no Dashboard row and no Reports row — and §66, decided the same day, puts the kitchen-ready fire *on the dashboard it already reads*. If that account is meant to read it, the fix is one tick in Settings → Team → Roles, not code. **Verified in Chromium against the real rail markup**, both ways: the reporting account's cap set lands on Orders with Sales and Manage team gone, and a role holding `dashboard:view` keeps its dashboard and its row. `scripts/test_backend_nav_parity.js` (fast shard) holds all three halves closed and every assertion was checked to fail with its fix reverted. No Chinese was composed — no string was added. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no preset or grant changed.

2026-09-08 · v4.155 — **§61's LEFTOVER HANDLER IS DELETED RATHER THAN WIRED, AND THE ENOBUFS TRIPWIRE v4.153 CALLED "FIXED AT THE HARNESS" IS CLOSED AT THE SEVEN SITES THAT NEVER WENT THROUGH THE HARNESS.** No new section: the first half is §61 carried out, and the second is v4.152's fix finished. **THE FAILURE WAS NOT A LINT NIT.** `scripts/test_mobile_screens.js` failed on main with `reg('kqAdvance') is registered but nothing can reach it`, and that check is STATIC and runs BEFORE the render pass, which the suite exits on — so the broadest coverage the mobile app has, 134 screens across warm, cold and Chinese, had been rendering NOTHING while reporting a one-line complaint that reads like tidiness. **WIRE IT OR DELETE IT WAS ANSWERED BY THE HISTORY, not by taste:** `73b263f`, the §61 split made on Ash's "they can split what they start making, what was made. its all one batch. need to fix that", removed the whole-order button `APP.cmd('kqAdvance',…)` and replaced it with the per-line `kqItemAdvance`, leaving handler and function behind. Wiring it back would have rebuilt the exact control §61 was asked to remove, so it is deleted. **What the deletion does NOT touch is recorded in the code**: `kqNote` still serves the two per-line callers, `hdResolve` on a whole order is still reached from the awaiting-batch path, and `hdStart`'s `item` parameter stays optional — no live caller omits it any more, but the shape is not dead, only that entrance to it. **THE SECOND HALF IS THE CITATION RULE BITING ITS AUTHOR.** Unblocking the render pass ran it for the first time and 167 of 402 screens failed on the same 1 MiB `--dump-dom` ENOBUFS cap v4.152 fixed in `scripts/lib/m-probe.js`. That fix closed one call site; **seven suites carry their own inlined copy of the spawn and never go through the helper** — `test_mobile_screens`, `test_kitchen_stock_visibility`, `test_stock_home`, `test_stock_screens`, `test_stock_receiving`, `test_stock_picking`, `test_mobile_geometry`. CLAUDE.md says it exactly: *a finding filed as `file:line` is where it was found, not the extent of the problem; grep for the pattern before declaring any finding closed.* v4.152 grepped for USERS OF THE HELPER and called it done. **64 MiB is this repository's existing convention rather than a number invented here** — `test_mobile_customer_record`, `test_mobile_order_from_record` and `test_till_back` already set it. Each suite keeps its own timeout, which is what still bounds a genuinely runaway render. **v4.153's remark that two sessions hit one tripwire in an afternoon understated it: three did, and the third only because the first two had left the render pass dark enough to hide the other seven.** **RECORDED AND NOT FIXED HERE:** `scripts/test_mobile_geometry.js` exits 1 on three clipped-text findings and one header-rule finding, verified byte-identical on a clean `44def44` before and after this change. It is a UI defect, it is now VISIBLE rather than masked, and it is owed its own change.

2026-09-08 · v4.154 — **A QR ORDER CAN BE CANCELLED — BY THE CUSTOMER OR AT THE TILL — AND THE CUSTOMER STOPS LOSING IT WHEN THEY CLOSE THE SHEET. §44's "no login, no session, no cookie" IS NARROWED, NOT OVERTURNED — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08.** Two reports from the counter on the day §44's till flow went live, and they turn out to be one problem: *"if a customer eventually doesnt want the order there should be an option to cancel it from his side or from till"*, and *"after customer placed the order, closed the pop up window where his order number by mistake. he has no way to see his order, order number or anything its all dissaper."* **THE SECOND IS THE PREREQUISITE FOR THE FIRST**, which is why they are ruled together: a customer who cannot get back to their order cannot cancel it either, and the cancel would have been a control only reachable on the one screen they had just lost. **THE ORDER ALREADY HAD A DURABLE PAGE AND NOBODY COULD FIND IT.** §50 gave every QR order a `pay_token` and a page at `/s/:shopCode/pay/:token`, and that page only ever said whether the order was paid. It now carries the number, the name, the amount and the way to cancel, and is the customer's order page rather than a payment screen — **one page for "what did I order", "has it been paid" and "I changed my mind"**, which is three problems answered by a route that already existed. **§44's STATELESSNESS IS NARROWED TO IDENTITY, WHICH IS WHAT IT WAS ALWAYS ABOUT.** The menu now writes ONE thing to the phone that placed the order: the address of that order, the number and the amount, under a per-shop key, expiring in twelve hours. **It is a receipt, not an identity** — it says nothing about who anybody is, it is written by the phone that placed the order and readable only by that phone, and the unguessable token was already the authority it hands back. **The basket is still not persisted and that rule is untouched**: a basket surviving a reload would be a stale order waiting to be submitted by accident, while a PLACED order is the opposite — it exists, and forgetting it is the defect. **The twelve hours are load-bearing rather than tidy**: `shop_order_code` restarts at 1 each trading day (§49), so a bar left up overnight would not merely be old, it would name an order that belongs to somebody else today. **THE TOKEN IS THE AUTHORITY FOR CANCELLING, because on this page there is nothing else it could be** — no login, no session, no account. A wrong token, a malformed one and the right token through another shop's code all 404, the same answer the pay page gives, so neither route confirms which guesses hit something real; a suite drives all three and asserts the order is untouched by each. **ONLY WHILE UNPAID, and the transition is guarded IN the UPDATE rather than around it** (`AND status = 'pending_payment'`), so a customer cancelling at the same moment a cashier takes the money loses the race cleanly instead of both appearing to win. **It releases the reservation** — §45 has a QR order reserving on submit, and a cancel that left the hold behind would take a drink off the shelf for nobody until the sweep noticed. **No points, vouchers or balance are reversed, and that is a property of this door rather than an omission**: a QR order is placed with no `customer_id`, so there is no account any of them could have come from. **THE CONTROL IS A DISCLOSURE AND A PLAIN FORM — NO SCRIPT AT ALL.** This is the page a customer reaches when something has gone wrong, which is the worst possible place for a control that needs a working script, and it must run in every browser WeChat has ever shipped and in the camera-app browsers §50 already copes with. **Rejected: `confirm()`** — a browser dialog is the thing the till is asserted never to open, and a customer surface holds the same line; the disclosure IS the second step. **AT THE TILL, cancelling goes through the admin's own status transition**, which already releases the reservation and is the path staff have always cancelled by — nothing new is written for a state the system understands. **AND A WORD COLLISION IS CLOSED: the control that BACKS OUT of a recalled order said "Cancel"**, beside a control that cancels the customer's order. The same word for opposite outcomes, and the destructive one is the one a cashier reaches for by habit; backing out now says Back. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** Every string is a live pair from the mini app's own order screen, where a customer cancels exactly this — `Cancel order · 取消订单`, `Cancel this order? · 取消此订单?`, `You can place a new one anytime. · 您可以随时重新下单。` (`miniapp/pages/order/order.js:99-101, 275-277`) — plus `Cancelled · 已取消`, the admin's and the mini app's own label for this status. No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. **ONE FALSE ASSERTION IS CORRECTED IN PASSING, and it matters more than the line it was on.** `test_shop_menu.js` held that a cancelled order's page still said `请到收银台付款。` — it passed, and it was measuring nothing: the basket script is inlined by `shell()` on every page and contains that string as a literal, so the assertion matched the SCRIPT and would have gone green for a page that rendered nothing at all. It is now scoped to the rendered block, which is what it always meant to say. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration.

2026-09-08 · v4.153 — **THE WAREHOUSE IS TOLD THE KITCHEN HAS FINISHED ON THE DASHBOARD IT ALREADY READS, AS A ROW WITH A CLOCK ON IT — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08**, from the warehouse account: *"there is no real proper notification right now that i will be able to see properly if i look on mobile or pc … that notification need to come on the dashboard direct."* **THE SIGNAL EXISTED AND WAS UNMISSABLE ONLY IN THE SENSE THAT IT COULD NOT BE SEEN.** §48 gave this direction a `seen_at` fact, a phone dot and a push, and all three are correct; what none of them is, is ON THE FRONT DOOR. The dot is 6px of Sage two taps inside More, the toast needs the app already open, the push is one moment on one handset — and on the DESKTOP there was nothing whatsoever: grepping `public/retail-admin/` for `kitchen-ready` returned zero, because the code had never been written for it. **Rejected: a widget of its own on the desktop dashboard**, which is what was asked for and is the wrong shape — a tenth polling path, a card empty most of the day, and a fix reaching the desktop only. **The ruling is one server key.** `kitchen_ready` joins `/api/retail-admin/dashboard/ops`, which the desktop dashboard and the phone's Home already poll on the same 60-second cycle and already render as *Needs you* — so one change lands the row at the top of BOTH, in the strip that is full width, structurally first, and cannot be dragged away or hidden. **THE ROW IS AMBER AND CARRIES AN AGE, and that is the decision, not the styling.** Needs-you sorts severity, then oldest-first, and a fire with NO age sorts last. On the Stockroom role the only other fire that ever appears is *Restock needed*, which has no clock by design ("15 out of stock" is a state, not a queue) — **so a calm, clockless version of this row would have sat permanently underneath the one thing the warehouse already knew.** With an age it leads, every time, with nobody writing a rule to make it so; and *oldest 4h* is the fact that decides whether you walk over now or after lunch. **Rejected: the calm treatment**, truer to "nothing needs doing" and losing the ordering that makes the row worth having. **THE COST IS NAMED: the row sits under a heading that says *Needs you* and strictly nothing needs doing** — the kitchen shelves what it makes and records the stock itself. Put to Ash beside the alternative; taken. **THE CLICK OPENS THE LIST THAT ALREADY EXISTS, at `/stock?go=ready`, and this is load-bearing rather than convenient: opening the list is the ONLY acknowledgement this direction has** (§48 — the read is a server-side `seen_at`, so one person looking puts the row out for the whole warehouse and takes the dot off every other phone). **Rejected: a row that states the count with nowhere to go** — it could never clear from the desktop at all, and would burn until somebody picked up a phone. **Rejected: building a second ready list inside the admin**, a twin of a screen the Quick Stock app already renders and the phone already opens; the desktop leaves the shell for it instead, and the price — the sidebar goes, you return with Back — was named and accepted. **ONE CLAUSE, NOT TWO.** The four conditions behind the count move to `lib/kitchen-ready.js` and are REQUIRED by both routes rather than retyped in the new one, on the rule the Reviews fire already keeps: a fire that disagrees with the queue it opens means one of the two is lying. A suite asserts both the sharing and the absence of any second copy, and both assertions were verified to fail when the clause is forked. **The two audience gates are applied on the SERVER as well as the client** — the maker is not told about their own output, and an operator who cannot open the list is never told about it — **as an honest zero and never a 403**, this being polled in the background where a refusal bounces a pocketed phone to the login screen. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** Both strings are copied from locked live sources: `Ready from the kitchen · 厨房已完成` is the list's own name in `public/m.html` and `public/stock.html`, and `View · 查看` is live in `public/m.html` — so no entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed. **THIS SESSION INDEPENDENTLY FOUND AND FIXED THE `m-probe` ENOBUFS TRIPWIRE AND THEN DROPPED ITS FIX**, v4.152's `18ac4ae` having landed the same one — same file, same 64 MiB, same reasoning — while this branch was in flight. **The duplicate is recorded rather than quietly discarded**: two sessions hitting one tripwire on one afternoon is the evidence that it was load-bearing, and v4.152's account of it (m.html crossing 1.01 MB, ~1.2 KB tipping it) is more precise than this one's and is the one to read. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no capability grant changes.

2026-09-08 · v4.152 — **"ASK THE KITCHEN" GAINS A THIRD PURPOSE, `urgent`, AND IT SORTS THE QUEUE RATHER THAN ONLY COLOURING IT — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08.** §65 records it. **It is a THIRD VALUE OF `purpose`, not a fourth column.** `restock_orders.purpose` is untyped TEXT with no CHECK constraint (`database.js` `addColumn`), so `'urgent'` needs no migration and no back-fill: every existing row keeps the value it has and the two old ones mean exactly what they meant. **Rejected: a separate `urgent` flag orthogonal to `order`/`shelf`**, which buys an urgent SHELF restock nobody has asked for at the price of a schema column, a second piece of request state and a second question on a screen whose whole virtue is that it asks one. **What makes it more than a label is `ORDER BY`.** The queue's only sort was `created_at DESC` — newest first — so an urgent request raised at 09:00 sat below a routine one raised at 09:05 and the kitchen had to notice a chip to find it. Urgent rows now sort ahead of everything else, `created_at DESC` still ordering within each group. **The sort key is `purpose = 'urgent'` and nothing else**, so a store→warehouse row (purpose NULL) is unaffected — this endpoint serves both directions and the change had to be inert for the one it is not about. **It is added in FOUR places because `purpose` is read in four**, and a value understood by three of them is worse than no value at all: the picker in Tacet Mobile, the same picker in `/stock` (which §48 retires but has not yet deleted), the kitchen queue's chip in both its list and its detail, and the printed slip in `lib/feie.js`. **The Chinese is composed, not lifted**, and is declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.33 under the 2026-09-06 amendment, with the live pairs it was built from and the ones rejected.

2026-09-08 · v4.151 — **§64 ADDED: THE PHONE READS THE CATALOGUE TO ITS END, AND THE 500-ROW HALF THAT v4.149'S NEIGHBOURING FIX LEFT OPEN IS CLOSED.** PR #363 made `loadCatalogue` the only writer of `DB.products` and pointed the All chip at the server's `total`, then wrote in the code that the endpoint caps at 500 rows and that *"paging the phone past that cap is a separate change"*. **On a catalogue past 500 every symptom of the original report was still live** — Live / Draft / Low / Out counting a prefix while All counted the shop, a search that could not reach past the cap, a variant family cut in half at the boundary, and an order line's SKU chip refusing to open anything beyond it. `GET /api/retail-admin/products` now takes an `offset` and the phone WALKS the catalogue until it holds the whole shelf. **SERVER-SIDE FILTERING — the obvious answer, and what the Orders and Customers screens already do — WAS REJECTED, for a reason specific to this array: `DB.products` is not the Products screen's list, it is the phone's product lookup, and the ORDERS screen reads it.** A server-filtered array is a view, so an order line's SKU chip would stop resolving the moment a filter was set on Products — the same defect, from the other direction. **`id` is now the last ORDER BY key on that endpoint, and that is not tidiness:** the three sort keys are not unique between them, SQLite may order tied rows differently in two statements, and across LIMIT/OFFSET a tied row can land on both pages or on neither — a two-request read silently gaining a duplicate or losing a product. **The screen is honest at every instant rather than only at the end**: a count got by walking the array draws only while the array is the whole shelf, a refresh never paints fewer products than it already had, a read that reached nothing does not license a count of zero, and where the walk stops short an amber bar names the fraction. One composed pair, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.32. Four things are recorded as deliberately NOT fixed, including the blank screen a first-page failure still leaves and the desktop grid, which still reads one page and says so.

2026-09-08 · v4.150 — **THE IN-PAGE WECHAT RAIL IS SWITCHED OFF UNTIL THE DOMAIN IS ICP-FILED, EVERY QR ORDER NOW PRINTS ON PAID RATHER THAN ON SUBMIT, AND THE TILL GAINS THE LIST THAT MAKES BOTH SAFE — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08.** Three changes, and they are one change: the reason the first is survivable is the third. **THE RAIL WAS OFFERING A PAYMENT IT COULD NOT TAKE.** WeChat Pay JSAPI charges only on a domain registered as a payment directory in the merchant platform, and WeChat does not accept a domain onto that list without an ICP filing; `shop.rootskitchenchina.com` has none, so every charge §50's rail raised failed at WeChat rather than in our code. **The failure was upstream of the repository and no code change could have fixed it** — which is why this is a switch (`SHOP_QR_WECHAT_PAY`, default off) and not a deletion. §50's machinery is correct, is still in the tree and is still under test; what is missing is a filing. **Rejected: unsetting the Official Account credentials on the box**, which would have had the same effect here and silently taken out everything else the Official Account is used for. **The switch is tested in BOTH states, and the off state is tested WITH credentials present** — that being the actual production configuration, and the one a suite that only ever tested "no credentials" would have let a dead switch pass. **ICP IS NOT A BLOCKER FOR FACE-TO-FACE PAYMENT and that is recorded here so it is not rediscovered:** Alipay 当面付, WeChat 付款码 and any plain 收款码 are onboarded against a business licence and shop photos, never a website, and never touch the domain. The counter takes money on the terminal it already has. **§44's PRINT-ON-SUBMIT IS RETIRED, not narrowed a second time.** §50 had already carved out the in-page path; with the counter path joining it the rule has no remaining cases. **Its premise changed rather than its reasoning being wrong:** §44 put the ticket ahead of the customer because the counter had no way to see a QR order until the customer arrived with it. **The till now lists today's unpaid QR orders for the shop it is locked to**, so the kitchen's signal is that list. **The cost is named rather than discovered, exactly as §50 named it, and it now falls on every order:** the drink is started when the customer reaches the counter instead of while they walk. Bought against tickets printed for food nobody pays for — which on this page is not hypothetical, since submitting costs the customer nothing and closing the tab costs them nothing either. **THE NUMBER IS THE WHOLE RETRIEVAL MECHANISM and it already existed.** `lib/shop-order-code.js` has issued a plain per-shop, per-day number since §49 for exactly this purpose; the customer holds up 12 and the cashier taps 12. **Rejected: scanning.** A QR on the customer's screen scanned at the counter was specified and dropped — it needs hardware the counter does not have, and the number in `lib/shop-order-code.js` was designed to make it unnecessary. **Rejected: putting the list in the till's order rail.** Under 700px that rail is a bottom sheet behind a tap, and a list the counter works from cannot live one gesture away; it is a second face of the entry pane instead, taking turns with the product grid. **The switch between them is ABSENT when nothing is waiting**, so a badge on screen always means there is something behind it and a shop with no QR orders sees the till exactly as it shipped. **The pane DEFAULTS to the pending list when something is waiting and to the menu when nothing is, and a default is all it is:** it never moves the pane under a cashier who has chosen one or has a basket open. **One server capability was missing and is added: the orders list can now be narrowed by `shop_entry_method`.** §44 forbids splitting a shop's revenue across two channel lines, so `channel` cannot carry the door and the column has to be filterable instead; without it the counter would be shown its own till sales abandoned mid-settle as though customers were standing behind them. Validated against `SHOP_ENTRY_METHODS` rather than interpolated, so an unknown value narrows to nothing instead of widening to everything. **Settling a recalled order PATCHes the existing row and never POSTs a new one** — creating a second order would bill one customer twice, print two tickets and leave a phantom on the shop's day — **and it carries the wallet on the same request**, so an order cannot reach `paid` with no tender and become the unreconcilable row the settle screen exists to prevent. **NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** Both new labels are quoted from locked sources: the walk-in tab reuses this screen's own `Counter sale · 前台销售`, and `Pending · 待付款` is the admin's own label for `pending_payment` rows (`public/retail-admin/03-dashboard.js:3419`) — these ARE those rows, so it is the same word for the same state rather than an approximation of one. **One test window was widened and the reason is recorded rather than buried:** `verify-fulfilment-types.js` asserted that `switchStore` calls `loadCatalogue()` within 600 characters, a proxy for "inside the function" that the function outgrew; it is now 900, matching the assertion on the line below it, which has always used 900 for the same function and the same reason. The behaviour it guards is unchanged and still asserted. Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration.

2026-09-07 · v4.149 — **§44's QR `source` DEFECT IS CLOSED, AND A WRONG CLAIM IN THE AMENDMENT THAT RECORDED IT IS CORRECTED.** The 2026-09-07 amendment ruled that §44's "order source" means `shop_entry_method` and filed, as a live defect it deliberately did not fix, that the QR submit handler also wrote `source = 'qr'`. **That is now fixed: the handler writes no `source` at all, and every reader keys on `shop_entry_method`.** **`source` is not given a new value for QR — it is simply absent, and the absence IS the value**, matching every other self-service path in the system: the mini-app checkout, the web store and the Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery mirrors all omit the column, and only the staff-keyed manual-order endpoint writes a literal. The column now reads exactly as the amendment defines it — a value means staff keyed the row, NULL means it arrived by itself — and the QR path stops being the one self-service writer claiming otherwise. **THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX. The amendment said of the auto-print de-dupe "It is the only reader of the column anywhere". That was FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN.** There were two, and the second — the WeChat payment page in `routes/shop-menu.js`, which 404s an order whose door is not the QR menu — was already in the tree when the claim was made. **It was missed because the survey searched one file and stopped at the first hit rather than grepping the pattern across the tree, which is precisely the failure this file's citations rule names**: a finding filed as `file:line` is where it was found, not the extent of the problem. **It was caught by the test suite, not by review** — removing the writer turned six payment-page assertions red, all of them green on main a moment earlier, which is the only reason the second reader was found before it shipped. **The false sentence is struck in place and the correction recorded beside it rather than the sentence quietly deleted**, because the next reader is otherwise free to trust the same method. **NO BACKFILL**: historical QR rows keep the `source = 'qr'` they were written with and stay identifiable by `shop_entry_method`, which they also carry. Code, docs and two suites; no schema, no migration. §44 is amended in place — no section is added — so Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.148 — **§59 AMENDED A THIRD TIME: `hdStart` REPORTS WHY IT DECLINED, AND NO PATH OUT OF THE KITCHEN QUEUE SAYS NOTHING — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, after a fourth report of one symptom: *"once i click 'marked as made' thats it. nothing pop up"*. **The three amendments before this each removed a real cause and none of them removed the SILENCE, which is why it took four rounds to find one bug.** `hdStart` returned a bare `false` on every refusal, and `kqAdvance` fell back to the queue without a word — so an operator who had just closed a request saw an empty list and nothing else, whichever of the refusals had fired. **THE RULING: every refusal names itself.** `hdStart` returns `true` when the screen opened and otherwise a reason — `nocap`, `nolines`, `nostore` — which `kqAdvance` turns into a sentence on the queue it drops back to. **The note is a NOTE, not an error**: nothing failed and the operator did exactly the right thing; what is wrong is the state they are now in. **It renders ABOVE THE EMPTY STATE as well as above the list**, because *Nothing to make* with no explanation is precisely the screen this defect showed somebody — a queue that has just gone quiet reads as success. It clears on re-entry and on opening another request, being about the last one closed and nothing else. **WHAT EACH ONE SAYS matters more than that it says something**: `nocap` names `production:log` by the label an admin will see on the permissions screen (`Record what was made · 登记生产批次`, quoted from `lib/capabilities.js`), so the operator can ask for the right thing instead of reporting a blank screen; `nostore` names the missing store; `nolines` says the request carried no quantities. **THE GENERAL RULE THIS SETTLES, and it is worth more than the three sentences**: a refusal that lands on somebody who has just changed state — a request closed, stock still short — may not be silent, because silence there does not read as *nothing happened*, it reads as *that worked*. **Recorded as the fourth lesson in this section's run**: a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants (§59); a green suite is not evidence when its case was written to match the gate (v4.145); a fixture whose stubs answer instantly cannot see a race (v4.147); **and a diagnosis is impossible when the failure has no voice — the first three rounds were all spent guessing between causes the app could have named.** Two new cases hold it shut, each verified to fail without the change. **Version v4.148.** No schema, no migration, no capability grant changes. **Four composed Chinese pairs** are declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.29, per §30 rule 3. **No section is added** — §59 is amended in place — so Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.147 — **§59 AMENDED AGAIN: THE HANDOVER STOPS REFUSING ON A SHELF THAT IS MERELY LATE, AND ON LINES IT CANNOT MATCH — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, from the third report of one symptom: *"once i click marked as made it doesnt show me any restock for the kitchen"*, with a screenshot of Tacet Mobile's Kitchen queue reading *Nothing to make*. **The first two amendments fixed the GATE and this one fixes what was behind it.** §59 moved the gate off the quick-stock mode and v4.145 carried that to `/stock`; both were real and neither was the whole cause, because `hdStart` carried two further refusals that were silence rather than an answer. **THE CAUSE, REPRODUCED RATHER THAN REASONED**: `state.qs.items` starts `null` and is filled two CHAINED round trips after the queue first renders — `loadQsCtx`, then `loadQsItems` on its answer. `hdResolve` matches a request's lines against that list by SKU, so a list that has not arrived marks EVERY line unmatched, and the guard `!lines.some(l => l.id != null)` then refused to open at all. **An operator who taps *Start making* and *Mark as made* faster than two round trips on a phone — or whose shelf fetch simply failed — closed the request and got nothing.** The probe that proved it is one line: set `items` to `null`, its real initial value, and the tap produces exactly the reported silence. **THE RULING, in two parts.** (1) **A LATE SHELF IS NOT A MISSING PRODUCT**: the lines are HELD and the screen opens now in its loading state, `loadQsItems` resolving them the moment the shelf lands; a shelf that never lands gets a named failure carrying the way forward — Retry, and the batch door that needs no request — because the request is already closed by the time anybody is on that screen and there is no way back to it. (2) **NOT ONE LINE MATCHED IS A SENTENCE, NOT A SILENCE**: the screen has always drawn an unmatched line greyed, badged *Not on this store's list*, with the count named underneath and the operator told to go and fix the catalogue. **Refusing to open threw that sentence away and left nothing in its place, which is strictly worse than the problem it avoided** — a request whose lines this store cannot take is exactly what somebody needs to be told. **WHAT STILL REFUSES, and all three are about the request or the operator rather than about the app's own readiness**: no `production:log`; a request with nothing asked for; and no store to add to, once the context has ANSWERED and said so — `hdCommit` sends `store_id` and there is nothing to record without one. **BOTH APPS, IN THE SAME COMMIT.** `public/stock.html` carries the identical pair of refusals and is fixed with `public/m.html` rather than reasoned about: that file was scoped out once on a plausible argument and the same symptom came back, so the argument that its shelf loads at boot and the race is therefore unlikely is recorded as the reason it is LESS likely there, never as a reason to leave it. **THE THIRD FIXTURE LESSON, and the sharpest**: §59 recorded that a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants, v4.145 added that a green suite is not evidence when its own case was written to match the gate, and this adds that **a fixture whose stubs answer instantly cannot see a race the real network has** — the suites set `items` by hand and every stub resolved in a microtask, so no case had ever executed the ordinary path where the shelf is still in flight. Four new cases hold it shut in Tacet Mobile and one in `/stock`, each verified to fail without the change. **Version v4.147**; v4.144 was taken by PR #348, v4.145 by the previous amendment and v4.146 by PR #350 — the sixth and seventh collisions of this kind, both of them a header bumped with no changelog entry beside it, which is the one shape this file's own v4.141 note says a version collision hides in. No schema, no migration, no capability grant changes. **Two composed strings** are declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` in this commit, per §30 rule 3. **No section is added** — §59 is amended in place — so Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.145 — **§59 AMENDED BY INSERTION: THE RULING APPLIES TO `/stock` TOO, AND THE SCOPE LINE THAT EXCLUDED IT WAS WRONG — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, from the second report of the same symptom: *"i still cant see the stock window after production is ready"*. **§59 shipped the fix in `public/m.html` and scoped `public/stock.html` out**, on the reasoning that there the `kitchen` role does read `mode:'add'` so the flow works. **That is true of the `kitchen` role and of no other, and it is the wrong half of the users.** The word *Production* exists only in `/stock` — Tacet Mobile calls the same screen *Kitchen queue* — so the report named the app the fix had skipped. **Everyone else who can open that queue on `/stock` reads `'recount'`**: the owner, an admin, and any `retail` operator, none of them `stock_app_only`, all of them able to open a request, close it, and be handed nothing. **The original §59 diagnosis was right and its scope line was not**: the roles confined to `/stock` are exactly the ones that did not need the fix. **The remedy is §59's own gate, unchanged in substance** — `production:log`, the capability `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on. **`/stock` HOLDS NO CAPABILITY LIST**, only what `/quick-stock/context` tells it, which is why it had nothing to gate on but the mode; **the derivation moves into `lib/quick-stock-grant.js` as `mayLogProduction(req)`, beside the `quickStockMode` it replaces, and ships as `can_log_production` on that response** — one derivation, both apps, so they cannot answer the same question differently. **NO `req.backendUser` REQUIREMENT, unlike `mayRecount` beside it**: that one demands it so the recount GRANT stays revocable per tenant, while this is not a grant but the capability the write already enforces, and the legacy kitchen realm — no `backendUser` row, full capability set — can genuinely post to that endpoint. **It FAILS OPEN on an unresolvable capability set**, matching Tacet Mobile's `mCan()` and for the reason that function gives; the client reads `!== false` for the same reason. **THE LOG A BATCH TILE ON `/stock` STAYS ON THE MODE and is deliberately not moved**: that tile carries a separate decision written where it stands — stating what a batch yielded is the kitchen's job and a warehouse recount has no batches — and the handover is not that case, the operator reaching it having just closed a kitchen request. **§59's premise for Tacet Mobile (that `logbatch` already hands the same screen to a recount-mode operator) does not hold on `/stock`, and the ruling does not need it**: the gate is the capability the write is gated on, on its own. **A SECOND SUITE WAS ASSERTING THE DEFECT, and this is the second time in two days that a fixture has done so.** `scripts/test_stock_home.js` carried `a-recount-operator-gets-the-queue-back`, which asserted that a recount operator lands back on the queue and defended it in a comment — *a warehouse recount has no business being sent to a screen that adds*. It is replaced by two honest cases: a recount operator holding the capability is handed the screen, and one without it still lands back on the queue. **The lesson is recorded rather than left to be relearned a third time**: where §59 said a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants, this adds that a green suite is not evidence the flow works when the suite's own case was written to match the gate. **Nothing in §59's body is rewritten, withdrawn or re-worded** — paragraphs are added beside its scope section and dated, per this file's amendment convention. **VERSION COORDINATION: this claimed v4.144 and no longer does.** PR #348 (§60, a kitchen types its batch on the card) took that number on main while this branch was open — the fifth collision of this kind recorded in this file, arising the way every one of them has. **It is also noted, and deliberately not written for them, that #348 bumped the header to v4.144 and added §60 without a changelog entry of its own**; that gap is theirs to fill and inventing one here would put words in another author's mouth. This entry takes **v4.145**. Nothing is renumbered to make room and no live section moves. No schema, no migration, no capability grant changes, no new strings. **No section is added** — §59 is amended in place — so Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.143 — **§59 ADDED: THE KITCHEN QUEUE HANDS OVER TO "WHAT YOU MADE" ON THE CAPABILITY THAT SCREEN'S OWN WRITE IS GATED ON, NOT ON THE QUICK-STOCK MODE — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, from the report that *"the kitchen queue, after making the next window should be how many items reached the shelf but that window never open"*. **The window had never opened once in Tacet Mobile, for anybody.** `hdStart` in `public/m.html` gated the handover on `qsMode()==='add'`; `lib/quick-stock-grant.js` derives that mode from the ROLE, answering `'add'` only for a backend operator whose `tenant_users.role` is literally `kitchen` — and that role ships `stock_app_only`, which `server.js` uses to refuse it Tacet Mobile outright, every `/api/` call outside `lib/stock-app-only.js`'s list returning `kitchen_add_only`. **So the two conditions could not both hold**: every session that can reach the queue reads `'recount'`, `hdStart` returned false on every tap, and the queue's own promise one screen earlier — *The next screen asks how many reached the shelf* — was never kept. **The ruling: the gate is `production:log`, asked through `canRoute('whatmade')`** — the capability `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on, which is what the Record button actually calls. **The mode was never load-bearing and the proof was already shipped**: `logbatch` opens the SAME screen with the SAME write for a recount-mode operator and always has, and the endpoint has no mode gate at all — only a store-scope check on restricted roles. **The superseded reason is quoted rather than deleted**: *an absolute recounter has no business being handed a delta to apply*. This screen hands over no delta; it posts a production batch that moves the shelf server-side in one transaction. **A SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT IS FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE**: `hdOpen` returned `true` unconditionally while `push()` silently declines a route the operator cannot reach, so an operator without `production:log` closed the request and got a dead tap — no screen, and `kqAdvance`'s early return skipping even the re-render; `hdOpen` now asks first and the caller falls through to the queue. **THE SUITE PASSED THROUGHOUT AND IS THE THIRD FINDING**: `scripts/test_mobile_production.js` set `mode:'add'` by hand and its own note called that fixture load-bearing, so 70 assertions proved a flow in a state no live session can be in; the fixture now says `mode:'recount'` and the old code fails it. **`public/stock.html` carries the identical gate and is NOT changed** — there the `kitchen` role does read `'add'`, so the flow works, and §48 retires that app. **Recorded and deliberately not fixed**: neither production screen names WHICH store it is adding to, `state.qs.storeId` being the first active store with no picker — pre-existing, shared with Log a batch, and a separate change. No schema, no migration, no capability grant changes, no new strings. Appended as §59 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.142 — **§58 ADDED: A FRESH LINE ON AN ORDER THAT IS NOT GOING OUT TODAY IS DEDUCTED WHEN IT GOES OUT, NOT WHEN IT IS PAID — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, from an order screenshot: *"这是包含鲜食的预约单，明天发送。但是鲜食的库存已经自动扣除了"*. **The rule: a batch-made line (`store_products.is_batch_made = 1`) on an order that is not a counter sale does NOT decrement `physical_qty` at the paid transition; it decrements at the first forward transition into fulfilment**, where the existing Start-preparing / dispatch / waybill / parcel / rider calls already take it. **Everything else on the same order still decrements at payment, grocery lines in the same basket included — the 2026-08-31 "every paid order decrements, whatever its address" change STANDS for anything the kitchen does not make, and is not reopened.** **Why the fresh line alone earns it:** the shop sells a sold-out fresh item on the stated premise that the kitchen makes the next batch on a named day and the delivery date is floored onto that day — the premise the fresh pre-order exemption enforces and `promised_ship_date` records, printed on the kitchen slip as *MAKE FRESH 当天现做*. Deducting at payment contradicts it twice: **it takes tomorrow's food out of today's count**, so today's shoppers read sold out while the units sit in the fridge, **and where the shelf is already at zero — which that exemption deliberately permits — it drives `physical_qty` negative**, the decrement path having no availability check at all. **A shelf-stable jar has no batch behind it**, which is why the ruling is narrow. **Counter sales are excluded BY NAME** (`isCounter`, not the absence of an address): the goods leave in the same instant the money arrives. **Guangzhou same-day is untouched** — those orders reserve at checkout and commit on payment, and their food does leave today. **No new decrement site, no new ledger reason, no schema change, no migration**: the deferred line lands on the existing `order_prepare` row, and the per-product idempotency guard already lets a mixed order commit its grocery half at payment and its fresh half later without double-counting. **Refunds need no change** — the ledger-backed reverser caps each product at what the ledger says is still out, so a line never decremented returns nothing. **No new strings**: the operator's *Stock pending · 库存待扣* note is once again true of exactly these orders and is reused, so `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched. **ONE GAP THE DEFERRAL OPENED IS CLOSED IN THE SAME CHANGE**: the two auto-deliver sweeps claim straight out of `paid` (`AUTO_DELIVER_FROM_STATUSES`) and committed no stock, because until now payment had always taken it already — a sweep closing a local fresh pre-order would have stranded those units on the count with nothing left to fire, so both gained the same idempotent call every other forward transition makes. **THREE THINGS ARE RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED**: (1) **nothing caps how many pre-orders one batch takes** — forty orders against a batch of twenty are accepted today and still would be, and a batch-capacity gate needs a per-product per-day batch size that §40 defines for a recipe and nothing yet exposes to checkout; (2) the stock-pending note is **order-item deep, not bundle deep**, a bundle of batch-made components not being walked per list row, while the decrement itself runs on expanded components as it always did; (3) **`is_batch_made`, NOT `oos_policy = 'backorder_gz'`** — the broader flag opens any product to out-of-city pre-order including shelf goods with no batch behind them. Appended as §58 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.141 — **§44's "ORDER SOURCE" IS NAMED: IT IS `retail_orders.shop_entry_method`, VALUES `till` AND `qr`, AND NOT `retail_orders.source` — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07.** **§44 ruled that till and QR share the channel `shop` and are told apart by "order source"; it never named a column or a value, and a session sent to implement it stopped rather than choose** — correctly, because the tree offers two candidates and they disagree. **The ruling: `source` answers HOW THE ROW WAS CREATED — keyed by staff, or arrived by itself — and a till sale and a QR sale are both a person standing in the shop, so it cannot separate them.** `shop_entry_method` was added for this exact distinction and its own suite says so: `scripts/test_shop_channel.js` opens by recording that the column exists to name "which of a shop's two doors an order came through" and that it is **"deliberately NOT new values on `source`"**. **`routes/retail.js`'s rule that a client may not claim `source` STANDS and is affirmed as correct** — the till goes on posting through the manual-order endpoint, that endpoint goes on binding `'manual'`, and staff did key the order in, which remains true. **AMENDMENT IS INSERTION ONLY**: §44's Channel-and-source paragraph is not rewritten, not withdrawn and not re-worded; four paragraphs are added beside it and dated. **A LIVE DEFECT IS RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: the QR submit handler writes `source = 'qr'` as well as `shop_entry_method = 'qr'`** (`routes/shop-menu.js`, the `'shop', 'qr', 'counter'` value row in `POST /s/:shopCode/order`), which is the widening its own test file records as deliberately not done — so the tree contradicts itself and the contradiction is now written down rather than left to be re-derived. **Removing it is NOT a one-liner, which is why it is filed rather than done**: the paid-order auto-print de-dupe reads `prior.source === 'qr'` (`routes/retail.js`, inside `autoPrintOrder`) and is the column's ONLY reader anywhere, so dropping the writer without moving that predicate onto `shop_entry_method` would reprint every QR order's kitchen ticket on payment — the reader and the writer move in one commit or neither. **NO BACKFILL is ruled, implied or performed**, on `source` or on `channel`; historical rows are untouched and out of scope. **VERSION COORDINATION, and this entry has already been moved once by it.** **It first claimed v4.139 and no longer does**: main took that number for §54 (the phone's order drawer on a mirrored order, PR #340) while this branch sat open, and because both sides carried the identical header line the merge resolved it SILENTLY rather than conflicting — the collision was found by reading the log, not by git. **Recorded because that is the failure mode this file keeps meeting**: a version collision between two open branches does not announce itself, and the one place it shows is a duplicated number in the changelog. **This entry now takes v4.141.** **v4.140 is RESERVED and deliberately skipped here** — PR #328's three Finance rulings take it, renumbered in the same pass to §55, §56 and §57 after all three of the numbers it claimed were taken on main (§52 by PR #335, §53 by PR #336, §54 by PR #340). That renumbering is done and pushed; this entry is written against it rather than predicting it. **PR #333 also edits this file but claims no version** (it inserts a live-defect block under §36's Finance routes and leaves the header line alone) and carries no section cross-reference at all, so it collides with neither. **Nothing here is renumbered to make room and no live section moves.** Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration. **No section is added** — §44 is amended in place — so Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-07 · v4.140 — **§55, §56 AND §57 ADDED: THREE FINANCE RULINGS — DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07.** **§55: REVENUE IS ORDERS, AND ONLY ORDERS.** Finance revenue counts orders across every channel — manual, Meituan, Eleme, mini app, till counter, and any channel a tenant adds later — one row per order, and **hand-typed `income_entries` rows are NOT revenue**: they are money in, on their own staircase row below the revenue line, feeding Net. **The defect it fixes is a real disagreement one tab apart** — Summary reported money-in from `retail_orders` while Transactions reported it from `income_entries`, never reconciling, so whichever a chart or an AI picked up was arbitrary. **§55 carries an OPEN survey question that binds any Finance chart**: the Summary counts `retail_orders`, the kitchen POS writes `sales_entries`, and if till-counter takings land in the latter Tacet's revenue is short today with no screen saying so. **§56: COST OF GOODS AND GROSS PROFIT STAY BLANK.** Both remain null and **both rows render blank**; Net is revenue minus operating expenses and is **structurally higher than true net, known and accepted**. **REJECTED: deriving cost of goods from ingredient purchases inside the window** — purchases are lumpy and sales are not, so a ¥2,000 delivery on the 3rd would crater one window and inflate the next with no change in the business. The two rows fill from §31 when it lands and from nothing else, and **the AI's finance read is forbidden margin, gross profit and cost of goods in any form, including inference** — a hard prompt constraint. **§57: FINANCE CHARTS ARE HAND-ROLLED SVG, SHARED WITH REPORTS.** No charting library; the primitives are **extracted into a shared module BEFORE Finance draws anything**, both pages consuming it, because two hand-rolled copies is the never-re-implemented rule broken and it drifts silently. **FIVE LIVE CROSS-REFERENCES ARE CORRECTED FORWARD AND NO DATED ENTRY IS REWRITTEN**, per this file's own convention that superseded text keeps its body and gains a pointer: §36's staircase spine gains a row and loses two; *Revenue derives from orders* is extended to exclude the typed ledger as well as `sales_entries`; **the "no remaining live writer" line under *Counter and market sales become orders* is QUALIFIED** — it states a consequence of a decision and was never a measurement, and §55 puts it back in question; and *A missing staircase step is shown and marked Not recorded* plus *Finance is not floored at the cutover date* are **SUPERSEDED IN PART** on the token only — the rows are blank rather than Not recorded, while never-hidden, never-zero, no-dash and the unconditional no-date-condition rule all stand, and the §1.12 seventh state is untouched everywhere else. **ONE COLLISION IS RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT RESOLVED**, against *Settlement receipts are excluded from Finance entirely*: §55 puts `income_entries` on the staircase, that subsection gives settlement no place on it, and **¥151,895.69 of the 26 live rows are settlement summaries filed as Mini App income with no column distinguishing them** — Transactions could draw them harmlessly because a list is not a summand, and a staircase row is. Neither ruling is bent to fit the other; a ruling from Ash is owed before the money-in row is summed. Docs only — no code, no schema, no routes. Appended as §55, §56 and §57 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38. **WRITTEN AS §52, §53 AND §54 AND RENUMBERED TO §55, §56 AND §57 ON REBASE, 2026-09-07 — DECIDED by Ash, who ruled that the rulings do not change and only the numbers move.** All three numbers were taken on main while this branch sat open: **§52** by PR #335's *a mirrored order has no parcels* (v4.137), **§53** by PR #336's *the Quick Stock and Add Stock feature switches are deleted* (v4.138) — itself renumbered on rebase for the same reason — and **§54** by PR #340's *the phone's order drawer reads the fields it already holds on a mirrored order* (v4.139). The version moved with them, from the **v4.137** this claimed to **v4.140**, v4.137 through v4.139 having been taken by those same three. **THE FOURTH COLLISION OF THIS KIND RECORDED HERE**, after the two branches that each defined a §39 and after §46/§47, and it arose the way every one of them did: branches open at once, each taking what was the next free number when it was written. **Nothing was renumbered to make room and no live section moved** — this branch took the next free numbers and every one of its own five forward references into the Finance subsections above moved with it, in the same pass. **The three rulings are untouched in substance**: revenue is orders and only orders, cost of goods and gross profit stay blank, Finance charts are hand-rolled SVG shared with Reports. **The heading style is also left as written** (`## §NN — TITLE`, where the sections above use `## NN. Title`), because the ruling was that only the numbers move; it is noted here rather than corrected silently.

2026-09-07 · v4.139 — **§54 ADDED: THE PHONE'S ORDER DRAWER READS THE FIELDS IT ALREADY HOLDS ON A MIRRORED ORDER — DECIDED by Ash**, from a phone, on GZ-140695: *"on PC you can find address and name. can gather all info that PC version have for gzgrocery order and add them to mobile"*. **§52 settled what the drawer must NOT show on a mirrored order; 2026-09-06 · v4.138 — **§53 ADDED: THE QUICK STOCK AND ADD STOCK FEATURE SWITCHES ARE DELETED AHEAD OF §48's LAST STEP — DECIDED by Ash**, whose framing was that Quick Stock became part of Tacet and is no longer connected to the kitchen app, so the two switches no longer describe anything an operator recognises. **The finding that prompted it is that both were already half-dead**: `features.quickStock` and `features.kitchenAdd` are not members of `lib/features.js` `FEATURES`, so they never had an entitlement layer and the `feature:` tags on `quickstock:add` / `quickstock:recount` in `lib/capabilities.js` could never fire; no role is unlocked and no flow moves. **A tenant holding either preference at `false` has that app switched back on**, and a migration deletes both `storefront_config` rows so a stored `false` cannot sit in the database meaning nothing. **The context endpoint keeps sending `enabled: true` as a constant** because `/stock` is an installed PWA and a cached shell that still tested the field would read an omitted `enabled` as falsy and show every staffer the off screen; it goes when the app does. **Rejected, both offered and declined:** narrowing the labels to name the separate `/stock` app and deleting them with it at §48 step 4, and wiring the flags into Tacet Mobile so the switches became true rather than removed.
