2026-09-06 · v4.137 — **§52 ADDED: A MIRRORED ORDER HAS NO PARCELS — DECIDED by Ash.** Raised from a phone, on a gzgrocery order: *"no way I'll for gzgrocery. this is mobile. no land it air option."* **The "Land · No waybill on this parcel yet — add it on the desktop" card the phone was showing is NOT a display bug — the parcel is real, and we create it on every read.** The chain is four steps and each one is correct in isolation: `scripts/gzgrocery-order-daemon.js` mirrors the order in as `fulfillment_type='delivery'` with no address; the order-detail GET runs `shipsNothing(o) ? [] : ensureShipments(id)`, and `shipsNothing` knows only pickup and counter — **it has never heard of a channel**; `planShipments` reads an empty city, finds neither Guangzhou nor Guangdong, and falls through to the air/land split, where the default `ship_modes` of `'air,land'` yields one **Land** parcel; and the legacy back-fill then stamps that phantom parcel dispatched and delivered because the order's status is `delivered`, which is what makes it render. **The instruction on the card could not be followed**: the desktop routes read-only channels to `renderReadonlyOrder`, which shows no parcels, no tracking and no waybill field at all — so the phone was sending an operator to a screen that does not offer the thing. **The desktop was never right, only silent**: it hid the rows it was still causing to be written on every drawer open. **Ruling: BOTH ENDS — the server stops planning them and the phone stops showing them.** Either alone is a half-fix, and the reason is asymmetric rather than belt-and-braces: stopping the planner leaves every gzgrocery order already opened once carrying its Land row, and guarding only the phone leaves the rows accumulating for every other reader. **Ruling: the rule is the CHANNEL SET, not gzgrocery** — Meituan (`routes/meituan-internal.js`) and Eleme (`routes/eleme-internal.js`) mirror in the same shape, `fulfillment_type='delivery'`, and grow the same phantom parcels; the set is the one the desktop's `ordIsReadonlyChannel` has always used. **The guard goes INSIDE `ensureShipments`, and that deviates from this repo's own convention deliberately** — fulfilment type is guarded at each of the eleven callers, and §24's split/undo entry records what that convention already cost: one branch that did not guard, creating Air/Land parcels for a counter sale, with no self-heal because the detail read returns `[]` for those orders rather than reconciling them. A channel that ships nothing of ours is a property of the ORDER, not of one read path, so it is enforced where it cannot be forgotten. **`shipsNothing` is deliberately NOT widened to cover channels**, and the reason is a live dependency rather than caution: `maybeEnqueueQingyunPush` gates on it, and a Meituan order IS fulfilled by a Qingyun rider — widening it would stop the rider push on the channel that most needs it, and the desktop's read-only drawer shows that rider card on purpose. **Mobile gains the channel set the desktop already had**: `viewOnly` was computed from a display key that has no Eleme entry, so an Eleme order was not read-only on the phone at all. **Not fixed here and recorded rather than left to be found:** the ship-by tile still says "Ship when ready · courier" on a mirrored order — same class of fiction, different tile, and a separate change; the waybill POST answers `no_shipments` with a **500** where a mirrored order deserves a 4xx; and mobile's `CH_ICON`/`CH_BACK` still have no Eleme entry, so an Eleme order wears the mini-app icon. No new user-facing strings, so `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched. Appended as §52 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-06 · v4.136 — **§51 ADDED: A KITCHEN REQUEST PRINTS ON PAPER WHEN IT REACHES THE QUEUE; ONE KITCHEN PRINTER, AND THE TENANT SAYS WHEN IT PRINTS — DECIDED by Ash.** A warehouse→kitchen request has announced itself by push since #261, which reaches a phone; Ash raised the gap as what it is — *"except of notification, i want to have a printer that printer the order for them in the kitchen"* — and the slip is an ADDITION, the push going out unchanged. **Nothing new is wired for it, which is most of why it was a day's work**: the store printers already run on Feieyun's cloud (`lib/feie.js`), the kitchen's printer is one more device on the SAME account, and the paid-order auto-print is copied wholesale — best-effort, fire-and-forget, recording BOTH outcomes. **Ruling: ONE kitchen printer, not a map keyed by location** — the per-location alternative was offered and declined, and **the cost is recorded rather than glossed**: a second kitchen means a config shape change, a migration and the routing touched again. The single SN is also what the data model already forces, so the two answers do not conflict today — a kitchen request carries NO locations at all, `routes/restock.js` nulling both ends for anything with a kitchen on it, so there is nothing for `printer.by_store` to key on. **Ruling: WHEN it prints is per-tenant and Roots prints on arrival only** — in Ash's words *"It depends on the tenant. For roots only when job arrive"* — because **the people who would read a completion slip are the people who just cooked it**, and whoever is waiting to hear is at the other end of a push. `delivered` never prints in any setting: the kitchen direction closes at `prepared` and `PUSH_AUDIENCE` already gives it no `delivered` entry. **The slip carries no money anywhere** — a production ticket is not priced, and a cost column would invite the kitchen to think a transfer owes it something. **A failed print is recorded, not swallowed** (`print_status`/`printed_at`/`print_error` on `restock_orders`, the three `retail_orders` already carries), and a result that never reached a printer is explicitly NOT a failure — no SN, event off, or not a kitchen request would otherwise put a red mark and a reprint button on a request that was never owed a slip. **TWO DEFECTS THE NEW SUITE FOUND ARE FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT and both would have shipped green**: the reprint leaned on `kitchenScopedOrder` to refuse a store transfer, which that middleware does not do for the roles that hold `restock:pick` — it is a SCOPE limiter confining a kitchen-only account, not an object-type guard — so the refusal was not refusing; and the reprint stamped its outcome unconditionally, so refusing a transfer stamped a failed print on the transfer. **The middleware is correctly left alone**, and the concern first filed against it — that it is "a no-op for a Tacet session" — was AUDITED THE SAME DAY AND WITHDRAWN in §51's NOT DECIDED, where the working is kept: across every shipped preset exactly one role is scoped by it, `kitchen`, and every other role reaching these endpoints works transfers legitimately. **A wrong finding is left corrected rather than deleted**, because the next reader is otherwise free to file it again. Vocabulary goes to v1.24 in the same commit per Rule 4's standing delegation — twenty-one entries, fifteen already live, six composed and all six in the settings block, with one live pair (`重打小票`) REJECTED and the rejection recorded, because `小票` is a receipt and this slip is not one. Appended as §51 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-06 · v4.135 — **§50 ADDED: IN-PAGE WECHAT PAYMENT FOR THE QR MENU IS PURSUED; ALIPAY STAYS A COUNTER PAYMENT — DECIDED by Ash.** §45's deferred in-page WeChat payment is picked up rather than left open: Ash ruled to build it, with Alipay customers continuing to pay at the counter on the existing cashier-pay path — no new architecture for that half. **The block §45 named is confirmed, and it is four things, not one**: no verified 服务号 (only the Mini Program's appid exists anywhere in the schema), no OAuth code capable of producing an openid outside the mini program, no JS-SDK code to trigger payment in-browser, and the merchant domain verification §44 already anticipated needing. **The first and the fourth are administrative steps with WeChat that only the merchant-account holder can complete and are not removed by this ruling** — recorded so a later session does not read "decided" as "credentials exist." The OAuth/JS-SDK build can proceed against WeChat's published contract without live credentials, mirroring how `lib/tenant-creds.js` already holds WeChat Pay's other secrets per tenant; there is no sandbox for a verified official account, so the first real end-to-end test is against production credentials. **Rejected: shipping WeChat Pay Native (a second scannable QR) as an interim** — buildable today with no new registration, but not what was asked for, and Ash chose the real in-page path over a stopgap. **§50 also carries two rulings taken the same day, and the first NARROWS §44.** **The kitchen ticket's trigger now follows the payment path**: an in-page WeChat order prints on payment success, not on submit, because a customer can submit and close WeChat and the food is already made — while Alipay, cash and anyone routed to the counter keep §44's print-on-submit unchanged; the consequence for §49's clock is recorded, an unpaid order dying at twenty minutes now leaving no printed ticket behind it. **There is no in-page payment fallback outside the WeChat browser**: a customer who opens the menu with a phone camera lands in Safari or Chrome where WeChat's in-page payment cannot run, and pays at the counter, **where staff scan the customer's payment code on the existing terminal** — no new code, and a Native QR rendered on the page is rejected as a worse counter than the counter. **§50 also records an apparent contradiction with §47 and dissolves it rather than leaving it to be found:** the PAYMENT page reads the user agent, because WeChat's in-page sheet cannot run outside WeChat and the customer who is outside it must reach the till rather than WeChat's error page; §47's byte-identical rule governs the MENU, still holds, and its three-user-agent test now runs with the rail switched on. Appended as §50 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.

2026-09-06 · v4.134 — **RULE 4's CHINESE LOCK IS AMENDED: THE DELEGATION BECOMES STANDING — DECIDED by Ash**, in his words, *"i want to change the role that you dont decide which chinese words to use. i want you to be able to decide yourself."* **The rule amended is `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` Rule 4**, which §30 rule 3 points at as the language half of its copy-never-compose principle; **§30 rule 3 itself is UNTOUCHED**, its subject being the identity of a value bound to an external system, which this does not reach. **It is the first time a rule in that document changes rather than gaining a section**, and it goes to v1.19; rules 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 there are unchanged. **The default flips**: whoever is building decides the Chinese and does not stop, where before the answer when nothing fit was to leave the string blocked and ship the control without it. The three preferences from the 2026-09-02 amendment keep their order — copy a live pair, lift from the source, compose — and **only the last one's status moves, from a last resort carrying a review debt to an ordinary outcome.** **WHAT IS NOT DELEGATED IS COMPOSING SILENTLY**, and that is the whole of what the amendment holds back: every composed pair is still written into the vocabulary document, marked composed and by whom, with the live candidates it rejected, **in the same commit as the code that uses it**. That is not a hedge against the ruling — Ash changed WHO DECIDES, not WHETHER IT IS WRITTEN DOWN — and the document had already ruled on the distinction in its own words at v1.17: *composing Chinese is not the failure, composing it silently is.* An undeclared string is indistinguishable from a locked one to everyone who comes after; a declared one can be read, corrected and locked. **PROVISIONAL is retained and narrowed** to pairs whose CONCEPT is unsettled, rather than to strings a machine rather than a person chose. **THE COST IS RECORDED BESIDE THE BENEFIT rather than left implicit**: the rule being lifted is the one that stopped a garbled string reaching a customer, its failure mode is SILENT — a wrong character looks correct to whoever composed it and wrong to every Chinese reader who sees it — and that risk now sits with Ash to catch on review instead of with a blocked control. It was lifted for a real cost of its own: work stalled on labels, and a control shipping without its Chinese half is a worse screen than one carrying a correctable label. **`CLAUDE.md`'s Chinese strings section is rewritten in the same pass and the change is named here rather than slipped in**, per that file's own rule about changes to how sessions work. **The first exercise ships with it**: `Pick-up number` · `取餐号`, the label on §49's counter number in the orders list and the order drawer, composed under the delegation and declared in the vocabulary document's new section with the two live candidates it rejected — `序号`, a SKU-rule counter, and `取餐`, a rider's pickup verb in `lib/tracking.js`'s courier stages. Docs, one label and its tests; the rule change is the substance.

2026-09-06 · v4.133 — **§49 ADDED: THE SHORT ORDER CODE IS A PLAIN NUMBER THAT RESETS EACH TRADING DAY, AND AN UNPAID COUNTER ORDER DIES AT TWENTY MINUTES — DECIDED by Ash.** §44 said a QR order issues a short code "what staff use to retrieve the order" and did not say what it looks like; this says. **Plain numbers, reset daily** — the day's first order is 1, tomorrow's first is 1 again, with no prefix, no letter, no shop initial and no date inside it. **Per shop, per TRADING day**, resolved through `lib/business-date.js` for the order's own location, so a shop trading past midnight keeps one sequence for one night's work and the reset follows the location's timezone rather than the server's. **The consequence is stated rather than discovered: the code is NOT unique** — two shops may both call number 7 on the same afternoon — so it is never an identifier, nothing joins or reconciles on it, `order_no` remains the order's identity everywhere else, and any screen or report showing a short code shows it with its shop and its date or not at all. **The rejected alternatives are recorded so they are not re-proposed:** a random code cannot be called across a noisy counter, a never-resetting one reaches five digits within a month at one shop, and a prefixed one (`TH-7`) mints tenant data — a shop initial — which §0 forbids. **§49 also records the counter clock: an unpaid counter order is cancelled after twenty minutes, or by staff at any moment, whichever is first**, closing the timing §45 deliberately left open when it exempted counter orders from the existing sweeps. It **keys on the order's age (`placed_at`) and not on a reservation**, because a made-here order reserves nothing under §43 and a reservation-walking sweep would let it live forever. `orders.counterAutoCancelMinutes` sets it per tenant and `0` switches it off, restoring staff-only cancellation. **That half is recorded AFTER the code that implements it shipped, and the section says so rather than tidying it away** — the wrong order under `CLAUDE.md`'s decisions-before-code rule, named where the next reader will see it. **The code landing with this entry is step 5b part 2 of the location commerce module: `POST /s/:shopCode/order`, the endpoint behind the menu page.** Prices, every one of them, are read from `shop_listings` inside the handler and a price posted by the customer is ignored; availability is re-checked at submit on §47's rules rather than trusted from a page that may be minutes old; a submit that cannot be honoured whole is refused whole rather than silently shortened; the order is an ordinary `pending_payment` counter order from the moment it exists, because a status no screen and no sweep understands would hide it from both. **The page itself still carries no cart** — that is the next piece — and a test holds it to that. **Two columns are added to `retail_orders`** (`shop_order_code`, `shop_order_date`) with an index, and `routes/retail.js` exports three more helpers so the endpoint's order numbering, tax and cost snapshot cannot drift from the till's. Code, docs, schema and one migration; no change to any existing route's behaviour.

2026-09-06 · v4.132 — **§48 ADDED: THE STANDALONE STOCK APP IS RETIRED, AND IT IS MIGRATED BEFORE IT IS DELETED — DECIDED by Ash.** There is no second app: `/stock` retires and every job it holds moves into Tacet Mobile. **The ORDER is part of the ruling rather than a preference** — deleting first strands two roles and six flows that exist nowhere else, and the section carries the inventory that makes that a fact rather than an estimate. **Already in Tacet:** Receiving, Waste, Purchasing, Delivery, Inbox, Sales, Trend, Invoices, New order, and Add stock with §46's count and correction. **In `/stock` only, with no home in Tacet:** Pick; Receive delivery, which is the store end of a transfer and NOT the supplier Receiving row; Ask the kitchen; Ask for stock; Ready from the kitchen; Quick stock, the absolute recount that is the whole job of `store_stock`; and Log a batch. Kitchen queue and Transfers have rows already but both are departures rather than screens. **TWO ROLES ARE LOCKED TO THE APP BEING DELETED**: `kitchen` and `store_stock` carry `stock_app_only`, server.js refuses them Tacet Mobile outright and redirects `/retail-admin` and `/backend/*` back to `/stock`, so deleting before unlocking leaves both with nothing to open; `lib/stock-app-only.js` retires with the confinement. **It is an installed PWA** with its own manifest and icons on staff phones, so `/stock` leaves a redirect into Tacet rather than a 404 and the manifest goes only once nobody is opening the shortcut. **Four steps, in order**: §46's port onto Tacet's Add stock screen (done); move the homeless flows one at a time; unlock Tacet Mobile for both roles once and only once their work lives there; then delete the app, its login, its manifest, its routes and its suites, leaving the redirect. **What must not happen at any point is a role with no app.** Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration.

2026-09-06 · v4.130 — **§46 ADDED: A KITCHEN SHARING A FACILITY WITH THE SHELF SEES THE COUNT AND MAY CORRECT IT, AND A CORRECTION IS NEVER A BATCH — DECIDED by Ash.** The kitchen Add stock app has never shown a quantity, and that is enforced in three places rather than merely unimplemented: the stock list is rebuilt for a kitchen operator as id, names and SKU only, the stock PATCH refuses anything but a `delta` with `kitchen_add_only`, and the screen hides the Low/Out chips, renders `+N` in place of the total and opens its keypad on the pending amount. **The recorded reasoning is not overturned** — production is request-driven, the queue and the "What you made" prefill say what to make, and a visible shelf number invites a tray nobody asked for — **but it assumed the shelf is somewhere the kitchen cannot see, and at Tianhe it is the same facility.** **Ruling: where the kitchen and the shelf share a facility, the count is shown and may be corrected**, granted per tenant and defaulting off, because an off-site kitchen is the case the current behaviour was written for and remains correct for it. **A total shown without a way to fix a mismatch is the worse design**: the operator who reads 45 and counts 40 has no honest door and one dishonest one — tapping +5 through the add path — and that write enters the record as food that was cooked. §39 ruling 7 settled the same shape on a purchase-order receipt: if 8 arrived against 10, the 10 is the lie and blocking the correction protects it. **Ruling: adding and correcting are two writes and the app must never let one become the other** — a positive delta recorded as production, an absolute count recorded as a recount, separate controls and separate entries; merged, every yield figure downstream becomes a guess, which is what `made_fewer` exists to prevent in the production gap. **Ruling: a correction that lowers the count asks why, and the question is a fork rather than a reason picker** — the count was wrong, which saves; or something is actually gone, which does not save at all and routes the loss to whoever holds `waste:record`, **the shelf figure not moving until they record it.** **THE KITCHEN RECORDS NO WASTE ON THIS SCREEN and the waste vocabulary is deliberately absent from it — DECIDED by Ash.** The obvious design is recorded as rejected: offering the waste codes here and writing a record from them puts loss-recording in the kitchen's hands through a side door, and offering them without writing a record is worse, a loss named by the operator and filed nowhere. **Ruling: only a downward correction asks why; a correction that raises the count is saved without a question** — the friction argument won, raising a count being overwhelmingly a miscount, and the cost is named rather than left to be discovered: an unlogged batch entering that way leaves no reason behind it, and only the entry itself distinguishes it, a recount being recorded as a recount and never as production. **Ruling: the batch screen keeps its full gap vocabulary, waste codes included.** `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on `production:log`, which the kitchen preset holds, and it already writes a waste record through `recordProductWaste` when the gap is a loss — **so the kitchen already records waste there, and the no-waste rule does not reach it.** The distinction ruled: a gap on a batch just made, against a request that says how many were expected, is production reporting bounded by that batch; opening a fridge and writing off what is in it is not. Stripping the seven codes would file two broken jars as "made fewer" and collapse the distinction `made_fewer` exists to hold open. **THE GRANT IS AN EXISTING CAPABILITY, NOT A NEW FLAG.** `quickstock:recount` (快速库存—盘点(门店)) is already in the registry, already held by the `store_stock` preset and already accepted by `lib/cap-routes.js` for the stock routes; granting it to a tenant's kitchen role is the whole mechanism, and it stays off in the kitchen preset. **The server must therefore decide by capability and not by job title** — `routes/retail-inventory.js` branches on `req.backendUser.role === 'kitchen'` today, which is why the behaviour is all-or-nothing, and `req.caps` is resolved on every request regardless of `tenants.rbac_enforce`, so reading it needs no tenant to switch enforcement on. **The API inconsistency is closed by the same change**: `requireInventoryRead` also admits a plain `users` row carrying `retail_store_id` with no `retail` permission, and such a row whose role is `kitchen` lands in add mode with quantities in the response and only the UI hiding them; keying the strip on the grant rather than the role covers both realms. **One thing stays NOT DECIDED and it blocks one control rather than the build**: the Chinese for the fork's two answers, with no live string in the tree fitting either — blocked for Ash per §30, the control shipping without them rather than composing them. Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration.

2026-09-06 · v4.131 — **§47 ADDED: A STOCKED LISTING WITH NO COUNTED STOCK AT ITS SHOP IS SOLD OUT — DECIDED by Ash**, and the public QR menu is built at `/s/:shopCode`. **The ruling settles an edge §42 left open.** §42 says a stocked item becomes unavailable when store stock reaches zero; it does not say what a shop menu shows for a product the location has NEVER counted, which is a different record — absent rather than zero. **Ash ruled it sold out**: a stocked listing claims the shop holds stock, a shop that has never counted any holds none anyone can vouch for, and absent is no claim rather than a smaller one. **The online store deliberately answers the opposite way and the divergence is recorded rather than reconciled** — its catalogue availability falls back to a product's flat legacy quantity when no per-location shelf record exists anywhere, so a new product is not born sold out before anyone stocks it, which is right for a catalogue offering to fulfil from wherever stock is and wrong for a menu offering to hand something over at one counter now. **Neither is to be changed to match the other.** Made-here listings are unaffected: they have no shelf record by design and §42's manual switch is their whole availability. **Appended as §47 under the append-only convention; Related documents stays at §38.** §47's body carries no `file:line` by instruction. **The code that lands with it is step 5a of the location commerce module: the public QR menu page, and only the page.** No cart, no ordering and no order creation — that is step 5b, deliberately built behind this so the menu can be reviewed and corrected while the order flow is written. The page is server-rendered in one response, mobile-only, and carries no Roots literal: colour, fonts, brand name and currency all come from the tenant's own configuration through the same brand-theme map the mini app and the web storefront already share, so it renders as a Roots page for Roots without being one in the code (§0). **Both languages ship in the DOM and CSS chooses**, which is what makes the toggle a class swap rather than a reload — a reload would re-run detection, which §26's narrowing forbids once the reader has chosen. Opening language resolves session toggle, then `?lang=`, then the client's own language, then English. **Nothing on the page branches on the user agent**, WeChat's included, and a test holds that line. **Chinese is copied, never composed:** 售罄 (sold out) and 暂无商品 / 请稍后再来 (the empty menu) are already live on the web storefront and are reused verbatim; category headings come from the tenant's own bilingual tree and product names from its own catalogue. **Two labels are not rendered at all rather than minted:** the uncategorised group has no heading, and there is no "wrong code" wording — **an unresolvable code, a switched-off shop and a switched-off location all return the empty-menu page byte-identically at 404**, which also stops the page acting as an oracle for guessed codes, the shop code being the whole of what protects one shop's — and one tenant's — prices from anyone editing the address bar. **Three changes to how sessions and builds work are named rather than slipped in, per `CLAUDE.md`:** the public-tenant middleware is mounted on `/s` so the menu reads the right tenant's catalogue by Host (the public tracking page's failure to do this is filed for the audit, not fixed here); `scripts/test_shop_listings.js`'s reader allowlist admits the new route, its guard otherwise intact; and `routes/retail.js` exports two helpers so the menu's photo fallback and money format cannot drift from the storefront's. **A pre-launch gate ships with it:** `scripts/check_shop_listing_names.js` refuses a shop whose listed products lack an English or a Chinese name, naming the product and the language — §44 makes both names a launch prerequisite and nothing enforced it. It is a script rather than a gate on shop activation because activation runs through an existing admin route this build does not touch. Code, docs and tests; no schema, no migration, no change to any existing route's behaviour.

**RENUMBERED FROM §46 TO §47 ON MERGE, 2026-09-06.** This section was written as §46 on an unmerged branch while PR #284 was writing a different §46 on another. #284 merged first, so its §46 — a kitchen sharing a facility with the shelf may correct the count — is the live one and keeps the number; this one takes the next. **Nothing was renumbered to make room and no live section moved**, which is the whole of the append-only rule at the head of this file. The collision is the second of its kind recorded here (the first was two branches each defining a §39) and it arose the same way: two branches open at once, each taking what was the next free number when it was written. **Version becomes v4.131**; v4.130 is #284's and is not touched.

2026-09-05 · v4.129 — **§41–§45 ADDED: A SHOP IS A RECORD ATTACHED TO A LOCATION, FULFILMENT MODE LIVES ON THE SHOP LISTING, MATERIALS MAY BE HELD AT ANY LOCATION, QR ORDERING IS A PUBLIC WEB PAGE, AND A QR ORDER RESERVES ON SUBMIT AND DECREMENTS ON PAID — DECIDED by Ash.** Five sections appended under the append-only convention v4.125 adopted; Related documents stays at §38. **§41** — a shop is a separate record attached to a location, not columns on it; a location with no shop record has no menu, no QR code, no till, no opening hours and no payment binding, and the record's presence is the module gate, with no separate feature flag. **§42** — one catalogue, no menu-items entity; a shop listing joins a product to a shop and carries the price there and the fulfilment mode, **stocked** or **made here**, a property of the listing and never of the product. **§43** — materials at a shop are the same records as materials anywhere else, distinguished only by location id per §34, transferred on the same mechanism as finished goods, and a transfer is a movement of value rather than a cost event, on §37's double-count reasoning. **§44** — the in-location ordering surface is a public web page per shop opened by QR, no login, no phone number, order created unpaid at `pending_payment`, ticket prints on submit, paid at the counter; in-page WeChat payment is deferred on a verified 服务号. **§45** — physical stock still decrements on paid; a QR order reserves on submit through the existing reservation path the counter path never used, cancel releases the reservation, and the stale-order and reservation sweeps must not apply to counter-fulfilment orders on their existing timings. **The five contradictions the append surfaced were put to Ash and ruled the same day, and four of the rulings NARROW THE NEW SECTIONS rather than the old ones.** **§13's "`counter` is dead; delete it" is marked superseded by §45** — factually out of date, since `public/till.html` writes `fulfillment_type='counter'` through the manual-order endpoint and the sales summary buckets on it (`routes/retail.js:13493`). **§3's "materials are kitchen-only" and "everything sold is packed first" are marked superseded in part by §42 and §43**; the rest of §3 stands. **§42 is narrowed against §16**: shop listings govern availability only where a shop record exists, locations without one keep the product-level IN SHOP state, and §16 is not superseded. **§42 and §43 are narrowed against §29 and §31 rule 6**: packaging and label lines are excluded from made-here depletion, being cost carried by the product and never countable stock — a cup is costed into the drink and never counted at the shop — and packaging is neither transferred as stock nor depleted on sale. **§43 is narrowed against §10**: the never-block rule applies only to material shortfalls on made-here items, and negative-stock policy for finished goods remains the tenant setting §10 defines. Softer cross-references in §9, §6, §32, §39 and §28 are noted and left unedited; the dated entries in §24 and §9 are not touched. **The four open questions the append raised on §44 were then put to Ash and ruled the same day; §44 gains four paragraphs.** **Channel and source**: till and QR sales share the single channel value `shop` and are never split, with order source recorded separately so scan uptake can be measured without dividing a shop's revenue across two channel lines — and the existing counter rows tagged channel `wechat` are named as a defect, a tender name standing where a channel belongs, with remediation noted for a separate ruling. **Routing**: the menu page is served at `/s/:shopCode`, public, unauthenticated and outside the admin route tree, where `shopCode` is a non-sequential opaque code that is never a shop id, never derivable from one, and never typed — a guessable URL would expose other shops' and other tenants' menus and pricing. **Domain**: the page is served from the existing customer-facing domain under `/s/`; a new domain is rejected for launch on ICP filing and WeChat merchant domain verification grounds, and a tenant-neutral domain remains a later branding decision that arrives as a redirect. **Language**: the page opens in the language detected from the client — inside the WeChat browser, WeChat's own language setting rather than the device OS — with a mandatory visible toggle as the correction, and consequently every product listed at a shop requires both a Chinese and an English name before launch, the Chinese string copied or supplied per §30 and never composed. **Two consequential corrections follow from those rulings.** **§14 gains `shop` as an eighth channel** — sales originating at a physical shop, till or QR, with the two distinguished by order source and not by channel — **and a channel-versus-tender note**: channel is where a sale originated as a business relationship, tender is how it was paid, and a tender name is never a valid channel value. **§44's opening paragraph is corrected** to say the QR carries an opaque shop code that resolves to the shop, not the shop id; the earlier wording predated the Routing ruling and contradicted it. **§26 IS NARROWED TO IDENTIFIED SURFACES, NOT OVERTURNED — DECIDED by Ash.** §44's language ruling contradicted §26's *NO AUTO-DETECTION* outright; Ash ruled that auto-detection stands for the public QR menu and that §26 is narrowed rather than reversed. §26 gains a narrowing note in the house blockquote form and nothing in its body is edited: it governs surfaces where the reader is identified — admin, staff tools, any signed-in customer surface — because its purpose is that a chosen language is never silently overridden, and it does not reach anonymous public surfaces with no reader identity and no stored preference, where an opening language may be inferred, the inference selects only the initial render, an explicit language control must be present, and a reader's use of it governs for the rest of the session and is never re-inferred. §44's Language paragraph is cross-referenced as that anonymous-surface exception. **§43 IS REWRITTEN TO DEFER MATERIAL STOCK ENTIRELY, AND ITS FALSE HISTORY IS WITHDRAWN — DECIDED by Ash.** The Step 3 survey established that **no material quantity has ever been held anywhere in this system**: materials and ingredients are one table, nothing on it holds an amount, no per-location material stock table exists, and the invariant is asserted against the live database by `scripts/diagnose_phase1b_live.js`. **§43's opening sentence — that materials had historically been held at the kitchen — was therefore wrong when it was written, and it is WITHDRAWN rather than superseded;** the section is new and unmerged, so its body is replaced outright rather than carrying a marker over a claim nobody should read. **The section keeps its number and now defers rather than rules:** materials are cut from the location commerce launch scope entirely. **A made-here item consumes no counted material stock** — its build lines and its materials' unit costs give a true cost and a true margin, which is the half that works, while an on-hand figure for a material is simply not tracked and not claimed: **a shop knows what a drink costs it and does not claim to know how much milk is in the fridge.** **Finished goods are untouched** — transferred on the existing store-to-store mechanism, decremented on the paid transition per §45. **Material quantities, a kitchen location row, materials moving through transfers, and consumption at the point of sale are one SEPARATE project, and none of them is a dependency of the QR menu or of any shop launch.** **Three constraints that project inherits are recorded so they are not rediscovered:** the stock ledger and `waste_records` both carry hard foreign keys to `retail_stores`, so **the kitchen cannot be written against stock or loss until it has a store row — a foreign key, not a missing flag**, which is why kitchen-ness lives on transaction columns today; creating that row **redefines the tenant's business day**, because `lib/business-date.js` falls back to the first active store carrying a timezone, ordered by sort order; and **a second active store switches on the wait-longer prompt at customer checkout**, which order routing suppresses only while there is one. **One positive finding is recorded beside them: `waste_records` already carries the material subject in full** — `subject_type`, `material_id`, the exclusive-or CHECK and the foreign key to `ingredients` — **and only the API refuses it**, so material waste will need the API opened and a writer added rather than a schema change. **That is the unblocker §32's addendum named** when it deferred the material subject until material stock was designed; this section is that decision and it defers, so the refusal stands. **§42's made-here bullet is corrected in the same pass** to say the build lines determine cost rather than depleting material stock; packaging remains cost-only per §29 and §31 rule 6, unchanged. **§3's superseded-in-part marker is narrowed to §42 alone**, since the half of it resting on materials being held at a location no longer stands. **A second house-rules block is added at the head of the file: a `file:line` citation in a dated entry is a historical coordinate and must be re-verified before use, never quoted as a current position.** The same survey re-read every position it needed and found drift of up to several thousand lines across the `docs/` surveys and design notes — `retail_stores` cited at `database.js:2565` now sits at `:3383` — **while the prose at those addresses held up in every case**, so the coordinates rotted and the findings did not. **Version stays v4.129 and no new entry is opened.** Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration.

2026-09-04 · v4.128 — **§39 GAINS RULING 7: A DOWNWARD CORRECTION ON A PURCHASE-ORDER RECEIPT GOES NEGATIVE — DECIDED by Ash, AND E2 IS CLOSED.** E2 was the last thing gating implementation of any kind and had been recorded with only two candidate behaviours — **clamp silently** or **refuse**; **Ash chose a third nobody had proposed.** **If only 8 boxes actually arrived against 10 on the system, the 10 is the lie and blocking the correction protects it** — a negative balance is ugly and true, and says stock was sold that was never held. This is Ruling 1's reasoning arriving at the other end of the same movement. **The clamp was doing something worse than permitting a bad number: it DISCARDED a real one** — removing 5 from a shelf of 3 removed 3 and recorded −3, with nothing anywhere saying 2 were unaccounted for, and on a transfer it floored the outbound half while the inbound half added the full figure, so a cleanly committed transaction **created units from nothing.** **The asymmetry with returns is now deliberate rather than deferred: returns refuse, corrections go negative**, because a return asserts goods left a shelf they were never on while a correction asserts the count was always wrong. **THREE THINGS SHIP WITH IT AND THE RULING DOES NOT STAND WITHOUT THEM: (1)** the "Needs you" dashboard filtered out-of-stock on `= 0`, so a negative matched neither that card nor the low-stock one and **vanished from the panel entirely — not shown wrong, shown nowhere**; both the count and the preview clauses move to `<= 0` together, because they are separate queries and a partial fix gives a card whose number and list disagree, while Low keeps `> 0` so nothing appears on both. **(2)** the Kitchen Quick Stock delta path is guarded by name (`delta_must_be_positive`) — its contract is "I made N more", and a reduction belongs on the absolute recount. **(3)** `docs/purchase-returns.md` item 3 is struck through and superseded in the same change. **Recorded debt, untouched: the four channel self-clamps** (Meituan, Eleme, Guanyi, gzgrocery) compute `Math.max(0, …)` in JavaScript and never reached this clamp, so they keep doing the very thing this ruling rejects. **`docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md` E2 loses its *STILL OPEN* heading and its "Do not act on it" line**, which would otherwise tell the next reader not to act on something already acted on. **Ruling 7 is the first of the seven to land with its code in the same change**, because deleting the clamp and making the negative visible are one act.

2026-09-04 · v4.127 — **§40 ADDED: A BATCH SIZE IS THE SUM OF WHAT WENT INTO THE POT, AND A SERVING COUNT FOLLOWS FROM IT — REQUESTED by Ash.** `recipes.batch_size` was a hand-typed number, and it is the number every per-gram cost divides by: `batchCost / batch_size` is `costPerGram`, which `lib/recipe-rollup.js` stamps onto a made material's unit cost, which reaches a product's cost and its margin. **It is now derived** — the sum of the ingredient lines, in grams — **and `servings` follows it as `batch_size / serving_size`, floored.** Three facts make that honest and all three are recorded rather than assumed. **NOT EVERYTHING THAT GOES IN COMES OUT:** `recipe_ingredients.in_yield` (default 1) marks a line that is paid for and discarded — a stock brewed for its flavour and poured away — and such a line is **still costed in full**; only the weight changes. **A RECIPE MAY STILL STATE ITS OWN YIELD:** `recipes.batch_size_auto` / `servings_auto` (default 1, decided independently of one another) turn the derivation off for reduction, evaporation, trim loss, or a pack filled to a stated weight — the operator's figure is the true one there, and the editor offers the ingredient total rather than applying it. **AND THE SUM IS REFUSED RATHER THAN UNDERSTATED:** grams are only added to grams, so one line in ml or pcs blocks the whole derivation and the recipe keeps whatever batch size it had, the editor naming the lines standing in the way. That is §7's addendum applied to weight instead of to price — a density and a piece weight are properties of a material and there are none to find — and it is the load-bearing half: **a batch size short one ingredient overstates cost per gram silently, all the way down to a margin, while an absent one has always refused out loud** (`lib/recipe-rollup.js`'s `no_batch_size`). Mass units convert among themselves with exact, stated factors and nothing crosses a dimension. **NO LIVE FIGURE MOVES ON DEPLOY:** `database.js`'s `recipe_yield_auto_v1` marks every recipe that already carried a typed batch size — or a typed serving count, decided separately — as stating it, so the derivation reaches only the recipes that had nothing, which are exactly the ones the cost cascade refuses today. **ONE DERIVATION, AS §29's cost half already is:** `computeYield` / `resolveYield` live in `lib/recipe-cost.js` beside `computeRecipeCost`, which now resolves both figures before dividing by either, so the material rollup, the Excel export, the waste valuation and the kitchen Cost Sheet inherit it without knowing it exists. **The column still follows the derivation** (`lib/recipe-yield.js`, called by both recipe doors after the lines are written and before the recompute divides by them) because a dozen readers — batch sheets, the kitchen picker, the AI tool surface — read `recipes.batch_size` raw and must never see a stale figure. **Both doors carry `in_yield` across their delete-and-reinsert**, including the kitchen Cost Sheet, which has no control for it: without that, a save from a screen that knows nothing about the flag would quietly put a discarded ingredient back into the batch weight. **Appended as §40 under the append-only convention v4.125 adopted — Related documents stays at §38 and is not moved.** A new decision that reverses no earlier rule; §7's addendum and §29's derivation rule are applied, not amended. Code, schema and one migration; no route contract changes.

2026-09-03 · v4.126 — **§39 GAINS RULING 6: A BATCH YIELDS ONE PRODUCT OR SEVERAL, AND THE MANY-PRODUCTS SHAPE IS THE MODEL — DECIDED by Ash.** This closes **the last open question** in `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md`; all six are now answered and **nothing in that document's open-questions list gates implementation.** **Both cases happen at Roots**, so the general shape is adopted **because it contains the specific one** — a single-product batch is a split with one line in it — and **there are not two code paths**, because a one-product branch beside a many-product branch is two implementations of one fact and they drift. **A batch records what came out of it per product: a link table, not a column**, one row per (batch, product, quantity); **`recipe_id` keeps its job — what was made from what — and does not determine what the batch yielded.** **The split is entered, never inferred**: it varies, so Tacet cannot compute it, must not default it from the recipe, and must not guess. **But the common case must not become a form** — a recipe that has only ever made one product pre-fills it and asks only for the quantity, one confirm, **the same code path with one line already filled**; a pre-fill offered for confirmation is convenience, never inference, and must never commit unconfirmed. **Stock increments per output line, one ledger row per product.** **Two proposals in the schema survey are WITHDRAWN by this ruling** — a `recipes.output_product_id` column and a `UNIQUE` index on `store_products.recipe_id` — because each asserts one recipe makes at most one product, which is now known to be false; the mapping must be single-valued **in neither direction**. **The scoping consequence is stated plainly rather than implied: production wiring is larger than a column addition and is its own brief, sequenced after the two-step transfer ships** — (1) a recipe→product mapping pointing the right way, (2) the batch output table, (3) the split-entry UI with the one-line pre-fill, (4) the stock increment. **Step 1 is the gate and carries a data question that is Ash's: the 36 ambiguous pairs `store_products_recipe_link_v1` deliberately left unlinked, which per §29's addendum nobody may resolve by inference.** **Also recorded: E2, the purchase-order receiving downward correction, is now the ONLY thing gating implementation, and it blocks ONE migration step (the clamp deletion), not the migration** — the two-step transfer can ship complete with the clamp still in place; it simply cannot ship honest until that step lands. **And Ruling 2's safeguard gains the column that makes it real:** an auto-settled line writes `qty_received`, so without a separate `auto_settled_at` stamp it would be byte-identical to a counted line and the permanent mark would be decorative — it is now in the migration steps, not only in the column proposal. **The two copies of `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md` stay as they are, by Ash's call**: the primary document naming the abandoned branch as superseded is sufficient, and no commit is made to an abandoned branch to satisfy a file count. Docs only; no code, no migration.
2026-09-03 · v4.125 — **THE APPENDIX-LAST CONVENTION IS RETIRED; APPEND-ONLY REPLACES IT — DECIDED by Ash. §39 GAINS FIVE RULINGS AND A PRECEDENCE RULE.** **The numbering rule is now stated once, at the top of this file, and it is the only place it lives:** section numbers are permanent, new sections append and take the next number wherever Related documents sits, **nothing is ever renumbered.** **Why the old convention went:** "the reference appendix stays last" was written down three times — v4.97-era, v4.101, v4.124 — but **only ever as narration inside changelog entries**, which is where a rule goes to be missed. v4.100 broke it once. A later session broke it again, and this time the repair caused the damage the rule was meant to prevent: **two unmerged branches each defining a §39**, one of them having renumbered a live section (Related documents §38 → §39) to obey a convention the other branch had never seen. **A number that moves is a citation that breaks; an appendix that is not last is only untidy.** The three old entries are historical and are **not edited** — the block at the top overrides them, and says so, so a future session meeting one of them does not reinstate the convention. **§39 gains a PRECEDENCE rule that dissolves an apparent contradiction rather than settling it:** "what the store counts is what the store holds" and the new end-of-day auto-settle **never apply to the same line** — a counted quantity always sets stock, the sent quantity is used only where nobody counted, and such a line is permanently marked unverified. **The record never prefers the warehouse's number to the counter's; it falls back to it only where there is no counter's number at all.** A counted **zero** outranks the sent figure absolutely. **§39 also gains five rulings** taken against `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md` after it was written, closing four of its six open questions: **a dispatch is never blocked by the record** (the zero clamp at `lib/inventory.js:1084` is deleted — **overruling that document's own recommendation that it should throw instead**); **abandoned counts auto-settle at end of trading day**, per tenant, conditional on a mandatory repeat-offender safeguard without which the ruling does not stand; **`storefront_config` as is**, with the tenant-handle requirement spelled out for the sweep that runs outside any request; **`qty_received` is `REAL`**; and **`delivered` stays** as a pure logistics timestamp. **Two things stay open and one of them BLOCKS the first ruling:** whether a recipe can yield more than one sellable product, and the purchase-order receiving downward correction, which now has three possible behaviours — clamp, refuse, or go negative — of which only the first two were ever considered. **Branch consolidation, recorded so the collision is not repeated:** `claude/roots-v2-stock-movement-survey-gkss7v` is primary and holds the code, the design artboards and the 502-line schema document; `claude/stock-movement-schema-decisions-av2e21` was a parallel document written without sight of it and is **superseded and abandoned**, its content folded in. Docs only; no code, no migration.
2026-09-02 · v4.124 — **§37 ADDED: COURIER COST IS A MANUAL EXPENSE ENTRY, AND NOTHING IN TACET MAY DEDUCT IT PER ORDER — DECIDED by Ash.** The money we pay a courier — JD, Qingyun/跑腿, SF, or in-house — is recorded **only** as a manual expense entry, and **no screen, report or order-level figure may deduct a courier cost from revenue or from margin.** The expense ledger is its single home. **The reason is a double-count, and it is not hypothetical: `expense_entries` already carries roughly ¥13,005 of courier spend across five channel-specific categories a person typed** — JD Delivery ¥7,913.40, Paotui Delivery ¥4,201.27, In House Delivery ¥1,101.02, SF Express ¥471.94, Meituan Delivery ¥332.90 — **so a per-order deduction would double-count all of it, over periods a report can already be run across.** **This ANSWERS the one question the courier-cost survey could not:** that survey established from code that no column anywhere holds a courier charge, and named as unanswerable whether the spend was nonetheless already in the ledger under names nobody chose. It was, under five of them. **The platform's own rider is NOT our cost and must not be recorded twice from the other side either:** on Meituan and Eleme the platform nets its delivery cost out of settlement before paying us, so it is already inside 预计收入 — **the test is whether money left our account for that leg, not which channel the order came from.** **The settlement panel keeps its meaning:** it shows what a platform pays us with the platform's commission netted out, and must not gain what we pay a courier, or it becomes a margin panel wearing a settlement panel's name and disagreeing with the platform screen it exists to agree with. **AUTOMATIC CAPTURE IS NOT PURSUED, and the survey findings are recorded so it is not re-attempted from scratch.** Qingyun's quoted `totalFee` is displayed and spent but never written; quote and settlement diverge by five mechanisms, **one firing on every dispatch** (the route re-quotes and spends the fresh figure, not the one the operator saw); **the settled truth is the prepaid wallet ledger, which nothing reads**; and `delivery_jobs.raw_order` carries no fee — `amountInfo` all zeros, `shippingFee -1` — which closes the survey's one recovery candidate. **JD declares a hardcoded 1kg / 100cm³ on every waybill** because the admin UI sends only shipment id, product and package count, **so no creation-time figure could be real**; the true charge is JD's weighing after pickup and the earliest sight of it is the merchant bill, and **no JD response has ever been retained.** Meituan, Eleme and GZ Grocery have nothing to capture. **If it is ever revisited it needs the Qingyun wallet ledger and JD's monthly bill AND a companion decision removing courier spend from the expense ledger — one or the other, never both**, which is the load-bearing clause: a later session that builds capture without withdrawing the ledger half will have built the double-count while it looks like progress. **Two items stay open and are NOT resolved:** two `Meituan Delivery (to customer)` rows totalling ¥332.90 need checking — already-netted platform fee (double-counted today) or a directly-paid leg (correct), and nothing in the ledger records which; and the Dashboard's conflation of platform customer-paid delivery with our own webstore charges, pre-existing and unchanged. **Related documents moves from §37 to §38, on the convention v4.101 restated — the reference appendix stays last.** The three inbound `§37` mentions are all in this changelog and are historical, so none is edited. The two surveys behind this ruling are unmerged branch documents (`claude/courier-cost-survey-e5s4a6`, `claude/jd-qingyun-pricing-survey-ldjdwz`) and are cited in §37 by branch and filename rather than added to the appendix, so the appendix carries no dangling pointer. A new decision that reverses no earlier rule and edits no existing section, hence a patch. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.
2026-09-02 · v4.123 — **§36 CLOSES ITS SECOND v4.119 OPEN ITEM: THE CATEGORY NORMALISER SNAPS EACH TARGET AGAINST ITS OWN LIST, AND SKIPS INCOME RATHER THAN REFUSING ON IT.** `scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js` read one master — `categories` where `kind='accounting'` — for all four of its target columns, `income_entries.category` included, so an income value one spacing or radical edit from an expense category would have snapped onto the expense spelling: the exact cross-list collision *Income categories move server-side* exists to prevent, found building it and never applied (the script is dry-run by default and had never run with `--apply`, so nothing was corrupted). **Fix 1: each target now reads its own master by its own `kind`** — accounting for the three expense-side columns, income for `income_entries.category` — never compared against each other. **Fix 2 is Ash's ruling on the refuse-on-empty-master contract, 2026-09-02: SKIP, DON'T REFUSE.** The accounting master's refusal on empty-or-colliding is UNCHANGED, because that list is well-established and the script's purpose depends on it. §36 ships `kind='income'` empty BY DECISION, so an empty income master is the shipped state, not a fault — `income_entries.category` is SKIPPED while it is empty, printed as its own block naming the row count and the reason, never refused, never silent, never treated as an error, while the other three targets run exactly as before. **One case outside Ash's ruling is answered by extension, not invention: a COLLIDING income master is refused on the same terms as a colliding accounting one** — a collision is a genuine fault, not the shipped empty state, so the pre-existing collision rule is applied to a second list rather than a second rule being invented. **Built and verified**: `scripts/test_normalise_finance_categories.js` (new, `npm run test:normalise-finance-categories`) proves it against a scratch database, including the case that matters most — the same spacing defect on both lists with different canonical spellings, income landing on its own and never the accounting one. **The closed bullet is REMOVED from §36's *Explicitly NOT decided here*, on the convention v4.115 set** — the doc's open list carries one fewer item, and no existing standing line is edited or deleted. The script remains dry-run by default; nothing here runs it against production. Code (`scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js`, new test, `package.json`) and this doc; no schema, no routes.
2026-09-02 · v4.122 — **§36 CLOSES ITS UNIT-COST-EXCEEDING-SELL-PRICE OPEN ITEM: TACET WARNS, IT DOES NOT REFUSE — DECIDED by Ash and BUILT.** A product's editor now flags `unit_cost > sell_price` at the moment the operator types it or opens the product, in the same field product 3 (Jackfruit Chips, §36 v4.117, ¥990.00 cost against ¥19.20 price) sat unremarked in. **The check is not new: `pdRenderMargin()`'s existing `m.money < 0` — cost greater than price — already rendered the words `'selling below cost' · '低于成本销售'` as a trailing clause on the margin line, before this build existed.** What changed is visibility, not detection: that clause is promoted into a `.pd-cost-warn` pill, the shape the editor's recipe-cost alerts already use, painted by a new `pdRenderCostSanity()` off the same trigger and a new host (`public/retail-admin/09-products.js`, `public/retail-admin.html:4635`). **Placement is the product editor only** — client-side and live, matching the decision's own wording "at the moment they set it" — not the server write path, which could only answer after a round trip and has nothing to enforce once refusal is off the table, and not the Products list margin cell, which already shows the damage passively as an extreme percentage and is recorded as a narrower, separate open item rather than built here. **Never fires on zero or null**: `_paMargin` already excludes a missing price or a missing cost before `m.money` exists, so an incomplete product is not this warning's case. **No cost read path is touched** — `productUnitCostYuan`, `lib/product-cost.js` and every reader stand exactly as they were; this compares two form fields already on screen. **The pair is ADOPTED, not minted**: `'selling below cost' · '低于成本销售'` was live at `09-products.js:1306` before it existed in any locked table, and is now locked into `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.13 as adopted from live code rather than composed, closing that document's own gap in the same change; confirmed by Ash 2026-09-02. **The closed bullet is REMOVED from §36's *Explicitly NOT decided here*, on the convention v4.115 set**, and a narrower item replaces it: whether the Products list should also flag an already-bad row without anyone opening it. Code (`public/retail-admin/09-products.js`, `public/retail-admin.html`), and both vocabulary and decisions docs; no schema, no routes, no cost read path.
2026-09-02 · v4.121 — **§36 LIFTS THE 1 AUGUST FLOOR OFF FINANCE, and the reason is that the cutover was decided for cost of goods and was never true of expenses.** Finance reads `expense_entries` and `income_entries` **for whatever periods they cover**: no floor on the Summary range bar, none on the Transactions range bar, and **none on the transaction form’s date field, on the add path and the edit path alike** — a person may legitimately correct an old row. **The cost half of the cutover reasoning STANDS UNCHANGED:** `unit_cost_at_sale` capture begins 31 August 2026, measured at v4.116, so gross profit does not exist before then and **both cost lines go on reading Not recorded UNCONDITIONALLY, in every period** — v4.113’s seventh-state decision is not touched and **no date condition is added to those rows**, which would turn one rule into two. **What forced it is the data:** production holds **111 expense rows across May, June and July totalling ¥180,332.28**, plus 62 in August; rent and wages are the same rows whether or not cost of goods exists alongside them, and **a screen that hides ¥180,000 of recorded spending to keep one line uniform is less true than one that shows the spending and marks the missing line as missing.** **THE SURVEY’S HEADLINE IS THAT THE FLOOR WAS NEVER BUILT, and it is recorded so it is not searched for again:** as of 2026-09-02, before this change, the literal `2026-08-01` appeared **nowhere** in `routes/`, `lib/`, `public/`, `reference/` or `docs/` — `resolveWindow` in `lib/finance-window.js` is the whole of Finance’s date logic and clamps nothing, both endpoints filter on the window alone, the range bar’s presets are unclamped, and **`#fin-tx-date` carries no `min` and never did.** **So the floor existed only as PROSE, in three places, and prose is what this change removes** — two comments asserting the cutover as a live constraint (`routes/finance-transactions.js`, `public/retail-admin/22-finance.js`) and one now-false premise in `scripts/export_kitchen_ledger.js`, whose header said the pre-cutover rows would be **“reachable by nothing”**; they are reachable on Transactions today, and **the export is NOT withdrawn by that** because a CSV in the accountant’s hands needs no login and is a snapshot a live screen cannot be. **The absences are now asserted rather than merely true**, in the markup and in two regression tests, so the floor cannot be reintroduced by a later reader who meets the old prose and believes it. **A consequence is recorded rather than treated as a defect:** `income_entries` runs 13 June to 31 July 2026 and stops, so **the money-in list is empty in the default trailing-30 window and fills when the range is widened back** — the ordinary §1.12 empty state, unchanged. **This supersedes the form’s date min of 2026-08-01, decided earlier the same day**, and supersedes the date filter in *Tacet’s Finance begins on 1 August 2026*, which keeps its body and gains a pointer. Comments, markup and tests; no schema, no routes, no query changed.
2026-09-02 · v4.120 — **§30 gains an amendment giving the Chinese-strings rule a route forward when NO LOCKED SOURCE EXISTS.** The rule itself is unchanged and restated: Chinese strings are copied from locked sources, never composed. What it lacked was an answer for the case where no locked source is available, and the consequence was that **work stalled rather than proceeding.** The amendment gives three preferences in order. **Lift from the channel** — where a string names something a platform already shows us, a fee, a status, a settlement line, the platform's own wording is used verbatim, **Meituan's and Eleme's merchant screens being locked sources for their own vocabulary**, with the platform and screen recorded. **Ask the operator** — for anything staff-facing with no channel equivalent, because the person running the store beats a correct translation. **Compose provisionally, and mark it** — only where the first two are unavailable or would block delivery, shipping marked PROVISIONAL in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` against review by a native operator before the feature leaves beta. **It is a last resort with a debt attached, not a shortcut**, and the closing line is the one that carries the weight: **never invent silently, and a composed string that is not marked provisional is a rule violation regardless of whether it turns out to be correct.** **`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` goes to v1.12 in the same pass and is the first exercise of it**, opening a ninth amendment section for the channel money breakdown that uses two of the three preferences in one table: `顾客配送费`, `商家对顾客的活动补贴` and `预计收入` are lifted verbatim from the Meituan and Eleme merchant apps under preference 1, and `明细不完整` and `结算明细` are composed and marked PROVISIONAL under preference 3. Nothing live is retrofitted by either document. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-02 · v4.119 — **§36 gains TWO open items, both found building *Income categories move server-side*: the list is now shareable and NOTHING CAN ADD TO IT, and the history-correction script snaps income onto the expense list.** **The first is an absent surface, not a missing decision.** §36 already says a tenant with genuine non-sale income creates their own categories in Settings; **no such Settings surface exists in either app** — Tacet's admin has no finance-category editor at all, and the kitchen app's income editor writes to browser localStorage and nowhere else. **The kind is valid server-side and the list ships empty, which is exactly the intended state, but the two facts together mean the empty list cannot stop being empty** and a tenant with sublet income or a sold fridge has the decision made for them by an absence rather than by §36. **The obvious shortcut is recorded as explicitly NOT the answer, because it looks like a one-line change: pointing the kitchen app's `saveFinCats()` at the new kind.** `syncCategoriesToServer` diffs the local list against the server's and **DELETES whatever is absent locally**, so the first browser to open the kitchen Finance page would push its four localStorage defaults — 堂食, 外卖, 外送, 活动 — into the shared list **and delete anything a Tacet operator had created**: the seed §36 bans, arriving by the back door, from the app being retired, with a delete attached. **The second is a cross-list snap in the history-correction script.** `scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js` reads its canonical values from `categories` where `kind='accounting'` and applies them to all four of its targets, **`income_entries.category` included** — so it would move an income value onto an expense name, **precisely the collision the server-side move exists to prevent**, and the one place that now has a name for it. **Nothing is corrupted and no repair is owed: the script is dry-run by default and has never been applied.** **The fix is a decision rather than a rename** — it needs a per-target master list, and a ruling on what the script's refuse-on-empty-master contract means for a list that **ships empty by decision**, since refusing to run on an empty master is the right instinct for the expense list and the ordinary state of the income one. **Neither item is answered here and no existing standing line is edited or deleted.** **Docs only — no code, no schema, no routes;** the server-side move these two were found building ships alongside on the same branch.
2026-09-02 · v4.118 — **§36 settles what the Transactions screen reads, correcting a build brief that said the order record: TRANSACTIONS READS TYPED ROWS.** The screen lists **`income_entries` and `expense_entries`, and does NOT list orders.** **Reading money in from the order record would make Transactions a several-hundred-row-per-month restatement of the Orders screen** — Roots ran 587 orders in August alone — **and the Summary already carries order revenue as its top line**, so the two would disagree about nothing while one buried the other. **The two screens answer different questions: Summary is the totals, Transactions is the ledger of what was entered by hand**, which is the reading §36 already implies where it argues PO rows must not be hidden ("Transactions would then hold only what people typed") and where it calls Transactions "the only surface where a person types". **The consequence is recorded rather than treated as a defect: `income_entries` has no rows after 1 August**, the cutover date, **so the money-in list is empty until somebody types one — and that is the ORDINARY EMPTY STATE, not a missing-data state** and not the §1.12 seventh state either, because something will arrive as soon as anyone records non-sale income. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-02 · v4.117 — **§36 records a SEVENTH cost trap, and it is a different kind from the six: A COST CAN BE WRONG AT THE SOURCE, AND NOTHING REFUSES IT.** The six recorded traps all concern a correct cost read wrongly; this is **a wrong number written to the catalogue, snapshotted faithfully, and read correctly** — no error anywhere on the path. **Measured on production 2026-09-02:** order 1494, line 5015, Jackfruit Chips, product 3, qty 1, `pack_units` 1, `unit_price` ¥19.20, `unit_cost_at_sale` **¥990.00** — **a cost-to-price ratio of 51.6**, against siblings on the same order at 0.092, 0.262 and 0.219 — and `store_products.unit_cost` for product 3 **is ¥990.00 today, so the catalogue still holds it.** **It did not enter through receiving:** no purchase order line has ever been received for product 3, so **it was typed in the product editor, which accepts any value greater than zero**, and **there is no guard anywhere against `unit_cost` exceeding sell price** — the figure draws a large negative margin on the Products screen with no refusal and no alarm. **The permitting mechanism is broader than the instance and is recorded with it:** `po_line_items` carries `qty`, a free-text `unit` and `cost_per_unit` and **no pack-size column**, so `cost_per_unit` means cost per whatever the buyer typed; `store_products` has **no unit, pack-size or sellable-unit column at all**; and `productUnitCostYuan` returns `store_products.unit_cost` **verbatim** for anything that is not a bundle — so **the chain from purchase to reader contains no conversion step and no assertion about what one unit is.** **The consequence for the cost reader is that a single bad catalogue cost does not error:** it renders one product as catastrophically unprofitable and drags the period's gross profit with it — on order 1494 **three products cost ¥14.15 together and the fourth claims ¥990.** **Product 3's true cost is unknown and is a manual correction in the product editor, not a code fix, and is recorded as OUTSTANDING.** **One open item is added to §36's *Explicitly NOT decided here*:** whether Tacet should refuse or warn on a `unit_cost` exceeding sell price, and whether such a guard belongs at the write, at the read, or on the Products screen. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-02 · v4.116 — **§36 records what the Finance Summary build actually ships, and the headline is a REFUSAL: THE SUMMARY SHIPS WITHOUT A LOCATION FILTER.** No store select; the staircase ends at Net, with **no Contribution line, no excluded-costs line and no *Not location-specific* row.** **The reason is a column that does not exist:** `expense_entries` has no location field and no way to set one — `schema.sql:229-240` carries `id`, `date`, `amount`, `category`, `description`, `po_id`, `created_at`, `created_by`, and only `payment_method` and `updated_at` have been added since — while **`retail_orders` carries `store_id`, so revenue can be store-scoped and expenses cannot.** A store filter would therefore **scope the top line and not the bottom one, reporting one shop's revenue against the whole business's expenses and calling the difference Net** — which §36 already rejects by name: **a filter that silently returns a wrong answer is worse than no filter.** **This is the mockup's state 4, and it is a legitimate rendering rather than a degraded one**; what differs from the mockup's framing is that **today the whole tenant has no location dimension in Finance, not only single-location tenants.** **The three vocabulary pairs minted for those rows — `contribution`, `notLocationSpecific`, `excludedCosts` — stay LOCKED in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` and unrendered, and are NOT withdrawn: the rows they serve are deferred, not cancelled**, with a test in the Summary suite asserting none of the three reaches the screen. **Unblocking it needs a location column on `expense_entries`, and §36's *An expense may carry a location* leaves that column's placement and shape explicitly undecided — so it is a DECISION before it is schema work.** **Two build notes are recorded alongside it.** **`.td-notrec` uses `--r-lg`, not `--r-control`** — `--r-control` is `public/till.html`'s own token and does not exist on the retail-admin surface, whose scale is `--r-sm` 4 / `--r-md` 6 / `--r-lg` 10 / `--r-xl` 14. And **both cost rows carry the not-recorded treatment but SHARE ONE past-tense sentence, per §1.12** — a second copy would assert a second cause, and both lines are absent for one reason. **§36 also gets the measurement v4.113 said had not been taken: THE COST CAPTURE CUTOFF IS 31 AUGUST 2026, AND IT IS ONE DATE RATHER THAN FIVE.** v4.113 records that the commit date must not be quoted as the cutoff and that the trustworthy figure is the earliest non-null `unit_cost_at_sale` per channel, from a production query that had not been run; **it has now been run**, on 2026-09-02 against `/root/roots-v2/data/roots.db`. The earliest cost-bearing order per channel is **gzgrocery 2026-08-31 01:30:00, wechat 2026-08-31 03:17:19, eleme 2026-08-31 04:01:34, wechat_chat 2026-08-31 09:01:45, meituan 2026-08-31 09:26:20**, with **116 of 4,857 order lines carrying a cost** — so the boundary is a single day, deploy having landed the day after `6cc03f6c`, and **the cost reader takes ONE cutoff constant rather than a per-channel table.** **The cutover consequence stands unchanged:** capture starts 31 August against a cutover starting 1 August, so **June, July and all but one day of August have no cost data and never will.** **A collateral finding comes free with the query: gzgrocery's first cost-bearing order is the SAME date as every other channel** — had `backfillGzMirrors` stamped present-day cost onto historic orders, gzgrocery would show an earlier first date than the rest, and it does not, **so that failure has not occurred on the data in production as of 2026-09-02.** The v4.113 finding **stands for orders mirrored after this date and is NOT repaired** by this measurement. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.115 — **§36 closes its last cost-of-goods open item: GZGROCERY COUNTS, ON BOTH HALVES.** Finance includes gzgrocery orders in revenue AND in cost of goods, read from the order record like every other channel, and **the existing dashboard exclusion is NOT inherited.** The exclusion exists to prevent double-booking against takings counted elsewhere; **Finance never reads `retail_stock_ledger`, so there is nothing to double-book against and the condition it protects against does not arise.** **The dashboard's own treatment is recorded so it is not mistaken for precedent:** its revenue SUM excludes gzgrocery via `COALESCE(channel,'') != 'gzgrocery'` and then **adds gzgrocery takings back from `retail_stock_ledger` through `guanyiPickupSales()`** — so **gzgrocery revenue is in the dashboard headline, arriving by a different road, and a reader that "follows the revenue side's exclusion" would exclude a channel the headline includes.** **Revenue and cost must stand on the same population: a channel in one half and not the other makes the staircase arithmetically wrong rather than merely incomplete.** **The decision does NOT repair the mirror backfill** — `backfillGzMirrors` stamping present-day cost onto historic orders stands as recorded at v4.113, and gzgrocery lines stamped at mirror time carry **a wrong number, not a missing one**, which this does not change. **A companion FINDING: Finance does not reuse the dashboard revenue aggregator, because that aggregator is a three-source cash-basis blend** — the order SUM, gzgrocery takings from `retail_stock_ledger`, and **wallet top-up cash from `retail_topup_transactions` on `date(paid_at, '+8 hours')`.** **A wallet top-up is money received before any sale**; §36 defines revenue as coming from the order record and separately rules settlement receipts out entirely, and **a top-up is a third thing that was not previously addressed — it is EXCLUDED from Finance revenue, because money becomes revenue when an order consumes it, not when it arrives.** Finance therefore writes its own revenue query against `retail_orders` and `retail_order_items`; **reusing the dashboard aggregator would silently import both folds.** **A count is corrected: the literal `date(COALESCE(paid_at, placed_at), '+8 hours')` appears ELEVEN times, not five** — v4.113's "five sites" was a count of aggregation handlers, and the raw occurrence count is higher. The eleven are **nine textual occurrences in `routes/`, all in `routes/retail.js`, spread across five route handlers (`/sales/summary`, `/dashboard`, `/products/highlights`, `/products/:id/sales`, `/products`) and two module-level helpers (`guanyiPickupSales()`, `storeCreditRedeemed()`), plus two more in `scripts/`** (`test_sales_summary_partition.js`, `funnel_report.js`); the v4.113 line is corrected in place to carry the same full breakdown, so **eleven is never read as the count within `routes/` alone.** **The closed bullet is REMOVED from *Explicitly NOT decided here* rather than left standing — a deliberate departure from the convention the three preceding closures followed — so §36's open list now carries five items rather than six.** **The superseded *gzgrocery must be ruled in or out of cost explicitly* subsection keeps its body unedited, but its heading moves from OPEN to CLOSED and it gains a closing line pointing at the decision**, on the phrasing the three earlier closures use: a reader who meets it first should read it as answered there. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.114 — **Three corrections to §36 from the finance-summary survey, each verified against the code before it was written, and one to the patterns doc.** **The route count was wrong: `routes/finance.js` declares SEVENTEEN routes, not thirteen** — the `tdb()` half of that line was right and stands, but the number was not, and it is recorded with its consequence because the number is load-bearing: **blocking "the thirteen write routes" by count would miss four.** **The blocking decision was written in the present tense and reads as shipped; it has NOT shipped, and the passage is rewritten as planned work with an explicit status line.** `blockCostWrite` exists in `middleware/block-kitchen-cost-writes.js` and is imported by `routes/ingredients.js`, `routes/purchases.js`, `routes/recipes.js` and `routes/admin.js` — **`routes/finance.js` does not import it**, and its nine write handlers carry only `requireAuth`, `requirePermission('finance')` and `requireDelete`, so the leak the decision describes as closed is open. **The PO-derived-rows safety argument was incomplete rather than wrong** — the edit and delete refusals on a `po_id` are real and the conclusion holds, but the invariant rests on a second mechanism the argument never named: **`POST /api/finance/expenses` never sets `po_id`**, inserting only `date`, `amount`, `category`, `description`, `payment_method` and `created_by`, **so a hand-entered row cannot acquire a `po_id` at all** and the refusals never have to catch one. **In `docs/tacet-desktop-patterns.md`, §1.12's heading is corrected from six states to seven** — v4.9 added *Not recorded* beneath it and left the heading undercounting the rule, which is a rule a reader can satisfy and still miss a state; that doc goes to v4.10 and no page rule is added, removed or altered. **These are in-place corrections to standing text, not superseding entries**, because each replaces a claim that is false as written rather than one that has been overtaken — a wrong count and a shipped-tense description of unbuilt work are re-derived as fresh findings if they are left standing. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.
