**Nothing is scheduled, designed or built here.** Settlement reconciliation remains unbuilt work. This records its cadence and the comparison it makes, not its delivery.

### `wechat_chat` and `pickup` are mapped, and the open item asking what they are rested on a wrong premise — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**Closes "What `wechat_chat` and `pickup` are", the open item §36 has carried since v4.108.** That bullet is left standing in *Explicitly NOT decided here* below rather than struck out, on the convention that superseded text is not edited. This subsection supersedes it: a reader who meets the bullet first should read it as answered here.

**They are not platform channels and they were never unmapped.** They are staff-keyed order ORIGINS — how the customer reached the shop — written by the New order form's "Order came from · 订单来源" dropdown, alongside `wholesale` and `other`. All four are `MANUAL_ORDER_ORIGINS` in `routes/retail.js`, and `source` already records that a person keyed the row.

**The Sales-summary partition defines `direct` as a residual rather than an inclusion list.** Its bucket predicate is `NOT (claimed by wechat, web, meituan, gzgrocery or counter)`, so every channel value that exists — and every one invented later — lands in exactly one bucket. No revenue can fall out. `scripts/test_sales_summary_partition.js` asserts exactly this property and already carries `pickup`, `wechat_chat`, `wholesale` and `other` as fixtures expecting `direct`. **What these values lack is a card of their own, not a mapping.**

**The collision this uncovers is recorded here because it is a trap for any Finance query.**

**`pickup` is the same string in two columns with two unrelated meanings.** As `retail_orders.channel` it means the customer came to the shop to order. As `fulfillment_type` it means the customer collects later. The two are independent: a row can legitimately be `channel='pickup'` with `fulfillment_type='delivery'` — someone who walked in to order a thing that is then shipped to them. **Any Finance filter, query or screen touching either value must name its column explicitly. A bare reference to "pickup" is ambiguous and must not appear in a spec.**

**`wechat_chat` is not `wechat`.** `wechat` is the mini-app storefront, which writes its own orders. `wechat_chat` is a customer who messaged the shop and had the order hand-keyed. **`wechat` and `web` were deliberately removed from the manual origin list** because staff-keyed rows claiming them were being summed into the Mini app and Web shop cards, inflating self-serve revenue with hand-entered sales.

**Both carry line items and `unit_cost_at_sale`, like any other order.** The operator can override the selling price and cannot override the cost.

### PO-derived expense rows stay delete-and-reinsert projections — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**Closes "Whether PO-derived expense rows remain delete-and-reinsert projections in storage", the third open item on §36.** That bullet is left standing in *Explicitly NOT decided here* below rather than struck out, on the same convention. This subsection supersedes it.

**The rows stay projections. Both posters continue to delete every row for a purchase order and re-insert them on each status change.**

**They are safe to churn, and the safety is enforced rather than incidental.** `routes/finance.js` refuses both edit and delete on any row carrying a `po_id` — *PO-linked expenses cannot be edited directly · 关联采购单的支出不能直接编辑*, and the same for delete — so no human-authored value can ever accumulate on one of these rows and be lost when it is regenerated. And no foreign key anywhere points at `expense_entries.id`; no table joins to it. The reference runs the other way, `expense_entries.po_id` at `purchase_orders`. **So regenerating the ids breaks no stable reference, because nothing holds one.**

**The invariant holds by a second mechanism the argument above does not name:** `POST /api/finance/expenses` never sets `po_id`, inserting only `date`, `amount`, `category`, `description`, `payment_method` and `created_by`. A hand-entered row therefore cannot acquire a `po_id` at all.

**The consequence, recorded because it is the one thing that can go wrong with this.**

**`created_at` on a PO-derived row is not an audit timestamp.** It records the last re-post, not when the purchase happened. A purchase order flipped back and forward in April carries April rows stamped with today. **It must never be presented as a purchase date, and never used as evidence of when anything occurred.** The purchase order's own date is the date to display.

**Tacet's projection carries the purchase order's date, not the re-post moment.**

### The boot-time expense backfill is an uncontrolled ledger writer — FLAGGED FOR CUTOVER 2026-09-01

`backfillOrderedExpenses()` in `routes/purchases.js` runs on every server start, two seconds after boot. It finds any purchase order in a postable status — Ordered, Delivered or Confirmed — that has zero rows in `expense_entries`, and posts it.

**It is a writer to the money ledger that fires without anyone touching a purchase order.** It is also the mechanism behind the expense table continuing to grow after the export: the cutover subsection above records 168 rows on 2026-09-01 against the 92 a survey found on 4 August, and this is one of the paths that number came in by.

**No split of that growth is derivable from `expense_entries` at all.** Both this backfill and the ordinary receive path call `postPOExpenses()`, nothing on a row records which caller posted it, and `created_at` is rewritten on re-post — so the table cannot say how many of the 76 were this. The answer would have to come from purchase-order status history or from the boot logs, and neither is established as retained: PO `status_change` entries live in `activity_log`, which every startup purges beyond 90 days (`ACTIVITY_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 90), and the backfill writes no `activity_log` row at all — it only `console.log`s a one-line summary, whose destination and retention are not established here. **Do not carry 76 forward as a backfill count.**

**This is recorded as a cutover concern, not resolved here.** The kitchen expense table is not a closed archive while this runs. **Any statement that the exported ledger is final must account for it.**

**No decision is taken on whether Tacet carries an equivalent.** The question is recorded as open below rather than answered.

### Income categories move server-side, and the list ships empty — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**Closes "Where income categories live", the second open item on §36.** That bullet is left standing in *Explicitly NOT decided here* below rather than struck out, on the same convention. This subsection supersedes it.

**Today income categories cannot be shared, and not merely by omission.** They live in each browser's localStorage under `roots_v2:incomeCats`, and `saveFinCats()` pushes only the expense list to the server. `routes/lookups.js` would refuse the income list anyway: its `VALID_KINDS` is `recipe`, `product`, `accounting`, `role`, `item_kind` and `payment_method`, with no `income`, so the endpoint returns *Invalid kind · 类型无效*. Expense categories are shared properly under `kind='accounting'`. **Income never could be.** Every browser therefore holds its own list, and a list edited on one machine is invisible on every other.

**The decision: income categories move to the same `categories` table as expense — shared across users and browsers, hydrated from the server on load, on the same mechanism.**

**The list ships empty. No defaults.**

**The reasoning is recorded because a later session will otherwise be tempted to seed it.** The current four defaults are 堂食 Dine-in, 外卖 Takeaway, 外送 Delivery and 活动 Events — every one of them a fulfilment or channel fact the order record already carries. Since revenue comes from the order record, an income category that restates the channel is a dropdown with exactly one correct answer, and **a dropdown with a wrong option available is what produced the ¥152,309 Mini App mis-filing**. **An empty list cannot offer a wrong option.** Channel breakdown on the Summary screen comes from the order's own channel, never from a typed category.

**A tenant whose income is entirely sales never opens this list.** A tenant with genuine non-sale income — sublet space, sold equipment, grants, supplier rebates — creates their own.

### The income category field is optional and hides when the list is empty — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**With an empty list, manual income entry shows amount, date and note, and no category field at all.** Not a disabled field, not an empty dropdown: absent.

**The "add income" action stays visible regardless.** It is never hidden behind having created a category first. Gating it that way would leave a tenant with non-sale money in hand, no route to record it, and no sign on the screen explaining why.

**The category field appears once the tenant has created at least one income category in Settings.** Nobody is asked to categorise before they have anything to categorise with.

**A standing fact from the same survey, not a decision.** `routes/finance.js` calls `storeCategory` zero times. It stores category values raw, with no trim and no normalisation, in both directions. The category column is free text with no foreign key. Purchasing normalises earlier in the chain, at PO-line save, so PO-derived rows arrive already clean; **Finance is the exception.** This is context for *Categories are normalised on write* above, which already stands, and is not a new decision.

### Per-location contribution is not available from current data — DEPENDENCY 2026-09-01

**Correcting an assumption carried through the location-dimension design.** Contribution for a market day — or for any location, over any period — cannot be computed from what exists today.

**Cost is recognised at purchase, not at sale.** `postRetailPOExpenses` posts expense rows when a purchase order reaches Ordered or Delivered, dated to the purchase order. **Buying is the expense event; selling is not.**

**Nothing in the repository values inventory.** `retail_store_stock` holds quantities and has no cost column. There is no valuation, no layers, no FIFO and no average cost anywhere.

**`unit_cost_at_sale` is written on all six sale paths and read by nothing.** Its own schema comment says so — *nothing reads it yet; capture starts now so the history exists when a margin report is built on it* — and a repository-wide check confirms every hit is a write or a comment.

**So stock carried to a market and not sold has already been expensed on the purchase order's date**, whether it sells or not, and selling it changes nothing about cost.

**This is recorded as a DEPENDENCY, not a decision, and nothing above is reversed.** *An expense MAY carry a location* stands. CONTRIBUTION stands as the word. *Finance reads `unit_cost_at_sale`, which by then is a number* stands as the design. **What is recorded is that the reader does not exist yet:** Finance's per-location contribution figure depends on cost of goods being read from the order line, and that is unbuilt work which must be scheduled before the figure can be drawn. **A contribution figure computed from the expense ledger alone would be wrong in a way that looks right**, because the purchase and the sale fall in different periods.

### Cost of goods does not exist before capture started, and cannot be backfilled — FINDING 2026-09-01

**Recorded ahead of the decision it forces**, because the decision only makes sense once this is on the record.

`unit_cost_at_sale` capture landed in a single commit — `6cc03f6c`, 2026-08-30 14:44:32 UTC — which added the column and wrote it from all six sale paths at once. **Every order line written before that commit is NULL, permanently.**

**The column's own comment records why a backfill is refused.** `retail_product_versions` keeps only 25 versions per product, `activity_log` `cost_update` rows are written only by PO receiving, and the recipe rollup records nothing at all. A backfill would therefore fall back to TODAY's cost and **produce a column that looks like a snapshot without being one.**

**The commit date is NOT the data cutoff, and must not be quoted as one.** Deploy time is not commit time. `release.json` is stale. There is no deploy log in the repository, and two commits on the main line around 2026-09-01 concern the deploy hook shipping nothing silently. **The trustworthy cutoff is the earliest non-null `unit_cost_at_sale` per channel, which is a query against production and HAS NOT BEEN RUN.** Any statement of the cutoff date must come from that query, not from the commit.

**The consequence for Finance is the substance of this finding.** The cutover starts 1 August and capture starts at the end of that month. **June and July have no cost data and never will.** August — recorded above as the first complete month, 587 orders and ¥123,454 — has cost for its final days only. **Gross profit does not exist for substantially the whole period the cutover covers.**

### A missing staircase step is shown and marked Not recorded — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**Where cost of goods is unavailable for a period, the Summary screen still renders both the cost of goods line and the gross profit line, each reading Not recorded.** Revenue, operating expenses and net render normally from the data that exists. **The step is never hidden and never zero.**

**Three alternatives were considered and rejected.**

**Hiding the two lines for affected periods.** Rejected: a reader opening July finds no gross profit and no explanation, and reasonably concludes the screen is broken.

**Suppressing the middle step everywhere until coverage is complete.** Rejected: it discards real data for September onward to keep the screen uniform.

**Rendering zero, or a dash.** Rejected: **zero claims the goods were free** — the same failure the cost column refuses at write time, where every write site passes null rather than zero and `productUnitCostYuan` returns null rather than a stored zero, for exactly this reason. A dash is already banned as a value.

**Not recorded is not a new state.** It is the existing seventh state on §1.12 of `docs/tacet-desktop-patterns.md`, added there from the pre-24-August Meituan orders. **Same problem, same treatment.**

**SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-09-07 — the two cost rows render BLANK, not Not recorded. See §56.** `cost_of_goods` and `gross_profit` stay null on the Finance summary and both rows render blank, in every period. **What still stands is most of this subsection, and it is what makes blank the right token rather than a fourth rejected option:** the step is still **never hidden** — both rows render, and a reader opening any period finds them — and **zero and a dash are still refused**, zero because it claims the goods were free and a dash because it is banned as a value. **What does not stand is the Not recorded LABEL on these two rows specifically.** The seventh state itself is untouched and goes on being used everywhere else it applies; §56 simply does not put it in these two cells.

### Six ways the cost reader will silently miscount — BINDING ON ITS BUILD 2026-09-01

**Each of these produces a plausible wrong number rather than an error.**

**PACK UNITS.** `unit_cost_at_sale` is per single unit. The line's cost is `unit_cost_at_sale × qty × COALESCE(pack_units, 1)`. On Meituan and Eleme a `qty` of 1 against a 6瓶 listing is six units off the shelf, with `pack_units = 6`. **The asymmetry is recorded explicitly:** `SUM(line_total)` on the same row is already correct, because `line_total` is per line. **The revenue half and the cost half do not take the same multiplier**, so a reader that treats them alike is wrong on one of them.

**PARTIAL REFUNDS, ITEMISED.** `applyRefundedQty` stamps `refunded_qty` and stops. Order status stays `paid` or `delivered`, `qty` is never reduced, `line_total` is never reduced, and **nothing in the codebase subtracts `refunded_qty` from any aggregate today.** A cost reader must sum `qty − COALESCE(refunded_qty, 0)`.

**PARTIAL REFUNDS, AMOUNT-ONLY — and this is the hole the line-level fix does NOT close.** Where a refund is issued as an amount with no `lines` array, `refunded_qty` stays 0 and nothing is written to the line at all. The refund is recorded on the order and in a `retail_refund_events` row, and nowhere on `retail_order_items`. **A reader working from order lines cannot see it at any level of sophistication**; recovering it means going back to the order's refund columns and apportioning by hand. **`qty − refunded_qty` is necessary and NOT sufficient** — recorded so a later session does not treat the itemised fix as complete.

**Full refunds are survivable by accident** — status flips to `refunded` and every existing predicate excludes it. **Partial refunds are the dangerous half, and the amount-only variant is the dangerous half of that.**

**OPTIONS CARRY PRICE BUT NO COST.** `options_json` holds the chosen labels and their price deltas, and the deltas move `unit_price`. **There is no cost counterpart.** A paid option that costs the business something is unrepresented, so cost is under-counted wherever options carry real cost.

**ADD-ON LINES GO NULL, NOT ZERO, ON A FAILED RE-DERIVATION.** Add-ons are separate real lines and belong in a sum, but cost is written only where the settlement-time re-derivation succeeded. Where a product or option choice was deleted between staging and settlement, the line is NULL.

**BUNDLES ARE SAFE FROM DOUBLE-COUNTING AND UNSAFE IN ONE OTHER WAY.** One line per bundle, components never written as lines, and cost derived through `bundleUnitCostYuan` rather than read raw — a raw read of `store_products.unit_cost` would record every bundle ever sold as free. **But the derivation is all-or-nothing:** one unpriced component blanks the entire bundle's cost, on the stated reasoning that a sum missing one component is confidently low and low reads as plausible. **So a bundle NULL means one component was unpriced, not that the bundle was.**

### Two ways a non-null cost is still not what it appears to be — FINDING 2026-09-01

**Recorded separately from the miscount list above, because these are wrong numbers rather than missing ones.**

**THE COMPLETENESS FLAG DOES NOT REACH THE LINE.** `store_products.cost_incomplete` is three-state — unanswered, complete, or something missing, typically packaging per §31. **A product flagged incomplete still returns a positive number from `productUnitCostYuan`**, and that number is snapshotted with no trace of the flag. The flag lives on the mutable product row, not on the immutable line, **so it cannot be recovered for a past sale.** A line whose cost is knowingly understated is indistinguishable from one that is right.

**THE GZGROCERY MIRROR BACKFILL STAMPS TODAY'S COST ONTO HISTORIC ORDERS.** `backfillGzMirrors` runs at daemon startup in live mode and mirrors historical gzgrocery orders into `retail_orders` for the first time, stamping `gzUnitCost` — the catalogue cost read at mirror time — onto an order placed months earlier. **For any gzgrocery order first mirrored after capture started, `unit_cost_at_sale` is a present-day figure wearing a historic date.** This is precisely the failure the backfill refusal above exists to prevent, occurring on one path anyway. Orders already mirrored before the column existed insert no items and stay NULL.

### gzgrocery must be ruled in or out of cost explicitly, and no existing query answers it — CLOSED 2026-09-01

gzgrocery mirror rows are real fulfilled orders. **Existing aggregators include them in order counts, trend and AOV, and exclude them from revenue sums**, to avoid double-booking takings counted elsewhere. **Nor is the exclusion itself consistent** — some sites include gzgrocery and some exclude it, with the companion predicate declared separately four times.

**A cost reader must decide which side it follows, and no precedent exists, because no existing query touches cost.**

**Recorded as an open item rather than decided here.** It is added to *Explicitly NOT decided here* below.

**Closed 2026-09-01 by the gzgrocery decision below: gzgrocery counts, on both halves.** A reader who meets this subsection first should read it as answered there.

### The aggregation predicate and the order date are both inconsistent today — FINDING 2026-09-01

**Thirteen sites read `retail_order_items` in aggregate and none of them reads cost.**

**There is no shared predicate** — the string is copy-pasted with variations at every site. An allow-list is declared once and re-declared inline four more times; a deny-list is live at two sites and **is not equivalent**, since it admits any status added later while the allow-list excludes it. **Neither addresses partial refunds.**

**Four date conventions are live simultaneously:** `COALESCE(paid_at, placed_at)` shifted `+8 hours`, at five aggregation handlers and dominant — **"five sites" counts handlers, not occurrences: the measured occurrence count is NINE in `routes/`, all in `routes/retail.js`, plus TWO in `scripts/`, ELEVEN in total**, as broken down below under *Finance does not reuse the dashboard revenue aggregator*; `paid_at` alone with no shift, which silently drops orders with a null `paid_at` and puts its day boundary in UTC; `placed_at` alone with no shift; and no date filter at all.

**The concrete consequence, recorded so it is not re-derived:** an order placed 31 July at 22:00 Guangzhou and paid 1 August lands in August on one screen and July on another.

**Which predicate and which date column the cost reader adopts is a decision to be taken when it is built, deliberately.** **It must not be inherited by copying whichever site is nearest.**

### A market or till sale has no cost of goods anywhere — FINDING 2026-09-01

**Two live writers record sales that never reach `retail_order_items`:** the market-stall POS and the kitchen app's manual sales entry. Both write `sales_entries`, which has `qty`, `unit_price` and `total` and **no cost column at all.**

**§36 already decides that a till or market sale is an order carrying `unit_cost_at_sale` per line.** What is recorded here is that **the decision is taken and the work is unbuilt**, and that until it is built **a market sale contributes revenue with no cost — which on the staircase reads as pure gross profit.**

### Location attribution is through the order header, and is wrong in three known cases — FINDING 2026-09-01

**There is no location column on the order line.** Attribution runs through `retail_orders.store_id`, which is nullable with no default, **so rows predating the column carry NULL and are silently dropped by any grouping.**

**A drop-ship line never passes through a store yet inherits the order's `store_id`**, so a per-location cost figure would charge stock to a shop that never held it. **A split shipment reports one location for lines that moved separately**, since the store lives on the order and not on the shipment. **`routing_reason = 'fallback_no_stock'` means the order went to a store that was not the natural one** — accurate about fulfilment, misleading about origin.

**This compounds the contribution dependency already standing above.**

### gzgrocery counts, on both halves — DECIDED 2026-09-01

**Closes "Whether gzgrocery counts toward cost of goods", the open item added to §36 at v4.113.** The bullet is removed from *Explicitly NOT decided here* below. The *gzgrocery must be ruled in or out of cost explicitly* subsection above is superseded by this one: **its body is left unedited, its heading now reads CLOSED, and it carries a closing line pointing here**, so a reader who meets it first is not left thinking the question is still open.

Finance includes gzgrocery orders in revenue and in cost of goods, read from the order record like every other channel. The existing dashboard exclusion is not inherited.

The exclusion exists to prevent double-booking against takings counted elsewhere. Finance never reads `retail_stock_ledger`, so there is nothing to double-book against. The condition the exclusion protects against does not arise here.

The dashboard's own treatment is recorded so it is not mistaken for precedent: its revenue SUM excludes gzgrocery via `COALESCE(channel,'') != 'gzgrocery'`, and then adds gzgrocery takings back from `retail_stock_ledger` through `guanyiPickupSales()`. gzgrocery revenue is in the dashboard headline, arriving by a different road. A reader that "follows the revenue side's exclusion" would exclude a channel the headline includes.

Revenue and cost must stand on the same population. A channel in one half and not the other makes the staircase arithmetically wrong rather than merely incomplete.

This decision does not repair the mirror backfill. `backfillGzMirrors` stamps present-day cost onto historic orders, recorded above as a finding, and remains true. gzgrocery lines whose cost was stamped at mirror time carry a wrong number, not a missing one, and this decision does not change that.

### Finance does not reuse the dashboard revenue aggregator — FINDING 2026-09-01

The Reports/Dashboard handler's `kpi.revenue` is a cash-basis blend of three sources: the order SUM, gzgrocery takings from `retail_stock_ledger`, and wallet top-up cash from `retail_topup_transactions` on `date(paid_at, '+8 hours')`.

A wallet top-up is money received before any sale. §36 defines revenue as coming from the order record, and separately rules settlement receipts out entirely; a top-up is a third thing and was not previously addressed. **It is excluded from Finance revenue. Money becomes revenue when an order consumes it, not when it arrives.**

Finance therefore writes its own revenue query against `retail_orders` and `retail_order_items` rather than reusing the dashboard aggregator. Reusing it would silently import both folds.

**The literal date expression `date(COALESCE(paid_at, placed_at), '+8 hours')` appears eleven times, not five.** §36's earlier "five sites" was a count of aggregation handlers; the raw occurrence count is higher. **The measured breakdown, stated in full so the two figures are never conflated again: NINE occurrences in `routes/`, every one of them in `routes/retail.js`, plus TWO in `scripts/` — ELEVEN in total.** Eleven is the total across both directories, **not the count within `routes/` alone.** The nine in `routes/retail.js` sit across five route handlers — `/sales/summary`, `/dashboard`, `/products/highlights`, `/products/:id/sales` and `/products` — and two module-level helpers, `guanyiPickupSales()` and `storeCreditRedeemed()`; **the five handlers are what "five sites" counted, and they check out exactly.** The two in `scripts/` are `test_sales_summary_partition.js` and `funnel_report.js`.

Counted are both textual forms — the `'${TZ}'` template and the inline `'+8 hours'` literal — with or without an `o.` table alias. **Deliberately not counted, being different expressions rather than occurrences of this one:** `strftime('%H', COALESCE(…))`, `time(COALESCE(…))`, `MIN(COALESCE(…))`, the bare `COALESCE(o.paid_at, o.placed_at) AS waiting_since` at two sites, and one comment.

### Finance Summary ships without a location filter — DECIDED 2026-09-02

The Summary screen carries no store select. The staircase ends at Net: no Contribution line, no excluded-costs line, no *Not location-specific* row.

`expense_entries` has no location column and no way to set one — `schema.sql:229-240` carries `id`, `date`, `amount`, `category`, `description`, `po_id`, `created_at`, `created_by`, with only `payment_method` and `updated_at` added since. `retail_orders` carries `store_id`, so revenue can be store-scoped and expenses cannot. A store filter would therefore scope the top line and not the bottom one, reporting one shop's revenue against the whole business's expenses and calling the difference Net. §36 already rejects this by name: **a filter that silently returns a wrong answer is worse than no filter.**

This is the mockup's state 4, and it is a legitimate rendering rather than a degraded one. What differs from the mockup's framing is that today the whole tenant has no location dimension in Finance, not only single-location tenants.

The three vocabulary pairs minted for these rows — `contribution`, `notLocationSpecific`, `excludedCosts` — stay locked in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` and unrendered. **They are not withdrawn; the rows they serve are deferred, not cancelled.** A test in the Summary suite asserts none of the three appears on the screen.

Unblocking this needs a location column on `expense_entries`. §36's *An expense may carry a location* decides the dimension exists and leaves the column's placement and shape explicitly undecided, so **that is a decision before it is schema work.**

### Two build notes on the Summary — RECORDED 2026-09-02

**The `.td-notrec` class uses `--r-lg`, not `--r-control`.** `--r-control` is `public/till.html`'s token and does not exist on the retail-admin surface, whose radius scale is `--r-sm` 4 / `--r-md` 6 / `--r-lg` 10 / `--r-xl` 14.

**Both cost rows carry the not-recorded treatment but share one past-tense sentence, per §1.12.** A second copy would assert a second cause; both lines are absent for one reason.

### The cost capture cutoff is 31 August 2026, measured — FINDING 2026-09-02

§36 v4.113 records that the commit date must not be quoted as the cutoff and that the trustworthy figure is the earliest non-null `unit_cost_at_sale` per channel, from a production query that had not been run. **It has now been run**, on 2026-09-02 against `/root/roots-v2/data/roots.db`.

The earliest cost-bearing order per channel: **gzgrocery 2026-08-31 01:30:00, wechat 2026-08-31 03:17:19, eleme 2026-08-31 04:01:34, wechat_chat 2026-08-31 09:01:45, meituan 2026-08-31 09:26:20.** 116 of 4,857 order lines carry a cost.

**The cutoff is therefore a single date, 31 August 2026, not a per-channel boundary.** Deploy landed the day after commit `6cc03f6c`. **The cost reader takes one cutoff constant rather than five.**

The consequence for the cutover stands as recorded: the cutover starts 1 August, capture starts 31 August, so **June, July and all but one day of August have no cost data and never will.**

**One collateral finding: gzgrocery's first cost-bearing order is the same date as every other channel.** Had `backfillGzMirrors` stamped present-day cost onto historic orders, gzgrocery would show an earlier first date than the rest. It does not, **so that failure has not occurred on the data in production as of 2026-09-02.** The finding stands for orders mirrored after this date; **it is not repaired.**

### A cost can be wrong at the source, and nothing refuses it — FINDING 2026-09-02

The six recorded miscount traps all concern a correct cost read wrongly. **This is a seventh and different kind: a wrong number written to the catalogue, snapshotted faithfully, and read correctly.**

**Measured on production 2026-09-02.** Order 1494, line 5015: Jackfruit Chips, product 3, qty 1, `pack_units` 1, `unit_price` ¥19.20, `unit_cost_at_sale` **¥990.00** — a cost-to-price ratio of **51.6**. The three sibling lines on the same order ratio at 0.092, 0.262 and 0.219. `store_products.unit_cost` for product 3 is ¥990.00 today, **so the catalogue still holds it.**

**No purchase order line has ever been received for product 3** — the `po_line_items` query returns nothing — so the figure did not enter through PO receiving. **It was typed in the product editor, which accepts any value greater than zero.**

**There is no guard anywhere against `unit_cost` exceeding sell price.** The value produces a large negative margin on the Products screen with no refusal and no alarm. **Closed by *Unit cost exceeding sell price now warns*, below.**

The mechanism that permits it is recorded here, and is broader than this instance: `po_line_items` carries `qty`, a free-text `unit` and `cost_per_unit`, and **no pack-size column**, so `cost_per_unit` means cost per whatever the buyer typed. `store_products` has **no unit, pack-size or sellable-unit column at all.** `productUnitCostYuan` returns `store_products.unit_cost` **verbatim** for anything that is not a bundle — no division, no normalisation. **The chain from purchase to reader contains no conversion step and no assertion about what one unit is.**

**Consequence for the cost reader: a single bad catalogue cost does not error.** It renders one product as catastrophically unprofitable and pulls the period's gross profit down with it. On order 1494 three products cost ¥14.15 together and the fourth claims ¥990.

**Product 3's true cost is unknown and is a manual correction in the product editor, not a code fix. Recorded as outstanding.**

### Unit cost exceeding sell price now warns — DECIDED AND BUILT 2026-09-02

**DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-02: Tacet warns when a product's unit cost exceeds its sell price. It does not refuse the save.** A product genuinely bought above its own sell price is possible, so refusing would block real work; a warning catches the typo behind product 3 without asserting something that is not always false.

**THE CHECK IS NOT NEW. WHAT CHANGED IS VISIBILITY.** `_paMargin(price, cost)` already returned `money = price − cost`, and the product editor's margin line (`public/retail-admin/09-products.js`, `pdRenderMargin()`) already appended `'selling below cost' · '低于成本销售'` whenever that figure went negative — arithmetically identical to cost exceeding price. **That comparison did not stop product 3**, because it rendered as a trailing clause on a small money-and-percentage line, easy to type past. **A later reader must not take this build as the moment the comparison was added; it is the moment it became legible.**

**PLACEMENT: the product editor only — client-side, live, on the same `m.money < 0` trigger.** Surveyed against three candidates. The product editor matches the decision's own wording, "visible to the person setting the cost, at the moment they set it" — `pdRenderMargin()` already repaints on every keystroke in Cost or Price (`09-products.js:5589`) and on opening a product (`09-products.js:2718`), so a reopened product 3 would show the warning immediately too. The Products list margin cell already shows the damage passively, as an extreme percentage, without a dedicated flag — closing that gap is catalogue-wide review, a different feature from a data-entry guard, and is recorded below as a separate possible item rather than built. A server-side check on the write path would only surface after a save round-trip, which is not "at the moment they set it," and item 2 already rules out any refusal for the server to enforce, so there is nothing for a server-side copy to do that the client check does not already do sooner.

**WHAT WAS BUILT.** The existing plain-text clause is promoted into a `.pd-cost-warn` pill — the same shape `pdCostPill()` already uses for the recipe-cost alerts in this exact field (`09-products.js:1001,1078-1082`) — painted by a new `pdRenderCostSanity(m)`, called from inside `pdRenderMargin()` on the same `m` it already computes. A new host, `#pd-cost-sanity`, sits between `#pd-cost-alert` and `#pd-margin` in the editor markup (`public/retail-admin.html:4635`). The margin line's own trailing clause is suppressed for the List-margin figure it duplicates (a `noteBelowCost` flag on the `line()` helper) and left exactly as it was for the separate Meituan-actual figure below it, which compares cost against a different revenue and is outside this decision's scope.

**NEVER FIRES ON ZERO OR NULL**, per instruction: `_paMargin` already returns `null` whenever price is missing/≤0 or cost is null/empty/negative, before `m.money` is ever computed — a product with no sell price yet is `cost_incomplete`'s case, not this one, and nothing further was added to exclude it.

**NOT TOUCHED: `productUnitCostYuan`, `lib/product-cost.js`, or any cost read path.** This is a client-side comparison of the two form fields already on screen, not a change to what cost means or how it is read.

**THE PAIR IS ADOPTED, NOT MINTED.** `'selling below cost' · '低于成本销售'` was already live at `09-products.js:1306` before this pair existed in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`'s locked tables. Rather than compose a second string for the same condition, it is locked into that document as of this change — v1.13, ADOPTED FROM LIVE CODE rather than newly composed, and confirmed by Ash 2026-09-02.

**Closes "Whether Tacet should refuse or warn on a `unit_cost` exceeding sell price", the open item added to §36 at v4.117.** The bullet is removed from *Explicitly NOT decided here* below. **A new, narrower open item replaces it**: whether the Products list margin cell should also flag an existing row whose cost already exceeds its sell price, independent of anyone opening the editor — surveyed above and explicitly not built here.

### Transactions reads typed rows, not the order record — DECIDED 2026-09-02

**The Transactions screen lists `income_entries` and `expense_entries`. It does not list orders.**

Reading money in from the order record would make Transactions a several-hundred-row-per-month restatement of the Orders screen, and the Summary already carries order revenue as its top line. **The two screens answer different questions: Summary is the totals, Transactions is the ledger of what was entered by hand.**

`income_entries` has no rows after 1 August. **The money-in list is therefore empty until someone types one, and that is the ordinary empty state rather than a missing-data state.**

### The category normaliser snaps each target against its own list — DECIDED AND BUILT 2026-09-02

**Closes the second open item §36 gained at v4.119: what `scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js` snaps income against.** Before this, the script read ONE master — `categories` where `kind='accounting'` — and matched all four of its target columns against it, `income_entries.category` included: an income value one spacing or radical edit from an expense category would snap onto the expense spelling, moving it onto the wrong list's vocabulary — precisely the collision *Income categories move server-side* exists to prevent. **Nothing was corrupted**: the script is dry-run by default and had never been run with `--apply`.

**FIX 1, the per-target master.** Each of the four targets now reads its own master by its own `kind` — `kind='accounting'` for `ingredients.accounting_category`, `po_line_items.expense_category` and `expense_entries.category`; `kind='income'` for `income_entries.category` — and the two are never compared against each other.

**FIX 2, Ash's ruling on the refuse-on-empty-master contract, 2026-09-02: skip, don't refuse.** The accounting master's existing refusal is UNCHANGED — empty or colliding still blocks the whole run, because that list is well-established and the script's purpose depends on it. The income master is different: §36 ships `kind='income'` empty BY DECISION, so an empty income master is the shipped state, not a fault. `income_entries.category` is therefore SKIPPED while its master is empty — not refused, not evaluated silently, not treated as an error — printed as its own block naming the row count and the reason, while the other three targets run exactly as before. The moment a tenant creates a first income category, the master stops being empty and the target is evaluated like any other.

**One case Ash's ruling did not name is answered by extension rather than invention: a COLLIDING income master** (two entries differing only by spacing or case, so there is no single canonical value) is refused on the same terms as a colliding accounting master, because a collision is a genuine fault — a vocabulary decision nobody made — not the shipped empty state Ash's ruling addresses. This is the pre-existing collision rule applied to a second list, not a second rule.

**Built and verified, not merely decided:** `scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js`, proven by `scripts/test_normalise_finance_categories.js` (new, `npm run test:normalise-finance-categories`) against a scratch database built from the shipped schema — including the case that matters most, two categories carrying the SAME spacing defect on BOTH lists with DIFFERENT canonical spellings, which proves income lands on its own list's spelling and never the accounting one. The script remains dry-run by default and this change does not run it against production.

### Explicitly NOT decided here

Do not treat any of the following as settled:

- Whether PO-derived expense rows remain delete-and-reinsert projections in storage. Their display is settled above — one row per purchase order, read-only, linking to Purchasing — but a projection and a persisted record both render that way, so storage is untouched by that decision.
- Where income categories live. Normalisation is settled above, but income categories have no server-side master list at all — they sit in browser localStorage and are never synced — so normalising them makes the values consistent without producing a shared list. This is a Settings question, not a Finance one.
- Where settlement receipts belong. Money arriving from a platform weeks after the sale is not revenue — the order already counted it — but Roots records it today and every channel business has it. Recording it in Transactions would double-count. Nothing in Tacet's model holds it.
- What `wechat_chat` and `pickup` are. Both appear as order channels from August 2026, ¥4,043 across 3 orders, and are named in no channel mapping in the repository.
- Whether Tacet carries an equivalent of `backfillOrderedExpenses()`. The kitchen app's boot-time backfill is flagged above as an uncontrolled ledger writer; whether Tacet should post missing expense rows automatically at all, and if so on what trigger, is not answered here.
- Whether the Products list margin cell should also flag a row whose `unit_cost` already exceeds its sell price. The product editor now warns at the moment the figure is typed or the product is opened (*Unit cost exceeding sell price now warns*, above); an existing bad row does not self-flag on the list until someone opens it. A catalogue-wide passive flag is a different, larger feature and is not answered here.
- Where income categories are CREATED. The subsection above says the tenant creates their own in Settings, and **no such surface exists in either app**: Tacet's admin has no finance-category editor at all, and the kitchen app's income editor writes to browser localStorage and nothing else. The kind is valid server-side and the list ships empty, which is the intended state — but **nothing can add to it**, so a tenant with genuine non-sale income has a decision made for them by an absence. The surface is a build that must follow; where it sits is not answered here. **Explicitly NOT the answer: pointing the kitchen app's `saveFinCats()` at the new kind.** `syncCategoriesToServer` diffs the local list against the server's and **DELETES what is absent locally**, so the first browser to open the kitchen Finance page would push its four localStorage defaults into the shared list and delete anything a Tacet operator had created — **the seed this section bans, arriving by the back door, from the app being retired, with a delete attached.**

## 37. Courier cost is a manual expense entry, and nothing deducts it per order

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-02.**

### The rule

**The money we pay a courier — JD, Qingyun/跑腿, SF, or in-house — is recorded ONLY as a manual expense entry. No screen, report, or order-level figure in Tacet may deduct a courier cost from revenue or from margin. The expense ledger is the single home for it.**

That is the whole rule, and it is a rule about where a cost lives rather than about how a screen is built. It binds every surface that has a revenue or a margin figure on it today and every one that is built later.

### Why — the same yuan, counted twice

Attaching courier cost per-order while it is also recorded as an operating expense **counts the same money twice and understates profit everywhere.** It is not a rounding difference and it does not localise to one screen: every figure downstream of either half is wrong, in the same direction, by the same money.

**The ledger is not empty, and that is what makes this urgent rather than theoretical.** Surveyed 2026-09-02: `expense_entries` already carries roughly **¥13,005** of courier spend, across five channel-specific categories a person typed:

| Category | Amount |
|---|---:|
| JD Delivery (to customer) | ¥7,913.40 |
| Paotui Delivery (to customer) | ¥4,201.27 |
| In House Delivery | ¥1,101.02 |
| SF Express Delivery (to customer) | ¥471.94 |
| Meituan Delivery (to customer) | ¥332.90 |

**Any per-order deduction would double-count all of it.** Not some of it, and not only the orders built after the deduction shipped — the expense rows are already in the books for periods a report can be run over today.

**Recorded because the survey that preceded this ruling could not see it.** The courier-cost survey of 2026-09-02 established from code that no column anywhere holds a courier charge, and named as its one unanswerable question whether courier spend was nonetheless already in the ledger under names nobody had chosen. **It was, under five of them.** The rule is the answer to that question, not a precaution against a hypothetical.

### What is, and what is not, the platform's cost

**On Meituan and Eleme, when the platform's own rider delivers, the platform nets its delivery cost out of settlement before paying us. That cost is already inside 预计收入 and must not be recorded again.**

**Only a courier we pay directly is an expense entry.** The test is not which channel the order came from and not who carried the parcel — it is whether money left our account for that leg. A Meituan rider on a Meituan order costs us nothing we ever pay: it is deducted upstream, and by the time the figure reaches us it is already gone from it. Recording it as an expense would be the same double-count as the per-order deduction this section forbids, arriving from the other side.

### What the settlement panel does and does not show

**The channel money breakdown shows what a platform pays us, with the platform's commission netted out. It does not and must not include what we pay a courier.**

It is a statement of a platform's arithmetic, reproduced so an operator can check it. Adding our own costs to it would make it a margin panel wearing a settlement panel's name, and it would disagree with the platform's own screen — which is the one thing that panel exists to agree with.

### Automatic capture — NOT PURSUED, and why

**Surveyed 2026-09-02** on two branches, `claude/courier-cost-survey-e5s4a6` (`docs/tacet-courier-cost-survey.md`) and `claude/jd-qingyun-pricing-survey-ldjdwz` (`docs/tacet-jd-qingyun-pricing-survey.md`). Both are unmerged at the time of writing; the findings are summarised here so this ruling stands without them.

**QINGYUN.** The quoted `totalFee` is displayed and spent but **never written**. Quote and settlement can differ by five mechanisms, **one of which fires on every dispatch**: the dispatch route re-quotes and spends the fresh figure, not the one the operator saw. **The settled truth is the prepaid wallet ledger, which nothing reads.** `delivery_jobs.raw_order` carries no fee — `amountInfo` is all zeros with `shippingFee -1`, which closes the one recovery candidate the courier-cost survey left open.

**JD.** Every waybill declares a **hardcoded 1kg / 100cm³**, because the admin UI sends only shipment id, product and package count. **JD is not pricing from that, so no creation-time figure could be real.** The true charge is JD's own weighing after pickup; the earliest we could see it is the merchant bill. **No JD response has ever been retained.**

**MEITUAN / ELEME / GZ GROCERY.** Nothing to capture — either already netted from settlement, or not our cost.

**IF AUTOMATIC CAPTURE IS EVER REVISITED, it requires the Qingyun wallet ledger and JD's monthly bill, AND a companion decision removing courier spend from the expense ledger. One or the other, never both.** That last clause is the load-bearing half. A later session that builds capture without withdrawing the expense-ledger half will have built the double-count this section exists to prevent, and it will look like progress while it does it.

### Open, and NOT resolved by this ruling

- **Two `Meituan Delivery (to customer)` expense entries totalling ¥332.90 need checking.** If they are the platform's own delivery fee they are **already netted from settlement and are double-counted today**. If they are a directly-paid courier leg on a Meituan order they are correct. The rule above decides which of the two is permitted; it does not decide which of the two these rows are, and nothing in the ledger records it.
- **The Dashboard delivery figure conflates platform customer-paid delivery with our own webstore delivery charges.** Pre-existing, unchanged, and untouched by this ruling.

Eight processes, twelve in-process schedulers of which eleven run, the read-triggered writes, the inbound callbacks classified by what they tell the caller when the write fails. **Read before anything that takes the database away.**
- docs/tacet-operating-findings.md — **the findings that outlived the Postgres migration**, v1.0, 2026-08-23. Five instruments that lied, ten refusal rules, the live defects, the operational facts about this box.

## 39. Stock movement — settled decisions

**Decided 2026-09-03.** Ruled by Ash ahead of implementation. Everything below was settled during the picking and receiving design work and had never been written down; it is recorded here so the schema and route work that follows has something to be checked against. **No implementation code exists for any of it yet**, and that is deliberate — this section is the brief, not a description of the product.

**Decision — the kitchen is not a stock location.** At Roots the kitchen and the warehouse share the same building and the same freezers. When the kitchen makes 100 units, those units are warehouse stock the moment they exist. There is no handover to record because nothing travels. Production output lands at a CONFIGURED OUTPUT LOCATION, per tenant. Roots points it at the warehouse; a tenant whose kitchen is genuinely somewhere else points it at that location instead. See §0 — the location is a setting, not an assumption about Roots' building.

**Decision — logging a production batch changes stock.** `production_batches` is a pure log today with no write path to inventory, and its schema comment has said "once that's wired in" since it was written. A logged batch increments stock at the output location, ledgered through the same path as every other stock change, and closes off the request that asked for it.

**Consequence — a warehouse-to-kitchen request correctly moves no stock.** It asks the kitchen to MAKE something, not to move something. Stock changes when the kitchen makes it, not when someone asks. The existing `skipped: kitchen_direction` behaviour is right and stays. It is restated here so it is not read as a bug the production work should fix.

**Decision — warehouse to store is a two-step movement.** The van run takes one to two hours at Roots. Stock leaves the warehouse at dispatch, exists IN TRANSIT belonging to neither location, and arrives at the store on receipt. A single-step transfer would either double-count the units or vanish them while the van is moving, and there is no third option: the units are somewhere for those two hours.

**Decision — what the store counts is what the store holds.** The RECEIVED quantity sets stock, not the dispatched quantity. A short delivery becomes 47 at the store immediately, not 50. If the record ever preferred the warehouse's number to the counter's, the shelf and the record would part company and the store would be the one to find out.

**PRECEDENCE — which quantity sets stock, stated out loud.** Added 2026-09-03, because the decision above and the end-of-day auto-settle below read as a contradiction without it, and a session lost time treating them as one. **They never apply to the same line.** The rule:

> **A counted quantity always sets stock.** The sent quantity is used **only** for a line nobody counted, and any line settled that way is **permanently marked unverified** and is never indistinguishable from a counted line. **The record never prefers the warehouse's number to the counter's — it falls back to the warehouse's number only where there is no counter's number at all.**

The order of preference per line is therefore **counted → sent (marked unverified) → nothing.** A counted **zero** is a counted quantity and outranks the sent figure absolutely — "nobody counted it" and "someone counted it and found none" are different facts and the schema must keep them apart. The permanent mark is a schema requirement, not a UI one: an auto-settled line has its received quantity **written**, so without a separate marker it becomes byte-identical to a verified one the moment the sweep runs.

**Decision — the picker allocates every shortfall.** When a line comes up short, Tacet pre-fills nothing. Filling stores in list order was rejected because the same store loses every time; proportional splitting was rejected too. Some products a store can do without for a day and others it cannot, and only the person in the freezer knows which. **One-tap shortcuts are permitted; defaults are not.**

**Decision — short and over receipts are recorded, never blocked.** No reason field, no confirmation step, no accusation. The discrepancy stays open against the transfer and is visible to the warehouse. The store's number updates immediately; nobody waits on anybody.

**Decision — there are two yardsticks and they are not interchangeable.** A line can differ from WHAT THE VAN CARRIED, or from WHAT THE STORE ASKED FOR. These are different failures with different owners: the first belongs to the road, the second to the warehouse's allocation. **Both are shown only after counting.** Showing either beforehand would bias the count, and the count is the entire value of the receiving screen.

**Decision — no automatic cascade.** If a store asks for 50 and the warehouse holds 20, Tacet shows the shortfall and a human decides whether to ask the kitchen. **It does not raise a production request by itself.**

**Design rules established during this work, applying product-wide.** They are recorded here rather than only in `docs/tacet-design-system.md` because each was settled against a real screen and the reasoning is in this document's register:

- **Contrast carries attention.** Graphite means resolved — stop looking. Full Ink means this still wants you.
- **Controls on resolved work recede with the work.** A tick on a finished line is an UNDO control, not a state marker; state is already carried by fill and edge.
- **No copy may assume a location count.** Strings must read correctly at one store, two, or nine.
- **No layout may assume a location count.** Any pattern that only works at two locations is disqualified regardless of how well it reads.
- **`短少` is the only Chinese word for short, product-wide.** See the eleventh amendment in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`.

### §39 addendum — seven further rulings, 2026-09-03, taken against the schema survey

**These were ruled after `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md` was written, and they close ALL SIX of that document's open questions — and, with Ruling 7, E2 as well, which was the last thing gating implementation of any kind.** They are recorded here in short; the reasoning, the code citations and the debt they leave are in PARTS D and E of that document. **One of them goes against the survey's own recommendation, which is stated rather than smoothed over.** Rulings 1–6 were recorded before any implementation code existed; **Ruling 7 is the first of them to land with its code in the same change**, because deleting the clamp and making the negative visible are one act — a negative balance nobody can see is worse than the floor that prevented it.

**Ruling 1 — a dispatch is never blocked by the record.** If the warehouse's figure says 20 and the picker physically finds and sends 50, the send goes through for 50 and the warehouse goes to **−30**. His hands are right and the record is wrong; blocking stops real work to defend a number reality has already contradicted, and a visible −30 is a truer record than a silent zero. **The zero clamp at `lib/inventory.js:1084` is deleted, not made conditional** — which **overrules the survey's own B4 recommendation** that a dispatch exceeding stock should *throw*. **A negative on-hand must also be visible somewhere a person looks**, and one concrete place it currently would not be is named in that document's PART E. **Two things gate the deletion and are NOT settled**: the PO-receiving downward correction (below), and the fact that four channel ingest paths clamp in their own code and so keep doing the very thing this ruling rejects — separate, per-channel work, deliberately out of scope.

**Ruling 2 — abandoned counts auto-settle at the end of the trading day.** Counted lines land at the counted quantity; **uncounted lines land at the sent quantity and are permanently marked unverified** (see PRECEDENCE above). End of trading day, not a rolling timer — a fixed timer fires at 8pm one day and 2am the next; end of day is predictable and matches how a shop already thinks. Store and warehouse are both told the next morning, and any line stays correctable afterwards as an ordinary stock correction. **Recorded honestly: this is a global accept with a timer standing in for a button.** A "mark the rest as sent" button was rejected because it would become the fast path on the busiest days; the timer is defensible **only** because it catches genuinely abandoned counts rather than being reached for, and leaves a permanent mark. **MANDATORY SAFEGUARD, without which this ruling does not stand: repeated auto-settling at one store must surface somewhere a person actually looks.** One abandoned count is a busy Tuesday; four in a fortnight means that store has stopped counting. The boundary is **per tenant, not per store** — the per-store hours and timezone columns are optional, routinely unset and fall back to always-open, and no day-boundary calculation in this codebase reads a per-location zone today.

**Ruling 3 — `storefront_config`, as is.** The warehouse is named per tenant through `cfgValue('stock.warehouseStoreId')` on the existing table. **No rename, no new settings table** — it works, it is already per-tenant, and renaming a live config store mid-build is a gratuitous risk. **The name's poor fit is deliberate, recorded debt.** The read must be on the **tenant handle**: `cfgValue` already resolves on `tdb()`, but the auto-settle sweep of Ruling 2 iterates tenants rather than living inside one tenant's request, and a read there on the shared handle would hand every tenant Roots' warehouse — the same class of bug as the `:333` stamp.

**Ruling 4 — `qty_received` is `REAL`, matching `qty_sent`.** A column disagreeing in type with the one it is compared against on the same line is worse than the wider REAL/INTEGER split, **which is real, is named, and stays separate work** — quantities are `REAL` from the purchase order down through `restock_items`, then land on `retail_store_stock.physical_qty` and the ledger's `delta`/`balance_after`, all `INTEGER`. It already costs a live rounding step in PO receiving.

**Ruling 5 — `delivered` stays.** Once it stops carrying stock meaning it still records a true, distinct fact: **the driver finished his leg.** At Roots that is near-simultaneous with counting; on a longer route it is not. It becomes a pure logistics timestamp — and it is the only field that answers how long a delivery sat uncounted after arriving, which is what Ruling 2's safeguard is built on.

**Ruling 6 — a batch yields one product or several, and the model is the many-products shape.** Ash, 2026-09-03: **both happen at Roots.** So the general shape is adopted **because it contains the one-product case** — a single-product batch is a split with one line in it — and **there are not two code paths.** Four parts. **A batch records what came out of it, per product**: one batch, one or more output lines each naming a product and a quantity, which is **a link table, not a column** on `production_batches`; `recipe_id` stays the record of what was made from what and **does not determine what the batch yielded.** **The split is entered, never inferred** — it varies, so Tacet cannot compute it, must not default it from the recipe, and must not guess; whoever logs the batch states it. **But the common case must not become a form**: where a recipe has only ever produced one product the log **pre-fills that product and asks only for the quantity, one confirm** — the same code path with one line already filled, and a pre-fill offered for confirmation is convenience, never inference. **Stock increments per output line**, at the configured output location, through the ledgered path, **one ledger row per product.**

**What this does to scope, said plainly: production wiring is larger than a column addition, and it is its own piece of work with its own brief, sequenced after the two-step transfer ships.** In order: **(1)** a recipe→product mapping that points the right way — today `store_products.recipe_id` is product→recipe, has no `UNIQUE` index (and under Ruling 6 must never gain one), and is partial by design, while the kitchen-side `products.recipe_id` is documented as wrong data by the very migration that refuses to use it; **(2)** the batch output table; **(3)** the UI for entering a split, with the one-line pre-fill; **(4)** the stock increment itself. **Step 1 is the gate, and it carries an open data question that is Ash's: the 36 ambiguous pairs `store_products_recipe_link_v1` deliberately left unlinked.** Per §29's addendum, no automatic signal is trustworthy as a silent discriminator here — **nobody may resolve those 36 by inference.** Production depends on nothing in the transfer work; the transfer work depends on nothing in production.

**RULING 7 — a downward correction on a purchase-order receipt goes NEGATIVE. DECIDED 2026-09-03, and it closes E2, the last thing gating the clamp's deletion.** The entry that stood here recorded the question as open and named only two candidate behaviours — **clamp silently** (`docs/purchase-returns.md` item 3) or **refuse** (matching the returns path). **Ash chose the third, which nobody had proposed: the correction is neither clamped nor refused, and the shelf goes below zero.**

**Why.** If only 8 boxes actually arrived against 10 on the system, **the 10 is the lie and blocking the correction protects it.** A negative balance is ugly and true: it says stock was sold that was never held, which really happened and which someone should be able to see. This is Ruling 1's reasoning arriving at the other end of the same movement — there the picker's hands are right and the record is wrong; here the count is right and the record is wrong. **A record that cannot be corrected downward is not a record, it is a floor.**

**What the clamp was actually doing, which is worse than permitting a bad number.** `Math.max(0, oldQty + deltaQty)` **discarded a real one**: removing 5 from a shelf of 3 removed 3 and recorded −3, with nothing anywhere saying 2 were unaccounted for. On a warehouse→store transfer it floored the outbound half while the inbound half added the full figure, so a cleanly committed transaction **created units from nothing**.

**The asymmetry with returns is deliberate and stays: returns refuse, corrections go negative.** They are different assertions. A return says goods left the shelf, which is false if they were never there. A correction says the count was always wrong — a claim about the record, not the goods — and refusing it keeps a number everybody already knows to be false.

**Three things ship with it, and the ruling does not stand without them.** **(1) A NEGATIVE MUST BE VISIBLE.** The "Needs you" dashboard filtered out-of-stock on `= 0`, so a negative matched neither that card nor the low-stock one and vanished from the panel entirely — not shown wrong, shown nowhere. Shipping negatives while hiding them would be worse than the clamp. Both the count and the preview clauses move to `<= 0`, together, because they are separate queries and a partial fix gives a card whose number and list disagree. Low keeps `> 0` so a product cannot appear on both. **(2) THE KITCHEN QUICK STOCK DELTA PATH IS GUARDED BY NAME.** Its contract is "I made N more"; with the floor gone an unguarded negative delta there would write a negative through a door nobody meant to open, so it is refused with `delta_must_be_positive` and pointed at the absolute recount, which is what a correction actually is. **(3) `docs/purchase-returns.md` item 3 is struck through and superseded** in the same change, as the entry it replaces required.

**Untouched, and recorded as debt: the four channel self-clamps.** Meituan, Eleme, Guanyi and gzgrocery compute `Math.max(0, …)` in JavaScript and pass an absolute figure, so they never reached this clamp and are unaffected by its removal. They keep doing the very thing this ruling rejects — per-channel work, deliberately out of scope.


**Rationale.** Every decision above is about a moment when goods and the record could disagree — the two hours the van is moving, the gap between what was asked for and what was found, the count that contradicts the dispatch note. Each is settled the same way: the record follows the person who can see the goods, and the system never guesses on their behalf. The screens are drawn in `design-handoff/warehouse-picking/` and `design-handoff/store-receiving/`, and their annotations carry the per-screen reasoning this section summarises.


## 40. A batch size is the sum of what went into the pot

**DECIDED 2026-09-04, requested by Ash.** `recipes.batch_size` is derived from the ingredient lines rather than typed, and `recipes.servings` is derived from it and the serving size. The rules, in the order they bind:

1. **The batch size is the sum of the ingredient lines that end up in the product, in grams.** Mass units convert among themselves with exact factors (g, kg, lb, oz). Nothing else is converted.
2. **A line may be paid for and not come out.** `recipe_ingredients.in_yield` (default 1) is a per-line fact a human states — a vegetable stock brewed for its flavour and then poured away is the case it exists for. **An excluded line is still costed in full.** It leaves the weight, never the money.
3. **A recipe may state its own yield instead.** `recipes.batch_size_auto` and `recipes.servings_auto` (default 1, independent of one another) turn the derivation off. Reduction on the stove, evaporation, trim loss and a pack filled to a stated weight are all cases where the sum of the inputs is not what comes out, and the operator's figure is the true one. The editor **offers** the ingredient total there; it never applies it.
4. **A sum that cannot be completed is refused, never understated.** One line counted in ml or in pcs blocks the whole derivation, and the recipe keeps whatever batch size it already had. This is §7's addendum — no conversion without a stated factor — applied to weight rather than to price: a density is a property of a material and there is none recorded, and a piece weight likewise. **The asymmetry is the whole reason:** an absent batch size has always refused out loud (`lib/recipe-rollup.js`'s `no_batch_size`), while a batch size short one ingredient overstates cost per gram silently, and that overstatement reaches a material's unit cost, a product's cost and a margin.
5. **Servings are `batch_size / serving_size`, floored.** 224.55 g at 25 g a serving is eight sellable servings and 24.55 g still in the pot — not 8.98 of anything. Flooring also errs the safe way: the remainder stays inside cost per serving rather than being costed as if it had walked out of the door. The remainder is named on screen rather than hidden.
6. **No live figure moves on deploy.** `database.js`'s `recipe_yield_auto_v1` marks every recipe already carrying a typed batch size as stating it, and does the same separately for a typed serving count. The derivation therefore reaches only recipes that had nothing — which are exactly the ones the cost cascade refuses today.

**ONE DERIVATION, and it is §29's rule applied to a second question.** `computeYield` and `resolveYield` live in `lib/recipe-cost.js` beside `computeRecipeCost`, which resolves both figures before dividing by either. The material rollup, the Excel export, the waste valuation and the kitchen Cost Sheet inherit the derived batch size without any of them knowing the feature exists, and the Recipes editor reads the same two functions over HTTP rather than summing the lines itself.

**THE COLUMN STILL FOLLOWS THE DERIVATION.** `lib/recipe-yield.js` stamps the resolved figures back onto the row, and both recipe doors call it after the ingredient lines are written and **before** the recompute that divides by them. This is not redundancy: `recipes.batch_size` and `recipes.servings` are read raw — off the column, nowhere near a cost breakdown — by the production batch sheets, the kitchen picker, `routes/products.js`, the AI tool surface and every diagnostic in `scripts/`. A derivation that corrected the figure only on the cost path would give one recipe two batch sizes depending on which door asked, and the one printed on a batch sheet would be the wrong one.

**BOTH DOORS CARRY `in_yield` ACROSS THEIR DELETE-AND-REINSERT**, the kitchen Cost Sheet included, which has no control for it. A door that knows nothing about the flag must not be able to put a deliberately discarded ingredient back into the batch weight, silently, in the number every per-gram cost divides by. Same rule, same reason, as `lib/recipe-cost-data-write.js`'s absent-versus-cleared distinction.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE.** Volume-to-mass stays unconvertible until a density is recorded on the material — the same open item §7's addendum left, now with a second consumer. A recipe whose lines are mostly in ml therefore still needs a typed batch size, and says so.

## 41. A shop is a record attached to a location

A location in Tacet is a stock-holding site. Some locations sell to walk-in customers; others, such as the Roots central kitchen, produce and ship and never face a customer. Shop capability is therefore a role that some locations have and others do not.

Ruling: a shop is a separate record attached to a location, not a set of columns on the location itself. A location with no shop record has no menu, no QR code, no till configuration, no opening hours and no payment binding.

The presence of the shop record is the module gate. Enabling physical-location features for a tenant means creating a shop; there is no separate feature flag for it.

Rejected: adding nullable shop columns to every location. It would put menu, QR, till and payment fields on warehouses and production sites that will never use them.

## 42. One catalogue; fulfilment mode lives on the shop listing

There is one product catalogue. Tacet does not have a separate menu-items entity.

A shop listing joins a product to a shop and carries the price at that shop and the fulfilment mode. Two modes:

- **stocked** — the product is built elsewhere (typically the kitchen), arrives as finished goods, and a sale decrements finished-product stock at the shop.
- **made here** — the product is built at the shop at the moment of sale. Finished-product stock never exists for it. **The product's build lines determine what it COSTS at that shop; they deplete nothing**, because material stock does not exist — see §43, which defers it. Packaging and label lines are cost carried by the product and never countable stock, per §29 and §31 rule 6. A cup is costed into the drink and never counted at the shop.

The same product may be stocked at one shop and made here at another. Mode is a property of the listing, never of the product.

Where a shop record exists, a product is available at that shop if and only if a listing exists for it. This is how a product can be sold at one location only. Locations with no shop record are unaffected and continue to use the product-level IN SHOP visibility defined in §16. Introducing shop listings at one location does not migrate any other location, and §16 is not superseded.

Price lives on the listing, not on the product, so the same product may carry different prices at different shops.

Availability behaves differently by mode. Stocked items become unavailable automatically when store stock reaches zero. Made-here items do not run out on paper and require a manual on/off switch on the listing for daily use — for example when a milk alternative runs out mid-shift.

Rejected: a parallel menu-items table. The difference between a packaged product and a made-to-order one is when the build is consumed, not what kind of record it is.

## 43. Material stock is deferred; a made-here item is costed, not counted

**MATERIAL STOCK DOES NOT EXIST IN TACET AND NEVER HAS.** No table holds a quantity of a material. Materials and ingredients are one table — the `ingredients` masterlist, wearing the tenant-facing name §28 gave it — and nothing on it holds an amount: no stock column, no per-location material stock table, no material ledger, no count. The invariant is asserted against the live database by `scripts/diagnose_phase1b_live.js`, which fails if an on-hand column ever appears on that table.

**The first version of this section asserted a history that does not exist, and that assertion is WITHDRAWN.** It opened *"Materials have historically been held only at the kitchen, because the kitchen was the only site that built anything"*, and no material quantity has ever been held at the kitchen or anywhere else. **This is not a narrowing and not a supersession — the sentence was wrong when it was written**, and because this section is new and unmerged its body is replaced outright rather than marked. A reader who meets the earlier claim in the v4.129 changelog entry above should read it as corrected here.

**Ruling by Ash, 2026-09-05: materials are cut from the location commerce launch scope entirely.**

**A made-here item consumes no counted material stock.** Selling one decrements nothing. What the shop gets is COST, and that half is real and accurate: the product's build lines and its materials' unit costs give a true cost per drink and a true margin, through the machinery §31's addendum already establishes as a product's only cost source. What the shop does not get is an on-hand figure for any material, because there is none to get and none is claimed. **A shop knows what a drink costs it, and does not claim to know how much milk is in the fridge.**

This narrows §42 rather than contradicting it. Made here still means the product is built at the shop at the moment of sale and that finished-product stock never exists for it. What changes is what the build lines are FOR: **they determine cost, and they deplete nothing.** Packaging remains cost carried by the product and never countable stock, per §29 and §31 rule 6 — unchanged, and no longer a special case, because now nothing is depleted at all.

**Finished goods are untouched by this and behave exactly as they do today.** They transfer between locations on the existing store-to-store mechanism, and they decrement on the paid transition per §45. Nothing in this deferral changes a stocked listing, a transfer, a reservation, or any till behaviour.

**What is deferred, named individually so the scope cannot be read narrowly or widely by mistake:** material quantities and whatever table would hold them; a location row for the kitchen; materials moving through the transfer mechanism; and the consumption of a build list against material stock at the point of sale. **Those four are one project, and it is a SEPARATE project.** None of them is a dependency of the QR menu, of a shop listing, or of any shop launch — which is the whole point of this ruling. **The launch is not waiting on material stock, and material stock is not waiting on the launch.**

### Three constraints the material stock project inherits — RECORDED 2026-09-05 so they are not rediscovered

Established by the Step 3 survey. Each cost real time to find, and none of the three is visible from a schema listing alone.

1. **The kitchen cannot be written against stock or loss until it has a store row, and the obstacle is a foreign key rather than a missing flag.** The stock ledger's location column and `waste_records.location_id` both carry hard foreign keys to `retail_stores`. For a place with no row there is no legal value to write, in either table. **Kitchen-ness lives on transaction columns today** — a purchase order's scope, a restock order's roles, a ledger reason — **precisely because the location columns will not accept it.** So the kitchen's location row is that project's first decision, not an incidental step inside it.

2. **Creating that row redefines the tenant's business day.** `lib/business-date.js` resolves a business date from a store's timezone, and where the caller names no store it takes the first active store carrying one, ordered by sort order. **A new row with a timezone and a low sort order silently becomes the whole tenant's date anchor.** This is §32's addendum — the business date resolves from the LOCATION — meeting a location created for an unrelated purpose.

3. **A second active store switches on a prompt at customer checkout.** Order routing carries a single-store shortcut that suppresses the "willing to wait longer?" confirmation; any second active store turns that prompt on for customers. **A row created to hold flour changes what a customer is asked at checkout.**

**None of the three is a blocker.** They are recorded because each is a consequence a reasonable person would not predict from the change that causes it, and all three fire on the same single act.

### The waste half is already built and waiting — FINDING 2026-09-05

**`waste_records` already carries the material subject in full.** `subject_type`, a nullable `material_id`, the exclusive-or CHECK admitting exactly one of the two subjects, and a foreign key from `material_id` to `ingredients` are all in the schema and have been since the waste build. **Only the API refuses a material subject**, and it refuses with a message giving the true reason: materials have no stock to move.

§32's addendum deferred that subject and named its unblocker: *"Material waste unblocks when material stock is designed, which is its own decision and must not be smuggled into a waste build."* **This section is that decision, and it defers rather than grants — so the refusal stands.** But when material stock is built, material waste needs the API opened and a writer added, **not a schema change**. Recorded as a positive finding: the shape was got right in advance, and it is the one part of this that is waiting rather than missing.

## 44. QR ordering: a public web page, not a mini-program
