The narrow flag is the one that means *the kitchen makes this*, and it is the one the rest of the fresh machinery already reads.

### ADDENDUM, 2026-09-11 — a parcel going out is not the order going out

**Reported by Ash from the stock ledger:** *"明天发快递的订单，鲜食自动扣了库存。原因，订单的陆运部分，点击发货，触发了扣除库存"* — TC000656 and TC000647, four fresh units off the count the evening before the food was due to leave, one of them driven to **-1**.

**This is the section's own opening complaint, one route over.** The ruling above says the fresh line decrements at *the first forward transition into fulfilment … a parcel dispatched*. That is right for an order with one parcel and wrong for an order with two, and the wrongness is not incidental: `planShipments` fans an out-of-Guangdong mixed basket into an 空运 parcel and a 陆运 one, and the land box is sent **days ahead so that it arrives with** the air box carrying the food. **The first parcel out of a split order is, by construction, the one with no kitchen line in it.**

**Nothing in the rule was wrong and no guard misbehaved.** Three routes — `shipments/:sid/dispatch`, `shipments/:sid/deliver`, `orders/:id/jd-waybill` — each stamp ONE shipment's `dispatched_at` and then handed `prepareCommitUnreservedOrder` the whole order id. The per-product commit guard then did exactly its job: it found the held-back fresh products uncommitted, and committed them. **Every part behaved as written; none was ever told what had actually shipped.**

#### The rule, restated so it survives the next shape

**A batch-made line decrements when the parcel CARRYING IT goes out.**

- A parcel-level caller passes `shipmentId`. `parcelsStillInTheBuilding` names the order's other parcels with no `dispatched_at`, and kitchen lines riding those are held back exactly as the paid transition holds them.
- **A whole-order caller passes nothing and takes everything** — PATCH /status, Start preparing, both auto-deliver sweeps. That is unchanged, and it is the backstop that makes the hold-back safe rather than a way to strand stock. The last parcel to leave has no other parcel still here, so it sweeps up whatever the earlier ones held.
- **Held back whole-product, and the direction is deliberate.** The commit guard is per product and cannot hold back part of one, so a fresh product split across both boxes waits for the later of them. §58's error to avoid is taking the food off EARLY; one dispatch late is the same count a day nearer the truth, and the sweep-up guarantees it lands.
- **Read on the EXPANDED lines**, so a bundle sitting on the waiting parcel is held by the components that carry `is_batch_made`, not by a wrapper that does not.
- **A line whose `shipment_id` is NULL is claimed by no parcel and is NOT held back.** This rule only ever defers a line that is demonstrably somewhere else.
- **A supplier (drop-ship) parcel is not special-cased**, because it carries nothing the kitchen makes.

#### What this did not need

No schema change — `retail_order_items.shipment_id` has recorded which box a line is in since the split-shipment table existed. No new ledger reason, no new decrement site, no new strings; `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.

#### Recorded, and deliberately NOT done

**The four units already taken are left on the ledger.** The per-product guard means the air parcel's dispatch will skip them, so the count is one day early and was never double-counted; a manual add-back today would leave the shelf over by four from tomorrow, needing a matching correction the next day. Ash was given the choice and the fix shipped without the adjustment.



## §59 — THE KITCHEN QUEUE HANDS OVER ON THE CAPABILITY THAT SCREEN'S WRITE IS GATED ON, NOT ON THE QUICK-STOCK MODE

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the report that *"the kitchen queue, after making the next window should be how many items reached the shelf but that window never open"*.

### What was wrong

"What you made" is the screen between closing a kitchen request and the shelf being right. Marking a request `prepared` moves no stock — that is §39 and is correct — so the queue is supposed to carry the request's own lines straight onto the screen that adds them. The queue says so on the button's own screen: *The next screen asks how many reached the shelf.*

It never did. `hdStart` in `public/m.html` opened only when `qsMode()==='add'`. That mode comes off `/api/retail-admin/quick-stock/context`, and `lib/quick-stock-grant.js` derives it from the **role**, not from a capability: `'add'` is returned only for a backend operator whose `tenant_users.role` is literally `kitchen`. That role ships `stock_app_only`, and `server.js` uses that flag to keep it out of Tacet Mobile entirely — a page request to `/retail-admin` is redirected to `/stock`, and every `/api/` call outside `lib/stock-app-only.js`'s allowlist is refused `kitchen_add_only`.

**The two conditions could therefore never both hold.** Everybody who can open this queue reads `'recount'`. `hdStart` returned false on every tap, `kqAdvance` fell through to the queue, and the promise made one screen earlier was kept for nobody.

### The ruling

**The handover is gated on `production:log`, asked through `canRoute('whatmade')`** — the capability `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on, which is the call the Record button at the bottom of that screen actually makes. The quick-stock mode is not consulted.

**The reason the old gate carried is quoted rather than deleted**, because it was a real argument and it is worth knowing why it fails: *an absolute recounter has no business being handed a delta to apply.* This screen hands over no delta. It posts a production batch, and `routes/retail-production.js` writes the batch and moves the shelf inside one transaction, with no mode gate of its own — only a store-scope check on the restricted roles. **The proof was already shipped one row up the More list**: `logbatch` opens this same screen, with this same write, for a recount-mode operator, and always has. A gate that refuses from one door what it grants from the other is not a rule; it is a defect with a comment on it.

### The second defect, fixed in the same change

`hdOpen` answered `true` unconditionally, while `push()` silently declines a route the operator cannot reach. An operator holding `restock:fulfil` without `production:log` therefore closed the request and got nothing: no screen, and `kqAdvance`'s early return skipping even the re-render. `hdOpen` now asks `canRoute('whatmade')` first and returns false, so the caller falls through to the queue exactly as it does for a request with nothing to hand over.

### The suite proved a state the app cannot be in

`scripts/test_mobile_production.js` set `mode:'add'` in its fixture by hand, and the note beside it called that line load-bearing for the same reason `hdStart` did. Seventy assertions passed across every version of this flow while the flow itself was dead, because the fixture reproduced the only session that would have worked and no session can be it. **The fixture now says `mode:'recount'`**, which is what every operator who can reach these screens actually holds, and the old code fails it. This is the general lesson and it is not new here: a fixture that asserts the state a gate wants, rather than the state the app is in, tests the gate against itself.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **`public/stock.html` carries the identical gate and is not touched.** In that app the `kitchen` role does read `'add'`, so the flow works there; §48 retires the app.

  > **AMENDED 2026-09-07 (v4.145) — THIS LINE WAS WRONG, and the same symptom was reported a second time because of it.** It is true of the `kitchen` role and of no other. Every other operator who can open that app's *Production* queue — the owner, an admin, a `retail` operator, none of them `stock_app_only` — reads `'recount'` there exactly as they do in Tacet Mobile, so the handover was shut for them too. The roles confined to `/stock` are precisely the ones that did not need the fix; the reasoning covered the users who were not reporting it. **The word *Production* appears only in `/stock`** — Tacet Mobile calls the same screen *Kitchen queue* — which is how the second report named the app the first fix had skipped.
  >
  > **`/stock` now takes the same gate**, and because that app holds no capability list of its own the answer is computed server-side: `mayLogProduction(req)` in `lib/quick-stock-grant.js`, beside the `quickStockMode` it replaces, shipped as `can_log_production` on `/api/retail-admin/quick-stock/context`. One derivation, both apps. It carries **no `req.backendUser` requirement** — unlike `mayRecount` beside it, this is not a revocable grant but the capability the write already enforces, and the legacy kitchen realm can genuinely post to that endpoint — and it **fails open** on an unresolvable capability set, as Tacet Mobile's `mCan()` does.
  >
  > **The Log a batch tile on `/stock` stays on the mode.** That tile carries its own decision, written where it stands: stating what a batch yielded is the kitchen's job, and a warehouse recount has no batches. The handover is not that case — the operator reaching it has just closed a kitchen request. §59's Tacet Mobile argument leaned on `logbatch` already opening the same screen for a recount-mode operator; that premise does not hold here, and the ruling does not need it.
  >
  > **A second suite was asserting the defect.** `scripts/test_stock_home.js` held `a-recount-operator-gets-the-queue-back`, defending it as *a warehouse recount has no business being sent to a screen that adds*. Two honest cases replace it. Where the section below says a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants, add this: **a green suite is not evidence the flow works when the suite's own case was written to match the gate.**

  > **AMENDED AGAIN 2026-09-07 (v4.147) — THE GATE WAS NOT THE WHOLE CAUSE.** Both amendments above were real and neither closed the report, because `hdStart` carried two further refusals that were silence rather than an answer. **`state.qs.items` starts `null`** and is filled two CHAINED round trips after the queue first renders — `loadQsCtx`, then `loadQsItems` on its answer — and `hdResolve` matches by SKU against that list. A list that has not arrived marks **every** line unmatched, and `!lines.some(l => l.id != null)` then refused to open at all. An operator tapping through faster than two round trips on a phone, or whose shelf fetch failed, closed the request and got nothing. Reproduced, not reasoned: set `items` to `null` — its real initial value — and the tap produces the reported silence exactly.
  >
  > **A late shelf is not a missing product.** The lines are held and the screen opens now, in its loading state; `loadQsItems` resolves them when the shelf lands. A shelf that never lands gets a named failure carrying the way forward — Retry, and the batch door that needs no request — because the request is already closed by the time anybody is on that screen and there is no way back to it.
  >
  > **Not one line matched is a sentence, not a silence.** The screen has always drawn an unmatched line greyed, badged *Not on this store's list*, with the count named underneath. Refusing to open threw that away and left nothing in its place — strictly worse than the problem it avoided, since a request whose lines this store cannot take is exactly what somebody needs to be told.
  >
  > **What still refuses**, all three about the request or the operator rather than the app's own readiness: no `production:log`; a request with nothing asked for; and no store to add to *once the context has answered and said so*, since `hdCommit` sends `store_id`.
  >
  > **Both apps, in the same commit.** `public/stock.html` carries the identical pair and is fixed alongside rather than reasoned about. Its shelf loads at boot, so the race is *less* likely there — recorded as a fact, never again as a reason to leave a file out.
  >
  > **The third fixture lesson, and the sharpest.** §59 said a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants; v4.145 added that a green suite is not evidence when its own case was written to match the gate; this adds that **a fixture whose stubs answer instantly cannot see a race the real network has.** Every suite set `items` by hand and every stub resolved in a microtask, so no case had ever run the ordinary path where the shelf is still in flight.

  > **AMENDED A THIRD TIME 2026-09-07 (v4.148) — THE SILENCE WAS THE REAL DEFECT, and removing it should have come first.** Each of the three amendments above removed a genuine cause; none of them removed the silence, which is why one bug took four rounds. `hdStart` returned a bare `false` on every refusal and `kqAdvance` fell back to the queue without a word, so an operator who had just closed a request saw an empty list and nothing else — whichever refusal had fired, and with no way to tell which.
  >
  > **Every refusal now names itself.** `hdStart` returns `true` when the screen opened and otherwise `nocap`, `nolines` or `nostore`, which `kqAdvance` turns into a sentence on the queue. It is a **note, not an error** — nothing failed, and the operator did the right thing; what is wrong is the state they are now in. It renders **above the empty state** as well as the list, because *Nothing to make* with no explanation is exactly the screen this defect showed somebody: a queue that has just gone quiet reads as success. `nocap` names `production:log` by the label an admin sees on the permissions screen, so the operator can ask for the right thing rather than report a blank screen.
  >
  > **The general rule, which is worth more than the three sentences: a refusal that lands on somebody who has just changed state — a request closed, the stock still short — may not be silent.** Silence there does not read as *nothing happened*. It reads as *that worked*.
  >
  > **And the fourth lesson in this section's run:** a diagnosis is impossible when the failure has no voice. The first three rounds were spent guessing between causes the app could have named.
- **Neither production screen names which store it is adding to.** `state.qs.storeId` is the first active store from the context response and there is no picker. This is pre-existing, shared with Log a batch, and unchanged by this ruling — recorded here so it is not re-derived, and left for its own change.
- No schema change, no migration, no capability grant changes, no new strings.

## §60 — A KITCHEN TYPES ITS BATCH ON THE CARD; A RECOUNT KEEPS THE SHEET

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the report that entering a batch still took two
taps: *"i want to click one time on the number and input a number directly. now
need 2 click."* Two mockups were put up and **Option B was chosen.**

### What was wrong

§46's add door had just been given a keypad (v4.142): tapping the count on an
Add stock card opened the shared ask sheet with a Quantity field. That removed
the hundred-and-thirty taps and left a smaller defect behind, which is what this
ruling is about.

**The sheet opened with nothing focused.** `sheetAsk()` renders its `<input>`
with no `autofocus` and no `focus()` call, so the keyboard stayed down until a
SECOND tap landed on the field. One tap to open the sheet, one to reach the
field it exists for. The field also asked for `inputmode="text"` — the full
keyboard rather than a number pad — for a control that accepts only digits.

### The ruling

**In add mode the count IS the field.** One tap turns the cell into an
`<input inputmode="numeric">` with the caret already in it; the commit button
takes the correction door's place on the card while it is open; there is no
sheet. **In recount mode the sheet stays**, and the two are reached by different
functions on purpose.

**The asymmetry is the ruling, not an inconsistency.** A recount is a bounded
decision about a figure that is not the operator's own, it is the number §46
guards, and the drop fork hangs off it — a sheet naming the product and offering
Cancel is the right shape for one of those. A kitchen entering what it made is
the opposite: its own count, no fork on the way up, and twenty of them in a row
down a list a sheet would cover between every one.

### What the change must not do, and how each is held

- **The two writes stay apart (§46).** `qsTypeOpen` and `qsAskCount` are
  separate functions, not one function branching on mode — deriving one from the
  other is how a delta and an absolute count become one write. While the count
  is being typed the correction door is **not on the card at all**: the commit
  button stands in its place, so the two are never one fat finger apart even for
  the moment the keyboard is up.
- **The shelf total still never seeds this control (§46).** The field opens on
  the pending amount, and empty at the usual +0 — a "0" would have to be cleared
  before anything could be typed over it.
- **Typing never re-renders.** This is the rule already written at the head of
  the Onwards commands and learned on the waste picker: `render()` rewrites the
  whole app in one `innerHTML`, and destroying a field under a thumb does not
  reliably keep an Android soft keyboard up — Ash saw it drop a letter at a
  time. `qsTyped` stores the digits and does nothing else; no `render()`, no
  `state.focus`. The one focus this control arms is the tap that opens it.
- **The digits are held in state, not read off the DOM at commit**, so they
  survive a render this card did not ask for — a toast, or a poller's dot
  changing state.
- **A non-number is not stripped to the digits inside it.** `13o` silently
  becoming `13` writes a quantity nobody entered, so the field stays open and
  says why. That message carries **no Retry**: Retry belongs to a failed write,
  and this is not one — hence `typeErr` beside `rowErr` rather than inside it.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **An empty field is zero, and goes through the same call as any figure.** The
  field IS the amount, so clearing it and committing means add nothing — and it
  CLEARS the pending amount rather than leaving it. Returning early instead
  stranded those taps: opening the field stands the 700ms pause down, so a `+5`
  left behind would have sat on the card for ever, never flushing, until another
  tap restarted a timer nobody knew was gone. Found by the suite, on the one case
  written with taps already made.
- **That is also the way out of a card opened by mistake**, and there is no
  separate Cancel, matching the mockup that was approved. If it proves too quiet
  in the kitchen, a Cancel beside the commit button is the fix, and it is not
  made here.
- **`public/stock.html` is untouched.** Its own keypad opens from the count in
  both modes and always has; §48 retires that app.
- **No new strings.** `How many did you make? · 制作了多少?` moves from the
  sheet's title to the field's `aria-label`, `Add to stock · 加入库存` from the
  sheet's confirm to the card's button, and the composed validation pair locked
  at `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.26 keeps its job. `Quantity · 数量`
  is no longer used on this screen — a field with the count in it needs no label
  above it — and is recorded as retired there rather than deleted from the lock.
- No schema change, no migration, no capability change.

### AMENDED 2026-09-07, from the floor, on the first build of this ruling

Reported by Ash against the deployed v4.144: *"* and - doesnt work now if i edit
a number manually, also if i dont add a number and i just click on the row it
stay blank even if i leave the row. it should go back to the same dfult it is."*
The screenshot carried three cards blank and open at once.

**Both defects were one mistake: the field was a MODE WITH NO WAY OUT, and the
two keys were switched off inside it.** A card tapped by accident stayed blank,
and stayed blank with dead keys beside it, until something else re-rendered the
app. Nothing on the card said how to leave, because there was nothing to say —
no path existed. The empty-field escape this section already described only ran
when the operator pressed the commit button, which is not what anyone does with
a card they opened by mistake.

**Two corrections, and neither changes the ruling above:**

1. **The keys stay live and FOLD what was typed.** Typing 130 and tapping `+`
   is 131; the field closes and the pending amount carries on as it always has.
   The field and the keys are two ways at one number, not two modes. A
   non-number is still not folded — `13o` says so rather than becoming 13 and
   then 14, exactly as committing it would.
2. **Leaving an empty field puts the card back** to the `+N` it opened on. A
   field with digits in it is left alone: closing that on the way past would
   throw away work nobody asked to discard.

**THE REVERT PATCHES ONE CARD AND NEVER CALLS `render()`, and that is the whole
reason it is safe.** Blur fires on the way to whatever was tapped next, so a
`render()` there would rebuild the entire app under that tap and the click would
land on a node that no longer exists — the `+` being reached for, or the next
card's count. `qsTypeBlur` replaces that card's own two elements and touches
nothing else, so the stepper buttons either side stay the same DOM nodes and
every pending tap still lands. A probe asserts that identity directly.

`qsCountCell` and `qsCardFoot` exist for the same reason: the full render and
the patch draw an idle card through ONE function, so a patch cannot disagree
with a render about what the card goes back to.

## §61 — THE KITCHEN QUEUE SPLITS: EACH LINE HAS ITS OWN STATUS, NOT THE WHOLE ORDER

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from a screenshot of the Kitchen queue detail
screen (PR-260907-010, four lines, one "Start making" button) and the report:
*"they can split what they start making, what was made. its all one batch.
need to fix that."* Asked which axis "split" meant — which item(s) get
started, or a partial quantity within one item — **the ruling is per-item
status only.** A line still moves as a whole; different lines no longer have
to move together.

### What was wrong

A kitchen request (a `restock_orders` row with `to_role='kitchen'`, numbered
`PR-`) carried one `status` for the entire order — `sent → received →
prepared`, `routes/restock.js` `STATUS_FLOW` — and `public/m.html`'s
`screenKitchenQueue` drew exactly one button off it: *Start making* /
*Mark as made*. Four items on one request meant four items forced through
the same two taps together, whether the kitchen was working on one of them
or all four. There was no way to start item 2 without also claiming item 1,
3 and 4 had been started, and no way to finish one while the rest were still
being made.

`restock_items` had no per-line state to hang a split off — `qty_requested`,
`qty_sent`, `is_checked`, nothing else. This is a different axis from the
proposed, unbuilt "batch output split" in `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md`
§D6 (one batch yielding several PRODUCTS); that remains undecided and is not
touched here.

### The ruling

**`restock_items` gains its own `status` (`sent|received|prepared`,
`received_at`, `prepared_at`), mirroring `STATUS_FLOW`.** The kitchen queue
detail screen draws one *Start making* / *Mark as made* button per line
instead of one for the whole order; a line with nothing left to do shows a
check. `PUT /api/restock/:id/item/:item_id/status` (`routes/restock.js`)
advances one line, forward only, same rule as the order-level endpoint.

**`restock_orders.status` stays as the ROLLUP, not a second source of truth.**
It advances to a status only once every line on the order has reached that
status — `_advanceOrderStatus`, called from both the per-item endpoint (when
the last line catches up) and the existing whole-order `PUT
/api/restock/:id/status` (used by transfers and the legacy kitchen app,
neither of which knows about per-item state). This is deliberate: dispatch
(`_applyDispatch`), the push fan-out, the kitchen slip print, and the
What-you-made handover (§59) are all keyed on the ORDER'S status, and none of
that logic is touched — it fires exactly when it always did, at the moment
the whole order is actually done, whether that moment was reached by one tap
or by four spread over an hour. `_advanceOrderStatus` also carries every line
forward to at least its own new status, so a caller that never touches an
item — a transfer, or the legacy kitchen app hitting the whole-order door
directly — cannot leave the two out of step.

**The split is kitchen-only.** The item endpoint 403s on an order whose
`to_role` is not `kitchen` — a transfer between locations has no such
concept — and it is on `lib/stock-app-only.js`'s allowlist beside the
whole-order status door, or the confined kitchen role (the only role that
reaches this screen at all — `restock:fulfil` without `restock:pick`) would
get `kitchen_add_only` on every tap, same failure mode `test_kitchen_queue_
reachable.js`'s history is entirely about.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **No partial quantity within a line.** Ash's answer to the axis question
  was per-item status only; "make 8 of 12 now, 4 later" on a single line is a
  different, larger change and is not this ruling.
- **Backfill is main-database only.** `restock_item_status_backfill_v1`
  (`database.js`) copies each existing line's status from its parent order's
  status/timestamps the day this ships, since up to today the order's status
  WAS every line's status. Tenant databases get the new columns (via
  `reconcileTenantColumns`) with the plain SQL default, no backfill — the
  same gap `_transferContext`'s comment on `stock_applied_at` already
  documents for `restock_goods_state_backfill_v1`. An in-flight kitchen
  request on a tenant database shows its lines as freshly `sent` until each
  is worked again; worst case is one extra tap per line, never a wrong stock
  movement, and it heals itself as the queue is worked.
- **No new strings.** *Start making · 开始制作* and *Mark as made ·
  标记完成* move from the order-level button to the per-line one, unchanged.
- **`public/stock.html`'s own Production queue is untouched, and that is a
  gap rather than a judgement that it does not need this.** It carries the
  identical whole-order `kqAdvance`/single-button shape this ruling replaces
  in Tacet Mobile, and per §59 it is reached by exactly the operators
  `stock_app_only` confines — the `kitchen` role among them — so a kitchen
  account working from `/stock` still gets the old all-or-nothing button. The
  report and screenshot this ruling answers were both Tacet Mobile
  (`public/m.html`'s `Kitchen queue` chrome, not `/stock`'s `Production`
  heading); porting the same split there is real work — its own render
  function, its own DOM-patching discipline (§60) — and is left for its own
  change rather than folded in unread, the way §59's first round found out
  costs a second bug report.

### AMENDED 2026-09-07, same day, by Ash: the What-you-made hand-over splits too

Reported minutes after the ruling above deployed: *"the current problem is
that the what you made ( stock update ) come up only after all products in
the list market as maid. it shouls should up after every product marked as
made, after stock updated it goes back to the products list that not made
yet."*

**What was wrong.** The ruling above only split which STATUS door each line
goes through. `kqItemAdvance` still called `hdStart` — the §59 hand-over to
the shelf-quantity screen — only once the ORDER rolled to `prepared`, i.e.
once every line had caught up. Four items meant three of them opened no
hand-over at all; the fourth (whichever happened to be last) opened one
carrying all four. That is the same all-or-nothing shape §61 was written to
remove, just moved one screen downstream.

**The ruling.** The hand-over now fires per LINE, independently of the order
rollup: the moment any one item is marked `prepared`, `hdStart(order, item)`
opens the shelf-recording screen for THAT item alone, and pressing *Back to
the queue* returns to the same order's item list — showing the one just
recorded (checked) beside whatever is still not made — rather than exiting
to the top-level queue. The order-level rollup is untouched: dispatch,
push, print and `restock_orders.status` itself still advance only once
every line has reached the same point, exactly as the ruling above states.
Only the shelf-recording screen's trigger moved from the order to the line.

**Mechanics.**
- `hdStart(order, item)` takes an optional `item`: every existing guard
  (`nocap`, `nolines`, `nostore`, the shelf-not-loaded wait) reads identically
  either way: `state.hd.awaitingItemId` carries which single line is owed if
  the shelf has not loaded yet, alongside the existing `state.hd.awaiting`.
  Omitted, `hdStart` is exactly the whole-order hand-over §59 built.
- `hdResolveItem(item)` is `hdResolve({items:[item]})` — one line, wrapped
  rather than a second matching implementation.
- A refusal (no capability, no store, nothing asked) still drops back to the
  top-level queue with a note, per §59's "never silent on a refusal that
  lands right after the operator changed state" — that one case is
  unchanged, because a note only makes sense on a screen the operator can
  read without more taps.
- **"The request is closed." no longer follows automatically from `h.rs`
  being set.** That sentence was written for the whole-order hand-over,
  where it was always true; recording one line out of four is not closing
  the request. `hdOpen` now takes a fourth argument, `closesRequest`, and
  stores it as `state.hd.closesRequest` — decided by `hdStart` at the moment
  it opens (`item ? order.status==='prepared' : true`, since `order.status`
  is already the post-rollup value the item PUT was re-fetched for), not
  re-derived later from `state.kq.order`, which the whole-order path clears
  before opening the hand-over and would have made this false even when the
  whole order genuinely had just closed. `h.done.closed` is a plain copy of
  that flag taken when the batch finishes recording. The sentence shown when
  it is false is the SAME neutral line an unrequested batch already used
  (`Across N products.`) — no new string, a fallback that already existed
  for a different reason.
- No schema change, no migration, no new capability, no new strings.

### AMENDED AGAIN 2026-09-07, by Ash: a line made and left unrecorded keeps its door

Reported against the amendment above, from the record screen itself: *"if I'm
on this page and going back I can't come back to this page again, no
option."*

**What was wrong, and it is the amendment above's own defect.** Splitting the
hand-over per line made the record screen reachable four times a request
instead of once — and made it losable four times too. Marking a line made
sets its status to `prepared` on the server BEFORE the screen opens, so an
operator who backs out of that screen leaves a line that is closed with a
shelf that is still short. The queue drew that line with a tick and no
control, so there was no way back to the only screen that adds the units.
The one remaining route was Log a batch, which names no request — the stock
would land, and nothing would say which morning's request it answered.

**This is the shape §59 spent four rounds on, one layer further in.** There,
a refusal that landed on somebody who had just changed state was silent;
here, a state change succeeds and then strands the half that matters. The
rule generalises: **a step that leaves work outstanding must leave the way to
finish it visible on the screen the operator lands on.**

### The ruling

**A line that is made but whose batch is not recorded keeps a door back to
the record screen**, labelled with `production:log`'s own live pair —
*Record what was made · 登记生产批次*, quoted from `lib/capabilities.js`, the
words an admin sees on the permissions screen and the ones §59's refusal
already names. **The tick now means made AND on the shelf**, which is what
anybody reading that list assumes it means.

**Whether a line has been recorded is DERIVED, never stored on the line.**
`_attachRecorded` in `routes/restock.js` answers it on the request's own GET,
by reading the batches written against that request (`production_batches`
carries `request_id` already) and matching them to lines the way the record
screen matches them to the shelf — SKU first, exact name as the fallback,
because a kitchen request carries no `product_id`. Three reasons, in order:

1. **A flag and the batches behind it can disagree; a derivation cannot** —
   `docs/tacet-stock-movement-schema.md` B3's argument for deriving in-transit
   rather than counting it, and it holds here for the same reason.
2. **It needs no migration and is right about every request recorded before
   it existed.** A stored column would have needed a backfill computing
   exactly this join, and would have been right only as far as that backfill
   was.
3. **It is per LINE and per REQUEST.** A batch against another request, for
   the same product, does not tick this one off.

**It fails open, deliberately.** Any error in the derivation leaves every
line unmarked, which offers the way back to a screen that may already have
been used. A wrongly-offered door costs a tap and a second batch the operator
can see themselves about to write; a hidden one costs the stock, silently.
That asymmetry is the whole reason the default falls this way.

**Reopening advances nothing.** `kqItemRecord` issues no PUT — the status
work is finished — it only calls the same `hdStart(order, item)` that the
tap on *Mark as made* runs. A second status call would re-fire the rollup's
push and print on the last line of a request.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **The queue's tabs are untouched.** A request whose every line is made
  moves to *Done* even when a line still owes a batch, so the way back to it
  is through that tab rather than *To make*. Keeping it in *To make* means
  putting this derivation into the list query for every restock row,
  including transfers that have no such concept; it is left for its own
  change, and named here so the next reader does not have to re-derive that
  it was a choice.
- **Only the request's own GET carries `recorded_at`/`recorded_qty`**, and
  only for `to_role = 'kitchen'`. A transfer line carries neither key.
- **`hdCommit` refreshes the open request** (`kqRefreshOpen`) as well as the
  list, so the line just recorded comes back ticked rather than still
  offering the door it has been through. Quiet on failure: the write already
  succeeded, and a stale tick is not worth an error over.
- No schema change, no migration, no new capability, and **no new strings** —
  the button's pair is `production:log`'s own label, copied.

## §62 — AN AFFILIATE'S REWARD REACHES THEM THROUGH THE EXISTING IN-APP INBOX, AUTOMATICALLY, NOT A NEW PUSH CHANNEL

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the retail-admin affiliate ledger (`Jess → Piper` flipping Waiting → Rewarded): affiliates should be told when their referral reward lands. Two questions were open before any code was written — who is told, and on what trigger — and both were put to Ash rather than guessed.

### The ruling

**Who: the affiliate — the referrer — not staff.** The retail-admin ledger already shows the reward to staff; the gap was the referrer's own side, in the mini app.

**Channel: the existing per-customer in-app inbox (`retail_notifications`, written through `notifyCustomer()`), not a new WeChat subscribe-message template and not the operator-composed `retail_broadcasts` campaign feature.** All three notification surfaces already exist in this codebase and are easy to conflate:
- `routes/push.js` is Web Push to tenant STAFF browsers only — no route from it reaches a customer's mini app.
- WeChat `subscribeMessage` (`miniapp/utils/notifications.js`) reaches customers, but only per-order, and only after an explicit system-prompt consent tied to a registered template ID. No template exists for this event, and minting a new WeChat template + consent flow was not what was asked.
- `retail_broadcasts` / `fanOutBroadcast()` is the ADMIN-composed announcement campaign — one message, an operator-picked audience, always operator-initiated (per the existing comment at `routes/retail.js:6814`: *"'broadcast', which is always operator-initiated"*). This event has exactly one recipient, decided by an order paying, never by an admin composing anything — the wrong shape for that feature.

The mechanism that actually fits is the one every other automatic per-customer event already uses: `notifyForOrder`/`notifyCustomer` writing straight into `retail_notifications`, the same path `refund_paid`, `invoice_issued` and `feedback` notifications take. New category `affiliate`, type `reward_earned`.

**Trigger: automatic, one notification per reward, fired from inside `creditReferralReward()`** the instant the referrer's wallet is actually credited — not a manual "broadcast" button an admin has to press per reward. Confirmed by Ash directly (second question, answered "Automatic, per reward"). Only fires when `reward > 0`: a blocked referrer (`affiliate_blocked`) earns nothing on this order, so there is nothing to announce.

### What is NOT changed

- No new WeChat template, no new consent flow.
- No change to `retail_broadcasts` / `fanOutBroadcast` — this event never goes through it, and an admin still composes and sends those by hand exactly as before.
- The referee's own one-shot welcome credit (`refereeReward`, paid to the invited friend on their first order) is untouched — only the referrer is notified, matching exactly what was asked ("every affiliate that just got rewarded").

### Vocabulary

Two composed pairs (notification title + body) plus the notification-center category chip are recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` under *Affiliate reward notification — the mini app inbox*, reusing `已到账` from the already-locked refund-paid pair and `邀请` / `奖励` / `完成首单` / `钱包` from the affiliate and wallet pages' own live copy.

### AMENDED 2026-09-07, by Ash: a tenant can turn this off

The ruling above named the gap and left it for later — *"`notifCategoryEnabled('affiliate')` has no explicit entry… an admin cannot currently mute this category from Settings. If muting it turns out to be wanted, that is a separate, later ask."* Ash asked for exactly that: a toggle so a tenant can turn the affiliate reward notification on or off.

**No server code changed, because none needed to.** `notifyCustomer()` — the one place every automatic in-app notification funnels through — already calls `notifCategoryEnabled(n.category)` unconditionally, for whatever category string it's handed; that check was never hardcoded to `order`/`invoice`/`refund`, so `creditReferralReward()`'s `notifyCustomer(..., { category: 'affiliate', ... })` call from the ruling above was already muteable the moment it shipped. The only thing missing was a switch in the admin UI to flip it, on `PUT /api/retail-admin/config`, which already takes any dotted key (`notifications.categories.affiliate` included) with no whitelist.

**What was added is one row.** A fourth `.nc-row` beside Order/Invoices/Refunds in `public/retail-admin.html`'s automatic-updates panel (Marketing → Broadcasts), wired with the same generic `data-notif-cat="affiliate"` attribute the other three already use — `loadNotifCategories()` and `saveNotifCategory()` in `public/retail-admin/05-marketing.js` read and write it exactly as they do the other three, no new logic. The one-line summary's `NAME` map gained `affiliate: ['Referral rewards', '邀请奖励']` so the folded row's on/off summary names it too.

**Off means neither half fires**, per the existing comment on `notifCategoryEnabled` (`routes/retail.js:6811`): *"Off means neither the in-app row nor the WeChat push is created."* This category has no WeChat push (§62's ruling above), so off means only the in-app row stops — the wallet credit and the retail-admin ledger's Waiting → Rewarded flip are unaffected; only the affiliate's own notice of it is switched off.

Two bilingual strings, both in `public/retail-admin.html`: the row's title reuses the `邀请奖励` pair this document's vocabulary section already locks, and its subtitle — *Sent to the referrer when their reward is credited · 邀请奖励到账时发送给邀请人* — is composed, recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` alongside the rest of this feature's strings.

## §63 — A BROADCAST IS WRITTEN ON THE PHONE; THE "AUTHORING STAYS ON DESKTOP" RULE IS NARROWED, NOT KEPT

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the phone: *"board section mobile — can't create broadcast + no setting. gather all broadcast function same as PC version, make it available on mobile."* Put to him that this reverses a standing decision, with the alternative (settings only, authoring left on the desktop) offered beside it, he chose the reversal.

**THIS OVERTURNS A DECISION THAT WAS MADE TWICE, and the earlier one is not deleted.** `docs/tacet-mobile-parity.md` records — at its line 70, in its Broadcasts parity table, and again in its §4 *Decided* — that composing coupons, flash sales and broadcasts belongs on a keyboard; the mobile create-sheet was **deleted outright** on that reasoning rather than wired up, because it had a submit handler that closed the sheet and toasted "Created" without sending anything. That record stands as the account of what was decided then. What follows is what is decided now, and it moves ONE of those three.

### The ruling

**Broadcasts are written, targeted, scheduled and sent from the phone.** The mobile screen had a read-only feed and a Cancel button, and told the operator in its own empty state that broadcasts "are written and sent from desktop" — a sentence that is now false and has gone with it.

**Coupons and flash sales are NOT moved.** The parity document's rule survives for them, narrowed rather than repealed: what earned the exception is that a broadcast is a *sentence and an audience*, decided in the moment something is worth interrupting customers for — the shop is out of something, a batch just landed, the doors are shut today — while a coupon is a rule with money in it and a flash sale is a schedule against stock. **The test the next reader should apply is not "is it authoring" but "is the decision made standing up?"** A broadcast is. Do not read this ruling as opening the other two.

### What is NOT built, and why the parity document was right about it

- **No rich text, no image, no template library.** The desktop composer has none of these either; the payload is a title, a body, an audience, a time and an optional deeplink.
- **No draft state.** The desktop has no draft either (`status='draft'` exists in the column and nothing writes it), and a half-written broadcast surviving on one phone is a message that goes out later than the moment that prompted it.
- **The form opens empty on every entry**, on the same reasoning as the kitchen request screens: what is left in it after a send is the last thing sent, and re-opening on it is how one announcement goes out twice.

### What it is built on — and the server is untouched

**Not one line of server code changed.** Every endpoint the phone now calls already existed for the desktop: `POST /api/retail-admin/broadcasts`, `GET /broadcasts/audience-count`, `GET /broadcasts/regions`, and `PUT /config` for the automatic-updates switches. This is a client that had been kept away from a finished API.

**Who may send is decided in one place and it is not this screen.** `lib/cap-routes.js` maps every write under `/api/retail-admin/broadcasts` to `broadcasts:send`, so the phone gates the Write button and the composer route on that same capability — the Waste screen's pattern exactly: the screen is `broadcasts:view`, the button carries the write. An operator holding only view gets the list and an empty slot rather than four steps ending in a 403.

**The audience count is the server's, never the phone's.** The count under the buttons comes from `/broadcasts/audience-count`, debounced, and every answer carries the sequence it was asked under — chips tap faster than a request returns, and a late reply for a filter nobody is on any more is the number that would get believed. It is also the number the send button says, from the same call, so the two can never describe different audiences.

**A local time typed into a phone is converted once.** `<input type="datetime-local">` yields the operator's own wall clock and `scheduled_for`/`expires_at` are UTC; the conversion happens in `bcfWhenISO()` and nowhere else. This is the first datetime input in `public/m.html`.

### The four switches, which are the other half of the report

*"No setting"* named a real absence: the desktop's Broadcasts tab carries the **Automatic updates** panel — Order & shipping, Invoices, Refunds, Referral rewards (§62) — and the phone had no route to any of it. It now has the same four switches, reading and writing the same `notifications.categories.<key>` on the shared storefront config, reached from a row on the Broadcasts screen exactly as the desktop reaches them from that tab. A category with no entry is ON, so nothing is backfilled and no shop's messages change because this shipped.

**The switches use the phone's own ink track, not the desktop's sage checkbox.** The two surfaces have disagreed about what "on" looks like since both existed (`public/m.html`'s `toggle()` is ink — *"a shop owner flipping their own setting is the owner acting, not Tacet"* — and `public/retail-admin.html`'s `.bx-tgl` is sage). Each surface keeps its own, because a switch that matches every other switch on the screen it is on beats one that matches a screen the operator is not looking at. **The collision is recorded, not resolved** — a ruling on it is a sweep of both files and is not this change.

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **THE CANCEL-SEND BUTTON ON THE LIST IS UNGATED.** `POST /broadcasts/:id/recall` is `broadcasts:send` server-side like every other write there, and the phone's existing Cancel button has never checked it — an operator with view-only sees a button that 403s. It is left alone in this change because it predates it and touching it here would hide a working button on a stale capability read; it is named so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.
2. **REGIONS ARE CAPPED AT TWELVE CHIPS.** The desktop lists every city with a saved address; the phone shows the first twelve and no "more" control. A shop with a long tail of cities can still send — it simply cannot narrow to a thirteenth from here.
3. **THE DESKTOP KEEPS `Send again`.** Repopulating the composer from a sent broadcast is a list-row action the phone does not have; nothing depends on it and it is a separate change.

## §64 — THE PHONE READS THE CATALOGUE TO ITS END; IT DOES NOT FILTER ON THE SERVER

Decided 2026-09-08, closing the half that §63's neighbouring fix (PR #363, "stop a fifty-row page standing in for the catalogue") named as still open and left open on purpose. That fix made `loadCatalogue` the only writer of `DB.products` and pointed the All chip at the server's `total`. It then wrote, in the code, that the endpoint caps at 500 rows and that **"paging the phone past that cap is a separate change"**. This is that change.

### The defect it was left holding

`GET /api/retail-admin/products` capped at 500 rows and took no page number, so on a catalogue past 500 the reported bug recurred one order of magnitude up, and every symptom of it with it:

- **The four chips beside All under-counted silently.** Live / Draft / Low / Out are got by walking `DB.products`, so they described the first 500 while All — which reads the server's count — told the truth. Two figures on one chip row, disagreeing, with nothing saying why.
- **Search and the category chips could not reach past the cap.** `prodFiltered()` matches within the array; a product at position 501 was unreachable from the phone with nothing saying so.
- **A variant family straddling the boundary lost its siblings.** `prodUnits()` groups by walking the same array — exactly the "2 sizes" loss that made the original report legible.
- **`openProduct` and an order line's SKU chip failed past the cap**, because both resolve a sku against this same array.

### The ruling

**The phone walks the catalogue a page at a time until it holds the whole shelf. It does NOT push its filters to the server.** `routes/retail.js` gains an `offset`; `loadCatalogue` reads 500 at a time until a short page or the server's own `total` says the shelf is finished.

**Server-side filtering — the obvious answer, and the one the Orders and Customers screens already use — was rejected, for a reason specific to this array and not to lists in general.** `DB.products` is not the Products screen's list. It is the phone's product lookup, and the Orders screen reads it: `openProduct(sku)` and the SKU chip on an order line both resolve against it. A server-filtered array is a VIEW, so the moment a filter was set on Products, an order line's SKU chip would stop opening products the filter excluded — the same class of defect just fixed, arrived at from the other direction. Two more things are derived by walking the array whole: the variant families (`prodUnits`), which a page boundary cuts in half, and the category chips (`prodCategories`), which would list only the categories present on the page. Making the server carry all of that is a much larger change than paging, and paging keeps the phone doing what the desktop grid already does — hold the catalogue, narrow it in the browser — rather than making the two surfaces disagree about what a catalogue is.

### Two things without which the paging would be unsound

1. **`id` is now the last ORDER BY key on that endpoint.** The three sort keys are not unique between them — two unpublished products can tie on `sort_order` and `name_en` — and SQLite may order tied rows differently in two statements. Across `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` that is not cosmetic: a tied row can land on both pages or on neither, so a two-request read silently gains a duplicate or loses a product. Adding a unique final key changes nothing for a single-page read except the order of exact ties, which had no defined order to change.
2. **Rows are de-duplicated by id as they arrive, and the offset advances by what the SERVER sent.** A walk is not an instant; a product created underneath it shifts every later row by one. Advancing the offset by what survived the de-duplication instead would re-ask for the row just dropped, and the walk would sit on the spot.

### The screen is honest at every instant, which is the point rather than a trimming

**A count got by walking the array is drawn only while the array is the whole shelf.** `state.catalogueComplete` is a property of the array as it stands — set by whatever last wrote it — not of the read that is running. Where it is false the four derived chips draw no badge at all, exactly as they draw none before the first read lands, and All keeps its own count because All never came from the array.

**A refresh never paints fewer products than it already had.** Pages accumulate in a local array and are published mid-walk only when the new prefix is at least as long as what is held: on a first load that is every page, so the shelf fills in front of the operator; on a refresh of a complete catalogue it is none of them, because publishing page one would replace 900 rows with 500 for the length of a round trip and every lookup past the cap would fail during it. The final publish is unconditional, so a catalogue that genuinely got smaller still lands.

**A read that reached nothing does not license a count of zero.** A first page that fails publishes nothing rather than an empty catalogue — otherwise a phone that could not reach the server would announce a shop of zero products, which is the same substitution as a page standing in for the shelf, at the other end of the scale.

**Where the walk stops short, the screen says which fraction it is holding** — an amber bar reading `Showing the first 500 of 900 products.` with a Try again beside it, drawn only where the two figures actually disagree. The string is a near-copy of the desktop's own J-01 truncation banner; it is declared, with the sentence that was dropped and why, in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.32.

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **A catalogue read that fails on its FIRST page still leaves a blank screen.** No cards, no message, no retry — the four chips draw no counts, which is honest, but nothing names the failure. This predates the change (the previous loader did the same) and the partial bar deliberately does not cover it, because the bar's whole content is two figures and in this state there is only one. Orders and Customers both have the "Could not load…" + Try again pattern this wants; wiring it here is a separate change with a string of its own.
2. **The runaway guard's advice is wrong in the one case that trips it.** `CAT_MAX_PAGES` is 20 — ten thousand products, far past any tenant — and a phone that reached it would be offered a Try again that does the same thing and stops in the same place. It is left as one message for both stopping conditions because the reachable one is a failed page, and a second string for an unreachable state is a string nobody will ever read and everybody will have to maintain.
3. **The desktop grid still reads one page.** `paLoad()` fetches without an offset and sets `PA_TRUNCATED`, so a catalogue past 500 is still short there — the banner `tdShowTruncation` exists for exactly that and the grid says so rather than lying. The endpoint can now serve it the rest; making it ask is a separate change on a separate surface.
4. **The boot seed still reads `?limit=50`.** It is a lookup seed, it stands aside the moment `catalogueTried` is set, and it never sets the flag the counts read — all three asserted by `scripts/test_mobile_catalogue_count.js` §3. It is not touched.

## §65 — "ASK THE KITCHEN" HAS A THIRD PURPOSE, AND URGENT MEANS THE QUEUE MOVES

**DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-08.** Code: this section is written before it.

### The question

"Ask the kitchen" asks one question before it asks anything else — *What is it for?* — and it had two answers: **For an order**, a customer is waiting; **For the shelf**, restocking what we hold. Neither says *make this one first*. A warehouse operator with an order due in two hours and a routine shelf top-up had the same sentence available for both, so the only thing that decided what the kitchen made first was the order the requests happened to arrive in.

### What is decided

**1. `urgent` is a third value of `purpose`, not a new column.**

`restock_orders.purpose` is TEXT with no CHECK constraint — added by `addColumn` in `database.js`, which is how every column on that table arrived. A third value therefore needs **no migration, no back-fill and no default**: existing rows keep `'order'`, `'shelf'` or NULL, and each still means precisely what it meant. The server's whitelist gains one name.

**REJECTED: an `urgent` boolean orthogonal to the purpose.** It would let a shelf restock be urgent, which nobody has asked for and which the request itself argues against — a shelf is by definition the thing that is *not* being waited on. Against that it costs a schema column, a second piece of state in `state.rq`, a second control on a screen whose whole virtue is that it asks one question, and a second thing for the kitchen to read on the card. §39's no-prefill rule also gets harder to hold: a toggle has a default and a default is a reason nobody gave.

**REJECTED: asking about urgency only after "For an order" is picked.** Two taps on the commonest path to spare a third button on the least common one.

**2. Urgency is a SORT, not a colour.**

`GET /api/restock` ordered by `created_at DESC, id DESC` and nothing else. Under that sort an urgent request raised at 09:00 sits *below* a routine one raised at 09:05, and the kitchen finds it only by reading every card. The list now sorts `purpose = 'urgent'` first, with `created_at DESC` still ordering inside each group, so the queue's existing shape is unchanged for everything that is not urgent.

**The key tests `purpose = 'urgent'` and nothing else, deliberately.** That endpoint serves store→warehouse rows as well, where `purpose` is NULL by design; the expression evaluates the same for every one of them and their order does not move. A change to a shared query that is not inert for the direction it is not about is a change to two things.

**3. It is added in four places, because `purpose` is read in four.**

A value that three readers understand and the fourth does not is worse than no value: the fourth prints a blank where a reason belongs, and a blank on a kitchen slip already means *this request predates the field*. So: the picker in Tacet Mobile (`public/m.html`), the same picker in `/stock` (`public/stock.html` — §48 retires that app but has not deleted it, and a slip printed from either must read the same), the kitchen queue's chip in both list and detail (`public/kitchen.html`), and the printed slip (`lib/feie.js`). The two "what was this for" label helpers — `krPurpose` in Tacet, `kqPurpose` in `/stock` — are the same reader and are counted with the pickers.

**4. The Chinese is composed and declared.**

`加急订单` and its sub-line are composed, not lifted, and are recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.33 under the 2026-09-06 amendment with the live pairs they were built from. `加急` is live in `public/retail-admin.html` ("当日达加急"); `优先` is live in the dashboard ("最早优先", "库存最少优先"); `制作` is live in this very screen ("制作完成前库存不变"). Nothing here is a character this repository had not already committed to.

### What is NOT decided here

- **Urgency does not reach the store→warehouse direction.** Those rows carry no purpose and this change gives them none.
- **Nothing is escalated over time.** An urgent request does not become more urgent, and a routine one does not become urgent by ageing. Both are questions about a policy nobody has stated.
- **No new push.** An urgent request broadcasts on exactly the channel every kitchen request already broadcasts on; a separate alarm is a decision about who is woken up and is not this one.

## §66 — THE WAREHOUSE IS TOLD ON THE DASHBOARD IT ALREADY READS, AND THE ROW CARRIES A CLOCK

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the warehouse account: *"i have products that are ready from the kitchen, there is no
real proper notification right now that i will be able to see properly if i look on mobile or pc … that notification
need to come on the dashboard direct. maybe another widget for that? or maybe you have a better advice."*

Put to him as two calls — how loud the row is, and where its click goes — with mockups of each option drawn in the
product's own tokens, he chose the amber row with an age on it, opening the list that already exists.

### What was already true, and why it was still missed

§48 gave `warehouse→kitchen` a server-side `seen_at`, a dot on the phone and a push, and **all three are correct.** What
none of them is, is on the front door:

- the dot is 6px of Sage on **More**, two taps from Home, and deliberately never a count and never red;
- the toast only lands if the app is already open;
- the push is one moment on one handset — pocket, silent, or swiped off a lock screen;
- **and on the desktop there was nothing at all.** Grepping `public/retail-admin/` for `kitchen-ready` returned zero
  hits. This was never a permission or a setting: the code had not been written.

### The ruling

**One server key, two dashboards.** `kitchen_ready` joins `/api/retail-admin/dashboard/ops` — the snapshot the desktop
dashboard and the phone's Home already poll on the same 60-second cycle, and already render as **Needs you**. The row
therefore appears at the top of both, in the strip that is full width, structurally first, and cannot be dragged
elsewhere or hidden.

**Rejected: a widget of its own.** It is what was asked for, and it is the wrong shape — a tenth polling path, a card
empty most of the day, and a fix that reaches the desktop only.

**The row is amber and carries an age.** This is the decision, not the styling. Needs-you sorts severity, then
oldest-first, and **a fire with no age sorts last.** On the Stockroom role the only other fire that ever appears is
*Restock needed*, which has no clock by design — so a calm, clockless version of this row would sit permanently
underneath the one thing the warehouse already knew. With an age it leads, every time, without anyone writing a rule to
make it so.

**Rejected: the calm treatment.** Truer to "nothing needs doing", and it loses the ordering that makes the row worth
having.

**The cost is named rather than discovered:** the row sits under a heading reading *Needs you* while strictly nothing
needs doing — the kitchen shelves what it makes and records the stock itself. Offered beside the alternative; taken.

### The click, which is load-bearing

**It opens `/stock?go=ready` — the list the phone's own More row opens.** Not a convenience: **opening the list is the
only acknowledgement this direction has.** The read is a server-side `seen_at` (§48), so one person looking clears the
row for the whole warehouse and takes the dot off every other phone with it.

- **Rejected: a row that states the count with no door.** It could never clear from the desktop at all — the fire would
  burn until somebody picked up a phone — and every other row on that card opens something.
- **Rejected: a second ready list built inside the admin.** A twin of a screen the Quick Stock app already renders and
  the phone already opens. The desktop leaves the shell instead, and the price was named and accepted: the sidebar goes
  while you read the list, and you come back with the browser's Back button.

### One clause, not two

The four conditions behind the count — kitchen direction, made, not archived, not yet read — move to
`lib/kitchen-ready.js` and are **required by both routes rather than retyped in the new one.** A fire that disagrees
with the queue it opens means one of the two is lying. `scripts/test_kitchen_ready_dashboard.js` asserts both that the
shipped SQL carries the shared clause and that no second copy has grown back anywhere in the tree; both assertions were
verified to fail when the clause is deliberately forked.

**Both audience gates are applied on the server as well as the client** — the maker is not told about their own output,
and an operator who cannot open the list is never told about it — **as an honest zero and never a 403.** This endpoint is
polled in the background, where a refusal bounces a pocketed phone to the login screen.

### No Chinese was composed

Both strings are copied verbatim from locked live sources: `Ready from the kitchen · 厨房已完成` is the list's own name
in `public/m.html` and `public/stock.html`, and `View · 查看` is live in `public/m.html`. The age renders through the
existing bilingual age helpers. **No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed for this change.**

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **THE PHONE'S HOME AND THE DESKTOP GATE THEIR FIRES DIFFERENTLY.** `tdAttnRender` runs every row through
   `dashCardWants()`; `opsFires()` on the phone gates only some of them, so a role without `orders:refund` can still be
   shown *Refunds waiting* on Home. The new row is gated on both surfaces. The pre-existing divergence is named so the
   next reader does not take this row's gate as evidence the others have one.
2. **THE DESKTOP HAS NO READY LIST OF ITS OWN**, by the ruling above. If that is ever revisited, the thing to preserve
   is that `seen_at` is stamped by whatever screen actually shows the rows — not by the dashboard row being clicked.

## §67 — THE RAIL OBEYS THE SAME CAPABILITY RULES AS THE PHONE, AND A ROLE IS NEVER LANDED WHERE IT CANNOT COME BACK TO

Reported by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the Stockroom account — two messages, one defect:

> *"this is the warehouse account, it has the dashboard but the moment i click anything on the left menu i cant go back
> to dashboard"*

> *"basically there is no syncing between what the warehouse account sees on mobile compared to what it sees on pc with
> the same permission. one thing obvious is the dashboard differences."*

### What was actually happening

The account holds neither `dashboard:view` nor `reports:view` — its rail showed Orders, Sales, Counter till, Products,
Waste, Customers and Manage team, and hid Dashboard and Reports. **That is not a bug in the gate; it is the gate
working.** The bug is everything the shell does around it.

`#tab-dashboard` carries `class="active"` in `public/retail-admin.html`: it is the section the backend boots showing,
before any capability is known. `applyCapGates` then hides the Dashboard rail row and **leaves the operator standing on
the section**. So the account was handed a screen its role excludes, and the instant it picked any other row that screen
became reachable only by reloading the page. From the desk that reads exactly as it was reported.

The phone has answered this since its tab bar was capability-filtered — `landOnSomethingReachable()` in `public/m.html`,
whose own comment says it plainly: *"THE APP OPENS ON HOME, and Home is a board of revenue. An operator without
`dashboard:view` was therefore shown, for the length of one render, the one screen their role exists to exclude — and
then had no way to leave it."* **The desktop was built first and never got the rule.** That is the whole of the
"no syncing" report: not two tables disagreeing, but one surface having been taught something the other had not.

### The ruling — three halves, all of them the phone's rules applied to the rail

**1 · A role is landed somewhere it can come back from.** `landOnSomethingReachable()` joins `01-core.js` under the
phone's name, so the two read against each other. It runs ONCE, from `setCaps()`, the moment the operator's real
capabilities arrive — not from `applyCapGates`, which a dozen render paths call and which would otherwise yank an
operator off the page they are working on. It moves nobody whose current section still has a rail row leading back to
it, and nobody at all when caps are null (fail-open, as everywhere else). The row it lands on is **the top of that
operator's own menu**, read in the order the rail draws it — CSS `order` first, DOM order as the tie-break, the pair
flexbox itself resolves by — and a root row rather than a folder's child, because landing inside a folder opens a level
nobody asked for and hides the other tools behind a back arrow. The phone makes the same choice for the same reason.

**2 · Hiding a row is not refusing it.** A hidden rail button is still in the DOM and still answers `.click()`, which is
what `goTab()` does — so every in-page route into a section was ungated: the dashboard's own *"The full numbers live in
Reports"* foot link opened Reports for a role holding neither key. `canTab()` asks `TAB_CAP` (so a tab with no rail row
of its own — a channel admin, the Product Page Editor — is gated too) and `goTab()` refuses **before** it looks the
button up. The foot link carries `data-cap="reports:view"` so it is not a control that visibly does nothing, and the
command palette indexes only pages the operator can open — `gatedOff()` read the feature gate alone.

**3 · Every screen the phone gates, the rail gates.** Two rows carried no capability at all:

- **Manage team is `team:view`** — the key `ROUTE_CAP.team` has always named. The row moved to the rail from the avatar
  menu on 2026-07-14 and arrived without a gate, so since then every operator on every tenant could open the roster:
  names, roles, and each person's permissions, from a role built to count stock.
- **Sales is any-of, and deliberately wider than the phone's.** `ROUTE_CAP.sales` is `dashboard:view` alone because the
  phone offers no channel admin at all. On the desktop this page is the **only** door to the Meituan / Eleme / Guanyi
  screens — they lost their own rail rows in the Sales redesign, and `salesGo()` is a thin alias for `goTab`. Gated on
  `dashboard:view` alone it would shut those screens away from the very role that holds `meituan:sync`, the role whose
  own dashboard tells it to go and restart a stalled channel. So it admits `dashboard:view` **or** any of the three
  channel view keys **or** `integrations:view`.

**And the money on the far side of that wider door carries its own gate**, or the widening would have handed a stock
role exactly the revenue it was widened to avoid: `#sales-summary` and all seven `.sales-ch-metrics` blocks are
`data-cap="dashboard:view"`, so a stock role gets the channel cards and their Configure buttons with the revenue, order
counts and AOV gone.

**Rejected: gating Sales on `dashboard:view` and giving the channel admins a rail row of their own.** It is the tidier
answer and it is a new row in the rail — a fourth destination for a job that has one door already, added to fix a gate.
If the channel screens are ever wanted outside Sales, that is its own decision.

**`setup` is the one deliberate divergence from the phone**, and its reason is written where the table is:
`#setup-nav`'s display is OWNED by `suRefreshChrome`, which writes the same `style.display` the gate pass does. A second
writer would fight it — `applyCapGates` runs on a dozen render paths, so *"Open your store"* would return to the rail
every time an operator painted a `[data-cap]` button after setup had finished. The row is already absent for everyone
once the store is open, which is the case that matters; a narrowed operator on an unfinished tenant still sees it.

### What this does NOT decide, and is Ash's

**Whether the Stockroom role should hold `dashboard:view`.** On the reporting tenant it does not — which is why that
account has no Dashboard row and no Reports row, and why the shipped `warehouse` preset (which *does* carry
`dashboard:view`) is not what that account resolves to: roles are tenant data now, edited in the matrix.

This matters beyond the rail, because **§66 was decided the same day and puts the kitchen-ready fire *on the dashboard
the warehouse already reads*.** A Stockroom role without `dashboard:view` never sees that row on either surface. If the
account is meant to read its dashboard — and §66's own quote, *"if i look on mobile or pc"*, says it is — **the fix is
one tick in Settings → Team → Roles, not code.** Ticking it makes the Dashboard row appear, which is the reported
complaint answered directly; leaving it unticked now lands the account on Orders instead of stranding it. The change
above is correct under either answer, which is why it did not wait on one.

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **Cards INSIDE a section are still indexed by the palette on the feature gate alone.** Only the top-level tab loop
   consults `canTab`. Closing the card level means teaching `gatedOff` to read an inline `display:none`, which would
   also drop every legitimately-collapsed-but-reachable panel out of the index — a silent shrinking of search, traded
   for a leak nobody has reported. Named so the next reader knows the level was chosen, not missed.
2. **`opsFires()` and `dashCardWants()` still gate the dashboard's fires differently on the two surfaces** — §66's own
   "deliberately NOT fixed" list already carries this, and nothing here touched it.

### §67 addendum — the role's Dashboard cards reach the phone, and Today gets the money gate it never had (decided 2026-09-08)

§67 above closed the desktop's half of "no syncing between what the warehouse account sees on mobile compared to what it
sees on pc". The report continued, with a screenshot of each side — the Roles editor for Stockroom, and the phone's Home
under it — and the second half is the mirror image of the first: **where the rail had rules the phone already had, Home
had none of a rule the desktop already had.**

**The setup, as configured.** *Has a dashboard* ticked. Layout **The full view**. Cards: *Needs you*, *While you were
away*, *Inventory*, *On the way / Drafts*, *On the road*, *Ready to hand off* and *Delivery* ticked — **Today**,
**Customers** and **Unhandled orders** unticked.

**What the phone showed.** *Today*: Revenue (all channels) ¥732, Orders 5, Avg. order ¥222.45, New customers 10. And
*Also today*: Sessions, Conversion, Returning, Refunded. Both of the cards the owner had turned off, and both of them
the money ones.

### Why it happened

`/api/backend/me` has carried `dashboardCards` since the field existed, and the desktop has honoured it since then —
`dashCardGate()` in `03-dashboard.js`, applied as an inline style so it beats the `body.pos-*` rules on specificity.
`public/m.html` calls the same endpoint and **never read the key.** There was no gate to break; there was nothing.

That is also why the *layout* half could not have saved it. `recapNoMoney()` narrows the Recap and *Also today* for the
`warehouse`, `dispatch` and `customer_service` boards, and this role's layout is **`default`** — the full view. A board
that is not one of those three was always going to be handed the owner's numbers.

### The ruling

**Four of the ten catalogue keys have a section of their own on Home, and each is gated on exactly the key its desktop
twin carries:**

| Card key | Desktop block | Phone section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recap` | *While you were away* | `recapCard()` |
| `needs` | Needs you (full-width, outside the grid) | the fires list |
| `orders` | *Today · 今日* | *Today* |
| `customers` | *Customers · 客户* (New today, Sessions, Conversion, Returning) | *Also today* |

**The other six — `unhandled`, `inventory`, `incoming`, `onroad`, `ready`, `delivery` — are desktop cards with no phone
twin, and that is recorded rather than closed.** Home surfaces those states as Needs-you fires and Quick actions, not as
cards of their own. **Rejected: inventing a section on Home for each so every tick has something to hide.** A checkbox
that grows a card nobody asked for is a worse answer than a checkbox that governs the desktop only, and the mapping
above says plainly which is which. The suite asserts the catalogue is still ten, so a new card cannot be added without
someone deciding what it means on the phone.

**`null` stays "no override" on both surfaces.** Every role whose owner has never opened that field resolves to null,
and a null that hid everything would empty Home for the whole product on the deploy that shipped this.

### The money half, which is worse

*Today*'s desktop twin is hidden for the `warehouse`, `dispatch` and `customer-service` boards by `retail-admin.css`. On
the phone **that card had no money gate at all** — not the card override, which did not exist, and not even the
`recapNoMoney()` line its own immediate neighbour `vitalsBlock()` carries three lines further down. A stock or delivery
role read the shop's takings off the first screen the app opens, on a board built to exclude them.

It now carries both, **in the desktop's order of precedence: either gate hiding is enough.** An owner's card override
cannot switch the money back ON for a board that hides it — on the desktop an allowed card has its inline display
*cleared* rather than forced, so the board's CSS rule still wins, and the phone matches that rather than inventing a
precedence of its own.

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **The layout dropdown offers "The full view" to any role**, and that is what this account is set to. Nothing here
   changes it: which board a role opens on is the owner's call, and the card override is the control that answers it
   per-card. Named only so the next reader knows the `default` layout was the configuration, not a fault.
2. **Quick actions are not in the card catalogue** and are not gated by it. They are the operator's own six, chosen on
   the handset from what their capabilities already allow, which is a different question from what an owner puts on a
   role's board.

## §68 — A VARIANT FAMILY IS EDITED FROM THE SHEET IT COLLAPSES INTO, AND SAVE WRITES THE FAMILY

Reported by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the phone, with a screenshot of the product sheet open on
`Raspberry Mango Sorbet · SKU (3-210) X5`: *"on mobile, if product have variants - cant change"*.

### What was actually broken

The phone's catalogue collapses a variant family into **one card** — three sizes of one sorbet are three rows and one
card, which is right and is what the card was built for: without the collapse the list reads as three unrelated
products with almost the same name. The card prints the sizes along its second line, `X1 · X5 · X10`.

**That line is text.** Tapping the card ran `openProduct(rep.sku)`, where the representative is
`members.find(m => m._id === p.gid) || members[0]` — whichever size happens to own the group. Every other size in the
family was on screen, named, and **reachable from nowhere on this phone**: not from the card, not from the sheet the
card opens, not from search (`prodFiltered` matches the same collapsed units). A price or a count on any size but one
could only be changed from a desktop.

### The ruling

**The sheet carries the family.** A row of size chips sits under the quick-edit note; the marked one is the size being
edited; tapping another switches the sheet to it. One tap target on the card, as before — the card is a picture and a
name, and turning its size line into three small buttons is a worse thing to hit at 390px than a chip row inside the
sheet that opens.

- **Rejected: the size line on the card becomes buttons.** Three ~40px targets inside a scrolling list row, and the
  operator still has no way to compare the sizes once they are in the sheet.
- **Rejected: one row per size in the catalogue.** That is the list as it read before the families were collapsed, and
  it is the thing the collapse was built to fix.

**Switching a size writes nothing.** It is a change of view, not a save.

**Therefore Save writes the family, not the size on screen.** This is the decision the rest follows from. Once the sheet
can move between sizes without writing, an operator can set a price on `X1`, a count on `X10`, and press Save — and a
Save that took only what was in front of them would drop the rest **silently**, which is the failure mode this record
exists to refuse. Pending edits are held per product id (`sheetPrice`, and `sheetStep` keyed `st_<pid>_<storeId>`), and
Save walks every size and writes the ones that changed. A family of one is a family of one and behaves exactly as
before.

- **Rejected: save-on-switch.** It writes on a navigation, which no other control in this app does.
- **Rejected: warn-on-switch.** A modal between two chips, on every switch, to protect a case the state can simply
  carry.

**A failure part-way through a family says so.** `That did not save. Nothing has changed` is the message for one write;
across several it can be a lie, and an operator told it will retype figures that are already in. The count of writes
that landed decides which of the two messages is shown, and the partial one says the rest can be pressed again — a
figure written twice writes the same figure. The pair is composed and declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.34.

### The one it uncovered, fixed in the same pass because it is the same box

`render()` rewrites the whole shell, so the price `<input>` is rebuilt on every paint. A price **typed and then
