followed by a tap on a stock stepper** was painted back to the stored figure, and the typing was gone — no variants
required, and shipping for as long as the sheet has had both controls. The price now lives in state and is captured on
input, which is also what lets it survive a trip to a sibling size.

## §69 — "READY FROM THE KITCHEN" COUNTS PRODUCTS AND NAMES THEM; THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT SPLITS WITH IT

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the phone: a screenshot of the Kitchen queue
on `PR-260908-005` — three lines, `Maple Cinnamon Almond Butter`,
`Peanut Butter (100% Peanuts)`, `BioCurcumin+ (Organic)`, one of them already
marked made — beside a screenshot of the desktop Needs-you strip showing no
kitchen row at all, and the report: *"if only 1 product marked as made , it
wont show it on dashbaord ,thats a problem , why not to mention the speicifc
product kitchen made directly on the dashbaord this way the user wont need to
open the order and check inside ,too many clicks"*.

Two sentences, one defect and one ask, and they have the same fix.

### What was wrong

§66 gave the warehouse a Needs-you row for work the kitchen had finished, and
§61 — decided the day before it — split the kitchen's WORK to the line while
leaving `restock_orders.status` as a rollup that catches up only once every
line has reached the same point. That rollup is deliberate and stays: dispatch
(`_applyDispatch`), the push fan-out and the kitchen slip print are all keyed
on the ORDER's status, and each must fire exactly once, at the moment the whole
request is actually done.

**Every outward signal was written against that rollup**, and there were three
of them, all reading the one clause in `lib/kitchen-ready.js`:

- `GET /api/restock/kitchen-ready` — the phone's dot
- `/dashboard/ops → kitchen_ready` — the Needs-you row, desktop and phone Home
- the list at `/stock?go=ready`, and the phone's own `kitchenready` screen

So a request with one of three products made sat at `status = 'sent'`, and all
three answered zero about a jar that was already on the shelf. **The §61
addendum had fixed this exact shape one screen downstream** — the What-you-made
hand-over now fires per line — and the outward signal was never brought along.

The second half of the report is about the same row. A fire that says
`Ready from the kitchen · 3 · oldest 2h` names a COUNT and an AGE, and to find
out *what* the kitchen made you open the list, open a request, and read its
lines. **The request number is the one fact about a finished jar that nobody in
the warehouse can act on.** The name is the whole of what they came for, and it
was two taps down behind a row whose entire purpose is to save the trip.

### The ruling

**The grain of the signal is the LINE, not the request.**
`lib/kitchen-ready.js` now joins `restock_items` to `restock_orders` and counts
finished lines. A finished product is news on its own, whatever its request's
status says. The pill counts products; the row names them.

**`restock_items` gains its own `seen_at`, and the count forces it.** With one
stamp per request, reading the news about the first product made would silence
the second — the acknowledgement has to be as fine-grained as the news. Opening
the Ready list stamps the LINES it drew, exactly as it stamped the requests it
drew before.

**The two legacy arms are what make the new clause a strict SUPERSET of the old
one rather than a different set**, and they are the load-bearing part of this
ruling:

- **`OR r.status IN ('prepared','delivered')`.** §61's backfill
  (`restock_item_status_backfill_v1`) ran on the MAIN database only; a tenant
  file got the new columns with their plain `'sent'` default and no data
  migration. Reading the rollup as well means a request that closed before §61
  shipped — or on a tenant that never ran the backfill — still counts, because
  `_advanceOrderStatus` guarantees an order at `prepared` has every line at
  `prepared` whether or not the row says so.
- **`AND r.seen_at IS NULL`.** `restock_items.seen_at` is added and
  **deliberately NOT backfilled.** Under the old clause `seen_at` could only
  ever be stamped on a request whose every line was done, so an acknowledged
  order means acknowledged lines. Dropping this arm would relight months of read
  history as unread news on the morning this ships. Copying the parent's stamp
  down would say the same thing twice; leaving it NULL and reading both says it
  once, and keeps the record of who was told what before this column existed.

**`POST /api/restock/kitchen-ready/seen` takes `item_ids` and still honours
`ids`.** A page cached on a phone before this deploy goes on sending request
ids, and the sentence it is making — "I have read this request" — is exactly as
true per line as it was per request, so `ids` is resolved to that request's own
unseen finished lines rather than dropped. Reading it as item ids instead would
have silently acknowledged whichever unrelated lines happened to carry those
numbers.

**The row names two products and tails the rest.** `retail-admin.css`'s
`.td-nmeta` truncates at a narrow width by design — a row that wraps to two
lines makes a five-row card jump every time an age ticks over — so a third name
would ellipsize mid-word rather than read. `+N more` is honest about what is not
shown, the hover title carries the whole string, and the list behind *View*
carries all of it. **The tail counts off the COUNT, never the preview**, which
is capped server-side at 8: a tail computed from the preview would say `+6`
while 14 sat waiting.

**Both name columns travel in the payload, not the one matching the request's
language.** The dashboard's language toggle repaints from the snapshot it
already holds without re-fetching, so a payload carrying one language would flip
the row into the wrong one until the next poll.

**The screens the fire opens list products too.** A fire that disagrees with the
queue it opens means one of the two is lying — the rule `lib/kitchen-ready.js`
exists to keep — so a row naming products over a list of request numbers is not
a cosmetic mismatch. `GET /api/restock/kitchen-ready/lines` is the list's
endpoint: the same clause, minus the two seen arms, because the LIST is a record
("what did they make today" has to answer the day after somebody glanced at it)
and only the COUNT is unseen-only. The request is still one tap away, on the row.

**And both detail screens stop lying about a partly-made request.** They can now
be opened on one — a state they could never be in when only whole requests
reached them — and *"The kitchen has put this on the shelf and recorded the
stock. Nothing to do here."* would be a lie about two thirds of the page. Made
lines carry the tick; the rest carry the kitchen queue's own
*To make · 待制作*; the request-wide note appears only when it is true of the
whole request; and progress is stated as the numeral `1/3` beside the live
*made · 完成*, rather than a clause composed for "some of it is still cooking".

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **`restock_orders.status` is still the rollup and still fires everything it
  fired before.** Nothing about dispatch, push, or the slip print is touched.
  §61's ruling on that stands word for word.
- **`restock_orders.seen_at` is not dropped or migrated.** It is the record of
  every acknowledgement made before `restock_items.seen_at` existed, and the
  clause reads it forever.
- **No partial quantity within a line**, exactly as §61 ruled. "One of three
  products" is the axis here; "8 of 12 of one product" remains undecided.
- **One row per fire, not one per product.** Considered and rejected: three
  finished products would push three other fires off the top of a strip that
  sorts oldest-first across all of them, and Needs-you is a strip of what needs
  answering rather than a feed.
- **The row fires on MADE, not on made-AND-recorded.** The §61 addendum notes a
  line can be marked made and its batch left unrecorded; that is the kitchen's
  own follow-up, tracked on the kitchen's own screen, and the warehouse's
  question is answered the moment the food exists.
- **No Chinese was composed.** `more · 更多` is live in
  `public/retail-admin/16-purchasing.js` in this exact `+N more` construction;
  `, · ，` is `public/m.html`'s own meta-fragment join; `made · 完成` and
  `To make · 待制作` are both already live on the screens being edited. No entry
  in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed.

## §70 — THE RECEIVE SCREEN SAVES ITSELF, AND ONE VISIT IS ONE DELIVERY

Asked by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the phone, with a screenshot of a nineteen-product order open on the receive screen:
*"no need the button 'record delivery' should be auto saving"*.

### What the button cost

`Record delivery` sat at the foot of the list, under the summary card. On the order in the screenshot that is nineteen
products and sixteen still unanswered — a scroll away from the work, reached after every visit, and disabled until at
least one product had been marked. It was the last thing between a delivery somebody had counted and a delivery the
system knew about, and it earned nothing by being there: every answer above it was already a complete, unambiguous
statement about one product.

### The ruling

**There is no save button. Every answer schedules the write; the pause sends it.** A tap marks the screen dirty and
starts a 1200 ms timer, the last tap wins, and leaving the screen — Back, or the phone going to the lock screen — spends
whatever the timer was still holding. The summary card's eyebrow changes tense to say which of the two states the screen
is in (`About to record` while something is owed, `Recorded` once it is in), and a strip where the button stood reports
the write.

- **Rejected: a write per tap.** Twelve stock-and-finance passes over one order where one belongs, and see below for
  what it does to the journal.
- **Rejected: save only on leaving the screen.** It is the simplest thing that removes the button and it has the one
  failure this screen may not have — an app killed mid-count loses the delivery. `scripts/test_mobile_receiving.js`
  names that at its head as the failure nobody forgives.

**The pause is 1200 ms, not Add stock's 700 ms.** Add stock is a stepper under one thumb; this is read the product name,
find the box, answer. Sized to the gesture, and the number is not load-bearing for correctness — the ruling below is
what makes the journal right at any pause length.

### The collision this actually turned on, and how it was settled

**A delivery is not a save** (`public/m.html`, the Receiving header; `routes/retail-purchasing.js` `DELIVERY_SQL`). The
Received list shows one row per receipt that brought a line **for the first time**, so that a person reading it sees
van-loads rather than button presses. A screen that writes on every pause would have put one van in that list as many
times as the counting paused — destroying the derivation the list is built on, and only the operator would have known
it was one van.

**Therefore a save may name the receipt to add its lines to.** The first write of a visit opens the delivery and answers
with its id; every later write in that visit names it and amends it. `received_at` is not touched — it dates when the
delivery started being counted. A line answered twice in one visit is **replaced** on the receipt, not listed twice: the
delivery brought four, not "five, then four". Corrections **across** visits are still their own receipt, which is what
the journal reads as a revision, and that is unchanged.

**The desktop passes nothing and is untouched.** One press of Save there is one delivery, as it always was.

**A named receipt that no longer qualifies opens a new one rather than refusing.** The desk can undo a receive while the
door is still counting. An extra row in the journal is a blemish; a delivery refused at the door is the failure above.

### What it cost elsewhere, recorded because both are real

**An answer that has been recorded can no longer be un-answered by pressing the control again.** Clearing `qty_received`
back to null would leave the booked units on the shelf behind it — `applyReceivedToStock` skips a null line and so
reverses nothing. So the press that used to undo now **opens the line to be corrected**, and `Not 40` books the zero
that does reverse the stock. Undo is untouched for the second or so before the pause is spent, which is where a mis-tap
is caught.

**A confirmed short line with no reason yet is held back, not blocking.** The server refuses the whole payload over one
such line (`planReceiptReason`), and with no button to grey out that refusal would have stranded the twelve lines that
ARE answerable behind the one that is not. It is held, and the amber line says those are not recorded — the new half of
that message, because everything around them now is. The pair is composed and declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.35.

**The confirmation screen is gone with the button that reached it.** It was the receipt for one deliberate save; there
is no such moment now, and a screen that threw the list away and said "done" would be lying about a visit with sixteen
products still to answer. What it said is said in place: the summary card carries the tally, under a heading that says
whether it is recorded yet.

Proved by `scripts/test_receive_amend.js` (the journal, server-side) and the cases added to
`scripts/test_mobile_receiving.js` (the screen).

### §70 addendum — the undo was wired to the wrong control (2026-09-08)

§70 above rules that an answer the server has already recorded cannot be taken back by pressing its control again, and
that the press should open the line to be **corrected** instead. **That ruling stands. Where it was applied was wrong,
and the screen was broken by it for an hour.**

The guard went into `recvArrived`. The only control that reaches `recvArrived` on an already-answered line is the
"Not checked yet" undo — the arrived chip is rendered only when the line is UNanswered, and the folded row's own tap
goes straight to `recvOpenLine` and always did. So the guard's entire reach was the undo, and on a reopened line it set
`recvOpenLine` to the id it already held: the handler ran, the render changed nothing, and the row had no other way to
close. Reported within the hour, on RPO-0030's Goji Berries: *"cant click now , not checked yet"*.

**What I checked and what I did not.** I checked that the rule was sound — that un-answering a recorded line cannot
reverse booked stock, which is true and is why `applyReceivedToStock` skips a null line. I never asked which control
would actually hit the guard. The rule was right about the world and wrong about the screen.

**The ruling, restated where it belongs:**

- **Not yet recorded** — "Not checked yet" un-answers the line, exactly as before. Nothing was written, so nothing is
  owed.
- **Already recorded** — that sentence is no longer available to say. The button becomes `Done` and folds the
  correction away; the way back to nothing is the counter beside it, where a zero is a correction and a zero *does*
  reverse the stock.
- **Drawn only where it would move the screen.** On a recorded line mid-correction — a changed count, or damage — there
  is no button rather than an inert one. The row stays open on its counter, which is what a short line looks like
  anyway.

**A second defect, older than auto-save, fell out of the same reading.** "Not checked yet" borrowed `recvArrived`'s
toggle, whose first test is `on && recv > 0`. On a line answered *nothing arrived* that is false, so the press fell
through to the else branch and marked the line **fully arrived** — the one control for "I have not checked this"
asserting the whole order had turned up. The undo has its own command now (`recvUnanswer`) and states only what it does.

**Still open, and not decided here: taking a recorded line back to *unanswered* has no path at all.** Correcting it to
zero is the nearest thing, and it is a different fact — it says the goods did not come, where the operator may mean
they have not looked yet. Giving the screen the true undo means teaching `applyReceivedToStock` to reverse a line whose
`qty_received` goes back to null, which is a change to the shared stock and money path and is Ash's to rule on. It is
recorded rather than smuggled in behind a bug fix.

`Done · 完成` is taken verbatim — live six times in `public/m.html`, including on this same screen. No Chinese was
composed.

## §71 — THE KITCHEN QUEUE CARRIES A CLOCK, TELLS THE COOK WHAT ARRIVED, AND CLOSES A LINE IN ONE TAP

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the kitchen, against three screenshots of Tacet Mobile's Kitchen queue — the Done
list, the To make list, and `PR-260908-009` open on its two lines:

1. *"picture 1 time is miising of each request"*
2. *"picture #2 - if for exmaple im on 'done' amd i get a new order 'to make' need to have some kind of a small dot
   notification"*
3. *"picture #3 - start making step is not neccesary. should stRT FROM MARK AS MADE. save one click for the kitchen"*

Three separate observations of one screen, taken in one sitting, and they are one change: the queue as the kitchen
actually stands in front of it.

### 1. The clock is the REQUEST's, and it is the same clock on both tabs

Every row said what to make and never when it was wanted. A request raised at 08:10 and one raised twenty minutes ago
read identically, so *which of these has been waiting* could not be answered from the list at all — on the one screen
where it is the whole question.

**It is the time the request was RAISED (`sent_at`, falling back to `created_at`), on the To make tab and the Done tab
alike.** One meaning for one column: the same request read on either tab shows the same clock, and the list's own sort
— urgent first, then newest first (§65) — becomes legible instead of arbitrary.

- **Rejected: the finish time on the Done tab.** More useful in the moment and it makes the column mean two different
  things depending on which tab you are standing on. A column whose meaning moves is a column that gets misread on the
  morning somebody is in a hurry, which is every morning.
- **Rejected: an age ("40m ago").** §66 put an age on the warehouse's Needs-you row, and that is a fire in a strip that
  sorts by it. This is a worklist somebody reads down; a wall clock is what a kitchen already runs on.

**The day is carried with the hour, not instead of it.** `fmtDay` answers "Yesterday" and drops the time with it —
precisely on the row where how long a thing has been sitting matters most. Kitchen prep legitimately spans days, which
is why these rows are the one direction exempt from the queue's own overnight archive sweep (`routes/restock.js`), so
the queue holds genuinely old work by design. Today renders as the clock alone.

### 2. A dot on "To make", and it is the SCREEN's dot, not the account's

The queue was fetched exactly once per visit. A request raised while the cook was reading Done, or standing inside
another request, was invisible until they thought to leave the screen and come back.

**One 6px Sage dot on the segment, never a count and never red** — the same chrome every other piece of arriving work
in this app gets (§48, §66). No chime and no toast: the ding belongs to a customer arriving, and a new kitchen request
already fires a push and prints a slip.

**It is per-device and per-session, and that is the deliberate difference from `seen_at`.** The warehouse's dot (§48)
is a shared server-side fact because one person looking should clear it for the whole team. This one answers *something
arrived while I was reading the other tab* — a fact about the screen in front of one person, which another phone
clearing would be wrong about.

**The poll runs only while the queue is on screen.** There is nothing to poll for when nobody is looking at the tabs,
and the app already carries two background heartbeats (orders, kitchen-ready). Twenty seconds, its own `fetch` rather
than `api()` for the reason `fetchUnseenOrders` states at length: a 401 out of a heartbeat would navigate a phone
sitting on a counter to the login screen.

**The first answer of a session is a baseline and lights nothing** — a queue holding four requests when the app opens
is a backlog the cook can see, not four things that just arrived. Same rule as the other two pollers.

**Standing on "To make" IS reading it,** stamped where the rows land rather than in each of the three commands that can
bring them up. On that tab the list itself is the notification and the poll refreshes it in place; it repaints only when
the rows actually changed.

### 3. "Start making" is deleted, from both queues

A kitchen line walked `sent → received → prepared`, and the middle step recorded something nothing reads: **no push, no
print, no stock movement, and no screen anywhere hangs off a kitchen line or order being `received`** —
`routes/restock.js` fires on `sent` and `prepared` only. What it cost was a tap per product, in a kitchen, on a phone,
with wet hands — and a queue where half the lines read "Start making" and half read "Mark as made" for no difference
the cook could act on.

**The server is not changed.** Its guard is a FORWARD move, so `sent → prepared` was already legal; the clients simply
stopped spending a round trip on the middle status. The rollup, the push fan-out and the slip print still fire exactly
once, on the roll to `prepared`, from a request that now never passes through `received` —
`scripts/test_kitchen_queue_item_split.js` case 8 asserts exactly that, because those side effects had only ever been
exercised from `received`.

**A line left at `received` by the old flow reads exactly like a fresh one:** one button, still to make. Nothing needs
migrating and nothing is stranded.

**Both queues change in the same commit.** Tacet Mobile moves one LINE at a time (§61); `public/stock.html` still moves
the whole order and is the whole product for a role locked to it. A workflow that differs between two screens the same
kitchen may open is worse than either version of it.

- **Rejected: keeping `received` as an optional "I've started this" marker.** Nobody reads it, and an optional step is
  a step somebody still has to decide about.
- **Not done: removing `'received'` from the per-item endpoint's accepted statuses.** It is what makes an in-flight line
  from the old flow harmless, and the whole-order door still uses it for transfers.

### No Chinese was composed

`Mark as made · 标记完成` (mobile) and `Mark as made · 标记已完成` (`public/stock.html`) are both already live on the
screens being edited and are used exactly as they stand; `Start making · 开始制作` is deleted, not replaced. The clock
renders through the existing `fmtDay`/`fmtTime` helpers — a numeral needs no label in either language — and the dot has
no text at all. **No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed for this change.**

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **`scripts/test_mobile_production.js` has eight cases failing on `main`, and they are not this change's.** They drive
   `APP.cmd('kqAdvance', …)` — the whole-order command §61 deleted — so they have been red since §61 shipped, unseen
   because the suite lives in the slow shard, which is not run (`CLAUDE.md`). Verified by running the suite on the base
   commit before this change and after: eight failures both times, and every case this change adds or edits passes.
   Repairing them means deciding what the whole-order hand-over cases should now assert, which is §61's question, not
   this one's — a separate PR.
2. **`public/stock.html`'s queue rows carry no clock and no dot.** Only the one-tap rule crosses to that surface,
   because the rule is a fact about how the kitchen works and must not differ between two screens; the clock and the dot
   are screen furniture on a list Ash was not looking at.

## §72 — AN ANSWER ON THE RECEIVE SCREEN CAN ALWAYS BE TAKEN BACK

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-08, from the floor, against a screenshot of `RPO-0030` open on the receive screen — three of
sixteen lines checked, Red Lentils sitting on its counter at the ordered 10, and the word **Done** circled in red
underneath it:

> *"this changed to somethnig i didnt confirm , i should have an option to undo an action for example if i click arrive
> i should be able to undo that"*

### What was actually on that screen

§70 took the Save button off this screen: every answer schedules a write and a 1.2-second pause sends it
(`RECV_PAUSE`). That pause is also, until this section, the entire window in which an answer could be taken back.
Before it fired a line offered *"Not checked yet"* and the undo worked. After it fired the control was **withdrawn** and
*"Done"* — which only folds the row — stood in its place, because clearing a count the server already held would not
have taken the units off the shelf: `applyReceivedToStock` skips a null line and so reverses nothing.

So the screen offered an undo for one and a bit seconds, then quietly replaced it with a button that reads like
agreement. That is what Ash was looking at.

The three lines checked without a confirmation are the same defect from the other end. `recvAllArrived` undid by
**skipping every line the pause had already carried**, so pressing *"All 16 arrived"* and pressing it again a moment
later left behind whatever had been written in between — with nothing on screen to say why those three stayed.

### The decision

**A null arrived count on the receive payload is an UNDO, and the route reverses it.** It asserts this product never
came — the same assertion `/undo-receive` has always made about a whole order — and it goes through the same planner
(`planPOReversal`, now taking an optional set of lines) on the same terms.

**Every answered line carries the undo, recorded or not, under one word: *Undo*.** It used to carry two different
sentences depending on a fact the operator cannot see — whether a 1.2-second timer had fired. One operation gets one
name. *"Done"* stays beside it on a line that can fold, meaning what it always did: fold this correction away without
making one.

**A reversal that cannot complete in full is REFUSED, and writes nothing at all — counts included.** Goods sold since
they were booked cannot be given back, and the same `undoBlocked` pair the desktop shows is lifted verbatim onto the
phone (`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`, LOCKED 2026-08-27). The button is still drawn on such a line: a control
that withholds itself teaches nobody why.

**Undoing the last recorded line returns the order to Sent.** Otherwise a mis-tap leaves an order that says Delivered
with not one line claiming a delivery — out of To receive, and the operator hunting for the order in front of them.

- **Rejected: a longer pause with a more prominent undo.** It moves the cliff without removing it. Ten seconds later
  the operator is in exactly the position this section exists to answer, and it costs the delivery journal a slower
  write for nothing.
- **Rejected: an "undo this delivery" control for the whole order.** One mis-tap would cost the whole van's counting.
- **Rejected: leaving the correction-to-zero path as the only way back.** A zero says *nothing arrived* — a short line,
  owing a reason, written into the journal as a delivery of none. That is a different fact from *nobody has said yet*,
  and asking an operator to state the wrong one to undo a mis-tap is how a screen teaches people to lie to it.

### What is NOT in this

1. **The desktop receive screen is untouched.** It has a Save button, so it has never had this cliff.
2. **No new Chinese.** *Undo · 撤销* is a live pair (`public/retail-admin/04-orders.js`, `public/cms-mobile-v2.html`)
   and the refusal is the locked `undoBlocked` pair lifted whole. Nothing was composed, so
   `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is unchanged.

## §73 — THE DESKTOP GETS ITS OWN "READY FROM THE KITCHEN" LIST, AND §66's REJECTION IS SUPERSEDED

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-08, from a PC on the store back office. The dashboard's *Ready from the kitchen* row was
tapped and the whole tab left for `/stock?go=ready&from=dashboard` — a 390px phone app, titled **Quick stock · 库存**,
with the back office gone from around it:

> *"why it change address and called 'quick stock' the whole quick stock indenended app is over. i need it to go away.
> i want all to be unified as one. tacet app."*

### This section decides the DESKTOP only, and §48 is untouched

**§48 already rules the retirement itself** — *"there is no second app"* — and its four-step sequence, its inventory of
homeless flows and its migrate-before-delete ordering are not reopened here. §48 is written entirely about the phone:
it names Tacet Mobile as the destination for every flow and says nothing about the desktop admin at any of its four
steps. **The desktop is the half its step 4 leaves unanswered**, and that is what this section closes.

**Step 2 of §48 is complete as of this section's date, verified against the tree rather than assumed.** Every flow §48
listed as living in `/stock` alone now has a screen and a row in `public/m.html`: `SUBS.pick`, `SUBS.receivexfer`,
`SUBS.askkitchen`, `SUBS.askstock`, `SUBS.kitchenready`, `SUBS.stockadd` (both modes, per §46), `SUBS.logbatch` and
`SUBS.whatmade`. Both departures §48 required to become screens did: the Kitchen queue is native, and the Transfers
row is deleted outright — *"the row goes with the last of them"*, which it has. What remains of §48 is step 3, the
unlock, and step 4, the deletion.

### The ruling

**The desktop admin gets its own Ready-from-the-kitchen list, and the dashboard row opens it in the shell rather than
navigating away.** No address change, no separate document, no phone page on a PC.

**§66's rejection of "building a second ready list inside the admin" is SUPERSEDED, and its reasoning is not
overturned — its premise is.** §66 rejected the twin because *"the Quick Stock app already renders it and the phone
already opens it"*, and on that day both halves were true. §48 step 4 deletes the app that made the first half true.
**A rejection resting on a screen that is being deleted stops being a rejection when the screen goes**, and the price
§66 explicitly named and accepted — *"the sidebar goes, you return with Back"* — is the cost that was reported from
the floor above.

**The drift argument inverts once the app is gone, and that is the whole of why this is safe.** §66 was right that two
surfaces rendering one list is drift this codebase works to keep out. After step 4 there is exactly ONE other renderer
— Tacet Mobile — and the desktop has none. Building it makes the second of two, which is what every comparable screen
in this product already is: Receiving, Waste, Purchasing and Delivery each render on the phone and on the desktop from
one server clause. This list becoming the fifth such pair is the house pattern, not an exception to it.

**THE NAVIGATION STAYS LOAD-BEARING, and this is a requirement rather than a note.** Opening the list is the only
acknowledgement this direction has: the read is a server-side `seen_at` (§48), stamped for the rows the screen draws,
and one person looking puts the row out for the whole warehouse. §66 rejected *"a row that states the count with
nowhere to go"* precisely because such a row can never clear. **The desktop list must therefore stamp `seen_at`
through the same endpoint the phone posts to, or the dashboard fire it opens will burn forever.** A desktop list that
merely renders is worse than the departure it replaces.

**ONE CLAUSE, NOT THREE.** The four conditions behind the count stay in `lib/kitchen-ready.js` and are REQUIRED by the
desktop renderer as they already are by both routes. §66's rule holds unchanged and now covers a third reader: a fire
that disagrees with the queue it opens means one of the two is lying.

### Rejected

- **Pointing the desktop at Tacet Mobile's version of the list** (`/m?to=…` in place of `/stock?go=ready`). It costs
  nothing to build and it is the option that looks like unification without being it: the separate app's name and
  address go, and a PC operator is still handed a phone-shaped page with the back office gone from around it — the
  exact thing reported above, wearing a different URL.
- **Leaving the dashboard row where it is until step 4 forces the question.** §48's own rule — *what must not happen
  at any point is a role with no app* — has a desktop counterpart, and shipping the deletion before this screen exists
  would give the PC a fire with nowhere to go for however long the gap lasted.
- **A widget of its own on the desktop dashboard.** Already rejected by §66 for reasons this section does not disturb:
  a tenth polling path and a card empty most of the day. The row stays where §66 put it, in *Needs you*, off the same
  `dashboard/ops` key; only its destination changes.

### The cost, named

**This is the one net-new screen in §48's retirement, and it is desktop code that has never existed.** §66 recorded
the same zero when it looked — grepping `public/retail-admin/` for `kitchen-ready` returns the dashboard row and
nothing else. Every other step of §48 moves or deletes; this one builds. That is accepted as the price of the ruling,
and it is the reason the desktop was left out of §48 in the first place rather than an oversight in it.

**NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** Both strings this screen needs are already live and are lifted verbatim: *Ready from the
kitchen · 厨房已完成* is the list's own name in `public/m.html` and `public/stock.html`, and *View · 查看* is live in
`public/m.html`. No entry in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is owed.

**SETTLED IN THE BUILD, 2026-09-08 (v4.172): it is a compact side drawer off the Needs-you row.** This was left open
above as a placement question inside the admin's own patterns, not Ash's to spend a decision on, and building it
answered it: the dashboard already opens two such drawers (`#db-activity-drawer`, `#db-stock-drawer`) from the same
card, so the same gesture keeps the same shape and the list reuses the global `.side-drawer` chrome rather than
inventing a third way to show a board's detail. **Its foot carries no primary, and the empty slot is the decision** —
the stock drawer beside it offers *Open restock*, and this one has nothing to offer because nothing on the list needs
doing (§1.7 forbids filling the slot with a secondary).

**Two things the build found, recorded because neither is visible from the ruling:**

1. **`/stock` has been drawing that time in the VIEWER's timezone, not the store's.** `krMade` there formats through a
   local `clock()` built on the browser's own hours, so the "made 15:07" on the screen this replaces is the reader's
   clock — the zoneless-UTC bug class `public/td-datetime.js` exists to close, and which `public/m.html` closed for
   itself. **The desktop renders that figure corrected rather than copied**, through `tdWhen`, comparing `'machine'`
   against `tdToday()` so "today" is the store's day too. The fault is left standing in `/stock`, which §48 step 4
   deletes; it is named here so the deletion is not read as having lost something.
2. **A bare clock for today, the date as well for anything older.** The first build asked for `'dateTime'` on every row
   and truncated to *"made Sep 8, 5:…"* at the drawer's own width — losing the one fact the row is read for, on a list
   where almost every line was made this morning.

Docs only; no code, no schema, no migration.

---

## §74 — A SOLD-OUT FRESH MEAL IS ORDERABLE FOR TODAY WHILE TODAY'S BATCH IS STILL COMING

**Reported by Ash, 2026-09-08, as the shape of the loss rather than as a bug in a screen:**

> *"fresh meals and wraps ready at 11am. lets say day before, wraps and meals are out of stock at 5pm. we put out of
> stock 5pm. next day customer at 8am in guangzhou goes to the app, want to order lunch but the app say out of stock.
> we open at 10 am. he want the meal for lunch. he has no way to order it at 8am. kitchen staff add the fresh meals at
> 11am and update the stock, too late, the customer already ordered from a different place."*

**THE CATALOGUE ANSWERS FROM THE SHELF, AND THE SHELF IS A STATEMENT ABOUT NOW.** Every availability decision for a
Guangzhou shopper resolves to `inventory.getAvailable` — physical, less the safety buffer, less active reservations —
and that figure is true and useless at 08:00 on a batch morning. It knows what is on the shelf; it does not know that
the kitchen is three hours from putting forty wraps on it. Between the evening the shelf empties and the moment a cook
records the batch, the app tells the truth and the customer hears something false: not *"we have none"* but
*"you cannot have one"*, when the meal he wants for lunch will exist before lunch.

**THIS IS NOT THE PRE-ORDER §-RULE, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE SECTION.** `localPreorderLine` refuses a sold-out
`backorder_gz` line to a shopper on the same-day local run, and its reasoning is sound and unchanged: their order is
served off the shelf that run loads from, so there is nothing behind the line. The fresh exemption already carved out
of it (`freshPreorderOk` / `local_fresh_date`) moved the DELIVERY DAY onto the next batch, which made the promise
keepable by moving the customer. **That is the right answer for every day except a batch day, and on a batch day it is
the expensive one** — it names tomorrow to a customer whose meal is being made this morning, and he buys lunch
somewhere else.

### The ruling

**On a day the kitchen is scheduled to cook, before the hour the batch reaches the shelf, zero stock stops being proof
that today is unreachable.** `earliestBatchMakeDate` returns TODAY with a new reason, `today_batch_pending`, and the
delivery calendar keeps today WHOLE.

**THE CALENDAR IS NOT TOUCHED — RULED BY ASH against the first build, which withdrew today's windows starting before
the ready hour and withdrew "right away" with them:** *"I don't think that necessary. people can pre order fresh meals
and request 10-12 slot as it is now."* **It was redundant twice over, and the second reason is the load-bearing one.**
A window is a WINDOW: 10:00–12:00 is honoured by a batch that lands at 11:00, so withdrawing it refused an order the
kitchen could serve — the same over-promise-avoidance that costs a day, applied where it costs an order instead.
**And the honesty it reached for is already enforced one layer down, and enforced better**: a sold-out same-day
Guangzhou cart meets `analyzeShortage`'s five-option modal, and its `wait_for_restock` branch CLEARS `scheduled_for`
outright, refunds the same-day surcharge and relabels the order *Ships when restocked* — so a parked order carries no
time promise whatever window was picked, `right_away` included. **The modal is the mechanism; a calendar rule beside it
is a second one that can only disagree with it.** The floor stays a plain date, and a floor of TODAY reads as no
constraint everywhere downstream — which is the intended effect rather than a loophole in it.

**THE HOUR IS CONFIGURATION AND ITS ABSENCE IS THE OFF SWITCH.** `batch.schedule` gains `ready_hour` (0–23,
optional). Unset, every function below behaves exactly as it does today, for every tenant, with no migration and no
backfill. A tenant opts in by naming the hour its kitchen finishes.

**ONLY THE STOCK REASON IS FORGIVEN.** `earliestBatchMakeDate` folds stock, an unresolvable store and the day's cutoff
into ONE roll-forward, and that is deliberate. This unpicks exactly one strand: a shortage on a batch morning. An
unresolvable store still rolls the day — we cannot prove today's batch reaches a shelf we cannot identify — and
`cutoff_hour` still rolls it, because a day whose ordering window has closed is genuinely gone. A `ready_hour` later
than `cutoff_hour` is operator error and the cutoff wins, which is the safe direction.

**THE BROWSE PILL AND THE CHECKOUT MUST NAME ONE DAY, and that is a standing requirement rather than a nicety.**
`nextFreshBatchDate` exists only because the browse surfaces have no cart, address or store to reason about, and its
header already commits it to the same arithmetic on the same config. It takes the same exemption here, or the grid
offers a meal for today and the calendar refuses it — the exact contradiction PR #400 has just finished removing from
the web product page.

### What the customer meets, and why no string is composed

**NOTHING NEW IS SAID TO HIM, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE.** §30 locks Chinese to live sources; no live pair says *"made
this morning, ready from 11"*. So this ships the CONTROL without the sentence: the calendar simply does not offer a
window the batch cannot reach, and the customer picks an afternoon slot the way he would on any other day.

**The machine behind it already exists and is already live.** A Guangzhou same-day order that is short reaches
`analyzeShortage`'s five-option modal, whose `wait_for_restock` branch parks the order as `awaiting_restock` holding no
stock, takes payment, and is promoted to `paid` by `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` the moment a cook records the
batch — reserving and deducting only when the FULL quantity is there. **So the back half of this problem was solved
before it was asked**, and every word the customer reads on that path is copy that already ships.

**Wanted, and blocked on Ash rather than invented:** a local-fresh notice for this case, the sibling of
`computeLocalFreshNotice`'s *下一批现做*, saying the batch is today rather than a future day. `computeLocalFreshNotice`
therefore still fires on `rolled_stock` ALONE and stays silent on `today_batch_pending`, which is the honest state
until the pair exists.

### What this does NOT do, named so it is not read as done

**IT DOES NOT CAP THE SELL AGAINST THE BATCH SIZE.** Nothing in the system knows forty wraps are coming:
`production_batches` records what WAS made, after the fact, and `kitchen_orders` is an ingredient requisition. So a
morning can take more orders than the batch will cover. **It does not oversell silently** — the excess parks in
`awaiting_restock` and `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` promotes an order only when its full quantity is free, so the
surplus waits for the next batch rather than being confirmed against stock that never arrives — **but it does mean a
customer can be told "today" and get tomorrow.** The cap needs a forward production plan (a row per date, product,
planned quantity and ready hour, entered the evening before), which is its own section and its own build. **Until it
exists, `ready_hour` should be set only where the batch reliably covers a morning's orders.**

### Rejected

**A nightly job that resets fresh stock to a planned figure at dawn.** Cheapest possible, needs no code path at all —
and it writes stock the kitchen has not made, so an under-run oversells against a number nobody entered, with no
`awaiting_restock` queue to catch it. It moves the lie from the calendar into the ledger.

**Letting `requiresStockGate` fall through on a batch morning.** It would open today by removing the stock gate
entirely, which also removes the shortage modal — the customer would be given an ordinary same-day order against an
empty shelf and no `wait_for_restock` park behind it. The gate is what makes this safe; the calendar is what needed to
change.

**A per-product ready hour.** One kitchen, one morning, one finish time; a column per product buys nothing today and
would have to be reconciled with the schedule's single cadence.

Code, tests and docs; no schema, no migration, no new route, no new strings, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §76 — THE KITCHEN STATION APP IS DELETED, AND IT WAS ALREADY UNREACHABLE BY THE PEOPLE IT WAS FOR

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-08): **`/kitchen` is retired.** `public/kitchen.html` is deleted, the route answers **302 to `/m`**, and no second app stands beside Tacet for kitchen work. This is §48's ruling — *there is no second app* — applied to the one standalone shell §48 did not name, and it follows that section's ordering: what the page did already exists in Tacet, so deleting it strands nothing.

**THE PAGE WAS UNREACHABLE BY THE COOKS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS SAFE RATHER THAN MERELY TIDY.** It self-authenticated against the `kitchen` PERMISSION, which lives on the `users` table — the old realm — and the people who actually cook are Tacet `tenant_users` holding capabilities. They have no login for it. This is not inferred here: `routes/retail-production.js` recorded it in its own header when it was built, as the reason that file exists — *"`production_batches` has been in the schema since the beginning and is empty. Not because anybody forgot… The log was unreachable by the only people with anything to put in it."* **A screen whose write table is empty since it shipped, because its own realm excludes its users, is not a screen being retired early.**

**ITS TWO JOBS BOTH HAVE HOMES IN TACET, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS STEP-2-COMPLETE RATHER THAN A DELETION AHEAD OF ONE.** Logging a batch is `/m`'s `logbatch` screen writing through `routes/retail-production.js`, the door built in the realm the cooks are actually in. The kitchen queue is `/m`'s `kitchenqueue` screen (§59, §61, §71), which by §71 carries a clock, names what arrived, and closes a line in one tap. Nothing in the deleted page is homeless.

**WHAT STAYS, AND WHY EACH:**

- **`routes/kitchen.js` (`/api/kitchen/*`) STAYS.** `public/app.html` calls it four times and is still the app served at the root of `food.*`, `app.*` and the bare domain. The API retires with that app, not with this page. **A deleted screen is not a deleted endpoint**, and conflating the two here would break the surface this change does not touch.
- **The manifest and the four icons STAY**, on §48 step 4's reasoning verbatim: the shortcut is installed on kitchen tablets NOW and resolves its manifest and icon on launch, so deleting them buys nothing the redirect has not already bought. They go in their own small change once the redirect has been live long enough that nobody opens the shortcut.
- **`/kitchen` itself STAYS, as a door rather than an app.** It is the `start_url` of that installed manifest. Deleting the route turns every installed tablet into a 404 mid-shift.

**302, NEVER 301.** A permanent redirect is cached by the browser and by the installed service worker essentially forever, so if `/kitchen` ever has to mean something again a 301 would be unrecallable from every tablet that followed it. Identical to `/stock`'s door and for identical reasons.

**THE COST IS NAMED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the installed shortcut stops opening full-screen.** The manifest's `scope` is `/kitchen`, so a tablet launching the shortcut now follows the redirect and lands on `/m` — outside its own scope — which browsers open in a normal tab instead of standalone. **This is a downgrade in feel, not a break**, it is exactly what the retired `/stock` shortcut does today, and it is preferred to editing the manifest of an app being retired. It resolves when the manifest goes.

**THE LOGIN PAGE'S KITCHEN ROUTING IS DELETED, NOT REPOINTED, AND THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS THE WRONG ONE.** `public/login.html` sent a `kitchen`-permission holder to `/kitchen` in two places. Repointing them at the redirect's destination would forward a `users`-realm session into Tacet Mobile, which authenticates on `backendUserId` (`tenant_users`) — **an app their login cannot open, bouncing them straight back to `/backend/login`.** A dead end is worse than the dashboard, so both branches are removed and a kitchen-only holder falls through to `/` like everybody else. Ash's standing fact makes this a formality rather than a migration: **all staff are already on Tacet.**

**A CONSEQUENCE, COLLAPSED RATHER THAN LEFT STANDING: `_smartRedirect` now has one answer.** With `/restock` gone (2026-08-04) and `/kitchen` gone here, every surviving branch in that function returned `'/'` — it was deciding between one destination and the same destination. It is reduced to `return '/'`, and `_lastAppRedirect`'s `isAdmin` and `permissions` reads went with the branches that used them. **Branching that can only reach one answer reads as routing and is not**, and the next reader would reasonably conclude kitchen staff still land somewhere of their own. Same treatment, same reasoning, as §48 step 4 giving up `test_app_home`'s byte-comparison of two copies of `homeFromDoor` once one page was left.

**WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* DECIDE.** The legacy kitchen app (`public/app.html`) is untouched and is not retired by this section. Its remaining Tacet gaps are, as surveyed on this date: kitchen purchase orders (`/api/purchases`, with lot and expiry tracking on `/api/lots`), the Sprout AI chat (`/api/ai/chat`), the alerts feed, gzgrocery analytics, and two lookup lists. **Ash has ruled that market-stall sales are not needed and that the counter till is already correct** — `public/till.html` is a Tacet-realm surface writing `retail_orders`, so till takings already count as revenue, and the `sales_entries` gap §55 flags applies to the market POS and the old app's manual sales page only. **Packaging is NOT a gap**: §31 moved it onto the product's build list and `public/retail-admin/21-product-build.js` carries it; `docs/packaging-findings.md` describes the state *before* that fix and must not be read as current.

**`scripts/diagnose_deployed_tree.js` still lists the deleted file and is deliberately NOT hand-edited** — it is a generated snapshot declaring the commit it came from, and editing it by hand would make it lie. §48 step 4 left it alone for the same reason.

**THE DEPLOY INSTALLER ONLY ADDS FILES; DELETIONS NEVER REACH THE BOX.** `public/kitchen.html` therefore stays on the server until removed by hand, and stays fetchable at `/assets/kitchen.html` until it is — the same standing condition already recorded for `public/app.html.bak`. The page self-authenticates, so a stale copy grants nothing; it is named here so the deletion is not read as having removed it from production.

## §77 — KITCHEN PURCHASING HAS ALREADY MOVED TO TACET, AND LOT / EXPIRY TRACKING IS DROPPED RATHER THAN PORTED

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-08), in two parts, the first a finding and the second a decision.

**PART ONE — THE MIGRATION IS DONE, AND WAS DONE BEFORE THIS SECTION WAS WRITTEN.** §48's ordering is migrate-then-delete, and for purchasing the migrating already happened in ordinary use rather than as a project. **`RPO-0031` is a live retail PO carrying eleven material lines, Ordered, ¥2,750, raised against Tianhe.** Nothing needed building: `routes/retail-purchasing.js` shares the kitchen procurement engine outright — the same `suppliers`, `purchase_orders`, `po_line_items` and `expense_entries` tables — and §28 addendum point 4's Phase 1b gave a retail PO line an `ingredient_id` subject. **Tacet's purchasing is the richer of the two**, holding supplier documents, 发票 matching and rematch, landed-cost allocation, returns, reorder and undo-receive, none of which the kitchen screen has. See the correction appended under §28 addendum point 4 for how its stale "no live retail PO has carried a material line yet" misled a survey.

**PART TWO — LOT NUMBERS AND EXPIRY DATES ARE DROPPED. Decided by Ash, asked directly: "we don't use it."** The kitchen app records `po_line_items.lot_number` and `expiry_date` on receipt and reads them back through `/api/lots/search`, `/api/lots/expiring` and `/api/lots/all`, with an expiring-soon board and expiry notifications. **Tacet has never had any of it** — not a route, not a screen, not a field, on desktop or phone. That asymmetry was the one genuine gap between the two purchasing surfaces, and it is closed by removing the requirement rather than by building the feature.

**THIS IS RECORDED AS A DELETION OF SCOPE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT, and that distinction is the entire reason this part exists.** A later reader comparing the two modules will find recall traceability in the old one and nothing in the new one, and the obvious inference — that it was missed in the port — is wrong and would send somebody building it. **It was found, costed, put to Ash, and declined.** The columns keep their rows and their data; nothing is migrated, nothing is backfilled, and no Tacet screen learns to read them.

**WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE: whether the lot columns and `/api/lots/*` are deleted.** They live in `routes/purchases.js` and `public/app.html`, which this section does not touch — they retire with that app, on its own change. Deleting them now would widen a purchasing ruling into the legacy app's retirement, and the two are separate pieces of work.

**`routes/purchases.js` CANNOT BE DELETED WITH THE KITCHEN APP'S SCREENS, and this is the trap worth naming before somebody meets it.** `routes/retail-purchasing.js` **requires six functions out of it** — `firePriceAlertsForPO`, `allocateLandedExtras`, `planReceiptReasons`, `recordReceipt`, `appliedReceiptStore` and `postPOExpenses` — deliberately, so there is one price write-back and one expense poster rather than two that drift. **Tacet's purchasing depends on the kitchen module at require time.** Retiring `public/app.html` therefore does not retire this file; extracting the shared six into `lib/` is the work that would, and it is not started here.

**WHAT THIS SECTION SHIPS is the coverage the migration never had.** `scripts/test_retail_po_material_line.js` drives a material line through the real router — create, place, receive — and asserts the contract `routes/retail-purchasing.js`'s own header states: the line carries `ingredient_id` and no `store_product_id`; a line carrying both is refused `line_conflict` **before the transaction opens**, writing nothing; placing the order posts the expense and writes the price back through the real `firePriceAlertsForPO` (¥26 the bag over 500g becomes ¥0.052 the gram, with a `ingredient_price_history` row); **receiving a material line records the arrival and never calls `inventory.adjustStock`**; and a product line on the SAME PO does move stock, so the skip is proved per LINE rather than per PO. `routes/purchases.js` is deliberately NOT stubbed — stubbing the price write-back would leave the suite asserting that the router calls something rather than that a price landed. `lib/inventory.js` IS stubbed but **recording**, because "never touches stock" is a claim about a call that must not happen and an absence is only provable against a record of what did.

**THE SUITE WAS MUTATION-PROVED RATHER THAN TRUSTED FOR PASSING.** It passed on first run, which is a reason for suspicion rather than confidence, so the guard it exists to protect was deliberately broken. **The first mutation changed nothing** — removing `if (l.ingredient_id) continue;` left the material line still skipped by the `!l.store_product_id` test on the very next line, which is **defence in depth worth knowing about**: two independent guards, either sufficient. Only with **both** removed did the suite fail, and it then failed on exactly the three assertions that describe the rule — `adjustStock` called once, `stock_applied_qty` at 2, and the material line applying its arrival. **A suite that cannot fail is not evidence, and this one was made to fail before it was believed.**

## §78 — THE KITCHEN APP IS DELETED, AND SPROUT WITH IT

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-08), given as a question that was really an instruction: *"why keeping anything in the kitchen app? we are not using it."* **`public/app.html` is deleted**, with thirteen route modules, its stale backup, and the Sprout agent. What remains of the kitchen realm remains because **Tacet calls it**, never because it belonged to that app.

**THE QUESTION WAS THE RIGHT ONE AND THE EARLIER ANSWER WAS SLOPPY.** A survey had reported five things as "kept", which read as keeping the app. The honest statement is the one this section is built on: **nothing is kept because it is the kitchen app.** Five files sit in kitchen-named paths and have live Tacet callers — `purchases.js` (six functions `routes/retail-purchasing.js` requires at load, per §77), `restock.js` (Tacet Mobile's kitchen queue and the desktop dashboard), `push.js` (the service worker), `ai.js` (the product editor's composer), `auth.js` (the login page and the CMS). Those are shared plumbing in a badly-named folder, and renaming them is separate work.

**WHAT WENT.** `public/app.html` (28,639 lines) and `public/app.html.bak` (24,704 — a stale copy that the deploy's `/assets` handler served to anyone who guessed the name, recorded as a finding in `docs/tacet-audit-2026-09.md` and closed here as a side effect rather than as its own change). Thirteen route modules whose only client was that page: `ingredients`, `recipes`, `admin`, `finance`, `alerts`, `waste`, `kitchen`, `sales`, `lookups`, `production`, `pos`, `markets`, `feedback`. **`routes/kitchen.js` had already lost its other client** when §76 deleted `public/kitchen.html`, so this is the second half of that retirement rather than a new one.

**WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS DELETED, because "we are not using it" is true of the app and not automatically true of every file under it.** Every kitchen API namespace was mapped against every non-`app.html` client in `public/` and `miniapp/`, and every module was checked for a `require` from a surviving file. **Two survived that check and would have been deleted without it**: `routes/events.js`, required by `purchases`, `restock`, `auth` and `feedback` — deleting it takes out Tacet Mobile's kitchen queue — and `routes/products.js`, which `public/retail-admin/20-waste.js` calls live. Neither has a screen in the old app any more; both stay.

**SPROUT IS SCRAPPED, INCLUDING THE HALF ASH DID NOT KNOW ABOUT.** `routes/ai.js` goes from 3,459 lines to ~730: the chat endpoint, the ~25-tool agent loop, the memory and app-help stores, `/api/ai/status` and `/api/ai/sales-analyze` are all gone. **The CMS had its own Sprout button** — an "Ask Sprout" design check in the mini-app editor, calling the same `/api/ai/chat` — which was surfaced and put to Ash rather than deleted quietly; he killed it too. **ONE ROUTE SURVIVES AND IT IS WHY THE FILE DOES**: `/api/retail-admin/ai/compose-blocks`, the product-block composer the store product editor and retail-admin's products screen both call. Its kitchen-realm twin `/api/ai/compose-blocks` is deleted — the live editors have always called the backend-realm mount, so nothing that still exists lost a door. **The provider abstraction is therefore not Sprout's leftovers**: `callLLM()` has a real caller.

**`/` IS A DOOR NOW, AND THAT IS THE THIRD INSTALLED PWA THIS RETIREMENT HAS HAD TO RESPECT.** It answers **302 to `https://store.rootskitchenchina.com/`**, where the staff work. It is the `start_url` AND the `scope` of `public/manifest.webmanifest`, installed on staff devices as "Roots Kitchen Management" — so, exactly as with `/stock` (§48 step 4) and `/kitchen` (§76): **302, never 301**, because a permanent redirect is cached by the browser and the installed service worker essentially forever. **The manifest and icons stay** until the redirect has been live long enough that nobody opens the shortcut. **`requireAuth` went with the page it gated**: a redirect to another host discloses nothing and the destination runs its own gate, while leaving the gate would bounce a signed-out visitor to `/login`, which now leads only to the CMS.

**THE LOGIN PAGE NOW LANDS ON `/cms`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON IT STILL EXISTS.** `_smartRedirect` returned `'/'` after §76 collapsed it; `'/'` is now a redirect off this realm entirely, and Tacet authenticates on `backendUserId` while every session reaching that function holds `userId`. Sending them there would forward them into an app their login cannot open. **`/cms` is the one surface left that reads the `users` realm.** A remembered `last_app` of `'/'` is deliberately NOT honoured — every browser that ever opened the SPA wrote it.

**THE `users` REALM OUTLIVES THE APP, AND THE CMS IS WHY.** `public/cms.html` self-authenticates against `/api/auth/me`. Until the CMS moves onto Tacet's login, that realm, its accounts and `/login` all stay. **`routes/admin.js` is deleted anyway, and the consequence is named rather than absorbed**: it was that realm's user management — create, delete, permissions, password reset — and `public/app.html` was its only UI. **Managing a CMS account is now a one-off script**, the path this repository already uses for database repair (`.github/workflows/oneoff.yml`). Flagged to Ash before the deletion, not after.

**WHAT THIS COSTS IN TESTS, recorded rather than absorbed.** Eleven suites broke. **Three were deleted with the code they tested**: `test_ingredient_form_cost` and `test_product_ctx_no_cost` extracted and ran functions out of `app.html` itself, and `test_finance_category_normalization` mounted the deleted `routes/finance.js`. **Eight were repaired, and none by lowering a bar to green.** `test_price_writeback`'s alerts-feed section was **re-aimed at the rows rather than deleted** — it read `/api/alerts/feed`'s costSkips projection, and now asserts `ingredient_cost_skips` directly, one layer closer to the `firePriceAlertsForPO` that writes them; what is genuinely gone is the round trip, since there is no longer an HTTP reader. `test_compose_prompt`'s Sprout section was **inverted rather than removed**: it guarded against a Roots-facts-carrying assistant gaining a merchant-realm mount, and that risk outlives the code, so it now asserts the absence — and the `SPROUT_SYSTEM` check matches a **declaration**, not any mention, because this file's own historical notes would otherwise trip it. `test_po_supersede` lost its second reader and says so: a cross-check that two independent readers agreed cannot exist while there is one of them. `test_recipe_yield_auto`'s "both doors" checks became one-door checks, each marked where it narrowed, and its statement floor dropped from 8 to the 5 one door actually prepares — **to the real count, not to a number that would pass on an empty match.** `test_restock_tenant2_split` lost Case E; re-pointing it at `routes/retail-production.js` was considered and refused as a rewrite wearing a repoint's name, and that door carries its own suites. `test_invoice_no_invoice_mark` lost two screen assertions and kept its server half. `test_po_cost_unit_guard` lost Part 3 — four cases pinning Sprout's `compute_margin` to the shared derivation, which guarded a CALLER and not the rule.

**ONE ORPHANED `package.json` ALIAS was caught by the runner PR #401 added for exactly this**, and removed. That guard is four days old and has now paid for itself twice.

**WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE, so it is not mistaken for finished.** The five shared files keep their kitchen-named paths; moving them to `lib/` is its own change. The CMS still logs in through the old realm. `routes/purchases.js` still cannot be deleted (§77). And `public/app.html` **stays on the production box until removed by hand** — the deploy installer only adds files — so it remains fetchable at `/assets/app.html` until someone deletes it there. That is the same standing condition §76 recorded for `kitchen.html`, and it now covers the larger file and its backup.

## §79 — DELIVERY IS A SETTINGS PANEL, NOT A RAIL DESTINATION

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-09): *"move the delivery section inside setting"*. The
`Delivery · 配送` row leaves the left rail and becomes the eighth panel of
Settings, between Customer service and Operations.

**WHY IT WAS ALWAYS A SETTINGS SCREEN.** Nine cards live on that page — zones,
fees and free-shipping bar, store pickup, holiday mode, same-day cutoff, fresh
batches, Kuaidi100 tracking, JD Logistics, Qingyun riders — and **every one of
them is a rule the shop configures once and then forgets.** Nothing on the page
is a thing an operator DOES during a shift: the orders being delivered are on
Orders, the riders in flight are on the Dashboard, and the zone editor is a
form. A rail row is a place you go to work; this was a place you went to change
your mind. It sat at `order:6`, above Sales, and cost a top-level slot for a
screen most tenants open twice a year.

**WHAT WAS ASKED AND WHAT WAS OFFERED.** Two readings of the instruction were
put to Ash rather than guessed between, because they are different jobs: a
Delivery LINK in the Settings sidebar that opens the page as it stands (the
pattern Brand and Billing already use, ~20 lines), or Delivery as a real
Settings PANEL. **He chose the panel**, and it is the better answer for the
reason the link version is cheap: a link leaves the Settings screen the moment
it is clicked, so the sidebar that just said "you are in Settings" disappears.
The panel keeps it beside the cards.

**IT IS A MOVE, NOT A REWRITE.** The ~1,090 lines of markup are relocated
verbatim from `<section id="tab-delivery">` into `.settings-body` as
`<div class="sub-panel" id="sub-delivery">`, re-indented and otherwise
untouched: same input ids, same save functions, same `dlvGo()` hub/sub-view
switching, same wizard. **A `<div>` and not a `<section>`, and that is
load-bearing** — `goTab()` clears `active` off every `main section` on each tab
switch, so a `<section>` here would have the panel switched dark by any rail
click.

**THE CAPABILITY GATE MOVED WITH THE PAGE, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT COULD HAVE
SHIPPED UNGATED.** `TAB_CAP.delivery = 'delivery:view'` is deleted with the
row it keyed off, and the same capability is now `data-cap="delivery:view"` on
the Settings nav button, where `applyCapGates`'s generic hook enforces it.
**`delivery:view` is also added to `TAB_CAP.config`'s any-of list**, without
which a role holding delivery and nothing else in Settings would have watched
its one screen disappear behind a Settings door it is not allowed to open.

**THREE CALLERS WENT THROUGH `goTab('delivery')` AND WOULD HAVE BROKEN
SILENTLY** — the setup guide's "set up delivery" step, the integrations
screen's "Review zones" button, and `salesGo('delivery')` from the shipping
card. All three now call `dlvOpen()`, which does the same
`goTab('config')` + nav-button click the setup guide already used to reach
Settings → Operations.

**THE SEARCHES BOTH GAIN AND ONE OF THEM NEEDED A FIX.** The command palette
indexed Delivery through its rail button; it now picks the panel up through the
`#settings-nav button[data-sub]` walk instead, and `indexCards('#sub-delivery')`
still finds every `.group-card-head h3` on it, so the deep "jump to this card"
entries survive. Settings' own card search (§G-03) now covers delivery cards
for the first time. **But most of those cards sit inside a hidden `.dlv-view`**,
so both searches would have scrolled to an invisible element — `_dlvReveal()`
switches to the card's own sub-view first, and both callers use it.

**WHAT IS NOT DONE HERE.** The delivery side-drawers (`#dz-edit-bg` and the
carrier drawers) stay where they are as siblings in `<main>` — they are
fixed-position overlays and belong to no panel. The phone (`public/m.html`)
keeps its own `delivery` row; it was never the desktop rail and is not touched.
Delivery cards are NOT given `data-sees="customer"` marks in this change even
though several qualify — that list is a judgement per §G-03 and belongs in its
own pass.

**HOW IT WAS PROVED, because a thousand-line DOM move that still passes a string
match has proved very little.** The shipped page was driven in Chromium over a
local static server with `/api/backend/me` stubbed, and the panel exercised the
way an operator reaches it: `dlvOpen()` lights Settings and the panel, the
sidebar stays up beside it, the hub shows and the zones view does not, the
shared Save bar is off, `#dz-kpis` is hidden on the hub and shown on zones —
which is the CSS rename proving itself rather than being asserted — and
`_dlvReveal()` opens the fees view for a card on it while leaving a `#sub-shop`
card alone. `scripts/test_delivery_in_settings.js` is the committed guard: 33
assertions across the four files, in the fast shard, needing no browser.
**It was mutation-proved rather than trusted for passing.** Five deliberate
breaks — the panel back to a `<section>`, the nav button's `data-cap` removed,
`delivery:view` dropped from `TAB_CAP.config`, one CSS rule left on
`#tab-delivery`, the palette's reveal deleted — each turned exactly the
assertions that state that rule red. **Two assertions passed for the wrong
reason and were tightened before any of that**: one was a tautology, and one an
alternation that would have matched any `dlvGo('hub')` anywhere in the file.
`npm run test:fast`: 181 passed, 0 failed. eslint: 0 errors.

## §80 — NOTHING IS SHORT FROM THE CUSTOMER'S SIDE WHILE THE BATCH IS ON ITS WAY

**§74 made the meal orderable and stopped one step short.** Walked through its own Guangzhou scenario, Ash stopped at
the checkout step:

> *"why tell him its short? he doesnt need to wait. there is a new batch made and ready at 11, we deliver on time
> according to his request. am i wrong?"*

**He was not, and what shipped was worse than the walkthrough describing it.** §74 opened the catalogue and left the
checkout untouched: `requiresStockGate` still read Guangzhou + same-day + an empty shelf, `analyzeShortage` still
returned `options_5`, and the customer still met a five-option out-of-stock modal. Worse, the only way through it —
`wait_for_restock` — **clears `scheduled_for`, refunds the same-day surcharge and relabels the order *Ships when
restocked***. He asked for 12:00–14:00 and got an order with no delivery time.

That clearing is not a bug. Its comment says why: the kitchen must not see *"Today 18:00–20:00"* on an order whose
restock might land at 19:00. **It is right whenever nobody knows when stock lands, and wrong here, because the
schedule names the hour.**

### The ruling

**While today's batch is still coming, and it lands before the customer's own window CLOSES, that line is not short.**
No modal, no interruption, and the window he picked survives onto the order.

**THE END OF THE WINDOW, NEVER ITS START.** Ash settled it in one line when the design was put back to him: *"it can
also be 10-12."* A batch landing at 11:00 serves a delivery window closing at 12:00, so keying on the start hour would
have refused exactly the slot he named. Keying on the end is also what keeps the rule honest in the other direction: a
window that closes BEFORE the batch lands is correctly not covered, which is what a late `ready_hour` needs.
`'right_away'` is never covered — it names no window to close by, and promising "soonest possible" against a batch
that does not exist is the over-promise the whole area exists to avoid.

### Where the rule lives is itself a decision

`lib/inventory.js` knows shelves. **It is not taught a production cadence.** `routes/retail.js` resolves which lines
today's batch covers, beside the schedule that defines them, and hands the ids down as `coveredProductIds`; a covered
line then counts as OK and the gate never opens. A case asserts `inventory.js` never learns the words, so the next
person to need this cannot answer it in the wrong file.

### The order parks, and keeps its window

The automatic parking path that already existed for stock-gate-OFF orders **gains one arm rather than a twin.** Every
other guard is unchanged and still applies to both — no bundle, no stock-backed add-on, backorder lines only — and
with the gate ON, *every* short line must be covered or the order does not park silently: one uncovered line means the
order genuinely is short, `analyzeShortage` said so, and the customer met the modal.

`isBatchPark` shares `isWaitFlow`'s reservation skip, because there is nothing on the shelf to hold, and deliberately
does not share its slot-clearing. `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` promotes the order the moment a cook records the
batch, reserving and deducting only when the full quantity is there — unchanged, and the reason the back half of this
needed no new machinery at all.

### Three copies became one

`todaysBatchStillComing()` holds the four conditions — an hour is configured, it has not arrived, the cutoff has not
passed, today is on the cadence — that were written out separately in `earliestBatchMakeDate`, in `nextFreshBatchDate`
and again in this gate. For a rule whose whole job is that the pill, the checkout and the order name one day, three
copies was two too many.

### What is still not done

**Nothing caps the sell against the batch size.** A busy morning can promise more windows than the batch covers. The
surplus parks rather than overselling silently, but a customer can be told a time and get the next batch instead.
**Ash chose this shape knowing that** — offered the capped alternative, he answered *"i choose option a."* The cap
needs the forward production plan (a row per date, product, planned quantity and ready hour) and is its own section.

### Rejected

**Leaving the modal and only preserving the window.** Half the complaint. He is still told his lunch is out of stock
when it is being made, and still has to answer a question that should not have been asked.

**Widening `requiresStockGate` itself.** It is read in several places and means "this order needs a stock decision
today", which is still true here — the decision is just satisfied. Loosening it would have turned the shortage
machinery off for this order rather than answering it, taking the `awaiting_restock` park with it.

## §81 — THE KITCHEN REALM IS RETIRED: THE CMS MOVES TO TACET AND THE `users` LOGIN IS DELETED

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-08): finish it. §78 deleted the kitchen app; this deletes the **realm** it authenticated against — `session.userId`, the `users` table and its `permissions` row — and moves the one surface still using it.

**THE CMS WAS THE LAST REASON THE REALM EXISTED, AND IT NEVER NEEDED IT.** `public/cms.html` and `public/cms-mobile.html` read `/api/auth/me` to decide who was signed in. **Every other call either page makes was already `/api/retail-admin/*`** — the Tacet realm — and `requireRetailAdmin` has always accepted a tenant operator. So the editor's work had migrated long ago and only its sign-in check had not. Both now read `/api/backend/me`, and a signed-out editor goes to `/backend/login` rather than a page that no longer exists.

**THE PERMISSION GATE MOVES FROM A FLAG TO A CAPABILITY, AND FAILS OPEN ON PURPOSE.** It tested `role !== 'admin' && !permissions.retail` — columns on the deleted realm's table. It now tests `content:edit`, this editor's own capability. **`caps` is null when the server could not resolve them** (`routes/backend-auth.js` fails open on that read), and a null must not lock an operator out of the tool they use all day: this is a VIEW gate, and `requireRetailAdmin` on every write below it is the security boundary.

**A DEFECT SHIPPED IN §78 IS FIXED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT.** §78 deleted Sprout's backend on Ash's instruction — including, explicitly, the CMS's "Ask Sprout" design check — **but removed only the endpoint, leaving the button, its panel, its Apply cards and ~150 lines of CSS live in the page, calling a 404.** That was live in production between the two changes. All of it is gone now. **The deterministic design check is untouched**: `dcRunChecks()` and its findings never needed a model, and what went is only the half that asked one.

**`requireRetailAdmin` IS NARROWED TO ONE REALM, and this is the single most load-bearing edit here.** It fronts every `/api/retail-admin` endpoint and had a second branch: fall through to `requireAuth` plus the `retail` permission, then hand that session **the full capability set** on Roots' tenant. With no way to create such a session, that branch could only refuse — but a second way into every admin endpoint is exactly what outlives the app it was built for. **It answers 401 for every refusal, including a suspended tenant or a deactivated operator**, because those reached the kitchen path before and were answered 401 by `requireAuth`; `test_point_search` asserts it, and splitting it into a 403 would have been a behaviour change smuggled in as a cleanup — which is what the first attempt did, and what that suite caught.

**THE PLATFORM CONSOLE WOULD HAVE BEEN LOCKED OUT, AND WAS FOUND BEFORE IT WAS.** `/saas-admin` was gated on a **kitchen `admin`** session, and `lib/platform-admin.js`'s `currentActor` accepted the same thing as a platform `super`. Retiring the realm silently would have taken the tenant-provisioning console with it. **It is re-gated onto `platform_admins`** — the realm built for it, seeded at boot, already serving `store-admin` at `system.rootskitchenchina.com` — and the kitchen branch in `currentActor` is deleted, closing a back door from a kitchen login to every tenant's billing and credentials. Historic `activity_log` rows still record `actor_kind: 'kitchen'` and are **not rewritten**: they are what happened.

**WHAT WENT, in full.** `public/login.html` and `routes/auth.js`; the `/login` route; `routes/products.js` (**dead, and §78 kept it by mistake** — the grep that "found" a caller matched `public/retail-admin/20-waste.js`'s comment saying *"Never call /api/products here"*, which is the opposite of a call); `routes/purchases.js`'s 22 endpoints under `/api/purchases` and `/api/lots`, leaving a library; `routes/push.js`'s six kitchen endpoints; `routes/events.js`'s SSE stream and its who-is-listening diagnostic; `routes/restock.js`'s kitchen branch and its drafts-only delete; `routes/retail-inventory.js`'s kitchen read branch and its store-assignment endpoint; and the four gates in `middleware/auth.js` — `requireAuth`, `requireAdmin`, `requirePermission`, `requireDelete`.

**`logActivity` STAYS AND IS WHY THAT MODULE DOES.** It is realm-agnostic, 139 call sites across both surfaces write the shared `activity_log` through it, and its FK note is now history rather than a live branch: with no `users` rows being created, every id it is handed is a tenant operator's — exactly the case that comment already said to store as NULL.

**THE SERVICE WORKER TOLD BOTH REALMS AND NOW TELLS ONE.** Its mute button posted to `/api/push/pref` and `/api/backend/push/pref` together, because one browser could carry either login. The first would now 404, **and a 404 inside `Promise.all` is a silent no-op that looks like it worked** — the worst shape for an off switch. Its suite's assertion is narrowed and now also holds the absence.

**FOUR SUITES BROKE AND ALL FOUR WERE REPAIRED, none by lowering a bar.** `test_point_search` caught the 401/403 slip described above — a real defect, not a stale expectation. `test_push_mute_action`'s "tells BOTH realms" became "tells the one realm that is left, **and only it**", asserted against the raw fetch record because `bodyOf()` asserts a call EXISTS, which is the opposite of what was wanted. `test_tenant_branding` **inverted** its `/api/push/test` case rather than dropping it: the audit's concern is that a push endpoint here might carry Roots' name to another tenant's customers, and an absence is the strongest form of that guarantee. `test_invoice_no_invoice_mark` lost the three sections that drove the kitchen API and kept every rule — the two columns, the writers that must move together, the boot reconciliation — on the Tacet endpoints that still exist.

**STILL OWED, named rather than absorbed.** `routes/push.js` keeps `sendPushToUser`, `sendPushToUsers`, `sendPushToAll` and `sendPushByPermission`, which target the `users` table and can now reach nobody. They are **not** removed here because their call sites need reading first, and widening this change into those callers is how a retirement becomes a refactor nobody can review.
