   sites. The pin moved from eleven to twelve; the RULE it guards (no call site
   passes a handle) still runs over every site including the new one.

### What is left open

Nothing in §98 blocks a complete case any more. Still not decided, and unchanged
by this: **which parcels raise a case** (air only, delivered only, more than a
day late — a late land parcel or same-city rider still raises nothing, and each
mode needs its own threshold), and **whether evidence lives in Tacet**.

### §98 addendum 5 — the last two open items, and §98 closes (2026-09-11)

**Which parcels raise a case, and evidence in Tacet.** Both were recorded as
open from the first section; both are now built, and nothing in §98 is
outstanding.

#### Air-only was a hole, not a conservative default

The alert matched `mode = 'air'`. `planShipments` sends **every Guangdong order
by land** — its own comment: *"the province ships by ground regardless of any
item's air flag, so a single land shipment carries everything (an 'Air only'
product still goes by land within Guangdong)"*. So the destination closest to
the kitchen, carrying ice-pack goods, was the one whose late parcels raised
nothing at all. That is the gap this closes, and it was larger than the feature
that had been built on top of it.

**The thresholds are per mode and live in one place** — `LATE_AFTER_DAYS` in
`lib/delay-case.js`. Air stays **1**, unchanged, because widening must not
restate a case that already exists. Local is **1**: a same-city rider against a
same-day promise, a day past which is a failure rather than a slow day. Land is
**3**: ground freight is legitimately slower, and at 1 it would fire on ordinary
two-day deliveries until the badge became noise, which is how an alert stops
being read. A mode absent from the map never raises one, so a supplier-direct
parcel — not ours to claim against — is excluded without being named.

**FIXED IN THIS PHASE AND NOT TENANT-EDITABLE**, exactly as §32 fixed the waste
reason codes. A number somebody can change is a settings screen, a migration and
a per-tenant default, and none of it is worth building before anyone has run the
alert for a month and said it is wrong.

**The rule was written out four times in `routes/retail.js` and twice more on
the two clients** — the same drift the paid predicate had, found the same way,
and consolidated the same way. The clients no longer do date arithmetic at all:
the server computes `late_days` per parcel and both screens render it.

**The `air_` names on the wire and in the database are historical and stay.**
`air_delivery_delayed` is read by both clients and `air_delay_cleared_at` has
production rows behind it; renaming them is a migration and two client releases
in exchange for nothing an operator can see. The function was renamed
(`orderHasDelayedAirShipment` → `orderHasDelayedParcel`) because that one is
free, and the header now says what the `air_` prefix means.

#### Evidence is attached, and it never gates the close

A child table rather than a column, because a claim is several photographs where
`staff_expenses.receipt_data` is one receipt. **The bytes never travel with a
list**: `forScreen` returns each file's id, label and size, and the picture has
its own route — `staff_expenses`'s own rule, in its own words, *"bytes travel
when somebody asks to look at them, not when a list is drawn"*.

Only a `data:image/...;base64,` URI is accepted; the two screens render these
into an `<img src>`, so a column that took any string would be an injection with
a UI attached. A file is reachable only through its own case, so an id on its
own opens nothing. The phone downscales to 1280px and JPEG 0.7 before uploading,
as the staff-claim photo already does, because a phone camera outruns the 4mb
body limit on its own.

**Evidence does not gate closing a case, deliberately.** Plenty of claims are
settled on a phone call, and a checklist that refuses to finish without a
photograph teaches people to attach a blank one.

#### §98 is complete

Four stages, five addenda. Nothing in the section is now open.

### §98 addendum 6 — the cutover, and three things widening the alert broke (2026-09-11)

Reported by Ash off the live phone within the hour: **"Delivery needs a call · 7,
oldest 79d"**, and tapping it opened a screen showing unrelated orders from today
and yesterday. Four faults, three of them introduced by addendum 5.

#### 1. Widening a live alert is retroactive unless you stop it

The rule changed from `mode='air'` to every mode. The query behind the card does
not care when the rule changed — it asked the same question of every parcel ever
shipped and correctly answered that a pile of them were late, the oldest
seventy-nine days. **Nobody is going to ring a customer about food from
seventy-nine days ago**, so every one of those rows was work that would never be
done, on the one card whose whole job is to list work that will be.

**Decided by Ash: "no need to raise a case for previous orders, only from
today."** `CASES_FROM` in `lib/delay-case.js` is a fixed date, not a rolling
window — a window would re-raise history every time somebody changed its length,
where a cutover says plainly that the feature began on a day, which is what
happened. **A parcel that already has a case row stays in scope however old it
is**, or a dispute already being chased would vanish mid-chase. `lateDays()`
mirrors the cutover, so no screen can draw a checklist the query has filtered
out.

#### 2. The age query kept its air-only test

`waiting_since` is a sibling subquery of the EXISTS, and addendum 5 replaced the
EXISTS and not it. A late land or same-city parcel therefore came back with **no
age at all**: the card skips an item with no `waiting_since` when it computes
"oldest", and `ORDER BY` sorts NULLs first — so the new modes went to the top of
the preview showing nothing, while the age beside the card described some older
air parcel instead of them. It now uses the same predicate as the EXISTS.

#### 3. The card had nowhere to send anybody

Tapping "Delivery needs a call" ran `ordersGo('dispatched')` — the **Dispatched**
tab, which by definition cannot contain these orders, because the alert is about
a parcel that has already been **delivered**, late. The card counted one set of
orders and opened a screen showing a different one.

This one is older than addendum 5 and was merely exposed by it: the card used to
be mostly in-transit tracking alerts, so "dispatched" roughly matched. Once
delivered parcels started alerting it was simply wrong. There is now a `delayed`
pseudo-status on the orders list — the same shape as `refunds_open` and
`needs_invoice` — **built on the very predicate the card counts**, so the number
and the list are one fact rather than two queries that have to agree.

#### 4. The list badge still said AIR

Both surfaces labelled a late land or same-city parcel `AIR DELAYED · 空运延误`.
Addendum 5 made the drawer's heading mode-neutral and missed the list row. Both
now read `DELIVERY DELAYED · 配送延误`, the pair already locked in v1.58, and the
phone's icon is a truck rather than a plane.

#### What this cost, and what it is worth writing down

Three of the four were mine, all in one change, and all of the same kind: **a
predicate was consolidated and its neighbours were not.** The EXISTS moved and
`waiting_since` stayed; the drawer heading moved and the list badge stayed; the
rule widened and the thing it navigates to stayed. `scripts/test_paid_predicate.js`
guards exactly this for the money predicate — a test that fails when a copy comes
back. There is no equivalent for the alert's *neighbours*, and there could not
easily be: they are not copies of the predicate, they are things that have to
agree with it. The cheap defence is the one now taken — one definition, and
everything that reads it reads it from there.

## §99 — THE FAPIAO CHASE: A REQUEST NOBODY ISSUED ASKS AGAIN, AND ONLY ISSUING IT STOPS THE ASKING

**2026-09-11 · Asked from the phone, with a screenshot of the Invoices screen:
"why we have 2 open invoices and the system doesn't alert me with a reminder to
close them … if customer close the notification and invoice still open, system
should recognize it and pop up again a reminder after certain time."**

**THE SCREENSHOT CONTAINED TWO DEFECTS WEARING ONE COAT, AND THE SECOND WAS
FOUND BY ASH.** The screen read *Pending 2* — TC000342 from 21 August and
TC000407 from 26 August, on 11 September. Both had crossed a month boundary.
Asked why nothing had alerted, the survey found no operator push for fapiao at
all; told by Ash that *"those invoice that not settled came from canceled
order"*, it found the reason there was nothing to alert about: **five call sites
asked which fapiao were pending and the Invoices list was the only one that did
not require the order to be alive.** Home's `/dashboard/ops` row, the unseen dot,
the Orders tab's `needs_invoice` pseudo-status and its badge all excluded
`cancelled` and `pending_payment`; `GET /api/retail-admin/invoices` filtered on
`needs_invoice = 1` and stopped. So the list counted the dead and Home did not,
and the operator — reading two sincere numbers that disagreed — concluded the
alerting was broken rather than that the list was wrong. **That is the more
damaging of the two available readings and it is the reasonable one to draw.**

**THE PREDICATE IS ONE PLACE NOW: `lib/fapiao-queue.js`.** Not a fixed clause in
a sixth location — the defect was never a wrong clause, it was five copies of
one, four of which were maintained together and one of which was not. The
regression guard is in the suite rather than in review: `test_fapiao_queue.js`
fails if `routes/retail.js` states the cancelled/unpaid exclusion anywhere
itself.

**CANCELLED AND UNPAID ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE COUNT AND NOT HIDDEN FROM THE
LIST**, and they are deliberately not the same fact: a cancelled order has no
sale to put a fiscal document behind, an unpaid one has no money received to
issue against. Both stay under All wearing the order's own status from the live
`ORDER_STATUS` pairs (`已取消` / `待付款`) with the muted pill, so no new string
was needed and no row silently vanishes. **`counts.blocked` is new** so the All
chip still sums the rows beneath it, and so that "two requests nobody can act
on" is a fact an operator can see rather than a gap between two other numbers.
**AN ISSUED FAPIAO KEEPS READING AS ISSUED whatever became of its order** — that
row is a 红冲 waiting to happen and is the one thing here nobody should lose.

**THE REMINDER IS A WINDOW, NOT A LATCH, AND `lib/alert-latch.js` HAD ALREADY
DRAWN THE DISTINCTION.** That file says a latch answers "is this condition still
flagged?" and is the wrong question for an ADVISORY, which has no moment at all
— "true all week", needing "not a flag but a WINDOW". An unissued 发票 is exactly
that shape. So `lib/delivery-reminders.js` could not simply be given a fifth
case: its claim is `UPDATE … WHERE reminder_ship_sent_at IS NULL`, where a
non-null stamp means never again. `invoice_reminder_last_at` is the same atomic
claim with the window in the WHERE, so overlapping ticks and restarts still
cannot double-fire but the row becomes claimable again once the gap passes.

**DISMISSING A NOTIFICATION WRITES NOTHING, WHICH IS THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION
ASKED.** There is no dismissed column for a sweep to read because there must not
be one — a swipe is a statement about a phone, not about the work. The order
still matches `pendingSql` on the next sweep and asks again. **Only ISSUING
stops it**, and it stops it by dropping the row out of the queue, so no reminder
state ever has to be cleared. Each order carries the tag `retail-fapiao-<id>`,
and `public/sw.js` already sets `renotify` whenever a tag is present, so the
second reminder REPLACES the first in the tray and still re-alerts: one invoice
holds one slot however many times it has asked.

**THE CADENCE KEYS OFF MONTH-END, NOT ELAPSED DAYS.** Silent for the first 24h
(the request is already on Home and an operator gets their working day), then
every 48h, then **DAILY in the last three days of the month, with Home's row
going from amber to brick on the same boundary.** What makes a late fapiao
expensive is not its age but the tax period closing: a 发票 requested in August
and issued in September is issued against an August order in the wrong period,
and no "it is 12 days old" says that. Both of the requests in the screenshot
would have been asking daily from 29 August. **The window is computed from the
month's own length** so February is not quietly exempt, and the phone reads the
SHOP's date (`shopTodayDate()`) so a handset in another timezone cannot disagree
with the server about which month it is.

**AT 10:00, AND THAT IS NOT THE QUIET HOURS `lib/push-events.js` REFUSES.** The
difference is worth stating because the two look alike: quiet hours silence an
alert that has already become true, by a clock typed once, and that file is
right that "an operational alert dropped by a clock is indistinguishable from
one that failed". This is the reminder's own schedule — the same `DAYOF_HOUR =
10` delivery-reminders uses for a date-only delivery. Nothing is dropped; it is
sent at ten, so a fapiao never wakes anybody at 03:00.

**ONE DIGEST ABOVE THREE.** Two pending, a push each, naming the customer — that
is what makes it actionable. Twenty pending, twenty banners is how a merchant
learns to switch the category off, and the notification that then goes unread is
the refund one; `lib/low-stock-digest.js` reached this conclusion first and for
the same reason. **A digest claims every row it covered**, or the three it did
not name re-send on the next tick.

**THE AUDIENCE IS `invoices:manage`, NOT `invoices:view`** — `lib/capabilities.js`
says it plainly: "Issuing a 发票 is a fiscal act, not a record of one." Whoever
can do the thing, not everyone who can read the list. **`invoice_pending` is a
switch** in `lib/push-events.js`, starting ON by that file's own rule that an
absent preference is consent — and it exists so that the control somebody
reaches for is "not this one" rather than push off entirely.

**THE PUSH OPENS `/?to=invoices`, THE PHONE'S OWN PARAMETER, DELIBERATELY.**
`?tab=invoices` on the desktop opens the PURCHASING invoices screen — supplier
invoices, the other direction entirely, and a worse landing than the default.
The phone is the surface holding the push subscription, so it is the one that
gets deep-linked.

**NOT BUILT, AND NOT DECIDED: THE SNOOZE.** Proposed in session and deliberately
held back to its own change. An explicit "remind me tomorrow" — distinct from
swiping, which must keep doing nothing — is what stops the only available way of
saying "I know, not today" from being switching the category off. It needs a
column, a write endpoint, a control on a screen that cannot itself issue a
fapiao, and a decision about whether a snooze survives month-end. None of that
belongs inside the change that fixed the counting.

**ALSO OPEN, AND RAISED IN SESSION: WHY AUTO-ISSUE IS OFF.** The screen says
*"Auto-issue is off · issue fapiao on desktop"*. If it is off for a fixable
reason, most of these requests would never become a reminder at all, and a
well-engineered nag for work that should not need nagging is the more expensive
answer. The reminder is worth having either way — auto-issue will never cover
every case, and the cases it misses are the ones that sit for three weeks — but
the question is not answered here.

**Chinese:** `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.56, two composed pairs and
one lifted, neither composed pair introducing a word the repository did not
already ship. Three pairs for a whole feature because most of it needed no
string: the ordinary title is the live pair Home already prints, the bodies are
numerals and names, and the month-end escalation on Home is a colour.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_fapiao_queue.js` (20 assertions) and
`scripts/test_fapiao_reminders.js` (32), both fast shard. The load-bearing
assertions on each side were checked to FAIL with the change reverted — the
window claim replaced by a once-ever latch, month-end replaced by a fixed date,
the digest removed — and to pass with it restored. `npm run test:fast` green.

**TWO COMMITS ON ONE BRANCH, NOT TWO PRs, and the reason is a session
constraint rather than a judgement about the change.** The one-PR-per-change
rule wants these split: the predicate fix stands alone and is worth landing
whether or not the reminder ever ships. The session was pinned to a single
designated branch and may not push to another, so the split is expressed as two
clean commits — the predicate fix first, the reminder on top of it — on one PR.
Either commit reverts without the other. Recorded because the rule was bent and
a silently bent rule is the kind that stops being read. Sessions live against this repo at the time
(`store-section-setup`, `spoiled-shipment-workflow`) touch neither path; §99 is
the next free number as of `6555ecb` and neither had pushed a branch.

### §99 addendum 1 — the snooze is built, and it is not a dismissal (2026-09-11)

§99 recorded the snooze as **not built, not decided**, and named four things it
needed: a column, a write endpoint, a control on a screen that cannot itself
issue a fapiao, and a ruling on whether a deferral survives month-end. Ash asked
for it after §99 shipped. All four are settled here.

**WHY IT EXISTS, RESTATED, BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION.** §99 gave a
dismissed notification no effect whatsoever — no dismissed column, so a swipe
writes nothing and the next sweep asks again. That is correct and it is the
feature. On its own it leaves an operator who genuinely cannot act today with
exactly one working control: switching every push off. `lib/push-events.js` is
written about that failure in its own words — *"The switch that gets used is the
one that turns the whole thing off, and then the pick that mattered arrives
nowhere."* The snooze exists so that the control within reach is "not this one,
not today" rather than the one that silences somebody else's refund.

**IT IS A DECISION, NOT A GESTURE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE DESIGN.** A swipe on
a banner still writes nothing and still must. The deferral is a press on the
Invoices screen, by somebody holding `invoices:manage`, recorded in
`retail_orders.invoice_reminder_snoozed_until`. Three properties stop it from
becoming a way to never do the work:

- **It reaches tomorrow's reminder hour and no further.** One press hides at most
  ONE ask. There is no "next week", and `snoozeTarget()` is the only thing that
  decides where tomorrow is.
- **IT QUIETS THE PUSH ONLY.** The order still matches `pendingSql`, so Home's
  Needs-you row keeps counting it and still goes brick at month-end. The work
  never leaves the screen an operator walks past; only the interruption moves.
  This is the safeguard, and `test_fapiao_reminders.js` asserts it directly.
- **The row is skipped, never claimed.** The sweep does not touch
  `invoice_reminder_last_at` for a deferred row, so a snooze DEFERS the cadence
  rather than restarting it — press it on a 48-hour row and the chase resumes on
  its own schedule, not two days after the press.

**MONTH-END HONOURS IT, AND THE HONEST SHAPE OF THAT IS RECORDED IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS.** The control means *do not ask me again before tomorrow's reminder
hour*. Inside month-end the cadence is already daily, so a press made BEFORE the
day's ask defers it and a press made AFTER it changes nothing — tomorrow is when
the next one was coming anyway. **That second case is not a defect and must not
be "fixed" by lengthening the snooze at month-end**: a control cannot defer below
the cadence it is already on, and the alternative — a longer deferral in exactly
the three days the tax period is closing — inverts the rule §99 turns on. The
suite pins both cases for that reason. Disabling the control at month-end was
rejected outright: it would leave a button that reads as set and buzzes anyway,
and a lying control is worse than one day of chosen silence on a row Home is
showing in brick the whole time.

**THE GATE IS THE ONE THAT ALREADY EXISTED.** `lib/cap-routes.js` maps every
write under `/api/retail-admin/invoices` to `invoices:manage`, so the route
needed no new mapping — and the suite proves it through the real middleware
rather than asserting it from source: an operator holding only `invoices:view`
gets `403 forbidden_capability` and writes nothing, while still reading the list.

**ONLY A ROW THAT IS WAITING MAY BE DEFERRED.** Issued, cancelled, unpaid, never
requested and non-existent all answer `404 not_pending`. A date written onto work
that no longer exists is a stale stamp for whoever reads the column next, and the
column is deliberately one nobody has to tidy: `isSnoozed()` treats a lapsed,
blank or UNREADABLE stamp as not snoozed, so nothing ever has to clear it and an
unparseable value fails towards asking, which is the safe direction for a debt.

**`snoozed:false` LIFTS IT, EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN AS A TOGGLE**, so a double tap
cannot flip a deferral back on by accident.

**ONE STRING FOR BOTH STATES.** The control is the app's own `.chip` with its
`on` fill, so `明天提醒我` reads as an offer when empty and as "set" when filled.
No date is printed beside it: the button promises tomorrow and the server writes
tomorrow, and a timestamp would be a second source for one fact. Chinese:
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.57 — one composed pair, one lifted, with
`忽略` and `跳过` rejected because both describe a dismissal and a word that made
the two sound alike would undo the distinction this rests on.

**A NOTE ON WHAT THE PHONE CANNOT DO.** The Invoices screen still says
*"Auto-issue is off · issue fapiao on desktop"*, and the snooze does not change
that — it is a control for deferring the reminder, on the surface that receives
it, not a step towards issuing from a handset. **Why auto-issue is off remains
open**, raised in session twice and unanswered; it is still the larger win if it
turns out to be fixable.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_fapiao_snooze_route.js` (18 assertions, the endpoint and
its gate through the real middleware) and nine more in
`scripts/test_fapiao_reminders.js` (the sweep's half). Load-bearing assertions on
both sides were checked to FAIL with the change reverted — the `not_pending`
guard removed (5 fail) and the sweep's skip removed (4 fail) — and to pass with
it restored. `npm run test:fast` green at 206.

**One correction to a claim in §99's own record.** That section said the snooze
"needs … a ruling on whether a snooze survives month-end", implying the two
outcomes were survive-or-not. The real answer is a third: it survives, and at
month-end it is frequently a no-op by construction. Left standing and corrected
here rather than edited, per this file's rule about dated claims.

### §99 addendum 2 — the auto-issue switch is removed; the integration stays dormant (2026-09-11)

**§99 left "why is auto-issue off" open and asked it three more times. Ash
answered it: the shop's fapiao provider issues no 发票 for us and offers no open
API.** That closes the question and settles the control.

**THE SWITCH WAS NOT A SETTING.** `maybeAutoIssueInvoice` returns on its first
line unless `fapiao.autoIssue` is on AND Nuonuo credentials are present. The
phone showed only the first lock. Ash turned it on from the phone during this
session, the screen said *"Auto-issue is on · 自动开票已开启"*, and nothing
happened, because nothing could. **That is precisely the defect the §99 snooze
was designed around — a control that reads as set and does nothing — arriving
from the other direction**, and it was worse here: the server ALREADY computes
`credsReady` on `GET /fapiao-settings` and **neither surface has ever read it**,
so an operator had no way to find out.

**WHAT WAS REMOVED: the control, and every trace of its state.** The settings
row, `toggleFapiao`, `loadFapiao`, the `r.fapiao` branches in both settings
renderers, the four `state.fapiao*` slots, and the phone's only call to
`/fapiao-settings`. A hidden control whose fetch survives is one render away
from coming back, so the suite asserts the endpoint is not reachable from
`m.html` at all rather than merely unrendered.

**WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT REMOVED, AND WHY ASH WAS ASKED.** The session
proposed ripping out Nuonuo entirely and put the scope to Ash as a choice,
because **the credentials are PER-TENANT** (`lib/tenant-creds.js`: Roots reads
`NUONUO_*` from env, every other tenant stores its own encrypted under
`nuonuo.app_key` / `app_secret` / `saler_tax` / `env`). This shop's provider
having no API is a fact about ONE tenant. Deleting `lib/nuonuo.js`, the
auto-issue path and the credential keys would take a platform capability from
every tenant to solve that, and rebuild it for the first tenant who has an API.
**Ash chose UI-only.** `scripts/test_fapiao_no_auto_issue.js` fails in BOTH
directions for that reason: if the switch returns, and if a later session
"finishes the job" by deleting the integration.

**BOTH GUARDS STAY, AND NEITHER MAY BE RELAXED.** With no switch on the phone,
`fapiao.autoIssue` can no longer be raised from a screen — but the credential
check is what has kept this harmless all along, and a future session must not
drop either guard to compensate for the missing control. The `/fapiao-settings`
GET and PUT stay: the desktop still reaches them, and so would a tenant who one
day has a provider with an API.

**THE NOTE BAR KEEPS THE HALF THAT IS TRUE.** It read *"Auto-issue is off ·
issue fapiao on desktop"*, which reported a state nobody could change while
inviting the question of how to change it. It now reads *"Issue fapiao on
desktop · 请在电脑端开具"* — **the live pair's own tail with its first clause
dropped, so NOTHING WAS COMPOSED and `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is
untouched**, the same treatment v4.211 recorded for a heading that was deleted
rather than reworded.

**ONE LEFTOVER OF THE SESSION'S OWN, FIXED HERE.** §99 addendum 1's snooze
recovery set `state.fapiaoTried = false` when a row came back `not_pending`.
That flag gated the SETTINGS read, never the list, so it did nothing for that
recovery; `loadLiveInvoices()` beside it was already doing the refetch. Removed
with the rest of the state.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE.** The fapiao queue and its chase (§99) are
untouched and are now the whole answer: every 发票 this shop owes is issued by
hand at a desk, and the reminder is what stops one sitting for three weeks. The
two from the screenshot that started this were on cancelled orders and were
never work at all.

**STILL NOT DONE, AND NOT A DEFECT: `credsReady` is still read by nobody.** With
the switch gone the phone has no use for it, and the desktop's fapiao settings
panel is outside this change. Recorded because the next person to find the field
should know it is unused on purpose here, not overlooked.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_fapiao_no_auto_issue.js` (13 assertions, fast shard),
checked to fail in both directions — the switch restored (1 fail) and
`lib/nuonuo.js` deleted (1 fail). `scripts/test_mobile_settings.js` loses the two
`state.fapiao` fixtures and gains an assertion that the row is absent from the
RENDERED screen rather than from source; **that suite is in the slow shard, which
this repo does not run** (CLAUDE.md, Ash's standing instruction given twice), so
it is edited and NOT verified, and this entry says so rather than implying it
passed. `npm run test:fast` green at 208.

## §100 — CONVERSION DIVIDES ONE CHANNEL BY ITSELF, AND THE CARD SAYS WHICH ONE

**2026-09-11 · Asked from the phone, with Home's second card circled in red:
"this part should only reflect the mini app channel, nothing else. title should
say that as well. this only make sense. it's the only private sale channel
platform that can count conver[sion]. others are meituan, eleme, gzgrocery. so
for roots it make sense."**

**THE SCREENSHOT IS THE PROOF.** The card read *Sessions 25 · Conversion 68.0%
· 17 orders ÷ 25 sessions · Returning 6 of 8 who bought today · Refunded 0*. The
25 were mini-app opens. The 17 were the day's paid orders across every channel —
the mini app, Meituan and the counter till together — because `kpis.orders` is
`COUNT(*)` over `retail_orders` with only gzgrocery's mirror rows excluded.
A conversion rate was being computed from two different populations.

**WHY IT CAN ONLY EVER BE WRONG, RATHER THAN SOMETIMES WRONG.** `retail_visits`
has exactly one writer: `miniapp/utils/track.js`, posting to the public
`POST /api/retail/track`. Nothing else in the tree calls that route — not
`shop.html`, not any daemon. So a session is a mini-app session by construction.
Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery hand over finished orders and will never report a
browse; that is a fact about what a marketplace is, not a gap in our tracking we
might one day close. **The error therefore runs one way only: every marketplace
order the shop wins inflates a number that is supposed to describe browsing we
can watch.** The better the Meituan day, the healthier the mini app looked.

**THIS IS §36's FINANCE FINDING FROM THE OTHER SIDE.** That one recorded a ratio
whose NUMERATOR was blended (all-channel revenue over storefront orders, which
pushed one ¥3,000 top-up into an average-order tile). This is the same fault
approached from the denominator: a ratio's two halves must stand on the same
population. m.html's own AOV note already says so in those words; the card
beside it was breaking the rule the note states.

**DECIDED, and the shape of the fix.**

1. **`kpis.conversion_rate` is corrected AT SOURCE, not on the card that
   reported it.** It is now mini-app paid orders ÷ mini-app sessions. There is
   no all-channel conversion to lose — only an arithmetic mistake to stop
   repeating — so no caller can want the blended figure and none is offered it.
2. **`kpis.mini_app_orders` rides alongside it**, so every screen that quotes
   "N orders ÷ M sessions" can name the numerator it actually divided by. The
   Orders card two along still shows the bigger all-channel count, and without
   this the two read as a contradiction.
3. **A `mini_app` block joins the payload** — sessions, orders, conversion_rate,
   buyers, new_buyers, returning_buyers, refunded_orders, refund_rate. Each is
   one of the existing all-channel figures with the channel predicate added and
   **nothing else changed**: same paid window, same date convention, same
   "new means first-ever paid order" rule. They are the headline measures
   narrowed, never second definitions of them. It is a block rather than eight
   more `kpis` keys deliberately: **a screen reads the whole of it and says
   "mini app" over the result, or it reads none of it.**
4. **The predicate is the one `/sales/summary` already uses for its WeChat
   card** — `COALESCE(NULLIF(channel,''),'wechat')='wechat'` AND not counter
   fulfilment. The NULL/'' default is load-bearing: mini-app rows that predate
   the column default carry no channel, and `channel='wechat'` would drop them
   and read as a decline. The counter exclusion is load-bearing too: a till sale
   is written through the manual-order endpoint and can wear a storefront
   channel, so `fulfillment_type='counter'` is the till's real signature.
5. **Home's second card reads that block and nothing else, and carries the
   heading "Mini app · 小程序".**
6. **Returning stays a fact about the PERSON, not about the channel.** Only the
   outer set — who bought today — narrows to the mini app; the inner "when did
   they first ever buy" subquery stays all-channel. A customer who has ordered
   on Meituan for a year and opens the mini app today is a returning customer
   having their first mini-app order, and calling them new would be a claim
   about them that is false. Scoping the subquery too would make loyalty read as
   churn on exactly the day a shop's regulars move channel.

**THE HEADING IS PART OF THE FIX, AND IT IS NOT A RETURN OF "ALSO TODAY".** §97's
sweep retired that label because it named the card's POSITION rather than its
contents. The rule it set is that a heading must say what sits under it — and
this one does: it names the card's POPULATION, the one thing the two cards under
"Today" do not share. The money card above genuinely is all channels and says so
in its own first label ("Revenue (all channels)"). An unlabelled card of
one-channel figures sitting beside it under a shared heading is exactly the
confusion that produced 68.0%. `todaySection` still draws one section heading
and it still says Today. `test_backend_nav_parity` §4 holds both lines, with the
distinction written out beside them.

**THE DESKTOP IS PARTLY DONE, DELIBERATELY, AND HERE IS THE LINE.** Everything
forced by the corrected rate is done: the KPI card is relabelled
`Conversion (mini app) · 转化率（小程序）` and its sub-line names
`mini_app_orders`; the Customers card's conversion cell does the same on both
sides of its small-denominator threshold; the AI digest carries
`mini_app_orders` beside `conversion_rate_pct` so a model reading it cannot
divide by the wrong count; and the "money path" funnel's first two rows — a
session count above an order count, with a percentage between them — are now
**Visited the mini app → Ordered in the mini app**, which is the same fault this
entry is about, wearing a bar chart.

**What is NOT done on the desktop: its Returning and Refunded remain
all-channel.** Those two are legitimate all-channel questions (a refund rate
across every channel is a real number an owner wants), and the desktop presents
them in a different layout from the phone — Returning in the Customers card,
Refunded in the Today strip — so scoping them is a layout decision, not a
one-line narrowing. **The phone's card scopes all four because Ash asked for
that card.** The divergence is recorded here rather than left to be discovered:
until the desktop is rebuilt to match, its Refunded figure and the phone's are
answering different questions, and only the phone's says which.

**Tests:** `scripts/test_mini_app_conversion.js` (20 assertions, fast shard).
It **lifts the predicate out of `routes/retail.js` by regex** and runs it against
an in-memory database seeded with one order per channel, so a later edit that
widens the predicate — tidying the COALESCE away, dropping the counter
exclusion, adding a channel — fails here rather than shipping. Checked to fail in
both directions: numerator reverted to `kpi.orders` (1 fail) and the counter
exclusion removed (4 fails, three of them the seeded rows rather than the lift —
which is the point of seeding them). `test_mobile_home.js` gains two rendered cases (the
heading draws above Sessions, under the one Today; and it leaves with the card
it labels when the `customers` gate hides it). `test_backend_nav_parity` §4 gains
two. `scripts/lib/m-fakeserver.js` grows a `mini_app` block that is **smaller on
every figure than its all-channel neighbours** — a fixture where the two agreed
would pass whether or not Home read the right one.

## §101 — THE NIGHT'S ORDERS RAISE THEIR OWN KITCHEN REQUEST IN THE MORNING, BECAUSE THE PUSH AND THE PRINTER ALREADY KNOW HOW TO CARRY ONE

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-11. The question was put after a walkthrough of what
§84 actually delivers: *"if the meal the customer order is automatic at the
kitchen queue for them to know the orders that already made so they know how
many to prepare"* — answered honestly (the number is there, on one screen, if
somebody opens it) — and the instruction came back in three words: **"we need
it to be push, print"**.

### What was already built, and the one thing that was not

§84 computes the number: `lib/batch-owed.js`, owed units per (store, product),
a negative shelf plus the lines of `awaiting_restock` orders, rendered as
*Customer orders waiting · 有客户订单等待* above the kitchen queue's **To make**
tab.

§51 and §71 built the delivery mechanism: a push to everyone holding
`restock:fulfil` with a deep link onto `kitchenqueue`, a slip on the kitchen's
Feieyun printer, a card in the queue, §61's per-line close, and §61's handover
to *What you made* — the screen that actually moves the shelf.

**Every part of that second list keys on a `restock_orders` row.** A night of
pre-orders creates no such row, so it fired none of it. The two halves were
built four days apart and nothing joined them: the kitchen's own number existed
in exactly one place, behind a tap nobody is prompted to make.

### The ruling

**One kitchen request, raised by the server, once a day, at an hour the tenant
sets — `fresh.morningRequestHour`, default 6, blank turns it off.**

Two alternatives were put to Ash and declined, and the reasons are the useful
part:

- **A digest push and slip carrying the same numbers.** It is a second
  notification to build and a second place the kitchen reads, and at the end of
  it they still have nothing to close and nothing that moves stock. The
  request-shaped answer reuses six existing mechanisms and ends on the screen
  that fixes the shelf.
- **Push and print per order, as each one lands.** Thirty orders on a Friday
  night is thirty slips, most of them at 2am, and not one of them states the
  total — which is the only number the question was ever about.

### The row, and why it looks like every other kitchen request

`from_role` warehouse, `to_role` kitchen, `purpose` `'order'`, `status`
`'sent'`, a `PR-` number, both locations NULL per §51, `created_by` NULL.

`purpose='order'` is not a new value and was not chosen for tidiness: it
already renders *For an order · 用于发货* on the slip (`lib/feie.js`) and in the
queue (`krPurpose`), and §65 already sorts it below urgent. The request needed
no vocabulary at all because the vocabulary for "the kitchen is making this
because customers are waiting for it" was written in §65 and §84.

`genRsNumber` is **injected by `routes/restock.js`, not copied into the new
lib**. §80's copy rule is the whole reason: a second implementation of the
per-prefix daily sequence is how two requests end up called PR-260911-002.

### One new column, and what it buys

`restock_orders.auto_source` — `'morning_owed'` on a row this job raised, NULL
on a row a person raised, which is true of every row already in the table. One
`addColumn`, no backfill, no migration.

It exists because **the once-a-day guard has to be exact.** The inferable
marker — `created_by IS NULL` — is also true of rows predating
`drop_created_by_user_fk_v1`, and a guard that is usually right raises a second
request on the morning it is wrong, which means the kitchen cooks the night's
orders twice.

**The guard is the database, not a file latch.** `lib/alert-latch`'s
`claimWindow` was the obvious reach and is deliberately not used: it is
per-box file state, so a rebuilt container forgets it and sends again, and what
is being guarded here is not an advisory that can repeat harmlessly but a row
somebody cooks from. Asking whether today already holds an `auto_source`
request is also the correct answer after a restart, a redeploy, and on a second
app server.

**It catches up, then stops.** The job fires at the configured hour or up to
three hours after it, so a box that was down at 06:00 still prints at 07:10,
while an order landing at 15:00 does not raise a surprise request for food
wanted the following morning.

### The lines

**Summed per product across shops.** A kitchen request carries no locations at
all (§51), so there is nowhere for a per-shop split to live — and which shop
gets the wraps is a transfer's question, asked once they exist.

**SKU and both names, and no `product_id`** — the shape every live kitchen
request has, because §61 derives whether a line has been recorded by matching
SKU first and exact name second. A line carrying a `product_id` the derivation
does not read would look identical and fail to tick off.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not done

- **A human request for the same food is not subtracted.** Doing it means
  matching lines across open requests by SKU-then-name and then trusting the
  result to *reduce* what gets cooked. Wrong in that direction, the kitchen
  under-makes and a customer who has paid gets nothing; wrong in the other, a
  visible over-make sits on a card somebody can read. The asymmetry decides it.
  Named here so it is known to have been weighed rather than missed.
- **`lib/batch-owed.js` is not touched** and learns nothing — no cadence, no
  request vocabulary. The derivation runs one way only.
- **The on-screen block is unchanged.** It now agrees with a slip instead of
  being the only place the fact lived.
- **No new push channel, no second printer, no new capability**, and no change
  to who can reach the queue.
- **Nothing is minted in Chinese for the request, the slip or the push.** The
  note reuses `有客户订单等待` verbatim from §84's own block. The two settings
  strings are arrangements of live fragments, declared in
  `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.60 with the candidates rejected.
## §102 — THE PRE-ORDER WINDOW OPENS THE SYNC GATE, AND THE TENANT SAYS WHEN IT OPENS

**2026-09-11 · Asked from the phone, off the Home card reading *"Meituan not
syncing · stock updates waiting since Sep 7, 5:56 PM · 19"*: "meituan syncing
only on the morning it's a problem for pre order. check how the system work and
give a solution for pre orders meituan, same eleme."** Decided by Ash on the
survey below: **(1) the tenant chooses when pre-orders open, defaulting to
midnight; (2) overnight order reading is approved** — *"tenent can choose when
start , defult can be midnight"*, *"ok do it"*.

**TWO CLOCKS WERE SET INDEPENDENTLY AND NOTHING CHECKED THEY AGREED.** §85 opens
the pre-order window at **00:00** and closes it at `lock_hour` — there is no
lower bound in `preorderWindow`, so midnight is not a choice anyone made, it is
where the absence of a condition happens to land. The daemons' own sync gate
opens at the store's *"Channel sync starts · 渠道同步开始"* time, or
`open − DEFAULT_PREOPEN_LEAD_MIN` (two hours) when that is blank — 08:00 for a
shop opening at 10:00. **The hours between the two are dead**, and they are the
hours §85 exists to sell in.

**WHAT THAT COSTS, PER CHANNEL, AND THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME FAULT.**

- **Meituan.** `flipTick` fires at 00:00 and enqueues every mapped batch-made
  product; `pushableStores()` then drops every store because `isStoreOpen()` is
  false, so the rows sit. The listing shows the previous day's post-lock number
  — the bare shelf, usually zero — until 08:00. **The allowance never reaches
  the platform during most of the window it is open for.** That queue is the
  card Ash photographed.
- **Eleme, and this one can oversell.** Eleme's `processStockQueue` is gated on
  the operator's channel-close switch and **not** on hours, so the allowance
  *does* publish at 00:00. But Eleme's order poll **is** hours-gated. §85 is
  self-capping only because each pre-order drives the shelf down by one and the
  next published figure falls with it; **an order nobody reads moves no shelf**,
  so the published figure stays at `shelf + qty` while orders accumulate. A
  twenty-unit allowance can take sixty orders before 08:00. That is precisely
  the oversell §85 was built to be incapable of, arriving through the one edge
  §85 did not look at.

**DECIDED.**

1. **The pre-order window's start becomes a tenant setting — `preorder_open_hour`,
   defaulting to 0.** The lock hour was Ash's to choose and is; the start was
   nobody's and now is too. **Zero is the default because it is today's
   behaviour**, so a tenant that never touches the field sees no change — the
   same no-migration shape §74 and §85 both chose.
2. **An open pre-order window opens the daemons' sync gate.** `isStoreOpen()` in
   `scripts/meituan-daemon.js` and `scripts/eleme-daemon.js` is satisfied by the
   store's ordinary sync window **or** by `preorderWindow(channel).open`.
   **Every one of §85's five off switches still holds**: the widening happens
   only on a batch day, only before the lock, only for a channel the operator
   named, only with an allowance set, only with the schedule enabled. A tenant
   with the schedule off — which is most of them — has an unchanged daemon.
3. **Order polling is widened with it, deliberately, and that is the half that
   matters.** `isStoreOpen()` gates the poll as well as the push, and widening
   only the push would publish an allowance nothing could ever decrement — the
   Eleme fault above, extended to Meituan. Ash approved the overnight read
   knowing its cost.
4. **The widening lives in ONE place**: `batchCadence.preorderSyncOpen()`, which
   both daemons call. §80's rule about a fourth copy of the cadence is the same
   rule here — two daemons each holding their own version of "and also when the
   pre-order window is open" is how they come to disagree about a morning. It
   swallows its own errors for the reason `flipTick` does: a config read must
   never take a daemon loop down.

**WHY NOT JUST SET "SYNC STARTS" TO 00:00, WHICH NEEDS NO CODE AT ALL.**
`syncWindow` clamps `syncStart ≤ open`, so 00:00 is already accepted, and it is
the correct lever for one morning in an emergency. It is the wrong rule: it
widens **every day, batch or not**, and it turns on a full five-minute order
poll at 04:00 on a Sunday the kitchen is not cooking. The code warns about
exactly that in three places, and it is a fingerprint, not a preference. The
window-following rule widens only on the mornings there is something to sell.

**THE STORE'S OWN "SYNC STARTS" FIELD IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL MEANS WHAT IT
MEANT.** It answers "when does this shop's stock start moving every day"; §102
answers "when does a cooking day open the gate early". A store that wants its
stock live from 07:00 daily still sets the field; the two widen the same front
edge and the earlier of them wins, which is what `within()` already does.

**WHAT IS NOT BUILT, named so it is not read as done.**

- **`lib/channel-sync-stale.js` still counts Eleme's waiting time as
  hours-aware** (`hoursAware: true`), when Eleme's pushes have never been
  hours-gated at all. The Home card therefore under-reports how long an Eleme
  row has waited. **It is a real defect and it is a different one** — it
  predates this section and is not this section's to fix. Recorded here because
  it was found here.
- **The 19 rows on the card are NOT explained by this section.** They date from
  2026-09-07 17:56, which is inside the sync window on any reading of the
  store's hours. The likely shape is the one `lib/channel-sync-stale.js:105`
  already documents from production — a `latest`-per-target row left at `error`
  that the drift sweep never re-queues because the stock now matches what the
  platform last accepted, so the card nags forever over targets that are
  perfectly in sync. **Unconfirmed**, and confirming it needs the two read-only
  diagnostics run against production, not a code change.
- **The order that arrives one minute after the lock** is still §85's open item
  and this section does not touch it.

### §102 ADDENDUM — THE STALE CARD LEARNS BOTH WINDOWS, AND ONE OF THEM WAS §102'S OWN FAULT (2026-09-11)

**Two defects in one denominator.** `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` answers "how long
has this channel's oldest unresolved push been waiting, of time the channel could
actually have used". Both of its wrong answers were about that clause, not about
the query.

**ELEME WAS NEVER HOURS-GATED, AND THE CARD THOUGHT IT WAS.** The channel table
declared `hoursAware: true` on the reasonable-looking ground that
`scripts/eleme-daemon.js` gates on opening hours the way `meituan-daemon.js`
does. **It does not.** Its `processStockQueue` filters on
`channelClosedStores('eleme')` and nothing else; only its ORDER POLL reads the
hours. So an Eleme push could always go out at 03:00, and scoring its wait as
zero for those hours meant **the card was quietest exactly when Eleme was most
likely to be stuck**. Corrected to wall-clock, which is what the flag is for.

**AND §102 BLINDED IT ON THE MEITUAN SIDE, which is this section's own to fix.**
Before §102 a daemon's gate was the store's sync window and nothing else, so one
interval a day was the whole truth and `pushableElapsedMs` walked one. §102 added
a second: an open pre-order window opens the gate whatever the hour. A Meituan
queue jamming at 00:30 on a batch morning therefore scored **zero elapsed until
08:00** — the card would have stayed silent straight through the window §102
exists to keep syncing, and the operator would have learned about it from the
shelf. The sum now walks the union of both intervals, merged so an overlap is
not counted twice.

**THE CADENCE IS ASKED, NOT MIRRORED.** `preorderSpans()` reads
`lib/batch-cadence` for the schedule and `nextBatchDate` for the day, including
taking that module's own ruling that the ordering cutoff beats a lock set past
it. §80's copy rule again: a card that decided for itself which days were batch
days would eventually disagree with the daemon it is reporting on.

**IT COSTS ONE NULL CHECK FOR EVERYONE ELSE.** Every off switch — no schedule, no
allowance, channel not named, no lock hour, a start at or after the close —
returns null before any day is walked, and the config is read once per channel
rather than once per day.

**WHAT PRODUCTION SAID WHEN ASKED, and it corrected this session twice.**
`diagnose_meituan_sync_window.js` against the live database at 01:51 on
2026-09-12 reported **neither store has `open_time`/`close_time` set**.
Meituan falls back to `LEGACY_STORE_HOURS`, so its gate really was shutting
overnight and §102 does the work claimed for it. **Eleme has no such fallback**:
blank hours read as always-open, so its order poll was already running around the
clock and **the overnight Eleme oversell §102 describes could not have occurred
on this tenant's data**. The mechanism in the code was real; the exposure was
not. §102's text is left as written, per this file's convention for a superseded
claim, and this paragraph is the correction.

**AND IT FOUND SOMETHING NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR: 越秀 MEITUAN IS DEAD.** 1,683
pending pushes, oldest 2026-08-24, **none queued in the last twelve hours**, and
**no successful push since 2026-08-22 05:57**. 天河 pushed eight minutes before
the diagnostic ran. It is invisible on the Home card because
`isStoreTradingOnChannel` excludes a store that is not trading, which is the
behaviour that file deliberately chose — a row that can never clear costs the
alert its meaning — and which here hid a three-week outage. **Whether 越秀 is
deliberately closed on Meituan or broken is NOT settled by this and is not
guessed at here.** Recorded as the open item.

## §103 — ONE VERDICT PER ITEM PER CHANNEL, ON ONE PAGE, IN THREE WORDS

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-11. The ask: *"extremely easy for a tenant to know
which items are not in sync with Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery … check how it is
today, what do you advise."* A read-only survey came first, then a light-theme
mockup with three visual options, then **"build it as you recommend"**.

### What the survey found

Three tabs, three vocabularies. Meituan's screen had seven state phrases,
Eleme's eight, GZ Grocery's a plain English-only table with a `no match` and a
`+/-` column — eighteen phrases for what is really four situations. No screen
answered the question across channels. The Products page mentioned no channel.
The phone carried one Meituan-only health card, whole-store, never per item.
The dashboard's only channel row fired when a whole queue jammed, never when a
single item was wrong.

And the worst of it was not the fragmentation. **The Meituan tab's "Synced" was
computed from the link setup alone** — a name that verified, a switch that was
on, an option that was claimed — and never asked whether the last push had
LANDED. Harissa Chilli Paste read green for 75 days while every push failed and
Meituan held 18 against a shelf of 3. `docs/channel-mapping-findings.md` F4 had
already measured the class: ~400 terminal failures, June to August, 17–35 a
day, *"surfaced by nothing"*.

### The ruling

**Four words, all live pairs, one read, one page.**

| k | word | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | Synced · 已同步 | the platform holds the number we would send it now |
| `att` | Needs attention · 待处理 | the platform holds a WRONG number, or cannot be reached for this item; the fix is on the item |
| `off` | Sync off · 已关闭 | listed, switch off — settled |
| `none` | Not listed · 未上架 | no mapping; not sold there, and that is normal |

plus `unk` — *Name not checked* — for a mapping whose store catalogue has never
been read. It is drawn like `none` and never amber: an unread catalogue is one
fact about the STORE, carried on the channel's own line, and the Eleme rebuild
already paid for the alternative (194 amber dots for one dropped fetch).

**Amber means the platform holds a wrong number.** The comparison is the drift
sweeps' own — `lib/channel-publish.js`'s figure against `last_pushed_qty`, per
claim, through `packQty` — or a latest queue row in `error`, carrying the
channel's own sentence. Nothing new is stored and there is no second definition
of drift: a row this read calls wrong is a row the sweep would re-queue.

**A push in flight is green** whatever its age. How long a channel has been
sitting on its queue is the channel's fact, answered once by
`lib/channel-sync-stale.js` and shown once on that channel's card. The forty
items behind a stalled queue stay quiet. One cause, shown once.

**Worst store wins per channel; worst channel wins per item.** Meituan has two
stores; an item is one row. Six dots per row was drawn and rejected.

**Not listed is quiet on every channel, Meituan included.** The Meituan tab
counts an active product on neither store as work. This page does not: 47 items
are deliberately not on Eleme, and a warning that fires on the normal case is a
warning nobody reads.

**Stores not trading on a channel are out of scope**, by the same predicate
(`lib/store-trading.js`) the stall check uses.

### What was built

- `lib/channel-sync-items.js` — the one read. Per active product, per channel,
  per trading store: state, reason, last accepted number, expected number, the
  channel's error text. `channelSyncSummary()` is the same read, counts only.
- `GET /api/retail-admin/channel-sync` — read-only, `requireRetailAdmin`.
- **Desktop: the Channel sync tab.** `public/retail-admin/29-channel-sync.js`,
  rail-less under Sales like the three channel tabs, gated any-of
  `meituan:view / eleme:view / guanyi:view` (the rule that admits Sales). A
  channel strip (one card per channel: syncing / not syncing since, waiting,
  catalogue freshness per store), chips (Needs attention / Synced / Not listed
  / Sync off / All), a channel filter that answers "which items are not on
  Eleme" directly, and a table opening on the reason and a button that lands
  on that item in the channel's own tab. A door beside *Get help* on Sales.
- **Dashboard:** a *Channel sync · 渠道同步* row off `channel_items_attention`
  on `/dashboard/ops` — items wrong on a channel, with a "wrong since" clock.
  The existing stall row is untouched and still outranks it.
- **Phone:** `channelsync` screen (one card per item, three pills, the reason,
  which desktop tab fixes it), a More row, a Home row — and the phone's
  existing "not syncing" row now opens that screen instead of a toast saying
  to use the desktop.
- **The three channel tabs are untouched.** They remain the repair shop; this
  is the alarm. Every amber cell ends in *Open Meituan · 前往美团* (and its
  siblings), which opens the tab on that item via `mtSelect` / `elSelect` /
  the GZ Grocery search box.

### Step 5 — BUILT 2026-09-12 (v4.230)

The three tabs' eighteen phrases fold into one table in `01-core.js`: four state
words, five named causes, `chWord(channel, k, reason)`. No state has two names
any more, GZ Grocery has a vocabulary for the first time, and the `饶`/`饿`
typo that shipped in Eleme's *Not on Eleme* label dies with the label.

**That gap is now CLOSED — §103 addendum, v4.232.** It was named here as not
built, Ash read the note and said do it, and it shipped on its own rather than
inside a wording change. `chApplyVerdict` (01-core.js) overlays the server's
verdict onto all three tabs in one direction only: a tab that says `ok` where
the push failed now says *Needs attention*, per store, with the page's own
sentence. Nothing else about a tab's classification changes. **Their "Needs
attention" chips count more as a result, and that is the correct number.**

### Steps 3 and 4 — BUILT 2026-09-12 (v4.228)

The mockup's build order was five steps and Ash took the recommendation as
given. Steps 1–2 shipped first as the 80%; **steps 3 and 4 followed the next
day** at Ash's word, in the same shape the mockup drew:

- **Step 3 — three dots on the Products list**, table column and card, from a
  `?compact=1` projection of this same read. Gated on whether the tenant has
  any mapping at all; a variant family's dot is the worst of its members;
  clicking opens Channel sync on that product.
- **Step 4 — a Channels card in the product editor**, one row per channel,
  with the reason and the fix button only where something is wrong.

**Step 5, folding the three tabs' eighteen phrases into these four**, is later
still and touches the tabs, which none of this did.

### Explicitly NOT decided here

- Whether an overselling item deserves Brick rather than Amber. Amber was
  chosen to match the tabs' own `att` and to keep Brick for a channel that is
  down; Ash was offered the switch and did not take it up.
- A per-item "push now" from this page. Read-only was the recommendation and
  the build; a write from the alarm is a different decision.

### Chinese

One composed string, `渠道同步`, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`
with the candidates rejected. Everything else is a live pair lifted whole or an
arrangement of live fragments.

## §104 — ONE CHANNEL ROW ON HOME, AND THE STALL KEEPS ITS VOICE INSIDE IT

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-12, from a live phone screenshot of Home. The ask:
*"we don't need anymore the individual channel sync notification like meituan.
we have the new one that all channels combined."*

### What the screenshot showed

Two rows, stacked, under a heading that says *Needs you*:

```
🔌  Meituan not syncing                                    3  ›
    stock updates waiting since Sep 7, 5:56 PM
🔄  Channel sync                                           2  ›
    Meituan 2, wrong since Sep 7, 5:56 PM
```

Same channel. Same minute. Two amber icons, two counts, two chips going to two
different places. §103 built the second row and deliberately left the first
alone — *"how long a channel has sat on its queue is the CHANNEL's fact, said
once on its own card, never repeated on the forty items behind it"* — which was
right about where the fact belongs and did not ask how Home would read with
both rows in it.

### The one thing that had to be checked before deleting anything

**A stalled channel's items are all GREEN.** That is §103's own ruling working
as designed: a push in flight is green whatever its age, and a queue that never
sends leaves every item's `last_pushed_qty` matching the number the platform is
still showing. So `channel_items_attention.count` is **0** for a channel that
has completely stopped.

Deleting the per-channel row and keeping only §103's would therefore have made
**越秀's 1,683 pending Meituan pushes silent on Home** — the outage §102's
addendum found, with no successful push since 2026-08-22. Ash's reading is that
the combined row already covers every channel; the build makes that true rather
than assuming it.

### The ruling

**The stall stops being a row and becomes a named channel inside the one row.**

- The row fires when any item is wrong **or** any channel has stalled.
- **A channel says one thing about itself, worst first.** A channel that is not
  syncing at all is not also described by how many of its items have been
  caught out — the stall contains them. *"Meituan not syncing, Meituan 2"* says
  one channel twice in seven words.
- **The two counts are never summed.** They have different denominators:
  `channel_items_attention.count` counts PRODUCTS wrong,
  `channelSyncStale().waiting_count` counts (store, product) push TARGETS
  waiting. 2 + 3 = 5 would mean neither — the trap the Restock pill three rows
  up carries its own comment about. The pill shows the items count, or the
  waiting count when a channel is down and nothing is yet provably wrong: the
  same either-or as Restock's `oosc || lowc`, with the state line naming which.
- **The clock is the older of the two facts**, and so is the age the row sorts
  on — the earliest moment a customer could have started reading a wrong
  number, whichever way it went wrong.
- **The stall-only chip lands on All items, not Needs attention**, which is
  empty in exactly that case. A chip that answers the row with a blank table is
  worse than no chip.

### What is unchanged

`/dashboard/ops` still sends **both** keys, and `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` is
untouched. The merge is on the screen only: dropping the key would have taken
the stall away from the Channel sync page's channel strip as well, which is the
one place it is still said in full — *"Not syncing since 5:56 PM · 3 stock
updates waiting — the numbers Meituan shows may be wrong."* That strip is where
the chip lands, so the detail the removed row carried is one tap away.

The three channel tabs, the Channel sync page and the Products-list dots are
all untouched.

### Where the channel's name comes from

v4.229 landed on main while this was being built: it took the Products page off
its own copy of the channel names and put them behind `csChannelName` /
`csChannelGlyph` in `29-channel-sync.js`, because two copies are how two
screens drift. That reasoning applies to this row without change, so **the
desktop resolves names through `csChannelName`**, guarded by `typeof` exactly
as `09-products.js` guards its own call, and keeps a pair map only as the
fallback for a page loaded without that module.

The phone cannot reach a desktop export at all, so `m.html` keeps its own pair
map — as §103's phone row already did. The suite's parity check is what holds
the two in agreement, and it runs the fallback path on every other case.

### The two surfaces are held equal

Desktop (`03-dashboard.js`) and phone (`m.html`) carry separate copies of the
row builder — they always have — so the suite runs **both through one case
table** and asserts the resulting rows are equal, in both languages. That check
earned its keep immediately: it found a pre-existing §103 mismatch where the
desktop joined its Chinese line with an ASCII `, ` and the phone with `，`. The
desktop was corrected to the phone's.

### Chinese

**Nothing composed, nothing to declare.** `未同步` came off the row being
removed and off `29-channel-sync.js`; `渠道同步`, `查看商品` and the
`自 … 起不符` pair off §103's own row; `美团` and `饿了么` off its `CH` map. The
suite pins the **exact set** of Chinese fragments in both blocks, so a string
that is ADDED goes red rather than shipping undeclared.

### Explicitly NOT decided here

- **Whether a stalled channel should turn its items amber.** It should not, and
  §103 already ruled so; this section does not reopen it. The stall is a
  channel fact and is said as one.
- **Brick rather than Amber for a dead channel.** Carried over from §103's own
  open list unchanged — Amber still, and Brick still reserved.
- **Whether the Channel sync page should lead with the stall.** It already
  carries it on the strip above the table; no change was asked for and none was
  made.

## §105 — A FAILED PUSH SAYS WHY, BECAUSE IT ALWAYS KNEW

Asked by Ash from a live phone screenshot reading *Push failed: transient push
failure — retries exhausted*: **"the system can tell the exact reason it won't
sync so the tenant can fix it faster?"**

### What was actually wrong

Not a missing message — a **discarded** one.

- `lib/eleme-browser.js`'s `_rpc` resolves the real cause: an HTTP status, a
  fetch error, or Eleme's own error object. `_apiUpdateFoodStock` **logged it
  and dropped it one statement later.**
- `lib/meituan-browser.js`'s `_apiSetSku` captures Meituan's own
  `{status, code, msg}`, **logged `res` in full to a daemon log nobody reads**,
  and returned `{ ok, apiRejected }`.
- Seven Eleme exits and six Meituan ones returned `{ ok, transient }` while
  holding the reason in scope.

So `last_error` — the one field an operator reads — said *retries exhausted*,
which is **not a reason but a count of how many times we gave up**.
`docs/channel-mapping-findings.md` F4 had already measured that exact string
appearing 17–35 times a day, every day, for two weeks. It was the dominant
error and it said nothing.

### The ruling

**Thread the reason out; classify it once; word it in the core.**

Thirteen returns across the two browser modules gained a field. **No check, no
order of checks and no `transient` flag changed** — nothing about what either
module *does*, only about what it says when it fails.

`lib/channel-push-reason.js` turns the raw sentence into a stable code plus the
detail worth keeping. **It classifies; it does not translate**, and the split is
the point: the raw text is English from the browser layer and some of it is the
PLATFORM's own Chinese, so wording it server-side would mean either shipping
English to a Chinese operator or inventing Chinese for Meituan's own words.
`01-core.js` holds the bilingual sentence for each code, beside the rest of the
channel vocabulary (§103 step 5).

| code | what it means |
|---|---|
| `rejected` | the platform answered and refused — its own words are the detail |
| `http` | a reply we could not use; the status is the detail |
| `signed_out` | the session is gone; a person has to sign in |
| `unreachable` | no usable answer at all |
| `option_gone` | the mapping points at an option the listing no longer carries |
| `name_not_found` | the name matches nothing |
| `unreadable` | nothing to compare against, so no verdict is possible |
| `gave_up` | what every failure used to say; survives for pre-§105 rows |

**An uncategorised failure comes back `code: null` with the raw text intact.**
The failure nobody has seen before is the one most worth reading, and a
confident wrong category is worse than none — §30 rule 4's own rule for a check
that cannot run.

**Rule order is load-bearing and tested.** `cannot reach Meituan (HTTP 502)`
matches both `http` and `unreachable`; a status an operator can act on must not
be swallowed by the general case.

### The Eleme daemon's preference was the wrong way round

Meituan's daemon already read `reason || (transient ? … )` and only ever lacked
a reason to use. Eleme's read `transient ? <generic> : (reason || …)` — so a row
that failed three times **discarded whatever the browser layer had learned**.
Corrected; the two now agree. A row still retrying says why too.

### Chinese: nothing composed

`无法连接同步服务` is live whole on the Meituan tab, `已退出登录` and `重新登录`
on both channel tabs, `找不到该商品` on Eleme's, `尚未读取商品` on its store
line, `多次重试仍失败` in both daemons' own logs — and **`{平台}返回：` is the
shape WeChat's own error already uses** (`微信支付未通过校验。微信返回：`) for
precisely this job: showing a platform's sentence about its own refusal. Two
arrangements of those fragments, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`.

**Meituan's own Chinese is kept verbatim.** A tenant reads
`美团返回：商品已下架 (code 10032)` — the platform's sentence about the
platform's own refusal, which nothing we could write in its place would improve.

### The risk, named

This edits the browser-automation layer, which drives live risk-controlled
sessions. The diff is return values and comments only.

### Explicitly NOT decided here

- **Whether an operator can retry a failed push from the alarm.** §103 kept the
  page read-only and that is unchanged; a write from the alarm is its own
  decision.
- **Whether `signed_out` should raise an ops alert of its own.** It is the one
  cause no amount of retrying fixes, so it probably should; not built.

---

## §106 — THE CHANNEL SAYS WHAT IS STOPPING IT, AND THE ITEMS STOP GUESSING

Asked by Ash, reading §105's own output: **"meituan refused it and couldn't
reach it — can't the system also provide the reason?"** Three things were
proposed and all three were approved with **"ok do they"**.

### The finding that decided the shape

§105 gave every item its own failure sentence and then shipped **"Cannot reach
the sync service"** onto forty rows at once — while `meituanStoreHealth` in
`routes/meituan-admin.js`, next door, already knew it was a **captcha on 天河
since 09:14** and had been driving the Meituan tab's store lines off exactly
that for months.

**The reason was not missing. It was one function away and nobody had asked.**
That is the same shape as §105 itself (the cause computed and discarded) and as
§103 step 5 (one rule, two copies, two screens drifting apart).

### 1 · The rule moves to `lib/channel-block.js` and both callers ask it

A store is blocked when its most recent **blocking** event with `status='error'`
has not been overtaken by either a successful `stock_push` or an explicit
**clearing** event. Two ways to recover because the daemons use both: some
faults are cleared by an announcement (`verify_cleared`), others simply stop
being true and the proof is that a push landed.

**`status='error'` IS THE WHOLE TEST.** `poll_paused` is logged with status
`ok` and means "outside opening hours". Reading the event type alone turned 天河
amber the moment it shut for the night; the warning is carried over verbatim
from the route it came from, because it is the kind of thing that gets
re-broken by someone tidying.

**Copying the algorithm into `lib/channel-sync-items.js` was rejected** for the
reason §103 step 5 spent a section on: a second copy of one rule is how two
screens start disagreeing about one fact. `routes/meituan-admin.js` now
delegates and keeps its exact fields; `scripts/test_channel_block.js` runs the
tab's ORIGINAL algorithm beside the shared one over nine fixtures and demands
they agree.

**ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE, and it is a fix rather than a slip: the shared list
also blocks on `proxy_down`**, which the tab's private list omitted even though
the daemon logs it as an error reading *"proxy cannot reach Meituan — sync
paused"*. A store in that state pushes nothing and the tab called it fine. It
will now read blocked, which is a change to what an existing screen says and is
called out here and in the PR body.

### 2 · Each channel's daemon has its OWN names, and the first draft got that wrong

The descriptor was first written by giving Eleme and GZ Grocery **Meituan's**
event names. It would have reported nothing at all for Eleme, for ever, in
silence — **Eleme calls a lost session `auth_required`, not `needs_login`**, and
writes no proxy events whatever. The names are now read out of each daemon's own
`logSync` calls:

| channel | blocking | clearing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Meituan | `needs_login` `verify_required` `queue_stalled` `proxy_stale` `proxy_down` | `verify_cleared` `queue_resumed` `poll_resumed` `proxy_elected` `proxy_up` |
| Eleme | `auth_required` `verify_required` | `auth_recovered` `verify_cleared` |
| GZ Grocery | `needs_login` `proxy_down` | `needs_login` `proxy_up` |

GZ Grocery announces its recovery with **the same event type as the fault**,
status `ok` ("session recovered"), which is why `needs_login` is in both of its
lists. That is safe because clearing must be strictly LATER than the fault row:
a fault cannot clear itself, and a second fault re-blocks at its own stamp. A
test pins all three directions.

**Only faults that stop the STOCK PUSH are listed.** Meituan's `sync_stalled` is
about order READS and its `browser_down` about a process that restarts itself;
neither is a reason to tell an operator their numbers are stuck. A test reads
the daemons' source and fails if a name in the table is one nothing writes —
the guard for the mistake above, because **a wrong string in a descriptor
produces silence, not an error**.

### 3 · Worst = EARLIEST, and it is said once

`channelBlockFor` folds a channel's stores to one cause and takes the
**earliest**, not the most recent: the fault that has been stopping pushes
longest is the one nobody has looked at. It rides on the channel entry
(`blocked: { by, at, msg, store, storeName, storeNameEn }`), so it is said once
on the channel's card — never repeated down forty item rows, which is §103's
founding rule.

### 4 · An item defers to it, in one direction only

`chCauseFor` (desktop, `01-core.js`) and `csCauseFor` (phone, `m.html`) swap an
item's cause for the channel's **only** when the item's own code is one of the
generic ones — `unreachable`, `http`, `signed_out`, `gave_up`, or none at all.
A captcha on 天河 is WHY this push could not reach Meituan; "cannot reach the
sync service" beside it is the same fact, worse told.

**A stated refusal always keeps its own words.** *Meituan returned: 商品已下架
(code 8003)* is a fact about this item that no channel fault explains, and
deferring there would lose the only actionable sentence on the row. Same for
`option_gone` and `name_not_found`.

### 5 · The Meituan codes: what the evidence actually said

The third item was "map the known codes to a what-to-do line". **Every code the
tree has ever seen turned out to be handled BEFORE an operator can reach it:**

- **10002** *SET REGION QUERY ERROR* — the session lost its store binding.
  `_isBindingError` catches it, flags the binding lost, returns the row
  transient so it flushes after the next login.
- **30000** *参数异常:acctId … null* — the same lost binding, a different
  sentence. Same catcher.
- **10048** — a 套餐 combo whose component is out of stock. Meituan is right to
  refuse, so `_apiSetSku` treats it as the correct end state.

**So a what-to-do line for any of them would be a sentence no operator can
reach — dead code that reads like coverage.** What ships instead is the evidence
path: `MEITUAN_CODES` in `lib/channel-push-reason.js` records what is known and
where it is handled, `meituanCodeOf` pulls the code back out of a rejection
sentence, and **`scripts/report_reject_codes.js` counts every code the logs
actually carry and names the ones missing from the table**. The table grows when
a real code turns up, not when somebody guesses one.

**It writes nothing and needs no schema.** The codes are ALREADY recorded — the
daemon's terminal path writes the platform's own sentence to both
`meituan_sync_log.error_msg` and the queue row — so the report reads what is
there, retroactively, across every tenant database on the box. It **refuses**
(exit 2) when nothing could be read rather than printing "no unknown codes",
per §30 rule 4.

### Chinese

Nothing new is minted. `验证中心风控，同步已暂停，需要人工验证` is the Meituan
daemon's **own merchant alert, verbatim** (`scripts/meituan-daemon.js`);
`同步已停` is the Eleme tab's own fallback for a store that is not syncing;
`同步服务已退出登录…请重新登录` and `无法连接同步服务` come from §105's own
declared set; `自` is the Orders page's own "since". **One arrangement is
composed** — `无法连接同步服务。同步已暂停。`, two live sentences joined —
declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` with the candidates rejected.

### Tests

`scripts/test_channel_block.js`, new, fast shard, **40 cases**: the rule and
every recovery path; `status` as the whole test; the Meituan tab's original
algorithm run beside the shared one over nine fixtures; the one deliberate
difference asserted in both directions; each channel's own event names, with the
Eleme mistake pinned as a failing case; GZ Grocery's self-named recovery; the
descriptor's names checked against the daemons' source; earliest-wins across
stores; and **both clients' deferral rules LIFTED out of the shipped files and
run**, desktop against phone, in both languages, including that every blocking
event a descriptor can report has a sentence on both surfaces. Four more in
`scripts/test_channel_sync_items.js` (**61 total**) pin that the cause rides on
the channel rather than the items, that the Meituan route delegates, and that
all three clients defer.

### Explicitly NOT decided here

- **The Eleme tab's own `blocked` flag stays as it is.** It reads the session
  file and the shop id, not the log — a different and more direct signal for the
  question that tab asks. Folding the two is its own decision.
- **Nothing here is a write.** No retry button, no clearing a captcha from the
  page; the Channel sync page stays read-only, as §103 decided.
- **No ops alert is added** for a channel that has been blocked for hours.
  §105 left the same question open for `signed_out` and it is still open.

## §107 — THE STALL CARD NAMES BOTH ITS COUNTS

Asked by Ash, reading the phone's Channel sync screen: **"why it say 3 stock
update when can see only 2"**. The Meituan card read *3 stock updates waiting
since Sep 7*; the Needs attention list two chips below held 2 items.

### This is §104's own divergence, not a new one

§104 already ruled, from the near-identical Home screenshot, that the two
counts must never be summed: `channelSyncStale().waiting_count`
(`lib/channel-sync-stale.js`) counts **(store, product) push TARGETS** whose
latest queue row is still `pending` or `error`; `channel_items_attention.count`
(`lib/channel-sync-items.js`'s `counts[ch.key].att`) counts **PRODUCTS**,
worst-store-wins, so one product wrong at two stores is two targets and one
card. §104 settled where each number is allowed to live and that Home's pill
shows only one of them at a time. It did not reach the Channel sync page's own
stall line, which has shown only the target count since §103 — correctly, on
its own terms, and still confusing on the one page that also shows the item
count a few pixels away.

### The fix names both; it does not reconcile them

`29-channel-sync.js`'s `strip()` (desktop) and `m.html`'s new `csStaleLine`
(phone, mirroring `csBlockLine`'s shape one function above it) append the
channel's own `counts.att` to the stall sentence they already had:

> *3 stock updates waiting since Sep 7 — the numbers it shows may be wrong.
> 2 need attention.*

**Shown only when `counts.att` is nonzero.** A channel stalled entirely on
pushes still in flight — nothing yet provably wrong, §104's other case — keeps
the original sentence unchanged rather than appending *"0 need attention"*,
which would read as a claim that nothing is wrong on a card whose whole point
is that something might be.

**The server is unchanged, same as §104.** `lib/channel-sync-stale.js` and
`lib/channel-sync-items.js` are untouched; both counts already travelled to
both surfaces (`channel-sync-items.js`'s per-channel `stale` and `counts`
fields, read by both the desktop route and the phone's `loadChannelSync`).
This is a display-only join of two numbers that were both already on the wire.

### Chinese: one pair lifted whole, one arrangement composed

Desktop's added clause, `N 个待处理`, is its own live fragment three lines
below `strip()`'s stalled branch, in the non-stalled branch's own status bits
— reused verbatim, nothing new.

The phone has no such sentence to lift: its counts are chip badges
(`chipRow`), not prose, so nothing on this screen has ever said "N need
attention" as words. `N 件商品待处理` joins two fragments already live on this
exact card — `件商品` from its own "every channel is in step" sentence
(`"N 件商品。无需处理。"`) and `待处理` from the Needs attention chip (`csWord`) —
declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` with the candidates rejected,
foremost `涉及 N 件商品` (borrowed from `02-settings-ops.js`'s unrelated `N 项涉及
