资金`, and rejected for naming a relationship the sentence does not need).

### Tests

No suite pinned the literal stall-line text on either surface, so none needed
changing to accommodate the new clause: `test_channel_sync_items.js` (61
cases), `test_channel_sync_stale.js` (23 cases) and `test_channel_sync_home_row.js`
(31 cases, §104's own — a different function on both files, untouched by this
edit) all pass unchanged. `test:fast` green at 215. No schema, no migration,
no new capability, no new state, no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §108 — ONE WORD FOR ONE WAIT: A FRESH MEAL NOT YET MADE READS `NEXT BATCH` TO EVERY SHOPPER

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-12**, against §80 as shipped. Reported from the live
mini app as two screenshots of one product: the shop grid reading **NEXT BATCH**
on the Falafel Wrap, its own product page reading **PRE-ORDER**.

### How this session got it wrong twice first

Recorded because it is why the ruling had to be stated three times, and because
the second mistake is the more instructive one.

1. It read the grid as the defect and built an address-aware grid badge. Pushed,
   then reverted unmerged.
2. Told **"that's not what's happening"**, it read Ash's description of the
   intended flow as a request to *silence* the product page, and built that.
   Also reverted unmerged.

Both readings shared an assumption nobody had checked: that the split between
the two words was correct and only its application was wrong. The ruling is that
the split itself is the defect. Ash, plainly:

> *"both of them have the pre order and next batch notification. all I want is
> that they all have the same wording"*

Nobody loses a notice; the two words become one. Asked which, he chose
**`NEXT BATCH`**, and **"match both heading also"** for the checkout pop-ups.

### What was actually wrong: two rules, each defensible, guaranteed to disagree

§80 keyed the word on the shopper's **ADDRESS** — NEXT BATCH on the local run,
PRE-ORDER off it — on the PDP hero, the favourites tile and both size sheets.
The shop grid card, the web card badge and the web mobile list keyed on
**`is_batch_made`** and had never asked where anyone lived. Neither is wrong on
its own terms. Together they guarantee that a shopper outside Guangzhou sees one
word on the list and a different word on the page it opens — which is the
screenshot pair exactly.

### The ruling

**The word describes the ITEM, not the SHOPPER.** A meal the kitchen has yet to
make is `NEXT BATCH · 下批现做` to everybody.

What legitimately differs between the two customers is the **DATE**: the local
run gets the make day, a couriered order gets make day plus a transit day. A
date belongs in the checkout notice, which states it and can explain it, not in
a pill, which can do neither.

### One §80 ruling survives intact, and is not softened

**Silence still belongs to the local run alone.** A shopper on the run whose
batch is TODAY'S is waiting for nothing worth naming — the kitchen serves it
inside the window they are about to pick — so that row keeps an ordinary ADD TO
BASKET, exactly as §80 built it. An out-of-city shopper on that same morning is
still waiting on a parcel, which is why the run is half of the test.

**That is also a defect §80 left behind, now fixed.** The old `madeToday` read
`local_fresh_today` with **no run check at all**, so an out-of-city shopper on a
cooking morning got a SILENT badge above a button still reading PRE-ORDER — the
page contradicting itself, for as long as §80 has existed. `silentToday` asks
both questions.

### The button says what the badge says

On Ash's instruction — *"next batch on the button for Guangzhou customers and
outside gz customers"*. The button read `preorder` (the ship-vs-run question)
while the badge read the batch, so a Guangzhou shopper waiting on a later batch
was offered a plain ADD TO BASKET beneath a NEXT BATCH badge. Both now come off
one `preKind` (`'batch'` | `'preorder'` | `''`) and cannot drift apart.

`preorder` itself is left alone: the add toast asks the ship-vs-run question,
which is genuinely its own question, and rewording that toast would mint Chinese
(see below).

### The grocery carve-out is Ash's own

Asked directly whether sold-out grocery rows should change too, the answer was
**"leave them alone"**. Nothing is being cooked for a sold-out bag of rice, so
`NEXT BATCH` would name a thing that does not exist. Those rows keep
`PRE-ORDER · 可预订` (and, on the grid and the web card, `SHIPS SOON · 现订现发`).
The carve-out has its own case on **every** surface so a later tidy-up cannot
sweep it in by accident.

### The two checkout notices are headed alike

`computeBatchNotice` (courier) and `computeLocalFreshNotice` (the run) describe
one wait to two shoppers and were headed differently for no reason but the order
they were written in — *Freshly made · 新鲜现做* against *Next fresh batch ·
下一批现做*. Both built-in defaults are now:

> **Next fresh batch · 下一批现做** — Made fresh for you · 为您新鲜现做

The local-run title drops the date it used to carry (`Made fresh on {make_date}`).
**It is not lost**: the message below names the same day and says the run
delivers it that day, which the title never had room to explain, and it still
rides as the `make_date` field. **The operator's own copy still wins** — the
`cfg.*` overrides are untouched, and the two notices can still be set apart
deliberately by whoever wants that. `public/retail-admin.html`'s placeholder
hints are corrected to the new defaults, so the form stops advertising copy that
customers no longer receive.

`computePreorderNotice` — the grocery notice, "Pre-order / Ships soon", dateless

## §109 — AN APPROVER CAN SEE THE RECEIPT THEY ARE APPROVING

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-13**, from a live Finance → Approvals screenshot:
two waiting claims, ¥22.70 and ¥20.58, the second showing **Could not read
that photo.** where the first showed its photo. Asked what was wrong, and
told the route scopes a receipt to its own submitter — so an approver
reviewing anyone else's claim gets nothing, every time. Ash: **"make the
picture visible."**

### The route was answering a different question than the screen asks

`GET /api/retail-admin/staff-expenses/:id/receipt` (`routes/staff-expenses.js`)
matched:

```sql
SELECT receipt_data FROM staff_expenses WHERE id = ? AND submitted_by IS ?
```

bound to the CALLER's own id. That is the right query for `/mine` — a
submitter looking back at their own history should see exactly their own
receipts and nobody else's, and the route's own header comment is explicit
that the ownership test belongs IN the query rather than as a fetch-then-
compare, so no code path can be one early return away from serving anybody's
private spending. It is the wrong query for `/pending`, the approval queue,
which is gated on a completely different question — *can this operator
approve somebody else's claim* — and hands the approver the amount, the
category, the date and the claimant's own name for every waiting claim
regardless of who submitted it. The receipt was the one field on that same
row the approver could never reach. The screenshot's first claim only
"worked" because Asher had submitted it himself and was self-approving
(§87 part five allows this); the second belonged to someone else, which is
the ordinary case an approval queue exists for.

### The fix: one predicate, asked by the route that had never asked it

`requireApprover` already existed and already answers exactly this
question for `/pending` and `/decide`: the owner passes outright; anyone
else needs a resolved capability set carrying `expenses:approve`, and a
control-plane failure to resolve one fails CLOSED rather than open, because
this is a money route. It is now split into the predicate and the gate:

```js
function isApprover(req) {
  if (req.backendUser && req.backendUser.role === 'owner') return true;
  return !!(req.caps && typeof req.caps.has === 'function' && req.caps.has('expenses:approve'));
}
function requireApprover(req, res, next) {
  if (!isApprover(req)) return res.status(403).json({ error: ERR.forbidden });
  return next();
}
```

`/pending` and `/decide` are unchanged in behaviour — they still gate on
`requireApprover` exactly as before. The receipt route now asks the bare
predicate and branches its query on the answer:

```js
const row = isApprover(req)
  ? db.prepare('SELECT receipt_data FROM staff_expenses WHERE id = ?').get(req.params.id)
  : db.prepare('SELECT receipt_data FROM staff_expenses WHERE id = ? AND submitted_by IS ?')
      .get(req.params.id, req.user?.id || null);
```

**The ownership test stays in the query, exactly as the route's own comment
requires** — it is just a choice between two queries now, made by the same
fail-closed predicate `/pending` already trusts to decide who sees
everybody's spending in the first place. A non-approver — someone who holds
`expenses:submit` and nothing else — gets the untouched original query and
can still reach only their own receipts; nothing here widens what a
submitter-only account can see. **No new capability was needed or added**:
an approver already holds `expenses:approve` and already sees everything
else about a stranger's claim through `/pending`; this closes the one gap
where that same authority stopped short.

### What was deliberately left alone

The failure sentence itself — `Could not read that photo. ·
无法读取该照片。`, the phone's own wording for the same failure on the
picker that takes these photographs — is untouched. It still fires, and
correctly: a receipt genuinely missing from the row, a dropped connection,
or a stale claim id all still need to say so rather than look broken. What
changes is that it no longer fires on a case that was never actually a
failure — an approver looking at a claim they are entitled to decide.

### Chinese

Nothing composed. No string changed, no string moved between languages.

### Tests

`scripts/test_staff_expenses.js`'s existing case ("the receipt route matches
on the OWNER in the query, not after it") is extended rather than replaced:
the original submitted_by-scoped query still has to appear verbatim in the
shipped source (it is still what a non-approver's request runs), and a new
assertion pins the approver branch — the widened query, gated on the shared
`isApprover` predicate — so a later edit that quietly re-narrows the
approver's query, or forks the predicate into a second copy, goes red.
`scripts/test_finance_approvals.js` gains its own case asserting the same
from the Approvals screen's side, and its pre-existing "a receipt that
cannot be read SAYS so" case is narrowed to what is still true: the failure
sentence exists and still ships, without asserting the now-removed
`submitted_by` restriction that used to make it fire on every stranger's
claim.

`npm run test:fast` 216 passed, 0 failed (unchanged file count; both new
cases land inside existing suites). `npx eslint` 0 errors on
`routes/staff-expenses.js`, `public/retail-admin/22-finance.js`,
`scripts/test_staff_expenses.js` and `scripts/test_finance_approvals.js`.
`node scripts/check-doc-numbering.js` PASS. `node
scripts/check-swallowed-errors.js` unaffected — no catch block touched,
456/456 against the standing budget. No schema, no migration, no new route,
no new capability, no new Chinese, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §110 — REVENUE UNFOLDS ONTO THE CHANNELS BEHIND IT

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-13**, from the Finance → Summary card with the
screenshot attached: Operating expenses open onto eleven category lines under
a ¥71,109 total, and Revenue sits above them as a single ¥129,246 with nothing
behind it. **"just like the expenses can unfold and show information, revenue
should do the same, it should be able to unfold and show each revenue channel
and amount of each."**

### The breakdown is the headline's own query, and the headline is folded out of it

`routes/finance-summary.js` summed revenue once and grouped nothing:

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS revenue, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM retail_orders
 WHERE <PAID> AND <odate> BETWEEN ? AND ?
```

It now groups, and the top line is the grouped rows added up rather than a
second sum standing beside them:

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(channel, ''), 'wechat') AS channel,
       COALESCE(SUM(total), 0) AS amount, COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM retail_orders
 WHERE <PAID> AND <odate> BETWEEN ? AND ?
 GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(channel, ''), 'wechat')
 ORDER BY amount DESC
```

**This is the shape the operating-expense block in the same handler already
uses, and it is here for the reason stated there**: two queries over one set
is two places the arithmetic is done, and the day they disagree the card shows
a total its own disclosure contradicts. The rows are accumulated in MINOR UNITS
and converted once (`money.fromMinor`), never by adding REAL yuan and rounding
at the end — the residue `lib/finance-window.js`'s header records is exactly
what a running total of REALs accumulates, and here it would accumulate into a
figure the lines beneath it must equal. A case asserts the route holds **exactly
one** `SUM(total)`; a second one is the failure this shape exists to prevent.

The payload gains `revenue_breakdown`, one `{ channel, amount, orders }` per
channel, heaviest first. Nothing else about the endpoint moves.

### The channel is the order record's own column, folded the way this product folds it

`COALESCE(NULLIF(channel, ''), 'wechat')` is not invented here. It is
`/api/retail-admin/order-channel-counts`'s expression verbatim, and the Sales
summary's beside it — both in `routes/retail.js`, both reading a mini-app order
that predates the column (NULL) as the mini app.

**A *Not recorded* bucket here would have been wrong in a way the expense
breakdown's own null line is not.** That line exists because Finance stores
expense category as raw free text a human typed, so inventing a name for the
blank would put a second wrong name on a known-dirty column. `channel` is the
opposite: it is written by the checkout from a known set, every screen in this
admin that counts channels already folds the blank onto the mini app, and a
seventh bucket here would put this card at odds with the chips on the orders
list over the very same rows.

### It is deliberately NOT the Sales page's six buckets

The Sales page (`/api/retail-admin/sales/summary`) partitions differently, and
copying it would have broken the one contract this feature has:

* It splits counter sales out on `fulfillment_type='counter'`, a second
  dimension, not a channel.
* It takes gzgrocery's revenue from `retail_stock_ledger` through
  `guanyiPickupSales()`. **Finance reads neither** — that ledger fold is the
  thing §36 exists to avoid — so a borrowed gzgrocery line would not be the one
  inside the total above it.

So a till sale, written through the manual-order endpoint with
`channel='manual'`, lands on the **Manual** line here. That is what the order
record says it is. The rule is the expense breakdown's rule, applied to the
other half of the card: **group what the total summed, and do not reshape it on
the way out.**

**FLAGGED, NOT FIXED.** An operator who wants counter takings on their own line
on this card is asking for a second dimension inside a one-dimension breakdown.
That is a decision, not a tidy-up, and it is Ash's. It is not made here.

### No drill-down, and that is a decision rather than an unfinished one

The expense lines open because `GET /finance/summary/category` lists the ledger
rows behind each of them. There is no such read for a channel, and this screen's
own standing rule — stated on the expenses row and again on the purchase-order
row — is that **a chevron which opens onto nothing is a control that lies.** The
channel lines are therefore plain rows: no chevron, no focus ring, no hover
cue. If the orders behind a channel are ever wanted, they get an endpoint first
and a chevron second.

### The tax line stays outside the disclosure

`of which tax` is a sibling of the revenue row, not a line inside it, and now
renders under the channels when they are open and directly under revenue when
they are not.

Inside the disclosure it would be wrong twice: it would be a line in a list
whose whole contract is that the lines add up to the figure above them, and it
does not — it is already inside that figure — and it would close with the
disclosure, when §36 is plain that a report showing revenue without showing
this is one somebody pays their own tax out of.

### A presentation bug caught before it shipped

Built through `finRow`, the channel lines came out in `--td-text` while the
expense lines eight pixels below them sat in `--td-text2`. `finRow` stamps
`.fin-input` on every row it makes, and `#tab-finance .fin-row.fin-input
.fin-lbl` outweighs `#tab-finance .fin-breakdown .fin-lbl` on specificity — two
breakdowns on one card in two different greys, with nothing meant by the
difference. `finRevBreakdown` builds its rows inline instead, as `finBreakdown`
already builds its own, down to the empty `.fin-sign` span that holds the middle
of the three grid columns the figures line up on. A case pins it, and pins that
both selectors are still the ones that decide it.

**No new CSS.** `.fin-breakdown` and `details.fin-exp` already style exactly
this; the revenue row uses the same `<details class="fin-exp" open>` the
expenses row does, and opens by default for the same reason — the two are the
same kind of thing, and a reader who found one openable and the other not would
have to learn which is which.

### Chinese

**Nothing composed.** All seven channel names are copied live pairs, which is
the standing rule's first preference:

| key | rendered | source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wechat` | `WeChat · 微信` | `csName`, `01-core.js` |
| `web` | `Web shop · 网页商店` | `csName`, `01-core.js` |
| `meituan` | `Meituan · 美团` | `csName`, `01-core.js` |
| `eleme` | `Eleme · 饿了么` | `csName`, `01-core.js` |
| `gzgrocery` | `Gzgrocery` | `csName`, `01-core.js` |
| `manual` | `Manual · 手动` | `DASH_CHAN_SHORT`, `03-dashboard.js` |
| `shop` | `Shop · 门店` | `DASH_CHAN_SHORT`, `03-dashboard.js` |

`Gzgrocery` keeps the **bare single-language form it has at its source**: the
wholesale partner's name is the same word in both languages, which is why
`csName` carries it as a plain string rather than a pair, and pairing it with a
transliteration here would be composing one. A case re-reads both source files
and fails if any pair stops being live there, so a rename cannot leave two
different words for one channel.

**An unknown channel key renders as itself** — the same fallback `payLabel`
uses on Reports. The row is inside a total that counted it, so it has to appear;
an internal word on screen is a smaller wrong than money with no line under it.

### Tests

`scripts/test_finance_summary.js` 67 → **83 cases**, in two halves.

The query half runs the **shipped** `revGrouped` SQL, sliced out of the route,
against its own fixture — separate from §36's worked set, whose totals are
quoted in the assertions around it and which the NULL and empty-string channels
this needs would have moved. It asserts the lines sum to the headline exactly,
that the two blank spellings fold onto one WeChat line, that gzgrocery's line is
the mirror rows rather than the ledger, that an unknown key survives, that
unpaid / refunded / out-of-window orders are absent from the channels as they
are from the total, and that the heaviest channel is first.

The screen half asserts the disclosure and its channel figures, that a channel
line is not a control, the plain-row fallback on an empty or absent field, the
empty sign column, both disclosures open by default, the live-pair provenance,
and the `.fin-input` regression above.

`npm run test:fast` 216 passed, 0 failed. `npx eslint` 0 errors on the three
changed files. `node scripts/check-doc-numbering.js` PASS. Code, tests and this
record; no schema, no migration, no new route, no new capability, no new
Chinese, no CSS, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §111 — WHAT IS ORDERED FROM A SUPPLIER BELONGS ON A PURCHASE ORDER, AND A THING IN NO CATALOGUE IS STILL ORDERED

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-13), on three questions put to him after a read-only survey of how
money out reaches the books. The ask, in his own words: *"when adding to expense an order
of an ingredient, office, equipment or anything other than invoice goods to be delivered
(not salary rent or transportation for example) it need to be part of the PO like any
other stuff that ordered (unless the user specifically say it's not)"*.

Three answers, of the options put to him:

* **THE RULE IS LEARNED FROM THE ANSWER, NOT CONFIGURED AND NOT ASSUMED.** The expense form
  asks on the first money-out row in each category, stores the answer **on that category**
  beside `is_operating` and `is_active`, and never asks for that category again.
* **A YES OPENS THE DRAFT.** No ledger row is written; a Draft PO is seeded from what was
  typed and the Purchasing wizard opens on it, so the buyer finishes the order rather than
  filing a draft nobody returns to.
* **THE FREE-TEXT LINE SHIPS FIRST, ALONE.** Nothing else in this section can be obeyed
  until a purchase order can carry an office chair.

### The finding this rests on, and it is most of the work

**FOUR WRITERS REACH `expense_entries`, AND ONLY TWO OF THEM ARE A PURCHASE ORDER.**
`postRetailPOExpenses` (`routes/retail-purchasing.js`) and its kitchen twin
`postPOExpenses` (`routes/purchases.js`) post from a document. `postClaim`
(`lib/expense-posting.js`) posts an approved staff claim, §87's path. And
`routes/finance-transactions.js` inserts a row somebody typed, with **no supplier, no
lines, no receiving, no 发票 to match and nothing to return it against.** That fourth
writer is the door this section is about.

**THE RULE COULD NOT BE OBEYED, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS BEING BROKEN.** `po_line_items` has
accepted a line naming neither a product nor a material since it was written —
`lineConflict` refuses a line carrying BOTH ids, never one carrying neither; the stock
apply skips it; the price write-back skips it; the expense poster groups it by its own
`expense_category` like any other line. **Nothing could produce one.** The wizard's only
way onto an order was a picker over `store_products` and `ingredients`, and a search that
matched nothing ended at *No match*. So a buyer who wanted to do the right thing with a box
of gloves had nowhere to put it, and Finance was the only screen that would take it.

**THE TWO DOORS ALREADY SHARE ONE VOCABULARY**, which is what makes the rest of this
possible rather than a second system beside the first: a PO line's `expense_category` and a
typed row's `category` both go through `storeCategory(db, …, 'accounting')`, onto the same
tenant list §87 part two created. The category is the join between what somebody is typing
and what a PO line would post.

### PART ONE — THE FREE-TEXT LINE (built 2026-09-13)

**A LINE THAT NAMES NEITHER CATALOGUE, TYPED IN THE PICKER.** The picker's last row now
offers to order what was typed; taking it adds a line carrying its own name, unit, price and
**expense category**, and no id. It is the last row and never the first — a buyer searching
"chair" wants the chair they already stock if there is one, and offering to invent a second
one above it is how a catalogue grows duplicates. *No match* still says so when nothing
matched.

**IT JOINS NO CATALOGUE, DELIBERATELY.** An id is what makes a line move stock or write a
price back. This line carries neither, so it does exactly one thing: it puts a named cost on
an order that can be sent to a supplier, received, matched against a 发票 and posted to the
books. Making a `store_products` record for an office chair to get the same effect would
leave a chair on the shelf report forever.

**THE CATEGORY IS THE POINT OF IT.** A product line defaults to `门店进货 Retail stock` and a
material line takes `ingredients.accounting_category`; a typed line has no master record to
take one from, so the buyer picks from the tenant's own list. Left blank it falls to the
poster's `COALESCE` default — stated here rather than discovered later: that is right for a
shelf and wrong for a chair, and a buyer who skips the field is still no worse off than the
Finance row this replaces.

**THE NAME IS REFUSED WHEN IT IS ABSENT.** `po_line_items.name_en` is NOT NULL and
`insertLineItems` satisfied that with `item.name_en || ''`, so a blank line would have saved
and then appeared on the order, on the receive screen and on the printed sheet as a quantity
and a price with no subject. `lineUnnamed` refuses it on create and on edit alike, as
`name_required` — a code `01-core.js` already renders bilingually. **A CATALOGUE LINE IS NOT
HELD TO THIS**: its name comes off its master record, and a product whose own name is blank
is that record's problem rather than something to refuse a purchase order over.

**THE UNIT IS EDITABLE HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE.** Nothing but the buyer knows whether the
gloves are bought by the box or the pair. A MATERIAL line's unit stays `ingredients.buy_unit`
and does not become editable alongside it: `firePriceAlertsForPO` refuses to write back a
price whose line unit does not match, so an editable unit there would silently kill the price
history §86 part four rests on.

### PART TWO — THE QUESTION ON THE EXPENSE FORM (built 2026-09-13)

On money out, one question before the row is saved: **was this ordered from a supplier?**
*Put it on a purchase order* opens the wizard on a new order carrying the cost as a typed
line; *Record it as an expense* writes the typed row exactly as today. **The answer is stored
on the CATEGORY** — `categories.needs_po`, beside the `is_operating` and `is_active` §87 put
there — so rent is asked about once, ever, and ingredients are asked about once, ever.

**NOTHING IS PRE-MARKED, AND THAT IS §36's RULE HOLDING.** "An empty list cannot offer a
wrong option" was written after a dropdown of four inherited kitchen categories produced the
¥152,309 mis-filing. A shipped goods/not-goods default would be that dropdown again, one
field further in: mark the list wrong and the app nags about rent every month or waves an
ingredient order through in silence. Learning the flag from the answer has no wrong default
to ship, and Settings can still flip it where `is_operating` already lives.

**THE COLUMN CARRIES NO DEFAULT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MECHANISM.** NULL is *nobody has been
asked*, 1 is *ordered*, 0 is *not ordered*. A `DEFAULT 0` would ship every category
pre-answered "no", the question would never be put, and the feature would be dead on arrival
with nothing on any screen to say so. The ledger payload therefore carries `category_needs_po`
as a map of the ANSWERED ones only: absence is the third state, and sending a 0 for the
unasked would be the same default wearing a different hat.

**DISMISSING THE QUESTION DOES NOTHING AT ALL** — no row, no wizard, nothing remembered, and
the form still open with every value in it. That is why it is `askChoice` and not a
two-button confirm: on a confirm, Escape and the scrim land on whichever answer sits in the
cancel slot, so "I pressed Escape" would either write a row nobody committed to or throw the
operator into another tab.

**NOTHING IS WRITTEN ON THE WAY TO PURCHASING — not even a draft.** Finance's form has no
supplier field and no store field (§36: the ledger has no location column, so the form never
grew one), and the create route requires a store. So the wizard opens on **step one**, where
those are the questions, with the part Finance already knew filled in. If the person walks
away, nothing was recorded in either place — the same as abandoning the Finance form itself,
and better than an orphan draft nobody returns to.

**THE AMOUNT ARRIVES AS ONE UNIT AT THAT PRICE.** Finance records a sum and has no quantity
field, so one at ¥680 is the only reading of ¥680 that cannot be wrong. The buyer splits it
into real quantities on the next step.

**A CATEGORY IS NEVER CREATED BY ANSWERING.** The answer endpoint takes a NAME — that is all
the form holds at the moment it is answered — snaps it through `storeCategory` so a typed
spelling lands on the listed row, and is a **no-op** when the tenant's list does not hold it.
§36 ships that list empty and the tenant decides what goes on it; a form that grew it from
whatever was typed would rebuild the list out of typos, which is the failure the list exists
to end. The person still gets the answer they gave for that row; it is simply not remembered.

**AND THE MONEY NEVER DEPENDS ON THE PREFERENCE.** A failure to store the answer is swallowed:
the row is still written, and the only cost is being asked again. An expense that could not be
recorded because a flag could not be saved would be this feature doing harm.

**IT DOES NOT ASK ON AN EDIT, OR ON MONEY IN.** §111 is about the moment money is recorded; a
row already in the books is a different question — converting one would mean deleting it and
raising an order in its place — and nothing asks for that. There is no such thing as ordering
revenue.

### PART THREE — STAFF CLAIMS KEEP THEIR OWN DOOR

§87 is explicit that a claim is money **already out of a pocket**. There is nothing to order
and nothing to receive: a cook buying ginger at the market made a spot purchase, not an
order, and routing it through Purchasing would invert the workflow §87 built. The claim path
is untouched here. If the day comes that it needs covering, the honest shape is attaching an
approved claim to an **existing** PO, and that is its own decision.

### THE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE THIS ACCEPTS, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED

**A typed row is in the books the moment it is saved; a purchase order posts nothing until
somebody presses Order** — `postRetailPOExpenses` is postable on `['Ordered','Delivered']`
and wipes its rows when the PO drops back to Requested. So routing a purchase into a draft
moves that money out of the month's figures until the buyer places it. That is correct, and
it is also how a cost goes quietly missing, which is the whole reason Part Two opens the
draft instead of filing it: the person who typed the cost is standing in front of the order
that replaced it. Posting early to keep the figure would put money in the books that nobody
has committed to spend, and that is worse.

### THE CAPABILITY THAT MAKES THIS A NUDGE AND NEVER A REFUSAL

Typing a ledger row is `finance:record`; creating a purchase order is `purchasing:edit`.
**A bookkeeper may hold the first and not the second.** A hard block on typing a goods
expense would strand them with a cost in hand, no route to record it, and nothing on screen
explaining why — the exact failure §36 names when it refuses to gate the add control. Hence
Ash's own *"unless the user specifically say it's not"*: the question always has a second
answer, and taking it is never punished.

### Rejected

**A HARD REFUSAL ON THE EXPENSE FORM.** See the capability note above, and §36's rule about
controls that vanish without saying why.

**A SEEDED "GOODS" FLAG ON THE CATEGORY LIST.** Considered because it is the obvious shape
and needs no prompting at all. Refused twice over: shipped ON it nags every rent payment
until somebody configures it, shipped OFF it never fires and the rule quietly does not exist,
and either way it is a list that offers a wrong option before anybody has answered anything.

**CREATING A CATALOGUE RECORD FOR THE TYPED ITEM.** A desk chair in `store_products` is a
desk chair on the shelf report, in the low-stock suggestions and in every channel sync that
reads the catalogue. The line exists precisely so that a one-off purchase does not have to
become a permanent product.

**MERGING TYPED LINES THAT READ ALIKE.** Two products with one id are one line by
definition; two typed lines reading "Repair" are two repairs, and folding them would silently
lose one of the two prices.

### What this does NOT decide

**Whether an approved staff claim can be attached to an existing purchase order.** Part
three's note is the shape it would take, not a ruling that it will be built.

**What happens to a draft nobody goes back to.** Part two lands the buyer in the draft, which
is the answer for the moment it is created. A draft ageing surface is a Purchasing question
and nothing yet asks for one.

**Whether equipment is an operating expense at all.** `categories.is_operating` already
carries that answer per category and it is the tenant's to give.

### Tests

`scripts/test_retail_po_typed_line.js`, **33 cases**, the sibling of
`test_retail_po_material_line.js` and on its harness: the real retail router,
`routes/purchases.js` real, `lib/inventory.js` stubbed but RECORDING — "a typed line never
touches stock" is a claim about a call that must NOT happen, and an absence is only provable
against a record of what did.

It asserts that a PO accepts a line naming neither catalogue and keeps its two name halves
apart; that a nameless one is refused `name_required` with nothing written, that a name of
spaces is refused too, and that a **product** line with a blank name is still accepted; that
the same refusal guards an edit and leaves the stored line untouched; that placing the order
posts the line under **its own** category rather than `门店进货 Retail stock`, and that a
blank category falls to that default; that receiving records the arrival and calls
`adjustStock` never; and that a product line on the same order still moves stock, because the
skip is per LINE.

**IT PASSES 25 OF ITS 33 CASES AGAINST THE CODE BEFORE THIS CHANGE, and that is the finding
rather than a weak suite**: everything but the name guard was already true of
`po_line_items`. What was missing was never the storage.

`scripts/test_wizard_typed_line.js`, **31 cases**, is the half the server suite cannot see —
the door itself. On `test_wizard_line_supplier.js`'s VM sandbox, reading the HTML back out of
the DOM stub rather than asserting against what we meant to render: that the picker offers
the row and offers it LAST, that taking it builds a line with no ids and the name split into
halves, that a typed line gets the three fields only it may have while a product line and a
material line get none of them, that the category menu is the tenant's own list, and that a
pick LANDS ON THE LINE — an input's value set from script leaves its dirty flag clear, so
without `commit` the pick would sit on screen and die at the next repaint. It cannot even
load against the old code: `puPickTyped` does not exist there.

`scripts/test_finance_po_question.js`, **31 cases**, is part two's server half: both finance
routers mounted for real against a fixture database. A fresh category has no answer and is
absent from the payload map; answering records it and the payload then says so; "not ordered"
records as a 0 that is PRESENT, which is what stops the asking; a name the list does not hold
is a no-op that creates nothing; a spacing-different spelling snaps onto the listed row; the
answer can be taken back to *not asked*, which is the way out of a mistake; a rename leaves it
alone; a hidden category leaves the map with the list; and none of it touches the ledger row.

`scripts/test_finance_po_question_client.js`, **41 cases**, is when the question is put and
what each answer does — including the one that is not an answer. Dismissal writes no row,
opens no wizard, remembers nothing and leaves the form open with what was typed still in it.
An already-answered category is not asked twice in either direction; money in and an edit are
never asked; an uncategorised row is still asked and its answer honoured, with nothing
recorded because there is nothing to record it on; a failure to store the answer still writes
the money; and if Purchasing cannot be opened at all the row is written after all, because the
"purchase order" answer is the one path that writes nothing and a half-working jump would close
the form on a cost that then existed nowhere.

`npm run test:fast` 221 passed, 0 failed. **Part one added no new Chinese**: every label
reuses a live pair — `添加`, `无匹配`, `名称`, `分类`, `采购单位`, and `name_required`'s own
sentence from `01-core.js`. **Part two composes six strings and declares all six** in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.70, with the live pair each Chinese term was lifted
from and the four candidates rejected. One migration (`categories.needs_po`, nullable, no
default), one new route (`PUT /finance/categories/answer`), no new capability, and no change
to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §112 — PERMISSIONS ARE MANAGED FROM THE PHONE, BECAUSE THE SHOP IS RUN FROM THE PHONE

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-13**, against the phone build: **"can't manage
permission from the mobile version, fix it fully. this feature should be fully
functional from mobile."**

**This section takes §112 and not §111 deliberately.** A concurrent session was
holding §111 when this was written, and the numbering rule at the head of this
file makes a number a citation target: a gap costs nothing, a collision costs a
reference that no longer resolves. It landed while this was being built — §111
above, merged as PR #550 — so the two sit in order and neither had to move.

### What was there, and why it was a decision rather than an omission

`docs/tacet-mobile-parity.md` ruled Team out in its own words: *"Inviting
somebody, assigning a role and setting a per-capability permission matrix is
authoring and stays on the desktop. What the phone gets is the other half —
WHO HAS ACCESS, and switching one of them off in a hurry."* The phone shipped
exactly that: a roster, a deactivate confirm, and three sentences pointing at a
laptop — *"Inviting someone, and what each role reaches, are set on desktop —
Settings → Team → Roles."*

The rule that produced it is still the right rule for a product with options
and variants in it: authoring belongs to a keyboard. **What it got wrong is
that permissions are not authoring.** Nobody writes a role the way they write a
product description. The acts are: somebody starts on Monday, somebody moves
from the counter to the kitchen, somebody needs to refund a customer standing
in front of them, somebody is given the books by mistake and must not have
them. Every one of those happens IN the shop, on the day, and the answer
"find a laptop" is a shop that stops while an owner walks to an office.

### The whole desktop tab is on the phone, in the shapes a phone has

Both of the desktop's tabs, all four of its write surfaces, and the same routes:

| Desktop (`02-settings-ops.js`) | Phone (`public/m.html`) | Route |
|---|---|---|
| People roster | `screenTeam` → People tab | `GET /api/backend/team` |
| Invite form + credential box | `teaminvite` | `POST /api/backend/team` |
| Edit modal (name · role · store · active) | `teamperson` | `PUT /api/backend/team/:id`, `POST …/password` |
| Per-person matrix + store scope | `teamperms` | `GET`/`PUT /api/backend/team/:id/permissions` |
| Roles pane (create · edit · delete) | Roles tab → `teamrole` | `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/backend/roles` |
| Enforcement switch | People tab, owner only | `PUT /api/backend/rbac-enforce` |

**Not a port of the markup — a port of the decisions.** The desktop's pane
prints a hundred-odd checkboxes into a scroller beside a role list; a phone
doing that is a column of toggles with no way to see where you are. So the
capability tree opens ONE GROUP AT A TIME, and the collapsed row states the
same sentence the desktop's collapsed group states — *"Run the shop · 18 of 30
on"*. A role is not a pane beside a list, it is a screen the list pushes to. A
person's role is not a `<select>` in a modal, it is a picker sheet, and picking
IS the act, so there is no second Save tap for a single field.

**Three things stay word for word, because they are the product's own
reasoning and not layout**: the blast radius above anything editable (*"2 people
hold this role. Every change here reaches them on their next screen."*), the
signed exception marks (`Added` / `Removed`, never one tint for both — the fact
an exception exists is not the fact of which way it goes), and the Quick Stock
lockdown's one precondition, said on the switch rather than discovered as a
refused save.

### The rules did not move, and the phone states three of them early

Every refusal in `routes/backend-team.js` is still the server's, and each is
rendered in the server's own bilingual words rather than a generic failure:
you cannot deactivate yourself, you cannot leave the shop with no active owner,
you cannot edit your own permissions, you cannot grant a role or a capability
you do not hold, and the owner is always everything. The first three are
**stated on the row before the tap** — a lock nobody can explain reads as a
bug, and a switch that springs back has told the operator nothing.

**Writing this surfaced a real gap of the same class the roster had in
2026-08.** `teamToggle` was once guarded only by not *drawing* the control,
which `APP.cmd` walks straight past; that was fixed then. `teamEnforce` — new
here — was written with the same hole and caught by its own probe before it
shipped: the renderer draws the switch for the owner alone, and the handler now
checks the roster's `isSelf` row too.

### The two capabilities are kept apart, because the server keeps them apart

`team:manage` adds a person, renames them, moves their role and store, resets a
password, switches them off. `team:permissions` decides what a person or a role
REACHES. An operator holding the first and not the second gets every control of
the first and no door to the second — absent, never disabled, the rule
`applyCapGates` keeps on the desktop — with one line saying which permission is
missing. `team:view` alone reads the roster and is offered nothing.

### The dashboard-default table now has a guard instead of a promise

Seeding the dashboard-card ticks for a role with no override needs the table of
what each board shows today, which lives in `retail-admin.css` and is mirrored
by hand in `RL_DASH_LAYOUT_DEFAULT`. The phone needs the same five rows, and a
third hand-kept copy is a copy that drifts — an owner ticking on a phone would
save a different board than the same tap on a desktop, silently.
`scripts/test_mobile_permissions.js` reads both files and fails the build if
they disagree. The desktop's copy has never had that.

### What is NOT on the phone, and why

**Team devices** — every operator's signed-in sessions across the tenant, with
per-row sign-out — is a separate desktop card reading `/api/backend/sessions/*`
and is left where it is. It answers a different question (which glass is signed
in) from the one this section is about (who may do what), and nothing in Ash's
brief asks for it. Recorded here as a deliberate absence rather than an
oversight, so the next pass does not have to rediscover it.

### What holds it

`scripts/test_mobile_permissions.js` — 90 assertions across 30 cases, over the
real routes' request bodies: the role write carries the role, a store-pinned
role asks for its store in the same breath rather than meeting the route's 400
afterwards, the matrix save carries the whole on-list plus the scope it was
read with, a role delete carries its destination, a new role posts `caps:[]`,
and an operator without each capability is offered nothing AND gets nothing
when the command is called directly. `scripts/test_mobile_team.js` keeps the
roster and the emergency switch. The sweep renders all four new screens warm,
cold and in Chinese.


## §113 — THE KEYBOARD GOES DOWN, ON EVERY FIELD, WITHOUT ANYBODY HAVING REMEMBERED THAT FIELD

**Reported by Ash, 2026-09-13**, with two photographs of the phone app and four
words: ***"keyboard doesn't go down."*** One is the expense claim, note field
holding `knifes`, the soft keyboard sitting across the bottom of the screen with
**Submit** behind its top edge. The other is Settings → Team → **Add someone**
with a password typed in, the keyboard covering the Role picker and **Add them**
below it. Two unrelated screens, one defect.

### A keyboard follows focus, and the app gave a field no way to lose it

`public/m.html` has **no `<form>` element anywhere in it** — every screen is
markup plus `oninput` handlers — so the keyboard's action key had nothing to
submit. With no `enterkeyhint` on the field, Gboard draws that key as **Go**
(前往 in the screenshot), and Go on a formless page does nothing at all. Nor
does anything else on the screen put the keyboard away: a tap on a heading, a
caption or the space between two fields leaves focus exactly where it was.

**The fields that DID close cleanly are the six that were rescued one at a
time.** `mExpAmt` carries `enterkeyhint="done"` and an `onkeydown` that blurs —
and it sits **two rows above** the note field in the same form, which has
neither. `mProdQ`, `mMbQ`, `qsnum-*`, `mbnum-*` and the ask sheet's input have
the same hand-written pair. Six rescues on a file with **fifty inputs** is the
shape of a rule that was never made: every field added since has been one more
field you cannot get out of, and nothing said so.

### The rule: three passes, and not one of them is a list of field ids

Under **PUTTING THE KEYBOARD AWAY** in `public/m.html`, beside the scrim
gesture rule it borrows its timing from. The reasoning for having no list is
the one `mTyping()` already carries: this app draws fields in sheets, in forms
and in pickers, and a list of ids would be one field out of date the day the
next one lands.

1. **Every typed field asks for a Done key.** `kbHints()` writes
   `enterkeyhint="done"` onto the inputs that do not declare one, on the paint
   that drew them — so a field added next year is covered without anybody
   remembering. Android closes the keyboard on Done by itself; iOS gives a
   Return that rule 2 finishes. A field that already says what its key is (the
   search boxes, `enterkeyhint="search"`) keeps it, and anything whose keyboard
   is not one — a date, a file, a checkbox — is left alone.
2. **Enter blurs**, delegated once. The six hand-rolled fields keep working;
   every other field gains it. A `<textarea>` is excluded, because Enter there
   is a new line, which is the whole reason it is a textarea. **And it is deaf
   during composition** — `isComposing`, or the `keyCode 229` spelling of the
   same thing, is a Chinese operator mid-pinyin pressing Enter to choose a
   candidate, and blurring there would take the word away instead of the
   keyboard.
3. **A tap on the page puts it down**, judged at `click` and never at
   touch-down. The scrim rule directly above it records what a decision taken
   at touch-down costs: *"the keyboard closing as the input blurs … reflows the
   page under a finger already in motion"*, and the lift lands where nobody
   aimed. By `click` the tap has been resolved and the control's own handler
   has already run, so blurring can take nothing away. It also stays out of the
   browser's way — where the tap moved focus itself, to another field or
   through a `<label>` to one, the field it would blur is no longer the focused
   one and the rule does nothing. A scroll fires no click, so a list dragged
   with the keyboard up keeps it.

### What this is not

**It is not an autofocus policy.** Nothing here opens a keyboard; all three
passes only ever close one. The one screen that deliberately opens with the
keyboard up (`mSearch`, `autofocus`) is untouched, as is the add-stock ruling
that put a caret in a cell on one tap.

**And no field's markup changed.** Four functions and two listeners were added;
not one `<input>` in the file was edited, which is what makes this a rule rather
than a fifty-first rescue.

### What holds it

`scripts/test_mobile_keyboard.js` — **47 assertions across 6 cases**, with the
four functions sliced out of the shipped `public/m.html` and driven against a
hand-built DOM, the technique `scripts/test_ask_to_buy_keyboard.js` uses on the
same file. It fails if Enter starts eating pinyin candidates, if a tap starts
closing the keyboard a `<label>` had just opened, if a textarea is handed a Done
key, if the tap rule is ever moved to `pointerdown`/`touchstart`, or if
`render()` stops asking for the hints. In the fast shard: no browser, 0.1s. The
sweep (`scripts/test_mobile_screens.js`) re-renders all 147 screens warm, cold
and in Chinese with the pass running on every paint — 441 renders, no uncaught
errors.
## §114 — A PURCHASE THAT HAS NOT ARRIVED IS TRACKED AS AN ORDER, WHOEVER PAID FOR IT

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-13), on a case that breaks §111 part three: *"an employee use the
company money to buy a food processor. it wasn't the person that do purchasing. here is an
example why need a direct PO access for it. the item didn't arrive and it need tracking"*.

Two answers, of the options put to him:

* **THE APPROVER RAISES THE ORDER, FROM THE CLAIM.** The employee records what they bought
  and says it has not arrived; approving raises an **Ordered** purchase order that owns the
  money, instead of the claim posting its own ledger row. **Nobody gains a capability.**
* **IT APPLIES TO THEIR OWN MONEY TOO.** The order tracks the delivery and owns the expense;
  the debt to the employee stays on the claim, so they are still paid back. Two facts about
  one purchase, kept apart.

### What §111 part three got wrong, stated plainly

§111 part three left claims alone on the reasoning that a claim is *money already out of a
pocket — there is nothing to order and nothing to receive*. **That is true of a cook buying
ginger at the market, which is the case it was written against, and false of anything bought
that has not arrived yet.** Ash's example is the ordinary shape of the second: an appliance,
paid for on the company card by somebody who is not the buyer, still in transit. **The money
is gone AND the goods are owed**, and neither door held it — the claim path has no delivery
to track, and the order path sits behind `purchasing:edit`, which the floor presets withhold
on purpose (`store_manager`'s own comment: *"Store managers receive inbound stock but don't
create POs or edit suppliers"*).

### The three findings that made this cheap

**RECEIVING IS ALREADY IN THAT PERSON'S HANDS.** `store_manager` holds `purchasing:view` and
`purchasing:receive`. What was missing was never the tracking — it was the CREATION. So this
section grants no new key to anybody, and the person who bought the thing can tick it in
himself when it lands.

**"PAID, NOT YET ARRIVED" IS A STATE THE ORDER RECORD ALREADY HAS.**
`postRetailPOExpenses` posts on `Ordered`; `Delivered` is what seeds `qty_received` and moves
stock. **An Ordered purchase order IS a purchase whose money has gone and whose goods are
outstanding.** No new status and no new concept — which is also why the order is raised at
Ordered and never as a draft: a draft posts nothing, and the money has already left the
account.

**AND §111 PART ONE IS WHAT CARRIES IT.** A food processor is in no catalogue. Before the
typed line existed this section could not have been built at all.

### PART ONE — THE EMPLOYEE ANSWERS IT; THE APPROVAL RAISES THE ORDER

One more answer on the claim form: **this has not arrived yet**. It is a single opt-in, not a
pair of chips, because the overwhelming case is goods in hand and the unticked state is
exactly today's behaviour — an opt-in cannot make an existing claim mean something new.

**THE EMPLOYEE ANSWERS, THE APPROVER ACTS.** Only the person who bought it knows whether it
turned up; only the approver may let money into the books. §87's split is unchanged and this
rides on it rather than beside it.

### PART TWO — THE MONEY IS POSTED ONCE, AND THE ORDER OWNS IT

A claim posts one row keyed on `claim_id`; an order posts rows keyed on `po_id`. **A purchase
that went through both would be in the books twice**, so exactly one of them posts:
`postClaim` writes nothing for a claim carrying a `po_id`, and the order's own poster carries
the cost — under the category the employee chose, on the claim's own date.

**THE LINK IS `staff_expenses.po_id`, AND IT IS ALSO THE IDEMPOTENCE.** Approving a claim
that already carries one raises no second order.

### PART THREE — OWN MONEY IS STILL OWED, AND THAT COSTS NOTHING

Verified rather than assumed: the owed figure reads
`status = 'approved' AND paid_by = 'employee' AND COALESCE(settled,0) = 0`
(`routes/staff-expenses.js`) and **never looks at `expense_id`**. So a claim whose money
posted through an order still stands under *Owed to your team · 应付团队*, and **Mark paid ·
标记已付** still settles it — posting nothing, exactly as §87 decided, because the money was
recorded once already.

### PART FOUR — ONCE AN ORDER STANDS, THE CLAIM IS NOT REVERSED FROM THE CLAIM

Rejecting or voiding an approved claim removes its ledger row (§87, §90). **A claim that
raised an order has no ledger row of its own to remove**, and quietly cancelling the purchase
order instead would reach into a document that may already have been received, priced and
part-delivered. So both are refused while an order stands, and the refusal names the way out:
**Cancel order**, Purchasing's own reversible exit, which keeps the row and zeroes it.

### PART FIVE — A DELIVERY NEEDS SOMEWHERE TO ARRIVE

`staff_expenses.store_id` is nullable and §87 part three gives NULL a meaning: the cost
belongs to the business rather than to any one place. **Goods do not have that luxury** — they
turn up at a door, and the receive path needs the shelf. So a claim marked *not arrived* must
name a store, and the form asks for one. A tenant with a single store never sees the question.

### Rejected

**A NEW CAPABILITY FOR THE EMPLOYEE** — `purchasing:record-own` or similar. Put to Ash and not
taken. It would be a second key meaning *may create a purchase order*, sitting beside the one
that already means that, and the two would have to be kept in agreement forever. The approval
already carries the authority; nothing needed inventing.

**THE EMPLOYEE RAISING THE ORDER DIRECTLY.** Same reason, plus: the buyer's screen shows
supplier prices, which is a `money: 'shows'` grant the floor presets withhold.

**LEAVING OWN MONEY OUT, for now.** Considered as the narrower build. Refused because it
leaves the identical gap one case over — a cook who pays for a mixer out of pocket because the
card is upstairs — and that is exactly how this gap was found.

**CANCELLING THE ORDER AUTOMATICALLY WHEN A CLAIM IS REJECTED.** See part four.

### What this does NOT decide

**The supplier on the order.** Left blank: the employee may not know what the shop is called,
and the buyer fills it in. Nothing here guesses one.

### Tests

`scripts/test_claim_purchase_order.js`, **47 cases**, both routers real against a fixture with
`lib/inventory.js` stubbed but RECORDING — a typed line must never move stock, and an absence
is only provable against a record of what did. It runs Ash's own case: a ¥1,280 food processor,
company money, not arrived. It asserts that the claim is refused without a shop and without a
description; that approving raises an **Ordered** retail order with one typed line carrying the
name, the whole amount at quantity one and the employee's category, and no invented supplier;
that **the money is in the books once and the order owns it** — nothing keyed on the claim, one
row keyed on the order; that approving twice raises one order; that an ordinary claim is
untouched and still posts its own row; that an own-money purchase is still owed and **Mark
paid** still settles it while posting nothing; that reject and void are refused while the order
stands and the refusal names the way out; and that receiving the delivery records the arrival
and moves no stock.

`scripts/test_staff_expenses.js` 75 → **82 cases**. Its file-wide *one table, and it is the
claim table* guard is **narrowed rather than dropped**: the allowed set is named, the two new
tables are pinned to `raiseOrderForClaim`, and a new case proves the SUBMIT path writes the
claim and nothing else and reaches none of the things a decision does — which is the assertion
that actually carries §87 part one, and which the file-wide regex only ever implied. The screen
half asserts the opt-in exists once with no opposite command, that the answer reaches the
server, that both local refusals match the server's, that the flag does not survive onto the
next claim, and that the approver is told before deciding and can reach the order after.

A further case re-reads every source the three composed strings were lifted from and fails if
any of them stops being live, so a rename elsewhere cannot quietly orphan them.

**Whether a 发票 is expected.** The order carries the existing invoice fields and nothing here
sets them; a purchase made in a shop by an employee is exactly the case
`no_invoice_expected` was built for, and marking it stays the buyer's call.

**What the buyer is told when an approval raises an order.** It appears in the purchasing list
like any other Ordered PO. §66 and §69 are the precedent for adding a notification later if
the day turns out to need one; inventing it now would be inventing the workflow.

## §115 — TWO WAYS OFF A KITCHEN JOB, AND NEITHER ONE NAMES THE SCREEN IT IS ALREADY ON

**Reported by Ash, 2026-09-13**, against a photograph of the Kitchen queue with
`PR-260913-001` open: ***"kit jen quote button is not clear."*** The button is
the chip directly under the title, and it read **Kitchen queue** — the same two
words as the `<h1>` six pixels above it. It is a label, or a tab, or the name of
the screen you are standing on. It is in fact the only door back to the list.

### Why a door was drawn as a label

The order detail is a STATE of the queue screen (`state.kq.orderId`), not a
route of its own, so the pushed stack knows nothing about it and the head's own
Back leaves for **More**. The chip was added to cover that, and it inherited the
screen's name because that is where it goes — which is exactly what makes it
unreadable as a control: nothing on it says back. No chevron, no verb, and a
destination it shares with the heading above it.

### The rule: a control is named for where it goes, and no two of them go to the same place

Three things on an open job, three answers:

1. **The title is the job.** `titleOf` on `SUBS.kitchenqueue` returns the
   request's own number — the list keeps the screen's name, an open job takes
   the number's. With it, `status` carries the day · lines · purpose line and
   `cta` carries **Reprint**: the three hooks `pageHead` has always offered,
   wired the way `SUBS.receivexfer` already wires them for a PO. So the body of
   an open job is its lines and nothing else, and the first thing to make is the
   first thing on the glass.
2. **The head's Back keeps saying More**, and keeps meaning it: out of the
   kitchen's tool, to the menu it was opened from. No `backLabel`. This was
   Ash's call over the alternative — a head reading `‹ Kitchen queue` with the
   number as title — and it is the better one: it leaves the app's global `back`
   command untouched, and it keeps a one-tap exit from the tool.
3. **The way back to the LIST is a bar at the foot of the job** (`kqBackBar`),
   because that is where the hand is. The operator works DOWN the lines and
   closes the last one at the bottom of the list; top-left is then the furthest
   point on the glass from the thumb that has just tapped. It carries what is
   waiting back there — this job excluded, and only on `active`, where waiting
   means something. A numeral needs no label beside the name of the list it
   counts, which is how Receiving's own segments already say it
   (*To receive 4*). The price is ~56px of every job screen; it was drawn at
   size and accepted before it was built.

### And the phone's own Back was going somewhere else entirely

Found while checking whether the split could work, and shipped with it because
the two must never disagree: `layers()` — the list that keeps the history stack
as deep as the app's own layers, so an Android edge swipe closes a layer instead
of the app — covered orders, customers, products, POs and every sheet, but **not
an open kitchen job**. A swipe threw the whole screen away and landed on More,
straight past the list. It is one line, and `kqDropOrder` is now the single
function both it and the bar call, so the gesture and the button cannot drift.

**`Ready from the kitchen` has the identical shape and the identical gap** —
`state.kr.orderId` is not a layer either. It is left alone here on purpose: that
screen's own way out is a different control that this decision has not looked
at, and fixing half of it silently is how the next session inherits a screen
whose gesture and button disagree.

### No Chinese was composed

`厨房制作队列`, `重打`, `项` and the purpose words are all live pairs already on
this screen; the count is a numeral. The one candidate that would have needed a
new string — *Kitchen queue · 3 more to make* — was restructured into the name
plus a numeral instead, which is the preference `CLAUDE.md` states.

---

## §116 — THE CUSTOMER SECTION IS THE WHOLE CUSTOMER SECTION, ON THE PHONE TOO

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-13**, against the phone build: **"customer section on
the mobile should be fully functional like the pc version. overview the customer
section all functionality and make sure it's all available on mobile also audit
that section."**

§112's shape, one section later, and the same sentence underneath it: the rule
that keeps authoring on a desktop is still right for a product with options and
variants in it, and it was never the rule that should have governed this. A
customer record is not authored. It is read at the counter with the person
standing there, and the acts on it — fix the flat number, note the allergy, tag
them wholesale, stop the referral code somebody is abusing, sign the stolen
phone out — all happen in the shop, on the day.

### The defect this audit found, which is not a parity gap

The record's four action buttons and the Block under them were drawn for
**every** operator. `lib/cap-routes.js` gates those writes — `customers:adjust`
for points and wallet, `customers:block` for block, unblock and force-logout,
`customers:edit` for the rest — and `lib/capabilities.js` hands
`customer_service`, warehouse and dispatch presets a narrower set than that.

**A refusal here does not fail politely.** `apiWrite` in `public/m.html` treats
`403` the same as `401` — as a lost session — and sends the browser to
`/backend/login`. So an operator holding `customers:view` who tapped Points was
logged out of the app mid-shift, with no message and nothing saved. Every
control in the section is gated now, absent rather than disabled, **and the
guard is in the command as well as in the view**: a guard the view enforces is
one `APP.cmd` walks straight past, which is the hole §112 found in `teamToggle`
and `teamEnforce`, and the probe asserts both directions.

`apiWrite`'s own 403 handling is left alone deliberately. Changing what a 403
means to that helper touches every screen in the file and belongs to its own
brief; what this section can honestly do is stop drawing the controls that
provoke one. Recorded here so the next pass does not read the gate as the whole
fix.

### Everything else was UI, and the data was already arriving

**No route, no schema, no migration, no new capability.** `GET /customers`
already returned `note`, `tags` and `tag_vocabulary`; `GET /customers/:id` is a
`SELECT *` and already carried `orders_by_month`, `affiliate.lifetime_mode` /
`lifetime_eligible` / `lifetime_eligible_since` and `stats.active_sessions`. The
phone was fetching all of it and rendering some of it.

Twelve gaps, closed over the desktop's own endpoints:

| | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Tier, channel | single-select against a `tier=a,b` endpoint | multi-select; `All` is the row's clear, not a fourth value |
| Tags | no filter at all | chips from the server's `tag_vocabulary`, with its counts; the row is absent until somebody has tagged somebody |
| Sort | no `dir` sent, so Name could only run A→Z | picking the ordering you are on turns it over |
| Tags + note on the record | nothing rendered | shown and editable, through the same `PATCH` |
| Profile | name and email | name, email, **phone, gender, birthday** |
| Add a customer | only inside the order wizard | the roster's own button |
| Addresses | first three, `city · district · detail`, read-only | all of them with the recipient, the street line and the default marked; add, edit, delete, set default |
| Sign out all devices | `➖` | on the record |
| Referring / ongoing share / reissue code | not on the phone at all | three controls, and the two **states** they turn, which were on no screen |
| Activity | `➖` | twelve columns and the busiest month named |
| CSV export | `➖` | the server's file, at the filters the screen is showing |

### The two reversals, said plainly

`docs/tacet-mobile-parity.md` recorded both as asked and settled on 2026-08-22,
so overturning them is a decision and not a tidy-up.

**The phone number.** Held back because records dedupe on it, so a mistyped
digit one-handed is a merge or a split rather than a typo. That describes a
SILENT collision, and `PATCH /customers/:id` has not been silent about one since
its own duplicate check went in: it answers `phone_taken` and writes nothing —
and this sheet has carried the wording for that refusal all along, with no field
that could provoke it. What is left is a number typed wrong into an unused slot,
which is the risk the name and the email already carry. The warning stays as a
warning rather than as a door.

**Sign out all devices.** Declined on the grounds that the device count is the
useful part. The count is the reason to have the control, not a substitute for
it: the sentence that precedes it is "my phone was stolen", said out loud, in
the shop.

### What stays on the desktop

**Print statement** — `m.html` has no browser-print path at all. Its printer is
the shop's thermal receipt printer (`POST /orders/:id/print`), and
`cuPrintStatement` builds a page through `tdPrintTable`, which the phone does
not load. A statement is a document, and that is a desktop affordance rather
than a withheld feature.

**CSV import** — bulk authoring, by the rule that still holds for products and
broadcasts.

**Reset test account** — `POST /customers/:id/reset-test` exists as a route and
the desktop draws no control for it either, so its absence is not a gap between
the two surfaces. Recorded so the next audit does not file it as one.

### One desktop label deliberately not copied

`08-customers.js` labels both the street line and the sub-address `详细地址`,
and its own refusal — `收件人、电话和详细地址都需要填写。` — means the street one
by it. Two fields under one label, in a form that refuses by naming the label,
is a refusal pointing at the wrong box. The phone splits them: `街道地址` and
`楼栋 / 楼层 / 房号`. Everything else on these screens uses the desktop's
characters unchanged, for §112's reason.

**Chinese:** 11 verbatim lifts, three arrangements that move only a clause
naming a device, and 38 composed pairs — declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.72 with the rejected candidates beside
them.

### What holds it

`scripts/test_mobile_customers.js` — **84 assertions across 30 cases**, over
request bodies rather than screens: tags save lower-cased and deduped through
the profile `PATCH`, a new address reads its province off the picked city, an
edit is a `PUT` to its own id, the ongoing share posts `customerId` to
`/affiliate/eligible` and not to a customers route, the export's query is built
by the roster read's own helper so the file and the screen cannot disagree, and
an operator holding only `customers:view` is offered nothing AND gets nothing
when each command is called directly. Five render cases join
`scripts/test_mobile_screens.js` (456 renders, warm, cold and Chinese), one of
them the view-only record. Registered in `run-suites.js`'s SLOW set, with the
comment saying why `isSlow()` cannot see the browser in an `m-probe` suite. No
CSS file, and no change to `.gitignore` or to CI.


## §117 — ALL SYNCING GATHERS IN ONE PLACE, AND THE PRODUCTS LIST SAYS NOTHING ABOUT IT

**2026-09-13 · decided by Ash. Part one built the same day; parts two and three are
decided and not built.**

### What was wrong

Four surfaces answered one question — *is this product's number right on this channel?*

1. The **products list** carried a Channels column: three dots per row (§103 step 3),
   and a fourth read of `/api/retail-admin/channel-sync` on every catalogue load.
2. The **Channel sync page** (`#tab-channel-sync`, §103) — the combined overview, which
   already did most of what was being asked for, and which was reached by a `btn btn-sm`
   in the Sales header's corner beside Get help.
3. The **Meituan** and **Eleme** tabs — twins: pagehead, tiles, store lines, sub-tabs,
   chips, list + panel.
4. **GZ Grocery** — none of that. Its own heading, two paragraphs of teaching copy, its
   own inline `<style>` block, a health strip, and a sub-nav of its own invention.

Ash, from the products list: *"now on product list page on pc I see channels sync. I
don't want that. I need all syncing should gather in one page … we also need to sync both
sections so they will have the same features and same style … we want tenant to have easy
understanding of each channel situation, problem, and how to solve the problem easily."*

### The decision

**One page. Three depths. The same frame all the way down.**

- **Depth 1 — all channels.** One card per channel, broken first: is it syncing, why not,
  how much is wrong. Below it, the combined table — one row per item, one column per
  channel. This is the one thing no other screen gives, and it stays.
- **Depth 2 — one channel.** **A STATE OF THE SAME PAGE, NOT A PAGE OF ITS OWN.** Same
  chips, same search, same store filter, same list; the channel picker merely narrows.
- **Depth 3 — one item.** The panel carries what the shelf says, what the channel holds,
  one sentence naming what is wrong, and **the controls that fix it**.

**Why depth 2 is a state and not a restyle.** The literal reading of *"same features and
same style"* is to restyle three channel pages into the overview's likeness. That is more
work and leaves three pages to keep in step by hand — and GZ Grocery is standing proof
that hand-kept pages drift. A per-channel view that is a state of the one page has nothing
left to drift, because there is nothing left to keep in step. Put to Ash as that exact
question; answered **"ok"**.

**Channel admin is not sync, and does not move.** Credentials, Meituan's Bundles, and GZ
Grocery's Billing/Statement stay where they are. Ash on Billing: *"it's got nothing to do
with syncing products"*. Only the sync half gathers; otherwise "one page" becomes one
enormous page.

**The name stays `Channel sync · 渠道同步`.** Ash asked for *"channel sync manager or
something like that"* and did not press it when the cost was named. The name is already
live in four places — the dashboard's alert row, the phone's nav row, the Sales button,
and §103–§107 throughout — and one word per thing is worth more here than "manager".

### Part one — built

**The sub-nav.** `#tab-sales` and `#tab-channel-sync` each render the same strip: two
buttons, same classes, only `active` moves. That sameness is the mechanism, not decoration
— it is what makes this a sub-nav rather than two one-way links, and it is how the
operator gets back. Both tabs already stand in on the Sales rail row (`01-core.js`
`RAIL_STANDIN`), so the rail does not move underneath the crossing. The Channel sync
button carries the same any-of gate as `TAB_CAP['channel-sync']`.

**The products list says nothing about syncing.** Gone: the `Channels` column and its
`<col>`/`<th>`/`<td>`, the card-grid equivalent, `paLoadChannels`, `_paChannelDots`,
`PA_CHANNELS` / `PA_CH_LIST` / `PA_CH_ON` / `PA_CH_RANK`, `_paChGlyph`, the CSS block, and
the per-load fetch of `/channel-sync?compact=1`. `csOpenProduct` and its scroll helper go
with the dots that were their only caller.

**What stays.** The editor's Channels card (§103 step 4, `pdLoadChannels`). One product
looked at in depth is not a second overview competing with the first, and Ash scoped the
removal to *"the products list page"*. `_paChName` survives because that card needs it.

### Part two — built, and NARROWER than part one promised

Part one wrote: *"fold the Meituan and Eleme sync views into the one frame, and carry the
repair panel into depth 3."* **The fold was not built, and on the survey it turned out not
to be the thing worth building.** What was built is the repair. The record of why:

**THE FOLD WOULD HAVE BUILT A THIRD LIST.** The Meituan and Eleme sync views are a
one-line-per-product list with a side panel. This page already has a
one-line-per-product list — its table — and the channel picker already narrows it to one
channel. Rebuilding `mt-list` / `el-list` inside it would add a second list to the page
that replaced them, to show the same rows.

**THE PANEL COULD NOT BE SHARED, AND THE SURVEY SAID SO IN THE ROUTES.** All three
channels write through `/products/:id/map`, and the three payloads agree on exactly one
field — `sync_enabled`. Meituan sends `meituanName` through `lib/meituan-map-write`; Eleme
sends `elemeName` plus a spec pair, an `extendCode` and a `remove` flag; GZ Grocery sends a
`skuId` and has no store field at all because it has one store. A panel driving all three
would carry that difference on the page §117 exists to take it off.

**SO THE LINE WAS DRAWN AT THE VERBS THE CHANNELS ALREADY SHARE**, and there are two:
every map table has `sync_enabled`, and every queue table takes the same five columns.
`lib/channel-sync-write.js` is those two verbs for all three channels, and
`routes/channel-sync.js` — until now a read — carries them. **Between them they clear four
of the seven reasons an item can need attention**: `sync_off` by the switch;
`push_failed`, `wrong_number` and `never_synced` by the push. The other three —
`no_name`, `name_not_found`, `no_option` — need the channel's own catalogue picker, and
every amber row keeps the button to the channel's tab for them.

**THE PUSH IS ALSO THE RETRY, AND THAT WAS ALREADY A KNOWN DEFECT.** The daemon picks up
only `pending` rows, so an item whose last push errored sits there forever
(`docs/meituan-findings.md` #6, and a session on 2026-09-12 that found Black Beans stuck
amber for exactly this). A fresh pending row is both the retry and the fix: the verdict
reads the latest queue row per (store, product), so the item leaves *needs attention* the
moment it lands.

**A PENDING ROW IS REFRESHED, NEVER DUPLICATED.** `routes/meituan-admin.js`'s push-all
carries the scar in its own comment — *"877 pending for 208 products"* — and this button
is worse placed for it, sitting next to a red row where it gets pressed twice.

**THE TRAP THE SURVEY CAUGHT: GZ Grocery's pre-order key is `gzgrocery`, not `guanyi`.**
Every surface in this codebase calls that channel `guanyi`; `lib/channel-publish` knows it
only as `gzgrocery`, which is the string `routes/guanyi-admin.js`'s own push-all passes.
Getting it wrong drops §85's allowance from every GZ Grocery push and looks like nothing at
all until a pre-order window closes itself. The mapping lives in one table and the test
pins it to the route rather than to a literal, so the two cannot drift apart.

**THE SWITCH IS THE CHANNEL PANELS' SWITCH.** `toggle-label` was styled under
`.mt-panel` / `.el-panel`; the Channel sync card is joined to that selector group rather
than given matching values of its own. A second set of numbers that happens to match today
is how three channel pages came to look like three channel pages.

**Chinese: nothing composed.** `Sync now · 立即同步` is `11-meituan.js`'s own push button;
`Sync on / off · 同步开关` is the title on both the Meituan and the Eleme panel switches.
The two refusals (`not_mapped`, `not_syncing`) carry `row_moved`'s existing pair verbatim
from `TD_ERR` — they are the same fact from the operator's side, *somebody moved this while
you had it open*, so they say it in the same words rather than two new ones.

**Both writes are gated** in `lib/cap-routes.js`: `push` answers `{channel}:sync` (the
same verb as push-all, one item wide), the switch answers `{channel}:map` (it changes a
mapping). That file **fails open for a mutation it does not know**, so a write missing
from it has no gate at all — which is why the test asserts all six.

### Part three — decided, not built

**GZ Grocery's page into the frame.** It is the one channel page that shares neither the
other two's layout nor their sub-nav, and it carries its own inline `<style>` block.
Billing/Statement and Mapping stay on it — Ash: *"it's got nothing to do with syncing
products"*. Its own PR (working rules: one PR per change).

### What part two still does not fix

The three picker reasons — `no_name`, `name_not_found`, `no_option` — still send the
operator to the channel's tab. That is deliberate and recorded above, not an oversight: it
is where the three channels genuinely differ. If it turns out to be the common case in
practice rather than the tail, the answer is a shared listing-name picker fed by the
catalogue this endpoint already reads — **not** three pickers on one page.

### The phone

`m.html` already ships a Channel sync screen with its own nav row, reading the same
endpoint. Nothing here changes it. **Any part-two change to the desktop's vocabulary or
verdicts must reach it in the same PR**, or the two surfaces will answer one question two
ways — which is the defect §103 through §107 spent five sections closing.

### Chinese

**Nothing composed, so nothing is due in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`.**
`Channel sync · 渠道同步` is the button this replaces (and the dashboard row, and the
phone's nav row). `Overview · 概览` is lifted verbatim from the GZ Grocery page's own
sub-nav — this same control, on a channel page.

## §118 — THE OPERATIONS MENU IS ENTERED BY THE JOB, IN THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDS

**DECIDED 2026-09-13 by Ash: OPTION B**, chosen from the two in
`docs/tacet-operations-clarity-options.md`. That document recommended option A
(grouping the twenty-two rows under eight headings) and named B as a layer to
build later on evidence; the recommendation was declined in favour of B. The
argument is kept there unedited, because a decision record whose losing option
has been tidied away afterwards cannot be re-checked.

**What B is.** A short block at the top of More, above the Operations heading,
that asks the operator what they need to do in plain words and routes each
answer to the screen that answers it. Seven questions, each gated on the
capability its destination is gated on.

**The twenty-two rows do not change.** No row is renamed, regrouped, reordered
or removed; `MORE_GROUPS` is read, never rewritten. B adds a way IN; it does not
reorganise what it leads to. An operator who knows the list keeps the list they
know.

### Why the questions carry the distinction rather than the rows

The options document said B's first row would answer one question with two
destinations, and that this was B's honest limit. **Built, it is not a limit but
the shape of the answer**: instead of one "Something arrived" opening a chooser
whose two entries both read 收货, B asks **two** questions — *Something arrived
from a supplier* and *Something arrived from another shop* — and each goes
straight to its screen.

That matters beyond the wording. It means **B has no dependency on option A's
renames.** The reading in the options document — that B could not be written
without them — was wrong, and is corrected here rather than silently: the
