very item it was waiting for was still missing, and hand back stock it had never
deducted. It now builds the same lines-plus-`options_json` map, checks
availability against it, and takes stock from it. Taking from the map rather than
the rows also means what is deducted is exactly what was verified a line earlier,
and writes **one** reservation and **one** ledger row per product where a cart
repeating a product across two lines used to write two — the same total, and a row
the ledger reads back without ambiguity.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, and both are load-bearing.**

`cartHasBundle` **stays an arm of the guard.** `expandStockLines` would expand a
bundle happily, but a bundle parks on COMPONENT ids that match no order line, and
both the drawer's Awaiting-restock card and its per-parcel *"Held — N lines
waiting"* pill key on line `product_id`. That is a separate question with its own
answer and this is not it.

**Supplier-direct lines are still counted WHOLE**, and this is why the park does
not simply call `expandStockLines`. That function drops them — correctly, for
reserving, since they hold no inventory of ours. But the release above demands
`av.exists` for every line, a supplier-direct line has no `retail_store_stock`
row and never will, so an order holding one could never satisfy it: parking such
an order would park it forever. Counting it is what refuses the park, through
`effectiveOosPolicy` returning `always`, which is not a pre-order policy. **The
first draft of this change did call `expandStockLines` and
`scripts/test_preorder_park.js` failed it on exactly that case** — the control
was already written, which is the whole return on having written it.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, said here rather than discovered later.** Order
TC000735 itself. `STATUS_TRANSITIONS` offers no `paid → awaiting_restock` step,
so an order that has already settled cannot be moved into the queue by any
operator; TC000735 is prepare-it-when-the-pita-lands or cancel-and-refund. Whether
that manual step should exist is a separate decision and is not taken here.

**NO CHINESE COMPOSED.** This change mints no customer-facing or operator-facing
string; the Awaiting-restock card, its pill and the status chip are the ones §80
and §128 already shipped. `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.

**HOW IT IS HELD.** `scripts/test_preorder_park.js` 16 → **20**: a sold-out
pre-order line beside an in-stock paid extra now parks and records only the short
line; the extra is not taken while the order waits; the short line is not driven
negative; and a sold-out `strict` extra is refused at checkout outright — 409
`insufficient_stock` naming the EXTRA's product id, from the pre-existing
`strictItems` reserve gate, which is a stronger answer than "does not park" and is
asserted so that no later change can quietly start parking on one. The new cases
are placed LAST in the suite on purpose: a parked order competes for the next
restock at that store, and placed earlier they ate the unit an existing release
case was waiting for. `test:fast` **245/245**, lint 0 errors. No schema, no
migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §135 — A SECTION CAN BE TAKEN OFF THE QR MENU WITHOUT LEAVING THE APP

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-15, in one sentence:** *"on the main menu qr, product
description — there are products that i dont want all blocks available. i want
less blocks. however in the mini app i want to keep it the same as now."*

**THE PROBLEM IS ONE ARRAY READ BY THREE SURFACES.** `description_blocks` is
authored once in the product editor and rendered by
`miniapp/components/product-blocks` (the mini app), `lib/product-blocks-read.js`
→ `routes/shop-menu.js` (the QR menu at `/s/:shopCode`) and
`public/shop/product-blocks.js` (the web storefront). Before this there was no
way to say *this section, but not there* — every surface drew whatever the office
had written, which is the right default and was the only behaviour available.

**THE DECISION: ONE FLAG ON THE BLOCK, HONOURED BY ONE READER.** A block may
carry `hide_qr: true`. `pageBlocks()` in `lib/product-blocks-read.js` skips it;
nothing else in the repo reads it. The mini app and the web storefront render by
block TYPE and ignore fields they do not know, so a trim on the QR menu is
invisible to both without either of them changing by a line. That property is the
whole design and is what the tests exist to hold.

**DEFAULT IS ON, AND THAT IS NOT A DETAIL.** An absent flag means the section
shows. A whitelist — "list the surfaces this block appears on" — was rejected:
it is tidier to read and it would have blanked the entire existing catalogue on
the QR menu the moment it shipped, until somebody re-ticked every block of every
product. `hide_qr: false` is never persisted either; the editor deletes the key
rather than writing a `false` nobody set onto every block the office happened to
open.

**THE WEB STOREFRONT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS.** Ash named two surfaces and
`public/shop.html` is a third. It renders the same stack as the mini app, nobody
has asked for it to differ, and a switch nobody uses is a third thing to keep
correct. The sibling flag is `hide_web` if that day comes; it does not exist.

**OFF IS NOT DELETE.** The block keeps its words, its order and its colours —
one reader skips it. This is what makes the control safe to try on a live
product, and the editor says so in as many words rather than leaving the operator
to find out.

**THE FALLBACK WAS THE TRAP, AND IT IS ONLY ABOUT NUTRITION.**
`routes/shop-menu.js` prints the `retail_products.nutrition` COLUMN when no
`nutrition_facts` BLOCK already said it — a product carrying both would otherwise
print its table twice under one heading (§132). A hidden block is absent from
`pageBlocks()`, so asking the FILTERED list "is there a nutrition block?" reads
*no* and prints the very table the operator had just switched off. The question
is therefore put to `blockRead.hasNutritionBlock()`, which reads the UNFILTERED
source. Nothing else about the flag needs this; nutrition needs it because it is
the one block type with a second home.

**AND THE SHEET STILL REFUSES TO OPEN ON NOTHING.** §120's rule is unchanged and
now has one more way to be reached: hide every section of a product and its card
stops responding on the QR menu, exactly as a product that never had any does. A
product with more than one size still opens, because the size picker lives in
that sheet.

**NUTRITION BECOMES A BLOCK LIKE ANY OTHER (the second half of the same brief:**
*"need to fix nutrition label so it will be part of the block same as any other
blocks"*). The hand editor was the only writer that stripped `nutrition_facts`
out of `description_blocks` and routed it to the column alone; the AI compose
path in `public/retail-admin/09-products.js` has always kept the block AND
mirrored the column, and all three surfaces have rendered the type for some time.
`paBlocksCollect()` now keeps it too. The mirror to `products.nutrition` STAYS —
a mini app build that has not been republished still draws its separate panel
from that column, and every surface suppresses that panel when a block exists, so
the mirror can never double-print. `peMount` synthesises the column back into the
stack only when the stack has no nutrition block of its own; without that guard a
product saved by this editor would come back carrying two nutrition sections, one
from each home.

**NO MIGRATION, AND NONE IS NEEDED.** Products whose nutrition lives only in the
column keep rendering through the fallback, unchanged, until somebody saves them
in the editor. Nothing is backfilled and no row is rewritten.

**WHERE IT IS IN THE EDITOR (Option A, chosen by Ash from three mockups,
2026-09-15).** A third fold in the existing block inspector — *Where to show ·
显示位置*, beside Content and Colours — carrying one switch. The section list on
the left marks a switched-off block with a struck-through eye, so "which of these
nine does the till page show?" is answered by looking rather than by nine clicks.
The two directions not chosen are recorded for whoever picks this up: **Option B**
put the mini app and the QR menu side by side as live previews with the hidden
section ghosted in place, and **Option C** replaced the three-pane editor with a
sections × surfaces matrix. Both were judged better to use and more expensive
than the ask; C is the natural second view if the editor is ever reworked.

**THE SKIN IS NOT IN THIS.** Ash also asked for the editor to look like Tacet —
it still carries the older IBM Plex / Tea-Green layer while `retail-admin.css`
has a live `--td-*` Tacet layer that only the Customers and Dashboard tabs
consume. That is a separate pass and a separate PR; this one adds a control in
the editor's existing vocabulary.

**CHINESE.** Four strings, three composed from live pieces and one live pair
lifted whole. Declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.88 under Rule
4's 2026-09-06 delegation, with the candidates rejected.

**TESTS.** `scripts/test_product_blocks_read.js` — seven checks on the flag
itself (dropped, neighbours kept, string and array forms alike, an absent flag
means shows, a `false` is not a hide, the source array is not edited, and
`hasNutritionBlock` seeing what `pageBlocks` dropped).
`scripts/test_shop_menu_render.js` — two end-to-end checks on a real rendered
page: a switched-off quote is gone while the visible one beside it is untouched,
and a hidden nutrition block does not come back out of the column on a product
that has both.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.** No schema change, no migration, no change to
the mini app, the web storefront, `.gitignore` or CI. No per-product "short menu"
flag. No control over section ORDER per surface — the order is the office's, once,
for everybody.

## §136 — A SHORTAGE FOUND AFTER THE MONEY LANDED HAS SOMEWHERE TO GO

**2026-09-15 · Ash decided, having been told §134 fixes the next order and can
do nothing for the one that prompted it:**
*"build all and automatically deploy to live."*

**WHAT WAS MISSING.** `awaiting_restock` could only ever be reached by the
CHECKOUT: the customer answered the shortage modal (`wait_for_restock`), or
§80 / §128 / §134's park caught a short pre-order line at order time. A shortage
discovered AFTER the money landed — the picker reaches the shelf and the item is
not there, a count was wrong, a channel order took the last one an hour ago — had
nowhere to go. `STATUS_TRANSITIONS` offered no step from `paid`, so the two ways
out were to prepare an order that cannot be picked, or to cancel and refund a
customer who would rather wait. TC000735 is the live case and the reason this
section exists: §134 stops that order being created again and can do nothing
whatever for the order itself.

**WHAT IS DECIDED.** `paid → awaiting_restock`, the only backwards step in that
table, offered as **Hold for restock · 等待补货** in the order drawer's
transition row.

**WHY BACKWARDS IS SAFE HERE** and is not a hole in a forward-only machine: the
two states differ in what the OFFICE is told, not in what the customer has paid
or what the shelf holds. No money moves. No stock moves. And `awaiting_restock`
already steps forward to exactly what `paid` steps forward to — `preparing` and
`cancelled` — so nothing downstream gains a path it did not already have. `col`
is null because there is no `awaiting_restock_at` column and this adds no schema;
the activity log records who moved it and when.

**THE PRODUCT LIST IS COMPUTED, NEVER TAKEN FROM THE OPERATOR.** They are telling
us the shelf is short; WHICH SKUs that means is a fact about the shelf, not a
judgement, and `awaiting_restock_pids` is not decoration —
`checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` only looks at an order when a product in that
list is restocked. Asking the operator to pick would invite a park on a product
that is not short (never released) or on one the order does not need (released by
a restock of something irrelevant).

**THE GUARD IS THE POINT, because a careless park is STRICTLY WORSE than the
problem it solves** — an order stranded in a queue whose whole promise is that
orders leave it by themselves. The move is refused, with the order left exactly
where it was, when:

1. **the order has no fulfilling store** — there is no shelf for it to wait on;
2. **some product it needs has no stock row at that store** — a supplier-direct
   line, or one simply never stocked there. The release demands `av.exists` for
   every product, so such an order could never clear. This is the same hazard the
   checkout park refuses by counting supplier-direct lines whole (§134), named
   here in the operator's own terms, and **the refusal names the item** so they
   know which one;
3. **nothing is actually short** — parking then would hold an order that had no
   reason to be in the queue, until somebody happened to adjust one of its
   products.

**THE HALF THAT BREAKS SILENTLY, and the reason this was not a one-line edit to a
table.** An order parked from `paid` HAS ALREADY TAKEN ITS STOCK.
`prepareCommitUnreservedOrder` decremented it at settlement, and on a shelf that
could not cover it that decrement is precisely why the count reads negative —
TC000735's pita at **-1**. A release that deducted again would take the same
units twice and put the count straight back under, which is the fault the park
exists to make visible.

So `checkAwaitingRestockForRestock` now reads `orderCommittedPids` — the ledger,
exactly as `commitUnreservedOrder` reads it — and **skips DEDUCTING what the
order already took, while still CHECKING it.** Both halves are deliberate:

* skipping the deduction is what stops the double-take;
* keeping the check is what makes the park mean anything. The order's units are
  already off the count, so a shelf that can cover it again is a shelf standing
  at or above what this order needs — exactly what the check asks. Skipping it
  would release the order the instant it was parked, which is the opposite of
  what the operator clicked.

**A CHECKOUT RESERVATION IS DELIBERATELY NOT ENOUGH to count as taken.** A
courier order reserves its `strict` lines at checkout and parks anyway, holding
stock it has not taken; those lines must still be deducted when it is released,
and the existing suite asserts exactly that. Only a written `order*` ledger row
means the shelf has already paid. For every checkout-parked order the set is
empty and every line below reads as it did before.

**ONE VIEW, TWO CALLERS.** `orderStockNeed` and `orderCommittedPids` are exported
from `lib/inventory.js` and read by both the release and the park's
preconditions. A precondition that disagreed with the release is exactly how an
order gets stranded, and two inline copies of the same map is how they come to
disagree.

**NOT IN THE BULK BAR, and that is a choice rather than an omission.** That bar
is explicitly forward steps on the fulfilment track; each park needs its own
shortage check against its own store and can be refused for its own reason, none
of which a bulk confirmation could state honestly.

**NO CHINESE COMPOSED.** 等待补货 is lifted verbatim from this same file's
awaiting-restock card (`cuT('Waiting on stock', '等待补货')`), so the button and
the card it produces say the same word; it is also the live pair behind the
status chip, the mini app and the web store. The English is restructured to read
as an action, which is what the rule asks for before minting.
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.88 records the lift.

**THE DELIVERY WINDOW IS NOT TOUCHED, said here rather than discovered later.**
§128's park clears the window because there is no date behind a pre-order. An
operator parking a settled order may be parking it for an afternoon, and silently
rewriting a date the customer was promised is a different decision from making
the order visible. The status, the card and the pill all say it is waiting; the
date stays the operator's to change.

**HOW IT IS HELD.** New suite `scripts/test_manual_restock_park.js`, **14/14**,
against the real route over HTTP and a real database: the reported shape parks
and records the computed pid, parking moves no stock, a partial restock does not
release it, a covering restock does — **and does not take the stock a second
time**, which is proven non-vacuous by disabling the skip and watching it fail.
Plus an add-on-only shortage parking on the add-on, all three refusals with the
order left untouched, and the forward step still working from the parked state.
`test:fast` 245 → **246**, lint 0 errors. No schema, no migration, and no change
to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §137 — A SALE MADE OVER THE COUNTER IS PROOF THE STOCK WAS THERE

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-15.** Shown the two shapes in plain words and asked
which: *"b and all four"*. **B** is this section. The "all four" half is a
different change and has its own section.

**THE FAILURE, as it reaches the shop.** The record says 0 green wraps at
天河店. There are in fact three on the shelf — somebody counted wrong last
week. A walk-in buys all three. Real wraps, real money, and the record now reads
−3.

Next morning the kitchen opens 制作队列 and reads `有客户订单等待 · 青酱卷 3`,
because `lib/batch-owed.js` sums `physical_qty < 0` for batch-made products and
calls all of it owed. So three wraps are made for nobody, and they go in the bin
at the end of their shelf life.

**WHY THE NUMBER LIED.** A negative shelf has two causes and they have opposite
remedies:

| cause | what −3 means | the repair |
|---|---|---|
| a debt | three were sold that were never held | make or re-order them |
| a miscount | three were on the shelf and the record was short | count the shelf |

§84 established the first and is untouched. The second is what a counter sale
produces, and the owed block cannot tell them apart because it reads the balance
and never asks how it got there.

**THE DECISION.** A counter sale that lands the shelf below zero corrects itself
to zero, in the same transaction, with a second ledger row (`counter_miscount`)
recording the lift. Two rows, not one netted figure: the sale really happened
and the correction really happened.

The reasoning is arithmetic rather than policy. If three wraps physically left
the shelf in a customer's hand, the shelf held three. §84's negative asserts
"sold and never held", and a face-to-face sale disproves that by having
happened. So the correction is not a clamp over an inconvenient truth — it is
the truth, and the negative was the error.

**THIS IS A FLOOR, AND §39 RULINGS 1 AND 7 REMOVED FLOORS ON PURPOSE. The
conflict is stated rather than glossed.** Those removals were for the CHANNEL
INGESTS, where a negative is the only record that Meituan or Eleme sold what we
did not have — real units owed to a real customer who is waiting. Nothing here
weakens that. The ingests, the delta path, and every non-counter commit still
write the honest negative, and the tests hold it. What is claimed is narrower
and is about this one door only.

**AND THE MISCOUNT IS NOT SILENCED, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF.** Correcting the
shelf removes the kitchen's signal, and the kitchen's signal was the wrong one.
The right one is the merchant alert shipped the same day (§135's
sibling work, `lib/channel-line-report.js`): a counter sale below zero already
says `可能是数错了` / *so it was likely counted wrong*, naming the product and
how far the record was short. That alert previously skipped batch-made products,
on the ground that the owed block carried them; on the counter path it no longer
does, so the exclusion is lifted THERE and only there. Supplier-direct stays
excluded on both paths — no inventory of ours, so no count to be wrong.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.**

- **No gate on the till.** A walk-in holding the item is still never refused
  because a row disagrees with the room. That is what makes this whole section
  necessary rather than avoidable.
- **No change to the delivery path.** A web or mini-app order that outruns the
  shelf still leaves the negative, and still reports `有客户订单等待`. Those
  units genuinely are owed.
- **No retrospective repair.** Negatives already on the shelf from past counter
  sales are left alone; a recount is the operator's, and §84's own refusal
  dialog now asks about it properly.
- **No schema change and no migration.** `counter_miscount` is a value in the
  existing `reason` column.
- **No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds
  work.**

## §138 — WHAT THE CUSTOMER WAS TOLD IS PART OF THE ORDER

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-15:** *"b and all four"* — the second half of that
answer. The first is §137.

**THE QUESTION IT ANSWERS.** A customer orders something we are sold out of. The
checkout tells them one of four things. Three weeks later: *"you told me it
would arrive on the 20th."* The order shows what they bought and what they paid,
and until now could not always say what they were shown.

**WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE, AND IT IS MORE THAN WAS ASSUMED.** The two notices
that carry a DATE already land on the order. `computeBatchNotice` (courier) and
`computeLocalFreshNotice` (local run) both stamp `promised_ship_date` and
`promised_delivery_date` in the best-effort block after the order is written.
**This was discovered while building, and it inverted the recommendation that
had been put to Ash** — the argument for "all four" was that the dated ones
matter most, and the dated ones were the ones already recorded. The real gap was
the other two, which is what the session that first reported it had said.

**WHAT IS DECIDED.** The two dateless notices are recorded too, completing the
set:

| column | what it holds |
|---|---|
| `preorder_pids` | the product ids sold as a pre-order on this order |
| `moved_from_store` | the store code that WOULD have served this address if nothing were closed — written only when it differs from the store that took the order |

**RECOMPUTED ON THE SERVER, NOT ECHOED BY THE CLIENT.** A record meant to settle
a dispute is worth nothing if the other party supplied it. Both run off the same
locals the order itself was built on, microseconds after the write.

**THE MOVE IS RECORDED AS A FACT, NOT AS THE NOTICE, and that is the one place
this deliberately does not mirror the checkout.** `computeStoreMoveNotice`
returns null when the operator has not written the copy for it
(`storefront_config` `notice.store_move.*`) — correct for a banner, and wrong
for an audit trail, because the order moved either way and the silence was ours.
So the write asks `inventory.routeIgnoringClosures` directly, which is the same
question the notice asks first. `routing_reason` could not answer it: `routeOrder`
drops closed stores BEFORE it ranks, so its answer can never say what the
closure changed.

**BEST-EFFORT, OUTSIDE THE ORDER TRANSACTION.** A record ABOUT an order must
never be able to cost us the order. Same discipline as the two date stamps above
it and the reroute pids below it.

**AND IT IS READ.** Both print in the order drawer beside `rerouteShortNote`,
which answers the same question in the same shape: why does this order look the
way it does. A column nobody can read is not an audit trail.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.**

- **No retrospective fill.** Orders placed before this carry NULL, which is
  honest: we do not know what they were shown.
- **No change to what the customer sees.** This is a record, not a notice.
- **The dated pair is untouched.** `promised_ship_date` / `promised_delivery_date`
  keep their existing writers and their existing meaning.
- **No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds
  work.**

## §139 — THE PRODUCT EDITOR WEARS TACET, AND THE PREVIEW INSIDE IT DOES NOT

**Asked for by Ash, 2026-09-15:** *"need a new mock up of the product editor,
right now it doesnt look like part of tacet."* Three directions were drawn and
Ash chose **Option A**: the layout stands, the skin changes.

**WHAT IT WAS WEARING.** `public/product-editor.html` carried a palette of its
own — Ink Charcoal `#12161A`, Tea Green `#6B8E6F` for selection, Aged Brass
`#B08D4A` for the primary action, IBM Plex throughout — minted before this
product had a design system. `public/retail-admin.css` has carried the Tacet
`--td-*` layer since 2026-07-26, and the Customers and Dashboard tabs consume
it. The editor was the last large surface still speaking the older language, and
an operator moving between the two tabs crossed a border.

**THE OLD TOKEN NAMES SURVIVE, REMAPPED IN ONE PLACE.** `--bg-app`, `--accent`,
`--brass` and the rest are referenced by some four hundred rules in that file.
Renaming them would have been a four-hundred-line diff in which a real mistake
could hide; they are remapped at the `:root` block instead, each with a line
saying what it became. The visible diff is the token block plus about thirty
rules, not the stylesheet.

**WHAT THE REMAP DECIDES, because the old palette had conflated them:**

- **Selection is Ink, not a hue.** Tea Green meant "selected / active / live" —
  three ideas in one colour. A selected row is now filled with the theme's own
  ink and its label flips to paper, which is what `.pa-chip.is-on` and the
  Orders checkbox already do in `retail-admin.css`.
- **Live is Sage, draft is Amber.** Two different statements that were one hue
  apart. Sage is the all-clear; Amber is attention.
- **The primary action is Ink.** Aged Brass carried the primary action AND
  attention at once. Tacet splits them: Save is Ink (the merchant acting),
  attention is Amber. The Customers modal note is explicit that a primary is
  never Dusk.
- **Dusk is spent once, on Smart paste.** It is the only control on this screen
  that hands work to the model, and Dusk means *Tacet did this for you*. The
  focus ring is also Dusk and does not count against the one-per-screen rule —
  `retail-admin.css` exempts rings by name and asks not to have it re-litigated.
- **`--bg-elev-2` is NOT `--td-header`.** The first draft mapped it there and
  every hovered row read as a table's column-header band. It gets its own step
  between raised and border; the hierarchy note beside `--td-header` is explicit
  that these must not converge.

**TYPOGRAPHY.** Inter 400/500, sentence case, no tracking on small labels — the
rulebook allows no uppercase anywhere and nothing heavier than 500. Thirty-two
chrome rules were shouting; the badges already carried sentence-case copy
(`Draft · 草稿`) and it was the stylesheet uppercasing them. **IBM Plex Sans SC
stays loaded behind Inter**: Inter carries no Chinese and every label on this
page is bilingual. The tenant wordmark stays a wordmark, at 500 and normal
tracking rather than 700 at `.18em`.

**THE PHONE PREVIEW IS NOT TOUCHED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART.** The
frame in the middle of the editor renders the CUSTOMER'S product page in the
CUSTOMER'S brand — lime `#CCD900`, forest `#365329`, olive, oat. Tacet is the
chrome around it, never a coat of paint over it. A session restyling the chrome
and reaching one rule too far would repaint the thing the office is here to look
at, and the office would then be approving a page that does not exist. Every
`.pa-prev-*` rule keeps its literal hex and is fenced off from the `--td-*`
tokens by test.

**NO GRADIENTS.** The canvas had two radial washes of the old green. Two
gradients remain and both are drawings rather than surfaces: the fade over a
template thumbnail (a picture of the customer's page) and the diagonal slash
over a checkerboard that means "no colour" in the swatch picker.

**NO COPY CHANGED AND NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** This is a stylesheet; every
string on the page is the one that was there yesterday.
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.

**TESTS.** `scripts/test_product_editor_tacet.js`, eleven checks in four
sections. The one that matters most holds the two Tacet layers together: every
`--td-*` the editor declares must match `public/retail-admin.css` value for
value, which is the same second-implementation-of-one-contract shape that
`scripts/test_product_blocks_read.js` holds against the mini app. It caught a
real drift on the first run — a light-mode `--td-dusk-hi` invented here that the
admin does not have. The rest hold the rulebook (no uppercase, no weight above
500, no gradients, Dusk spent at most twice and only on the AI) and the fence
around the preview. `npm run test:fast` 250/250.

**VERIFIED BY LOOKING, not only by assertion.** A throwaway harness served
`public/` with a stubbed admin API and drove Chromium through the editor at
1440×900 in both themes, plus the Templates pane, the open left-rail accordions
and the Smart paste modal. It is not committed — it stubs an API rather than
running one, so it would rot into a test that proves nothing.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.** No layout change — Option A was chosen
precisely because nothing moves. No change to the mini app editor
(`public/cms.html`), which wears the same older palette and is the obvious next
one. No JS, no markup, no route, no schema, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.


## §140 — A PACK CAN HOLD A COUNT, NOT ONLY A WEIGHT

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-15,** shown the editor's own screenshot of J-57 Label
Paper reading **Cost per unit ¥9.27/pcs** for a roll of 1000 stickers, and the
three ways out — buy them in labels on the PO, lie about the unit and call a
label a gram, or change the model: *“ok fix it properly”*.

**THE SHAPE THAT COULD NOT BE SAID.** `lib/ingredient-cost.js` keys its whole
decision on the RECIPE unit (2026-08-17): `g` and `ml` divide the pack price
down, `pcs` / `bag` / `bottle` / `box` do not, because a recipe calling for one
bag consumes one bag whatever weight is inside it — 29 live rows depend on that
and it is still right. A roll of labels is per-piece by that rule, so the
derivation handed back the price of the whole roll and every label on every
product carried ¥9.27 of cost instead of ¥0.00927. The two fields that could
have said otherwise, `pack_contents_qty` and `pack_contents_unit`, were built
for weight and volume and their dropdown offered only g / kg / ml / L.

**WHAT IS DECIDED.** `pcs` joins that dropdown, and a per-piece recipe unit
whose pack contents are COUNTED divides:

```
cost per unit = buy_price / (buy_pack_size × pack_contents_qty)
```

the same formula shape the weight path already uses, so the two fields mean one
thing in both. A roll: buy unit `pcs`, packs per order `1`, buy price `9.27`,
contents per pack `1000`, contents unit `pcs` → **¥0.00927 a label**.

**NOTHING INFERS IT, AND THAT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF.** Only
`pack_contents_unit` normalising to `pcs` opens the divisor. There is no table
to fall back on — nothing about the word *box* says how many labels are in one
— and no row in the catalogue carries `pcs` there today, because the UI never
offered it and no import writes it. So the 29 per-piece rows cannot acquire a
divisor by accident; they acquire one when a person types the count, and not
before. Contents recorded in GRAMS on a per-piece row keep meaning what they
have always meant: a ¥28 bag of tortilla chips used one bag at a time still
costs ¥28, and dividing by 300 would still be wrong.

**A ZERO PACK SIZE IS REFUSED, NOT WAVED THROUGH ON A DIVISOR OF 1.** The same
requirement the weight path makes, for the reason the module was written: a
divisor invented here stores the roll price as the label price, which is the
bug. `readBody()` in `routes/retail-materials.js` stores 1 for a blank, so this
is unreachable from the editor and is left for an import that does not.

**THE EDITOR PRINTS THE DIVISION.** Beside the figure, in numerals and nothing
else — `¥9.27 ÷ 1000` — so it carries no copy and needs no Chinese.
`buy_pack_size` meant *grams per buy unit* before the `pack_size_semantics_v2`
migration in `database.js`, and that migration could only normalise rows whose
buy unit was a MEASURE (kg, L, lb, oz). A pcs-bought row can still be sitting
on a stale 1000 nobody has ever been asked about — J-57 was, in the screenshot
that started this. Printed, a stale pack size reads as an absurd divisor the
moment somebody fills in the contents; unprinted, it reads as a cost that is
merely a bit small, which is the failure that does not get noticed.

**AND THE FIGURE IS SHOWN TO THE PLACES IT NEEDS.** `acMoney()` renders two
decimals — right for everything a customer or a supplier is charged, wrong for
a derived per-unit cost: ¥0.00927 read as ¥0.01, eight percent out, and sesame
at ¥0.0316 a gram had been reading ¥0.03 since long before this. `unitMoney()`
in `public/retail-admin/18-materials.js` gives four places below a jiao and five
below a fen, on the record line and the list column. Nothing at or above ¥0.10
changes shape, and it is deliberately local to this screen rather than a change
to `acMoney()`, which every other screen reads.

**NO MIGRATION, AND NONE WANTED.** A material is fixed by filling in its
contents; the save re-derives through the same `costFor()` and fires the recipe
recompute, so the recipes carrying it follow. Nothing is rewritten under
anybody's feet.

**THE PO WRITE-BACK NEEDED NO CHANGE, AND IT IS WHERE THE LOOP WAS.**
`firePriceAlertsForPO` already runs the one derivation, so the ¥9.27-per-label
row it wrote on every order — two of them sit in J-57's live cost history —
stops by itself. `buy_price` still stores the ROLL price: it is what the
supplier charges, and it is what the ±5% price alert compares the next invoice
against.

**NO CHINESE COMPOSED.** `pcs` is a unit token standing beside `g` and `kg`, the
arithmetic line is numerals, and no label changed.
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.

**TESTS.** New `scripts/test_material_piece_pack.js`, 18 cases in three parts:
the rule, run through the shipped derivation rather than a copy of it; the
editor wiring, asserted at source; and a guard band over the four shapes this
section promises not to touch. Proven non-vacuous — six cases fail when the
divisor is removed. `scripts/test_price_writeback.js` gains case 10, which
drives the same material through a real PO against a real database and holds
both halves: the cost divides, the buy price does not. `test:fast` 251 →
**252/252**, lint 0 errors, bilingual-banner gate passes. No schema, no
migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §141 — ONE PRIMARY ACTION, ONE COLOUR, ON EVERY SCREEN

**Found by survey, 2026-09-15, while looking for something else.** Asked to put
`public/cms.html` onto Tacet after §139 did the product editor, this session
checked first and found the premise wrong: **the mini app editor was already on
Tacet, and had got there before the product editor did.** All fifteen of its
light-theme colours match `public/retail-admin.css` value for value. The
recommendation to reskin it was an inference from a stale comment in
`product-editor.html` ("mirror of /cms + retail-admin") and should not have been
made without looking. Recorded here so nobody re-opens it.

**WHAT THE SURVEY DID FIND is worth more than the job it replaced.**

**THE PRIMARY ACTION WAS A DIFFERENT COLOUR IN EACH EDITOR.** `cms.html` pointed
`--brass` — its name for "the one primary action" — at Dusk, so **Publish** was
purple there while the same button is Ink in the product editor and on the
Customers tab. One operator, three screens, and purple meaning two different
things.

**DUSK DOES NOT MEAN "IMPORTANT". IT MEANS "TACET DID THIS FOR YOU."** That is
the most important rule in the design system and the reason Dusk is scarce:
`docs/tacet-design-system.md` §1 says one Dusk element per screen is the norm
and that ordinary operator controls are "Ink or Secondary, NEVER Dusk";
`retail-admin.css` says it again beside the Customers modal — *"Primary is INK,
not Dusk — a modal's primary is the merchant acting."* Publishing your own work
is the merchant acting. **`--brass` now points at Ink.**

**THE OLD REASONING IS KEPT IN THE FILE RATHER THAN DELETED.** `cms.html`
carried a comment defending the choice: *"Publish — the single Dusk primary
action ... because publishing is the deliberate act the whole screen leads
to."* True about the act, wrong about the colour, and left in place beside the
reversal so the change is legible to whoever reads that rule next.

**THE DARK ROOM HAD TO INVERT WITH IT, and this was nearly the bug.** `cms.html`
is light-first with a dark override, and the dark block restates `--accent` but
never restated `--brass` — which had not mattered while `--brass` was Dusk, a
colour that holds in both themes. Ink does not: pointing `--brass` at Ink alone
would have painted an Ink button on an Ink ground and the primary action would
have disappeared in dark mode. The dark block now restates it as Paper, exactly
as it restates `--accent`, and `.btn-primary` takes its label from
`--accent-ink` instead of a literal `#FFFFFF` that would have been unreadable on
that inverted fill.

**WHAT STILL WEARS DUSK IN THAT EDITOR, and why none of it is a button:** focus
rings (`input:focus`, `.btn:focus-visible`, `::selection`), which are exempt by
name; `.drop-zone.hover`, a transient drag marker; and `.block-wrap.selected`,
the ring around the selected block. That last one is a selection, which the
rulebook would ordinarily make Ink — the file's own note argues it is drawn OVER
the customer's page, where Ink would vanish on a dark brand block, and that
argument holds. **It is deliberately left alone.** Changing it is a design
decision and was not the one asked for.

**THE RULEBOOK PASS (the second half of the brief).** Forty-eight chrome rules
in `cms.html` were setting uppercase and forty-three a weight above 500, both
against §1.6 and the type scale. All are now sentence case at 400/500. Four
labels — `PAGE`, `BACKGROUND`, `TAB BAR`, `DESIGN CHECK` — were typed in capitals
in the MARKUP, where no stylesheet change could reach them, and are recased.
**That is a case change to an existing English string, not new copy:** the
Chinese half of each pair is untouched and nothing is composed, so
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` has nothing to record.

**THE `font:` SHORTHAND IS WHERE A PASS LIKE THIS GOES WRONG.** The first sweep
matched `font-weight:` and missed five rules that set the weight inside the
shorthand (`font: 700 11px …`) without ever writing the longhand. The test
below checks both spellings for that reason.

**`.phone-preview-*` IS NOT THE PHONE.** The fence that protects the customer's
page keys on `.b-*`, `.fsd-*` and `.phone` — and `.phone-preview-*` is the
"Preview on phone" MODAL, editor chrome that shares only a prefix with the
device mock. A first pass skipped two chrome rules on that collision. The
distinction is encoded in the test as a negative lookahead rather than left to
be rediscovered.

**THE NAMES ARE NOT UNIFIED, DELIBERATELY.** The palette is declared three times:
`--td-*` in `retail-admin.css` and `product-editor.html`, `--tacet-*` in
`cms.html`. Renaming one to match the others would touch some six hundred rules
to change nothing a reader can see — a large diff for a small tidiness, and a
good place for a real mistake to hide. **The values are what must agree**, and a
mapping table in the test says which name means which.

**TESTS.** `scripts/test_tacet_one_palette.js`, eleven checks, closing the
triangle that `scripts/test_product_editor_tacet.js` opened: all three files
against one palette, the primary Ink in both editors, the dark inversion, no
literal white on a filled primary, and the rulebook over the mini app editor's
chrome. **Both sides of the fence are asserted** — the chrome checks would pass
trivially if the preview rules had been swept along with them, so the test also
requires that at least twenty preview rules STILL set caps or a heavy weight,
because the customer's blocks are editorial and must be able to say so. **Proved
by mutation**: drifting one colour, pointing `--brass` back at Dusk, adding one
uppercase rule to the chrome, and sweeping the `.b-*` rules each fail the check
that exists to catch them.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.** No reskin of `cms.html` — it did not need
one. No rename of `--tacet-*`. No change to `.block-wrap.selected`. No layout,
no JS, no markup beyond the four recased labels, no route, no schema, and no
change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §142 — AN INVERTED CONTROL CANNOT RIDE A SYNC THAT MEANS "THE FIELD EQUALS THE INPUT"

**Reported by Ash, 2026-09-15, against §135 shipped the same day:** *"clicking on
any block here hide or unhide the block from menu qr code, but its not working
well ... i cant really click hide/unhide the same block, i have to click on one
block to hide and another block to unhide."*

**IT WAS WORSE THAN THE SYMPTOM, AND IT REACHED THE DATABASE.** No click was
needed at all. `public/product-editor.html` syncs its inspector into the block
model through one generic mechanism, `paBlocksSyncFromDOM()`, whose entire
contract is `b[dataset.bkey] = (checkbox ? el.checked : el.value)` — *the field
equals the input*. The QR switch is **inverted**: it is ticked when the block
SHOWS, and the stored flag says HIDDEN. Wiring it in with `data-bkey="hide_qr"`
therefore wrote `hide_qr = true` for a **visible** block.

The change handler had the inversion right. It was clobbered a moment later,
because that sync runs on every block selection, on every live preview, inside
`peSerializeState()` — the unsaved-changes fingerprint, which runs **on load** —
and inside `paBlocksCollect()`, **which is how it reached the save**. Measured
against the shipped build: open a product, touch nothing, and block 1 comes back
flagged hidden.

**THE RULE, AND WHY IT IS THE RULE RATHER THAN A SECOND INVERSION.** The fix is
not to teach `paBlocksSyncFromDOM` about this one field's polarity. That
mechanism is general, and a special case inside it is the same trap rearmed for
the next inverted control somebody adds. **An inverted control carries no
`data-bkey`.** `paSetHideQr()` is now the only writer of the flag, both controls
go through it, and there is nothing left to race.

**THE EYE ON THE ROW IS NOW A BUTTON, because the mark could not do the job it
looked like it did.** §135 drew a struck-through eye on a row only once that
block was already hidden — a mark you cannot click to hide with. Ash went to
click it and there was nothing there. It is rendered on **every** row now: a
faint open eye that comes up on hover, the amber struck-through one when off,
`stopPropagation` so it does not also open the block, and the inspector's switch
is moved in place when the open row's eye is clicked so the two cannot sit side
by side disagreeing.

**WHAT WAS WRITTEN TO LIVE DATA, AND WHY NOTHING IS REPAIRED AUTOMATICALLY.**
Between deploy #2067 and this fix, opening a product and saving it flagged
whichever block was selected — the first, unless the office had clicked another.
`scripts/diagnose_hide_qr_flags.js` is **read-only** and sorts what it finds by
the accident's fingerprint: the fault always landed on **block 1**, and always
**alone**. A product whose only flagged block is the first is the shape of the
bug; a flag further down, or more than one, was a person. **A blanket clear was
considered and rejected** — it would undo the real ones set deliberately in the
same window, and the flag alone cannot tell them apart. The list is read, then
the accidents are cleared from the editor in one click.

**TESTS.** `scripts/test_product_editor_hide_qr.js`, nine checks, in the FAST
shard. It guards the invariant rather than the symptom: the QR switch carries no
`data-bkey`; **no other checkbox in that sync is inverted either** (both that do
ride it — `lead` and `alt` — are honest, and `alt`'s label reads "Inverted"
about how its card is painted, not about its polarity, which is written down
because that is exactly what a later reader trips over); every write to
`hide_qr` is inside `paSetHideQr`; it syncs before it mutates; the eye is drawn
unconditionally; and its click does not reach the row. Proved by mutation —
restoring `data-bkey`, gating the eye on `hide_qr`, and dropping
`stopPropagation` each fail the check meant to catch them.

**WHY IT IS A SOURCE TEST AND NOT A BROWSER ONE.** A Chromium pass proves more
and belongs in the slow shard, which is not run — here or in CI — by standing
instruction, and a suite that never runs protects nothing. The browser pass WAS
run by hand, against this change and against the shipped code before it: seven
steps covering hide from the row, select two other blocks without either
flipping, show the same block again, and the inspector switch agreeing both
ways. The harness stubs the admin API and is deliberately not committed.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.** No repair of existing rows. No change to
`lib/product-blocks-read.js`, `routes/shop-menu.js` or what the flag means to
the QR menu. No change to `paBlocksSyncFromDOM` itself. No schema, no migration,
and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §143 — THE FILE NAME IS THE WHOLE OF THE PERMISSION, SO A TEST HOLDS IT

**Found while running the block-field usage report against production,
2026-09-15.** `.github/workflows/ro-query.yml` — "Read-only prod query" — will
run ANY file matching `scripts/diagnose_*.js` against the LIVE database, and its
only gate is that file-name shape. The workflow's own header promises what such
a file does: *"The script it runs opens SQLite with `readonly: true` and PROVES
that on the connection by attempting a write and aborting if the write is
accepted."* **That promise lived in a comment and in each author's care, which
is not a mechanism.**

**IT HAD BEEN BROKEN TWICE.** `scripts/diagnose_hide_qr_flags.js`, written by
this session earlier the same day, opened the database through
`require('../database.js')` — the APPLICATION'S handle, opened READ-WRITE. It
never wrote anything, and it failed on the box for an unrelated reason: the
workflow stages the named script alone in `/tmp` and stubs `database.js`, so the
require threw `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. **The mistake surfaced as a path error rather
than as what it was**, which is exactly the argument for a test.
`scripts/diagnose_variant_descriptions.js` opened `data/roots.db` with no
options at all, so read-write by default. Both are fixed.

**WHAT IS ENFORCED, AND WHAT IS ONLY COUNTED.** `readonly: true` on every open
of the LIVE database is the load-bearing rule and fails the suite. The run-time
probe — attempting a write and aborting if it succeeds — is what turns that flag
into a fact, and 13 of the 58 scripts that open the live database predate the
promise. **Failing those would make the gate red on a main that is not actually
unsafe, and a suite that is red for a reason nobody intends to fix is a suite
people learn to ignore.** So the probe is counted and the shortfall named, where
the number is visible and can be driven down, and asked of new work at review.

**THE CHECKER CRIED WOLF TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, and both are recorded
because each is a way this kind of test goes wrong:**

1. **It failed seven file-and-HTTP diagnostics** that never open SQLite at all —
   they read the deployed tree, a diff, a server response. There is nothing for
   those to be read-only about.
2. **It failed three seam audits that open a writable SCRATCH database on
   purpose** (`s.db`, `scratch.db` in a temp directory) — writing to a throwaway
   is the whole point of auditing the database seam. The question asked of each
   `new Database(...)` is therefore not *"is it readonly"* but *"is this the LIVE
   database"*, keyed on `DB_PATH`, `ROOTS_DB` or a literal `roots.db`.
3. **And then it failed five CORRECT scripts because of its own regex.**
   `/new Database\([^)]*\)/` cannot see past the `)` that closes
   `path.join(...)`, so on
   `new Database(path.join(__dirname, '..', 'data', 'roots.db'), { readonly: true })`
   it matched only as far as `'roots.db')` and never saw the options object. The
   scan now balances parentheses. **A checker that cries wolf is one whose next
   real finding gets waved through**, which is why this is worth twelve lines
   and a paragraph.

**THE USAGE REPORT THAT STARTED IT** is `scripts/diagnose_block_field_usage.js`,
also landing here: per block type, every field the editor offers against how
many placed blocks carry a non-empty value. Its first production run found **30
of 78 fields in the product page editor never filled in by anybody across 260
products** — `accent_color`, `bg_color` and `fg_color` on all ten block types
that offer them. **Deleting them was proposed and Ash declined**, on the reading
that nobody using a control buried in a closed fold is not the same as nobody
wanting it. Recorded so the finding is not re-derived and the decision is not
re-opened.

**TESTS.** `scripts/test_diagnostics_are_read_only.js`, four checks in the FAST
shard, reading the workflow itself so it fails loudly if the gate is ever
renamed out from under it. Proved by mutation: dropping `readonly: true` from a
live open, and borrowing the application handle, each fail the check meant to
catch them.

**NOT DONE, so it is not assumed.** No change to `ro-query.yml` or to
`oneoff.yml`. No probe added to the 13 scripts that lack one. No field deleted
from either editor. No schema, no migration, and no change to `.gitignore` or CI.

## §144 — THE PRODUCT EDITOR IS A FORM, NOT A BUILDER — AND THE READING ORDER IS OFFERED, NEVER IMPOSED

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-15, from three working prototypes:** *"option a"*.

### What the data said, before anything was drawn

`scripts/diagnose_block_spine_order.js`, run read-only against production, over
the **260 of 342 products that carry any `description_blocks` at all**:

| share | products | type |
|------:|---------:|------|
| 99% | 258 | `hero_intro` |
| 93% | 242 | `spec_strip` |
| 90% | 234 | `how_to_use` |
| 89% | 231 | `notes_callout` |
| 87% | 225 | `ingredients_chips` |
| 86% | 224 | `why` |
| 84% | 218 | `storage_box` |
| 83% | 217 | `big_stat` |
| 73% | 189 | `allergen_card` |
| 8% | 20 | `nutrition_facts` |
| 5% | 14 | `pull_quote` |
| 3% | 8 | `recipe_steps` |
| 0% | 1 | `ingredients_line` |

`image_band`, `pairings`, `faq` and `stat_callout` are offered by the editor and
carried by **no product at all**.

**There is a cliff between 73% and 8%, and it is the whole argument.** Nine types
are on nearly every page; everything else is an exception. An editor whose main
gesture is *choose a block and place it* is asking the office to re-decide, 260
times, a thing that was decided once. So the nine become a spine that is always
on screen: written sections show their fields inline, unwritten ones show as a
named line carrying **how many of your products do say this**, so a gap reads as
ordinary or unusual without opening anything.

### The half that matters more: the stored order is preserved

The same run found **71 distinct block orders in use**. Against the commonest,
only **145 of 260 products (56%)** already sit inside it.

**So an editor that rendered a canonical order and saved it would silently have
reordered 115 live customer pages on first save, with no edit made.** That is
rejected outright, and it is the reason this section exists rather than being a
paragraph in the previous one.

**What is built instead:** placeholders for missing sections are inserted at
their canonical position *relative to the blocks the product already has*. **No
stored block is moved by rendering, by typing, or by saving.** Putting a page
into reading order stays something the operator does — now available as one
deliberate action that says what would move before it moves it.

**The canonical order is the house's own, not an invention.** It is what 74
products already carry:

    spec_strip > hero_intro > big_stat > why > ingredients_chips
               > allergen_card > storage_box > notes_callout > how_to_use

Note that it puts the spec strip **above** the opening paragraph. No whiteboard
would have chosen that; the catalogue did.

### The frequency is read live, never frozen into a constant

A percentage compiled into the source is a percentage that is wrong by next
quarter and that nobody re-measures. `GET /api/retail-admin/products/block-usage`
counts the tenant's own products on demand. If the endpoint fails the line is
simply absent — a wrong number is worse than no number.

### The risk this change carries, named rather than discovered

`paBlocksSyncFromDOM` read **one** form at a time: find the single
`[data-blockid]` in the mount, then write every `[data-bkey]` under that mount
onto that block. With nine forms on screen at once, it must scope per section,
and a scoping bug writes one section's words into another's — silently, on a
page the office cannot see is wrong until a customer reads it.

**§142 is the same family of mistake eleven days younger** (an inverted checkbox
riding a sync that means "the field equals the input"). So the invariant is held
by a test, not by care: `scripts/test_product_editor_doc.js` renders two sections
and proves that typing into one leaves the other untouched.

`paChannelFlip` and `paSetHideQr` carried the same single-form assumption and
move to the enclosing section with `closest('[data-blockid]')`.

### Options B and C are recorded, not discarded

Both were built as working prototypes before the choice was made.

**B — keep the block list, move the settings beside it.** Fixes *"things are too
far apart on screen"* and leaves the assembly work exactly where it was: nine
blocks placed and ordered by hand on every product, forever.

**C — the customer's page is the editor.** Defeated by the bilingual pair. Only
one language is ever on the customer's page, so editing in place hides the other
half of every field and makes a missing 中文 string invisible until somebody
switches. Chips, allergens and tables have nowhere to sit on a customer's page
either, so about a third of the editing returns to a panel — which is the form,
back again, with extra steps.

### Not done, so it is not assumed

No field deleted — the 30 never-filled colour fields stay, per v4.280, folded
rather than removed. No schema, no migration. No change to the mini app, the QR
menu or the web storefront: `description_blocks` is written in the same shape by
the same collector. No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how
sessions and builds work.

## §145 — A LABEL TYPED 724 TIMES IS A LABEL TYPED SEVERAL WAYS

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** shown the measurements and asked which of them
to build: *"do all as you recommend"*.

### What the catalogue said

`scripts/diagnose_spec_strip_labels.js`, read-only against production, over the
**724 spec-strip cells carried by 242 products**.

**The same label, typed several ways:**

| label | cells | its twin | cells |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| `Net Wt` | 163 | `Net Weight` | 29 |
| `Certification` | 5 | `Certified` / `Certifications` | 4 / 4 |
| 类别 | 14 | 品类 / 分类 | 6 / 5 |

Nobody was careless. That is simply what happens when a label is retyped 724
times on different days.

**The values were the bigger find, and not what anybody guessed:**

| under this label | cells | the dominant answer |
|---|---:|---|
| Origin | 156 | **Guangzhou, China — 109 (70%)** |
| Shelf Life | 57 | **See packaging — 46 (81%)** |
| Diet | 29 | **100% plant — 28 (97%)** |

**242 cells whose answer was typed out by hand, in two languages, every time.**
And "See packaging" came out in Chinese three ways — 见包装标示 38, 见包装 8,
请见包装标注 2 — all three sitting on live product pages.

### What is decided

**Two dropdowns per cell**: one for the label, one for the value, the second
depending on the first. That dependency is not a nicety — "Guangzhou, China" is
an answer to Origin and nonsense under Net Wt, so a flat list of values would be
worse than no list at all.

**A pick fills both languages.** This matters more than the typing it saves. A
typed label is one somebody can finish in English and forget in 中文, and
nothing on the English view shows that gap. A picked one cannot be half-done.

**`Type` is deliberately not offered beside `Product Type`.** They are not
spellings of each other — they are two labels for one idea, 66 and 64 cells,
holding the same answers ("Ready-to-eat spread" appears under both). Only one
can be offered or the split continues. `Product Type` wins on the Chinese, where
产品类型 (83) already beats 类型 (40).

**Net Wt gets no value list, on purpose.** 67 distinct weights across 163 cells
is exactly what a weight field should look like. Certification and Storage get
none either — 13 and 5 cells is too thin to draw a list from.

### Nothing rewrites a page that is already live

The 66 cells that say `Type` keep saying it. `peMount` never consults the list
on load and `paBlocksCollect` never consults it on save: the list is an **offer**
at the moment of editing and nothing else. Cleaning up what is already stored is
a migration with its own risk, and it is a separate decision that has not been
made.

Two details protect existing wording from the list:

- **The match is on the English only, and case-insensitive.** A cell reading
  `Net wt` is the same answer as `Net Wt` and is not shown as though somebody
  had typed something unusual.
- **The 中文 is not part of the test.** An existing cell may carry a perfectly
  good Chinese that the list happens to spell differently; demoting it to
  "Something else" would invite somebody to overwrite it.

### The pick is a convenience layer, never a second writer

The `k_en` / `k_cn` / `v_en` / `v_cn` inputs **never leave the DOM**. They still
carry `data-bkey` and `data-cellidx` and still ride `paBlocksSyncFromDOM`
exactly as they always have. The two `<select>`s write into those inputs and
never into the block.

So there is no second writer, no polarity to get backwards (§142), and free text
is not a special case — it is what the control already was, merely hidden while
a list answer is in force.

### One ordering bug, caught in a browser rather than in review

`paSpecPickLabel` must write the inputs **before** it syncs. Syncing first —
which is what every other handler on this page does, so it is the natural thing
to write — reads the OLD input values into the model, and `paRenderDoc` then
paints them straight back over the pick. Choosing `Product Type` left the cell
still saying `Net Wt`.

Source review did not catch it; driving the page did. It is now held by a test
that asserts the three steps appear in that order.

### Chinese

**None composed.** Every pair in both lists is lifted from production with its
count, declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.92. This is the
preference order in `CLAUDE.md` working out the easy way: the office had already
written every one of these words, hundreds of times.

### Not done, so it is not assumed

No migration of existing cells. No schema, no migration, no change to the mini
app, the QR menu or the web storefront — `description_blocks` is written in the
same shape by the same collector. No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything
governing how sessions and builds work. `hero_intro` was measured alongside and
deliberately gets **no list**: its kicker is 172 distinct answers across 248
fills, its highlight phrase 207 across 256, its body 217 across 258. That is the
catalogue's voice.

## §146 — A COST FILED UNDER NOTHING IS FIXED WHERE IT WAS DECIDED, NOT BY UNDOING IT

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16, from a live row:** a ¥299 staff claim — *"bai ·
take taxi to the office and Ramada"* — approved and in the books with no
category, and no control anywhere in the product that could give it one.

### What was actually broken, in order

1. `lib/expense-claim.js` never required a category, and does not now. The phone
   sends `category: x.cat || null`.
2. `/decide` read a `note` from its body and nothing else, so the approver could
   see a blank category and had no way to fill it.
3. The approval row printed the category **only when there was one** — so a claim
   filed under nothing and one filed under Transport drew the same meta line.
   The gap was not merely unfixable, it was invisible.
4. `routes/finance-transactions.js` refuses to edit a claim-posted ledger row.
   **That refusal is correct** and is not touched here: the row is a projection
   of the claim, and any value typed onto it is lost the next time the claim
   re-posts. But nothing could edit the claim either.

So the only way to file that ¥299 was to **void the claim and ask the employee
to send it again** — destroying the approval record to correct a classification.

### It is not a prompt on approve, and that is the decision

The obvious shape — *if the category is blank, ask for one when Approve is
clicked* — is **rejected**. It catches the empty case and waves the wrong case
straight through, and a category picked by a submitter who does not know the
chart of accounts is wrong at least as often as it is missing. Wrong data reads
as good data in a report; blank data announces itself.

**What ships instead is one control on the row, in both queues**, carrying the
claim's current category and editable before the decision and after it.

### Nor is the category made compulsory

Also **rejected**: requiring a category on the phone form, or blocking Approve
until one is chosen. Forced, the approver clears the queue by taking whatever is
at the top of the list. That trades a visible problem for an invisible one, and
the visible one is the cheaper of the two to live with.

The claim form stays as it is. The approver — the person who keeps the books —
is who the picker is for.

### Why an uncategorised row is not merely untidy

`routes/finance-summary.js` gives a blank category **its own "Not recorded" line
and counts it as OPERATING**, because an unlisted cost is a real cost until
somebody says otherwise. A private or non-operating expense that arrives without
a category therefore inflates the operating total silently. Re-filing is the only
thing that moves it, and until this section there was no way to re-file.

### What re-filing is, and what it is not

**No money moves.** Same claim, same sum, same date, same person, same approval
record. `postClaim` deletes the ledger row and writes it again — the shape it has
always had — so the ledger says what the claim currently says, and the row's
description is rebuilt from the submitter's name resolved before the write.

**A settled claim is still re-fileable, and that is the one place this route
parts company with `/decide` and `/void`.** Those refuse a settled claim because
they would take an expense out of the books while leaving the repayment made.
Nothing leaves the books here; refusing would mean a category could only ever be
corrected before payday.

**A claim that raised a purchase order is refused**, on `awaiting_delivery` as
well as `po_id`. It has no ledger row of its own — the order owns the cost, under
the *line's* category — so re-filing the claim would move nothing. The refusal
names the way out, which is `ERR.onOrder`'s own rule.

### The three things a later edit could quietly undo

* **`category = COALESCE(?, category)` in `/decide`.** A bare assignment blanks
  the category on every claim decided by a client that does not send the field —
  which is every client older than this change, and the phone until it reloads.
* **`expense_id` cleared in the same UPDATE, before `postClaim` runs.** §90's FK
  trap, third occurrence: the column still points at the row about to be deleted,
  and SQLite refuses the delete while it does.
* **The submitter's name resolved before the transaction.** `claimDescription`
  reads `submitted_name`, which no `staff_expenses` row carries. A re-post that
  forgot it would rewrite the ledger line stripped of the one fact that makes a
  ¥299 line answerable months later — whose taxi it was.

### Held in state, not in the DOM

A category chosen on a claim that has not been decided rides with the Approve
click rather than saving on its own — one request, so a second call cannot fail
and leave the ledger holding a classification nobody chose. Both queues re-render
for reasons that have nothing to do with the pick: opening the receipt, another
row's decision landing. Held in the `<select>` alone, **checking the photo before
approving would throw the pick away** — silently, at the exact moment the
approver was being careful. `FIN_APR_CAT` on the desktop and `state.apr.cat` on
the phone hold it, keyed by claim id, and the decision spends it.

### Who may re-file — either key, and the asymmetry it removes

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16**, on being shown that the route as first built was
gated on `expenses:approve` alone: *"anyone who can remove a claim from the books
can certainly rename the heading it sits under."*

The `bookkeeper` preset holds `expenses:cancel` and **not** `expenses:approve`
(that stays an owner/admin/manager default). So the accountant could take a claim
out of the ledger entirely and could not change the category it sat under — the
bigger hammer and not the small screwdriver, for the one role whose job this is
and which already types ledger rows by hand under `finance:record`.

`requireFiler` accepts either key. It is not a third capability, for the reason
`/settle` gives about sharing one: a key gating a single picker is one more row
in a matrix somebody has to understand. `lib/cap-routes.js` returns both, which
it already supports — five routes name a pair.

**A permission with no screen is not a permission.** The picker was first built
on the approvals queue, and `/pending` is gated on `expenses:approve` — which is
exactly the key the bookkeeper lacks. So the claim row on **Transactions** gains
the same control, beside the Void link that is there for the same reason (§90:
requested by Ash off that screen). That is also where the ¥299 was noticed.

**Void is hidden once a claim is settled; re-filing is not.** Voiding after the
employee has been paid back would take the expense out of the books while leaving
the payment made, which the server refuses. Re-filing takes nothing out. One row,
two controls, two different rules — and the settled case is where the difference
is visible.

**One thing was nearly wrong and is recorded so it is not reintroduced:**
`finTxCatOptions()` branches on the *form's* kind, so a claim row drawn while the
income form had last been opened would have been offered INCOME categories. The
expense half is now `finTxExpenseCats()`, asked without the form's question.

### The ledger row draws the picker, it does not link to one

**Amended by Ash, 2026-09-16, off the live screen:** *"why is it not similar?"*

It shipped with a `Change` link on the Transactions row, opening the picker one
row at a time, on the reasoning that a ledger window can hold dozens of rows and
a dropdown on each would turn a list somebody opened to READ into a wall of
controls. **That reasoning was wrong twice.** Claim rows are a small minority of
a ledger — purchase-order rows and typed rows are the bulk, and neither draws a
picker — so the wall never arrives. And one screen that hides a control behind a
link while the other shows it is two products, not one, for the same act.

The row now draws the same `<select>` the approvals queue draws, in the same
place: under the line that describes the claim. It carries the approval row's
own classes so the two cannot drift into two shapes for one control.

**Void stays in the actions column**, where it was. It is an action; this is a
field. It also keeps its own rule — hidden once the claim is settled, where the
picker is not.

**The link also shipped a rendering bug**, which is how it was noticed: the
actions cell had never held two links, so nothing separated them and the pair
rendered as `ChangeVoid` — one word, and the wrong one. Drawing the picker in
the row's own cell removes the second link rather than spacing it.

### Where it is NOT offered

Rejected and voided claims, and claims on a purchase order: none has a ledger row
of its own. A tenant with no accounting categories gets no picker at all rather
than an empty one — §36's empty-list rule.

## §147 — TWO SNOWFLAKES THAT LOOK IDENTICAL AND ARE NOT

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16.** The rule was set in advance — *"you pick,
most-used wins"* — then *"ok do it"*.

### The case nobody could have found by reading

Across the **218 storage boxes** in the catalogue:

| icon | left card | right card |
|---|---:|---:|
| `❄️` (U+2744 U+FE0F) | 83 | 55 |
| `❄` (U+2744 alone) | — | 5 |
| `🌡️` (U+1F321 U+FE0F) | 18 | — |
| `🌡` (U+1F321 alone) | 9 | — |

**These are the same two icons, typed with and without the invisible variation
selector.** On screen they are identical. To a string comparison, to a filter,
to anything that groups by value, they are different characters.

No amount of care finds that, and no amount of proofreading fixes it. A picker
ends it in one click. This is the clearest argument for the whole family of
change made since §145, and **nobody made it before the data was read** — it
came out of the measurement, not out of a design discussion.

### The rest, same method as §145

**Heads** (218 cells, 22 distinct left / 29 right) and **units** (49 / 64
distinct) become lists with free text. **The big word stays typed** — it is a
per-product figure, a temperature or a count of days, and a dropdown there is a
dropdown nobody can find their product in.

**Most-used wins**, which was Ash's rule, set before the data was shown:

| kept | cells | dropped | cells |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| `Refrigerate` | 52 | `Keep refrigerated` | 13 |
| `Shelf Life` | 57 | `Shelf life` | — |
| `After Opening` | 41 | `Use After Opening` | 16 |
| `Freeze for longer` | 9 | `Freeze` / `Freezing` | 8 / 7 |
| `Unopened` | 11 | `Before Opening` | 6 |
| 冷藏保存 | 59 | 冷藏 | 12 |
| 阴凉干燥 | 34 | 置于阴凉干燥处 | 16 |

Every loser is recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.94 rather than
quietly dropped.

### The note list is deliberately two entries long

The note field has **77 distinct answers**, and the usage report truncated the
long ones. Pairing an English sentence to its 中文 would therefore have meant
**guessing which belongs to which** — the one thing this method exists to
prevent.

Only the two printed whole are offered. A test refuses a list that grows past
four without a fresh measurement, so the next person to add one has to go and
look rather than fill it in from memory.

### The picker §145 built is now general

This is the structural half. `_paSpecInputs` becomes `_paPickInputs`, and every
picker on the page sits inside one `[data-pickscope]` marker: a spec strip's
three cells, a storage box's two cards, and its note. **Five scopes can be on
screen at once, each carrying a `head_en`.**

That is §144's bug and §142's before it, at a smaller scale. The same mistake
has now been available twice on this page, so there is **one** helper rather
than two copies free to drift apart.

**The list name reaches the handler as a name, never as source.** It is written
into an inline `onchange` attribute, so it resolves against a fixed map and
never through `eval`. An attribute value must not reach the JS parser.

### Nothing rewrites a live page

Per Ash's standing answer when asked — *"lists only, for now"* — `peMount` never
consults the lists on load and `paBlocksCollect` never consults them on save. A
card saying `Keep refrigerated` keeps saying it, and shows as typed rather than
as an error.

### A mutation that passed, recorded because it taught something

Four mutations were run against the new suite. Three were caught by the check
meant for them. The fourth — replacing the icon input's scoped lookup with an
unscoped `document.querySelector`, so clicking the right card would write the
left card's icon — **passed**, because the check asserted that the scope line
existed rather than that it was used.

The check was tightened and the mutation now fails it. Recorded because a
mutation that passes is the only way to learn that a check was testing the wrong
line, and the instinct on seeing it is to assume the mutation was badly chosen.

### Not done, so it is not assumed

No migration of existing cards. No schema, no migration. No change to the mini
app, the QR menu or the web storefront. No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or
anything governing how sessions and builds work. `free_of` and the allergen card
are the next two pieces of the same brief and are deliberately **separate PRs**:
they touch different screens, and the allergen wording carries a decision that
should be readable on its own.

## §148 — THE ESCAPE HATCH TOLD US WHAT THE LIST WAS MISSING

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** asked whether a fully vegan shop should offer
these at all: *"add all three as checkboxes"*.

### What the tail said

The Free-of boxes have been `Nuts · Soy · Gluten · 5 Spice` and nothing else.
Anything else gets typed into the free-text tail, which `pdFreeOfSet` preserves
rather than dropping.

Reading that tail on production says exactly what the list lacks:

| typed by hand | products |
|---|---:|
| `animal products` | 75 |
| `dairy` | 15 |
| `egg` | 14 |
| `5spice` — a spelling twin of the `5 spice` **checkbox** (154) | 16 |

**This is the escape hatch doing its job**, and it is the argument for always
building one. A list without a tail teaches people to pick the nearest wrong
answer, and nobody ever learns the list was short.

### The question Ash was asked, because it is not obvious

The shop is fully vegan — stated in `public/product-editor.html`. So *free of
animal products / dairy / egg* is true of all 342 products, and yet only 75 say
so. Either it is a marketing line applied deliberately, or it is arbitrary.

Ash's answer keeps it a per-product editorial choice: **offered, never
assumed.** Which is what the office is already doing by hand — the change is
only that it stops being typed.

### The two lists must agree, and that is what the suite is really for

These flags are drawn **twice**, from two files that know nothing about each
other:

- `PW_FREE_OF` in `public/retail-admin/09-products.js` — the new-product wizard
- hand-written markup in `public/retail-admin.html` — the details panel

Both write into the same `free_of` column, keyed by id. **A flag added to one
and not the other is a flag a product can be given in the wizard and silently
lose the next time the details panel is saved**: the panel would not recognise
the token, park it in the free-text tail, and never tick the box. Nothing goes
red. The product just quietly stops claiming something.

`scripts/test_free_of_options.js` compares the two lists directly.

### A suspected bug that was not one

Recorded so it is not re-investigated. `pwReviewHtml` renders these flags
through `cuT(en, cn)`, which reads as though the wizard stores a
language-dependent **label** — meaning a product created while the interface was
in 中文 would store `无坚果` and the panel would not recognise it.

It does not. That `cuT` is the review screen's display. `pwFreeOfStr` maps
`([id]) => id`. The two paths already agreed; a test now holds them there.

### The typo fold is on read only

`5spice` ticks the `5 spice` box when a product is opened, and the next save
writes the canonical spelling. **Nothing sweeps the catalogue** — per Ash's
standing answer, *"lists only, for now"* — so a product nobody opens keeps
saying what it says.

### Chinese

One composed string, two lifts.

- **无动物成分** — lifted verbatim from `miniapp/pages/faq/faq.js`
- **无乳制品** — lifted verbatim from `miniapp/pages/product/product.js`
- **无蛋** — **composed**, on the live `无X` shape its five siblings already
  use, over the rejected 无鸡蛋 and 不含蛋. Declared in
  `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.95.

### Not done

No sweep of existing values. No schema, no migration. No change to the mini app,
the QR menu, the web storefront, `.gitignore` or CI. The allergen card is the
third piece of this brief and is a separate PR: its wording carries a decision
that should be readable on its own.

## §149 — PEANUTS AND TREE NUTS ARE NOT THE SAME ALLERGEN

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** asked about this one specifically rather than
shown a usage count: *"Peanuts and Tree nuts separate"*.

### The one block where a wrong word has a consequence

The catalogue had **five words for nuts**:

| word | cards |
|---|---:|
| `Nuts` | 55 |
| `Tree nuts` | 36 |
| `Other tree nuts` | 15 |
| `Other nuts` | 14 |
| `Peanuts` | 7 |

**These are not spelling variants.** Somebody allergic to peanuts is often fine
with almonds, and the reverse. A customer reading `Nuts` cannot tell which they
are being warned about.

So **most-used-wins was deliberately not applied here.** It decided every other
list from §145 to §148; here the most-used word is the one being dropped. That
is why Ash was asked rather than shown a count.

**The 55 cards saying `Nuts` are not rewritten.** They keep their wording, the
editor shows it as typed, and they become a visible worklist instead of a silent
inconsistency.

### A finding that changed an answer already given

Asked which of three hand-typed sentences should be the single form for *nothing
to declare*, Ash chose `None declared` / 未声明常见致敏原, from:

| typed | cards |
|---|---:|
| `None declared` | 43 |
| `None` | 15 |
| `No known allergens` | 8 |

**Reading the renderers afterwards shows all three surfaces already print
`None declared` / 未声明 when the contains row is blank.** Each carries its own
copy: `lib/product-blocks-read.js`, `public/shop/product-blocks.js`, and the
mini app's product-blocks component.

Two things follow, and the first was mine to have found before asking:

1. Those 66 cards produce a **chip** saying what the empty state says quietly.
   The system has always had a fourth answer, and it was not among the three
   offered.
2. **The built-in Chinese is 未声明**, not the 未声明常见致敏原 Ash was shown.
   What would print is not what he picked.

**His choice is implemented through the mechanism that already exists** rather
than by adding a fourth variant: the form now says in both languages that
leaving both boxes empty prints it. The three surfaces are held in agreement by
a test — a product that reads one way on the counter menu and another in the app
is exactly the difference a customer with an allergy would notice.

### Quick-add chips, not checkboxes

The discussion said checkboxes; this is a deliberate departure and the reason is
the data shape.

Both rows are **one comma-separated string**, and the catalogue is more specific
than any checkbox: `Tree nuts (hazelnuts)`, `Sesame (tahini), Legumes
(chickpeas)`. A checkbox would have to decide whether `Tree nuts (hazelnuts)`
counts as ticked — and un-ticking it would have to decide what to delete.
**That is how an allergen line gets silently truncated.**

A chip **appends and never removes**, fills both languages with each one's own
separator (`, ` and `、`, both already read by `_paSplitChips`), and is a no-op
when the term is already present. The text stays editable underneath, so a
person does any deleting.

### A mutation that walked past its check, for the second time

Four mutations were run. Three were caught. The fourth — a removal written as
`split(term).join('')` — **used none of the method names the check forbade**,
so it passed.

The check stopped naming methods. It now pins the invariant instead: **the field
is assigned exactly once**, inside the only function that can grow it. A second
assignment anywhere is a second thing that can happen to an allergen line.

This is the second time in two sections (§147 was the first) that a mutation
revealed a check watching the wrong thing. Both are recorded because the instinct
on seeing one is to assume the mutation was badly chosen.

### Not done

No rewrite of existing cards. No schema, no migration. No change to the mini app,
