the QR menu or the web storefront — only a test that holds their three copies of
the empty state in agreement. No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything
governing how sessions and builds work.


## §150 — THE COUNTER SELLS WHAT THE SHOP HAS AND WHAT THE SHOP MAKES

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** reported from a Tianhe till: *"i cant see the
products made in the location in the counter till"*.

### What was wrong

The counter till built its list from the catalogue filtered to `is_published`,
joined to the location's shelf. That flag is the **online store's**. §42 puts a
counter on the other side of it and the public QR menu has read it that way
since §47:

> is_published governs the ONLINE STORE; a shop listing governs the SHOP.

Nothing made at a location is sold on a website. So nothing made at a location
was ever published, so nothing made at a location reached a till — and ticking
it published to force it onto the screen would have put a latte on the website
and still drawn it greyed out, because a made-here listing has no shelf record
by design and the till reads a missing count as zero.

### What the till shows now

Three sources, one list:

1. **This location's menu**, at the listing's own price (§42). A `made_here`
   row is never stock-gated: its stock is `null`, not 0, and §42's manual
   switch is the whole of its availability, exactly as §47 says.
2. **Anything counted on this location's shelf**, published or not. Publishing
   is a decision about a website. It has never had anything to do with whether
   a cashier may sell a box somebody put on the shelf in front of them.
3. **Everything the till already showed.** Named so the change is additive: no
   tile a cashier can see today disappears.

**A listing governs its product absolutely.** Where a listing exists it decides
the price, the mode, and whether the row appears at all. A product switched off
for the day is ABSENT — not shown two rows lower at the catalogue price, which
is what merely concatenating the two halves would have done.

### Why not menu-only

That shape was put to Ash and refused, in his words:

> people might order from the mini app products that offered in the warehouse of
> that location, the till will not show them because they are not on the menu
> list

The mini app already sells that location's warehouse stock. A till narrowed to
the menu would take the walk-in customer's sale off a shelf the app is selling
from. **The counter is where anything physically present can be sold; the menu
is a subset of that, never the whole of it.**

### What was deliberately not changed

- **`shops.is_active`** is not consulted. It governs the `/s/:shopCode` page —
  switching a QR menu off is a statement about a public URL, not about whether
  the counter may ring up a coffee. The till's own closed-store gate is
  untouched.
- **The order path.** `resolveManualOrderLines` resolves on `is_active` alone
  and has always taken a per-line `unit_price`. The till posts one on menu lines
  and only on menu lines: a listing's price is the one figure that endpoint
  cannot resolve for itself, and posting its own number for every line would
  charge a stale price whenever the office corrected a catalogue price between
  two reloads of the tablet.
- **The containment around `shop_listings`.** The new route lives in
  `routes/retail-shops.js` for the reason `/products/:id/shops` gives there: a
  reader in `public/till.html` would have forced the allowlist open, and a
  reader here widens nothing. The till fetches the route and never names the
  table.

### Not done

No schema, no migration, no new table. No change to the mini app, the QR menu or
the web storefront. No new UI string in either language. No change to
`.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds work.


## §151 — A LOCKED DATABASE IS NOT A SIGNED-OUT OPERATOR

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** shown the finding and asked whether to fix it:
*"fix it"*.

### How it was found

A test failed once. During the §150 build, one parallel run of
`npm run test:fast` reported `scripts/test_manual_restock_park.js` failing
`401 !== 200`. It passed alone, and passed on three later full runs.

**A flake is not a root cause**, so the code was read instead of re-run.

### What was wrong

`requireRetailAdmin` wraps its two control-plane queries — the operator row and
the tenant row — in a try/catch written for a first boot, where `tenant_users`
does not exist yet and the gate must not 500. The catch swallowed **everything**
and fell through to `401 Not authenticated`.

`SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked` is an error. And `public/retail-admin/01-core.js`
sends a 401 to `/backend/login` without asking. So a moment of write contention
signed an operator out mid-task, and nothing in the answer mentioned a database.

The suites share one sqlite file, which is why a test met it first. Production
has one file and several writers too.

### What ships

`lib/sqlite-errors.js` tells the two cases apart, and the gate answers each one
honestly:

- **Schema not ready** → falls through to the same 401 as before. That refusal
  is correct: there is nobody to be signed in as yet.
- **Anything else** → `503`, code `service_busy`, and a log line.

**Matched on the message, not the code**, and that is forced rather than chosen:
better-sqlite3 gives `no such table` and `no such column` the generic
`SQLITE_ERROR`, which a constraint violation and a syntax error also carry. The
match is narrow on purpose — anything unrecognised counts as a real failure, so
a miss costs a first boot one wrong status, where the opposite default would
put the original bug back.

### The same swallow, one floor down

Found by grepping for the pattern rather than closing the finding on the one
`file:line` it arrived as. `lib/require-cap.js`'s `loadCaller` catches
everything around its tenant read. A swallowed error there leaves `tenant` null,
which sends `resolveOperator` to the **shipped preset** instead of the tenant's
own edited role — a request then allowed or refused on capabilities nobody
granted. **A silently wrong permission decision is worse than a failed one.**
Both catches are narrowed to the schema gap they were written for.

### A claim made and withdrawn in the same build

The first draft also moved `next()` out of the try and said this fixed a second
bug: a handler throwing synchronously, after its write had landed, reported as a
login problem.

**It did not.** A mutation putting `next()` back inside the try changed no
status the suite could see — express catches a handler's throw at the layer
boundary and turns it into `next(err)`, so it never reached this gate.

The code stays, because this catch should be about this gate's own two queries
and nothing downstream of them. The comment now says plainly that it fixes
nothing observable. A comment claiming a bug that does not exist is how the next
reader is sent hunting for one.

### What the operator reads

`service_busy` → *The system is busy right now — try again in a moment.* /
系统繁忙,请稍后重试。 One composed string, declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.97 with the three live alternatives it
beat: they blame the operator (操作过于频繁, 尝试次数过多) or describe a read
only (加载失败), and the person clicking did nothing wrong.

### Not widened

**401 remains the only status that sends anybody to the login page**, and every
ordinary refusal — no such operator, an inactive one, a suspended tenant — is
still exactly 401. A fix to a gate must not quietly open it, and a test holds
each refusal.

### Not done

No schema, no migration. No change to the mini app, the QR menu, the web
storefront, `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds work.

## §153 — A PICK-ANY QUESTION CAN NOW SAY HOW MANY

**Decided by Ash, 2026-09-16,** from a screenshot of the product editor showing
a three-choice group headed *Choose 2 crunchy sides · 爽脆配菜（选2款）*:
*"need to limit how many can choose. in this example can choose only 2 from the
3 option."*

### What was wrong

"Pick any" (`retail_product_options.type = 'multi'`) took **any** number of
answers, including none. The sentence *Choose 2* lived in the label and nowhere
else: the sheet let a customer tick one side or all three, and the checkout
accepted whichever arrived. The label promised two; the kitchen packed what came.

`is_required` was the only control, and it is a yes/no — it can say *at least
one*, never *exactly two*.

### Two numbers, not one

`min_choices` and `max_choices` on the option row. **0 on both is no limit**,
which is what every group written before today carries, so nothing already
authored changes shape.

**A maximum alone was asked for and is not what was built.** With `max = 2` and
nothing else, a customer ticks one cracker and checks out — the label still
promises two and the complaint still arrives, one control later. *Choose 2* is
`min 2 / max 2`, and a floor is the half a customer is actually blocked by.
Adding the second column later would have meant a second pass through the same
seven files.

`is_required` and the floor say the same thing and are **kept in step on save**:
a floor of 1 or more IS required, and Required with no floor means a floor of 1.
Single-answer questions are untouched — a radio is exactly one by construction.

### The floor is not absolute, and that is the whole trap

*Choose 2 crunchy sides* with two of the three sold out cannot be answered. An
unanswerable required question does not make a product unbuyable here — it stops
being a floor. Both storefronts and the counter menu are served a floor already
**clamped to the choices still pickable**, and the checkout measures pickability
the same way.

**Clamp one side and not the other and the endpoint refuses the very order the
page told the customer to place**, with nothing on screen able to explain it.
That is the assertion `scripts/test_option_limits.js` exists for. It is the same
principle §120 states for a question whose answers have all been deleted: a
question with nothing to answer it is not asked.

### The limit is not a client-side nicety

The sheets grey out the tick-box that would break the ceiling and block the Add
button under the floor — and every checkout path checks both again against the
database, where a post straight at the endpoint cannot skip it. Both paths, not
one: the QR menu's basket (`routes/shop-menu.js`) and the customer order-create
plus add-to-a-live-order (`routes/retail.js`). A limit enforced on one of two
checkouts is not a limit.

A **repeated choice id counts once**. A tick-box is on or off, so posting it
twice is one answer — counting the repeat would refuse a correct line, and
counting it toward a floor would let one side satisfy a request for two.

### One module for the rule

`lib/option-limits.js`. The save path normalises what the editor posts; the menu
and both checkouts clamp. The browser clients deliberately get **no copy of the
arithmetic** — they are handed the already-clamped numbers and obey them. A
limit the client computes is a limit the client can compute differently.

`addonAvailabilityById()` in `routes/retail.js` was extracted from the product
response for the same reason: the floor needed to ask "is this extra still on
the shelf" and a second copy would have been a second answer.

### What was deliberately not changed

- **The wizard (`pw*`) offers no limit control.** It is the simplified flow; a
  group it creates has no limit, exactly as before. The full editor is where a
  limit is set.
- **`is_required` is still not enforced by `routes/retail.js` order-create.**
  That gap predates this work and is a separate change — a floor of 1 or more
  now closes it for pick-any groups, and nothing else moved.
- **`public/shop.html` still does not grey out a sold-out paid extra**, although
  the server has answered `addon_available` since §120's follow-up. The mini app
  does. Recorded here rather than fixed: one PR per change.
- **No per-choice quantity.** Two sides cannot both be corn chips. That is a
  different feature reaching the order lines, and nothing here walls it off.
- No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds
  work.

## §154 — A POLL IS SOMETHING YOU MADE, NOT A SETTING

**Decided by Ash 2026-09-17**, from three page directions drawn against the
design system and put to him on a canvas: *"lets go with c"*.

**THE ARCHETYPE IN `tacet-ia-blueprint.md` §4 ROW 24 IS WRONG, AND THIS SECTION
AMENDS IT.** Voting is filed there as an **A4 Console**. It is not one. A poll
is written, published, run and closed — an authored object with a lifecycle,
which is the definition of an **A2 Library**, and its editor is an **A3
Composer**. The tell is in the Console's own rules: a Console opens on a master
switch with the consequence in words, and **Voting has never had a master
switch** — there is no on/off for this feature anywhere in the code. Drawing the
Console faithfully meant inventing one, and a rule that can only be satisfied by
inventing a control is a rule pointed at the wrong page. The genuinely
Console-shaped part of Voting is two settings (the intro tagline and whether
customers see vote counts), and two settings do not make a Console — they make a
card at the foot of a Library. **A later survey that finds Voting rendering as a
Library has found this decision, not drift.**

**WHAT THE OLD PAGE DID, named because each one is a rule already written down.**
It opened on its settings card, so the first thing an operator saw was
configuration rather than what customers were saying. Its title was a
`text-transform: uppercase` eyebrow and its state pills were uppercase too
(§1.6 — there is no licensed uppercase in Tacet). Under the title sat a
four-line bilingual paragraph describing what the page was for, which is the
purpose line §1.7 cut product-wide. An **open** poll was painted `#E96174` — a
pink-red off the palette entirely, for a state where nothing is wrong (§1.10:
colour is state, and that colour says *error*). **Featured** was a black chip
with lime text, which is neither a Tacet colour nor a status — featured is a
property, and properties get neutral treatment. Editing a poll injected a tall
form above the list, so the thing being authored and the list it came from were
on screen at once; §1.13 sends anything with a draft state to a full page.

**WHAT SHIPS.** The live poll **is** the page: its question at 22px, its
turnout, and a bar per option with the leader in Ink — the one question an
operator opens this tab to answer, in the first screenful, with no list to read
first. Everything else — drafts, other open polls, closed ones — is a quiet
shelf below it, one row each with the single action that row actually needs
(Publish a draft, Close an open one, Reopen a closed one) plus Edit. The two
settings fold away at the foot behind a disclosure. Authoring is a **full-page
takeover** (§1.7a): the shelf is `display: none` while it is up, so the page's
Dusk CTA is gone from the tab order rather than sitting live underneath, and the
browser Back gesture is trapped to return to the shelf — the same mechanic the
product lightbox already uses. The editor carries a **phone preview** that
settles at 200ms as fields change, because the merchant is authoring for their
customer's phone. **One Dusk element per page**, and on the editor it is the
commit; every other control is Secondary or Ghost.

**THE DOUBLED LANGUAGE FIELDS ARE GONE.** The old editor stacked `Question · EN`
beside `问题 · 中文`, `标签` beside `Label`, for every field — a form that is half
noise to both readers, and §1.11's own failure in form. The editor now has one
language picker at the top of the question group, and the fields below it are in
whichever language you picked. The picker itself shows both words, which is
§1.11's single licensed exception: it is the control for choosing, not a label.

**THE SHIELD IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN SILENTLY.** Every echo of
merchant-authored text on this page — a question, an option label, a meta line
built from them — is wrapped in `data-no-i18n`. The live language walker treats
` · ` with Chinese on the right as an `English · 中文` pair and blanks one half;
an English question followed by a Chinese option label is exactly that shape, so
a poll named in one language and answered in the other would have half
disappeared in the language nobody had open, with nothing in the console. The
old code escaped this text but never shielded it.

**Every write control disables while it writes**, with the button captured
**synchronously at the top of its handler** rather than read after the confirm
dialog resolves — §1.12's shape C, where `event.currentTarget` is null by the
time an awaited handler reads it and the disable silently no-ops. Four of this
page's five write paths run a confirm first, so all four would have had it.

**FRONT END ONLY. No schema, no migration, no server change** — `routes/retail.js`
already served everything this page needs, including the display-vote floor
whose real→shown arithmetic the editor mirrors exactly rather than
approximating. The mini app, the web storefront and the QR menu are untouched.

**96 STRING PAIRS, 38 lifted and 58 composed**, declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.106 with the three contested word choices
and their rejected candidates. Every noun and verb is a lift; what is composed
is the consequence line beside each control, which the old page did not have in
either language.

**THE SUITE HOLDS THE RULES, NOT THE PIXELS.** `scripts/test_voting_page.js`,
**69/69**: the header contract, the absence of every dead-brand signature by
name, each badge's colour against the state it encodes, both halves of every
label pair, the synchronous button capture on all four write paths, the
takeover's `display: none`, and the arithmetic — who leads, and what the
customer will be shown — driven in a sandbox against hand-built polls. **Proven
non-vacuous by four mutations**, every one caught: an amber open pill, an
`adminWrite` call that never disables its button, a leader on a poll with no
votes, and a display floor that shrinks real turnout. The render half drives
the real templates through a DOM stub rather than a browser, because the
browser shard is not run here and a template that throws on its first real poll
is exactly what static checks cannot see. `test:fast` 269 → **270**; lint 0
errors. No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything else governing how sessions
and builds work.

## §155 — A BILINGUAL PAIR IS ONE TEXT NODE, AND A TAG INSIDE IT BREAKS THE PAIR

**Found in production 2026-09-17**, hours after §154 shipped, by Ash looking at
the page: *"there is some chinese here."* An English screen was rendering a
Chinese sentence.

**THE MECHANISM, because the symptom looks like a translation bug and is not.**
§1.11's walker works on **text nodes**. It considers a node only if it contains
` · ` (space-middot-space), and splits it when the left half is Chinese-free and
the right half is not. The hint that leaked was written correctly as a pair —
but with markup in the middle of it:

```html
<span>Write <code>{pts}</code> where the points number goes … no republish. ·
      在需要显示积分数字的位置写 <code>{pts}</code> —— 它会自动填入…</span>
```

That is not one text node. It is five. The third one holds the ` · ` and gets
split correctly, so the English half looked right and the swap appeared to work.
The **fifth** — everything after the second `</code>` — contains no ` · ` at
all, so the walker never touches it, and it renders in **both** languages
forever. Half a sentence in Chinese, sitting under an English label, on a screen
the operator explicitly set to English.

**Nothing errors, nothing logs, and the English reader is the one who sees it.**
The Chinese reader sees a screen that is entirely Chinese and correct, which is
why this can survive review by whoever can actually read it.

**THE RULE.** An `English · 中文` pair is **one text node**: plain text, no
elements inside it. Copy that needs markup — `<code>`, `<b>`, a link — is not
written as a pair at all. It is written as **two blocks, one per language**,
each marked `data-lang-block="en"` / `data-lang-block="cn"`; the i18n engine
already hides whichever is not current (`10-extras.js`, the `html[data-ui-lang]`
rule it injects at init). That mechanism existed and was in use elsewhere; what
was missing was the reason to reach for it.

**This is not the same failure as `data-no-i18n`, and the two are opposites.**
`data-no-i18n` shields text the walker must NOT touch (outside-system strings).
`data-lang-block` declares text the walker does not need to touch because the
markup already carries both halves separately. Reaching for the shield here
would have produced the same bug it was meant to prevent: both languages glued,
permanently.

**IT IS CHECKED, not remembered.** `scripts/test_voting_page.js` §10 scans every
text node in the Voting section: each run of Chinese must either sit in a proper
pair (left half Chinese-free) or inside a declared `data-lang-block="cn"`. The
language picker's own `中文` label is the single allowed exception, and it is
named in the check rather than pattern-matched. The check was proven by
re-introducing the exact broken markup, which it catches.

**Scope, stated honestly:** the check covers the Voting section only. The same
shape is almost certainly live elsewhere in the admin — any hint that puts a
`<code>` or a `<b>` inside a bilingual pair has it. Widening the scan is a
separate pass on a separate ratchet, not something to bolt onto this one; what
this section buys is that the next person meeting the symptom has the mechanism
written down instead of rediscovering it from a screenshot.
## §156 — THE PAGE IS THE FORM, AND EVERY SHOP FILLS ITS OWN LISTS

**2026-09-17 · Decided by Ash**, from the automatic design feature: *"seems that
now need to fill up some information in product page editor so that the
automatic design feature will work well. seems like waist of time."* Then, shown
the survey and the proposal: *"this need to work for every tenant not just for
roots, so how we do it if im a new tenant what i will see"* — and, on the
answer: *"ok lets do it"*.

### The measured fault, first, because it is smaller than the decision

**Two doors reach the same compose endpoint and they do not carry the same
load.** The products sheet (`pdAutoComposeBlocks`, `public/retail-admin/09-products.js`)
fills the five Product-details boxes from the description first via
`/api/retail-admin/ai/extract-facts`, then posts the description AND the weight
AND those five boxes. The product page editor (`peAutoFillFromKitchen`,
`public/product-editor.html`) posts the product id, both names and the category —
and nothing else — although `GET /api/retail-admin/products/:id` has already
handed it `product_facts` and `weight AS size` in the same response it mounted
from.

The compose prompt in `routes/ai.js` names those facts *the source of truth* for
`spec_strip`, `storage_box`, `ingredients_chips` and `how_to_use`. So the
editor's door asks the model to guess what the office already typed, three
screens away. **That is the "waste of time" in one sentence: the editor's design
is worse because the editor forgets to send what it is already holding.**

Three smaller faults live in the same function and are named here so they are
not read as style. It adds the product to `_peAutoFilledFor` **before** the
fetch, so a failure cannot retry in that session. Every failure is silent by
design — the catch is empty and commented as a convenience. And **no control
anywhere in the editor runs the compose against the product's own description**:
`Smart paste` asks the office to paste in text the database is already storing.

### But the doors are not the decision

Fixing the doors makes the current flow work as drawn. It does not remove what
was complained about, because the shape is the fault.

**A product's content lives in three places today**: the prose description, the
five Product-details boxes, and the designed page. The machine copies the first
into the second into the third. That is the whole "automatic design", and it
sets a trap with no good exit — edit the description and the page is marked out
of date, press Rebuild and **the rebuild replaces the page**, taking every hand
edit with it; edit the page instead and the description drifts away from what
the customer reads. The office keeps two documents in step by hand and the AI is
the courier between them.

Two measurements already in this file say what to do about it. §144 found the
same nine sections on 73–99% of products and a cliff to 8% — **nobody composes a
page, everybody fills in the same one.** §145 found the answers barely vary:
Origin is *Guangzhou, China* on 109 of 156 cells, Shelf Life *See packaging* on
46 of 57, Diet *100% plant* on 28 of 29. **Most of what the AI "generates" is
either a default that could have been filled for free, or a pick from a short
list.** The genuinely written part is three sections: the opening paragraph, the
why, and the notes.

### What is decided: the sections are the only form

1. **A new product's page opens already carrying what the platform knows.** Net
   Wt from the weight field. Origin from the shop's own city. No AI call, no
   wait, and right most of the time.
2. **One box of raw material** — *anything you have about this product*: a
   supplier blurb, label text, scattered notes, either language or both. It is
   material, not a second truth to keep in step.
3. **One button: draft the empty sections.** The model writes **only what is
   blank**, reading the raw material *and the sections already filled*. It never
   touches a section carrying words. Pressed again next week it fills whatever
   is still blank.
4. **The plain description becomes derived** from the sections on save, in both
   languages, so the not-yet-republished mini app and the `use_block_design: 0`
   fallback never render an empty page. Derived, not authored — nothing to keep
   in step.
5. **"Out of date" and "Rebuild" retire with the copying.** There is nothing
   left for the page to be out of date *with*, and no pass that replaces work.

### What makes it work for a tenant that is not Roots

This is the half that was asked for second, and it is the half that decides
whether the feature ships at all.

- **§145's value lists are Roots' catalogue compiled into source.**
  `PA_SPEC_VALUES` in `public/product-editor.html` names *Guangzhou, China*,
  *See packaging*, *100% plant*. A candle shop in Shanghai opening its first
  product would be offered a Guangzhou origin and a vegan claim as its
  defaults. **So the values stop being source.** They become a tenant-scoped
  count over that tenant's own spec cells — the same shape
  `/api/retail-admin/products/block-usage` already uses to print *N% of your
  products say this*. Roots' list stops being code and becomes what the counter
  computes from Roots' own products: the same answers as today, arrived at
  honestly instead of typed in once.
- **Labels stay in source; values do not.** *Net Wt · 净含量*, *Origin · 产地*,
  *Shelf Life · 保质期* are what the section IS, and they are neutral in any
  trade. The answers belong to the tenant.
- **The seed for a shop with no history is that shop's own setup**, never
  Roots'. `retail_stores.city` — what the setup wizard writes from its City box —
  is what Origin suggests. Suggested, one tap to change. Nothing else is
  pre-filled, because nothing else is known.
- **The colophon is gated on having one.** `PA_IP_CHARACTERS` is ten of Roots'
  own mascots backed by files under `public/brand/ip-*.jpg`. A tenant with no
  characters sees no grid and the fold does not open — not an empty grid, and
  never Roots' radishes on somebody else's page.
- **The voice is already split and this does not re-open it.**
  `composeSystem(shop)` in `routes/ai.js` gives Roots the plant-based Guangzhou
  sentence and every other tenant a neutral one carrying their own brand name,
  with the animal-emoji ban applied only where it is true.

### What a new tenant sees on day one

Stated plainly, because it is the test of the whole decision. Nine empty
sections. **No percentages** — there is nothing of theirs to count yet, and §144
already rules that a failed count prints no number rather than a wrong one. Net
Wt filled from the weight they typed. Origin suggesting their own city. One box
for whatever they have, and one button. **No Guangzhou, no diet claim, no
mascots, no Roots.** By their tenth product, their own answers are their
defaults.

### The food shape is not solved and is not pretended to be

The nine sections are food sections — allergens, ingredients, storage,
nutrition. Every tenant on the platform today sells food, so that is what is
built. A non-food tenant needs a second spine, and that is a later decision with
a real signup behind it rather than a guess made now. Recorded so nobody reads
silence as coverage.

### What does not move

- **§144's invariant is untouched.** No stored block moves by rendering, typing
  or saving; `scripts/test_product_editor_doc.js` holds it, and the defaults
  above are inserted at their canonical position exactly as `paDocWrite` already
  inserts a written section.
- **§145's 66 cells that say `Type` keep saying it.** Nothing here rewrites a
  live page. A learned default is offered on a NEW product, never written over
  an old one.
- **Nutrition keeps both homes** — the block and the `nutrition` column —
  exactly as §144 left it.

### Build order — three PRs, and the first is useful on its own

1. **The editor sends what it holds.** Weight and `product_facts` into the
   compose call, the facts filled first when empty, a visible *draft the empty
   sections* control with the fill-only-blanks rule, and failures that are loud
   and retryable. Relief today, and step 3 of the new flow.
2. **The shop fills its own lists.** Tenant-counted spec defaults replace the
   compiled value lists; the city seed; the colophon gate.
3. **The derived description on save**, and only then the five boxes leave the
   sheet — last, once nothing reads them.

No change to `.gitignore`, CI, or anything governing how sessions and builds
work.


### AMENDED 2026-09-17, in the building (v4.291)

Three things in the decision above did not survive contact with the code. They
are recorded here rather than edited into the text, so what was decided and what
was learned stay separable.

**The city seed is withdrawn.** The decision seeds a new tenant's Origin from
the shop's own city. Two objections, the second fatal: `retail_stores.city` is
stored in whichever language the setup wizard was filled in, so the seed could
fill only half a bilingual pair — precisely what §145's dropdowns exist to
prevent — and **the shop's city is not the product's origin.** Roots' 109 of 156
holds because Roots makes what it sells; a Shanghai shop reselling Vietnamese
goods would be handed a false provenance as its default. The rule stated three
paragraphs above it — *nothing pre-filled that we do not actually know* — decides
against it. A new tenant's Origin is empty on product one. The Net Wt seed goes
for the same reason: a weight typed as `250g` has no Chinese half to offer.

**"Net Wt gets no value list" stops being a named exception.** §145 gave that
field no list because 163 cells held 67 distinct weights. A per-tenant count
cannot carry a hard-code for the words *net wt*, so the judgement is read off
the data: an answer must have been used **twice** before it is offered back. A
field of one-offs collapses to nothing — §145's point, now self-applying to any
field and any trade — while the three or four sizes a shop actually repeats do
become a list, which §145 never argued against.

**The colophon was three leaks, not one.** The decision named the character
grid. Grepping the pattern rather than trusting the citation — the house rule at
the head of this file — found three more, one of them worse than the one named:

- `_paResolveColophonChar` resolved through Roots' category map to a literal
  `soilsoul` fallback, so a tenant who had chosen nothing got Roots' character
  drawn onto their page **by default, with no operator action at all.**
- `From Soil to Soul` and `Roots · ESTD 2017` were printed into the live
  preview, and again into the template thumbnail's colophon — a SECOND render,
  missed on the first pass and found by a test that counts them.
- The tagline input offered Roots' slogan as its placeholder, to everybody.

All of it now comes from `GET /api/retail-admin/brand/signature`: Roots' cast,
line and name byte-identically, and for every other tenant its own name, no cast
and **no invented slogan** — a shop's motto is not something a platform can
supply, and printing one it made up is worse than printing none.

### Still Roots' in source, after this PR

Named so that silence is not read as coverage.

- **§147's storage-box lists** — `PA_STORAGE_HEADS`, `PA_STORAGE_UNITS`,
  `PA_STORAGE_NOTES` — are the same fault one section over, and the next PR.
  Held meanwhile by a check in `scripts/test_spec_strip_picklists.js` that fails
  if a fourth such list is added.
- **The mini app carries its own copy.** `miniapp/pages/product/product.js` has
  the category map, the `soilsoul` fallback and the Roots tagline written into
  it, so the CUSTOMER-FACING page still signs every tenant's product as Roots.
  That is a separate surface needing a WeChat release, and it is the more urgent
  of the two: the editor leak was seen by the office, this one is seen by the
  shopper.

## §157 — THE SWEEP §155 ASKED FOR, AND THE TWO SHAPES IT FOUND THAT §155 DID NOT

**Ash, on §155's own scope note — *"the same shape is almost certainly live
elsewhere in the admin"* — 2026-09-17: *"ok do it"*.** This is that sweep.

**SCOPE, established before anything was counted.** The bug needs the language
walker, so only surfaces that run one can have it. Grepping for the engine's own
`hasChinese` guard found **three**: `public/retail-admin.html` (the engine lives
in `10-extras.js`, with a second copy inline in the page), the
`public/retail-admin/*.js` modules that inject markup into it, and
**`public/product-editor.html`, which carries its own copy of the same walker**
and would not have been found by looking at the admin alone. Pages that do their
own translation with `T()` — the mini app's `m.html`, `cms.html`, the storefront
— cannot have this bug and were not scanned.

**FOUND AND FIXED: 16 elements, 19 leaked text nodes.** Fifteen in
`retail-admin.html`, one in `02-settings-ops.js`. Every one of them a helper or
hint paragraph — Settings, Delivery, Shop, FAQ, Media, the mini-app pages — where
a `<b>`, `<em>`, `<strong>` or `<code>` sat inside the pair. The product editor
was clean.

**THE SWEEP FOUND TWO SHAPES THE ORIGINAL SECTION DID NOT NAME**, which is the
argument for sweeping rather than fixing the one you were shown:

1. **A Chinese glyph in the English half.** *"…fill in both EN and 中. · 顾客会根据
   微信语言偏好…"* — the walker's guard is `if (!hasChinese(cn) || hasChinese(en))
   return;`, so a single 中 in the English half makes it **refuse the node
   entirely** and both languages render. The tag shape strands the tail; this one
   strands the whole sentence. Fixed by rewording the English to *"fill in both
   the English and the Chinese"* — the Chinese half is untouched.
2. **Dynamic data inside the pair's Chinese half.** `Stock staff · 库存员 —
   ${name}` splits into `Stock staff` and `库存员 — 门店名`, so **the store's name
   is present in Chinese and absent in English**. Nothing looks broken in either
   language; the English screen is simply missing a fact. The name now sits
   outside the pair, shielded with `data-no-i18n` as outside-system text.

**THE GATE: `scripts/check-glued-language.js`, two ratchets.** It parses text
nodes with an element stack, so a shield on an **ancestor** counts, and it scans
each module's template literals **one at a time** — concatenating them, which the
first draft did, invents elements that never shared a parent and produces a page
of nonsense findings.

| ratchet | budget | why |
|---|---|---|
| **broken** — Chinese stranded after a tag inside a pair | **0** | structural, unambiguous, swept today |
| **orphan** — Chinese in a node that is neither a pair nor shielded | **234** | a real backlog that needs a person per string |

**THE ORPHAN BACKLOG IS NAMED, NOT HIDDEN, AND IT IS NOT ZERO ON PURPOSE.** Those
234 nodes are three different things and only a reader can tell them apart: a
Chinese-only hint whose English half was never written (the Reviews page has
several); a pair glued with no separator at all, so the walker never sees a pair
(*"(for screen readers and SEO)(用于读屏与 SEO)"*, *"Body — 中文"*); and text that
is **correctly** Chinese under §1.11's own scope note — the preview of a WeCom
card, or a quoted WeChat menu path (*"mp.weixin.qq.com → 功能 → 订阅消息"*), where
the reader of that surface cannot choose a language. Clearing it means writing
new English strings and making a judgement per string, which is a separate pass.
**Counting it at its current size is what stops it growing** while that pass
waits, and that is the half that binds new work.

**PROVEN BY THREE MUTATIONS, one of them the real thing:** the exact markup that
shipped the production bug, restored verbatim — caught; a brand-new Chinese-only
hint — caught; a Chinese tail injected from a module template — caught. **An
earlier pair of mutations MISSED, and that is recorded because it changed the
gate.** They removed a `data-lang-block` attribute, which does not recreate the
bug — but working out why exposed that the gate as first written failed only on
the structural shape and would have let a plain Chinese-only leak through. The
orphan ratchet exists because a mutation that proved nothing about the code
proved something about the test.

**NOTHING WAS MINTED.** Every Chinese string in this change is the one that was
already there, moved. The single copy edit is English. `docs/tacet-delivery-
vocabulary.md` is deliberately untouched, and a reader looking for a v1.108 that
matches this section will not find one because there is nothing to declare.

**RENUMBERED FROM §156 WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN.** The product-editor
session merged its own §156 (*The page is the form*) into main first, so this
took the next free number rather than renumbering theirs — section numbers are
permanent, and the one that lands first keeps it. Its changelog entry moved from
v4.292 to v4.294 for the same reason. This is the third time the numbering rule
has been exercised by two sessions building at once, which is what the
enumerate-first rule in `CLAUDE.md` exists to make visible.

`test:fast` **272 on the merged head** — this gate is one of the two suites added
today, the other being the product-editor session's; lint 0 errors. No schema, no
server change, no change to `.gitignore` or CI — `package.json` gains the checker's npm alias, matching
`verify:swallowed-errors`, and that is the only line outside the sweep itself.


## §158 — NOBODY'S PRODUCT PAGE IS SIGNED BY SOMEBODY ELSE

**2026-09-17 · Decided by Ash**, on the item §156 recorded as owed and named as
the more urgent of the two: *"do it"*.

### What it was

§156 took Roots' illustrated cast, house line and name out of the product page
editor, and listed in its own *still Roots' in source* section that
`miniapp/pages/product/product.js` held its own copy of all three.

**The mini app is published once per tenant, each under its own WeChat AppID**
(`miniapp/utils/api.js`), off this one shared codebase. So those literals were
not Roots' page signing itself. They were every merchant's **shopper-facing**
product page signing itself as Roots — and the category map's `soilsoul`
fallback made that the default rather than an edge case: a shop that had chosen
no character had Roots' mascot drawn onto its product, with nobody having
touched anything.

The editor's leak was seen by the office. This one was seen by the customer,
which is why §156 named it the more urgent half.

### One module, because a second copy of an answer is a second answer

Which is the fault itself, repeating one surface along. `lib/brand-signature.js`
holds the cast, the category map, the fallback, both taglines, the house line
and the resolver. It is read by **both**:

- the operator route the editor asks — `/api/retail-admin/brand/signature`
- the public storefront config the phone asks — `/api/retail/config`, as
  `cfg.colophon`

The public side resolves its tenant with `resolvePublicTenant(req)`, the same
x-wx-appid-then-host resolver that had already entered the ALS scope for that
very request. **A customer request and an operator request therefore cannot be
answered differently**, and on both a null tenant means Roots — the same
equivalence `composeSystem(shop)` in `routes/ai.js` already relies on, because
the kitchen realm carries no tenant row and the kitchen is account #1.

### Roots is byte-identical, and that is asserted rather than intended

All ten characters in order, both taglines, the house line, every category
mapping and the `soilsoul` fallback. Every character's image file is also
checked to exist on disk: a colophon that renders a broken tile is not an
improvement on one that renders somebody else's mascot.

### The duplication that remains is the RULE, never the DATA

A WeChat bundle cannot require from `lib/`, so `resolveColophonCharacter()` in
the page is a real and permanent second copy of `resolveCharacter()` — the same
permanent duplication `scripts/test_nutrition_rows.js` exists for, and it says
so in its own header. It is **lifted out of the shipped file and executed**
against the server's copy over 144 combinations of signature, override and
category, including a malformed map that must break neither.

The data cannot drift at all, because the cast, the map and the fallback arrive
over the wire. That is the part worth having.

### Two bugs caught by reading rather than assuming

Both would have shipped, and both are the kind a review reading the diff would
have called fine.

1. **`recomputeDisplay()` has no `app` of its own.** The `getApp()` above it
   lives in a different method, so the first draft's `app.globalData.config`
   was a **ReferenceError on every product page** — not a degraded colophon, a
   dead page.
2. **`app.globalData.config` is only set once the launch fetch resolves.**
   `app.js` fires it fire-and-forget on purpose (onLaunch step 4) so a page can
   paint before it lands, so the product fetch racing it would have left
   **Roots' colophon blank at random on a cold launch.**

Both are fixed the same way: read through `config.get('colophon', {})`, which
hydrates from the persisted last-good copy and so answers on the first paint of
any launch after the first that ever completed.

### What is drawn, and what is not

Each part hides itself when the shop has none, and the block hides itself when
the shop has nothing: no character, no line and no name is not a colophon, it is
three empty elements and two hairlines.

An override the office typed is honoured **as typed**, cast or no cast. It is
the product's stored choice, and second-guessing it would unsign a page somebody
deliberately signed — and would drop a character a shop uploaded after this
signature was cached.

### This does not reach a customer by itself

A mini-app change ships only after `node scripts/upload_miniapp.js` and a
release in the WeChat console, which is Ash's to do. The deploy puts the server
half live at once, and **an un-republished build keeps drawing its old colophon
until then — Roots' either way**, which is what makes that order safe rather
than merely convenient.

### Still outstanding

§147's `PA_STORAGE_HEADS`, `PA_STORAGE_UNITS` and `PA_STORAGE_NOTES` are
untouched by this and remain the next PR, still held by the check §156 left in
`scripts/test_spec_strip_picklists.js`.


## §159 — THE STORAGE BOX'S WORDS BELONG TO THE SHOP THAT TYPED THEM

**2026-09-17 · Decided by Ash**, on the remainder §156 named and §158 left
standing: *"fix whatever left them deploy live"*.

### The last of the compiled lists

§147 gave the storage box four pick lists exactly as §145 gave two to the spec
strip, and for the same measured reason. They carried the same fault one section
along: `PA_STORAGE_ICONS`, `PA_STORAGE_HEADS`, `PA_STORAGE_UNITS` and
`PA_STORAGE_NOTES` were Roots' catalogue written into the editor —
`Refrigerate · 冷藏保存`, `See packaging · 见包装标示`, `开封后请密封保存。` —
offered to every tenant on the platform, including one that sells nothing
perishable at all.

They are counted per tenant now, by `GET /api/retail-admin/products/storage-usage`.
**Roots' lists are not lost**: they are recomputed from the 218 storage boxes
that every number in §147's own comments was measured off in the first place.

### One counter, not two

`lib/pair-usage.js` holds the arithmetic both vocabularies share — tally
bilingual pairs, keep the commonest spelling of each, drop what does not repeat.
Writing it twice would be two rules that agree until they don't. `blocksOfType()`
likewise reads the `description_blocks` column once for both counts, and the
spec-usage handler was moved onto the shared module in the same pass, so the
rule has exactly one home rather than an original and a copy.

### The snowflake is the finding

This is the part that could have been silently undone, and it is why this was
not a tidy-up.

§147 exists because **❄ and ❄️ look identical and are not** — the second carries
U+FE0F, and the catalogue holds 83 of one and 5 of the other. A count keyed on
the exact string tallies them as **two** answers and offers **both** — extending
the very drift the picker was built to end.

So the single-value counter folds the variation selector before counting and
returns the commonest exact spelling. A test proves it over rows, and removing
the fold turns that test red. It was caught by §147's own suite failing on its
anchor rather than passing vacuously, which is precisely what that suite was
built to do.

### Five tallies, and the split is load-bearing

`Refrigerate` is a LEFT head and `Shelf Life` is a RIGHT one. Offering either on
the wrong card would be offering an answer to a question nobody asked. The icon
is tallied as a single value rather than a pair, because an emoji belongs to no
language — rule 1 cannot apply where there is no second half to be missing.

### Nothing to offer means no control, not an empty one

On a shop's first product every one of these lists is empty, so this is the
NORMAL state for a new tenant rather than a corner. A select whose only entry is
*Something else — type it* is a dropdown that cannot be used, sitting above the
boxes it would have filled. `_paPickField` renders the typed pair alone and
`_paIconChips` renders nothing, which is exactly what these fields were before
§147 gave them lists.

### What is deliberately left

`PA_TEMPLATES` and the preview/thumbnail samples still carry food wording, as
`num_en: 'Refrigerate'` and the like. **A template is a starting design the
office picks and previews before applying; a pick list is an answer offered as
though it were measured.** The first is the food-shaped part of this editor that
§156 already recorded as not solved and not pretended to be, and it is not
touched here. The test that checks for leaked list answers therefore matches on
list shape (`{ en: '…'`) rather than on a bare substring — `num_en:` ends with
`en:`, and a looser check reports the templates as the fault.

### Two suites rewritten, not weakened

- **`test_storage_box_picklists.js`** lost the seven checks that read a literal —
  every icon carrying its selector, no icon twice, the snowflake matching across
  cards, heads and units being pairs, the losing twin, case collisions, the note
  list staying short. All seven were claims about data the editor no longer
  holds, and all seven are now asserted against the counter that produces it,
  over rows, which is a stronger claim than a literal ever made. Everything it
  says about the pick MECHANICS stays, untouched.
- **The check §156 left in `test_spec_strip_picklists.js`** naming these three
  constants as the known remainder is **deleted**, exactly as its own comment
  instructed on the day they were counted.
- `test_spec_vocabulary_tenant.js` now lifts the shared block reader alongside
  the handler, so it still executes the shipped code rather than a stub.

### What this closes

With §156, §158 and this, no pick list, character, slogan or house name in the
product editor or the mini app is Roots' by compilation any more. The food shape
of the nine-section spine, and of the templates, remains — recorded, not fixed.

## §160 — A SAVE BUTTON THAT DOES NOT SAVE: §111 PART TWO IS WITHDRAWN

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-17), on the mechanism he had himself decided four days earlier
(§111 part two, v4.244/v4.245). Asked what the *Ordered from a supplier* checkbox was for
and whether it could go, having been told it is read nowhere else: *"yes remove it"*.

**IT LOST REAL MONEY, TWICE, BEFORE ANYONE WENT LOOKING.** Reported from the Yuexiu
office: August employee social insurance, ¥3,818.22, typed into Transactions —
*"它保存的时候就跳到了PO。两次都一样的问题。我在PO和财务都没查到这笔记录"* (on save it jumped
to PO; same problem both times; the row is in neither Purchasing nor Finance). It was in
neither because it was never written. `员工社保 Employee Social Insurance` carried a stored
`needs_po = 1`, so the question was never re-put and Save silently became Navigate: the
Purchasing wizard opened on a new order carrying the cost as a typed line, the bookkeeper —
correctly, social insurance not being a supplier purchase — did not place an order, and the
cost went nowhere.

**§111 PART TWO PREDICTED THIS AND CALLED IT THE BETTER OUTCOME.** Its own record: *"Walk
away and nothing was recorded in either place, which beats an orphan draft nobody returns
to."* That trade is wrong, and this is what it costs. An orphan draft is visible, listed,
and recoverable by anyone who opens Purchasing. An abandoned form is none of those things:
there is no row, no draft, no log line carrying the amount, and nothing on any screen that
would bring somebody back to it. The only trace the mechanism leaves of a lost cost is the
`activity_log` line recording that the CATEGORY was answered — which does not carry the
money. A failure mode with no artefact is not the cheaper of two failures; it is the one
that cannot be found.

**THE FLAG WAS ALREADY WRONG ON A SECOND CATEGORY AND NOBODY KNEW.** Read off the live
Categories screen in the same conversation: `Electricity 电费` also carried `needs_po = 1`.
An electricity bill is not ordered from a supplier. The next one recorded in Finance would
have been lost exactly as the social insurance was, and there was no screen, report or
alert on which that was visible as a pending fault — only the tick itself, on a settings
row nobody reads until something has already gone wrong.

**AND ITS OWN OPERATORS COULD NOT TELL AN ANSWER FROM A DEFAULT.** Asked about the tick,
the office replied *"这个选项是系统默认的"* — this option is the system default. It never
was. `addColumn('categories', 'needs_po', 'INTEGER')` carries no default and the create
route never sets it, so a new category is NULL and every 1 on that screen is a human
answer to the dialog. §111 part two rested entirely on the three states being legible —
NULL *nobody asked*, 1 *ordered*, 0 *not ordered* — and in the field the distinction did
not survive contact with the people using it. A mechanism that teaches its operators the
opposite of how it works is not teaching the rule it was built for; it is teaching them
that the screen is not worth reading.

**WHAT IS WITHDRAWN IS THE INTERCEPTION, NOT §111.** The ruling that what is ordered from
a supplier belongs on a purchase order stands, and parts one and three of §111 are
untouched. What goes is the attempt to enforce it *at the moment a cost is recorded*. The
person in Transactions is booking money that has already left the account; the Purchasing
wizard raises an order that has not happened yet. Steering the first into the second is
the wrong direction at the wrong moment, and §111 part two half-conceded it already — it
deliberately refused to BLOCK, on the grounds that a bookkeeper may hold `finance:record`
without `purchasing:edit`. Having given up the power to stop the wrong thing, the prompt
kept only the power to lose the row. The moment to steer a purchase onto a PO is when
somebody is buying.

**WHAT IS REMOVED.** The question (`finTxAskOrdered`), the lookup (`finTxNeedsPo`), the
answer write (`finTxRememberAnswer`) and the jump (`finTxToPurchasing`) in
`22-finance.js`; the *Ordered from a supplier* checkbox on Categories with its
indeterminate third state and `finCatPoFlag`; `PUT /finance/categories/answer` entire;
`needs_po` off `listCategories` and off the PATCH; `category_needs_po` off the ledger
payload; and `puNewOrderFrom` in `16-purchasing.js`, whose only caller was the jump — dead
code left behind by a removal is part of the removal. Money out now writes a ledger row,
always, which is what the form's button says it does.

**THE COLUMN STAYS, RETIRED RATHER THAN DROPPED.** `categories.needs_po` keeps its
migration and its stored values, with the comment rewritten to say it is dead and why.
Dropping a column in SQLite is a table rebuild, and removing the `addColumn` instead would
leave every existing database carrying a column that new ones lack — an asymmetry that
outlives the byte it saves, and the kind of divergence that makes the next schema question
unanswerable. Nothing reads it. If §111's intent is ever rebuilt at the buying end, the
answers are still there.

**TWO SUITES DELETED, NOT MOVED.** `test_finance_po_question.js` (31 cases) and
`test_finance_po_question_client.js` (41 cases) tested this mechanism and nothing else;
with the mechanism gone they assert the behaviour of code that no longer exists. This is
not the forbidden move — nothing red is being relocated somewhere it will not run. Both
were green, and both are removed along with what they covered.

## §161 — A DUPLICATED PRODUCT CARRIES ANOTHER PRODUCT'S PAGE, AND NOW SAYS SO

Reported by Ash, 2026-09-17: *"i dublicate a product, then i change all the info in
the product edit page them i click auto fill, then i go to product editor, all info
there still from the dublicate product, not the new iunformation i added. once i
clcik product editor i get a window pop up say this page might not be saved"*.

**THREE FAULTS WORE ONE SYMPTOM.** Two were mechanical and are recorded here only
because they made the third invisible.

1. `pdOpenPageDesign()` opened the editor without flushing the pending autosave.
   The editor re-fetches the product with `cache:'no-store'`, so anything still
   inside the 800ms debounce was not in the row it read. *Auto-fill from text*
   ends on `pdScheduleAutosave()`, so clicking straight through landed inside that
   window every time. `pdOpen()` and `pdRecipeLinkOpen()` already flushed; this was
   the one exit that did not.
2. `openProductEditor()` re-pointed the editor's **iframe** `src` with no word to
   the editor, so the editor's own `beforeunload` guard fired and the browser asked
   its generic question. That is the popup in the report — and **Cancel there aborts
   the navigation**, leaving the previous product on screen with nothing said, which
   is the other half of "it ignored my changes".
3. The real one, below.

### THE DECISION: DUPLICATE KEEPS COPYING THE PAGE. THE COPY IS MARKED INSTEAD.

Copying `description_blocks` is correct and stays. A 500g/1kg size variant wants the
same page, and that is most of what duplicate is for. **The rejected alternative was
to stop copying it**, which would have broken the common case to fix the uncommon one.

What was missing is that the copy had no way to SAY whose page it was carrying.
Nothing in the classic product form writes to `description_blocks`, so a copy whose
name, price, description and Product details had all been changed still opened the
Product editor holding the original's words, unmarked.

**`store_products.blocks_from_product_id`** — an `INTEGER`, normally NULL, added
through `addColumn` in `database.js` per the README's migration convention. Set by
the duplicate endpoint, and **only when there were sections to copy**: stamping a
copy of a product with no page would print "came from X" over an empty page.

**IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE ROW, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** The editor already had a
session-local *"Designed page is out of date"* nudge. It answers a different question
— *has this been edited since it was built?* — and it dies on every reload. A warning
you have to re-earn by typing is not a warning about a duplicate, which arrives wrong
before anybody types anything.

**THE MARK IS THE SERVER'S TO SET AND THE SERVER'S TO CLEAR.** It is deliberately
absent from `PRODUCT_PATCH_ALLOWED`: a request body does not get to assert this about
itself. It is cleared on **every** write of `description_blocks`, not on a rebuild
specifically — there is no write that leaves it true, and a client that had to
remember to clear it is a client that will one day forget.

### AND A FOURTH, CAUGHT ON REVIEW OF THE FIX ITSELF

The out-of-date nudge had gated on `use_block_design`. That flag only decides which
of the two descriptions the **shopfront** draws; the sections exist either way and the
Product editor shows them either way, so a copy whose source had *Design: Off* went
unwarned. Re-gated on the sections existing.

**That change put the nudge's Rebuild button within reach of a product showing its
classic description — which it never was before — and `pdAutoComposeBlocks()`
hardcoded `use_block_design: 1`.** Pressing Rebuild there would have quietly moved
shoppers onto the designed page: a button offering to refresh some words would have
changed what the shop shows. The flag is the operator's decision, made with the Design
switch, and is not a side effect of rebuilding. `pdAutoComposeBlocks()` now takes
`keepFlag`; the two callers that genuinely mean *turn it on* — the switch itself and
the wizard's "designed page" option — are unchanged.

### VOCABULARY

One pair composed: `Designed page came from X · 设计页来自 X`, declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.112 with both lifted halves and the live
candidates rejected. The compact summary row keeps the existing locked pair.

### COVERAGE

`scripts/test_product_duplicate_fields.js` section 5 runs the shipped duplicate
handler against a real in-memory database: the copy keeps its sections, records its
source, leaves the source unmarked, replies with the mark, and is **not** marked when
there was nothing to copy (`NULL` and `'[]'` both). `scripts/test_product_editor_open_
freshness.js` asserts the rest against source — the flush, the iframe handover, the
gate, `keepFlag`, and that the clear rides on the `description_blocks` write itself.
Every case red-proofed against the tree before the fix.

## §164 — A RECIPE IS NOT ONLY A COST, AND THE KITCHEN NEEDS THE HALF THAT ISN'T

Asked by Ash, 2026-09-17, while choosing how the desktop Recipes screen should land
on the phone: *"the only thing is that cost section should be only accessable per
role permission . kitchen staff for example can't reach there"*.

### THE FINDING: THERE IS ONE KEY WHERE THERE SHOULD BE TWO

`lib/capabilities.js` gives every other section of this kind a PAIR — a view key that
opens the screen, and a costs key that reveals the money on it:

| opens the screen | reveals the money |
| --- | --- |
| `materials:view` | `materials:costs` |
| `products:view` | `products:costs` |
| `waste:view` | `waste:costs` — off in both floor presets |
| `recipes:view` | **nothing** |

And `recipes:view`, alone among the view keys, carries `money: 'shows'`. MONEY_NOTES
says why:

```
'recipes:view': ['A recipe is a cost.', '食谱本身就是成本。']
```

**That sentence is true of the screen as it stands, which is why the coin is on the
wrong KEY rather than simply wrong.** With no costs key to carry it, opening Recipes
at all IS seeing money. So there is no way today to grant a kitchen operator the
ingredients and the steps without also granting the batch cost, the cost per gram,
and the margin on every product the recipe makes.

### THE DECISION: MINT `recipes:costs`, AND MOVE THE COIN ONTO IT

```js
{ key: 'recipes:costs', group: 'run', section: 'recipes',
  labelEn: 'See recipe cost & margin', labelCn: '查看食谱成本与毛利', money: 'shows' }
```

Placed beside `recipes:view`, modelled line for line on `products:costs`.
`recipes:view` loses `money: 'shows'`, and `A recipe is a cost.` is retired from
MONEY_NOTES — reworded onto the new key, which is now the thing that sentence is
about.

**THE COIN COMES OFF ONLY TOGETHER WITH THE GATE, IN ONE PR.** The Recipes list
prints Cost, Cost per gram and the whole-batch fallback in columns of its own.
Dropping the mark from `recipes:view` while those columns still paint would mark the
key safe while it still shows money — worse than the state it replaces, because the
role editor's coin is the one place an assigner is told what a key reveals.

### IT GOES ON THE DESKTOP, NOT ONLY ON THE PHONE

`public/retail-admin/19-recipes.js` is 3,031 lines and contains exactly one
capability check:

```js
function canEdit() { return typeof can !== 'function' || can('recipes:edit'); }
```

Cost & Pricing is visible to everyone who can open the screen. A gate added only to
the phone is a gate somebody steps around by opening a laptop, and it would be
security theatre rather than a permission. Three surfaces, one PR: the desktop
sub-tab, the desktop list's cost columns, and — when it is built — the phone's cost
tab and its list columns.

### WHAT THIS TAKES AWAY ON THE DAY IT SHIPS, AND FROM WHOM

Adding a gate to a screen already in use removes something on deploy. `public/m.html`
states the rule for its own rows: *"A new row can be born gated; an old one cannot be
gated retroactively inside an unrelated build."* This IS that kind of change, made
deliberately and on its own rather than folded into an unrelated build. The blast
radius is small but not empty:

- `owner` holds everything.
- `admin` and `manager` are `ALL_KEYS` filters and pick `recipes:costs` up on the
  same deploy that mints it.
- No floor preset carries `recipes:view` at all — it is ticked on per person by name,
  the way `PRESETS`' own note already says.

What is left is the operators ticked on **by name** with `recipes:view`. **Before the
gate ships, that list is read off live data and each person is granted
`recipes:costs` or deliberately not.** No session can see that list from the
repository; it is checked on the box.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE

Not the mobile Recipes build — that is its own decision and its own PR, and this one
only says what the permission looks like when it arrives.

And nothing in `lib/cap-routes.js`. `requiredCapFor()` returns `null` for GET, HEAD
and OPTIONS — *reads open* — so `recipes:costs` is a CLIENT-SIDE read gate over data
the same endpoint already returns. Whether the API should withhold cost fields per
capability is a separate question nobody has asked yet, and inventing an answer here
would gate a dozen live readers on a decision made in passing.

### VOCABULARY

One pair composed: `See recipe cost & margin · 查看食谱成本与毛利`.

Both halves are the live `products:costs` pair — `See product cost & margin ·
查看产品成本与毛利` — with its one noun swapped for the noun `recipes:view` already
carries: 产品 → 食谱. Every character is lifted rather than minted: 查看 from five
sibling view keys, 食谱 from `recipes:view`'s own `查看食谱`, and 成本与毛利 from
`products:costs` untouched.

**Rejected:** `成本与定价`, the desktop record's own Cost & Pricing sub-tab pair. It
names a TAB, and this key is not the tab — it also gates the list's columns — and
定价 claims a pricing write the key does not grant.

The MONEY_NOTES sentence composed alongside it: `Recipes show batch cost, cost per
gram and margin. · 食谱显示整批成本、每克成本与毛利。` — 显示 and the sentence shape
from `products:costs`' own note, 整批 and 每克成本 from the Recipes list's live column
headings.

Composed by Claude under the fourth amendment's standing delegation. Both are
declared HERE, with their sources and the rejected candidate, and **locked in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` in the commit that ships the code, not before** —
that file records what is in the tree, and neither string is yet.

### COVERAGE

None yet: this is a decision ahead of its code, per CLAUDE.md's *decisions before
code*. The PR that implements it carries

- a test that `recipes:view` no longer carries `money` and that `recipes:costs` does;
- a test that the desktop Cost & Pricing sub-tab and the list's cost columns are
  absent without `recipes:costs` and present with it;
- the by-name grant list above, read off live data and acted on before merge.

### ADDENDUM, 2026-09-17 — the wire, and the data loss the screen gate armed
§164 above records that it deliberately did not gate the server: *"whether the
API should withhold cost fields per capability is a separate question nobody has
asked yet."* Ash asked, on being told the figures were still readable in the
network tab. This is that decision, and what implementing it turned up.
**THE WIRE.** All four reads strip money; the one write refuses it. The rules
live in `lib/recipe-cost-visibility.js`, extracted from the route the way
`lib/product-cost-visibility.js` was and for the same reason: a rule reachable
only by standing up a database is a rule that gets tested loosely or not at all.
Waste's and materials' three rules are followed to the letter so all three read
alike — fail closed, delete rather than zero, refuse a field rather than a
request — and `costs_hidden: true` rides the envelope.
**THE COST OBJECT IS ALLOW-LISTED.** Every other shape is built in the route, in
sight, where a `delete` beside its construction stays honest. `computeRecipeCost()`
is not: thirty-odd keys, fifteen of them money, and it has grown twice since the
first of them. A deny-list is a list of what was money on the day it was written.
**THE ONE 403.** Every column `PUT /:id/cost` writes is money, so a caller
without the capability has nothing legitimate to say there. That is the only
request in the file that is refused rather than answered with less.
**AND THE FINDING THAT MATTERED MORE THAN THE GAP.** §164's screen gate had
armed a silent data loss, live from the moment #669 deployed. `draftCostData()`
reads the Cost & Pricing inputs out of the DOM; §164 stopped rendering that tab;
an absent element reads `null`, and `parseFloat(null) || 0` is `0`. So an
ordinary autosave — after correcting a recipe's NAME — sent
`{labour: 0, overhead_pct: 0, sell_price: 0, target_food_cost: 30}`, and the
writer stored it. Labour, overhead and sell price wiped; every margin built on
that recipe with them.
No preset holds `recipes:edit` without `recipes:costs`, so the exposure was the
by-name grants alone — the same list §164 already asks to be read off live data.
**It should still be read now, and any recipe those operators saved between
#669 and this fix should be checked against its version history**, which is
intact: the loss goes through the ordinary cost write, so `recipe_versions`
holds the displaced state.
**OMITTING THE KEYS WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT.** `lib/recipe-cost-data-write.js`
grants preserve-on-absent to `packaging_type_id` alone and says so in terms:
*"an absent `labour` still writes 0, an absent `target_food_cost` still writes
30."* The packaging comment inside `draftCostData()` is about that one column
and does not generalise — reading it as a general rule is exactly how this bug
would have been "fixed" and left live. Not sending the request is the only shape
that preserves what is stored.
**COVERAGE.** `scripts/test_recipe_cost_visibility.js` — 106 assertions:
the registry, the presets, the screen, the wire, and both halves of the write
fix. Including that a money key added to `computeRecipeCost()` tomorrow does not
leak, that the product's sell price survives, and that no GET in the file 403s.

## §166 — A CHOICE THE CUSTOMER MAKES IS PART OF WHAT THE PRODUCT COSTS
Reported by Ash, 2026-09-17, working outward from the waste ledger: *"fresh meals
sometimes are waste without the dressing, we keep dressing many time in the
freezer"*, and then, on Beet Salad: *"beet salad is an example of a salad that we
offer to choose 2 types of dressing. the staff made a mistake and put both of them
inside the recipe."*
**THE SECOND REPORT SUPERSEDED THE FIRST, AND KILLED A FEATURE THAT WAS ALREADY
DESIGNED.** The first proposal was a tick on the material (*packed separately, can be
kept*) and a two-chip question on the waste sheet that subtracted the dressing's share
when the answer was *kept*. It was measured and worth about ¥65 a month
(`scripts/diagnose_dressing_waste.js`, live, 2026-09-17: ¥121.93 written off in
thirteen days, of which ¥27.65 was separately-packed dressing). **It is withdrawn.**
It was a workaround for the dressing being buried inside a recipe, and once the
dressing is its own stocked product a binned salad is a binned salad and a binned
dressing is its own record. No tick, no question, no subtraction. **Waste is the one
reader this section does not change.**
### WHAT THE LIVE DATA SAID
`scripts/diagnose_dressing_waste.js` and `scripts/diagnose_option_cost_gap.js`, both
read-only against production:
- **Beet Salad is the only genuine instance.** Five recipes carry two or more
  dressing-ish lines; the other four (Tabbouleh Bowl, Marinated Tempeh, Seitan,
  Ginger Tahini) genuinely contain all of theirs. The data fault is ONE product.
- **And it is not a waste problem.** Beet Salad's recipe holds `Beet salad dressing`
  (¥3.11/unit) and `Ginger Tahini` (¥2.10/unit) against a ¥6.22 base, so the product
  carries ¥11.43 where the truth is ¥8.31 or ¥9.33 — **20–27% too high on every sale,
  at a ¥48 price**, not merely on the two that were thrown away.
- **The hole this opens is much wider than dressings.** 54 live option choices carry
  a `stock_product_id` — a real shelf, reserved one per unit by `expandStockLines` —
  and only 15 can be priced at all. 542 of 6,393 order lines (8.5%) carry options.
  `routes/finance-summary.js` had already written the gap down in its own words:
  *"OPTIONS carry a price delta with no cost counterpart."*
### THE DECISION: MODEL THE CHOICE AS A CHOICE, AND GIVE ITS COST SOMEWHERE TO LAND
A recipe describes one fixed thing. A choice is not a recipe line, and a recipe
holding every branch of one is wrong in a way that cannot be rounded away. So:
1. **The recipe holds the salad WITHOUT the dressing.** Each dressing becomes a real
   product and a stock-linked option choice. This is DATA work, and it is Ash's:
   neither `Beet salad dressing` nor `Ginger Tahini` exists as a product yet.
2. **`retail_order_items.options_cost_at_sale`** — a new snapshot column, ¥ per unit
   of the line, written by `lib/option-cost.js` `chosenOptionCostYuan()` at every
   sale path that records options.
3. **The catalogue answer is the DEAREST required choice**, not the chosen one and
   not a mean — `requiredOptionFloorYuan()`. At the moment a margin is drawn nobody
   has chosen, and a mean reads plausible while flattering. **Only REQUIRED groups
   count**: an optional *Add extras?* is revenue the customer volunteered, and
   charging every unit for it would be the same error in the other direction.
### WHY A SECOND COLUMN RATHER THAN A WIDER `unit_cost_at_sale`
The smaller change was to fold the extras into the existing column, and it is
**provably wrong**. `unit_cost_at_sale` is multiplied by `pack_units` downstream — a
Meituan qty of 1 against a 6瓶 listing is six units off the shelf — while
`expandStockLines` adds a linked choice **once per unit bought**, with no pack factor
anywhere in it. One column cannot be multiplied by `pack_units` and left unmultiplied
by it in the same breath: a six-pack would have been charged for six oat milks. The
COGS sum therefore takes the refund factor on both terms and the pack factor on only
one, and both ends carry the warning.
### THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR IS THE WHOLE POINT
Taking the dressing out of the recipe fixes a cost that was too HIGH and, on its own,
replaces it with one that is too LOW — the salad's price still includes a dressing its
cost no longer does. **Too high makes an operator cautious; too low gets a price cut
that cannot be afforded.** That is why the margin change ships in the same PR as the
modelling advice rather than after it, why the floor is the dearest rather than the
mean, and why a required choice nobody has priced **blocks the margin outright**
instead of falling back to the typed cost. An em dash is the honest answer; a
confident number built on a partial sum is not.
### WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, DELIBERATELY
- **Waste.** See above. The first design is withdrawn, not deferred.
- **`cost_coverage`.** The fraction still asks only whether `unit_cost_at_sale` is
  present, so a line whose product is costed and whose oat milk is not still counts
  as covered. The fraction has a published meaning and redefining it quietly is worse
  than a gap that is written down.
- **The channel ingest paths.** Meituan's and Eleme's `options_json` carries the
  channel's own attribute labels, not our `choice_id`/`stock_product_id`, so there is
  no link to price and nothing to write. Left alone rather than wired to return null.
- **Nothing reads `is_default` for cost.** A default is what the customer is shown
  first, not what we are obliged to hand over, and the floor is about obligation.
### ONE GAP LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE, AND IT LEANS THE WRONG WAY
**The catalogue LIST's margin column carries no floor.** `_paMarginCell()` reads
`unit_cost` off the list payload; only the editor's `pdRenderMargin()` adds the
required choices. The floor is a per-product derivation over two more tables, priced
through `productUnitCostYuan()` so a bundle chosen as an extra resolves, and 261
active products would be 261 of those on every list paint. The list is a scan; the
editor is where a price is set, and that is the one this ships for.
**The disagreement is zero today** — nothing live has a required choice linked to a
costed product — **and when it appears the list will read HIGH**, which is the same
flattering direction this whole section exists to close. So it is written down at the
call site as well as here, and the fix when it is wanted is a batched floor on the
list endpoint, never a second derivation in the browser.
### LANGUAGE
Two pairs COMPOSED under Rule 4's fourth amendment and declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.114 with every lifted half named and the live
candidates rejected: `含必选项 ¥X` and `毛利 — 必选项暂无成本`. `必选` is lifted from
the checkbox that sets the very flag being read, on the same screen; `暂无成本` from
the waste screen's own words for the identical fact.
### COVERAGE
`scripts/test_option_cost.js` drives `lib/option-cost.js` against a real in-memory
database: a label-only choice costs a real zero, a linked-but-unpriced choice blocks
rather than contributing nothing, a required multi takes its `min_choices` dearest, an
optional group never counts toward the floor, and the two nulls (nothing linked vs
nothing priceable) are told apart by `linked`. Every case red-proofed against the tree
before the fix.

## §167 — MAKING ONE: SCALE IT, GATHER IT, WORK THE STEPS — AND WRITE NOTHING

Asked by Ash, 2026-09-17, after stage one shipped: *"do it"* — option C of the
mockups, the bench tool.

### WHAT IT IS

*Make it* on a recipe opens a screen with a batch multiplier in halves, the
ingredient list scaled live and tickable as each thing is gathered, and a
full-height step sheet that works one step at a time. The sheet covers the tab
bar on purpose: nothing else on the phone is wanted while both hands are busy.

### THE DECISION: IT WRITES NOTHING

The scale and the ticks are facts about **this afternoon**, not about the
recipe. Doubling a batch to cook for a party does not make the recipe twice the
size, so nothing here is stored — not the multiplier, not which lines have been
gathered, not which step somebody reached. The screen needs no write capability
and carries no save.

**This is a decision and not an omission.** §164's addendum, a few hours old at
the time of writing, records what happened the last time a phone-side change met
a save path: hiding the Cost & Pricing tab left `draftCostData()` reading inputs
that were no longer there, and an ordinary autosave after a NAME correction
wiped labour, overhead and sell price. A new screen that writes to recipes from
a phone is not what this wants next. If stage three ever needs one, it gets its
own decision and its own survey of what reads those columns.

### THE FINISH HANDS OFF RATHER THAN INVENTING A SECOND WRITE

The mockup's third screen logged a recipe-shaped batch: a yield in grams, a
serving count, what it took off the shelf. That is **not built**, and the reason
is that it presumes an answer to a question nobody has settled: what does a
recipe PRODUCE? It may back a material (~27 do), feed several products at
different pack sizes, or neither. `logbatch` already answers that question in
product units, and `scripts/test_production_log.js` holds it to it.

So the foot of the screen OPENS `logbatch` — gated on `canRoute('logbatch')`,
because `production:log` is a different key from `recipes:view` and a kitchen
operator holding the second need not hold the first. A button that 403s is
worse than no button.

### TWO THINGS THE MOCKUP DREW THAT THE DATA CANNOT BACK

`recipe_steps` holds `id`, `recipe_id`, `step_number`, `name`, `instructions`.
That is all.

- **The per-step ingredient list** (*"This step uses — Lemon-herb dressing 720 g"*)
  has no link behind it. There is no step→ingredient relation anywhere in the
  schema, so drawing one would have been invention dressed as data.
- **The rest timer** (*"Rest 10 minutes before the next step"*) likewise: no
  column holds it.

Both are absent, and `scripts/test_mobile_recipes.js` asserts their absence
rather than leaving it to whoever reads the mockup next. Adding either means
adding a column first, which is its own decision.

### VOCABULARY

Mostly lifted, and the best find is that the step counter already existed:
`Step N of M · 第 N 步,共 M 步` is the broadcast composer's own pair, and the
test asserts that pair is still live so an edit there cannot silently orphan
this one. `Back · 返回`, `Next · 下一步`, `Done · 完成`, `None · 无` and
`Log a batch · 登记批次` are all the app's own.

Two pairs composed, each two live words joined, declared in
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` with their rejected candidates.

### COVERAGE

`scripts/test_mobile_recipes.js`. The load-bearing cases: the screen contains no
write verb at all, it draws no money, the sheet cannot paint over the record
underneath it, and neither invented block from the mockup is present.

## §168 — THE FACILITY NAMES COME INTO ENGLISH, AND §30's "KEEP IT CHINESE" NARROWS TO ONE CASE

Asked by Ash, 2026-09-17, looking at TC000761 on the English side: *"can we do
city and provinces also in English?"* — then, to the recommendation below,
*"build and once you done merge and deploy live"*.

### WHAT WAS DECIDED BEFORE, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG

Earlier the same day, shipping the carrier-event translator (PR #676), this
session decided that FACILITY names inside an event sentence would stay in
Chinese — `Arrived at 广州黄埔集货分拣中心` — on two arguments: they are proper
nouns, and the Chinese is the string a customer needs if they ring the carrier.
