Administrative place names (`广州市`) were translated, facility names were not.

**Both arguments fail on a real timeline.** A customer quotes a WAYBILL to a
carrier, never a sorting centre; the facility name is not the string they need.
And the line

    Left 深圳航空分拣中心 — heading to 北京大兴航空分拣中心

withholds the single most useful fact on the screen — the parcel flew from
Shenzhen to Beijing — from precisely the reader the translation exists for.
Half the sentence was English and the half carrying the geography was not.

### THE DECISION: PARSE THEM, DO NOT TRANSLITERATE

Chinese logistics facility names are structured, not arbitrary:
`[city][district][type]`. So they are parsed against three tables — the city
table already built for the location field, a district table, and a facility-type
table (`集货分拣中心` → Consolidation Sorting Centre, `营业部` → Branch, `站` →
Station, and so on) — and reassembled in English.

    广州黄埔集货分拣中心   →  Guangzhou Huangpu Consolidation Sorting Centre
    深圳航空分拣中心      →  Shenzhen Air Sorting Centre
    广州黄村站           →  Guangzhou Huangcun Station

**ALL OR NOTHING.** If any part is unknown, the WHOLE name stays Chinese.
`广州市-保利天汇项目接驳点` contains a property development this cannot name, so
it renders unchanged rather than as a half-English `Guangzhou 保利天汇项目
Transfer Point`. This is the same rule the location field already follows, and
it is what keeps a growing table from producing mixed-language lines while it
grows.

### WHAT STAYS CHINESE: PICKUP POINTS, AND ONLY PICKUP POINTS

`菜鸟驿站`, `快递柜`, `代收点`, `自提点`. **The customer physically walks to one
and has to match the name against a sign on a shopfront.** This is the one case
the original "keep it Chinese" reasoning was actually right about, and it is now
the whole of that rule rather than a blanket over every facility. The pickup
rule does not call the facility translator; the transit rules do.

### ALSO DECIDED HERE: AIR LEGS ARE EVENTS TOO

TC000761's NEWEST event — the top line of the screen, the first thing a customer
reads — was `您的快件在【深圳市飞往北京】的航班上,已起飞` and had no rule at all.
Air legs now translate (`In flight — Shenzhen to Beijing, departed`), with the
two names read as cities rather than facilities, because that is what they are.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE

§30 rule 3 and `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` Rule 4 govern COMPOSING
CHINESE. Nothing here composes any: every string added is English, read out of
Chinese that the carrier wrote. The vocabulary lock is not engaged, and this
section is not an amendment to it.

### WHERE IT LIVES

`lib/tracking.js` — `translateFacility()`, `FACILITY_TYPE_EN`, `DISTRICT_EN`,
applied inside `TRANSLATION_RULES` via the `fac()` alias. Pinned by
`scripts/test_tracking_translation.js` section 6, which previously asserted the
opposite and now carries the reversal in its own comment so the change is
readable rather than merely absent.


## §169 — BUYERS ARE A BREAKDOWN, NOT A NUMBER

Asked by Ash, 2026-09-17, reading the phone's Trend screen: *"people bought I
see low number it can't be all channels"*.

### THE FAULT

Every customer figure on both halves of the product — People bought, First-time
buyers, Top spender, retention — is keyed on `retail_orders.customer_id`.
`routes/meituan-internal.js` and `routes/eleme-internal.js` have never written
that column; their INSERTs do not carry it. SQL's `COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)`
skips NULL, so every marketplace order is invisible to all of them, while the
revenue four tiles above counts every one.

That is how **79 buyers** comes to sit under **¥149,344**. Neither number is
wrong. They describe different populations and nothing said so.

### THE DECISION: THEY STAY SEPARATE

**One "people bought" across all channels is not available and never will be.**
A single total would count the same human twice the moment they order in the
mini app and on Meituan, and no join exists that could detect it: our
`customer_id`, Meituan's `wmUserId` and a wholesale phone are three identity
spaces that do not reconcile. Adding them produces a number that is confidently
wrong and unfalsifiable.

A breakdown is the closest to real that is also true.

### WHAT CAN BE COUNTED, AND ON WHAT

| Channel | Counted on | Exact? |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront — mini app, web, QR, POS | `customer_id` | yes |
| Meituan | `channel_customer_id` (wmUserId) | yes, from 2026-09-15 |
| Wholesale — gzgrocery | `recipient_phone`, real and unmasked | yes |
| Eleme | — | **cannot** |

**Eleme's absence is evidenced, not assumed.** The shape digest the daemon has
recorded all along was read back on 2026-09-17. Its `userInfo` object — the only
person-shaped container among 189 field names — holds 33 keys: consignee name,
phones, address, distance, image and IM state. No `userId`, no `uid`, no
`openid`, nothing that survives from one order to the next. It identifies a
DELIVERY, not a customer. The masked address is `天河区**大厦 3*号` and the phone
is a 隐私号 that rotates; neither is an identity.

### NEW-VS-RETURNING IS NOT ONE DEFINITION

They are labelled by channel and never added together, because they answer
different questions:

- **Storefront** — *new* means the customer's first-ever paid order falls inside
  the window. We compute it from our own history.
- **Meituan** — *new* means `channel_customer_orders = 1`, which is **Meituan's
  own lifetime count** at the moment the order arrived. It counts business done
  before this daemon existed, which ours cannot.

Both are honest. Presenting them as one figure would not be.

### THE MEITUAN COUNT UNDER-REPORTS UNTIL MID-SEPTEMBER, AND IS SHOWN ANYWAY

`channel_customer_id` has only been stored since 2026-09-15 (PR #614). A 30- or
90-day window therefore reads low and will climb as history accrues. Backfilling
it means re-reading every historical order from Meituan's most-audited endpoint
and is **not done**.

A figure that carries *from 15 Sep* is honest. One that silently reads 3 is not.

### WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE

Revenue, orders, products, stores, payments and visits are untouched. This
section decides the customer figures and only those.

### NOT DECIDED HERE

**Whether wholesale product lines join the product ranking.** gzgrocery revenue
is in the headline and its order lines are filtered out of `topProducts` by the
same `NOTGZ` guard that stops its takings being counted twice. Including them is
defensible — the ranking is its own aggregation and is not added to the
headline — but it changes a desktop panel a year old, and it is a different
question from who bought. Left for its own decision.

**Whether Eleme's order tags carry a returning-customer label.** `orderTags`,
`cqsOrderTag` and `deliveryTag` are in the payload, and Meituan answers
"returning?" with a label rather than an id. Settling it means reading tag
VALUES, which the shape digest deliberately strips. That is a different
permission from reading field names and is not taken in passing.

## §170 — THE WAIT GETS A DATE ON THE CARD, AND §108's "A PILL CANNOT" IS OVERTURNED

**DECIDED BY ASH, 2026-09-18**, reading the mini app Shop from a Shenzhen
address at 10:04 on a batch morning: *"our real issue isn't the tag — it's that
a Shenzhen shopper sees NEXT BATCH with no date attached until they're deep in
checkout. The word alone sounds like an indefinite wait."*

**NOTHING WAS BROKEN, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A FIX.** The
reported row — a sold-out Tabbouleh Bowl carrying `NEXT BATCH` on a day the
kitchen was cooking — was three correct rules meeting. The shelf was at zero, so
`_stockState` made the row reservable rather than dead. Today WAS on the cadence
(anchor 2026-06-16, interval 2 → 2026-09-18 is a batch day, confirmed against
`lib/batch-cadence.js` rather than by hand) and the hour was before the 11:00
ready hour, so the server stamped `local_fresh_today`. And the address was
Shenzhen, so `local_run` was false and §108's silence — which belongs to the
local run alone — correctly did not fire. That shopper genuinely waits for a
courier. The label was honest and it was still the wrong thing to show.

**WHAT §108 GOT RIGHT AND WHAT IT GOT WRONG.** Right: *the word describes the
item, not the shopper* — a meal not yet made is `NEXT BATCH` to everybody, and
that stands here untouched. Wrong: *"the DATE ... belongs in the checkout
notice, which states it, not in a pill, which cannot."* The pill can. The date
was already on the wire when §108 was written — `decorateFreshBatch` has stamped
`local_fresh_date` on every browse row since §80 — and the only thing missing was
the one day of transit between the make day and a couriered arrival. **A
customer decides whether to tap on the card, not in the checkout**, so putting
the answer three screens after the question was the defect, and it was a design
choice rather than a limit.

**THE CARD NAMES THE ARRIVAL, NOT THE MAKE DAY**, and those are different dates
for different shoppers: the local run is served the day the batch is made, a
couriered order the day after. Both are computed on the SERVER and stamped per
row — `fresh_ship_date` and `local_fresh_in_days` beside the existing pair — for
exactly §82's reason. "Is this tomorrow" is a question about the tenant's
calendar, and a handset in another zone, or with a wrong clock, must not be the
thing that answers it. The client adds one to an INTEGER and formats a string it
was handed; it performs no date arithmetic and reads no clock.

**THE WORD IS BOUNDED AT TWO DAYS.** `TODAY · 今天` and `TOMORROW · 明天` are
worth more than a date because they need no reading; past that a relative count
("in 3 days") makes a shopper do the arithmetic the card was supposed to save
them, so the card prints the date itself — `SEP 20 · 9月20日`. Both forms are
LIFTED whole from live pairs (`checkout.wxml:400` for the two day words,
`checkout.js:1911` for the Chinese date), so **no Chinese is composed** and
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` Rule 4 is not engaged as an amendment; the
lift is recorded there as v1.123 so the pairs can be found from either end.

**ALL SEVEN BROWSE SURFACES MOVE TOGETHER, and that is the whole of §108's
lesson rather than an enlargement of the brief.** Ash asked for the card. The
card is one of seven places the word is drawn — the shop grid, the shop size
sheet, the PDP badge, the PDP button, the PDP size rows, the favourites tile and
the web shop card — and §108 exists BECAUSE two of them disagreed and Ash caught
it in a screenshot pair. Dating one and not the rest would rebuild that bug with
the same two products. One derivation answers all of them
(`miniapp/utils/fresh-eta.js`); `public/shop.html` carries the only second copy
because it is a standalone single-file storefront that requires nothing, and its
copy names the original.

**THE ADD TOASTS AND `add-to-order` STAY OUT**, keeping §108's own carve-out: a
toast is read after the decision it would inform, and the add-on picker is not a
browse surface. **THE CHECKOUT NOTICE IS UNTOUCHED.** It answers a harder
question than the card does — it knows the cart, the fulfilling store and the
zero-stock roll-forward — and the two can differ legitimately, the card being the
optimistic per-item answer and the checkout the binding per-order one. Where they
differ the checkout is right, which is the safe direction: the card can only ever
name a date the checkout then confirms or pushes back, never one it pulls in.
## §171 — A PRINTER IS A BRAND, NOT A CONSTANT: THE SLIP RAIL TAKES A SECOND VENDOR

**2026-09-18 · Asked by Ash**, holding a 商鹏 SP-T6-H bought for the new Yuexiu
shop: *"we need to add this printer as well to our system"*, and then, against a
recommendation to send it back and buy a Feie unit: *"think about different
tenant, not all of them will use the same printer brand, so adding more printer
options its better"*. **The second message is the decision and it overrides the
first recommendation, which was argued on Roots' costs alone and was wrong on
the product.** Roots is one tenant of a platform. A tenant arrives with the
printer already screwed to the counter, and "buy a different printer" is not a
thing an onboarding can say.

**THE RECOMMENDATION THAT WAS OVERRULED IS RECORDED BECAUSE ITS ONE GOOD
ARGUMENT SURVIVED.** The case against a second vendor was that the slip
templates would exist twice — two renderers for two brands of the same 58mm
paper, drifting the first time somebody edits one and not the other. That
objection was correct about the danger and wrong about the necessity, and the
shape below exists to answer it: **there is exactly one renderer and there will
only ever be one.**

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY VENDOR-SPECIFIC IS SMALL.** `lib/feie.js` is 1210 lines and
reads as one thing; it is two. Roughly 120 lines are transport — the endpoint,
the signature, the byte cap, the success test. The remaining ~1090 are 58mm
layout: column arithmetic, the bilingual name join, slot absolutisation, the
full-width yuan sign, the five markup tags. **Only the tags touch the vendor.**
So the split is not "a renderer per brand", it is **one renderer emitting house
markup, and a translation table at the wire.**

**THE HOUSE MARKUP IS FEIE'S TAG SET, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS NOT LAZINESS.**
`<CB> <B> <L> <BOLD> <C>` become the canonical vocabulary every slip is written
in, and the Feie adapter is a pass-through. The alternative — a neutral
intermediate form, invented here — would have rewritten every renderer in the
file on day one to gain nothing a translation table does not already give, and
would have put a second untested layer under the one surface in this product
that a customer holds in their hand. **A vendor adapter translates house markup
into its own on the way out. That is the whole contract.**

**THE VENDOR IS A PER-STORE FIELD, NOT A TENANT-WIDE ONE.** A tenant with four
shops may well have three Feie and one Shangpeng, because printers are bought
one at a time by whoever opened that shop. So `printer.by_store` rows take an
optional `vendor`, the kitchen takes `printer.kitchen_vendor`, and **an absent
`vendor` means `feie`** — which is what every row saved before today is, so
there is no migration and no backfill, and a tenant who never touches this
notices nothing.

**THE CREDENTIALS ARE PER VENDOR AND PER TENANT, ON THE RAIL THAT ALREADY
EXISTS.** `integrations.spyun = { appid, appsecret }` sits beside
`integrations.feie = { user, ukey }`, through the same secret-box and the same
boot hydration as every other integration. A tenant configures the brands they
own and leaves the rest blank. **The global "is printing on?" gate stops being
`feieEnabled()` and becomes "is ANY vendor configured?"** — otherwise a
Shangpeng-only tenant is told printing is unconfigured while their printer sits
there working.

**WHAT THE DEVICE LABEL IS FOR, CORRECTED.** An earlier reading of this in
chat had Shangpeng authenticating per-device on the SN + KEY printed on the
label. **That was wrong and is corrected here before it becomes folklore.**
Shangpeng authenticates exactly as Feie does: an account-level pair from the
developer console (`appid` + `appsecret`), with the device's SN naming which
printer to print at. The label's KEY (`pkey`) binds the device to the account
once, in the console or the app, and the server never sends it. **This is the
same mistake the Feie block in the admin screen has warned about since it was
written** — *"the USERKEY is from your developer console, not the secret on the
label"* — and it is the same warning, for the same reason, one vendor over.

**THE SIGNATURES DIFFER AND THAT IS ALL THE TRANSPORT REALLY IS.** Feie:
`sha1(user + ukey + stime)`, form-posted to `api.feieyun.cn`, success is
`ret === 0`. Shangpeng: every parameter sorted by key, joined `k=v` with `&`,
`&appsecret=…` appended, MD5'd, posted to `open.spyun.net/v1/printer/print`,
success is `errorcode === 0`. Both endpoints and both signature shapes were read
off the published `@xesam/cloud-vendor-spyun` client and cross-checked against
the base URL compiled into Shangpeng's own developer console bundle, **not
recalled** — the vendor's documentation sites are client-rendered and would not
open through this session's proxy.

**ONE THING IS NOT VERIFIED AND IS MARKED AS SUCH IN THE CODE.** Shangpeng's
markup tag names could not be read from a primary source for the reason just
given. The adapter's translation table therefore ships as an explicit,
one-screen map with every entry commented, defaulting to pass-through on the
reading that the Chinese cloud-printer vendors share this convention. **It is a
table, not a belief** — if a test print comes back with literal `<CB>` on the
paper, the fix is one line in one file and no renderer moves. **The enlarged-line
width is the same class of unknown**: `BIG_WIDTH = 16` was measured off a Feie
FP-V58-D head and is not promised to hold on an SP-T6-H, so it moves into the
adapter where a per-vendor value can live.

**THE SP-T6-H HAS NO AUTO-CUTTER** (`自动切纸:不支持` on its label), where the
FP-V58-D does. Nothing in the code depends on this — the slip is the same
bytes either way — but the Yuexiu counter tears by hand and it is recorded so
the first person told "the printer is broken, it doesn't cut" can find out here
that it never did.

**NO CHINESE WAS COMPOSED.** The admin screen gains a vendor picker whose two
options are the vendors' own registered names — 飞鹅 and 商鹏 — and the labels
around it reuse strings already live on that panel. `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`
Rule 4 is not engaged.

**WHAT IS NOT DECIDED HERE.** Label printing, order-status polling and the
queue-clearing calls that both vendors expose are not wired: nothing in this
product asks for them, and an adapter contract wide enough to cover a feature
nobody has asked for is how the interface gets fixed wrong before the second
implementation arrives. The contract is `enabled` and `printContent`, and it
grows when a third vendor or a real requirement makes it grow.
## §172 — WHAT THE SHOP KNOWS ABOUT A PERSON IS READ ON EVERY ORDER, AND IS EDITED IN ONE PLACE

**DECIDED BY ASH, 2026-09-18**, looking at TC000750's drawer: *"an order note
will appear only for that order. however we need a note that will appear for
this customer order everytime he place an order."*

**THE FIELD ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS NOT READ.** `retail_customers.note` and
`.tags` have been on the customer since the drawer's Know block was built — free
text the operator types, plus a comma-separated tag list, both editable in the
customer drawer and searchable from the Customers list. Nothing on an order ever
looked at them. So the knowledge existed, in the right place, and reached nobody
at the moment it was needed: the person packing the parcel. This decision adds
no storage. It adds a read.

**THREE NOTES CAN SIT ON ONE ORDER AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME NOTE.**
`customer_note` is what the BUYER typed at checkout, for that order.
`staff_note` is what the SHOP typed, for that order. The third —
`retail_customers.note`, aliased `customer_standing_note` on the order read — is
what the shop knows about the PERSON, and it is true of every order they place.
An allergy, a lift that does not work, invoicing monthly: none of those are
facts about a parcel.

**THE COPY RULE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ARCHITECTURE.** The note is READ from the
customer on every order and never copied onto one. `GET
/api/retail-admin/orders/:id` already `LEFT JOIN`ed `retail_customers` for the
nickname and phone; the note and tags ride the same join. Correct the note once
on the customer page and every order — past, open and future — reads the
corrected text, because there is only ever one copy. Had it been stamped onto
the order at checkout, an order would keep a note the customer page had already
retired, and no one reading the order could tell which was true.

**READ-ONLY IN THE ORDER DRAWER, AND THIS IS THE PART TO NOT UNDO.** The Edit
button navigates to the customer; it does not open a field. The alternative —
an editable box in the drawer — puts a permanent note a few pixels from the
per-order Shop note, wearing nearly the same label. The failure is not
hypothetical: it is "no ice **this time**" typed into the note that then follows
a person for a year, invisible to whoever typed it. One copy, one place to
change it, and the place is the one screen that is about the person.

**IT DOES NOT GO TO THE CUSTOMER.** The customer-facing read is
`loadOrderForCustomer`, which names its columns by hand and does not select
this one. That is deliberate and load-bearing: the standing note is what the
shop says about a customer, and some of it — chases, disputes, "check the
address twice" — is not written to be read by them. A future session widening
that column list widens it past this note.

**NOT SHOWN WHERE THERE IS NO PERSON.** Walk-ins and most channel orders carry
no `customer_id`, so the note is null and nothing renders. No empty state, no
placeholder: §160's rule that a control which does nothing is worse than no
control applies to labels that say "no note" just as well.

**WHERE IT LANDS, AND WHAT WAS LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE.** The desktop order drawer
(both the main one and the mirrored channel view) and the phone app's order
detail, all three off the one endpoint. The Orders LIST and the kitchen/packing
print were considered and deliberately left for their own change — the list is
where tag filtering would earn its keep, and the print is where an allergy note
does, but each is a separate surface and a separate PR under the one-PR-per-
change rule.

**NO CHINESE IS MINTED.** The label pair is `About this customer ·
关于该顾客的备注`, and its Chinese half is LIFTED WHOLE from the live aria-label on
the very textarea this text is typed into, in the customer drawer. Same string,
same thing, both screens. Recorded in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md`
v1.124, which locks nothing new.

**ADDENDUM, 2026-09-18 (v4.309) — THE WRITE END. A NOTE NOBODY CAN FIND IS
WORTH NOTHING.** Ash, minutes after the read end was built, on the customer
page with the control three inches from the cursor: *“im on customer page wher
is it”*. With nothing stored, the Know block collapses to a bare `Edit` under
the customer's name — correct about space and silent about purpose. It now
carries `What we know · 备注与标签`, which is not a new string but this
block's own heading, live on the phone's customer record for the same block
and already locked. Shown ONLY while the block is empty, which is the only
state that was ambiguous: a note prints its own line, tags print chips, and
beside either the button's job is plain. The block costs one line when empty
and not a pixel more once used, so the saving that collapsed the old 210px
card stands. **The empty-state string this block once rejected is still
rejected**: `暂无备注。` names the ABSENCE of a note, which anyone looking at
an empty block can see; the heading names the CONTROL. That distinction is the
whole of this addendum and is the thing to keep if either is ever revisited.
Recorded as `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` v1.125, which locks nothing
new. Covered by the same suite as the read end.
